in writing. the italian presidency of the council has opened its six-month term virtually at the same time as the new european parliament term. the challenge we faced last july was clear: the commission's proposal is to show that the european institutions can change and break free from the dogma of austerity, and can respond to the economic and social crisis with concrete actions, with policies that are attentive to the needs of citizens and businesses and not just to budgetary balances. today, as president renzi is speaking in parliament, the commission is meeting to approve the proposal for a regulation on the 315 billion investment fund and the new guidelines on the flexibility of national budgets. can we say that europe has changed in just six months? i think rather that with the new parliament, the commission which took office in november and the exceptional contribution of the italian presidency we have finally started the manoeuvre to change direction. in italy, the government has chosen the motto "step by step". i think that's a message that can work in europe as well. the manoeuvre has begun, the engines must now be given a boost, and to do this parliament must be able to convert the pressure of the citizens into the best fuel.
in writing. as regards investment, italy has been working since the beginning of the semester to put this issue at the centre of eu policy action. the purchase of liquidity at low prices will be an important resource for the market in the next two years, thanks to the ecb's action, and effective and strategic projects will be a useful tool to this end. the last ecofin meeting of the italian presidency then finalized the details of the 'single resolution fund' which will be capitalised over the next eight years, taxing european banks for an amount equal to 1% of deposits. the italian presidency also gave the final impetus to a number of environmental dossiers, culminating in their adoption. among the many: - the directive on freedom from the prohibition of the cultivation of gmos; - the agreement on standards for the disposal of single-use plastic bags; - ratification of the extension of the kyoto climate agreements. finally, a number of cases concerning tax evasion and avoidance were successfully prosecuted during the italian semester: - the directive on the taxation of the parent company of a company and its subsidiaries in different countries; - the one on the automatic exchange of tax information. austria and luxembourg have also renounced banking secrecy. this is perhaps the area in which italy has been most successful in playing its role as mediator.

on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, today marks the end of a negotiating process which has lasted over four years and during which parliament has already expressed its position at first reading by a very large majority. this parliament had clearly indicated its willingness to introduce into the text of the agreement certain elements which it considered to be fundamental. the most important changes included the possibility for member states to act as public health and environmental risk managers when deciding whether or not to grow gm plants, to ban their use because of environmental and health hazards that efsa continues to ignore, to ensure the application of the polluter pays principle and more. these same amendments were confirmed at second reading and voted by a very large majority in the committee on the environment, which had also expressed its total opposition to the obscene proposal of the council that it could be expected that a member state would have to recognize biotech companies as the interlocutors with whom to agree national restrictions, and it was on these guidelines that we had given the green light to the trilogue. none of the points mentioned, however, survived the final negotiations, were removed from the text and ended up in a long list of unnecessary recitals. farms will be able to give their consent to the restriction of the geographical scope of the authorizations, but will not be required to provide reimbursement in the event of contamination. political agreements are the result of compromises where both sides give up some of their initial positions. in view of parliament's capitulation to the council's demands, we can only vote against the conclusion of this agreement.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, after four years of work we have finally reached agreement on a sensitive subject such as genetically modified organisms, which is of great interest to the public and is the subject of important scientific and political debates. i would first like to thank my colleague, the rapporteur, mrs ries, for the work she has done for parliament, as well as colleagues from all the other political groups who have helped to improve the text and who have worked effectively towards an agreement on this dossier. i also thank mr galletti for the italian presidency for the excellent cooperation during the negotiations which enabled us to reach agreement on a joint text by the end of last year with his support, mr commissioner. in my view, this compromise is the only possible agreement and, like any good compromise, it must leave the same bitter taste in everyone's mouth. parliament wanted to take forward certain positions on certain issues and it was unable to do so, it had to sacrifice them on the altar of an agreement and this is the only possible agreement. i think it should be remembered, however, that, apart from the various positions that can be taken on this matter, the main objective that we set ourselves as politicians and as legislators was to create a certain legal basis on this matter. in fact, in the face of a situation of uncertainty which had given rise to many appeals, we shall finally have legal certainty. i therefore urge all members to support this agreement, which i repeat was the best possible agreement of all those we have examined.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i too think we have done a good job, a good compromise, certainly a step forward after four years of deadlock. of course, not everything is as we would have liked, but we are certainly building a text that takes us a step further and that is not comparable to the current situation. for those of us who, like myself, want to preserve our traditional products, who want to protect the biodiversity that is a richness of our land, who want to avoid product approval, this text is a step forward. the commissioner is right, europe defines the criteria, the safety net, the authorization methods and the national states finally have a certain legal basis for intervening. it is a step forward that allows us to overcome years of uncertainty and allows all those who care about - i repeat - the defence of typical products to finally be able to say: we did it! madam president, ladies and gentlemen, mrs evi has just mentioned the questionable role played by efsa. we are convinced that the lack of confidence of the europeans in gmos and also in the control agencies is based precisely on the failure of this european agency to demonstrate impartiality and independence in its assessments, also and especially on gmos. efsa has never felt it should deny authorisations to any gmos, even when it was the biotech companies themselves who recognised the existence of statistically significant differences between genetically modified and conventional plants or, for example, in the physiological response of gm-fed animals compared to controls. on top of this are sad stories of conflicts of interest and disturbing episodes of revolving doors involving experts on the gm evaluation panels. and perhaps it is easier to understand the public's mistrust of gmos and of the efsa itself. for this reason, we believe that member states can and should be able to intervene by banning gmos, also because of the environmental and health risks that their cultivation and use pose. this directive does not go in that direction and we shall vote against it.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms on their territory. the five star movement has been strongly opposed because the text adopted today will make it easier to obtain authorization at community level and will therefore give the green light to gm crops in member states which so wish. that is why we voted against it, together with our colleagues from the greens and the eldr groups.
in writing. today we are completing a piece of legislation of great importance to the citizens of europe. we all know how polarizing the issue of gmos is and how much concern it is creating in the public. it was not obvious that an agreement could be reached after five years of negotiations. we now have a certain regulatory framework, based on the fundamental principles of freedom of choice and scientific security. the final say on the entry and production of gmos now rests with the member states: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the protection of personal data are respected. the role of the member states in introducing control measures for contamination zones and coexistence between border countries remains crucial now, when the new legislation is being implemented from next spring. health protection, consumer protection and the promotion of local products are some of the principles on which europe bases its sustainability model: today we are making a concrete and important gesture to strengthen europe as a place of quality and food security.

in writing. following the acquisition, as of 1 january 2014, of the status of an outermost region of the european union, the exclusive economic zone (eez) of mayotte is now an integral part of the union's waters and, therefore, it is the responsibility of the relevant community authorities not only to manage fisheries resources but also to negotiate and monitor any bilateral agreements signed. in this connection, the european parliament is called upon to express an opinion on the agreement in question, which in this case can only be favourable to us, since it is beneficial to both parties: the commission considers that the proposed measure is in line with the objectives of the common fisheries policy and the ctoi in terms of conservation of resources. although we do not have specific powers to amend the agreement, we would like to stress today the need to involve mayotte's fishermen in the meetings of the joint committee set up by this agreement and to ensure their participation in all stages of its implementation, as well as to provide for structural investment and administrative control frameworks to promote the sustainable development of the fishing and processing sectors on the island.

in writing. fisheries relations between the eu and the republic of seychelles are governed by the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement (sfpa) which entered into force in 2003 and has been renewed twice. i remember how this is the most important agreement the eu has in the indian ocean, and consequently the seychelles are the eu's main partner in the region. the agreement allows vessels flying the flag of seychelles to have access to the waters and marine biological resources of mayotte, which has the status of an outermost region of the eu. it is clear that this agreement is exceptional in that it allows vessels from a third country to fish in european territorial waters. the reason why the agreement was promoted, and i am in favour of it, is to limit the number of seychelles vessels fishing in mayotte's waters, in accordance with the rules of the common fisheries policy. this is to protect tuna stocks because of their migratory nature. i am also reassured that the agreement includes a mid-term review clause which will allow the effectiveness of the agreement to be assessed three years after its entry into force.
in writing. - i decided to vote in favour because the recommendation allows the agreement with the seychelles to be respected, allowing their vessels to fish in the waters of the outermost region of mayotte and bringing a benefit to local shipowners resident in an area under eu jurisdiction.
in writing. with today's vote we have given our consent to the first 'access agreement' allowing third country vessels to fish in european waters. this will allow a limited number of vessels flying the flag of seychelles (8 tuna seiners and 2 support vessels) to continue fishing in mayotte's waters for a period of six years, in compliance with european rules on the common fisheries policy. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the agreement can bring benefits not only to seychelles but also to the economic development of mayotte. the fees charged for the issuing of licences will enable this outermost region of europe to respond effectively to the sectoral needs of the island in terms of port infrastructure, landing, control and placing products on the market.

in writing. the european commission's white paper on transport presents the eu's roadmap towards a single european area with reference to competitiveness and sustainability. the white paper published in 2011 sets ten targets to achieve the 60% greenhouse gas emissions reduction target. it has aspects which can be shared, such as the gradual abandonment of cars powered by traditional fuels until they are completely phased out, the use of means of transport with a lower environmental impact, and the improvement of passenger safety. at the same time, however, there are negative aspects such as the ten-t networks and the use of large-scale projects and transnational corridors. it was decided to prepare an own-initiative report to assess the implementation of the white paper on transport with regard to detection and pathways to sustainable mobility. i voted in favour of asking the european economic and social committee to be consulted on this matter. under rule 137 of parliament's rules of procedure, parliament can ask the economic and social committee to be consulted on general matters or on specific points, as in this case.

in writing. - in 2011, the commission adopted the white paper on transport, with the aim of outlining a competitive system that can increase mobility, remove the main obstacles in urban areas and foster growth and jobs, while ensuring sustainability. among the various ambitious targets, there was also the reduction of both europe's dependence on oil imports and carbon emissions from transport (a reduction expected to reach 60% by 2050), as well as the withdrawal of traditional fuel cars from the city market by 2050, and the switch, by 2050, of more than 50% of goods from road transport to alternative, efficient and green means. the committee on transport is preparing a report to assess the implementation of the measures contained in the white paper, and i support the request to consult the economic and social committee on this because i believe it is essential to listen to the voice of the associations representing the categories and the citizens, who are better aware than any other body of the needs of the actors involved and of the population in general. the findings will undoubtedly be of great use in making the report more complete and effective.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the cultivation of gmos is still a subject of heated debate, not only between member states but also within the countries of the european union, where public opinion is still sharply divided, especially because the effects on the health of the citizens are still unclear. the text voted today comes after three years of negotiations: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be given the opportunity to present their opinions on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. states are given a free choice based not only on the assessment of environmental risk and the effects of crops on the health of citizens, but also on consideration of socioeconomic impact and agricultural policy considerations. i therefore believe that the compromise is in the right direction, ensuring greater protection of the health of the citizens, which is why i voted in favour.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we voted with great conviction on this text, which we have been waiting for for almost four years and which allows member states to restrict or prohibit transgenic cultivation in their national territory. i believe that it is essential to have applied the principle of subsidiarity to such a sensitive issue as environmental safety and security. the broad support that this text has received from the various parliamentary groups once again underlines that parliament is an institution sensitive to the demands of the citizens, who have once again stated forcefully that they want to preserve the foundations of a healthy, safe and quality agriculture. there is only one regret that the question of financial responsibility was left out of the text. i think we have to do more on this, because it is crucial, in my view, to consider the economic damage that can be caused by gm crops to the surrounding crops and it is also crucial to establish who has to pay for the damage that is caused.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we all know how much the debate on gmos is heating up, but this fervour is confusing public opinion, which we know is for the most part - about 58% - against gmos. from an oversimplification, two contradictory positions seem to emerge: the scientific one, which belongs to the so-called bad guys, those who are in favour of gmos; the emotional one, the good ones, all those who are against gmo cultivation because they're actually afraid. in fact, it is the scientific world that is not in agreement on this subject: unfortunately, the lack of a single answer from scientists has inevitably led to the development of an ideological debate, which has marginalized the scientific aspect and thus limited the important factor of research. each of us in this house will be helping to encourage research and debate in our own countries to make responsible and profitable choices. the agreement reached is a more than balanced agreement, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. the plenary today voted on a text on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of gmos. the legislative text seems to give full power to the member states to decide whether to restrict or even prohibit this type of cultivation on their national territory. unfortunately, that is not the case. important points which were long negotiated and voted on by a large majority in the envi committee were not included in the new text. among these, the obligation to insure gm crops to cover any compensation in case of contamination of conventional or organic crops. instead, clauses have been inserted which give biotech companies the opportunity to negotiate directly with national governments, who will be under tremendous pressure. the latter will not be able to use specific national environmental impacts in the grounds for calls which do not give the same result as the environmental impact conducted by efsa (european food safety authority). the member state may only block the cultivation for socioeconomic reasons. we believe that the question of gmos is primarily concerned with the health of the public and only secondarily with the economic aspects. our delegation voted against this.
in writing. the compromise text reached between parliament and the council, after almost four years of debate, introduces for the first time in european legislation a set of procedures to allow a member state to ban a gmo on its territory, even if it has been authorised in the eu. this decision puts the choices of the european citizens at the centre. member states will have the possibility to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their national territory for reasons other than those relating to the environmental risk identified by efsa. the entry into force of this directive also sought to create a transparent mechanism and a sound legal basis which could avoid the numerous cases of litigation brought before the court of justice of the european union in recent years on the authorisation of a gmo. for these reasons i voted in favour of the text of the agreement.
in writing. - i voted against the dossier on the cultivation of gmos in europe because i believe that the mechanism which gives the member states the right to prohibit cultivation, which is in itself a positive thing, is far-reaching and remains 'sub judice' in relation to the commission's wishes; only time will tell how far the free choice of european citizens on gmos will be respected. the danger today is that behind this supposed freedom there is a ruse which in fact makes it possible to 'break the dam' of their entry into the community territory, to the detriment of biodiversity and europe's rich varietal heritage.
in writing. i voted against this proposal for a directive because i believe that it was a wasted opportunity for the european union to protect itself definitively from the pressure of the large multinational companies of agricultural microtechnologies (such as the monsanto company, owner of mon810 maize, which is already grown in 5 european states). under the previous rule, member states could veto gmo crops, invoking health and environmental safeguards, without being regularly dragged before the court of justice of the european union. the new directive was also intended to provide member states with greater protection, but this objective has not been achieved. the directive does not have a fixed time-limit for its application and farms will not be required to provide reimbursement in the event of contamination. the measure was born with the best of intentions, but then, in its legislative process, it bowed to the council's demands until it lost its legal force, leaving the member states once again exposed to the influence of multinational companies that follow market logic, rather than the common sense and good of european citizens.

in writing. i voted today in favour of the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) on their territory. almost five years after the european commission's original proposal, thanks also to the work of the italian presidency, the eu institutions have finally reached an important agreement on this issue. i think that parliament and in particular the envi committee have been able to make a positive impact on the text we have adopted. i refer, for example, to the fact that member states where the cultivation of gmos is permitted will be obliged to adopt coexistence measures for border areas to avoid contamination of traditional crops in neighbouring countries, and to the important strengthening of the rules on risk assessment by the european food safety authority prior to the placing on the market of gmos. i think that on other points, such as the environmental reasons which member states can invoke to prohibit the cultivation of gmos, a stronger and more ambitious text could have been adopted. however, given the difficulty with which this agreement was reached after more than four years, i have decided to vote in favour of the text.

in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on gmos because it is intended to give member states greater freedom to restrict or prohibit their cultivation. more specifically, the two levels of intervention granted to the member states, i.e. at the authorisation stage or after that stage provided that there are adequate grounds, allow them to carry out a 360-degree assessment since they are not bound by any time limit. the proposed text also provides a sound legal basis without, however, interfering with the free movement of gmos, creating conflicts within the world trade organisation or calling into question the expertise and scientific assessments of efsa.
in writing. the resolution aims to relieve member states of the need to provide new scientific data to support any ban on the cultivation of gmos introduced at national level. in return, the commission hopes to achieve a majority in the committee where the new authorization proposals are discussed. i voted against this resolution because the grounds on which gmo cultivation can be banned are very weak from a legal point of view and the enactment of extended bans on gmo groups could make the measures even less defensible in the event of an appeal to the wto or the court of justice of the european union. i vote against because the legal instrument adopted at the end of the negotiations is a directive, but it does not contain any obligations for member states to transpose it. it also remains to be clarified from a legal point of view whether and how the measures will be possible to implement without updating national legislation with appropriate transposition acts.
in writing. the text adopted represents an important step forward, as it introduces clearer rules and greater legal certainty for all matters relating to the cultivation of genetically modified crops. at the same time, however, it gives member states greater flexibility in choosing whether to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. i believe that europe must be at the forefront of the fight for the diversity of traditional crops and to minimise the risks of genetically modified crops. only in this way, by being the first to set clear guidelines, can we be credible when we come to the international trade tables (especially ttip) to defend and claim the quality and uniqueness of our products.
in writing. i voted against the final text on the agreement reached on gmo cultivation, because the only elements added by parliament were the obligation to draw up coexistence plans, but, as we also suggested, limited to countries where gmo cultivation takes place, the possibility of banning groups of gmos and a list of conditions on the basis of which national bans can be established, which does not contain any reference to possible environmental impacts. the final text, however, provides that member states may decide whether to require companies to restrict the geographical scope of the authorisations under assessment or to impose unilateral bans. while this represents an improvement on the link between the two procedures in the council text, it will give firms the power to adopt different behaviour depending on whether the member state decides to involve them in the process or not. in addition, the grounds on which gmo cultivation may be banned are very weak from a legal point of view and the issuing of extended bans on groups of gmos could make the measures even less defensible in the event of an appeal to the wto or the court of justice of the european union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos, as the new text, the result of a significant compromise between parliament and the council, promoted by the italian presidency, has the merit of providing greater legal certainty to a subject which deserves to be approached with particular caution with the ultimate objective of consumer protection. the agreement gives eu member states ample scope to ban the cultivation of gmos authorised at european level in all or part of their national territory. each country will therefore be free to decide - without providing further reasons - to ban gmo crops also for reasons that go beyond the scientific assessments already under the responsibility of efsa: i refer in particular to the possibility of invoking agricultural and environmental policy objectives, land use and urban planning reasons, and the possible socioeconomic and public policy impact. i also think it is important to provide for mandatory coexistence measures which will protect traditional crops from the risk of crossborder contamination with gmos grown in neighbouring countries.
in writing. i supported the agreement reached between the council, commission and parliament on the reform of the gmo directive. the agreement provides for the right of member states to prohibit the cultivation of gm seeds on their territory for economic and agricultural reasons. the directive also provides that states which decide to use gmos must pay particular attention to preventing crossborder contamination with neighbouring countries.

in writing. with today's vote in the european parliament on the reform of the gmo directive, we have finally established the right of member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of genetically modified organisms on their national territory. this is also at the expense of an authorization granted at european level by the food safety agency. in the immediate future, therefore, italy may decide to say no to gm crops on its territory as a result of socioeconomic considerations, land use, land planning, transgenic contamination of other crops, and mere agricultural and environmental policy choices. this decision is a great achievement for our country, which has always been committed to a quality and environmentally friendly agri-food model. the only thing left to do is to activate the national transposition procedures without delay.
in writing. - after four years of negotiations, we have managed to reach a difficult agreement on the sensitive issue of gmos. it recognises the sovereignty and autonomy of each member state as regards the possibility, in full respect of the principle of subsidiarity, of prohibiting or restricting, in all or part of their territory, the cultivation of gmos which have been authorised or are under the authorisation procedure at european level. this choice can be made on the basis of strict criteria, not in conflict with the health and environmental risk assessment carried out by efsa, thus protecting the needs of citizens, consumers and individual states. i would like to thank the rapporteur, the colleagues who have worked on this dossier and minister galletti for the spirit of cooperation which has enabled us to reach the best possible agreement under all the circumstances.

in writing. the agreement on gmos, hailed by the italian presidency as a great success, hides serious pitfalls for those countries that really want to protect their crops. i did not vote for the agreement because it leaves too much of a role for biotechnology multinationals, allowing them to adopt different behaviours depending on whether or not they are faced with a state favourable to gmo crops. the agreement provides for states which prohibit gm crops to follow the conciliation procedure with the applicant farms, thus involving them in the decision-making process. secondly, this agreement makes the bans issued by the member states weaker and less defensible in the event of an appeal to the wto or the court of justice of the european union. finally, there are no compensation mechanisms for any environmental damage caused by gm crops. i voted in favour of the amendments tabled by m5s, gue and the greens to ensure that coexistence plans are drawn up in countries where gm crops are grown. this instrument, if used properly, would also make it very difficult to test gmos in the absence of safeguard measures such as containment and cover to prevent pollination.
in writing. - the outcome of the trilogy was disappointing to say the least. a handful of key elements put forward by parliament were upheld, including the requirement to draw up coexistence plans (but limited to countries where gm crops are grown) and the possibility of banning groups of gmos. the final text approved by the council provided that member states could decide whether to require undertakings to restrict the geographical scope of the authorizations under assessment or to impose unilateral bans: although this may be seen as an improvement, it will give firms the power to adopt different behaviour depending on whether the member state decides to involve them in the process. the reasons described for the prohibition of gmo cultivation are very weak and the legal instrument adopted at the end of the negotiations with the council is a directive which does not contain any obligations for transposition by the member states, thus leaving open the question of whether and how to implement the measures without updating national legislation with appropriate transposition acts. finally, the problem of coexistence is closely linked to the feared risk of accidental spread of gmo seeds or pollen to adjacent conventional crops, which could lead to economic losses due to damage between producers: if the crops had significant amounts of gmos in the harvest, they could no longer be certified as non-gmos. for all the reasons i have just described, i have therefore voted against the report.

in writing. i voted in favour of the legislative resolution amending regulation 1343/2011 because it aims to ensure the sustainable exploitation of red coral and to protect certain marine species from fishing activities which, without the necessary regulation, end up damaging the marine ecosystem. with particular reference to the latter aspect, the proposal for a regulation under consideration aims to ensure the sustainable use of marine resources through an ecosystem approach to the management of human activities, i.e. a methodology that envisages the human community as an integral part of ecosystems and the mechanisms that regulate them.
in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean was established in 1949 by an international agreement. its area of competence covers the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters. the main functions of the cgpm are: to promote the development, conservation and rational management of living aquatic resources. at its annual meetings in 2011 and 2012, the gfcm adopted measures for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the mitigation of by-catch of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans, the protection of sharks and rays, and the fishery for small pelagic fish in the adriatic sea. i voted in favour of this proposal, which aims to incorporate into eu law the recommendations of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal to transpose into eu law measures adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, thus amending regulation (eu) no 1343/2011, because i cannot deny the general good sense of the purpose and some of the provisions contained herein; i would like to stress, however, that as is often the case, many of the individual acceding states have already transposed the measures expressed by the gfcm and will therefore now be forced to ask for a derogation from the european commission whose present proposal in fact ignores the law already in use in the individual states which is often better in terms of protection and care for the environment. i am also concerned about the risk that a delicate species such as red coral may be subjected to treatments which, according to the text thus approved, are not environmentally sustainable.

in writing. we have today approved this proposal which aims to transpose into eu law the recommendations of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean on the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of bycatch of seabirds, sea turtles and cetaceans and the conservation of monk seals, sharks and rays. some of the measures envisaged go well beyond the protection already granted to the species concerned at community level by the habitats directive and other european union acts and therefore end up including some specific registration and reporting obligations for both operators and member states. we therefore consider that the gfcm recommendations establish a sufficient level of regulatory protection which must therefore be implemented by the contracting parties before any further measures can be envisaged in this regard.

in writing. - i decided to vote in favour of this report because it updates the commission proposal which contains technical measures for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles and cetaceans and the conservation of monk seals, sharks and rays in the area where the gfcm agreement applies. these measures go beyond the protection already granted to these species at eu level by the habitats directive and other union acts and include specific registration and reporting obligations for both operators and member states. in addition, the commission proposal is in many cases more stringent than the recommendations of the cgpm.
in writing. the report voted on today aims to transpose into union law a series of measures adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) at its annual sessions in 2011, 2012 and 2013. the text, which i have decided to support by voting in favour, seeks to take the cgpm's recommendations faithfully and in their entirety, avoiding that misinterpretations lead to the definition of more stringent and very often unjustifiable additional measures. i am referring, for example, to the european commission's initial proposal to classify as active small pelagic vessels those for which sardines and/or anchovies represent at least 50% of the catch made in each fishing trip. since this time frame does not fit the local reality of the adriatic where the time spent on board is generally less than 12 hours, i hope that in the next negotiations with the council and the commission the original text of the gfcm recommendation will be taken into account and a fair compromise will be reached in order to clearly identify the vessels which are actually engaged in active bluefin fishing, based on more representative catch data.

in writing. diversity necessarily leads to an improvement in the results and impacts of any production process. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to adopt the directive on the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of their employer. the problem is the penalties to be applied if a company does not reach the 40% quota of female non-executive directors. the real aim of the measure is not to protect women as such, but to promote meritocratic selection mechanisms, in which the best are assigned to positions without discrimination based on sex. in this respect, the recognition of rights is not only right but also useful. for this reason, an alternative approach is proposed: rather than focusing on quota-related sanction mechanisms or on simple eu indications of a quota to be reached, we introduce and promote reward mechanisms for companies that reach the quota. this would also have a positive effect on small and mediumsized enterprises which are currently excluded from the directive.

vice-president of the commission / high representative of the union for foreign affairs. - i am grateful for the invitation to discuss the situation in ukraine at a moment that is particularly important. i was wondering whether there were any moments that were not particularly important in relation to the situation in ukraine in the last 11, 12 or 13 months, and there were probably not. but this gives me the chance to report to you in plenary about the work that is going on at my level and also about my recent visit to ukraine. i visited kiev on 16 and 17 december 2014, almost one month ago. my messages there, which i also had the chance to share with the european council on my way back, were about the european union’s full support for the full and swift implementation of the minsk protocol and memorandum, the need for a credible process of reforms to deliver on public expectations for an improved way of governance, and the eu’s readiness to support and assist this process. a year back, you would probably not have expected that ukraine would now have a new president, a new parliament and a new government. this is to say that we have to give credit for the positive developments that the ukrainians have managed in these difficult months. i will come back, obviously, to the situation in the east of the country, but let me concentrate first – as the ukrainian leadership that i met in december did – on the internal situation of ukraine. we now have a relatively new leadership in place: a new government, parliament and president fully committed not only to a process to resolve the situation in the east but also to the core, necessary reforms in the country. the ukrainian reforms are crucial, first of all, in terms of responding to the high expectations and aspirations of the ukrainian people, who expressed those aspirations very clearly in the last two elections. meeting especially with civil society organisations and ngos and activists in kiev, i found it interesting to listen to how their focus was very much on delivering internal changes. there are systemic issues that need to be addressed, including corruption, constitutional reform and decentralisation. here, apart from the work that the european union can do, there is a lot that the council of europe and the venice commission can do to assist in judicial reform, energy sector reform, electoral reform and reform of the business climate. again, meeting with our 28 member states’ ambassadors to ukraine, i was impressed by the common indication from all 28 ambassadors in kiev that, on the one hand, they supported financial assistance but, on the other, that they recognised the need to create a business environment that enables private investment to continue, or to return to ukraine, in an effective way. the list of reforms is long and obviously very difficult, but ukraine will find – and is already finding – support for these reforms on our side. last week the commission proposed a third macro-financial assistance programme for eur 1.8 billion. this is an additional sign of the eu’s solidarity with ukraine and also part of a bigger international effort based, of course, on conditionality principles. in the light of the very difficult financial situation that ukraine is facing – and i remind you that this programme is not a blank check and will be strictly conditioned – i count on the european parliament’s support to finalise this assistance. however, it is very difficult to reform while facing a conflict on your own territory, and i think that here we have two main responsibilities. the first, as i have said, is to support the internal, difficult, challenging but needed reform process inside ukraine. the second is to work on the dramatic humanitarian impact of the conflict. this is an issue that i know is crucial for some of you, and i think that the international community, starting with the european union, needs to do more. support for those who have left and those who have stayed is crucial. we have been discussing this with the ukrainian authorities because the support has to come not only from the international community but also from the authorities in kiev, and they are willing to give it. the problem of access for humanitarian aid has to be solved. access needs to be ensured. so far, the union has committed eur 32 million in humanitarian and recovery aid, and it will continue helping if our support is increased. but then there is the security situation on the ground and the political process for talks and a solution to the conflict. let me state here again our committed and united position on the conflict, and let me also quote the latvian prime minister, who said, when presenting the priorities for the presidency this morning, that our strength is unity. it has been unity and it has to continue to be unity. i will keep this in mind not only during the debate today but also in relation to the work that we have to carry out in the coming months. our common, agreed and shared position in the european union is precious, and that is the need to work for a solution to the conflict in the east of the vpc/hr. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the members for this debate, which is not only timely but necessary, and for their contributions to the debate. the european union has been following the case of the two italian naval gunners, massimiliano latorre and salvatore girone, in constant contact with the italian government and the indian authorities since the beginning of their detention in india in february 2012. we note with satisfaction today the decision of the indian supreme court to extend the sick leave of massimiliano latorre, which rightly takes into account humanitarian reasons and the serious state of health of the soldier who required serious and urgent medical treatment in italy. we hope that this decision will mark the beginning of a process which will finally lead to a rapid, final, equitable and shared solution in the case of both italian soldiers, massimiliano and salvatore. at the same time, we must regrettably point out that, despite numerous attempts, no progress has been made so far. we therefore understand and share the concerns expressed by many members of the european parliament about a dispute involving two european citizens. this case has been dragging on for three years now, an unacceptable period of time during which the two italian soldiers have been and are still unjustly subjected to measures restricting their personal liberty, in the absence of a charge being laid. this situation of unlawful detention violates fundamental human rights recognised and protected by numerous international conventions. it is worth recalling that the two italian seamen were on board the oil tanker enrica lexie which was crossing international waters to take part in an official mission under international legislation on the fight against piracy and the protection of national shipping. in view of their involvement in the latorre and girona mission, they enjoyed the functional immunity of a state body in the exercise of its functions. this situation implies, in accordance with the principles of general international law, that military personnel on official duty are functionally immune from the exercise of the criminal and international jurisdiction of foreign states. it is no coincidence that the european union has consistently called on india to provide a speedy and positive solution to the dispute, in full compliance with international law and the united nations convention on the law of the sea, unclos, which states that jurisdiction over accidents occurring in international waters lies with the authorities of the flag state of the vessel, in this case italy. presidents van rompuy, barroso and schultz, as well as the high representative vice-president ashton, have raised the issue with their indian counterparts on several occasions in the past, underlining the european union's concerns. i am personally following this case with particular attention in my new role and i intend to use every opportunity to continue to raise it until i finally find a final solution acceptable to all parties. it is important to draw everyone's attention to the fact that cases like this risk having important repercussions on the global fight against piracy, which the european union has been seriously engaged in for some time and should continue to be. the indian navy has often been the target of criminal actions off the coast of somalia and thanks to operation atalanta many hostages have been freed. international cooperation has proved essential to limit the threat of piracy and to respond to attacks. the european union and india therefore share a common interest in protecting freedom of navigation, but the principles of cooperation and mutual trust must be respected. more generally, we share with india strategic values and interests and we wish to cooperate on the world stage, but it is good that everyone is fully aware of how much and how the unresolved dispute over two italian naval officers could impact on the strained relations between the european union and india. the european union wishes to honour its commitment to the full and effective protection of the fundamental rights of its citizens, of every european citizen in detention anywhere in the world, by promoting the peaceful settlement of international disputes and respect for human rights and international law. finally, let me stress that there are not only legal or political considerations involved in this matter. it is also - for some it is first and foremost - a very painful human story for the families of the two indian fishermen who died, to whom we are close, for the two sailors and their families who have been living for three long years in the most complete uncertainty. the situation is becoming more and more intolerable from every point of view, but above all i must say this to the families of the two moro people, to whom i extend my warmest human thoughts, having had the opportunity to be at their side for many months, not only from an institutional point of view but also from a human point of view. we in the european union will therefore continue not only to follow the case closely but also and above all to press everywhere, in close contact with the italian government, for a rapid, positive, shared and definitive solution to the case.

in writing. we express our full support for the activities of the european ombudsman, as he plays a key role in helping the institutions of the european union to become more transparent, effective and closer to the citizens, thus strengthening citizens' trust in the union itself. we consider it a priority to ensure that citizens' rights are fully respected and that the right to good administration reflects the highest standards expected of the union's institutions, bodies or agencies. transparency, openness, access to information, respect for citizens' rights and high ethical standards are essential principles for creating and maintaining trust in the european public service. transparency is a cornerstone of an advanced democracy, insofar as it allows the activities of public authorities to be examined, their performance assessed and they to be held accountable for their actions. we also agree with the opening up of documents and public access to them, but we also reiterate our firm support for the right of citizens to privacy and the protection of their personal data. finally, we wish to reaffirm the importance of the european citizens' initiative, which was introduced by the treaty of lisbon, as a new instrument for the direct participation of citizens in the decision-making process when european legislation is being drawn up.

in writing. this resolution calls on the european union to implement, within a limited timeframe, sanctions aimed at preventing further armed violence and human rights violations in libya. the reference to the need to support concrete actions, such as the freezing of assets to the detriment of the perpetrators of terrorist acts, aimed at weakening their influence within the country, is particularly acceptable. for all these reasons i felt it was my duty to give my consent to this document.
in writing. libya is in a state of chaos today, with two different political authorities (only one of which is democratically legitimized by national elections) and at the mercy of terrorists and other criminal groups. we strongly urge the cessation of all hostilities and the parties involved to commit themselves to promoting a constructive political dialogue at national level. we consider the role played by the un special representative, mr bernadino léon, to be fundamental in promoting dialogue between the various warring factions in the search for a peaceful mediation of the conflict, and we deplore the unjustified postponement of the new round of peace negotiations which had been scheduled for the beginning of january. we cannot ignore the fact that armed violence and the absence of a single political authority, recognised by all parties, represent a serious danger not only to the stability of the whole region but also to the security of europe and all the neighbouring countries. we therefore stress the need for joint diplomatic action by all the member states, which have hitherto acted individually, under the aegis of our high representative for foreign affairs, federica mogherini, who can certainly play a key role in mediating the conflict.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, in view of the european parliament's previous decisions on the situation in libya and the 1949 geneva convention, which requires respect for international humanitarian law in all circumstances, in view of the demonstrations in february 2011 in which libyan citizens demanded respect for and guarantees of their rights and which triggered nine months of internal conflict, in view of the increasing attacks on civilians and human rights violations, which in some cases are defined as real war crimes, and in view of the call for an end to all armed conflict and for dialogue between the two sides, i am voting in favour for these reasons.
in writing. repression, violence, political divisions: in libya, we have been in the middle of a civil war for far too long. first the conflict that led to the fall of gaddafi, now the internal power struggles. i voted for this resolution because it is europe's duty to put an end to this situation, which is a violation of human rights and international humanitarian law. over 400,000 displaced people and 150,000 libyans leaving their country for neighbouring tunisia: the figures from international organizations paint a very worrying picture. libya is now the scene of violent political clashes in a territory where, in fact, two rival parliaments and numerous opposing factions of nationalist, islamic, tribal and regionalist forces operate. the european union, by ensuring support for the tobruk house of representatives as the only legitimate body emerging from the 2014 elections, must play a central role in condemning these actions and imposing targeted sanctions against those responsible for the violence.
in writing. the libyan crisis has become increasingly critical over time due to the severe internal polarization that has degenerated into a full-blown civil war, resulting in the destruction of any semblance of state system and the detonation of a serious humanitarian emergency. i hope very much that the third session of the dialogue, with the mediation of the un, will take place as soon as possible, without further delay and postponement, and that the warring parties will be able to find common ground on the agenda and the main elements of the agenda: the establishment of a government of national unity, a ceasefire and the gradual withdrawal of the militias, and the safeguarding of the constituent assembly's path to the adoption of a fundamental charter by referendum. i also hope that a new super partes prime minister will be appointed to head a government of national unity which can put an end to the chaos and violence of this period. the lack of a stable institutional partner with full control over the african country has led to serious immigration problems in italy and europe, while when an agreement was concluded with the libyan authorities, there was a decrease in migration flows to italian and european coasts.

in writing. the new egyptian constitution states that "freedom, human dignity and social justice are rights recognized to every citizen" and that "dignity is a right recognized to every human being and cannot be violated". since its entry into force, however, very serious events have occurred which are contrary to these principles. the issuance of mass death sentences comes to mind, first in march 2014 of 1 212 people and then in december 2014 of 188 people. we are also alarmed by the fact that three months ago, in october 2014, president al-isi ordered that all "necessary and public services" be placed under military jurisdiction. this means that minors can also be tried by military courts. these judges are answerable to the ministry of defence and not to the ministry of justice. this can only raise concern about the large number of protesters, journalists, activists, trade unionists who are currently being detained without due process. furthermore, a clear separation of powers is desirable in order to ensure a peaceful conduct of the march 2015 elections. for all these reasons i am voting in favour of this resolution.

in writing. i voted with conviction for the european parliament's resolution on the case of the two italian sailors massimiliano latorre and salvatore girone, who, while carrying out anti-piracy activities off the coast of kerala, are accused of killing two indian fishermen. i share the concern expressed in the resolution about the restriction of the freedom of movement of the two gunmen and their detention without charge, both of which are signs of a serious violation of human rights by the indian authorities. i therefore consider it essential to make every effort to ensure that the two men are given a fair trial, while fully respecting the fundamental rights of citizens of the european union detained in a third country. in the light of the facts of the incident, which took place in international waters, i hope that jurisdiction will be given to the italian authorities and/or to an international arbitration. parliament also called on the commission to take all possible steps to ensure that the case was resolved peacefully and quickly, in the interests of the italian and indian families concerned.

in writing. almost three years after their arrest, the two italian naval officers are still in custody in india without knowing what the charges against them are. this delay, which is a clear violation of their fundamental rights, is no longer acceptable. under the international principle of functional immunity, military personnel of a state serving abroad under a provision of national law are subject, for acts committed in the exercise of their functions, exclusively to the jurisdiction of the country of deployment. for this legal reason too, i am convinced that the solution to the matter must necessarily be through a trial before the italian courts or, at the very least, through international arbitration under protocol vii to the montego bay convention. the resolution is a step in this direction, offering new ideas for continuing the difficult negotiations. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. we can 't hide it . the threat of terrorism in europe is serious and the community institutions must respond firmly. however, i believe that, after the events in paris, the term that must accompany eu action should be: "balance" is the word. balance between the need for immediate action and the obligation to think about long-term solutions; we need to balance data collection, the use of intelligence tools and the right to privacy, but above all, we need to balance security and freedom, the two pillars on which our democracy is built. the debate on the directive on the exchange of pnr data should therefore be speeded up, but the protection of personal data should also be guaranteed to european citizens. the control of the movements of foreign fighters should be stepped up, but without limiting european freedoms, starting with the closure of the schengen borders. we cannot accept that the threat of terrorism undermines the european model of society and the values associated with it. finally, it is crucial that the union should have a common security policy, which provides for the full sharing of information between the 28 member states, a key feature if we are to start talking about a true european intelligence.
in writing. the tragic events in paris have shown not only how fragile our democracies are, but also how europe and the member states must equip themselves with more effective intelligence tools in the face of the real threat of islamist terrorism. the solution to combating terrorism is not to close the borders, to suspend schengen, as some populist figures have been saying in recent weeks. on the contrary, the schengen information system, cooperation between police forces and the strengthening of europol and eurojust must be strengthened. it is necessary to establish measures under the control of the judicial authorities to monitor european 'combatants' returning from death training camps; we must be able to block the 'catchy' jihadist sites that are recruiting with alarming ease many, too many young people, not just those from pockets of social discomfort and marginalization. the cultural, educational and social aspects of the programme are therefore essential. the adoption of the passenger name record (pnr) directive for the registration of passengers on flights within the schengen area may also be a necessary measure, but it is imperative to strike the right balance between security and adequate respect for privacy. only a united eu response can be truly effective in fighting terrorism.

in writing. the european investment fund proposed by the juncker commission risks being yet another failed, haphazard project that is totally inadequate to stimulate the growth and jobs that europe needs. the proposed mechanism is based on the multiplier effect that the initial financing of some eur 16 billion would produce through private investment, with a view to reaching eur 315 billion. i would point out two points which show the inconsistency of the efsi mechanism. the first concerns the great difficulty faced by private individuals who, in conditions of low confidence and difficult markets, will have little incentive to invest. the second concerns the type of projects to be carried out, which, if not carefully examined and selected on the basis of strategic objectives, positive employment and environmental effects and maximum transparency, will turn out to be the next major infrastructure projects that feed organized crime and the interests of large groups and multinationals. finally, it is with grave concern that part of the planned funding is being reallocated from existing resources to the horizon 2020 research programme.

can influence their behaviour. this is all the more so when it is considered that at member state level it is estimated that between 30 and 50% of the total volume of slaughtered meat is processed into meat for use as an ingredient in food products, mainly minced meat, meat preparations and meat products. commissioner, today we must win back the confidence of european consumers who, also in the wake of the recent food scandals, including the fraudulent substitution of beef for horse meat, want stricter rules on traceability and information. the commission has already proposed a number of amendments to the proposal, including a proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of fraudulent use of foodstuffs. the resolution does not forget the role of small and mediumsized enterprises, which are central to our economy in terms of creating growth, employment and development, and the commitment to quality and safe food. i therefore believe that a balanced approach between the different positions and interests involved is the way forward in preparing the new legislation on this subject, which will have to take account of the transparency and readability of information for consumers, while at the same time allowing european companies to operate in a cost-effective and competitive manner, at conditions acceptable to the purchasing power of consumers. on one specific point we would like to ask the commission for more information, namely on the assessment of the possible effects of this measure on prices. the results of a survey carried out by a french consumer association differ considerably from the figures in the european commission's report on the costs of introducing the indication of the country of origin on the label. i therefore ask the commissioner to look at this matter in more detail in order to get a more general picture. however, this assessment should not prolong the time for the submission of the legislative proposal. when the commission publishes its proposal, we will of course react on the substance, together with the council, on the basis of our prerogatives as co-legislators, but we are ready to make our contribution now by working on this motion for a resolution containing our suggestions and our list of priorities. clear, consistent and harmonised rules are needed. we have a lot to do in the coming years and this is a sensitive area for our citizens. we therefore offer a concrete and specific contribution to the european commission today and with the vote on wednesday, asking it to submit legislative proposals to make the indication of the origin of meat in processed foods compulsory. we believe that the information on origin, which is currently provided on a voluntary basis, could mislead consumers and that mandatory information could ensure greater transparency along the food chain and better inform european consumers. finally, we ask that impact assessments be taken into account at the same time, avoiding excessive costs and administrative burdens for businesses. as i said at the outset, our aim must be to regain the confidence of european consumers by reassuring them of the quality and safety of food produced in our territory and by offering them the information they need to make an informed purchase.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, our movement has always defended consumers and their right to know where the meat they eat comes from. mrs willmott has explained this very well before, for environmental reasons for example. at present, there is no european obligation to indicate the origin of meat in processed products. this obligation exists only for meat when sold individually. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. this is absurd. this is why many producers indicate the country of origin of only one of the ingredients in the final product - of course the country which is more commercially convenient for them - or they freely choose to indicate only the country of final processing of the food, and still benefit from the marketing advantage that this gives. this kind of labelling is of course of no use, it only serves to create unfair competition between companies. in this way a product can be sold as if it were italian, spanish, greek or english, etc., even though the meat in it comes from a completely different country. commissioner, you spoke earlier of voluntary labelling as a possibility. for this reason, in the resolution we asked the commission to set clear rules for producers who decide to use voluntary labelling, but above all we asked for clear rules for those who decide not to use labelling. in our view, the traceability of a product is an added value to the product and if a company decides not to label at that point, it will not have to refer in any way to the origin of any of the ingredients of its product because otherwise consumers will be misled. this is the only position which allows the freedom of choice of firms to be safeguarded and at the same time to protect consumers from fraud. that is why, pending the mandatory labelling we want, we have asked for our position to be adopted by means of an implementing act so that we can adopt these measures much more quickly than directives or regulations. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, transparency and the indication of the origin of products are two essential elements of european policies. the best conditions for transparency promote the consumption of safe, high-quality products, linked to the territory and the typical excellence of the different european regions, and meet the needs of consumers who, as we have seen, want to know what they are eating and want to know what they are buying. the requirement of a compulsory indication of the origin of meat used as an ingredient in processed products is therefore exactly in this direction. so while it is right to promote the basic principle of compulsory indication of origin, i believe that at the same time we cannot ignore the fact that the mechanisms for ensuring this greater transparency could also, as someone else has already suggested, come at a cost to businesses and therefore to consumers. i listened very carefully to what commissioner katainen said about the cost-benefit ratio that labelling measures can have. we expect a serious and detailed assessment of these aspects, namely of the possible additional costs and the related operational problems, in the documentation which the commission should have already submitted. i also think that where excessive administrative burdens are found to be imposed on food business operators and law enforcement authorities, it would be appropriate not to say that nothing is being done, but rather to provide for a whole series of solutions and simplifications on a case-by-case basis in order to combine transparency and prices, which are undoubtedly high at the moment. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament is faced today with the important responsibility of having to adopt the new directive on the cross-border exchange of information on road safety offences before 6 may 2015, in order to avoid creating a legal limbo that could undermine road safety in europe. the directive has already shown its potential. since its entry into force in november 2013, the number of offences committed by foreign drivers, now aware that any offence committed abroad can be notified to them thanks to this new mechanism, has in fact decreased. however, legal certainty is needed and is therefore crucial, especially when we consider that, although the european union is on track to achieve the target of reducing road deaths by 50% by 2020, the economic crisis has led to an increase in the number of road accident victims due to the ageing of the car fleet and radical cuts in infrastructure maintenance costs. the introduction of binding and non-discriminatory measures against impunity on european roads must therefore be a priority for this parliament, including by urging the european commission and the member states to cooperate by strengthening the exchange of information and drawing up joint reports on road safety.

there's the outer dimension. i would not like the very rightful attention paid to ukraine to obscure the urgency of european action in the world. we can't outsource foreign policy to fighter and drone happening before our eyes because triton is a european mission, but we must strengthen this mission with men, means and instruments. answer to a blue-card question. we have been saying for months that the troika is an inadequate and undemocratic instrument and we are pleased that this same consideration was made by president juncker in his declaration of the birth of the european commission. the troika is not the right therapy. interlocutory work must take place between the national authorities and the european democratic institutions.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, tomorrow's summit has three different and distant topics on its agenda, but they are all very important for the european union's ability to react and to propose. the ukrainian question, the fight against terrorism and the crisis of economic and monetary union challenge us and involve us far beyond the respective technical plans. they question our determination to give substance to the founding values of the european union and our ability to put forward credible solutions. as far as monetary union is concerned, how can we deny that the greek question is increasingly a true measure of the meaning of this union? i believe that not only greece but also the many difficulties faced by other states as a result of the austerity policies imposed in the name of genuine economic and monetary union are showing that europe is unable to solve the problem of economic governance in the terms in which it is set. the solution will not come from technical reasoning or financial engineering. the solution can only be found by giving economic value to our common desire to achieve the process of european unification in the face of real difficulties. in other words, by establishing, justifying and spreading a vision of europe which will make it possible to have a clear view of what is valuable and what is not, what makes sense and what does not, and which will be able to put the dignity of the person back at the centre of every decision. the fight against terrorism is a challenge we cannot escape, one that must be met in a comprehensive way, not just in the field of internal security. we must respond with a broad, deep and not hasty strategy. today our fundamental values are subordinated to the economic dimension, in the belief that their role is secondary or even exhausted. the failure to counter inhuman and irrational ideologies has crept into this vacuum, which cannot be fought by perfect financial budgets, but only by proposals for shared values which are applied in practice, first and foremost by the european institutions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that we are facing many challenges today, as has been mentioned by many of our colleagues, but this is a time when we must not simply respond to the needs of the political moment, however delicate it may be. this is a collective challenge that we must take up and win. as my colleague alain lamassoure has said very well, do we want a european pmr or do we want 28 national pmrs? and so is everything. these challenges call on us to be europe, europe proudly europe, with our values, as the council has also said. we must put forward a positive narrative, i agree with what the council has said. then we're gonna be careful because we're looking at a very dangerous escalation. we have moved on from the cold war - and i am referring to the ukraine - which we thought we had forgotten, and in a few weeks we are fearful of the danger of armed conflict. i believe that europe, between nobel prize winner barack obama and putin, must not only seek but must find a way to peace. this is what our fellow citizens ask of us, this is our destiny if we want to be europe. and then there's the terrorism. we have to get out of the box. even with regard to immigration, the dead were mentioned first - and i am sorry that mr pittella is no longer here - but this is false goodwill, because when there was the expensive mission to pick up immigrants, we had 3,538 dead, we were always wrong. we have to get out of our preconceptions. we have to face things head on, listen to each other, recognize the real problem we're facing. and finally, greece. you said it right, the greek people deserve attention. i would say more than that, i would say that greece is the cradle of our civilization, there is no europe without greece and i am convinced that by finding a solution you will also be able to bring the solidarity of the whole parliament to the whole greek people.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, an agreement on greece is necessary and possible, and it would be good if everyone, instead of blowing on fire and playing at ideology, showed pragmatism and responsibility. on the one hand, it is clear that debts must be paid and aid cannot be unconditional, but to ask for a primary surplus of 4.5% in a country with 26% unemployment is economically unreasonable and puts the sustainability of the debt at risk and should therefore be a matter of concern to creditors first and foremost. it is possible to agree on an extension of the maturities, more rational conditionalities and a more democratic mechanism for their verification, although this will take time. in the meantime, the gap between a bridge loan and a technical extension of the programme with some revised conditions does not appear to be insurmountable and we ask the commission to help governments fill it by freeing them from their internal political conditioning. in fact, another lesson from this is that a more advanced balance between national democracy and european democracy is needed and this will also have to be one of the main lines of the new revival of the process of deepening economic and monetary union.
i'm asking for a blue card. the vow must always be respected, this is a fundamental condition. i hope that, in the face of so much austerity being imposed on greece, the commission will be aware of the poverty of the member states because, as it has been a problem for greece, it can also be a problem for other emerging countries, such as italy. so i hope that the commission and the commissioners are very well aware of the conditions of the greek people.
