in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common rules for exports. indeed, the interests of the eu may require the adoption of appropriate measures to prevent, remedy or fulfil international commitments entered into by the eu or its member states, especially as regards trade in commodities, in the event of a crisis situation due to a shortage of essential products. since the proposed regulation does not prevent eu countries from adopting or applying quantitative restrictions on exports, provided that they are justified on specific grounds, and since the proposal for the regulation itself was approved by the consultative working party of the legal services of the european parliament, the council and the commission, in that it merely codifies existing texts without any substantial changes, i considered that i would agree with the position of the consultative working party.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on common rules for exports. these reports concern proposals for the codification of eu law. it is a technical procedure provided for in article 103 of the regulation, which is intended to verify that the proposal for codification is in fact merely a codification without any substantial changes.
in writing. regulation (ec) no 1061/2009 deals with the common export regime. i will not support the regulation because the commercial aspects proposed and adopted are in opposition to the policies of the european commission.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of this report, which aims to start the codification of council regulation (ec) no 1061/2009 of 19 october 2009 establishing a common system of export refunds. the regulation introduces the principle that exports to third countries are not subject to any quantitative restrictions, subject to the derogations provided for in this regulation and to the measures which member states may adopt in accordance with the treaty. as i have already said in other votes on the agenda, i believe it is essential to simplify the legislation and to codify the provisions which have been frequently amended in order to operate with clear and transparent legislation.
in writing. the purpose of this proposal is to initiate the codification of council regulation (ec) no 1061/2009 of 19 october 2009 establishing a common system of export refunds. the regulation introduces the principle that exports to third countries must not be subject to any quantitative restrictions, save for exceptions. since the rapporteur's proposal is merely a codification of existing texts without any substantial changes to them, i thought it appropriate to support it by voting in favour.

in writing. the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction provides for cooperation between signatory states to return a child or young person under 16 who has been arbitrarily 'abducted' from a parent to the family residence pending a court ruling, unless such return would constitute a serious danger to the child's safety. i believe it is of fundamental importance for the protection of our children that this convention is ratified and respected by more and more states. i therefore intend to vote in favour of gabon's accession to the union as one of the new signatory countries.
in writing. — i voted yes because it is fundamental to have gabon’s adhesion to this convention in order to protect children in africa.
in writing. i voted in favour. the hague convention is a positive one and the protection of minors must be extended as far as possible to other states which wish to become parties to it.
in writing. some states exploit the lack of cooperation between national authorities to obtain custody of children when there is a pending case between two spouses from different nations. accession to the hague convention establishes the competent court in the state where the child is resident, limiting the possibility of disputes over jurisdiction and thus bringing about a more rapid procedure. that is why we are voting in favour.
in writing. the hague convention is a key instrument for ensuring the return of children who have been unlawfully removed or retained abroad by a parent and for ensuring that custody and visitation rights are respected in all states. my country, italy, was the only one to support, even before the court intervened, the exclusive competence of the union in this area, requiring full regulatory and operational coordination between states, instead of approaches aimed at protecting the parent, its own citizen, even at the expense of the child's interest and the rights of citizens of other countries. i believe that for the convention to be properly applied, the states will have to meet certain requirements: efficient central authorities which can really serve as a reference for administrative cooperation; rules which prevent discriminatory practices; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's acquis in this area. in view of this, i welcome gabon's accession and have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a major instrument which has been ratified by all the member states of the european union. it effectively enables the contracting states to cooperate in solving cases of international child abduction. the problem is manifest in separating couples where the spouses are of different nationalities, because there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between states. in the various states there are legal systems which tend to favour certain categories of persons on the basis of nationality, leaving the right of surety to be interpreted in a dubious way. to resolve such situations at the international level, the convention puts the child at the centre of the problem by stipulating that the court of jurisdiction is the court where the child resides. in view of all this, gabon's accession to the convention is to be welcomed, also in view of the favourable opinion of the rapporteur who fully supports the measure. the eu will thus protect minors with links to the gabonese community against abduction. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of gabon's accession to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 because it is an instrument of enormous importance, already ratified by all the member states of the european union. since the convention introduces a system allowing contracting states to cooperate in resolving cases of international child abduction, gabon's accession to the convention is to be welcomed as many citizens of the european union are from gabon. the children with links to the gabonese community will thus be protected against abduction.
in writing. i voted in favour of the council decision on the declaration by the member states of acceptance of gabon's accession to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. in an international context where the mobility of families across national borders is increasing, the phenomenon of child abduction is particularly important in the event of a crisis between couples. protecting children from wrongful removal or non-return is a global issue as well as a core element of the eu programme. article 24 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union states that children have the right to protection and that their interests "shall be considered as paramount". i therefore support the accession of the gabonese republic, since only through international cooperation is it possible to resolve the issues relating to the custody of minors and to ensure the immediate return of the abducted child. children with links to the gabonese community can thus be better protected from any danger of abduction.
in writing. under the convention, the vote is to decide whether to accept the accession of the member states, in the interest of the european union, to gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction has so far been ratified by 86 countries, including all eu member states. the objective of the convention is to restore the status quo through the immediate return of illegally transferred or detained children through a system of cooperation between the authorities designated by the contracting parties. the vote in favour is an obligation to guarantee the rights of all minors.
in writing. i voted in favour of gabon's accession to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction because this will give children with links to the gabonese community greater protection against this phenomenon. the convention allows for cooperation between the contracting states in order to find a solution to cases of international child abduction. this problem arises when spouses from different states, following their separation, take advantage of the lack of cooperation between the states concerned to obtain custody of their children. the aim of this convention is to settle such situations at international level by providing that the competent court and the applicable law shall be those of the state of residence of the child.
in writing. i welcome this proposal from the council to accept gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention. the issue of the protection of the rights of children is of central importance and it seems therefore very positive that an increasing number of states are included, especially considering that there are a great many people on european soil from countries which are now asking for accession, which will facilitate the resolution of cases of abduction between a member state and these third countries. however, while it is good that all the states of the european union have acceded to the convention, i cannot help but notice that the concept of the 'best interests of the child' is often interpreted in an instrumental way. i refer, for example, to the case of germany, whose jugendamt, the office for children, in effect exchanges the welfare of the child for the welfare of the german child, depriving the non-german parent and the child himself of a number of fundamental rights, including some of those which form the basis of the hague convention. unfortunately, the problem is not confined to germany alone, and europe is powerless to see these abuses, since it has no power to intervene in the family law of individual member states. i therefore believe that harmonization of legislation in this area is urgent.
in writing. i am pleased that gabon is acceding to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction and that is why i voted in favour of the report. the convention provides effective means for resolving disputes arising from international child abduction following separation or divorce, by providing that the competent court and the applicable law shall be that of the state of residence of the child.
in writing. i welcome the accession of gabon to the hague convention.
in writing. - i declare my vote in favour and my full support for gabon's accession to the hague convention of 25 october 1980, so that children with links to the gabonese community can also benefit from eu protection measures in the event of separation or dispute between their parents. the convention is in fact a very effective instrument for safeguarding children, since it brings the rights of children applicable in their country of residence to the centre of the conflicts of couples in crisis of different nationalities, overcoming the temptation to give preferential treatment to the parents' countries of origin and the dramatic risk of international child abduction. europe, the guardian of human rights, should extend the range of measures to protect children in all countries that so request, thus preventing unfair national legal favouritism and the misguided parental management of the fragility of children.
in writing. i voted in favour of gabon's accession, as well as that of other countries, to the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction in order to widen as much as possible cooperation between states and to guarantee maximum protection for children who are victims of conflicts between parents. too often the trauma of separation is compounded by the trauma of being taken away and alienated from one of the parents.

in writing. we believe that the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important instrument, ratified by all eu member states, as it introduces a system which allows contracting states to cooperate in solving cases of international child abduction. the aim is to avoid uncertainties or dangerous legal gaps. the competent court and the applicable law are those of the state in which the child is resident. however, while the european union has exclusive external competence in this area (as confirmed by the court of justice in opinion 1/13), i.e. individual member states no longer have the possibility of acting individually by reference to their own legal systems, the problem remains that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. to overcome this legal difficulty, the council decided that it would be for each member state to accept, each in respect of its own territory, the accession of new states to the convention. we therefore welcome albania's accession to the above convention, so as to ensure that children with links to the gabonese community can find protection against abduction at eu level.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important instrument. the convention establishes a system that allows contracting states to cooperate in resolving cases of international child abduction. in cases where spouses are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between the states concerned in order to obtain custody of the children, and there is often a tendency in the legal systems of individual states to favour one another on the basis of nationality. the aim of the convention is to address these situations at international level, and many citizens of the european union are of gabonese origin and minors with links to the gabonese community will thus find protection against abduction. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. the 1980 hague convention is a very important instrument because it allows the contracting states to cooperate in order to find a solution in cases of international child abduction. the european union has exclusive external competence in this area, which means that the member states cannot act on their own. however, the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations and for this reason the member states of the union must accept, each for its own territory, that third countries, in this case gabon, accede to the convention, so that the convention can be fully applied in cases between the eu and a third country. i therefore welcome the fact that gabon is joining the convention because, thanks to this accession, the children of the gabonese people will be able to find greater protection against the abductions of which they may be victims.

in writing. i welcome this proposal from the council to accept the accession of the seychelles to the 1980 hague convention. the issue of the protection of the rights of children is of central importance and it seems therefore very positive that an increasing number of states are being included, especially considering that there are a great many people on european soil from countries which are now asking for membership, which will facilitate the resolution of cases of abduction between a member state and these third countries. however, while it is good that all the states of the european union have acceded to the convention, i cannot help but notice that the concept of the 'best interests of the child' is often interpreted in an instrumental way. i refer, for example, to the case of germany, whose jugendamt, the office for children, in effect exchanges the welfare of the child for the welfare of the german child, depriving the non-german parent and the child himself of a number of fundamental rights, including some of those which form the basis of the hague convention. the problem is not, unfortunately, confined to germany alone, and europe is helplessly watching these abuses as it has no power to intervene in the family law of individual member states. i therefore believe that harmonization of legislation in this area is urgent.
in writing. i am pleased that seychelles is a party to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction and that is why i voted in favour of the report. the convention provides effective means for resolving disputes arising from international child abduction following separation or divorce, by providing that the competent court and the applicable law shall be that of the state of residence of the child.
in writing. i welcome the accession of the seychelles to the hague convention.
in writing. - i declare my vote in favour and my full support for the accession of the seychelles to the hague convention of 25 october 1980, so that children with links to the seychelles community may also benefit from the eu's protection measures in the event of separation or dispute between their parents. the convention is in fact a very effective instrument for safeguarding children, since it brings the rights of children applicable in their country of residence back to the centre of the conflicts of couples in crisis of different nationalities, overcoming the temptation to give preferential treatment to the parents' countries of origin and the dramatic risk of international child abduction. europe, the guardian of human rights, should extend the range of measures to protect children in all countries that so request, thus preventing unfair national legal favouritism and the misguided parental management of the fragility of children.
in writing. international child abductions following separation or divorce are unfortunately a regular occurrence. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a major instrument, ratified by all the member states of the european union. international cooperation is essential to resolve these disputes, and i therefore fully support this resolution. the accession of seychelles to the convention and consequently the effective entry into force of the convention in cases concerning the european union and this country is to be welcomed. it is our moral and political duty to ensure that the children concerned are protected at eu level.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of mrs hautala's report because it will ensure adequate protection against international abductions of children with links to the seychelles community. as i have said in the other reports adopted today, the hague convention of 25 october 1980 is a very important instrument for the protection of the rights of children and i am therefore in favour of the accession of a new state.
in writing. in favour of the report on the accession of the seychelles to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the convention is intended to provide that the competent court and the applicable law shall be those of the state in which the child is resident.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 provides the legal basis for the contracting states to resolve issues relating to international child abduction. i welcome the accession of seychelles to the convention, as i believe it will help to ensure adequate protection for minors with links to that community in the event of abduction.
in writing. we believe that the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important instrument, ratified by all eu member states, as it introduces a system which allows contracting states to cooperate in solving cases of international child abduction. the aim is to avoid uncertainties or dangerous legal gaps. the competent court and the applicable law are those of the state in which the child is resident. however, while the european union has exclusive external competence in this area (as confirmed by the court of justice in opinion 1/13), i.e. individual member states no longer have the possibility of acting individually by referring to their own legal systems, the problem remains that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. to overcome this legal difficulty, the council decided that it would be for each member state to accept, each in respect of its own territory, the accession of new states to the convention. we therefore welcome the accession of albania to the above convention, so as to ensure that children from the seychelles can find protection against abduction at eu level.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important instrument. the convention establishes a system that allows contracting states to cooperate in resolving cases of international child abduction. where spouses are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between the states concerned in order to obtain custody of the children, and there is often a tendency in the legal systems of individual states to favour one another on the basis of nationality. the convention is intended to address these situations at international level and the many citizens of the european union who are originally from seychelles and minors with links to the community of persons from seychelles will thus find protection against abduction. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. i am naturally in favour of seychelles joining the hague convention and approving the proposal, so that minors in this country can enjoy protection at european level.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the accession of the seychelles to the 1980 hague convention because i am convinced that international cooperation on international child abduction is one of the actions we have a duty to take for the benefit of the youngest, who in the not too distant future will be the basis of our society.
in writing. - i voted in favour because i believe it is essential to promote the protection of the rights of children.
in writing. the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction provides for cooperation between signatory states to return a child or young person under 16 who has been arbitrarily 'abducted' from a parent to the family residence pending a court ruling, unless such return would constitute a serious danger to the child's safety. i believe it is of fundamental importance for the protection of our children that this convention be ratified and respected by more and more states. i therefore intend to vote in favour of the accession of the russian federation to the convention.
in writing. — i voted yes because it is fundamental to have russia’s adhesion to this convention, in order to protect children in russia.
in writing. i voted in favour. the hague convention is a positive one and the protection of minors must be extended as far as possible to other states which wish to become parties to it.
in writing. i voted today in favour of the report on the draft council decision on the declaration by the member states, in the interest of the european union, of acceptance of the accession of the russian federation to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. the convention, to which more than 90 countries have already acceded, including all eu countries, provides for the immediate return of a child if he or she is unlawfully removed from his or her habitual residence without the consent of the other parent, in violation of the right of custody. the european parliament has voted today to ask the eu member states to formally recognise the accession of the russian federation to the convention. i hope that the gradual increase in accessions to the convention will help to resolve cases of child abduction more efficiently, including through improved international coordination on the civilian aspects of international child abduction.
in writing. some states exploit the lack of cooperation between national authorities to obtain custody of children when there is a pending case between two spouses from different nations. accession to the hague convention establishes the competent court in the state where the child is resident, limiting the possibility of disputes over jurisdiction and thus bringing about a more rapid procedure. that is why we are voting in favour.
in writing. the hague convention is a key instrument for ensuring the return of children who have been unlawfully removed or retained abroad by a parent and for ensuring that custody and visitation rights are respected in all states. my country, italy, was the only one to support, even before the court intervened, the exclusive competence of the union in this area, requiring full regulatory and operational coordination between states, instead of approaches aimed at protecting the parent, its own citizen, even at the expense of the child's interest and the rights of citizens of other countries. i believe that for the convention to be properly applied, the states will have to meet certain requirements: efficient central authorities which can really serve as a reference for administrative cooperation; rules which prevent discriminatory practices; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's acquis in this area. in view of this, i welcome the accession of the russian federation and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a major instrument which has been ratified by all the member states of the european union. it effectively enables the contracting states to cooperate in solving cases of international child abduction. the problem is manifest in separating couples where the spouses are of different nationalities, because there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between states. in the various states there are legal systems which tend to favour certain categories of persons on the basis of nationality, leaving the right of surety to be interpreted in a dubious way. to resolve such situations at the international level, the convention puts the child at the centre of the problem by stipulating that the court of jurisdiction is the court where the child resides. in view of all this, the accession of the russian federation to the convention is to be welcomed, also in view of the favourable opinion of the rapporteur who fully supports the measure. the eu will thus protect minors with links to the russian federation community against abduction. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of the accession of the russian federation to the important hague convention of 25 october 1980. this is an important and sensitive issue and i agree with the establishment of a permanent system of cooperation between the contracting states on the security of child custody. i welcome the accession of the russian federation to the convention, as the eu has close economic ties with this country. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to grant the right to vote to minors who are not citizens of the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of the council decision on the declaration by the member states of acceptance of the accession of the russian federation to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. in an international context where the mobility of families across national borders is increasing, the phenomenon of child abduction is particularly important in the event of a crisis between couples. protecting children from wrongful removal or non-return is a global issue as well as a core element of the eu programme. article 24 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union states that children have the right to protection and that their interests 'shall be considered as paramount'. i therefore support russia's accession, because only through international cooperation can the issues of child custody be resolved and the child abducted be returned immediately. children with ties to the russian community can thus be better protected from any danger of abduction.

in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a major instrument which has been ratified by all the member states of the european union. it effectively enables the contracting states to cooperate in solving cases of international child abduction. the problem is manifest in separating couples where the spouses are of different nationalities, because there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between states. in the various states there are legal systems which tend to favour certain categories of persons on the basis of nationality, leaving the right of surety to be interpreted in a dubious way. to resolve such situations at the international level, the convention puts the child at the centre of the problem by stipulating that the court of jurisdiction is the court where the child resides. in view of all this, the accession of the state of singapore to the convention is to be welcomed, also in view of the favourable opinion of the rapporteur who fully supports the measure. the eu will also provide protection against abduction for children with links to the singaporean community. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of singapore's accession to the hague convention of 25 october 1980. the reason for this is easily understood by the importance and the sensitivity of the subject under discussion, namely the protection of children against international kidnapping. i voted in favour of the convention all the more so because it introduces a system which ensures the immediate return of the child who has been abducted. my vote is consistent with the principle that the more states that join, the greater the effectiveness of the convention itself.
in writing. i voted in favour of the council decision on the declaration by the member states of acceptance of the accession of singapore to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction. in an international context where the mobility of families across national borders is increasing, the phenomenon of child abduction is particularly important in the event of a crisis between couples. protecting children from wrongful removal or non-return is a global issue as well as a core element of the eu programme. article 24 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union states that children have the right to protection and that their interests 'shall be considered as paramount'. i therefore support the accession of the republic of singapore, because only through international cooperation can the issues of child custody be resolved and the child abducted be returned immediately. children with ties to the singaporean community can thus be better protected from the dangers of abduction.
in writing. children's interests often take a backseat when parents are at odds with each other or disagree about where and with whom their children should be raised. in such cases we must set clear guidelines and stress the force of the law. the report on the draft council decision on the declaration by the member states, in the interest of the european union, of acceptance of the accession of singapore to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is an act to be voted in favour of for the protection of children.
in writing. i voted in favour of singapore joining the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction because this will give children with links to the singaporean community greater protection against this phenomenon. the convention allows for cooperation between the contracting states in order to find a solution to cases of international child abduction. this problem arises when spouses from different states, following their separation, take advantage of the lack of cooperation between the states concerned to obtain custody of their children. the aim of this convention is to settle such situations at international level by providing that the competent court and the applicable law shall be those of the state of residence of the child.
in writing. i welcome this proposal from the council to accept singapore's accession to the 1980 hague convention. the issue of the protection of the rights of children is of central importance and it seems therefore very positive that an increasing number of states are included, especially considering that there are a great many people on european soil from countries which are now asking for accession, which will facilitate the resolution of cases of abduction between a member state and these third countries. however, while it is good that all the states of the european union have acceded to the convention, i cannot help but notice that the concept of the 'best interests of the child' is often interpreted in an instrumental way. i refer, for example, to the case of germany, whose jugendamt, the office for children, in effect exchanges the welfare of the child for the welfare of the german child, depriving the non-german parent and the child himself of a number of fundamental rights, including some of those which form the basis of the hague convention. the problem is not, unfortunately, confined to germany alone, and europe is helplessly watching these abuses as it has no power to intervene in the family law of individual member states. i therefore believe that harmonization of legislation in this area is urgent.
in writing. i am pleased that singapore is a party to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction and that is why i voted in favour of the report. the convention provides effective means for resolving disputes arising from international child abduction following separation or divorce, by providing that the competent court and the applicable law shall be that of the state of residence of the child.
in writing. i welcome the accession of singapore to the hague convention.
in writing. - i declare my vote in favour and my full support for singapore's accession to the hague convention of 25 october 1980, so that children with links to the singaporean community can also benefit from eu protection measures in the event of separation or dispute between their parents. the convention is in fact a very effective instrument for safeguarding children, since it brings the rights of children applicable in their country of residence to the centre of the conflicts of couples in crisis of different nationalities, overcoming the temptation to give preferential treatment to the parents' countries of origin and the dramatic risk of international child abduction. europe, the guardian of human rights, should extend the range of measures to protect children in all countries that so request, thus preventing unfair national legal favouritism and the misguided parental management of the fragility of children.

in writing. international child abductions following separation or divorce are unfortunately a regular occurrence. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a major instrument, ratified by all the member states of the european union. international cooperation is essential for the settlement of these disputes. that is why i support this resolution in its entirety. the accession of singapore to the convention and consequently the effective entry into force of the convention in cases concerning the european union and singapore is to be welcomed. it is our moral and political duty to ensure that the children concerned are protected at eu level.

in writing. the convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, signed at the hague on 25 october 1980, introduced a system allowing contracting states to cooperate with a view to finding sustainable solutions to international child abduction. in view of the close economic ties between the eu and singapore, i have decided to support singapore's accession to the convention. it will give greater protection to minors with links to the community in this country.
in writing. we believe that the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important instrument, ratified by all eu member states, as it introduces a system which allows contracting states to cooperate in solving cases of international child abduction. the aim is to avoid uncertainties or dangerous legal gaps. the competent court and the applicable law are those of the state in which the child is resident. however, while the european union has exclusive external competence in this area (as confirmed by the court of justice in opinion 1/13), i.e. individual member states no longer have the possibility of acting individually by referring to their own legal systems, the problem remains that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. to overcome this legal difficulty, the council decided that it would be for each member state to accept, each in respect of its own territory, the accession of new states to the convention. we therefore welcome singapore's accession to the abovementioned convention, so as to ensure that children with links to the singaporean community can find protection against abduction at eu level.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a very important instrument. the convention establishes a system that allows contracting states to cooperate in resolving cases of international child abduction. where spouses are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between the states concerned in order to obtain custody of the children, and there is often a tendency in the legal systems of individual states to favour one another on the basis of nationality. the convention is intended to address such situations at the international level and the many eu citizens who are originally from singapore and the minors with links to the singaporean community will thus find protection against abduction. for these reasons, i voted in favour.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive to facilitate the crossborder exchange of information on road safety offences. with this vote, the european parliament had the responsibility to adopt the new directive in order to avoid creating a legal limbo on the subject with negative consequences for the road safety of european citizens following the judgment of the general court of the eu on 6 may 2014. the court of justice had declared the directive void because it had been adopted on an incorrect legal basis (system of exchange of information between the competent authorities of the member states), but had extended its effects for 12 months to allow the legislator to correct its shortcomings and adopt a new text in accordance with the legal basis on transport safety. i am pleased that parliament was able to adopt the new version of the directive quickly, as it had already shown its potential: since its entry into force in november 2013, the number of offences committed by foreign drivers, aware that any offence committed abroad would be notified to them thanks to this new mechanism, has in fact decreased.
in writing. we vote in favour of this directive. the exchange of information in the field of road safety is a key step in the process of european integration and in reducing the number of victims of accidents.
in writing. the measure in question contains the same text as directive 2011/82/eu to facilitate the cross-border exchange of information on road safety offences, which was approved by a very large majority in 2011 by parliament, with two amendments. the amendments are in line with the judgment of the general court of the eu of 6 may 2014, which held that directive 2011/82/eu was adopted on the wrong legal basis concerning police cooperation in criminal matters (article 87 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union). it also stated that the legal basis was that relating to transport safety. although the court of first instance declared the directive void, it recognised its relevance and ruled that, in order to avoid a legislative vacuum, the effects of the repealed directive would be maintained for 12 months and that in the meantime the legislator would adopt a new text in accordance with transport safety. the commission, although it had brought an action for annulment of the wrongful measure, submitted the new text to parliament, which was drafted quickly and provided for the amendment only of the aspects concerning the legal basis and the territorial scope of application. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. - in recent decades we have seen a surge in the production of legislation, both international and national, on terrorism. as a european parliament, we have a duty to participate in this process of nomopoetics, which is necessary for a number of reasons. first of all, there is an escalation of the threat: terrorist action can now be linked to any possible objective, ideology and fundamentalism. it may be indifferently bound to a territory or a nation and constitute the armed wing of national liberation movements, or it may have the characteristics of a transnational terrorist network. the power of terrorist acts, then, has increased due to a number of conditions, not least the willingness of terrorists to commit suicide and technological progress. the states have lost their "monopoly on the threat": the challenge comes from individuals and networks operating at sub-state level and using materials and resources that are beyond national monopoly control. it has therefore become difficult to identify which state has the right to take action against terrorists. the criteria for establishing a link between the exercise of jurisdiction have become elusive, and tend to be reduced to one: the nationality of the victims. for these reasons, together with a pressing security question, we have proposed this joint resolution on counter-terrorism measures with other colleagues.

in writing. - the internet is a multifaceted, multifunctional tool with many facets which are difficult to reduce to unity. the positive effects of the internet on the dissemination of information, the circulation of good practice and, last but not least, the promotion of the process of democratic participation from below, are now indisputable. at the same time, there are concerns about the use of the network by criminal or terrorist organisations, as well as fraudulent or criminal use against the most vulnerable and defenceless, such as minors and the elderly. in this context, the question of human rights is also of particular importance: the internet is now a right that must be guaranteed to every person. the latter is closely linked to freedom of expression, which is often threatened by restrictions on access to the internet or the sharing of information content imposed in some countries, including european countries. for these and other reasons, which are reflected in the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the internet global forum, i believe that this initiative launched by the united nations in 2006 to promote a joint and multilateral political dialogue on internet governance should be welcomed.

in writing. the renewal of the internet governance forum, which was set up by the un conference on the world summit on the information society (wsis) to discuss internet governance issues and, where appropriate, make recommendations to the international community, is an opportunity for the european parliament to underline the importance of the internet as a pillar of the digital single market. there is therefore a need to improve internet access worldwide, as the internet, among other things, promotes innovation, growth, trade, democracy, cultural diversity and human rights. it is equally important to ensure that the forum remains as inclusive as possible, ensuring the constant democratic oversight of the european parliament through its delegations at future forum meetings, so that it contributes effectively to the formulation of a coherent and comprehensive european approach. the collective effort must simultaneously focus on developing legal protection of net neutrality as an essential prerequisite for safeguarding freedom of information and expression, promoting growth and employment, not forgetting the economic and social importance of the rights to privacy and control over one's personal data and the development of appropriate measures to protect minor internet users.
in writing. we appreciate the work of the internet governance forum, which has helped to establish an increasingly democratic, transparent and multi-stakeholder political dialogue. the delegations sent by the european parliament certainly played a key role in promoting european values and in interaction with civil society organisations and representatives of national parliaments present at these events. the internet will play a key role in building a european digital single market and in promoting innovation, growth, trade, democracy, cultural diversity and human rights. for this reason, although the forum does not adopt formal conclusions, we cannot fail to stress the importance of them and to continue to make efforts to ensure the legal protection of net neutrality as an essential prerequisite for safeguarding freedom of information and expression. only then will we be able to really foster growth and jobs, by creating opportunities for innovation and business linked to the internet. the european union will continue to support this multi-stakeholder process, in defence of cultural and linguistic diversity, while contributing to the formulation of a coherent and comprehensive european approach, together with the member states and the commission.
in writing. the internet governance forum (igf) aims to implement the mandate given to it by the world summit on the information society (wsis) to establish a democratic, transparent and multi-stakeholder political dialogue through the organisation of forums. the igf's main role and function is to promote forward-looking discussions on a wide range of internet governance issues and, where appropriate, to make recommendations to the international community. the internet is the backbone of the digital single market and promotes, inter alia, innovation, growth, trade, democracy, cultural diversity and human rights. the main priorities of the european union during the 9th igf held in september 2014 were, inter alia, to extend network access globally, to maintain the internet as a global, open and shared resource, and to reject the idea of state control of the internet. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of renewing the five-year mandate of the internet governance forum because i find it essential that issues concerning the internet, which today, in fact, governs almost every aspect of our lives, are discussed in a transparent and immediate manner. our parliament, through its delegation, will have to continue to dialogue with all the stakeholders involved in order to contribute to this international process by proposing a coherent and comprehensive european approach. with the renewal of the mandate we also hope to see a greater presence and involvement of the eu in governance, which is heavily controlled by the us, whose presence will already be reduced in part by the transfer of internet surveillance functions to a global multi-stakeholder community, on which it will be essential in any case to ensure independence in order to be able to maintain the stability of the internet. we will continue to have to deal with security and privacy issues very carefully, so as to guarantee complete freedom of expression and information, in an environment that protects personal data from any misuse. protections that not only benefit individual citizens, but also ensure that businesses, especially smes, can develop their online potential without risk.
in writing. the internet governance forum, through its fruitful exchanges and multi-stakeholder approach, is helping to lay the foundations for what the future of the network could be. i believe that we need to move towards an open and independent network, protecting and developing net neutrality as a basic principle that can allow, for example, a newly established web company of an entrepreneur to have the same chance of success as the most established corporations, or ensure that the access to a young person's blog is not unfairly slowed down by an internet provider to allow advertisers to make more money. i hope that the european union will commit itself to trying to bring the negotiations to a conclusion and to reach a comprehensive agreement on the new governance of the internet and on rules that can guarantee the neutrality of the network at the interconnection points between the provider and the rest of the internet.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the horse meat scandal and other cases of food fraud have caused a collapse in consumer confidence and have consequently also caused serious damage to honest producers in the food chain. today europe is called upon to rebuild that confidence, but the right of consumers to know the country of origin of meat used in processed food must not be met by a sharp rise in prices and must not, therefore, generate new demons. importing raw materials is essential for the food industry, especially where domestic production does not meet all needs. along with more information on the origin, consumers should be aware that importing raw materials does not mean lower quality or lower safety. the keywords to be used are therefore 'more security', 'more information' and 'more transparency'.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, labelling the origin of processed meat will be an important step forward, a step forward in protecting the health of consumers, a step forward in combating fraud and counterfeiting. i voted in favour of this because it is in line with a demand for information and transparency from consumers, from european citizens. it will now be up to the commission to translate these indications into a clear rule. we must make it clear that this regulation does not impose any additional costs on consumers. the right to health is a right which cannot be turned into a greater burden. that is why the relationship between labelling and production costs must be carefully studied. that is why we must pay particular attention to small and mediumsized enterprises, which in some cases change suppliers three or four times a year, and we must pay particular attention to products which use more than one type of meat.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the need for greater transparency and traceability of foodstuffs has become a growing and increasing demand of european citizens, especially in the wake of the recent and repeated food fraud, not least that of horse meat. the request of this house, to which i subscribe, that the commission should submit legislative proposals to make it compulsory for the origin of meat used in processed food to be indicated on the labelling of foodstuffs, is in the direction desired by consumers, who should not, however, be burdened with additional costs. the existence of strict standards may not protect us from fraud, but i am sure it will help to detect it and, above all, provide consumers with the information they need to make a more informed and safer choice of products. that is why i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. according to a study commissioned by the european commission in june 2013, 90% of citizens surveyed believe it is important that the origin of processed meat contained in food is visible on the label. today, manufacturers of processed foods have the choice of whether or not to indicate the origin of the ingredients in their processed products. for example, lasagna made in italy may contain meat and other products from other european and non-european countries. the information thus promoted is not transparent and, in our view, does not correspond to what consumers are asking for. we believe that, in order to make an informed choice and to avoid food fraud, meat and other ingredients in italian products should be clearly labelled, as is the case with fresh beef. for the reasons mentioned above, i voted in favour of the resolution tabled by the envi committee.
in writing. i believe that every consumer has the right to know exactly where the meat in the foodstuffs he buys on the shelves comes from. the indication of the country of origin is of fundamental importance for the protection of the health of citizens. i therefore intend to support the text as presented.
in writing. the resolution we voted on today deals with a very important issue for the european agri-food sector: the commission's objective is to ensure greater transparency of information to consumers. i am convinced that transparency and traceability help to strengthen the relationship of trust between consumers and businesses, thus enhancing the many quality products that characterize the different european territories. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the end of the year, and i am therefore voting in favour of it. this will then allow us to enter the legislative phase and arrive at certain indications as to the origin of the meat in processed food, a result which will have to be achieved with particular care in order to avoid the increase in administrative costs and burdens.
in writing. i thought i could support, by my vote, the motion for a resolution which seeks to indicate the origin of processed foodstuffs containing meat ingredients, even though it is being put forward in a legislative framework which is totally inadequate to ensure the transparency due to european consumers and the correct value of agricultural raw materials. in the face of this, the food industry's unease about the additional costs that the indication of origin might cause is secondary, but i welcome the proposal in the hope that it can represent a cultural breakthrough for a europe whose citizens are enabled to make an informed choice and where the right price, not necessarily the lowest, is paid to remunerate fairly the entire agri-food chain and to bring out quality products.
in writing. — i voted yes because i consider this resolution important for the protection of the health of our citizens.
in writing. the need to know the origins of what we eat is a priority for all of us european citizens, because the safeguarding of our health and the freedom to choose as consumers are inalienable rights at the heart of all the health and environmental measures we have adopted here. we cannot but welcome the commission's call to provide for the indication of the origin of meat in processed food, because transparency for the benefit of consumers is the first criterion to be observed. i believe, however, that a careful analysis of the costs and benefits, including the legal impact on the internal market and international trade, of the provision of the mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance should be provided for. finally, i would like to remind you that the food chain is not limited to the raw material but is made up of processing steps, facts of history, culture and experience, such as those used to produce "made in italy" sausages. it is right to inform consumers about the origin of food, but it is equally important to promote and protect the know-how of our processing industry, which in many cases adds value to the raw material.
in writing. i voted in favour of the measure. the commission has urged the submission of legislative proposals for the mandatory indication of the origin of meat. i find the arguments of those who argue the opposite, that the indication would be too expensive, ridiculous! we protect our farmers, we protect our health and we always check where the products we eat come from!
in writing. today i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the indication of the country of origin of meat on the labelling of processed food products. with this resolution, parliament has sent an important signal to the european commission, clearly asking it to launch a legislative initiative on the labelling of processed meat which will strengthen the principle of compulsory indication of the origin of meat, making a decisive contribution to strengthening the health of consumers and ensuring that they can exercise an informed choice. it should be remembered that, according to a recent study by the european commission, 90% of the consumers interviewed consider it important that the origin of the meat be indicated on the label of processed food products. increased transparency would also help to ensure better traceability along the food chain and thus to detect and tackle any infringements, allowing authorities to conduct more effective investigations into cases of food fraud.
in writing. product traceability should be one of the most comprehensively applied principles in the european common market. consumers have the right to be informed and member states have the duty to inform and thereby protect their citizens. we believe, however, that labelling should be compulsory and not voluntary.
in writing. i voted against this resolution because i believe that the indication of origin for meat used as an ingredient does not represent added value for european consumers and is therefore not worth the cost. in fact, apart from the cases of fraud in recent years (where existing rules have been circumvented, so better application is needed rather than new rules), fixing on the origin kills the processing capacities of italian companies. the same applies to products protected by geographical indications of all kinds (pdo, pgi, etc.) and fresh meat, but we run the risk of flooding the consumer with irrelevant information which makes the important information less visible.
in writing. under regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, the commission should have adopted specific implementing acts by 13 december 2013 to make the indication of the origin of meat used as a primary ingredient mandatory where its absence could mislead the consumer as to the actual origin or provenance. however, the commission has never adopted implementing acts to that effect and at present there is no mandatory labelling for meat used as an ingredient in processed foods and voluntary labelling is a source of confusion and food fraud of various kinds. i could only vote in favour of this proposal, which is to urge the commission to make the labelling of origin compulsory also for meat used as an ingredient in processed foods. the movement, however, calls for a phased approach starting with the regulation of voluntary labelling through the adoption of implementing acts. in this first phase we want those who decide to use labelling as a tool to do so conscientiously and in accordance with precise rules, while those who decide not to adhere to the voluntary scheme will no longer be able to indicate the origin of the meat in question (with the consequent marketing disadvantages).
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution adopted today by the european parliament on the indication of the country of origin on the labelling of meat in processed foodstuffs. i believe that, as is already the case for unprocessed meat, the indication of the origin of meat in processed products is an essential, though not sufficient, element in ensuring a higher degree of traceability in the food chain, providing consumers with more information and encouraging more responsible behaviour on the part of operators in the sector in the choice of suppliers. we have always called for clear labelling to serve the consumer. the resolution also calls on the commission to submit legislative proposals in this area. of course, in the legislative process particular attention will have to be paid to the need to define european standards which are effective in protecting the consumer and which at the same time avoid excessive burdens and costs for businesses operating in the sector.
in writing. i voted strongly in favour of the resolution because it is a step in the right direction towards ensuring greater transparency, allowing consumers to make informed choices about what they buy and consume. it's a necessary measure. in fact, more than 90% of citizens think it is important that there is a label indicating the origin of the meat even in processed products. i hope that the european commission will publish a legislative proposal to this effect as soon as possible.

in writing. the vote on labelling opens the door to an important debate on consumer protection and their rightful demand for transparency. we have not voted today for or against the indication of origin for meat in processed foods, but we have simply asked the commission to come forward with a legislative proposal which we will then discuss in parliament. i know there are concerns, which are normal when the rules change. however, with the position adopted today we will have the opportunity to go further in the future through impact assessments and studies of how, where and whether to act in this regard. to say no today would be to take an ideological position which our consumers would certainly not understand.

in writing. since january 2002, community rules on beef labelling have been in force, which already include the indication of the place of birth, rearing and slaughter. those requirements have certainly raised high expectations among consumers regarding information on the origin of other types of fresh meat widely consumed in the union and of meat used as an ingredient in processed foods. in this resolution we call on the commission to come forward with clear, coherent and harmonised legislative proposals for the compulsory indication of the country of origin of meat also in processed products. we believe, however, that mandatory labelling requirements should take account of the principle of proportionality, as well as the administrative burden on food business operators and enforcement authorities, by providing for their own impact assessment and by seeking to avoid excessive costs. we believe that a rigorous traceability system will help to detect and combat fraud and may be able to restore the confidence of european consumers and influence their behaviour. the labelling of foodstuffs must take account of the transparency and legibility of information for consumers, while allowing european businesses to operate in a cost-effective manner.
in writing. depending on the member state, it is estimated that between 30% and 50% of the total volume of slaughtered meat is processed into meat for use as a food ingredient, mainly in minced meat, meat preparations and meat products. according to the abovementioned commission report on the mandatory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance for meat used as an ingredient, the existing traceability systems in the eu are not adequate to transmit information on origin along the food chain. article 26 (2) of the regulation on the provision of food information to consumers provides that the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance is mandatory where the omission of such indication is likely to mislead the consumer as to the actual country of origin or place of provenance of the food. according to the 2013 consumer survey on food categories conducted by the consortium for the evaluation of the food chain, meat products ranked first in terms of interest in the indication of origin on the label. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. i have expressed my support for this resolution because the consumer's right to know what is on his plate every day is sacrosanct. the eu already has one of the most stringent meat labelling laws in the world and we are certainly one of the places in the world where food safety is a constant priority for legislators. however, the quality of information also needs to be improved in relation to processed meat products, which we often consume without paying too much attention to what is in them. on the other hand, it must be borne in mind that the introduction of additional specifications on the origin of meat will lead to a significant increase in the costs for the processing companies and naturally the commission will have to take this into account when proposing a reform of the legislation on labelling.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there is a considerable gap between the legal recognition and the political application of fundamental rights. despite the wording of articles 2, 6 and 7 of the treaty on european union, the rights of millions of european citizens are still affected by the negative and disastrous effects of economic crises, austerity policies, illegal activities such as corruption and various forms of crime. the european union urgently needs an internal strategy on fundamental rights, democracy and the rule of law, so as to ensure consistency with the strategic framework already provided for in the field in external relations. there is no mechanism to assess and ensure effectively the protection and promotion of common european values, enshrined in european and national legislation. article 7 of the treaty on european union has remained a dead letter and the alternative mechanism proposed by the commission in its recent communication on the rule of law is not at all ambitious in preventing violations of the fundamental rights of the european union. it is necessary to provide for effective and appropriate monitoring and response arrangements and for the application of sanctions when such rights are violated. the institutions of the european union, and in particular the commission, therefore have a duty to ensure that all european policies are subject to careful analysis, in order to ensure that the union does not contribute directly or indirectly to violations of fundamental rights on its territory.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the european systems of protection of rights, the echr and the system developed within the community, are a bulwark against the risks of the degeneration of democracies and are designed to ensure respect for the fundamental values of the union. but there are still gaps and weaknesses in these systems. the charter of rights, for example, does apply to states, but only within the framework of union law. it is a questionable limitation which can lead to discrimination which is really contradictory, since these are fundamental rights. the infringement procedure, on the other hand, only concerns violations of specific provisions of the treaties, leaving open many conduct which also infringes or threatens the principles of the rule of law. even more difficult to use are the cumbersome procedures provided for in article 7 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union for cases of clear risk of a serious breach or of a serious and persistent breach of these principles. the commission's idea of opening up the dialogue on fundamental rights in the european union and of activating a sort of early warning mechanism in all cases of systematic violation of fundamental rights and values, regardless of specific violations of the treaties or of elements of connection with union law, is therefore to be welcomed. the commission's attempt to define the concept of the rule of law better by listing some of its essential principles closely linked to the protection of fundamental rights is also to be appreciated. the new operational framework outlined by the commission is, on the whole, to be welcomed, but it must be put into effect as soon as possible, starting with those situations which are of greatest concern today, thus ensuring protection against discrimination and marginalization, against persecution and against any violation of fundamental rights.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, access to medicines is part of the right to health, which is one of the most important of the rights enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights of the european citizen. however, in low- and middle-income countries, the price of medicines can reach up to 80 times the international reference price. in these countries there is very little availability of medicines in the public sector, while there is great availability in the private sector, where prices are much higher, thus making medicines inaccessible to huge sections of the population. so we have a problem of access to medicines, but we have a problem of over-medicine. i am referring to the excessive concentration of industrial production of medicines, which is entirely in the hands of a very few pharmaceutical companies. more than 90 percent of the medicines produced worldwide are produced in rich countries. over 70% of the world's medicines are produced in just five countries. over 45 percent of the drugs are made by just ten pharmaceutical companies, ten multinational drug companies. so these corporations have enormous power in their hands: the power to decide on the price of medicines; the power to lay down rules on intellectual property rights; the power to decide on the allocation of scientific research investments; the power to encourage so-called incremental innovation, that is to say, to encourage only small improvements in existing products. this perverse logic means that medicines which are not very innovative compared with those already on the market are still being introduced on the market, and this requires considerable investment in marketing alone. the result is that we have increasingly expensive but less innovative medicines, which have little impact on patients' health. i'm talking about cetuximab, which, at a cost of 80,000 euros per lung cancer patient, produces an average survival increase of only one and a half months. i'm talking about erlotinib, which, at a cost of $15,000 per patient with pancreatic cancer, produces an average survival increase of only ten days. we propose to open the market for generic medicines and biosimilars once and for all, which are as effective as the originals but cost much less and are therefore much more sustainable for the health systems of all the member states. we also propose the establishment of a large public and european pharmaceutical company which will be able to carry out research in all those areas which are snubbed by private pharmaceutical companies because they are considered commercially uninteresting, such as antimicrobial resistance or the development of vaccines against tragic pandemics such as the ebola virus.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to return to a subject which we have already touched upon, namely orphan drugs, those drugs which are intended for the treatment of rare diseases. pharmaceutical companies are usually reluctant to develop these drugs under normal market conditions, as there is clearly no economic return from the sale of these drugs. however, certain factors must be taken into account: it is estimated that there are between 5 000 and 8 000 rare diseases, affecting about 6 to 8% of the european population, an estimated 27 to 36 million people. so it is true that we have 28 different health systems and 28 different approaches to health, but one thing that all our member states have in common is the concept of the patient as a customer, because they are the customer of the pharmaceutical multinationals. it is therefore essential to change this paradigm and i would like to reiterate the proposal and the idea put forward by my colleague mr pedicini of a european public pharmaceutical company, which can really change completely the way we treat and care for health in europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, medical research is now making progress in the effectiveness of care of such a revolutionary scope that it is also reflected in the economic factors of health care. it is good and ethical that medicines should be cheaper. the aim of increasing universal health coverage means that the most modern techniques for testing and producing medicinal products must be adopted in order to meet the necessary criteria of efficiency and cost-effectiveness. however, as is well known, the lack of economic viability is now reflected in the very possibility of treatment due to the prohibitive cost of some medicines, such as sofosbuvir for hepatitis, which costs up to 50,000 euros. policy choices must be directed towards processes that can have a positive impact on the effectiveness of research and the cost-effectiveness of health care. i am thinking of the innovation of research processes, such as remote patient monitoring systems or even the development of molecular drugs called biological or intelligent. i also hope that the development of centres of excellence in research will be encouraged with increased subsidies from the member states, in order to promote greater economic viability of the drug and an ever-increasing sharing of information and knowledge, overcoming the logic of the research monopoly. another way of combining innovation and cost-effectiveness is through joint and coordinated policy action. it is true that the regulatory process is the responsibility of each member state, but the commission must encourage cooperation between the member states in order to curb price speculation. finally, a production method could be developed which would make it possible to produce medicines in a way which departs from the classical discontinuous batch system which is widely used today. i believe that this is the direction in which the member states and the commission should take action to ensure that medicines are accessible and thus that there is greater social equity.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are witnessing an unprecedented paradox in europe. for decades, we've asked research to give us the tools to fight cancer. today we are able to beat many cancers and we can chronicle many different types of cancer, but too many patients across europe do not have access to the new drugs that guarantee these results. the approach to drug pricing and reimbursement is too fragmented. each member state has to negotiate a price with the pharmaceutical companies and decide whether and how to reimburse the new medicine, and this brings unacceptable differences for european patients. we think it often takes up to ten years, if not more, before an ema-approved drug is available, and in addition the price of new drugs varies greatly from country to country and not always in relation to the cost of living. this is not good. this is not right. this needs to change. the price of a new medicine must be based on a balanced assessment of the real costs of producing and developing the medicine and the impact on patient health and society. the ema must be able to include a cost-benefit analysis and for this the commission must include the work of the health technology assessment agency. i believe that, for all that i have said, we must go far beyond the commission's proposal. let's just say it's a good start.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are convinced that the energy union is right and necessary, but if we look at the major projects being planned to solve new problems, we are reiterating the solutions of fifty years ago in a geopolitical and geological context that has changed substantially. we are talking about an energy union built only on macro-connections between nations and only on the ability to reverse macro-flows. it doesn't matter what form of energy is flowing through it. it is not a matter of whether there may not be as many suppliers outside the eu who are able or willing to give everyone the energy they need tomorrow. it does not matter if even today adjacent apartments are not made to exchange energy independently of monopolies. it's been assumed that this downhill union automatically generates resilience, but it leads us to another dead end, to new dependencies and great disappointments. for the times in which we live and will live, we consider appropriate another form of energy union where the indigenous generation and diffused food sources flow inverted compared to the past from individual houses and power stations to the large connectors necessary is true, but to calm the intermittency of renewables of local seasonal and circadian variations in climate and light between distant areas. we learn from water and plants: the smallest drop of dew still feeds its basin, rivers spring from countless branches, trees push their roots deeper in times of drought. we are the first in the world to achieve the renewable energy union, the democratic energy internet. let us free ourselves forever from the slavery of imports, from the devastation of climate and ecosystems, from wars, from political dependence.

in writing. the communications adopted this morning by the commission and at the heart of the debate on the energy union we are having in parliament are of major strategic importance. as commissioner šefčovič has rightly said, the european project must be firmly based on the principles of trust and solidarity if it is to continue to grow. until now, energy policies have been the preserve of the member states with the resultant and obvious problems of dependence, dispersion and insufficient interconnection. each step towards a single energy market strengthens security of supply and allows for a stronger common policy for the now indispensable energy transition to a low-carbon model. the need to reduce dependence on third countries is not the only factor, but also the need to provide investment certainty, which is a key lever for achieving this 'historic' transformation. a transition that benefits citizens, businesses and the environment. the commission has outlined its vision today, and it is now important to move as quickly as possible to the operational phase. it will be important to ensure that progress on energy efficiency remains central in the overall strategic framework, not only in transport and construction, but also in the generation phase.
