president-in-office of the council. - mr president, it is a pleasure to be with you again after this month’s meeting of the european council. the main purpose of informal summits is to discuss and consult, not to negotiate. our meeting was short and the outcome quite concise. it took place against the background of rapidly-changing events. of the four great challenges on the table, the first was ukraine. we had an exchange with ukraine’s president, petro poroshenko. he joined us to present the minsk ceasefire and to share his assessment of the situation on the ground. we thanked chancellor merkel and president hollande for their indispensable efforts for peace as the initiators of the normandy four talks. we gave the fragile agreement our cautious support. the european union still hopes for peace so that the independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity of ukraine can be restored as soon as possible. however, we remain very sceptical. the 2014 minsk agreement was not honoured. debate among the leaders focused on how to support the implementation of the new peace deal. if this does not happen, we will not hesitate to take the necessary steps. the ceasefire, which was supposed to take effect at midnight on 15 february, has been violated more than 800 times according to the osce. i am in contact with chancellor merkel and president hollande and in consultation with all leaders. the european union stands united on this question and will stay the course. additional sanctions remain on the table. we should be ready for any development, good or bad. on 12 february, leaders recalled the terrible attacks in paris which killed 17 people. we committed ourselves to a new counter-terrorism work plan. this is set out in the joint statement adopted at the summit. the new work plan mainly requires the european union to do what it is already doing in the field of internal security, but we need to do specific things better and faster, such as making far better use of the security arrangements of schengen or reviewing regulations for firearms. the recent fatal attack in copenhagen underlines the necessity. these attacks only strengthen our determination to fight all kinds of extremism and terrorism. i take this opportunity to express our deepest sympathy and support to denmark, the danish people and the families of the victims. although libya was not on the agenda of the february informal european council, the terrible and dangerous events in that country are the latest convincing reason to address this pressing issue. national security is a matter for national governments. nevertheless, there are important areas where we can support each other and where common action is even vital. in that respect, i warmly welcome the recent progress towards restarting the negotiations on an eu agreement on passenger name records. i have no doubt that we can effectively protect the security of citizens without diminishing the right to privacy. your help on this issue is absolutely crucial and invaluable. the european council will come back to this matter in june, amongst other things. meanwhile our countries will face this threat together, calmly and with determination. as for greece, our february meeting was clearly not the right moment for uncoordinated negotiations on the greek assistance programme. we heard from the president of the eurogroup, who outlined what the state of play was in discussions with greece. we welcomed prime minister tsipras as a new member of the european council, who gave us his view of the situation. we agreed that the talks would go on, as they did, at ministerial level so that common ground could be found. i had no doubt that this would happen. close contacts were maintained with all the relevant parties so that agreement could be reached in principle at the eurogroup last friday. i was glad to see eurozone ministers give the green light to greece’s reform plans yesterday. finally, we briefly considered the future of economic and monetary union itself. we need to improve economic policy-making in the eurozone. all the principal authors of the so-called four presidents’ report were in the room, so the setting was right to open this discussion. president juncker presented background analysis and posed questions that need to be answered if we are to achieve better economic governance. however, one point is already perfectly clear. after the recent decision of the ecb, the priority is to make national economies more compatible with monetary union. this cannot be done from brussels but through strong political ownership of economic reforms at national level. we now look ahead to the march european council. in the next three weeks we will follow the situation in ukraine and in libya day by day with great precision. the march summit will also be a time to consider the strategic outlook for the eastern and southern neighbourhoods. we will continue our discussion on the european economy and, of course, we will also focus on an issue that is as close to my own heart as it is to many in this parliament, that is, the urgent need for a european energy union, as vice-president šefčovič has just outlined. the european union can – and must – make progress in this area soon. president of the commission. - mr president, mr president-in-office of the council, ladies and gentlemen, the council meeting of 12 february was an informal council, without any decision being taken. it was a useful council and, despite the announcements that had been made, it was a council without drama. it was short and it was effective, as was its president. we have obviously discussed the fight against terrorism a few weeks after the events in paris and on this point we agreed that the schengen agreements are not a problem. schengen is a response to the problem and we have therefore rejected, on the basis of the commission's proposals, any idea of making massive and substantive amendments to the schengen agreements. when it comes to fighting terrorism, there is no room for haste. the answers to terrorism are not made in a hurry. remember the mistakes our american friends made immediately after the 9/11 attacks in new york and washington. you have to stay calm, but you have to stay serious. we have done this with the single european register of passenger data. on this point, mr president, i would like to pay tribute to this house for agreeing to reverse a decision taken by one of your committees. i would like to pay tribute to you personally, mr president, because you have done everything possible to bring parliament, its various committees, its bodies and its members closer to the viewpoint of the commission which preceded mine. i do not criticize parliament for the decision it seemed to have taken a few months ago, because respect for fundamental rights and civil liberties is one of the considerations which also motivate the commission's action. but on this point, we must act and react with severity. we discussed the european energy union at the council on 11 february. the commission took a decision this morning. personally, i have always considered - though i have not always done so - that major projects should be launched at the beginning of the parliamentary term. if i had done it in my previous life, the outcome would have been better. but as president of the commission, i would like to see major projects, those which reflect the commission's priorities, started immediately. the result was that we agreed on a green paper on the capital markets union. i know guy doesn't like the fact that the commission is presenting a green paper - he might prefer a blue paper, but that would have a partisan connotation. philippe, of course, likes the green books, but the answers have to be ultra-green, too. we'll see at the autopsy if i dare say so. we have launched, as i said, an energy union. we have made sure that the commission's work and working methods are made clear. we intend to take all the necessary decisions on the digital single market, and we will do so in may. all the commission's major projects have therefore been started and the related initiatives will be launched shortly and in order. at the council meeting chaired by president tusk, we presented an analytical study on the causes of the crisis in the economic and monetary union. since this was the easiest part, we presented our colleagues in the european council with a questionnaire on the main points concerning the future of economic and monetary union. i read that some people were sorry i only asked questions. but if you don't ask questions, you don't get answers. if we want answers - and i want answers on the essential dimension of economic and monetary union - we have to ask questions. we will discuss them with president tusk, president dijsselbloem and president draghi in the coming weeks and we will associate the president of the european parliament as closely as possible in this exercise. i should like to make it clear that this is a report by the four chairmen. so we'll include martin schulz. it is not a report of the four institutions plus the european parliament. it is a personal matter and i would therefore like, as the other presidents have done so far, that we should confine ourselves to examining our own ideas. not the ones from our institution. i personally have never had a debate in the commission. donald has never had a debate in the european council. as for mr draghi, as he is independent, i do not know what he has done, but we, the others, who are dependent, must know that this is a report which reflects the personal views of the five presidents and i welcome the fact that the president of parliament is associated with this exercise. as regards the investment plan, which is wrongly named after me - but i like it - i would like to pay tribute to the european parliament, its committees and its two rapporteurs, who are doing an excellent job. mr bullmann and mr fernández are working hard to enable parliament to take a decision on this plan and the accompanying legislative texts by june at the latest. i stress the need for a parliamentary decision in june. i would remind you, mr president, that i consciously chose the community method for adopting these texts. it would have been possible for the commission and the council alone to take the decisions, but i wanted to involve the european parliament in the community method, which i keep saying we must rehabilitate, and we have done so on this point. we have today, as the college of commissioners, taken a decision on budgetary aspects which concern a number of member states - not just one, but several member states. since the attention of the general public, including parliamentary attention, has been focused on the case of france, i wanted to tell you that we have just decided today to invite france to reduce its structural deficit this year, in 2015, by 0.5%, which will mean that the french government will have to amend the budget it voted for 2015 by 0.2%. we would like france to reduce its structural deficit by 0.75%, 0.8% or 0.9% in 2016. we will give france an additional two years, but we will intensify the procedure concerning macroeconomic imbalances. france will therefore be - excuse the expression - under increased surveillance. i would like to say that the commission will be more closely involved in the budgetary adjustments. so we work, we do what we can. we cannot do everything you want us to do, but we are waiting for the european parliament to support our action. without the european parliament, the commission is deaf and dumb. she can't speak or act. so let us act.

in writing. the discussion of european leaders on the fight against terrorism was fruitful and i hope that it will succeed in giving a really decisive direction to the strengthening of counter-terrorism measures in the european union. i think the heads of state or government have clearly identified the three pillars on which work will have to be concentrated in the coming months: the security of citizens, the prevention of radicalisation and the protection of european values, and cooperation with international partners. a general consensus is therefore emerging that a coherent and effective counter-terrorism strategy must be based on a multidisciplinary approach. the european leaders also stressed the need to adopt urgently a strong and effective directive on a european reservation code system (pnr) which also includes strong data protection safeguards. i believe that this approach to pnr should be a small-scale example of the whole european union's counter-terrorism strategy, which must include swift and decisive measures without compromising the fundamental rights of european citizens. we cannot accept that an external threat undermines the values on which the european union is founded.
in writing. the summit meeting on 12 february had on its agenda issues of great importance and urgency: the european council in brussels on 14 and 15 december last gave a clear signal to the european parliament that it was ready to take action in the field of the internal market. the summit, however, does not seem to have produced any major results. the most significant is the agreement on a declaration on the fight against terrorism, which indicates areas and a path for action, and calls for the rapid adoption of some measures already under discussion, including the european pnr. while we share the need to deal with the emergency of terrorism and international crime, we believe that any restrictions on freedom must strictly respect the principle of proportionality and must not go beyond what is necessary and essential to combat these phenomena.

in writing. after five years of waiting, the ecb has fired the last shot in a desperate attempt to revive the eurozone economy, but quantitative easing comes too late to effectively counter the deflationary spiral. as with previous ltros, the most likely outcome is that the surge of liquidity inflows will be trapped in the vortex of speculative finance and not reach the real economy. this is because the main issues that continue to block credit and productive investment in europe, primarily the fight against speculation and the need for fiscal harmonization, have not been resolved, and instead everything has been focused on structural reforms and austerity. for monetary policy to be effective, in fact, the eurozone urgently needs a genuine structural reform of the banking system, based on the separation of credit and financial activities, to bring banks back to the practice of accumulating savings for the sole purpose of guaranteeing credit to the real economy. moreover, the european version of qe, the quintessential unconventional monetary policy measure, has already become the symbol of a failed monetary union and of an 'unconventional central bank' which, as demonstrated by the need to limit the risk-sharing on the ecb to a paltry 8%, is not even capable of expressing a single monetary policy.

author of the book. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the oral question, which has been tabled with the agreement and support of many colleagues, and for which i thank you, is based on the article on endocrine disruptors published in the british newspaper the guardian on 2 february. the article denounces the european commission's cover-up of the proposal prepared by the environment dg in 2013 that would have led to the development of criteria for classifying a substance as an endocrine disruptor, thus launching a new strategy on the subject. with this proposal, the environment dg, pursuant to article 5 of the european union regulation concerning the placing on the market and use of biocidal products, obliged the commission to define the criteria for the identification of substances with endocrine disrupting properties by 13 december 2013. however, following external pressure, but also from other commission directorates-general, the environment dg's proposal seems to have been blocked and replaced by an impact assessment, which unfortunately will not be finalised before 2016, a measure which therefore appears instrumentally to circumvent the obligation to submit criteria. the commission has also been asked to draw up a report on the impact assessment of the proposed directive. the commission has included in it an option concerning the introduction of socioeconomic derogations for the placing on the market of substances containing endocrine disruptors, thus leaving the use of pesticides, for example, open. given that in its january 2013 report parliament strongly argued that the authorisation of substances containing endocrine disruptors should be limited, i ask the commission why and who authorised the derogations for the placing on the market of these substances. the guardian article argued that as many as 31 pesticides could be banned, causing a clear and significant negative economic impact on the industry. it is easy to see how the development of criteria for defining endocrine disruptors would have economic consequences not only for the pesticide industry but also for a very wide range of other products with which we interact in our daily lives and which contain endocrine disruptors: packaging, skin care products, cosmetics, building materials, electronic equipment, furniture and flooring and what are the costs of not developing the criteria for the health of european citizens? they seem to be very tall. evidence has shown that the increase in cancer, infertility, early puberty, cardiovascular disease, and fetal and genital abnormalities over the past 20 years may be associated with exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals. the costs in terms of health expenditure and lower productivity at community level are also affected by the lack of criteria. according to a recent study, they amount to €157 billion. it goes without saying that the presentation of the criteria could therefore bring important benefits both for the health of citizens and for the european health system. how does the commission intend to take account of the potential benefits of the introduction of the criteria in its impact assessment? and does the commission intend to carry out further studies on the benefits that may result from the introduction of these criteria? i would also like to know whether the commission intends to raise public awareness of endocrine disruptors, for example by making recommendations to citizens to reduce their exposure to them. i believe that, pending the development of the criteria, guidelines at european level should be developed as soon as possible to deal with this silent pollution, which is too little considered by public opinion and citizens, who currently do not have sufficient information to protect their health. i myself, however, have addressed these needs for clarity, awareness and protection with a question of my own in october 2014, in which i expressed my deep concern about the presence of endocrine disrupting phthalates linked to health problems of alarming magnitude, including in toys and children's articles, in order to improve their flexibility, malleability and durability. they have a wide range of applications and are used in cosmetics as fixatives, in the health and pharmaceutical industries and in many other industrial applications. finally, recent research on bisphenol a has demonstrated the need for greater coordination at european level on programmes dedicated to endocrine disruptors. i find it difficult to understand how it is possible that the french national agency for food safety has presented alarming studies on this substance between 2013 and 2014 and european experts have recently concluded that exposure to bisphenol a poses no risk to humans. the commission therefore considers that the establishment of a research centre on endocrine disruptors is necessary to carry out research on these substances and to coordinate knowledge on the subject at eu level, as proposed by parliament in its 2013 resolution.

in writing. infrastructure, transport and sustainable energy are the main areas we have decided to focus on during our work on eltifs: the long-term european investment funds. with this instrument, we have built a framework favourable to investment in europe. it is a balanced text that rewards the virtuous investors of small and medium-sized unlisted companies who decide to invest in real estate and infrastructure projects. in addition, the investors concerned are mainly institutional investors, represented by pension funds, insurance companies and private investors who have the possibility of committing their savings for a longer period. indeed, these types of activities are able to guarantee stable returns. we have decided to give priority to those projects which have the greatest impact on the local community and which guarantee the greatest impact on job creation. for these reasons, it is a key instrument for boosting growth and jobs in europe. the european central bank's expansionary measures and the new investment legislation have helped us to emerge from the economic and financial crisis.
in writing. long-term investment funds, beyond appearances, are a tool to pave the way for financial speculation and the wild privatization of common goods, rather than a clever tool to revive a model of finance at the service of the real economy and society. the way in which eltifs are structured does not provide investors with the right incentives to channel capital towards productive long-term investments in support of crisis-hit smes. the funds designed by the commission are by definition hedge funds, i.e. hedge funds, which are obliged to invest 70% of their capital in long-term investments capable of generating constant profits. these are investments in financial instruments of companies or other funds and in real assets, including non-productive assets such as infrastructure, real estate, ships and aircraft. it is clear that this means that we are once again endorsing an inefficient and consumer-oriented use of financial resources which could instead be channelled towards the financing of innovative projects and productive enterprises. unfortunately, with this further prestige play, the profit-oriented investments in public services, such as water and waste management infrastructure, or roads, schools and hospitals, are being let through the window, but without making too much noise.

in writing. ‒ i thought i would vote in favour of this measure because the european fund established provides support for workers who are being affected by the structural changes in world trade. the fund may not exceed the annual ceiling of eur 150 million (2011 prices). the necessary amounts shall be entered in the general budget of the union as a provision. the procedures which will be used to obtain the transfer of the funds seem to me to be good and efficient. the dialogue between the commission and the authority should ensure the success of the procedural agreement, see the case of zachem poland, which is going through a dark period due to the shift of production of chemicals to asia, with a higher production cost impact due to high labour costs. i consider the intervention of the european fund to be a positive and decisive procedure aimed at supporting and defending individual european workers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the present application, which concerns the mobilisation of the egf in favour of poland, and which aims to compensate 615 redundant workers, who worked in the zaklady chemiczne zachem company, specialised in the manufacture of chemicals and chemical products. these surpluses are the result of the major changes in the structure of world trade due to globalisation. in particular, the chinese market share in this sector increased significantly due to lower labour costs. i therefore regard the intervention of the european fund as a positive and decisive procedure aimed at defending european workers who are affected by the structural changes in world trade.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mobilising the egf in response to the request for financial assistance from poland following the insolvency of zachem and its two other suppliers in the manufacture of chemicals. the company faced strong competition from asian producers, which resulted in a sharp decrease in its market share. in particular, the production of ech (epichlorohydrin) has become unsuitable, both because of the increase in production costs in europe and the unexpected increase in the supply of ech from asia. zachem's subsequent decision to discontinue production operations and to undertake internal reorganisation also had an immediate impact on its suppliers and widened its effects. in addition, the region affected by the redundancies had an unemployment rate of around 17% in the reference period, the highest in poland, mainly as a direct or indirect consequence of the difficulties experienced by zachem. the egf will co-finance personalised services to help - hopefully quickly and in a timely manner - the jobless to return to work.
in writing. ‒ poland requested the mobilisation of the egf following the 615 redundancies at a chemical plant and two of its suppliers. the commission recalled that the union industry had a significant market share in the union during the period considered. the total contribution requested is eur 115.205. it should be noted that the measures supported by the egf are intended for 50 workers in a disadvantaged situation. in essence, recruitment and investment incentives are co-financed. furthermore, it should be noted that the factory in question was the largest employer in the region and that during the reference period, workers dismissed, directly or indirectly by zachem, represented 60% of all newly registered unemployed in the district employment office in bydgoszcz. given the importance of improving the employability of all workers through appropriate training and the recognition of skills and competences acquired during a worker's professional career, i consider that poland is entitled to a financial contribution under that regulation.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this recommendation because it is important for the safety and security of all that heavy goods vehicles and buses travelling within the union comply with certain standards as regards weight, height, length and width. it is also for safety reasons that it is right to grant exemptions and allow manufacturers to introduce newly designed devices. engineering and technology allow us to put vehicles on the road with better visibility for the driver, with shapes that improve impact in the event of collisions and technologies that reduce co2 emissions, among other things. the road hauliers provide a vital service and are responsible for much of the so-called free movement of goods, which is one of the symbols of a united europe. so we safeguard the category, we improve their difficult working conditions and we increase their safety and consequently our own.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the revised directive on the dimensions and weights of road vehicles which would allow manufacturers to introduce new truck designs, which could exceed the current maximum length and weight limits for heavy duty vehicles in order to improve overall safety and environmental performance. a more rounded cab would increase the driver's field of vision by improving the ability to spot vulnerable road users, such as cyclists, and reduce drag, while a shape that facilitates deflection would reduce the impact of collisions. the addition of aerodynamic fins at the rear would also help to reduce emissions and fuel consumption. member states are required to adopt the relevant national provisions within two years of the entry into force of this revised directive. it is essential that the commission revise the directive three years after the implementation of the national rules, also taking into account certain market segments such as car carriers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr jörg leichtfried, which seeks to amend council directive 96/53/ec laying down for certain road vehicles circulating in the community the maximum authorised dimensions in national and international traffic and the maximum authorised weights in international traffic. i believe that the objectives of improving road safety, energy efficiency and environmental performance of this specific transport sector are fully acceptable.
in writing. ‒ the measure under consideration introduces a new type of heavy vehicle which would minimise road accidents by improving the driver's field of vision and giving him a better ability to identify vulnerable road users, such as cyclists. the addition of aerodynamic accessories would help to reduce consumption and harmful gas emissions, thus protecting the air and the environment. the organizational revolution in transport envisaged by the measure is far-sighted and futuristic. each member state will have to adapt to its own requirements the provisions which will be enacted with the task of safeguarding road safety by means of a structural improvement in the design of heavy goods vehicles. i shall vote in favour of these rights.
in writing. ‒ the resolution sets the maximum authorised dimensions and weights for certain road vehicles on the community's roads, with the aim of improving the driver's field of vision by reducing blind spots, including those under the windscreen, and thus saving many lives of vulnerable users, such as pedestrians or cyclists. the addition of aerodynamic accessories would also help to reduce consumption and harmful gas emissions, thus protecting the air and the environment. for these reasons i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the data on european road safety show that the targets set with the launch of the european action programmes for safety have still not been achieved. this included halving the number of road deaths by 2010, an ambitious target which must spur us on to find the courage to introduce ever higher standards. the optimum implementation of the major road infrastructure projects under the connecting europe programme will certainly be of fundamental help. however, they may not be sufficient if the safety of vehicles is not also addressed. in addition, it should be stressed that improving intermodality at european level will make it possible to shorten journey times and, consequently, reduce co2 emissions, bringing closer the achievement of another valuable environmental protection objective for europe.
in writing. ‒ the committee on transport and tourism adopted the recommendation for the second reading of the jörg leichtfried report on the council's position at first reading on the adoption of a european parliament and council directive amending directive 96/53/ec laying down, for certain road vehicles circulating in the community, the maximum authorised dimensions in national and international traffic and the maximum authorised weights in international traffic. i'm voting for it.
in writing. ‒ the report to be voted on concerns the revision of directive 96/53/ec on the dimensions and weights of road vehicles, a revision which is necessary in view of the technological progress achieved in this field in recent years. the improvements in the proposal concern vehicle aerodynamics, energy efficiency and road safety. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the measure because future long vehicles could cause greater risks to driving, both for pedestrians and in creating road discomfort in certain areas (especially in italy).
in writing. given the target set in the 2011 white paper to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 60% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels, i am voting in favour of the proposal to revise directive 96/53/ec on the weights and dimensions of motor vehicles to limit their energy consumption, in the light of new technologies and current road safety needs. to this end, i also consider it important that the directive, in accordance with the guidelines contained in the document 'towards a european road safety area 2011-2020' and in line with the sustainability objectives set out in the horizon 2020 programme, be open to certain derogations aimed at three main objectives: the commission has also adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment against the adverse effects of ionizing radiation.

in writing. ‒ this directive provides for derogations from the maximum authorised dimensions and weights of vehicles and combinations of vehicles laid down in directive 96/53/ec. member states should address the problem of overloading violations in an appropriate manner in order to improve and ensure better road safety. i therefore voted in favour of the recommendation on the dimensions and weights of road vehicles in the community.
in writing. ‒ eu member states should implement specific measures aimed at identifying vehicles that may have exceeded the weight limits imposed on the specific category. that is why i have decided to support, by my vote in favour, the leichtfried report, which calls for the implementation of the european parliament and council directive setting maximum authorized dimensions and weights for certain road vehicles in the community.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of this directive will allow manufacturers to introduce new truck designs, which could exceed the current maximum length and weight limits for heavy-duty vehicles in order to improve overall safety and environmental performance. it will also eliminate the unnecessary red tape faced by hauliers who have had to apply for special permits to transport such containers. we believe, however, that legislative action by the member states is essential, both to encourage regulatory approval in this area and to provide for specific measures to identify vehicles which may have exceeded the relevant length and weight limits. this is a natural safeguard for road safety for european citizens.
in writing. ‒ directive 96/53/ec on the dimensions and weights of road vehicles circulating in the community has for many years contributed to the smooth functioning of the internal road transport market by setting maximum dimensions and weights for vehicles engaged in national and international transport of goods and passengers. in the light of the evolution of the market and of the technologies available, the question arises today as to whether the choices made when it was adopted in 1996 are still relevant. in particular, the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and the consumption of petroleum products has become crucial in the transport sector. for the reasons mentioned above, i thought it appropriate to vote in favour of the leichtfried report which stresses that a revision of the directive is necessary as improving the efficiency and environmental performance of road transport is an essential objective of the common transport policy.
in writing. ‒ having regard to the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve road safety, adapt the relevant legislation to technological developments and changing market needs and facilitate intermodal transport operations, while ensuring undistorted competition and protecting road infrastructure; technological developments offer the possibility of installing retractable or folding aerodynamic devices at the rear end of vehicles; i am therefore in favour of the proposal that this directive provides for derogations from the maximum authorized dimensions and weights of vehicles and combinations of vehicles laid down in directive 96/53/ec.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from vehicles by adapting existing legislation to the continuing technological developments in the sector and to a constantly changing market is a key objective, not forgetting to give priority to road safety. for these reasons, i welcome this directive from the european parliament which amends the maximum lengths of vehicles to give priority to new aerodynamic devices which allow for considerable advantages in the energy performance of vehicles. in addition, a new layout of the vehicle cabs contributes to improving road safety for all and to improving driver comfort. as regards the weight of vehicles, i think it is important that the competent authorities of the member states exchange information systematically to facilitate the carrying out of checks on the weight of vehicles. it is also important that the european parliament is informed of the controls carried out on road traffic by the competent authorities, so that it can determine whether the rules are being applied and whether additional measures are necessary.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which is the result of a long agreement between the council and the european parliament on the definition of weight limits for alternative fuelled vehicles and intermodal transport for certain containers. the aim of the report is to improve the aerodynamic aspects of commercial vehicles and their energy efficiency, thereby improving road safety and the environment.
in writing. i voted against because there is a risk that any future long vehicles could cause greater risks to drivers, to pedestrians and create road congestion in many areas.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the directive against so-called megatrans, so that their use, which is currently limited to the scandinavian countries, the united kingdom and ireland, is not extended to all eu countries. at present, 26% of co2 emissions from european road transport are from this type of heavy-duty vehicle, and further expansion of this type of vehicle would have dangerous effects on pollution. for this reason too, this directive not only imposes a weight and size limit on vehicles, but also encourages the use of combined transport, such as road and rail, or road and sea transport, in order to ensure that road transport is used less. the directive also calls for the development of safer and more environmentally friendly cabs, thanks to aerodynamic improvements that will reduce fuel consumption and allow drivers to have fewer blind spots, improving safety on european roads, which, with more than 120,000 fatalities a year, are the main cause of death in europe.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, at this time of severe economic crisis, from which it seems increasingly difficult to emerge, it is an urgent priority to lead the european union in creating jobs. long-term investment could achieve this by financing both tangible activities, such as infrastructure, and intangible activities, such as research and development, which are key sectors for growth. more importantly, long-term financing is a key tool for smart growth, so as to avoid new crises. the second point i would like to make is that the european longterm investment funds will be able to provide a vital source of income for all those who need longterm prospects, and i am thinking of municipalities and small and mediumsized enterprises. if we want this system to work, however, we must not forget the tax aspect. the union should show all member states the way to introducing tax breaks that are particularly beneficial to those who decide to invest in the long term.
in writing. ‒ the lamassoure report analyses the european long-term investment funds, a multiannual financial instrument whose purpose is to catalyse public and private investment to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. although i share some of the aims of the regulation, such as the aim of achieving a high employment rate, i abstained because i think the text is unbalanced and i do not think that, given the way the funds are structured, they will achieve the objectives they set.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this supplementary report because i do think that we need a regulation in order to boost european long-term investments in the real economy.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the supplementary report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on european long-term investment funds. i believe that long-term financing can be an important tool to help the european economy grow and to stimulate competitiveness and employment. furthermore, i believe it is very important that these funds are framed in the context of the europe 2020 strategy to promote smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. progress in achieving the objectives of this strategy could then make more capital available. i hope, therefore, that the european long-term funds will play an important part in financing the union's real economy and implementing its policies.
in writing. ‒ european long-term investment funds (eltifs) provide long-term financing for infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or listed small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) that issue debt instruments for which there is no readily identifiable buyer. the proposal for a regulation under consideration could indeed be an opportunity to set the stage for a strong economic stimulus, but the text, as it has been drawn up, does not seem to meet the real needs. the risk is that the main beneficiaries will be large infrastructure projects and multinational groups, while smes, which have no access to capital markets, will be effectively overlooked. these constitute a major part of the union's real economy, which is in danger of being overtaken by speculative interests.
in writing. ‒ competitiveness and growth, the cornerstones of the junker plan and of the ecb's action, contrast with a european scenario characterised by a highly fragmented market and tied to national logic. more than a problem of liquidity, there is a problem of lack of guarantees for private investors who, for this reason too, have little interest in investing in europe and, above all, in making long-term investments. the banking and economic union must be brought to fruition, since it would, together with political union, fully realize the european union project and contribute to the 'fidelization' of world liquidity. to this end, it would be beneficial to have instruments such as eltifs, which are available to both public and private investors and which remove barriers to investment, allowing investors to count on a stable return. this instrument would also make it possible to invest in smes, opening up this sector - which has been hit hard by the economic crisis - to foreign investment. the report is moving in that direction and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this measure, having analysed that long-term financing is a key enabling tool to put the european economy on a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the europe 2020 strategy, and of high employment and competitiveness by proposing a less risk-prone economy. the central objective of this regulation is to stimulate long-term european investment in the real economy (infrastructure, intellectual property, ships, equipment, machinery, aircraft or rolling stock and real estate). eltifs represent the first step towards the creation of an integrated internal market for raising capital that can be channelled towards long-term investment in the european economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this measure because i believe that the european long-term investment funds are a key instrument for a smart growth path, so as to avoid new crises. i agree with the intention of making these funds a revenue stream for all those who need long-term prospects, such as municipalities or small and mediumsized enterprises. if we want this system to work, however, we must not forget the fiscal aspect: i believe that the union should show all the member states the way to introduce disincentives for those who decide to invest in the long term.
in writing. ‒ the proposed eltif regulation aims to mobilise and channel private capital through alternative investment funds, such as hedge funds, towards long-term investments in the real economy. in particular, it is expected that eltifs invest at least 70% of their capital in financial instruments of unlisted companies and listed smes, in shares or units of other funds and in real assets of more than eur 10 million such as infrastructure, real estate, ships and aircraft. they are also intended as a priority instrument for the implementation of the juncker plan and for eib projects. i am voting against because of the many criticisms of the design of these funds and the doubts about their real economic and social utility. although presented as a long-term financing instrument to support the real economy, eltifs are nevertheless authorised to invest in non-productive real assets such as real estate, ships and aircraft as well as in public infrastructure, including transport infrastructure such as roads, airports, public transport, but also energy, water or waste management, industrial plants, public buildings. in this way the regulation facilitates access for hedge funds to financing of common goods and in fact opens the way to privatisation.
in writing. ‒ the sense of recovery that europe is experiencing is hardly maturing and strengthening to the point of creating the conditions to start producing wealth and new employment, reversing the trend of recent years. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial system is not affected by the crisis. even today, there is little evidence of a reversal of this trend. in this respect, the initiatives of the european institutions are essential in order to put in place instruments to support and finance the growth and development of enterprises and firms, enabling them to obtain the necessary capital. long-term investment funds are all the more important because they impact on high-risk projects which just as ambitious need long periods to produce profits. it will be important to clarify the parliament's monitoring role, especially in relation to the selection of projects, giving priority to those potentially most likely to have an impact on the labour market and the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. ‒ i abstain on the regulation on long-term european investment funds. i share some of the aims of the regulation (including the achievement of a high employment rate) but i am very critical of the fact that the current european commission is able to draw positive results in terms of wealth creation and/or development from this type of operation. some observers, however, have pointed out that instruments which can offer results in the short term are preferable.
in writing. ‒ with the european long-term investment funds, we have created a new tool for the eu to stimulate growth. these funds will help smes, individual and professional investors and insurance companies to invest in projects involving infrastructure, equipment, machinery, research and education, and in doing so, will provide a cascade of benefits to the eu economy. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution, but i am convinced that parliament must continue to examine this project so that the funds can really reach the citizens in an effective way without excessive bureaucratic steps.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr bidegain's report analysing the legislative proposal on interbank charges for credit card payments. i think this is a very balanced text, the legislative process has been long and the negotiations complex, but the final result is a widely shared legislative proposal which has put consumer needs first without imposing unsustainable market conditions on operators as is often the case.
in writing. ‒ there are about 760 million cards in circulation in the eu, an average of 1.5 cards per person, with a 6% increase in the number of transactions in 2013. however, payment by debit and credit cards comes at a cost to merchants, who pay a fee for each transaction. a cost, estimated at a total of 10 billion a year, that is often discharged on the sale price. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'commercial vehicle' to cover vehicles with a maximum mass exceeding 10 tonnes. the proposal will cap commissions at 0.2% for debit card transactions and 0.3% for credit card transactions. this is an action which should lead to a cascade of savings on retail prices and it will be important to ensure that this does not lead to a paradoxical increase in bank charges for consumers. the european commission's estimates are encouraging, with annual savings of €6 billion for traders and €730 million for consumers. my vote in favour is intended to support the developments in terms of transparency and competition in the sector which this measure is intended to produce.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this supplementary report on the interchange fees for card-based payment transactions because i think that we need legal clarity for eu citizens when they are paying with cards inside the european union.
in writing. ‒ interbank fees for card payments, paid by the cardholder's bank to the card issuing bank, are not transparent and differ across the eu. i voted in favour of this report today to ensure that the fees that banks charge retailers when they accept card payments are subject to ceilings. the limit will apply to both cross-border and domestic payments in order to reduce costs for debit and credit card users. this legislation, together with the forthcoming payment services directive, will create the same rules for all payments made in europe. it should improve the transparency of fees, stimulate competition and allow retailers and users to choose their card payment system on the most advantageous terms. the new rules mean that retailers who choose a payment card scheme will only be able to accept cards within that scheme that comply with the limits. in this case, the limits on fees will result in lower costs for both parties.
in writing. ‒ this regulation lays down uniform technical and commercial requirements within the union for card-based payment transactions where both the payer's payment service provider and the payee's payment service provider are located in the union. the intentions are certainly agreeable, but the text does not allow a full assessment of the practical effects of the measures introduced, as it does not go far enough into the analysis of the consequences themselves. i therefore decided to abstain, in order to show my interest in a measure such as the one under consideration while maintaining reservations about the text.
in writing. ‒ i considered that i would vote in favour of the measure as directive 2007/64/ec of the european parliament and of the council provided the legal basis for the creation of an internal market for payments in the union, as it substantially favoured the activity of service providers by providing uniform rules on the matter. today, payment cards are the most commonly used electronic instruments for retail purchases. there is a need to remove obstacles to the efficient functioning of payment cards, including in the area of card-based payments and payments via the internet and mobile devices based on cards. in addition to the uniform application of competition rules to interbank fees, the regulation of these fees would improve the functioning of the internal market and help to reduce transaction costs for consumers.
in writing. ‒ i am convinced that the removal of obstacles to the functioning of an integrated market for electronic payments is necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market, without any distinction between national and crossborder payments. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because it imposes common rules on interbank charges in the european union, introducing a maximum limit on payment card transactions. payment cards have become the most commonly used electronic payment instruments for retail purchases, so i believe that the regulation of interchange fees will improve the functioning of the internal market and help to reduce transaction costs for consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on interbank card payment charges. the text adopted sets a ceiling on interbank fees for payment transactions with debit and consumer credit cards (i.e. used by cardholders who are also consumers) of 0.2% and 0.3% respectively, to be calculated on the value of the transaction. the aim of this proposal is to prevent an unjustified variation in the level of these fees, since they are included in the costs incurred by the operator in the form of price increases, for receiving payments by debit or credit card. therefore, applying only to the most widespread 4-part circuits would, on the one hand, protect consumers by reducing prices and, on the other hand, prevent the creation of barriers between national payment markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of ending the cost of fees that banks charge retailers when they accept card payments. they will be subject to ceilings, thanks to new eu-wide rules. the limit will apply to both cross-border and domestic payments and should reduce costs for debit and credit card users. the vote and the payment services directive will create a single set of rules for all payments made in europe. it should improve the transparency of fees, encourage competition and allow merchants and customers to choose their card payment system on the most advantageous terms.
in writing. ‒ the number of non-cash transactions in the market is often considered as an indicator of a country's economic development. today in this room we have taken a step forward in building the most developed international platform in this field. together with the digital agenda, the regulation on interbank card payment charges is an indication of parliament's focus on building an innovative european platform for a strengthened single market. we have removed the barriers which today prevent further market integration and this will help to have a positive effect on our economy. we have also focused our attention on the main problems connected with this market. firstly, we have harmonized legislation at european level, avoiding the creation of shadow zones and of national markets which are more competitive than others. secondly, we have prevented high interbank fees from translating into higher final prices for consumers, by means of a system of maximum and minimum thresholds. i therefore voted with conviction for this text because it protects not only our consumers but also small retailers, as well as small and mediumsized enterprises in our territory.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of a legislative proposal which, compared with what the european commission initially presented, has now reached the end of a much improved legislative process. after lengthy negotiations, a much more balanced solution was reached, setting maximum values and leaving the member states free to intervene with further cuts in domestic transactions.
in writing. ‒ with today's vote, the european parliament has finally shown that it is able to stand by its citizens. interbank fees have for too long been a hidden cost to consumers as well as to traders, breaching antitrust rules, as the eu court of justice ruled last september. this regulation puts an end to the abuses of certain banks and sets limits on them, introducing a more transparent mechanism which balances the needs of the free market with those of the protection of the interests of consumers and traders. for these reasons i voted in favour of this proposal, hoping that this regulation will mark a new beginning in the direction of a european union which is increasingly at the side of the citizens and protecting their interests.
in writing. i vote in favour of the proposal for a regulation on interbank fees for payment transactions made by credit card, atm, online or by telephone applications. therefore, in line with the views of the european central bank and the european economic and social committee, and in view of the problems that the fragmentation of the internal market can cause for competitiveness and the fact that a single, controlled, effective and secure regulation would reassure traders against the risks of paying too high commissions on sales and at the same time encourage consumers to use electronic money for a physiological reduction in costs, i would like to express my support for setting a certain ceiling within the union, harmonizing and controlling interbank commissions, with the necessary adjustment periods for the member states, for a paneuropean market that is not limited by territorial restrictions, capable of technical interoperability between the different processing systems in the union and at the same time more open and also more stimulating for free purchasing.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the report by mr pablo zalba bidegain. the proposal for a regulation aims to improve the conditions for the functioning and development of the internal market in payments. the removal of direct and indirect obstacles to the functioning of an integrated market for electronic payments is necessary for the proper functioning of the european internal market.
in writing. ladies and gentlemen, this regulation, combined with the revised proposals of the payment services directives will create common rules for interchange fees in the european union by introducing a minimum level of fees for credit card payment transactions. it will also introduce transparency measures to allow retailers and consumers to choose their payment methods more clearly. the introduction of this regulation will limit the fixed costs that banks impose on sellers to process payments. the proposed rules aim to increase transparency, stimulate competition and allow both sellers and customers to choose the card scheme that offers them the best conditions.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, the european union has seen a fragmentation of its internal market. the proper functioning of the european internal market requires work to remove the direct and indirect obstacles to the full efficiency of electronic payments. i voted in favour of the bidegain report because it aims to improve the conditions for the functioning and development of the internal market in payments.
in writing. ‒ the adoption of this proposal is a further instrument for removing direct and indirect obstacles to the functioning and completion of the eu internal market. in this case, our aim is to promote the creation of an integrated market for electronic payments, without any distinction between national and crossborder payments. we are, unfortunately, fully aware of the damage that fragmentation of the internal market is doing to competitiveness, growth and job creation in the union. in order for consumers, merchants and businesses to fully enjoy the benefits of the internal market, it is essential that the electronic payments they use are secure, efficient, competitive and innovative. in order to ensure greater legal certainty, as administrative decisions in force in some member states often vary significantly from one another, it is necessary to find a way of more uniformising the levels of interbank fees. in addition to the uniform application of competition rules to interchange fees, the regulation of such fees would improve the functioning of the internal market and help reduce transaction costs for european consumers.
in writing. ‒ in an era of increasingly widespread card payments, a business model still prevails that favours the emergence of multilateral interbank fees (mifs) and that, by impacting on retailers' costs, ultimately affects prices charged to consumers. the regulation set out in the report proposes to introduce ceilings for the fees charged to consumers for transactions with debit and credit cards and prohibits the application of surcharges for these types of cards. surcharges are commonly used, particularly when buying air tickets. the caps on interbank fees will reduce the cost of card transactions at the expense of retailers considerably and will therefore eliminate the motivation behind the surcharges. as the proposed regulation will improve the conditions for the functioning and development of the internal market for payments and will promote greater consumer protection, i have decided to support the report with a favourable vote.
in writing. ‒ whereas the fragmentation of the internal market is detrimental to competitiveness, growth and job creation in the union; whereas the removal of direct and indirect obstacles to the proper functioning and completion of an integrated market for electronic payments, without distinction between national and cross-border payments, is necessary for the proper functioning of the internal market; whereas directive 2007/64/ec of the european parliament and of the council (8) provided the legal basis for the creation of an internal market for payments in the union, as it substantially favoured the activity of payment service providers by providing uniform rules on the provision of payment services, for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ it is to protect consumers that i am in favour of adopting this resolution which allows for the regulation of interbank transaction fees in a uniform and coordinated way at european level. for the internal market to work, we must ensure that the direct and indirect obstacles to the functioning and completion of an integrated market for electronic payments are reduced by eliminating the distinction between national and cross-border payments. applying european competition rules to interbank fees will improve the functioning of the internal market but above all will reduce transaction costs, to the benefit of all european citizens. it is also important that member states lay down penalties applicable to infringements of the regulation, ensuring that those penalties are effective and dissuasive and that they are enforced.
in writing. ‒ in the internal market of the european union, it is important that there are no barriers to the smooth functioning of transactions carried out electronically, without distinguishing between national and cross-border payments, with uniform rules in the way of payment services. of course, all users of electronic payments in the single market - consumers, merchants and businesses - need to know that they can make them safely, efficiently and quickly, now that electronic commerce is becoming more widespread. in order to facilitate the smooth functioning of the internal market and card-based payments, it is appropriate that interchange fees be uniform, whether they are minimal or zero. it would also be interesting if the commission were to provide a report examining the effects of this regulation on the internal market and the benefits it brings to trade.

in writing. the mif regulation will introduce a cap on interbank fees paid to banks by merchants for credit and debit card payments for the first time in europe. the regulation has aroused great enthusiasm but it does in fact conceal some areas of shadow and some critical points. the regulation does not apply to commercial cards, cash withdrawals and payments made through certain payment systems (such as american express, diners and paypal) where the service is operated by a single bank for each consumer and merchant. these derogations exclude a large market share from the regulation and make the legislation incomplete. to be effective and efficient, it would have been appropriate to include all payment systems and all cards. in the long term, it is possible that these exemptions will have a boomerang effect on consumers. in fact, it is very likely that the losses that banks will suffer as a result of the introduction of the ceilings will be offset by charges to consumers. this is supported by the recent spanish experience of roofing at national level. the regulation was negotiated during the previous legislature and therefore m5s did not have enough room to make significant changes. therefore, m5s chose to abstain.

in writing. ‒ europe has set itself virtuous goals in the europe 2020 strategy, but some of these will only be achieved if there is real equality between men and women. i am referring, for example, to the 75% employment target which will only be reached in 2038 given that the growth in female employment since 2002 has been only 4%. these figures, among many others, show us that the world of work is still hostile to women, especially when we consider that they represent as much as 60% of european graduates and yet they receive a remuneration that is calculated to reach full equality with that of men only in 2084 (equivalence that would lead to an increase in eu gdp of as much as 12%) with drastic consequences also on their pensions, which we know to be 39% lower than those of men. this is all just talking about the world of work, but there are many other areas where we can see a serious gender gap. i therefore vote in favour of this text because it seems to highlight the importance of achieving real equality between men and women for the growth of europe, including economic growth.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the 2013 annual report of the european central bank. the fragmentation of financial markets remains a key problem holding back the development of the economy and smes. the cost to the real economy of these imbalances is no longer sustainable, as are the distortions of the single market. with specific reference to financial stability, i welcome the new phase that has opened with the full operation of the single supervisory mechanism (ssm) entrusted to the ecb since november 2014. on monetary policy, i can only agree with the ecb's reactive impulse in the face of the critical situation. i also note with satisfaction that the ecb is proceeding with the purchase of asset-backed securities (abs) and covered bonds to support the credit easing effect of the lmtos, stressing that this is important in creating the conditions for a recovery in investment and the real economy.
in writing. ‒ to develop a truly effective monetary policy, a complete restructuring of the banking system, separating credit from finance, would be necessary in order to return the system to its true function, that of guaranteeing credit to the real economy. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget. its deflation-fighting measures are not sufficient in a context of austerity, however, where fiscal constraints and financial stability continue to outweigh the real needs of the real economy and citizens. the quantitative easing recently promoted by the ecb is certainly not a sufficient measure in this respect and my vote on the annual report is therefore negative.
in writing. ‒ i thought i would vote in favour of the measure, although i do not deny concerns about the continuing fall in the inflation rate since 2011 and the different inflation rates across all member states. monetary policy aimed at reducing tensions in the various financial markets seeks to restore confidence among the various investors in the single currency. i was optimistic about the ecb's reaction to such a critical situation. the overall positive reduction in long-term national yields in the more indebted countries suggests a more dynamic economic recovery. the ecb's positive vision and actions in a situation of both low economic growth and continuing inflation should be taken into account and motivated to continue.
in writing. ‒ while not denying my concern about the continuing decline in the euro area inflation rate since 2011 and the differences in inflation rates between member states, i welcomed the ecb's swift reaction in the face of a highly critical environment such as the current one, and the fact that monetary policy has been geared to reducing the level of stress in the euro area financial markets and restoring investor confidence in the single currency. i am confident about the future economic recovery thanks to the general reduction in long-term national yields, particularly in the most indebted countries of the euro area, which have fallen to unprecedented levels since the beginning of the crisis. i therefore voted in favour of the european central bank's annual report for 2013, especially in the hope that the quantitative easing programme which has been in place in recent weeks will bear the fruit it hopes for.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the 2013 annual report of the european central bank as it provides a comprehensive overview of monetary policy actions aimed at attempting to reduce the level of stress in financial markets and to try to regain investor confidence. the fragmentation of financial markets and the high level of unemployment remain a key problem to be addressed by consolidating good governance. i believe it is of the utmost importance to create a revival of public and private investment, to encourage the injection of liquidity into the system and to promote a fiscal union to have lower taxes and a more competitive market. all eu member states must commit to implementing appropriate structural reforms to restore a growth-friendly environment, safeguard price stability, promote sustainable social and economic progress and full employment, improve inclusion and optimise business conditions.
in writing. ‒ each year, the european parliament, in an own-initiative report, gives an assessment of the ecb's monetary policy. the report, which covers the ecb's 2013 annual report, also introduces a section on financial stability, in light of the ecb's new single supervisory function, which was introduced last november. the text contains numerous appreciations of the ecb's unconventional monetary policy interventions, and in particular the ltro programmes, the securitised asset purchase plan and the recent quantitative easing programme, as well as continuous references to the need to continue on the path of structural reforms and fiscal consolidation. in the econ committee, m5s voted against the report because it considered it unbalanced in highlighting only the positive side of the work of the ecb and the current system of economic governance. i find the total absence of critical reflection on the management of the eurozone crisis and an objective analysis of the negligible impact of monetary policy interventions on the real economy unacceptable. for the reasons stated above, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ the annual report of the european central bank is an important opportunity for reflection on economic and monetary policy within the european institutions. as regards monetary policy in 2013, the lowering of the reference rate and the start of unconventional monetary policies failed to boost growth in the continent. these measures have not led to the expected increase in credit to households and businesses, also due to austerity policies. today, we have the opportunity to learn from this lesson, and we can overcome this pattern, through a new european policy that looks at growth. to achieve this, the european institutions must be more committed to promoting long-term investment in a social and environmental dimension. i therefore consider the report to be a balanced text, emphasizing the social dimension of the economy and the need for greater growth in europe.

in writing. ‒ by adopting this annual report, we want to underline the importance of the ecb's rapid reaction in the face of an increasingly unstable and fragmented economic and financial environment. while we believe that it is essential to use this new monetary policy stance to reduce the level of tension in the euro area financial markets and to restore investor confidence in the single currency, we believe that the expansionary approach alone is not enough to resolve the situation. the right mix of fiscal consolidation policies, appropriate structural reforms and stimulation of new private investment will be essential. we also believe that, in view of the prospect of further accommodative policies such as quantitative easing, and bearing in mind the current legal challenges related to the omt programme, it is essential to ensure clarity and legal certainty in order for these instruments to be implemented effectively. finally, we urge the member states to create the conditions for a recovery in both public and private investment by implementing appropriate structural reforms to restore a business-friendly environment.

in writing. ‒ the 2013 annual report of the european central bank, in the preparation of which i had the opportunity to participate directly as shadow rapporteur for the s&d group, is the instrument through which the ecb's accountability to the european parliament is made explicit. the european central bank, which is independent by its very nature, is subject, by virtue of its statute, to a constant dialogue with the european parliament, which assesses its actions. in recent months, the european central bank has taken on a central role in countering the serious effects of the severe economic and financial crisis in europe. the numerous measures taken, some of which were considered "unconventional" for a central bank, although they did not lead to the desired recovery, prevented the collapse of the continental banking system and helped to create a climate of confidence in international markets, with the resulting lowering of the financing costs for the peripheral euro area states. the report highlights these achievements, while also highlighting the many challenges still to be addressed, including the low inflation and high unemployment that still characterize the euro area. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the 2013 annual report of the european central bank.
in writing. the resolution on the ecb's annual report does not contain a genuine critical analysis of the way in which the monetary policy instrument was used in managing the euro area crisis. the resolution fails to highlight, for example, that the measures taken by the ecb have had no significant impact on inflation and the recovery of the real economy. it also fails to highlight the enormous risks that the surge of liquidity provided to banks through the various programmes, from ltros to quantitative easing, will remain trapped in the business of finance, fuelling speculative bubbles and financial instability. in the absence of clear constraints and conditionality, banks obviously find it more cost-effective to reinvest cash in government securities and derivatives rather than using it to lend to households and small and medium-sized enterprises. the solution chosen by the ecb was 'more liquidity', whereas we propose a clear, simple and mandatory separation between traditional credit and speculative financial activities, a reform which is increasingly urgent and necessary to restore a sound and prudent credit transmission mechanism. because of these unacceptable shortcomings and the overly complacent assessment, i have therefore decided not to support this resolution.

member of the commission.– madam president, thank you for this interesting debate. it reflects the great importance the union continues to attach to the credibility of the enlargement process, which remains crucial for maintaining the momentum of reforms and public support for enlargement in the region and in serbia in particular. i take note of the discussion on serbia’s law on the organisation and competence of state authorities in war crimes proceedings. i fully understand the sensitivities of this matter and i believe that serbia and its neighbours need to look to the future in a spirit of regional cooperation and reconciliation. i take this opportunity to underline that effective and impartial handling of war crimes, in line with international standards, features high in the accession negotiations with serbia. it is covered by the specific recommendations in the screening report in chapter 23 about the judiciary and fundamental rights, stressing the need for efficient deterrent and impartial treatment of war crimes, equal treatment of suspects, and proportionality of sentences and protection of victims. all these recommendations will have to be addressed in the judiciary section of the action plan required for the opening of chapter 23. the commission is actively involved in the preparation of this action plan and is committed to reviewing the measures undertaken by serbia in this respect and in this framework. once again thank you for this very interesting debate. i would also again like to thank the author mr mcallister and his colleagues for this very balanced report.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i shall take a minute to list the four main causes of this crisis. firstly, the different policies pursued by the member states which then lead to fiscal dumping, social dumping. the council is full of hypocrisy and should make a move. two, the euro, a fixed exchange rate bond between nineteen different countries, which is boosting german exports: 217 billion surplus, 7% in 2014 and it's not the first year. we apply the rules to the strong, not just the weak. depressive fiscal policies that kill and depress weak economies; the european central bank's monetary policies are not designed to support the thousands of micro-enterprises that are failing in some countries, but to support the strategic plans of banks and lobbyists to do business and share the market. you should be ashamed of these things.
the debate is closed. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
