in writing. ‒ the rapporteur, andrzej duda, calls on the european parliament to lift the parliamentary immunity of bulgarian mep sergei stanishev (s&d) following the request of the chief prosecutor of bulgaria of 24 november 2014. the request for the waiver of parliamentary immunity is part of a criminal investigation into stanisev's disclosure of information covered by the state secret entrusted to him when he was prime minister of the republic of bulgaria. on the basis of the facts and circumstances described and the evidence gathered in the case, sergei stanishev is accused of having lost the above-mentioned documents, i.e. of having inadvertently lost control of them for non-compliance with the procedures for safekeeping, transfer and circulation of documents defined in the relevant implementing rules and in the internal rules of the council of ministers for the processing of classified information. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally sensitive products. there are therefore no grounds for opposing this and i am voting in favour of the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr sergei stanishev.
in writing. ‒ with regard to the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of sergei stanishev, considering the nature of the matter, i am in favour of a waiver of the immunity. what happened in this particular case is not a matter of duties or opinions connected with the office of member of the european parliament and therefore excludes the possibility of article 8 of the protocol being applicable. furthermore, parliament found no evidence of fumus persecutionis, i.e. a sufficiently well-founded and precise suspicion that the action was aimed at causing political damage to the member.
in writing. ‒ mr sergei stanishev has been accused of having lost, in the course of his duties as prime minister of the republic of bulgaria, seven documents containing information considered to be state secrets between 4 november 2005 and 27 july 2009. specifically, mr stanishev is alleged to have forwarded these documents in violation of the rules in force. given that the alleged offence in question is not directly connected with the performance of sergei stanishev's duties as a member of the european parliament and does not concern an opinion or a vote expressed in the exercise of his parliamentary prerogatives, i have decided to support the duda report, which calls for the waiver of his immunity.
in writing. ‒ sergei stanishev is accused of having lost, in the exercise of his functions as prime minister of the republic of bulgaria, seven documents containing information considered to be state secrets. this behaviour constitutes an offence punishable under article 358 (1) of the bulgarian criminal code. in accordance with article 9 of protocol no 7 on eu privileges and immunities, members of the european parliament enjoy the same immunities on their national territory as members of their country and, in accordance with article 70 of the bulgarian constitution, a member may not be subject to criminal prosecution, arrest or detention during the course of a parliamentary term without the consent of the parliament. in the light of the above, i have decided to support mr duda's request as the alleged offence has no connection with mr stanishev's position as a member of the european parliament. the crime is linked to his previous position as prime minister. moreover, there is no reason to assume that the proceedings are based on the intention to prejudice the political activity of the member (fumus persecutionis), as they were initiated several years before the beginning of the european mandate.
in writing. ‒ whereas the chief prosecutor of the republic of bulgaria has forwarded the request of the sofia city prosecutor's office to allow the prosecution of sergei stanishev for an offence under article 358 (1) in conjunction with article 26 (1) of the bulgarian criminal code; that the alleged offence in question has no direct or obvious connection with the performance of the duties of sergei stanishev as a member of the european parliament and does not concern an opinion or vote expressed in the performance of his parliamentary duties in accordance with article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union; i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the investigation, but that it should be involved in the investigation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the waiver of immunity in this case as well, because the inquiry against sergei stanishev was opened well before he began his term as a member of the european parliament and it cannot be linked to his position as a member of the european parliament. the accusation relates to a period prior to his election as an mep, when sergei stanishev was serving as prime minister of bulgaria. at that time, sergei stanishev had sent the president of the national assembly two written statements in which he gave his consent to the initiation of criminal proceedings against him in accordance with the provisions of the constitution of the republic of bulgaria.

in writing. ‒ the eu budget is the only item for investments and for financing programmes and projects that would not otherwise be possible. it provides for strategic investments that reduce inequalities in development and macroeconomic data. that's the theory. in practice, we are faced with the continuation of a phenomenon which is harmful to local economies, such as the exponential growth of the differential between commitments and payments. the budget can only return to an active and positive role if a realignment is restored and if all previous amounts are paid off. the member states are therefore responsible for the difficulties encountered in implementing programmes and funds, with the european citizens, both the beneficiaries and the companies, being the first to suffer. the 2014 budget was a record year for unpaid invoices, which could pale in the face of the risk that, coinciding with the end of the 2007-2013 programming period, there would be an unprecedented surge in payment requests. the risk of work and programmes being blocked is very high and the solution cannot be - as is also assumed - the untying of sums, but their rationalisation towards segments that guarantee absorption and positive results.

in writing. ‒ ladies and gentlemen, whereas the fight against fraud, corruption and money laundering in the union must be a priority of the political action of the institutions and whereas judicial and police cooperation between member states is essential to this end. in view of the alarming increase in the number of irregularities reported as fraud in relation to european union spending,i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i generally agree with the contents of the report on the fight against fraud and i think it is right that the member states' behaviour on reporting fraud to olaf (european anti-fraud office) should be homogenized. the possible measure of rewarding those member states which have a high performance in this fight can also be a valuable incentive. we must promote ever more effective and effective measures to combat fraud, particularly when we are talking about large-scale transnational fraud. i believe that this requires an efficient system of information exchange between the competent authorities of the member states and increased cooperation with third countries, all under the supervision and coordination of olaf.
in writing. ‒ the fight against frostbite is also a problem faced at community level. the report calls for measures to protect the commission's financial interests, together with other rules to encourage greater transparency by the member states. that is why i voted in favour of mr pirinski's report.
in writing. i decided to vote in favour because the text drawn up by the committee on budgetary control provides a fairly comprehensive analysis of the situation in the year in question and mentions the need for greater and better cooperation between the european institutions and the member states to protect the financial interests of the union (especially at this stage of economic constraints for the member states).
in writing. ‒ i strongly support the european commission's argument that the increase in fraud in 2013 is above all an indication of a better system for monitoring and detecting irregularities in the eu. however, i believe that much more needs to be done to ensure a uniform interpretation of the concept of fraud and to harmonise fraud reporting procedures at european level. only by coordinating the member states' anti-fraud measures more effectively and in a structured manner can we ensure sound management of the funds and thus protect the financial interests of the european union.
in writing. the report shows that there is still a long way to go to ensure that the eu's financial interests are properly protected. i am referring in particular to the need for a policy of transparency which is lacking both in the eib's financing and in the traceability of european funds transactions. i am glad that our amendment on the question of the meester's pass has been adopted: we want to show that we are in the front line against those who fight for healthy and transparent spending. the eib is proving that it does not protect investments from the abuses and tentacles of organised crime. in this respect, i am concerned that the new juncker plan does not seem to take account of these problems, and i would remind you how effective supervision can be achieved by a proper policy of transparency. we call on the member states to make an extra effort to ensure that the protection and use of european funds is transparent, and we urge the commission to create an effective network of law and protection.

in writing. ‒ the abuse and exploitation of children is one of the most flagrant violations of fundamental rights, as it is perpetrated against human beings who are by nature innocent and defenceless. the use of the internet has not only allowed the problem to become more acute - putting children at greater risk of online harassment by cybercriminals - but has also given this phenomenon a transnational dimension, which necessarily requires a solution of equal scope. the search for a more effective strategy for the protection of children's rights must involve increased cooperation and include the exchange of best practices between member states. i am therefore voting in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the sexual abuse of children online, because i believe that only a coordinated approach at european level between institutional bodies, civil society and companies operating in the information technology and social media sectors can result in improved measures to prevent, combat and respond to such violations.
in writing. ‒ whereas children are the most vulnerable group in our society and the legislator must pay particular attention to them in order to protect them; that particular attention should be paid to the correct use of terminology relating to the sexual exploitation of children in communication to the public; takes note that the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european union for the financial year 2012, has stated that it has obtained reasonable assurances that the underlying transactions are legal and regular; calls on the commission and the member states to promote and strengthen the resources dedicated to victim identification and victim-centred services, urging the rapid establishment of platforms and strengthening existing ones within europol; stresses, moreover, the urgent need to improve assistance to child victims of abuse through personalised recovery and reintegration programmes; calls on the member states to implement directive 2012/29/eu establishing minimum standards on the rights, assistance and protection of victims of crime. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the fact that the important resolution on combating the sexual abuse of children online was adopted by a very large majority. the protection of children and the obligation to provide them with a safe environment for their development must be one of the eu's priority objectives. this is why we must act with utmost firmness and effectiveness in taking measures to ensure that any illegal content posted online is removed and reported to the competent authorities and that adequate legal means are available to investigate the perpetrators of the offences. to achieve the best results, it is essential that there is better international cooperation and that transnational investigations can be carried out effectively with appropriate agreements. i hope that directive 2011/93/eu on combating the sexual abuse and exploitation of children and child pornography will be transposed as soon as possible by all member states and that the commission will monitor its full and complete implementation.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it is free from criticism and is the best of the proposals put forward by the various political groups. the committee also calls for greater cooperation between the various authorities in the member states and europol, including the rapid removal of content on the internet which is harmful to children. in addition, there are references to the need to combat the sexual exploitation of children.
in writing. ‒ in the resolution voted in strasbourg today, we called for further efforts to tackle online sexual abuse of children, prosecute the perpetrators, protect the victims and remove illegal content from the internet. the data provided by ngos on internet pages containing material concerning child abuse is chilling; 80% of the victims are under the age of ten. unfortunately, the prevention measures adopted by the member states so far have not always been effective, which is why a more global approach is needed, and international cooperation and transnational investigations must be strengthened, since each country has different laws on the matter. there is certainly a need for more education and awareness-raising among children about the potential risks of the network, and for measures to ensure that the social media sector takes its share of responsibility.
in writing. ‒ i am very pleased with today's vote. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of minors against sexual exploitation. we must not forget that children are the most sensitive and vulnerable group in our society and it is our duty to protect them from the dangers of the internet and new technologies. in particular, i believe it is essential to stress the need for all parts of directive 2011/93/eu on combating the sexual abuse and exploitation of children to be transposed by all member states, as it is no longer acceptable or justifiable that more than half of them have not yet done so. consistent and comprehensive policies are needed that lead to effective results and involve, in close synergy, national law enforcement agencies, europol and the service providers themselves.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament's report on human rights is an important tool for assessing the policies of the european union. i would like to stress at the outset the important work done by the special representative. we have chosen a thematic approach to this report rather than a geographical one, and we think it is very useful because it sets out some guidelines on which to base the european parliament, the european commission itself and the individual commissioners in their policies. ladies and gentlemen, in 1872 a small classic of legal liberalism appeared in vienna, the struggle for right, by rudolf von jhering, which was republished as an antibody to the years of fascism in my country by benedetto croce. today it is certainly more appropriate to speak of the struggle for rights, which extends from the defence of social and civil rights to the protests of young people in hong kong and which can be summed up in the words of hannah arendt, the "right to have rights". but to avoid this being just a slogan, we must remember that phrase in its entirety: "the right to have rights, or the right of every individual to belong to humanity, should be guaranteed by humanity itself". it is quite clear that the construction of rights is thus a challenge and requires a policy of humanity, the opposite of that policy of disgust which some have spoken of in the case of discrimination against homosexuals, but which we find in too many cases of rejection of the other. in our time, rights are being presented as a luxury incompatible with the economic crisis, the decline in financial resources and the need for internal stability in some countries - i am thinking of our neighbouring countries. but i wonder: the moment the promise of rights is not fulfilled or is removed, what are we saying goodbye to? when you restrict rights to work, health, education, civil rights, you are undermining the very foundations of a democracy. it is not rights that are insatiable: the problem is the claim of the economy to determine what rights are compatible with it. so reflection on rights brings us to the heart of a cultural debate that goes beyond contingency and reveals how references to the economic crisis and the new geopolitics have only made more evident a much deeper transformation and conflict, which concern the very way in which we should look at the evolution of our societies, of the global society itself. the report is intended to send a simple message: rights do not invade democracy but require us to reflect on how political discretion should be exercised: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. so there's a lot to do, and ultimately i think europe's job is to rise to the challenge, to show the consistency that's needed to really win this human rights challenge everywhere.

in writing. the panzeri report contains many inaccuracies, first and foremost the reference in paragraph 136 which calls on the member states of the european union to recognize the right to abortion under legal and secure conditions. the afet committee, of which i am a member and which voted on this report, has no jurisdiction over the member states of the union, but only over third countries. this paragraph should not have even been included in the final text of the report. furthermore, under the principle of subsidiarity, the possibility of abortion is a matter for the member states and the european union cannot interfere in the policies of the member states in this area. but that's not the only inconsistency. in fact, there are also valuable assessments of the same-sex marriage referendums that took place in 2014 and 2015 in slovakia, croatia and lithuania, references that cannot be taken into account as the panzeri report deals with human rights and democracy in the world in 2013. my impression is that they wanted to insert the issue of abortion and gay marriage at all costs, even where it had nothing to do with it, in order to set precedents, which, as far as i am concerned, i cannot accept.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted with conviction in favour of the resolution on the sexual abuse of children online. the horrific images of child abuse circulating on the internet, operated by unscrupulous criminals, constitute serious violations of fundamental rights enshrined in the united nations convention on the rights of the child and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the data provided by ngos on internet pages containing child abuse material is chilling: 80% of the victims are under the age of 10. unfortunately, the preventive measures taken by the member states so far have not always been effective. in order to combat the digital penetration of children, it is necessary to ensure that any illegal content is promptly removed and reported to law enforcement authorities, but they must be provided with appropriate legal tools to investigate and prosecute offenders. the international dimension of the phenomenon therefore requires a coordinated and global european approach, starting with greater education and awareness of minors about the potential risks of the network and measures that commit the social media sector to assume its share of responsibility.

in writing. ‒ the current transformation of the political order at world level has made the european union particularly vulnerable to phenomena such as terrorism, arms and drug trafficking and human trafficking. recognising the seriousness of this situation, i have decided to support the report by mr brok, a document which encourages the community institutions and the member states to take a proactive stance in defining a community foreign and security policy, aimed at safeguarding the security of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ we once again regret that the european union is not able to use its full potential to shape the international political and security environment. the lack of coordination and coherence between the eu's internal and external policies, exacerbated by recent financial constraints, further limits europe's influence in the world and its capacity to act as a guarantor of regional and global security, contributing to conflict prevention and crisis management. the eu will only be a credible actor if we are able to have a shared vision of key interests, values and objectives in external relations. we need common, strengthened and combined political, economic, financial and defence resources to maximise the eu's influence in the world, to produce synergies and to ensure peace and stability in europe and its neighbourhood. the community institutions and the member states can now make full use of the instruments provided for by the lisbon treaty to move from a hitherto mainly reactive approach to a proactive, coherent and strategic eu foreign and security policy, based on common values and in the common european interest.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr brok's report, which sets out a framework for evaluating the common european foreign and security policy. more specifically, it provides a set of recommendations to improve it in the light of the new challenges and threats facing the union. the eu has not yet been able to use its full potential to map the international political and security environment. in addition, the lack of coordination and coherence between community policies, as well as financial constraints, place further constraints on europe's influence in the world and its capacity to act as a guarantor of regional and global security, contributing to the prevention and management of conflicts. the report therefore reiterates the need to reform the internal workings of the european external action service in order to better assist the high representative and stresses the need to further rationalise the structure to provide a greater capacity for monitoring and responding to crises.
in writing. ‒ whereas, due to the dramatic deterioration of the security environment across the eu, the international law-based order, stability and security of europe is being called upon at levels unprecedented since the beginning of european integration, which highlights the ongoing transformation of the world political order; that an ambitious and effective union foreign policy must be based on a shared vision of key european interests, values and objectives in external relations, as well as on a common perception of threats to the eu as a whole; that a process of strategic reflection on the eu's foreign and security policy needs to be launched as a matter of priority; the european council in madrid, in the light of the recent developments, has decided that a new european security strategy is needed, one which takes account of the recent geopolitical changes and can therefore provide a response to new challenges and threats. i voted in favour of this.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that, given the current situation, the work of the high representative in the field of foreign and security policy is crucial, and parliament believes that the priorities should be multifaceted and aimed at reaffirming the eu's role as a global actor. we must first of all protect european values and interests by respecting the political and legal order of europe, and also improve territorial defence to protect member states from terrorist attacks and organised crime. it is necessary to promote and foster security, democracy and economic development in third countries, especially those bordering the eu, by taking a leading role in conflict resolution and in strengthening the global political, economic and financial order. we also call for the financial assistance for external action provided by the eu and its member states to be reoriented and used more effectively. this assistance should be directed to civil society and ngos working in the field, including by easing red tape so that funding projects can be adopted more quickly.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the brok report because it deals with the transformation of the eu into an armed and, if necessary, belligerent political entity which, not having its own strategies, adopts those of third countries. i think it is worrying that the geopolitical nature of ttip is being emphasized in this context. the eu was born as a peaceful community to overcome the horrors and divisions of the second world war. it must remain so. if the security of the eu has deteriorated, this is also (and in many cases above all) the effect of the disastrous and counterproductive eu policies towards its eastern and southern neighbours. in particular, the eu's strategy of providing 'aid' to third countries to the extent that they adopt the european economic model can be seen as a form of economic and cultural colonialism and diverts public money from the needs of european citizens already impoverished by unnecessary and harmful austerity policies.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world in 2013 and on the european union's policy on the matter. it is based on the view that the treaty of lisbon has strengthened the european union's commitment on the international scene. this document is inspired by the principles of democracy and the rule of law, upholding the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms, respect for human dignity, and the principles of equality and solidarity. in this context, i would like to emphasize the attention paid to the european union's action on migration and refugees. in this respect, i believe that more effective policies need to be developed to address the urgent issues connected with them and that this impetus should be given in a manner consistent with international law on human rights and fundamental human dignity. as i have said in other speeches on this subject, the building of a european area of rights which is genuinely inclusive in its complexity, and not just a geographical boundary, is an element which should be a priority on the agenda of the community institutions and the member states.
in writing. ‒ human rights and democracy are founding values of the european union, at the heart of its actions and policies. the european parliament's human rights report is an important tool for assessing the union's human rights intervention in third countries and their situation. it monitors the implementation of the strategic framework of the european union action plan on human rights and democracy. the thematic rather than geographical approach, which is new in the report, is, in my view, a modification which makes it possible to give a better idea of the problems. i voted in favour and we will ensure that the union's action in this area is actually based on the data collected.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament must ensure that human rights and democracy are at the heart of its actions and policies. the european parliament's human rights report is an important tool for assessing both eu human rights policies and the situation in third countries. it is a tool through which we can check the state of implementation of the strategic framework of the european union's action plan on human rights and democracy. the significant novelty of this report compared to previous ones is that it is thematic rather than geographical in nature, grouping the different human rights considerations into broad thematic areas rather than on a geographical/regional basis. i voted yes. i would like to stress that if these reports and votes are not to remain mere words on paper, the issues raised in parliament's urgent resolutions must be given institutional follow-up.
in writing. ‒ this is a sensitive and important report, whose adoption marks a new milestone in the union's ability to be at the forefront, not only in defence but also in promoting fundamental values such as democracy and human rights. it is important that it be the union as such, since it represents the uniqueness of the states which compose it in identifying and delimiting the scope of the very concept of democracy and human rights, avoiding unilateral acts or interpretations which could give rise to political or ideological polemics. i would like to stress here the extraordinary weapon at europe's disposal: the european union is one of the most competitive, reliable and ambitious trading partners in the world. we often, and rightly so, grant preferential treatment to the least developed countries. it is essential that this aspect should not be completely dissociated from the promotion of democracy and human rights. the countries that want to have trade relations with europe and that receive favourable treatment from europe must embark on a path, properly shared and monitored, to achieve adequate standards of respect, protection and, in turn, promotion of rights and democracy.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the sustainable exploitation of the sprat because the state of the sprat stocks is worrying, despite the emergency measures already adopted by the commission and the national management measures to conserve the species. the species is a highly sought-after species in the fishing industry because of its high economic value and its fishing is therefore of interest to a considerable number of vessels. the replenishment of the spruce population requires a very long period, given the still very high mortality rate and the fact that spruce is a slow-growing and late-maturing species. i therefore believe that the exploitation of the sea bass during breeding seasons should be particularly limited as it visibly slows down the renewal of the stock and prevents its replenishment. the resolution adopted by parliament also had the merit of inviting the commission to propose a multiannual management plan for plaice which would allow stocks to be raised above levels capable of producing maximum sustainable yield, involving professional fishermen, recreational fishermen and advisory councils in the preparation of such a management plan.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1380/2013 of 11 december 2013 on the common fisheries policy provides that stocks are to be restored or maintained above levels capable of producing the maximum sustainable yield. several studies show that the state of the stock of sprat is alarming, despite the emergency measures already adopted by the european commission. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i support the need to put in place comprehensive measures to manage the bluefin tuna fishery at european level in order to safeguard this species. i am firmly convinced that these measures must also take account of scientific knowledge and promote proximity management and the principle of rationalization.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution banning pelagic trawl fishing for plaice during the breeding season because it is precisely this breeding phase that plaice is dependent on in the seas. targeted fishing on those spawning aggregations during the period in question contributes significantly to the reduction in the number of adult specimens able to reproduce successfully. i am concerned that the reproductive biomass of the stock is about to reach historically low levels, given that current fishing mortality is almost four times higher than the stock can sustain. i therefore believe that measures should be taken to reduce fishing mortality substantially.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution because the state of the stock of plaice in union waters is worrying. the lack of scientific studies on this species has led to the adoption of emergency measures by the commission, although these will expire in april this year. the committee on fisheries therefore felt it necessary to table this resolution, urging the commission to consider the possibility of introducing a quota tac system for this species and to accompany it with a multiannual resource management plan, in line with the guidelines of the new common fisheries policy (cfp). the resolution takes account of the need to take certain measures to repopulate the stock without underestimating two important factors: the importance of recreational fishing for this species (an estimated quarter of catches come from sport fishing) and its high commercial value.
in writing. ‒ i cannot fully support the report, since the only known measure is a strict closure of fishing activities. if the text improves, i shall be happy to give my full support to the report.
in writing. i supported the resolution on the sustainable exploitation of the coastline. it recalls many shared principles, including the need to identify measures for the management of the spiny lobster fishery in the european territory aimed at ensuring adequate protection of the species. the scientific literature shows that the state of the stock of spelt is worrying, despite the emergency measures already adopted by the european commission in this field.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the motion for a resolution on the sustainable exploitation of the coastline, as this is a subject which is linked to a number of priorities at european level. a multiannual management plan for plaice is needed to bring stocks above levels capable of producing maximum sustainable yield, taking care to have sufficient scientific data for the calculation. identifying a total allowable catch and having a minimum landing size is part of the criteria necessary to implement sustainable fishing. the technical measures are varied, as are the problems connected with discards at sea, but all of them are necessary for a practice consistent both with the need to manage fisheries efficiently at a regulatory level and to meet the needs of those who carry out the work and thus protect the image of the fisherman in the best possible way.
in writing. ‒ several scientific studies indicate that the current state of the stock of sprat is worrying, despite the fact that the european commission has already implemented emergency actions in this specific sector. this resolution, which i have supported, draws attention to the need to identify community measures for the management of the anchovy fishery in such a way as to ensure adequate protection for this marine species. i consider that action to be absolutely necessary and have therefore decided to vote in favour of this document.
in writing. ‒ national management measures for the european hake fishery have so far proved insufficient to maintain the species and have not solved the problems of sharing and access to resources. new regulatory measures are needed to promote the management of proximity and the principle of regionalisation. we are asking that these decisions be made with the involvement of all the parties concerned. we call on the commission and the member states to use the european fisheries fund, which provides funding for the collection of scientific data, and to propose a multiannual management plan in order to maintain the stock at a maximum sustainable level. we recall that multiannual management plans should be prepared under the codecision procedure, and we therefore expect the ep to be actively involved in the whole procedure. account should be taken of the different management measures for commercial fisheries, the establishment of a tac (total allowable catch) and the need for a scientifically sound decision on the minimum landing size, as well as possible spatial and temporal bans, with the resulting difficulties in calculating historical catches, allocating quotas at national level and covering recreational fishing activities.
in writing. ‒ the longline is a slow-growing, late-maturing species whose fishing mortality rate is currently four times higher than maximum sustainable yield levels. in view of the worrying state of this stock, which could be on the verge of collapse, the resolution considers that management measures for the european eel fishery are necessary in order to safeguard this species and calls on the commission to propose a multiannual management plan for the eel which would bring the stocks below maximum sustainable yield levels. in the light of the foregoing, i have decided to support the resolution.
in writing. ‒ whereas scientific information on the state of the stock of sprat, in particular the data available on the exact boundaries, migratory routes of the stock and the breeding grounds of the sprat, is insufficient; whereas the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices) identifies four types of anchovy stock: celtic/manx/north sea, bay of biscay, waters west of the iberian peninsula and west of scotland/ireland; whereas the plaice is a noble species in great demand in the fisheries industry; calls on the commission to propose a multiannual management plan for plaice to bring stocks above levels capable of producing maximum sustainable yield; stressing the need to involve professional fishermen, recreational fishermen and advisory councils in the development of this management plan; considering that a multiannual management plan for plaice focuses in particular on the introduction of a total allowable catch and on the need for a decision with a sound scientific basis as regards the minimum landing size and spatial-temporal prohibitions to protect reproduction, as well as other technical measures; i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on plaice because i believe that it is of fundamental importance for the conservation of fish stocks that there are clear management measures for plaice fishing at european level. i therefore think it is right that a multiannual plan for the management of the cod fishery should be drawn up, firstly to determine commercial fishing, with maximum catch quotas and indications on minimum size, to identify the periods for reproduction, renewal of the stock and its replenishment is of primary importance, and then recreational fishing indicating quantitative and temporal limitations. the ultimate objective must be good management of the exploitation of the sprat to maintain the stock at the highest possible levels.
in writing. i decided to abstain because the proposal's mechanism contains elements useful only for monitoring and collecting data on the health status of stocks, also mentioning the useful difference between the recreational and the commercial fishing sector. however, the 'spirit' of the measure is too broadly oriented towards a strict closure of fishing activities and appears to be a 'delegation in blank' to the commission, which can thus reject a regulation which risks, on the basis of partial technical assumptions, having a negative impact on the sector.
in writing. ‒ i did not intend to support the report on the eu's priorities for the un human rights council with my vote, because it goes beyond a mere list of principles, without offering concrete ideas for shared solutions; the european union is also unable to be as forceful in condemning islamic extremism as it was in dealing with the paris attack last january.
in writing. today i voted in favour of the resolution on the 28th session of the united nations human rights council (unhrc). i think that the resolution we have adopted is a valid one, and one which has the merit of touching on many of the issues which are dear to parliament. it stresses the importance of addressing growing inequalities in order to combat poverty in general and to promote social and economic rights, including facilitating access to food, water, education, healthcare and adequate housing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the resolution also condemns the misuse of religion by extremist and jihadist groups in all countries, in particular in syria, iraq, libya, myanmar/burma, nigeria and central africa. finally, i think it is very important to refer to women's rights and to condemn in the strongest possible terms all forms of violence against women.
in writing. ‒ the document under consideration is a good resolution, which addresses the issues of respect for human rights at global level. i therefore voted in favour, hoping that the directive and the information contained therein will not remain a dead letter. we often do not have the direct means to prevent violations in the world, but we can do so through different policies.
in writing. - the un does a great job but with limits. the european parliament should try to learn from the problems of the other supranational institutions, whereas in the case of this report i have seen some attempts to fall back on diplomatic games which block decision-making. the practice of name and shame is not very sensible when it comes to states, and it fosters hatred which magnifies the problems instead of solving them. my vote is motivated by a desire to take the opposite approach.
in writing. ‒ all human rights are indivisible, interrelated and interdependent. the lack of respect for human rights and the absence of legitimate democratic participation are the causes of instability, state failure, humanitarian crises and armed conflict. these are concepts that must be constantly reiterated and supported. that is why i voted in favour. with particular reference to individual human rights, which i consider interdependent, i spoke in favour of lgbti rights. in europe, attitudes towards homosexuality and transsexualism vary widely from country to country. in many european countries including belarus, georgia, lithuania, macedonia, moldova, russia, serbia and ukraine lgbti people are denied the right to freedom of expression, assembly and public demonstration. authorities in several countries promote intolerance and fear against lgbti communities who are discriminated against in law and practice. pride events have often been banned or participants have not been protected from violent disruption by homophobic groups. that is why it is important to keep the focus high on the point and i have indeed spoken in favour of the point.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the resolution because it does not offer any points of particular interest and merely lists principles and good intentions.
in writing. on the occasion of the european parliament resolution on the priorities of the union for the 28th session of the united nations human rights council in 2015, i have the pleasure to welcome with the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy the issues and urgencies identified and set as essential and determined policies for the european union and its member states. in the light of the european charter of human rights, but above all of the eu strategic and action framework for human rights and democracy of 25 june 2012, europe, as a symbol of the safeguarding of the universality of human rights, confirms its commitment with adequate funding and with all support measures at its disposal to promote the work of the united nations human rights council and the unhchr. it is essential in this context to encourage the participation and involvement of civil society in the protection of freedom of speech, religion and association and to strongly condemn the death penalty, torture, forms of discrimination and violence, exploitation and repression. europe must remain the symbol and guarantor of a solid and priority system based on values, dignity and democracy, and must be vigilant in the face of emergencies and fragility that still persist.

first vice-president of the commission.– mr president, honourable members, i only have a few remarks to make. first of all, i want to thank mr nuttall for devoting all the time he had today to the tragic events yesterday in france involving the germanwings aircraft. i think he spoke on behalf of all of us and i want to thank him warmly for that. secondly, many of the members of the european parliament have addressed the issue of the energy union today and i just want to start by saying there is a common thread between three of the main projects of this commission – the juncker plan, investment, the energy union and the digital single market. all three of them have as goals the creation of growth and jobs in europe and not to do this in a traditional way. because i believe that if europe thinks it can win in this enormous global competition on the basis of competition on wages or of competition on production costs europe will lose. europe can only win if it wins on innovation, if it wins on sustainability, if it wins on making an early transition into sustainable energy resources and sustainable social relations as well, because sustainability is about energy, it is about the economy and it is about social relations. i would like you to see these three projects connected to one another on that basis. i would like to underscore what has been said by many of your members that the energy union is obviously meant to protect us against blackmail from outside energy sources and producers. obviously it has a geopolitical importance but, apart from that, it also has the huge advantage of helping us in the transition – which is inevitable – to less dependency on fossil fuels and to a greater use of the huge potential of renewable energy, which does not only contribute to a better environment but which is also a driving force in innovation and creating a new form of jobs and a new form of productivity and a new form of economy for the european continent. very concretely on the questions regarding vat, this legislation has come into force recently but it was decided a long time ago. the commission is carefully evaluating it in a very pragmatic way and obviously the commission will never want this legislation to have adverse effects on small entrepreneurs who are very often at the cutting edge of creating new employment and creating new forms of business. we will very carefully evaluate the effects. if the effects are not the effects intended by the legislation, or simply not foreseen by the legislation at the time it was drafted because the economy has developed in the digital area in particular and developed far more quickly than we could have envisaged at the time seven years ago, or if there are adverse effects, then certainly the commission will take that into account. the two speakers on behalf of the ecr can therefore be assured that this has certainly been taken on board and that we had started on it before prime minister cameron raised the issue with us, but we certainly feel encouraged by the fact that he did.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (the egf, set up to provide additional support to workers who suffer from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade) which refers to the application submitted by ireland in relation to redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland (ltai). the irish authorities argue that the shift towards the production of next generation aircraft and components, the shift to larger scale methods in the production of aircraft components and the geographical relocation of worldwide aircraft production have had a negative impact on the business model on which ltai was based, resulting in its closure. the surpluses therefore appear to be linked to changes in the structure of world trade. i therefore voted in favour of this measure. i regret that italian companies are not able to benefit more from the egf because of the lack of support from local and national institutions which have submitted only 14 applications in total between 2007 and 2014.
in writing. ‒ the request to mobilise the fund was made following 424 redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd (ltai) and two of its suppliers in ireland. the southern and eastern region, which has important pockets of local disadvantage, is expected to be strongly affected by the redundancies. the region is characterised by a low level of education, a lack of vocational qualifications and high levels of public housing. the workers employed in this sector have very specific skills which are difficult to exploit in other sectors, which makes it even more difficult to re-position. the intervention measures will therefore be particularly focused on career guidance and career planning.
in writing. ‒ the effects on unemployment in recent years are not only linked to the economic and financial crisis, which is certainly responsible for most of the job losses, but also to the consequences of globalisation. this is the case for the irish branch of lufthansa technik airmotive, which has been affected by the change in the goods and services market in the production of aircraft and of next-generation components. if europe is to remain competitive, and above all if production is to remain within the union, not only european industrial policy but also the overall strategy must be reviewed to enable our companies to remain competitive on the international scene. i therefore voted in favour of the request from ireland to the european commission, which was also welcomed by the council's budget committee, to mobilise eur 2 490 758.
in writing. ‒ the measure we have examined includes the commission's proposal to examine lufthansa technik's application to mobilise the egf to support the reintegration of redundant workers. the request amounts to eur 2 490 758 for the irish state and provides for the redundancy of at least 500 workers over a reference period of four months. it should be recalled that the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support to workers who are affected by the consequences of major changes in the structure of world trade. the irish state considers that the closure of ltai is the result of a major change in eu trade in goods and services, due to a technological migration towards the production of next generation aircraft and components, the shift to large scale methods in the production of aircraft components, with consequent market repercussions of the business model on which ltai was based, and finally the geographical relocation of worldwide aircraft production. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mobilising the egf for ireland because i believe that the fund is useful in overcoming the period of adjustment following the structural changes in world trade due to globalisation. i believe that the 149 redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd (ltai) in the 'machinery and equipment repair and installation' sector in the 'southern and eastern' region of ireland are linked to these transformations, as demonstrated by the trend of us and western european carriers to send their wide-body aircraft to china for heavy maintenance and the fact that even the parent company lufthansa technik decided to base its global mro operations for the airbus a330/340 at its subsidiary lufthansa technik philippines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the request to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund egf/2014/016 ie/lufthansa technik for the following reasons. the application concerns 424 workers of lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd who were made redundant as a result of the economic crisis. the irish authorities will provide a range of personalised education or training services co-financed by the egf for up to 200 unemployed young people under the age of 25 at the time of application. these redundancies, because the skills of workers in this sector are very specific and not otherwise exploitable, will have a negative impact on the east and south of ireland, which is currently experiencing a difficult situation both from a microeconomic and vocational qualification point of view. in conclusion, all the conditions for access to the fund appear to be met, which in this case consist in the loss of jobs due to the economic crisis and a considerable economic damage to the regional economy.

in writing. - i voted for the repeal. the content of the criminal proceedings in question coincides with the procedure under which the european parliament decided to waive the parliamentary immunity of mr uspaskich back in 2010; the mp was sentenced in the first instance to 4 years in prison for alleged irregularities in the financing of the party he chaired. the case is pending at the second instance and the ep is asked to give its opinion, also following new elements brought forward by the defendant which, according to the rapporteur, do not seem to change the substance of the decision already taken.
in writing. ‒ the charges against my colleague viktor uspaskich do not relate to an opinion expressed in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament. however, during the committee's examination, serious doubts were raised as to his actual responsibility in the matter and as to a possible fumus persecutionis.
in writing. ‒ the text under discussion sets out the european parliament's reasons for requesting the waiver of the immunity of viktor uspaskich. on 15 september 2014, the president informed, in accordance with rule 9 (1), that he had received a letter from the prosecutor general of the republic of lithuania requesting the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr viktor uspaskich. the committee considered that the commission should be asked to take a decision to waive the immunity of mr uspaskich, considering that the charges clearly had nothing to do with his membership of the european parliament but were related to his position as party chairman. at the time, he was accused of organizing a criminal association to commit various crimes by operating illegally and evading the obligation to supervise the correctness of the financing of the party of which he was president. in fact, a sham accounting was used to conceal income and expenses. in general terms, he has repeatedly instructed the authorities not to register or declare officially several commercial and financial transactions. furthermore, there is no reason to suppose that a fumus persecutionis exists. for these reasons i thought i should vote in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to the request to waive the immunity of viktor uspaskich. in my opinion, he should continue to enjoy immunity. as a guarantor, i will always vote against these revocation requests. parliamentary immunity is not a personal privilege of the member but a guarantee of the independence of parliament as an institution and of its members.
in writing. ‒ the vilnius district court has initiated a criminal case against viktor uspaskich, which is still ongoing. the latter is accused of committing certain offences punishable under the provisions of the lithuanian criminal code. although viktor uspaskich was acquitted of some of the charges, he was sentenced, with a sentence not yet final, to 4 years in a penal institution. i have decided to support the regner report, which calls for the waiver of mr uspaskich's immunity, as the charges against him are not connected with his parliamentary duties.
in writing. ‒ whereas the charges against mr uspaskich are not linked to opinions or votes expressed in the course of his term of office as a member of the european parliament and therefore article 8 of the protocol does not apply; that, in accordance with article 9 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members shall enjoy, for the duration of the sessions of the european parliament, the immunities accorded to members of their national parliament on their national territory; that immunity cannot be invoked in the case of flagrant misconduct and may not, moreover, prejudice the right of the european parliament to waive the immunity of one of its members; that according to article 62 of the constitution of the republic of lithuania a member of the national parliament (seimas) may not be subject to criminal proceedings, detention or other restrictions of liberty without the approval of the seimas; decides to waive the immunity of viktor uspaskich and instructs its president to forward this decision and the report of its competent committee to the competent authorities of the republic of lithuania without delay. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i am against the prosecution of members for their opinions.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice of the european union has ruled that a statement made by a member of the european parliament outside the chambers of the european parliament may constitute an opinion expressed in the exercise of his parliamentary functions within the meaning of article 8 of the protocol on the privileges and immunities of the european union, taking account of the nature and content of the statement. however, the link between the opinion expressed by the member and parliamentary functions must be direct and must be clearly apparent. as the statements referred to were made by gabriele albertini in his capacity as mayor, i voted in favour of the report by mr andrzej duda.
in writing. ‒ the text under discussion sets out the european parliament's reasons for gabriele albertini's request for immunity to be upheld. the reason for this request can be found in the documentation: by summons dated 12 october 2012, gabriele albertini was summoned to appear before the brescia court by alfredo robledo in relation to the statements made by gabriele albertini in a first interview published by the newspaper il sole 24 ore on 26 october 2011 and in a second interview published by the newspaper corriere della sera on 19 february 2012. these statements offended the honour of the magistrate who was conducting the investigation at the time. the statements were made in his capacity as mayor of albertini, not as a member of the european parliament. furthermore, there is no reason to suppose that a fumus persecutionis exists. so the committee felt that it did not uphold the immunity of gabriele albertini. for these reasons i thought i should vote in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ i do not find the report on the failure to defend the immunity and privileges of gabriele albertini and to follow up his request for review of the civil proceedings against him favourable. i am convinced, as guarantor, that the existence of immunity serves a purpose of considerable importance; and that is why i shall always vote against such relations. this is an important premise which must remain the basis for similar cases. freedom of expression must be and remains protected to allow the proper exercise of the functions.
in writing. ‒ whereas a former member of the european parliament, gabriele albertini, has requested the defence of his parliamentary immunity in the context of a criminal case pending before an italian court; that gabriele albertini also requested a review of his request for immunity in civil proceedings pending before the same court; that the request for immunity concerns the alleged defamatory views expressed by gabriele albertini in a statement submitted to the italian minister for security on 22 october 2012 to ascertain whether the activities of alfredo robledo, the public prosecutor who had launched an investigation into events dating back to 2005 involving the city of milan and concerning the duties of mayor of that city exercised by gabriele albertini, were liable to be disciplined in terms of professional ethics; confirms that it will not defend the immunities and privileges of gabriele albertini and will not follow up on his request for a review of the civil proceedings against him; it is for the same reasons that it is decided not to defend the privileges and immunities of mr gabriele albertini in the criminal proceedings against him. for these reasons i have voted against.

in writing. ‒ the report examines the commission's proposal to launch macrofinancial assistance to ukraine for around eur 1.8 billion in medium-term loans. the aid is part of a series of operations to deal with a deep economic recession in ukraine, aggravated by the armed conflict in the south-east of the country. in particular, macro-financial assistance shall aim at reducing short-term balance of payments imbalances, while supporting reform programmes through restructuring measures in many strategic sectors for the country. the assistance will be distributed in three tranches of 600 million each, the first of which will start as early as 2015. in the light of the above, i have decided to vote in favour of the report because i believe that the proposed additional mfa will help to mobilise a new package of international aid to ukraine, either directly, through the proposed amount of eur 1.8 billion, or indirectly, by mobilising contributions from other partners. it should also act as a catalyst for a gradual recovery of confidence and support reform efforts in the country.
in writing. ‒ the ukrainian economy is experiencing an acute and severe crisis, rooted in long-standing structural problems and exacerbated by the armed conflict in the eastern regions and russia's illegal annexation of crimea. the ambitious macroeconomic adjustment and structural reform plan of the new government, which took office in february 2014, was supported by an imf financial assistance programme and two eu macro-financial assistance (mfa) operations. parliament has repeatedly expressed its support for assistance to ukraine, the eu's associated partner, in its process of economic and political stabilisation and reform. in its most recent resolution on the situation in ukraine of 15 january 2015, the european parliament welcomed the commission's proposal to provide an additional eur 1,8 billion in macro-financial assistance to ukraine and called for the development of a major assistance plan for the country. in view of the above, the rapporteur proposes that parliament approve the commission proposal without amendments. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of allocating €1.8 billion in macro-financial assistance to ukraine to help the country close its balance of payments deficit. ukraine is affected by an economic crisis due to long-standing structural problems, now exacerbated by the armed conflict in the eastern part of the country, which is impeding the implementation of macroeconomic adjustment as well as the necessary structural reforms. the internal conflict, russian trade restrictions and the intensification of the natural gas dispute have led to capital flight and a consequent depreciation of the currency, which makes it necessary to resort to external financing to implement structural, political and economic reforms to overcome the crisis. i believe that it is our duty as the european union to help a country which has on more than one occasion shown its willingness to 'get closer' to the union. i therefore believe that it is necessary, in accordance with the principles of solidarity on which our community is founded, to provide ukraine with the financial instruments to overcome its crisis and to implement the reform programme agreed in the future memorandum of understanding to remedy the fundamental weaknesses which, in their accumulation, have led to the current deficit.

vice-president of the commission.– mr president, many thanks to all those who have taken the floor to speak in support of a positive vote later on in this chamber. let me just make four points in response to comments and also to the questions addressed directly to the commission. first, the impact on payments. our view is that it will be manageable, based on past payment profiles, but most importantly on the fact that, in dealing with the payment crisis we have had, together with member states we have done a very good job on obtaining better projections for payment schedules so we can structure payments in a more prudent and predictable manner. there was a question on whether there is a risk that countries will not be able to use the money. the n+3 rule applies and that means that once commitments are made there is time to execute the programmes that are approved. in fact the time is basically three years more than we have in the mff, so this should be possible with programmes being approved this year. for some, approval will come early next year. all the funds committed are to be used. i want to stress again that we have drawn very important lessons from the payment crunch in terms of how we can better manage the relationship between commitments and payments in our budget. let us remember that we are no longer in the days of plenty. we have to learn to live with tighter budgets; focusing on the quality of spending and not just on the spending itself form part of this learning. my second point is on simplification. i heard loud and clear those of you who said that we need to have simpler rules so that programmes can be implemented and the level of errors can be reduced. i could not agree more with this. in the commission this is a very high priority for us. we call also on parliament to work with us, please, and not to add new control rules when they may not be necessary, when they do not add much value. but this applies also to member states. member states sometimes gold-plate rules and, even if we come with something that is simpler, bells and whistles are added and it is no longer simpler. so we all have to work systematically on implementation. my third point concerns the value for money. is this something that should be supported? there were voices saying let us just give the money back to member states. i want to speak using the language of facts. cohesion money is there to benefit the countries that are on the receiving end but also the european union economy as a whole. analysis of the use of cohesion funds from the previous period demonstrates a very tangible impact on growth rates in cohesion countries: for latvia, 2.1 % higher growth, for lithuania 1.8 %, and for poland 1.7 %. these figures represent additional jobs but also purchasing power for goods and services from other countries. one more fact: there is a very interesting report on the european union, called golden growth, which says that we have invented the most powerful convergence machine in the world, one that has allowed european union countries to accelerate their transition from middle-income to high-income status in the most impressive way that has ever happened. over recent decades some two dozen countries have made this most difficult jump from middle to high income. half of them are members of the european union and the other half countries that have discovered oil or have used very aggressive competitive practices, sometimes without too much democracy attached. so we are the place where we are able to grow without compromising on democracy, human rights or social inclusion, and without discovering oil. that may be something we would have liked but, frankly, in terms of climate change, it is better not. my last point is on the mid-term revision. i have heard the points you made, which are very valid ones. we will certainly analyse very closely whether the mff still adequately reflects priorities and we will propose adjustments if necessary. if these priorities require revision, we will of course come up with a proposal for revision. i want to stress that we would make full use of the new flexibility instrument for new priorities and the global margin for commitments. we would, of course, work broadly with parliament – i see committee chair mr arthuis here with the committee on budgets – in order to make best use of our taxpayers’ money for the betterment of our economy and our people.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place at 6.30 p.m. today. the commission shall be assisted by the committee of the regions.
in writing. we are discussing a technical review which is needed in the face of significant delays in the approval of operational programmes for the use of european funds. in 2014, more than 300 programmes, 47% of the total, were not adopted. this is a situation which affects all the member states and which, without the approval of this revision, would result in a loss of 21 billion. with the investment deficit we know, such a delay in the use of the structural funds is unacceptable. the rules provide for the possibility of transferring these appropriations from 2014 to 2015, and we can only express ourselves positively in this respect. what we are doing is positive flexibility, but it does not solve a structural problem. the financing of structural and cohesion policies must be simplified and made more accessible. there is widespread recognition of the need for a revision which is not merely technical but which is political and also covers the multiannual financial framework. the attitude towards the european budget must change. the economic crisis requires our budget to play an active role in supporting development. this is one of the steps we must take in this new legislature if we want the eu to be the true architect of a new course based on growth and opportunities for citizens.

on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, genocide was not even a word a hundred years ago! it was only coined by raphael lemkin in 1944. that is why the armenian people carved in the words of metz yeghern, "great evil" the pain of their tragedy. it doesn 't matter if there were 800,000 or more than a million victims; it doesn't matter if more people died from cold, hunger and disease than from torture, rape and murder. the point is that the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets. because what could be more hateful and intolerable than persecuting another just because he is different from himself? this, ladies and gentlemen, is the greatest horror of genocide, of all genocides. but we are not here today to pass judgment, this resolution is not an act of condemnation, it is a fitting tribute to memory and a humble invitation to reconciliation with others and with oneself. accepting the mistakes of the past is a great relief for a people. we know this well, because we have not been able to prevent either the mistakes of the dictatorship or those of colonialism. you know my father, who was stained with both. it is precisely these wounds that make us true and sincere friends of armenia and turkey. that is why we are asking them to ratify the zurich protocols. the word 'hate' and 'revenge' can no longer be used together, not even in the past. the future is one of reconciliation, cooperation and peaceful coexistence. to know to recognize and be aware. primo levi wrote that the holocaust is a page in the book of humanity from which we should never remove the bookmark of memory. we ask the armenians, the turks, all the peoples of the world to mark this page and never take it off again.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, elie wiesel, nobel peace prize winner, says that the first act of genocide is the demonization of a people, the last is its denial. well, then i invite you to divide one and a half million human beings for 365 days. days during which their massacre was perpetrated. 4,100 men, women and children slaughtered every day in a way that is hard to imagine just because they are armenians, this is genocide. and no one in this assembly can afford to deny it. history says so, the ottoman court that condemned the perpetrators of the genocide says so, turkish historians say so, not least taner akçam who said that only the known archives would suffice to define that crime as genocide. so i'll tell you about armenia: turkish politics can call me a liar! but remember, history is written by the same people who hanged the heroes.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as commissioner kristalina georgieva has said, the historical truth of the genocide cannot be denied. moreover, according to the international association of genocide scholars, denial is the very last act of genocide. so we simply cannot deny this historical truth of what happened 100 years ago. moreover, we must consider that it is precisely on the basis of the armenian genocide that the term was coined to describe the crime of genocide on which the 1948 un convention is based. but i say this, ladies and gentlemen, if we have really learned the lessons of history, we must not repeat the mistakes we have made too many times in history. we turned our heads in the face of atrocities. today there are atrocities that call for our responsibility and we are still tempted sometimes to turn our heads the other way. they were taken to syria, the same sands that collected their blood today collect the blood of other martyrs: let's not turn our heads today either!
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the armenian genocide is a crime against humanity which ankara continues to deny, to erase from its political consciousness. unfortunately, it is also censured in the european negotiations with ankara, although some states and this parliament in 1987 called the massacres the murder of a people as such. it is as if we had united europe without german recognition of the nazi genocides. the union would not have been born without this recognition, which is a full acceptance of the legacy of the past. in the case of ankara, full responsibility for what was done by the young turks and the ottoman empire. this denialist policy prevents the turkish governments not only from making peace with armenia but also from self-criticism over the invasion and violence in cyprus in 1974. i would like to conclude by saying that i am sorry for what was said after the pope's denunciation by an italian minister, that there is not a single historical truth about the armenian genocide.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with this resolution the european parliament wishes to recognize the armenian genocide and to pay tribute to the memory of one and a half million victims, including thousands of intellectuals, artists and parliamentarians. if turkey wants to join the union, it must recognize the historical truth of the genocide of the armenians by the ottoman empire and start an effective peace process on this basis. only 22 countries have officially recognised the armenian genocide, including italy, and i therefore find the harsh words spoken by erdogan in recent days against pope francis, who is guilty of having spoken of genocide, truly unacceptable. we are proposing the establishment of a dedicated european day, but we are also calling on turkey to draw inspiration from the examples of reconciliation between the peoples of europe after the second world war.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we must work to create a barrier-free europe for the disabled. this was stated by the commissioner for employment and social affairs, marianne thyssen, during the hearing in the european parliament. unfortunately, the legislation on disability is still very weak: the 1978 directive 2000 establishes a legal framework for combating discrimination based on religion, personal convictions and disabilities in the field of employment. the point, however, is to move from a generic obligation to hire to a more structured process to properly assess the work capacity of people with disabilities and to place them in the right place. the aim of this type of targeted placement should not simply be to find a job for the disabled person, but rather to create a virtuous circle that can fully exploit the potential of the person, making him or her a positive and productive element in the work environment. although the union has responded to this challenge by adopting a number of initiatives, there is still a long way to go. it is time for the european union to establish strict rules so that the european union institutions also have greater quotas for the employment of people with disabilities.
