on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the current absence of a bilateral agreement between the european union and mexico on the transfer of pnr data means that european airlines cannot transfer pnr data to the mexican authorities without breaching european data protection legislation. at the same time, however, we have seen that in the face of such a refusal they risk being exposed to heavy financial penalties which the mexican authorities threaten to impose. we believe that the threat of heavy fines is not only absolutely condemnable, because it effectively strengthens the decision-making and negotiating power of the european institutions, but that it could also set a dangerous precedent, given that many other third countries, such as south korea and the united arab emirates, are already pressing russia to conclude pnr agreements with the european union. the european union currently has agreements on the transfer of pnr data with the united states, canada and australia. we know that before giving its consent to ratify the agreement, the european parliament recently referred the agreement to the court of justice for an opinion on its compatibility with european data protection legislation. obviously, the matter is extremely delicate: the debate on the european pnr has also recently raised a number of criticisms and concerns in relation to the protection of fundamental rights, in particular the protection of personal data and freedom of movement. many points which deserve further examination and which have led to a request for a ruling on the merits of the commission on the compatibility with the judgment of the european court of justice which declared the data retention directive unlawful because it violated the principle of proportionality in the balance between the right to data protection and the needs of public security. the first thing to be done is to identify what is meant by pnr data, i.e. what kind of data is intended to be included and therefore transferred. criteria are provided for differentiating the duration of data retention; there are substantive and procedural conditions to which access to the data is subject; and finally, which authorities are competent to access and process the data themselves. it is clear, therefore, that the examination of these criteria requires time and caution. the public security considerations in the name of which the transfer of pnr data is strongly requested cannot be subordinated to the protection of fundamental rights. we therefore ask the commission what measures it intends to take to ensure that the transfer of pnr data to mexico is in line with european data protection rules; whether it intends to take measures to ensure that air carriers do not face high fines or the withdrawal of landing rights when the mexican legislation enters into force. finally, is the commission aware of a sharing agreement between mexico, the united states and canada, and if so, what consequences will this agreement have for the transfer of personal data by air carriers to the mexican authorities, and, above all, what legal remedies european citizens will have in the event of a breach of their rights in relation to the processing of personal data? in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund to support 2,513 employees of mory-ducros sas, a company operating in the land transport sector whose redundancies affected 84 locations across france. the excesses are due to the global financial and economic crisis, which, due to the decrease in overall physical production in europe, has led to a reduction in the volumes to be transported. a price war has thus broken out in the sector, which, aggravated by the upward trend in various costs (gasoline, wages, materials), has led since 2007 to a continuous deterioration of operating margins and a series of losses for the sector in france, including the bankruptcy of several companies including mory-ducros sas. the total amount of eur 6 052 200 from the european globalisation adjustment fund is a single action to be carried out through a single window (cells de requalification) managed by three contracting agencies, the aim of which is to cover as much of mainland france as possible and to ensure the reintegration of as many workers as possible.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the recommendation on the draft council regulation amending regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014/2020. the european structural and investment funds constitute the most important investment policy of the union and it is therefore essential that all resources are used in a timely and effective manner. the revision of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 should therefore be carried out by ensuring the implementation of programmes that were adopted later than planned: the new programming period has already suffered too many and too significant delays and it is necessary to prevent any further delays. attention should be paid to the quality of the projects submitted and to ensuring that programmes are geared to stimulating growth and creating jobs, especially for young people. the procedures must also be simplified in order to ensure that all resources are used in a full, constructive and effective way and, above all, to enable citizens and local authorities to have access to these financial resources.
in writing. ‒ i voted on an amendment to the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. it is a major technical change with a very real impact. article 19 of council regulation (eu, euratom) no 1311/2013 provides that, where new rules or new programmes under shared management for the structural funds, the cohesion fund, the eafrd, the emff, the emff and the esf are adopted after 1 january 2014, the multiannual financial framework is to be revised in order to transfer to subsequent years the allocations not used in 2014. this vote allows us to make changes to reallocate over 21 billion over the next few years, which were previously allocated but have not been used.
in writing. ‒ pending a general review and deeper revision of the multiannual financial framework in 2016, the amendment we have approved will allow the 'recovery' and use in the coming months of some eur 21 billion of commitment appropriations which were unfortunately unused in 2014 due to delays in the finalisation of many important programmes. this will allow for the transfer of eur 16,5 billion to the 2015 budget and eur 4,5 billion to the 2016 budget. these resources should be allocated to key spending areas such as economic, social and territorial cohesion policy, sustainable growth and the exploitation of natural resources, in order to facilitate the development and implementation of local development programmes, and to trigger economic recovery and employment growth, especially among young people, including by encouraging the necessary re-launch of public investment at home. the commission will have to make every effort to avoid further delays in the preparation of programmes and commitment appropriations and all the possibilities provided for by the flexibility provisions of the mff will have to be used, both to provide payment appropriations on time and to strengthen employment support. that is why i voted in favour of the recommendation.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the time taken for road safety is closely linked to the reduction of the impact of accidents on the health and sometimes even the lives of the people involved. we therefore believe that the conclusion of the agreement on the ecall system for new passenger cars and light vehicles represents an important step forward for the protection of all european citizens. i thank mrs sehnalová and the italian presidency for their determination to pursue the objective of ensuring european legislation that raises road safety standards. in the eternal confrontation between privacy and security, and between the identification of ever-increasing standards and the needs of the manufacturing sector, which involves wide and diverse sectors of society, i believe that a fair compromise has been found in this case. i believe that this agreement is a significant example of the integrated, practical and citizen-friendly europe that we must develop more and more and i hope that the attempts of those who want to weaken it will be stopped by a rule that guarantees greater security for all european citizens.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, ecall, together with other driving systems incorporating wireless and dect technologies, is a priority in road safety. the system is able to provide rapid assistance to motorists involved in collisions anywhere in the european union, and this speed will make the difference between saving the lives of hundreds or even thousands of people in europe every year. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. however, and in any case of paramount importance, respect for privacy and the careful collection and management by qualified bodies and not by private individuals of the mass of information on the mobility flows of each car owner remain. i believe that this data should be managed and rationalised to achieve traffic flow planning for smart cities.
member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank the contributors to the debate for a very constructive dialogue, and it was good to have the opportunity to listen to all of the members who wished to speak on this topic. this debate certainly made it clear that there is overwhelming support for the e-call system and i am grateful for that support. i think overall that parliament has once again shown its strong support and its determination to realise the benefits of the e-call system, and it is certainly gratifying to witness such unity in general terms regarding road—safety issues. it is primarily about new technology being put in place during the manufacturing process in cars and vans to establish the precise location and the precise detail of the accident. it is not about personal details of any individual – and this regulation provides the balance and safeguards on privacy that many of you were concerned about and concentrates on helping save lives following on from the accident. of course accidents will always happen, unfortunately, due to driving behaviour, but no resources will be diverted, or should be diverted, by member states from road safety, due to the fact that this is a technology that is included in the manufacturing process. i know that ms ford was concerned about the economic cost to the consumer in relation to the installation of this new technology, but i would remind her that the eur 100 that she mentioned is at the upper end of the estimate, because key components such as gps systems or mobile phone antennae are now in many cars anyway, which brings down the costs substantially. i think it is a small price to pay to include this technology at the car manufacturing stage in order to help save lives. i wish to thank the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs and members for an excellent deliberation in relation to this very important issue.

in writing. thanks to the excellent work of mrs olga sehnalová, the european union today has taken a step forward towards building a safer future for its citizens. from 31 march 2018, all vehicles will be equipped with the ecall safety system which will automatically alert the emergency services in the event of a major accident. even if the victim is unconscious, the system will inform the exact location of the accident so that rescuers can leave within minutes. the benefits of a timely response to an accident are many. the implementation of the ecall system will reduce these times by 50%. what does all this mean in practical terms? it means human lives. in 2014, approximately 26,000 lives were lost as a result of road traffic accidents. it has been estimated that with a time saving of 50%, the system and call will help save up to 2,500 lives each year. as regards the criticisms raised by some with regard to the respect for privacy and the processing of data held by the ecall system, the commission has given us strong assurances in this regard and the institutions will be vigilant to ensure that security requirements do not conflict with those of confidentiality of personal data.

chairman of the envi committee. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, with the resolution adopted by the envi committee, parliament intends to make a contribution to the new alcohol strategy, which may be useful in view of future proposals by the european commission to support the member states in their action to reduce the health, safety and social damage caused by alcohol abuse. i would first like to thank the seven co-sponsors for the excellent work they have done on the resolution and the oral question which preceded it. i believe that the final text, which was negotiated between the political groups on 360 amendments, reflects the position of the european parliament in a balanced way. i start from a premise, which is that our work has focused on preventing and reducing excessive and extreme patterns of consumption, thus making a clear distinction between responsible consumption and harmful consumption of alcohol. recalling that responsible drinking is compatible with a healthy lifestyle, we have focused on the subject of alcohol abuse and its harmful consequences. harmful alcohol use is still the third leading cause of predictable death and disease in europe and is a risk factor for over 60 chronic diseases. but alcohol abuse is linked to other problems, especially social ones, linked to the habits of young people, addiction, road accidents and some forms of violence, including domestic violence. tackling alcohol abuse must therefore remain a priority on the european political agenda, not just in terms of public health; we must start from the assumption that not all alcohol consumption has the same consequences, since it depends a great deal on habits, methods and the type of drink. the european union's alcohol strategy has proved effective in supporting member states' measures to reduce alcohol-related harm, and the work of the european alcohol and health forum has helped to develop concrete and measurable actions to reduce the harm caused by alcohol abuse at local level across the european union, but we need to do more, commissioner. in our resolution, we strongly urge the commission to immediately start work on the new eu alcohol strategy for 2016-2022, with the same objectives as the previous one, but with a better differentiation within consumption habits and behaviours and attitudes towards alcohol consumption itself, in order to reduce the harms related to abuse. the new strategy would also be a powerful tool for reducing health and social costs linked to the direct and indirect effects of alcohol-related harm and for helping member states to step up their efforts to develop policies and actions to promote healthy lifestyles and to inform citizens about the harmful effects of alcohol abuse. we therefore call on the commission, in full respect of the principles of subsidiarity and better regulation, to step up its efforts to improve on what has already been done and to fully achieve the objectives of this strategy. in the resolution we also call for a review of existing european legislation on the need to improve the information on alcohol available to consumers today, and stress the importance of clear, concise and effective information on the effects of alcohol consumption and the health risks. but we would like to ask the commission for more information on a specific point, namely the assessment of the effects of a possible adoption of labelling at european union level warning consumers about the dangers of the abuse of alcoholic beverages during pregnancy, for minors and when driving. in conclusion, i would like to reiterate that our aim is to make a valuable contribution to the commission in view of the adoption shortly of a new european strategy which can stimulate prevention, health promotion and education, reduce road accidents caused by drunk driving and make a better differentiation within consumption habits and behaviours and attitudes towards alcohol consumption with a clear distinction between responsible consumption and harmful consumption. these, commissioner, are the priorities expressed by the envi committee in its oral question and subsequent resolution.

while european waste legislation has been set up on the "4rs" which are the basis for proper and effective sustainable management, the first "r", the reduction of waste generation, has not always worked. we have data in europe which, apart from the crisis, show us that the quantities of waste have on the contrary increased in recent years, partly because of the failure to implement serious prevention policies. this measure starts from there, that is, for the first time we are going to act on the first level of the waste hierarchy, we are going to tell the states that they must reduce the production of waste with a mandatory target by introducing a price. i now come to the other qualifying point of the provision. with this directive, the european union is providing an important tool to advance the circular economy, a new frontier in the sustainable economy. the new rules, through the reduction of waste, in this case lightweight plastic bags, are simultaneously promoting a more effective and efficient use of resources with a positive impact on the entire economy. we are in fact moving from the simple use and disposal of products, typical of a linear economy, to the need instead to find alternative solutions, which have less impact on resources and the environment and which also stimulate new green technologies, for example the green chemistry chain, to the production and research on organic matrix bags, one of the virtuous challenges of the green economy. i would like to conclude by saying that this is an important process which must go on, as we are committed to do as soon as possible with the new and more ambitious proposal which the commission will present on the waste cycle.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, international shipping remains the only mode of transport which is not included in the european union's commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, despite the fact that emissions from the shipping sector are a major contributor to both air pollution and climate change. the development of a european system for monitoring, reporting and verifying (mrv) co2 emissions from maritime transport is therefore essential. it can provide the basis on which europe can, or at least should, develop emission reduction policies for the maritime sector consistent with global policies on climate, air pollution and human health protection. the development of ambitious policies for reducing emissions in this area is all the more important in the light of the challenges facing the maritime sector in the coming years. in the future, world trade is expected to grow considerably due to the expected increase in population and it is therefore necessary and urgent to develop technologies and practices to be applied to fuel quality, emission reduction technologies and operational measures for ships.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution introducing an ecall system for our cars, compulsory and free of charge, to help and ensure the safety of european citizens. this device will not only lead to a reduction in the time required for intervention in road accidents, but will consequently lead to more immediate treatment of emergencies and thus to a reduction in road casualties. from march 2018, every new car will be equipped with such a device which, connected to the digital navigation service automatically in case of need, will send a distress signal with the details of the road accident to the emergency number 112, active throughout europe. the device will help to reduce road fatalities, which has always been a priority for this parliament. the speed with which we respond to emergency calls could save some 2 500 lives a year. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.

in writing. ‒ in the vast majority of cases, biofuels are neither environmentally friendly nor sustainable. three problems: put pressure on remaining natural ecosystems, from which new arable land is obtained: but swamps, forests or grasslands store carbon in the subsoil and in plant biomass. their conversion into fields and plantations releases climate-altering gases into the atmosphere (iluc, indirect land use change impact); biofuels from food crops (such as maize) put the car's fuel tank in competition with the stomachs of the poor; the production of biofuels requires fossil fuels, used both for agricultural machinery and for the production of chemical fertilizers and pesticides: in view of this, co2 emissions from the use of biofuels can be quite similar to those of diesel and petrol and the eroei (energy return on energy investment) is minimal or negative. i have voted in favour of the amendments in favour of advanced biofuels and non-food crops; the commission is also supporting those aimed at reducing the pressure of biofuels on food crops. i have said no to amendments which are contrary to the principles set out above and to those which open the way to safeguarding the investments of the 'business as usual' biofuels. the climate and the land are priceless.

in writing. ‒ the directive on the reduction of the consumption of lightweight plastic carrier bags requires member states to either (1) take measures to ensure that the level of annual consumption does not exceed, on average, 90 lightweight plastic carrier bags per person by the end of 2019 and not more than 40 lightweight plastic carrier bags per person by 2025 or (2) ensure that, by the end of 2018, plastic carrier bags are no longer provided free of charge at the point of sale of goods or products, unless other equally effective instruments are implemented. in order to assess the effectiveness of the reduction measures, a monitoring system is provided for, which requires member states, after 36 months from entry into force, to submit an annual report on the annual consumption of lightweight plastic carrier bags based on a common methodology to be adopted by the commission within 12 months. in addition, the commission is required to set specifications for the labelling of biodegradable and compostable plastic bags. the last point to be made is that the measures provided for in the directive are binding. i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ i am proud that my country was the first in europe to adopt legislation to reduce the per capita consumption of lightweight plastic bags. i would like to remind you that in italy, since 2011, the law has been in force prohibiting the sale of non-biodegradable plastic bags. i think that the agreement reached between parliament and the council gives the member states a fair amount of leeway to take different measures depending on the environmental impact, the compostability and the intended use of plastic bags. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of the measure.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of introducing new rules to reduce the consumption of lightweight plastic bags in the eu. under the new legislation, member states will be able to choose between two options: decide whether to limit the average consumption per capita to 90 bags by the end of 2019 and subsequently to 40 bags by 2025; or, to establish a price system for the bags. these rules are favourable to italy, which banned lightweight bags in 2011 and opened the way to the use of biodegradable bags, thus becoming a leader in the sector. this is an important measure, reflecting the 92% of eu citizens who believe that it is necessary to reduce the consumption of plastic bags (source: eurobarometer). these have a devastating impact on the environment: an estimated 8 million plastic carrier bags are dumped every year in the eu, ending up in rivers, lakes and seas, where they cause long-term pollution by the pollutant particles they release into the water, seriously altering ecosystems. since such pollution also endangers the safety of the food chain, it constitutes a threat to human health: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of consumers against the risks of chemical agents in foodstuffs.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement reached with the council on the adoption of the directive amending directive 94/62/ec as regards the reduction of the use of lightweight plastic carrier bags. the proposal introduces important, but improving, binding elements for member states to reduce the consumption of plastic bags: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to impose a minimum price for plastic bags on the market, such as the imposition of certain annual consumption levels or the payment of retail plastic bags. among the various measures included in the proposal which i welcome, but which certainly only solve part of the problem, is the labelling of plastic bags as 'oxo-biodegradable'. oxo-biodegradable bags, contrary to what the name suggests, do not represent a solution to the problem of environmental pollution by microplastics, but rather aggravate it because they contain an additive that causes the fragmentation of plastic into microparticles. the labelling of bags would give clear indications of the components of biodegradable bags and would thus give all citizens the opportunity to make an informed choice of those plastic bags which are truly biodegradable and compostable.
in writing. ‒ the legislation adopted today will oblige member states to take new measures to reduce the average annual consumption of plastic bags to 90 lightweight bags per citizen by 2019 and to 40 by 2025. a decision which not only preserves the environment in which we live, but also saves 740 million euros a year.
in writing. i decided not to support the proposed amendment because it was necessary to close a very imperative decision-making process. the elements which parliament and the council have inserted into the commission's proposal have led to a text which, while it can be improved, is probably the best that could be achieved, also in the light of the lack of cooperation on the part of the commission on this dossier. i think it is extremely important to ensure that the consumption of plastic by shoppers is reduced in a sustained manner, including the introduction of specific monitoring provisions, which require member states to submit an annual report on their consumption. finally, for the first time in 40 years of european waste legislation, there will be binding measures at eu level to reduce waste production, a measure which i can only support.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour because i believe that europe has a responsibility, also as an institution, to send a signal for respecting and protecting the environment. the exploitation of plastics, a highly polluting chemical process, can no longer be carried out indiscriminately and without limits. limiting the spread of plastic bags (often used only once as waste containers, also significantly increasing the cost of disposal processes) is a clear message first cultural, and then political, to try to make the continent more sustainable.
in writing. ‒ today we approved the call for eu member states to reduce the use of plastic bags. under the new rules, member states will have to drastically reduce the use of 'once-and-for-all' plastic, with a thickness of less than 0.05 millimetres, which is the vast majority of plastic bags used in the eu. from now on, we will have to halve our consumption compared to 2010, already by the end of 2019, and we will not be able to use more than 90 light bags per person, and then go down to 40 by the end of 2025. as an alternative, eu countries will have to ensure that consumers pay for the use of ultralight plastic bags by 2018. this is a huge environmental problem, as billions of plastic bags are released into the environment and seriously pollute waterways and aquatic ecosystems. i am therefore pleased that the recommendation has been adopted.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this measure, which aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in the shipping sector as well. what is envisaged is a system of monitoring, reporting and verification, with the aim of increasing information on the efficiency and emissions of ships, thereby encouraging the reduction of consumption and therefore of emissions. in transport, the maritime sector is the only one in europe today not affected by community measures to reduce co2 emissions. the text we are adopting today is a first step which takes account of the fact that the sector accounts for 4% of total eu emissions, which are estimated to increase by around 50% by 2030. this is a regulation which concerns vessels over 5 000 tonnes transiting european ports, irrespective of their country of registration, and which will also have to be taken into account in future negotiations within the international maritime organisation. a positive sign that reinforces the message that the transition to a more sustainable european system must necessarily involve all the sectors concerned.

in writing. ‒ the proposal under consideration introduces a system for monitoring, reporting and verifying greenhouse gas emissions from maritime transport. in order to reduce carbon dioxide emissions from maritime transport, it was proposed to set up a system for monitoring, reporting and verifying (mrv) co2 emissions from fuel consumption of ships as a first step in a phased approach to include maritime transport emissions in community policies for greenhouse gas reduction. the introduction of an mrv system allows for a reduction in emissions of up to 2% compared to the status quo and an overall net cost reduction of up to eur 1,2 billion by 2030. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the regulation.

in writing. ‒ the report on european statistics by hugues bayet tackled some fundamental problems, which had remained unresolved for years due to a lack of agreement between the council, the commission and parliament in the last legislature. statistics are very important for understanding and interpreting reality, especially if we consider the role they have played in economic and monetary policy decisions in recent years. the calculation of unemployment, poverty and inflation rates are just some of the most significant examples of their important contribution to european and national economic policies. three guidelines have been used to build this report. the first is to increase the quality of the independence and transparency of european statistics. the second concerns the appointment of the head of eurostat, a highly controversial issue which was resolved by involving parliament in the decision-making process. alongside this important issue, it has also been ensured that the selection process for the heads of the national statistical institutes is uniform at european level, thus ensuring an increase in quality and transparency. for these reasons, i am voting for this text with conviction, so that the european statistical system can be innovated in a more transparent and independent way.

in writing. ‒ this multiannual plan is the first of its kind in the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) and has been substantially amended by the european parliament. it is the first opportunity for us members to demonstrate the real role of parliament in the implementation of the cfp. this plan will serve as a model for future plans and therefore needs to be in line with the objectives of the common fisheries policy in ensuring environmental, economic and social sustainability and respect for the precautionary principle. the basic regulation clearly states that multiannual plans must include conservation measures to restore and maintain fish stocks above levels capable of producing maximum sustainable yield (msy). however, this criterion was not taken into account in the commission proposal. our group has tabled amendments to this effect, which have been adopted by a large majority in the committee on fisheries. it is important to follow the line already marked in order not to completely empty of meaning the efforts made so far. we must continue to act in the name of sustainability and the ecosystem approach in fisheries management to meet the objectives set by the cfp.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this multiannual plan because it aims to keep the size of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea above a minimum level, known as precautionary biomass. cod, herring and sprat are important components of the baltic sea ecosystem and there are strong biological interactions between them. i therefore believe that the precautionary approach is the right way forward, because proper management of the stock would avoid the risk of the reproductive capacity of the stock being compromised.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the multiannual plan as i share the objective of establishing a framework for the multi-species management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea where fishing is mainly directed at these three species. the baltic sea is a virtually closed body of water in which these three species are ubiquitous and interact continuously. therefore, it is essential to provide for legislation to recognise the interactions between regulated species, including the influence of cod on herring and sprat stocks and vice versa.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to establish a framework for the multi-species management of cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea. this is the first multiannual plan of this kind to be drawn up under the reformed common fisheries policy (cfp). i am confident that the approach adopted can ensure a more sustainable and balanced exploitation of these stocks on the basis of the most up-to-date scientific data on the interactions between the different fish species and with other elements of the ecosystem and the environment. in order to improve the stability and predictability of catches, i think it is necessary, however, to ensure a certain degree of flexibility in the plan, so that changes can be made quickly in the light of the evolution of the fish stocks concerned. today's vote is certainly a test case for adapting stock management to the principles of maximum sustainable yield and regionalisation on which the new cfp is based. i hope, therefore, that this proposal will set an example for future regional plans and help to redefine measures for the conservation of our precious marine resources and for the maintenance of stable and profitable fishing activities.
in writing. ‒ the multiannual plan for certain fish stocks in the baltic sea, which i voted in favour of, is the first such plan to be approved under the new common fisheries policy (cfp), which came into force in 2014. multiannual plans should allow for the long-term balanced and sustainable management of stocks of various fish species, providing greater certainty for fishing activities and the controlled exploitation of fishery resources by creating the conditions for their restoration. to achieve this, multiannual plans are based on the concept of maximum sustainable yield (msy), which is to set, on the basis of the latest scientific data, catch rates that allow stocks to reproduce and to ensure that they are exploited under economically and environmentally sustainable conditions. in view of the future development of the long-term plan for the mediterranean and the particular level of overfishing in this basin, it is important that we have voted for this first plan, which will give parliament a strong position on the protection of the environment and fisheries in the negotiations with the council.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in voting on this text, which, while presenting positive elements of simplification on the landing procedures for fish, does not address strong critical elements (such as the 'serious' infringement on non-compliance with the obligation).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report since i think that the incompatibility between the provisions regarding the landing obligation and those pertaining to discarding create a contrast that should be remedied as soon as possible, in order to better manage the fish stocks.
in writing. ‒ we are very pleased with the agreement reached with the council on the omnibus regulation because we have completed a necessary step to implement the reform of the common fisheries policy and make it a reality. the omnibus regulation, after long and cumbersome negotiations, will remove all obstacles to the ban on discarding and will provide a more solid basis for the landing obligation. the proposed amendments update the commission proposal with the new regulation no 1380/2013, which is the pillar of the cfp; in particular, we have repeatedly stressed the principle of regionalisation as a means of simplifying the proper management of marine resources and the de minimis rule. we have in fact introduced a minimum limit of 10% of live weight below which the landing obligation does not apply, and i am sure that this measure can help small-scale artisanal fishing vessels, which will therefore be relieved of excessive administrative burdens. in this way, we make the cfp environmentally sustainable without sacrificing the economic sustainability of the artisanal fishing industry.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the measure. i am in favour of bureaucratizing shipboard operations and i am against the system of managing minimum conservation sizes.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this proposal to give fishermen two years to adapt before the new discard ban comes into force. the obligation for fishermen to land unwanted catches and not to discard them is the main objective of the new common fisheries policy (cfp). these new rules require fishermen to land all the fish caught during a fishing trip. it will be extremely difficult to implement, especially for multispecies and artisanal fisheries. my concern is to preserve fish stocks while maintaining a sustainable economy. the compromise we have reached helps to mitigate some of the negative effects of the new rules for fishermen.
in writing. ‒ it could have been a first step towards what should be the ultimate goal, namely the total elimination of the possibility of discarding part of the catch at sea. it is a wasted opportunity, since it does not fully meet expectations and, on many levels, seriously undermines the initial idea. this is particularly true of the small-scale fisheries exception (which covers 80% of cases), i.e. the catch of less than 50 kilograms.
in writing. ‒ the reform of the common fisheries policy adopted during the previous legislature introduced some fundamental changes to the rules applicable to fishing activities. in particular, article 15 of the basic regulation of the common fisheries policy imposes the landing obligation for all catches. this obligation will be phased in between 2015 and 2019. fishermen will therefore have to discard all unwanted catches which are not marketable either because of the lack of a quota or because their size is below the minimum conservation reference size. however, this obligation is contrary to a number of regulations currently in force. the european commission has decided to present an 'omnibus' regulation to make these regulations compatible with article 15. i therefore decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution introducing the landing obligation, as i believe that the practice of discarding species subject to catch limits and species subject to minimum sizes is harmful to fish stocks, the marine environment and costly for fishermen. it consists of returning unwanted catches, whether alive or dead, to the sea. i think that the gradual introduction of the obligation to land all the fish caught could be a solution to the problem. the introduction of this measure will also make it possible to eliminate the contradictions in the current fisheries legislation arising from the reform of the common fisheries policy, which imposed the landing obligation. in order to align the different sources of regulation, the commission introduced this 'omnibus' regulation to make the regulations compatible with article 15 of the basic regulation on the common fisheries policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to ban, from 2015 and by 2019, the discharge of fish caught at sea when it is unsuitable for sale, for example because it is too small or exceeds the authorised quotas. the introduction of the landing obligation will help to reduce waste, to make a more accurate selection of catches and to collect more reliable data on the quantity of fish taken from the sea. the new legislation, which includes specific rules on how to handle fish, both on board and after arrival in port, as well as control procedures and possible penalties for fishing vessels, will ensure better food quality and consumer safety. finally, it is hoped that the new rules will promote more effective protection of marine flora and fauna both off the atlantic coasts and in our mediterranean sea.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this regulation because it provides for the application of the obligation to land all catches (the so-called 'omnibus') by applying the measures provided for in the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp). i am of course in favour of putting an end to the unacceptable practice of dumping precious and limited marine resources, also in order to give an incentive to fishermen to increase selectivity, to collect data and to increase control. however, there are a number of problematic points which weaken the regulation, in particular: first, the 50 kg threshold to be recorded in the logbook (could create loopholes in the application of the regulation. i would like all catches to be recorded, bearing in mind that one of the expected benefits of the landing obligation has been the improvement of recording). secondly, in the trilogy the reference to 'remote sensing' (method of evaluation of resources) had totally disappeared. finally, the introduction of several derogations from article 15 of the reform of the common fisheries policy weakens the proposal by creating gaps.
in writing. ‒ the obligation for fishermen to land unwanted catches and not to discard them has been in force since 1 january and is the main objective of the new common fisheries policy. the adoption of this measure today amends the regulation on the enforcement of this ban and postpones the application of the relevant sanctions for two years. this will give fishermen more time to 'adapt' to the rules on 'disposal' of waste fish.
in writing. ‒ i am against and regret the 'block' vote, which does not allow us to go into the substance of the individual elements of the proposal, save for the positive elements.
in writing. i vote in favour of the proposal put forward by the committee on fisheries which aims to make a fundamental change to the cfp, the reform of the common fisheries policy adopted in 2013. i therefore support the committee in its request to approve the revision of the reform by adopting the so-called 'omnibus regulation', which provides for the obligation to land all unwanted catches for non-marketable fishermen and which includes the exceeding of as many as seven of the previous ordering criteria for fishing activities (large and small pelagic fisheries, industrial fisheries and fisheries in the baltic sea) carried out between january 2015 and 2019.
in writing. i voted in favour of the ep and council regulation which introduced important elements of consistency with existing legislation on discards, because it has as one of its ultimate objectives the gradual elimination of discards. this regulation improves and further specifies the previous regulation which introduced an obligation to land catches of species subject to catch limits and species subject to minimum sizes in the mediterranean. since discards represent a significant waste and compromise the sustainable exploitation of marine organisms and ecosystems, and since compliance by operators with the landing obligation is essential to produce the desired results, it is of particular importance that this regulation sets out to classify violations of the landing obligation as a serious infringement under the regulation. since the landing obligation represents a substantial change for operators, it is appropriate to postpone the application of the rules on serious infringements of the regulation for two years. finally, the final text is a significant step forward compared with the commission proposal, which had not fully considered certain undesirable effects of the landing obligation, such as the possible emergence of non-compliant parallel markets.
in writing. european fisheries policies have a strong impact on the activities of our fishermen, and not always in a positive way. the contradiction between the possibility of discarding at sea and the obligation to land was liable to complicate working conditions and to cause confusion in the sector. i voted in favour of the report because it was necessary to clarify matters. now, under the omnibus regulation, it is clear that fishermen must bring to shore and land all their catches, including those which are not marketable. i think it is very important that these forecasts are valid for 2015 only, which will be a trial year to test the implementation of the new obligation. finally, i would like to stress that the attention paid to small-scale fishing and the reduction in bureaucratic and administrative burdens for vessels of less than 10 metres are very welcome. when imposing new obligations, the eu has a duty to take account of different realities.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr goffredo maria bettini because i believe it is correct to suspend the tariff benefits, established by regulation (ec) no 1215/2009, with bosnia and herzegovina from january 2016, in the wake of an agreement with the union, as the other balkan states have already done. the commission extended these benefits to all the other countries in the balkan area until 2020.
in writing. - i agree with the report on the landing obligation. this is a procedure aimed at implementing transparency to facilitate efficient monitoring. the fact that the fish caught must be landed in their entirety, even if they are of non-marketable species or smaller than the reference size, makes it possible to carry out comprehensive studies on the abundance and concentration of fish and the related trends in order to be able to carry out more comprehensive studies. this obligation, which will become fully operational in 2019, is in opposition to an existing rule of the obligation to discard certain species, which must be resolved at the regulatory level after numerous discussions and decisions related to combating the phenomenon of discards at sea. it is one of the institutions' duties to make policies homogeneous without any internal contradictions and it certainly promotes the use of effective rules by workers in the sector, who will thus be able to adapt more easily to the new rules.
in writing. ‒ following the reform of the common fisheries policy, which imposes an obligation to land, the european commission has presented an 'omnibus' regulation aimed at making parallel amendments to seven regulations, in order to make them compatible with article 15 of the basic regulation of the common fisheries policy. as the current rules require fishermen to discard non-marketable catches, i supported the cadec report, which considers that this contradiction should be eliminated by the landing obligation.
in writing. ‒ we welcome this proposal for a regulation, which is necessary because of the changes to the rules on fishing activities, in particular as regards article 15 of the basic regulation, which imposes a landing obligation for all catches and will enter into force gradually between 2015 and 2019. fishermen will therefore have to land all unwanted catches which are not marketable, either because of the lack of a quota or because their size is below the minimum conservation reference size. the rapporteur and i agree, however, that the legal alignment for fisheries subject to the landing obligation after 2015 will have to be implemented later, in line with the new technical measures framework which the commission will propose in a few months' time. the measures adopted today must therefore be of only provisional value: the 2015 will be a test year to assess the impact of the implementation of this new obligation. we are particularly concerned about the possible emergence of a parallel market which no provision of the existing framework allows us to control. we therefore propose that the responsibility of producer organizations for production and marketing plans be strengthened.
in writing. ‒ following the reform of the common fisheries policy (in force since 1 january 2015) which requires all catches to be landed in port, the european commission has presented a new 'omnibus' regulation to amend seven regulations currently in force to make them compatible with article 15 of the basic regulation on this matter. the proposal therefore aims to eliminate the contradictions with the legislation currently applicable and to convert the obligation to discard non-marketable catches or fish caught outside quota into an obligation to land these catches. in the light of the foregoing, i voted in favour of mr cadec's report.
in writing. ‒ in view of the introduction of a landing obligation for catches of species subject to catch limits and species subject to minimum sizes in the mediterranean, a number of provisions in the existing regulations on technical and control measures which conflict with the landing obligation in that they require fishermen to discard certain types of catches should be abolished or amended. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation because the recent reform of the common fisheries policy adopted by the legislator during the previous legislature introduces some fundamental changes to the rules applicable to fishing activities which are in conflict with previous regulations. an 'omnibus' regulation is therefore needed to amend seven regulations in parallel to make them compatible with article 15 of the basic regulation on the common fisheries policy.
in writing. i decided to vote against because the omnibus text proposed by the commission does not address the strong criticisms about the landing arrangements for fish, such as the 'serious' infringement of the obligation. i am also against the 'system' and the management of minimum conservation sizes, and the text does not provide for the bureaucratization of operations on board.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the amendments to the regulation on how to enforce the ban on discarding or landing obligation, which is one of the central objectives of the new common fisheries policy (cfp) and which was approved by the european parliament in 2013. the landing obligation for fishermen is to land unwanted catches (usually non-commercial species or of unwanted or prohibited size) and not to discard them, to avoid the economic and environmental damage resulting from the death of most of the fish discarded in this way. the rules approved by parliament meet the needs of fishermen, since they will now have two years to 'adapt' before the new discard ban comes into force, and they also limit the obligations of small fishermen to keep fishing logs for the most quantitatively important catches. this is another important step in the implementation of the new cfp, with a view to achieving the objective of sustainable management and restoration of fisheries resources.
in writing. ‒ fish is a staple food for billions of people. if we fish at a rate that exceeds the rate at which fish stocks are being replenished, billions of people will go hungry tomorrow. it's as simple as the concept of not cutting down the tree we're sitting on: yet the depletion of fish stocks is a reality. the eu is over-exploiting a very large proportion of its fish stocks and its fleet is oversized. the so-called incidental catches of fish of species other than the desired one, or still too small and too young to be marketed, play a considerable (but certainly not exclusive) role in the depletion of european fish stocks. the obligation not to discard by-catches but to return them to shore is a good incentive to reduce this practice. i have said no to all the amendments which in various ways tried to water down and postpone this obligation.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted against the own-initiative report by mr łybacka because i believe that, 15 years after the bologna process came into force, a serious and thorough budget is needed. we think that the report before us today misses a fundamental point, namely the profound impoverishment, not only economic, to which many of the counter-reforms applied in the member states have contributed and which have been invoked in various ways in the bologna process. i am thinking of the italian university system, brought to collapse first by the tremonti cuts, then by the gelmini reform, and i say this having experienced firsthand the precariousness of university research. we are imprinting the knowledge system on the logic of competition. we believe that we must change course and guide it along the lines of cooperation, the right to study, the right to university research free of market constraints.
in writing. - the vote is negative for one simple reason. we're tired of just words, now more than ever we need facts. m5s supports the public nature of education and the enhancement of the social dimension of knowledge. education is an inalienable right and is enshrined in all national constitutions. the fundamental function of the european higher education area must be human, social and cultural development, while the final text shows the will to bend universities to the interests of business. i have called for the elimination of public funding to private universities, avoiding support for processes of privatization of knowledge. the answer was to put the implementation of the juncker plan at the heart of the report, and the commission itself confirmed to us that 'private investment in the plan could have the effect of transferring majority control from the public to the private sector'. access to education must be open to all, funds allocated to private schools should be invested in the future of our young people, favouring the most disadvantaged students and increasing the number of scholarships.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this measure which aims to remove the bureaucratic red tape necessary for the development of the bologna process, the aim of which is to bring higher education systems closer together, not to unify them, by developing common rules of cooperation to offer students a wider and more transparent range of opportunities.
in writing. ‒ the education sector in each country is central to social and economic development and its improvement should be a priority for policies aimed at growth. it has been 16 years since the bologna declaration was signed. since then, a process has been under way to harmonize the european higher education system, while respecting the autonomy of the member states and the universities. much progress has been made, but the objective of supporting student mobility and the internationalisation of training pathways by ensuring a system based on compatibility and comparability of standards remains highly topical. with this resolution, which i support, parliament is sending a strong signal both to the member states, who must achieve the objectives of the process, and to the community institutions, which must support those countries which are having difficulties in this process. the main challenges highlighted in the resolution are, i believe, the promotion of innovative technologies in education and the work to be done to combat the skills gap in relation to job opportunities. the commission has also taken the initiative of drawing up a report on the situation in the former yugoslavia.
in writing. ‒ i decided to vote in favour of this report because implementation of the bologna process, with the creation of a european higher education area (ehea), plays a big part in the process of unification since an integrated education system would increase the mobility of students and faculty members in the eu and would have a very positive impact on scientific cooperation.
in writing. - i voted yes. it is important to remember that the aim of the bologna process is not to standardize higher education systems, but to bring them closer together by developing common standards of cooperation, while always taking into account the diversity and autonomy of individual countries and individual universities. i welcome the intention of the bologna process to eliminate the bureaucratic red tape of the system.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the follow-up to the implementation of the bologna process, which provides european higher education with the essential means to meet today's challenges. i believe that in the current context of economic and financial crisis, culture plays an even more strategic role with its profound impact on society and in particular on young people. it is also essential for a sense of european identity and cohesion and is one of the tools that can help to alleviate youth unemployment. the correct use of available resources should therefore be implemented, by focusing existing instruments on the useful result, while reducing shortcomings and promoting merit, with an increasingly results-oriented approach. the new technologies can also be of great help, since they enable the acquisition of skills also in teleconferencing and mobility. the links between higher education and research should also be strengthened by facilitating dialogue between the scientific community, society and smes. for all these important objectives, it is essential to promote synergy between actions supporting the bologna process, such as horizon 2020 and erasmus+, in order to contribute to the 'intangible' implementation of the thinking of national, european and world civilizations.
in writing. ‒ the 1999 bologna declaration, which gave rise to the creation of the seis european higher education area aimed to create the recognition of higher education at internal and external level in all signatory countries as well as the possibility of providing students with higher quality higher education. although progress has been made, much remains to be done, especially with regard to the delicate transition of students into the world of work, by encouraging dialogue with employers at a time of crisis such as the one the eu is currently going through. in addition, this system particularly conditions universities and makes them responsive to market demands.
in writing. ‒ the bologna declaration was signed by 29 european countries in june 1999, with the aim of creating a european higher education area (ehea) by 2010. the aim was and remains to offer students a wider and more transparent range of high quality educational opportunities, as well as to create a simplified recognition procedure, both internally and externally, in all the national higher education systems involved. meanwhile, all 47 current members of the bologna process have introduced major reforms to their higher education systems. over the last 15 years, the bologna process has achieved remarkable results in terms of quality of education, mobility and academic recognition. the measure analyses the main aspects of the bologna process and constitutes the european parliament's contribution to the interministerial conference to be held in yerevan in may. i therefore decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the implementation of the bologna process because i am convinced that the effective creation of a european higher education area could lead to the solution of some important contemporary problems. the objectives which have inspired and continue to inspire the process have not been achieved uniformly in the various participating countries and, above all, have not been pursued with the necessary impetus to achieve truly satisfactory results. the bologna process, if properly implemented, could lead to a development of knowledge and innovation levels, and ensure compatibility and comparability of standards and quality of different higher education systems. it could also be a response to the problem of youth unemployment, given that almost one in three employers in the european union are having problems finding adequately qualified workers and the imbalance between supply and demand is one of the challenges facing europe, to which a more homogenous labour market could provide a strong response.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of approving the progress report on the bologna process, covering priorities, achievements, failures by member states and suggestions on how to proceed with the implementation of the established framework. in particular, i share the founding principles and support the primary objective of achieving the highest possible level of knowledge and innovation for european citizens. education and research must be recognised as the pillars of our society and, above all, as the necessary tools for job creation. this awareness should in particular lead to a serious commitment to give young students, as well as jobs, the opportunity to enjoy quality continuing training and to enable them to compete with anyone else on a world scale. finally, i hope that efforts will be stepped up to adapt education systems to the labour market in order to promote employment. it is therefore important that states act in a coordinated manner by exchanging information and good practice, promoting international training programmes and facilitating the mutual recognition of qualifications. in this respect, much remains to be done.
in writing. ‒ i voted against because i believe that the łybacka report makes the education system work better than the market needs. indeed, its central objective is the implementation of the juncker plan (efsi), in relation to which the european commission has recently stated directly in the fields of education and training that leveraging private finance, as a central aspect of the plan, 'could have the effect of transferring majority control into the hands of the private sector'.
in writing. ‒ strengthening and improving the bologna process on the european higher education system and its annexes is a key step towards creating a european knowledge area that can respond to the new global challenges facing europe. much work still needs to be done to implement one of the inspirational principles of the bologna process, namely that cultural growth is rightly identified as one of the means of combating social inequalities and unemployment, especially youth unemployment. in conclusion, promoting culture means promoting social inclusion. that is what the member states will have to work on and that is why the vote in favour is of the utmost importance.
in writing. ‒ over the last 15 years, the bologna process has achieved remarkable results in terms of quality of education, academic mobility and recognition, and has made information on european higher education more transparent and easily accessible. while these results are commendable, there are still some areas which need further development. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution to give new impetus to the bologna process. it will be essential to focus on adopting a more student-centred approach to learning outcomes, to strengthen links between higher education and research, to facilitate dialogue between science and society and to promote the benefits of the use of technological innovation in teaching and learning.
in writing. ‒ this report is relevant to the ministerial conference to be held in 2015 to assess the state of play of the implementation of the bologna process, the aim of which would be to create the european higher education area, a common reference framework for the 47 countries that have acceded. as usual, however, there were delays in achieving by 2010 such objectives as increasing the ease of mobility of students in europe and the comparability of european education systems. the problem with this report, which is why i voted against it, is that it sets out a private higher education system, thus failing to give due weight to the importance of education as a public education and, on the contrary, cancelling any amendment aimed at abolishing public funding for private institutions. in short, the fear that the implementation of the juncker plan may transfer the education sector into private hands seems to be well founded.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because the implementation of the bologna process is an essential means of addressing the challenges facing higher education today. in order to increase the attractiveness and competitiveness of the european higher education area, the bologna process needs to be given new impetus so that it can meet the new challenges and ensure the quality and transparency of european education.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the bologna process and it is important to remember that its aim is not to standardise higher education systems but to bring them together by developing common rules of cooperation, while always taking into account the diversity and autonomy of individual countries and individual universities. in the committee on culture we have long advocated the need to eliminate the bureaucratic red tape which the bologna process would like to eliminate.
in writing. mr łybacka has the merit of bringing attention and value back to the bologna process a few weeks after the yerevan ministerial summit. i would like to highlight an important step which i consider particularly significant for the future of university cooperation in europe: it is very important to ask them to increase their efforts at economic and social level to enhance social inclusion by opening up equitable access to quality education for all, facilitating the recognition of academic and professional qualifications, periods of study abroad and previous training, transversal skills programmes and non-formal and informal learning, as well as by offering relevant education to a diverse student population, through lifelong learning.
in writing. i voted for this report because we hear nothing but news about stability, about budgetary constraints, about economic parameters. our newspapers and our citizens call it the europe of the banks. so i ask myself: where is the europe of culture? we must talk in numbers, in percentages, but when will we pay the same attention to culture, education, training? the bologna process paved the way towards the creation of a european area of education, it envisioned a europe in which students were 'european' first and foremost, where they had the opportunity to gain experience in all the member states, to study at any university, to experiment with different courses and languages. that path must not be abandoned, it is vital for europe to grow and train the new european citizens. to be united in diversity, we must know each other, we must study each other, we must live. we give our young people the right to a european education, and they will give us back a better europe.

in writing. ‒ the scourge of youth unemployment has been affecting most eu member states since the economic and financial crisis erupted in 2008. this situation is exacerbated by the fact that many european employers have difficulty recruiting adequately qualified staff. in this context, it is necessary for universities to offer their students less theoretical training, which prepares them for entry into the world of work. i have supported the łybacka report, which calls on the parties concerned to make greater efforts to achieve full implementation of the bologna process, as i believe that it is desirable to rationalise curricula with a view to providing young european graduates with adequate general and vocational skills.
in writing. ‒ in pursuit of the eu's goals for growth and a knowledge-based economy, we believe that the bologna process can play an important role in the revision of the europe 2020 strategy and in the implementation of the juncker plan for investment in europe. the results achieved so far have been remarkable in terms of quality of education, mobility and academic recognition. however, there are still gaps and areas which require further momentum. the objectives of the bologna process have not been achieved in a uniform way in the various participating countries, and it is therefore a priority to implement reforms by consolidating not only the bottom-up approach but also by ensuring adequate and sustained political commitment and cooperation by all the main actors. the development of additional tools and new working methods, such as the formation of clusters and the exchange of good practice, should be encouraged, which could help countries in difficulty to achieve more while encouraging others to make further progress. we can no longer accept budget cuts in higher education: the commission will therefore continue to invest and use the funds available more effectively, and it is also advisable to envisage and then develop new alternative funding models.

in writing. ‒ over the past 15 years, the bologna process, signed by 29 european countries in 1999 with the aim of creating a european higher education area (ehea) by 2010, has achieved remarkable results in terms of education quality, mobility and academic recognition. but i think there are still some areas which need further development and it is therefore essential to give a new impetus to the process so that it can face the new challenges, as set out in this resolution which i support. education and research are one of the main pillars of our society and greater investment in education is essential to effectively combat poverty, social inequalities and unemployment, in particular youth unemployment, and to promote social inclusion. this resolution is intended to be a strong signal to ministers of higher education to make greater efforts to achieve the objectives of the bologna process, to support those countries which are experiencing difficulties in its implementation, to strengthen links between higher education and research, and to promote the benefits of the use of technological innovation in teaching and learning.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process has allowed higher and more qualified students to be offered educational opportunities and at the same time the creation of a simplified recognition procedure in all national higher education systems. this has created the conditions for greater mobility, the adaptation of education systems to the needs of the labour market and the enhancement of the competitiveness and attractiveness of higher education in europe. the bologna process should be implemented in order to adapt it to the new challenges it faces, such as youth unemployment, economic constraints and demographic change. i believe that the bologna process can make a significant contribution to the eu's objectives for growth and a knowledge-based economy, the revision of the europe 2020 strategy and the implementation of the juncker plan for investment in europe.
