in writing. ‒ i have decided to abstain from voting on this resolution because, while i share the general approach, in particular the focus on the protective role of forests in preventing environmental disasters and the recognition of the importance of sustainable forest management and the coordination of national policies in this regard, i believe it is of paramount importance that forest management be viewed from the perspective of environmental and social protection, placing these interests above the logic of profit. therefore, an appropriate forestry strategy should invest in research to make the most of the potential of forests to safeguard the environment, in improving the training of workers to make the workforce more aware and informed, in adopting a system of protection for small local producers.
in writing. mr köstinger has given us a very important report, which welcomes the commission's communication on a new european forestry strategy, stressing that it should focus on sustainable forest management and its multifunctional role in economic, social, environmental and energy terms. this is the most appropriate framework within which to proceed with the development of this sector, which is so strategic for europe's environmental and cultural heritage.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the new eu forest strategy for forests and the forestry sector. forests guarantee a high quality of life, environmental protection and air quality and represent a great economic added value. the forestry sector, with over 3.5 million people employed, is the third largest sector in europe in terms of employment and has a triple function: ecological, economic and social. i agree with the importance of sustainable management of forests, whose resources, such as wood, are vital to rural areas and must be diligently managed to preserve them for future generations. it is therefore essential that member states implement national policies for sustainable forest management in order to respond to daily challenges such as forest fires, climate change, natural disasters and tree diseases. these policies should look at the multiple possibilities for the development of the green economy through forests, such as the processing of textile fibres, the bioeconomy, renewable energy and biofuels, and support research and innovation in this area.
in writing. i believe that the european union needs to formulate a coherent strategy for forests for several reasons. first of all, the number of players involved and the size of the sector. the forestry sector employs more than 3.5 million workers in 450 000 enterprises. it is therefore vital for rural economies, but also for the connected urban economies. secondly, the need to safeguard the ecosystem. the presence of "healthy" forests can prevent natural disasters such as avalanches, landslides and floods. and finally, because even though more than 50% of the forests are privately owned, the presence of forests benefits all citizens. forests thus play an ecological, economic and social role, although they are less and less known. the european union should therefore implement the strategy early, not to impose new bureaucracy and new obligations, but rather to promote forest knowledge and to shorten the distance between towns and rural areas.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mr köstinger, as it seeks to strengthen the social, economic and ecological role of forests and to emphasise the importance of wood as a sustainable raw material. forestry occupies 40% of the eu's land area, playing a very important multifunctional role, and forest biomass is the main source of renewable energy, accounting for around half of the total renewable energy consumption in the eu. for these reasons, i support the report and thank mr köstinger for the excellent work he has done.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the report on 'a new eu forest strategy: for forests and the forestry sector'. wood is indeed an important resource for the european union, both as a renewable resource and as a raw material with potential for development. effective forest management is of major importance, given the size, characteristics and capacity of our forests. it should also be borne in mind that forest biomass is a very important source of renewable energy, as european forests absorb around 10% of the eu's carbon emissions, and that managed forests have a higher effective capacity than unmanaged forests. finally, it should be stressed that, in view of the increasing urbanization, policies are needed to raise awareness among the population and to encourage them to discover and care for this type of resource.
in writing. ‒ european forests currently absorb and store about 10% of the carbon emissions from the eu member states. it is therefore a priority to ensure sustainable management of forest biomass, given that it is an important source of renewable energy. i voted in favour of the köstinger report, which refers to the need to adopt a forestry strategy at eu level focusing on the sustainable management of forests and their multifunctional role in economic, social and environmental terms, as i believe that greater coordination of european policies directly or indirectly linked to forestry is desirable.
in writing. ‒ with over 3.5 million people employed, the forestry sector is the third largest sector in europe in terms of employment. with the adoption of this report we intend to further strengthen the social, economic and ecological role of forests and the forestry sector and to draw attention to wood as a sustainable raw material and an important resource for europe. as many of the european union's policies, such as energy, environment and climate, also concern forest management, we believe it is essential that the new eu forestry strategy should focus on better coordination, so that forestry and forests are better integrated into the individual european strategies and a more coherent approach is followed. in this connection, it is necessary to promote the simplification and quality of regulation in the sector, while avoiding the imposition of additional bureaucratic and administrative obstacles. research and technological development will enable the full potential of innovation and development in the bioeconomy to be exploited, promoting the sustainable use of raw materials and providing a significant service to environmental and climate protection.
in writing. ‒ the current eu forestry strategy dates back to 1998. based on cooperation between the eu and the member states (subsidiarity and co-responsibility), it has established a framework of actions targeted at forests, in support of sustainable forest management. today, however, a new framework is needed to meet the growing demands on forests and the major changes that have affected forests over the last 15 years. the new strategy aims to create a policy framework that promotes forest coordination and the creation of synergies with other sectors that affect forest management, including rural development, business, environment, bioenergy, climate change, and research and development. at the same time, as a related initiative, the commission also proposed an action plan to draw attention to wood as a sustainable raw material and an important resource for europe. in the light of the above, i voted in favour of the report because it highlights the need for a holistic approach, recalling the importance of forests not only for rural development but also for the environment and biodiversity, for forestry industries, bioenergy and the fight against climate change.
in writing. ‒ whereas the european union has no competence in the formulation of a common forestry policy, but whereas certain union policies may have implications for national forestry policies, while it is for the member states to decide on the policy to be followed with regard to forestry and forests; whereas wood is a renewable and often under-utilized resource in europe and whereas it is necessary to ensure the intelligent and sustainable use of this raw material, including through the development and exchange of know-how; i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ it is important that there is a new and more precise eu forest strategy. the forestry sector is the third largest sector in terms of employment in europe. of course, sustainable forest management must be exercised if forest resources are to be conserved and the social, economic and ecological role of forests and the forestry sector is to be enhanced. i therefore believe that the standing committee on forests should be strengthened and a european forestry convention should be concluded. better coordination can give greater emphasis to research and development, allowing the forestry sector to exploit new opportunities and efficient production ideas. furthermore, with the further development of the bio-economy and the sustainable use of raw materials, there would be significant environmental and climate protection.
in writing. ‒ more than 40% of the eu's territory is covered by forests, which are a valuable resource that cannot be underestimated. that is why i voted in favour of the new eu forestry strategy, which aims at sustainable management of forests, highlighting their multifunctional role from an economic, social and environmental point of view. forests and forest industries offer valid answers for a new pillar of the economy, as well as being the best guarantors of a good quality of life, sustainability, jobs and value creation.
in writing. i decided to vote in favour because, although a 'community' framework for a forest management strategy is desirable, the text stresses the exclusive competence of the member states, and furthermore underlines the importance of national and, above all, local logics in their use. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's forestry policy and will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's forestry policy.
in writing. ‒ the report adopted today has the merit of drawing attention to the importance of forests for the european union and their economic, social and environmental role: 16 million forest owners, 3.5 million employees, 451 820 enterprises representing 7% of the eu's manufacturing sector gdp are figures that give us an idea of the high value of the european forestry sector. given the highly heterogeneous nature of european forests, which present considerable differences in ownership, size, nature and challenges to which they are exposed, it is important that the principle of subsidiarity and the competences of the member states are respected. however, the benefits that the forestry sector can derive from better and more active coordination at european level should not be underestimated. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the resolution on the new eu forestry strategy, which stresses the importance of sustainable management and the socioeconomic value of the forestry sector. with over 3.5 million people employed and 40% of europe's land area covered by forests, the forestry sector is the third largest employer in the eu, after metallurgy and food. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to combat illegal logging and illegal fishing. from the point of view of energy and environmental policies, smart forest management could contribute to the objectives of energy transition and climate change adaptation, through both the capacity to absorb co2 and the efficient use of wood as a renewable and versatile raw material. the resolution also calls for urgent clarification of the greenhouse effects caused by the different uses of forest biomass for energy production and for identification of those uses which can produce the greatest benefits in terms of mitigation within the timeframe provided for by relevant policies. the new strategy should also help to address cross-border challenges such as forest fires, natural disasters and invasive alien species.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the new strategy for safeguarding and protecting our forest heritage because europe must make a big ecological footprint of environmental sustainability. forests can no longer be used as a "base" for future cementation, nor can they be left to themselves by virtue of a "geographical divide" between urban and non-urban dwellers. the construction of a new europe also requires the intelligent and strategic use of its own heritage. not to phase it out (less concrete, more sustainability), but to use it as a resource for the community and as a possibility for the future: from clean energy to heritage conservation.

across europe – have been touched by this tragedy and the level of human suffering involved. europe did not cause this calamity. it is caused by poverty, war, instability, failing states and a in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the report on the proposal for the repeal of regulation (eec) no 3030/93 on the common system of importation of certain textile products from third countries. as is well known, the effectiveness of council regulation (eec) no 3030/93, which has been applied since 1 january 1993, has been affected by the following legislative developments: - the russian federation has joined the world trade organisation. as a result, the republic of serbia remained the last country with which the european union had a bilateral agreement on trade in textile products; - the stabilisation and association agreement between the european communities and their member states, of the one part, and the republic of serbia, of the other part, has been signed; - the interim agreement on trade and trade-related matters between the european community, of the one part, and the republic of serbia, of the other part, has entered into force; it follows that regulation (eec) no 3030/93 has since ceased to apply to imports from serbia. - in addition, the period of validity of title i of council regulation (ec) no 427/2003 has expired; regulation (eec) no 3030/93 should therefore be repealed in order to protect legal certainty.
in writing. ‒ following russia's accession to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, regulation (eec) no 3030/93 has lost its usefulness. it was also used to impose quantitative limits on imports of certain textile products from china for a limited period, and thus to implement the transitional safeguard mechanism for certain chinese products. this aspect also ended its life cycle on 11 december 2013. i therefore voted for repeal.
in writing. ‒ council regulation (eec) no 3030/93 on common rules for imports of certain textile products originating in third countries applies to imports of textile products originating in third countries with which the european community has concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols or concluded other agreements. in recent years, the european union has maintained bilateral agreements on trade in textile products only with russia and serbia. following the accession of the russian federation to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement (saa) with serbia, the main purpose of the regulation has been lost. it is therefore called for to be repealed. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of repealing the regulation in question, as it has now been emptied of any real purpose and is therefore a case of legislative obsolescence. this regulation allowed the import of textile products made in third countries with which the eu has concluded bilateral agreements, protocols or other agreements. in the past, the european union has had bilateral agreements on trade in textiles with the russian federation and the republic of serbia, and the import regime was governed by the regulation. following the accession of russia to the wto and the entry into force of the accession and stabilisation agreement with serbia, the regulation has been deprived of all purpose. quantitative restrictions on certain textile products were introduced in 2008 against china on the basis of the measures provided for in the regulation, however, attempts to safeguard trade in textiles from china failed in 2013, therefore i consider that in the presence of these conditions it is appropriate to repeal the regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to repeal regulation (eec) no 3030/93 on the arrangements applicable to imports from certain third countries. it is considered that the regulation in question applied only to those countries which had concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols or agreements of different types with the european union, that in recent years bilateral agreements remained in force only with the russian federation and the republic of serbia, that russia joined the wto in august 2012 and that since september 2013 the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia also started to take effect. it follows that regulation no 3030/93 was no longer useful for regulating trade relations with those two countries. after the trade in textile products between europe and china was also fully liberalised as of december 2013, it made no sense to maintain the above mentioned regulation, and i therefore voted in favour of its repeal.
in writing. ‒ i voted to repeal the regulation because i believe that after russia's accession to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, regulation (eec) no 3030/93 has lost its usefulness. the same utility was also lost in the case of the transitional safeguard mechanism for certain chinese products which ended on 11 december 2013.

in writing. ‒ whereas, in its certification of the final accounts, parliament's accounting officer stated with reasonable assurance that the accounts give a true and fair view of the financial situation of the european parliament in all material respects and that no element of concern has been brought to his attention, whereas control is also necessary to ensure that parliament's administration and policy-makers are accountable to the citizens of the union; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. ‒ an examination by the court of auditors has provided a true and fair view of the financial situation of the european parliament, which has not revealed any serious shortcomings in relation to the issues examined for this institution. the european parliament is the institution that most represents european citizens in the european legislative process and ensures the democratic functioning of the other eu institutions. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the 2013 discharge to the european parliament.
in writing. i voted against the decision proposing to grant discharge to the european parliament to demonstrate my opposition first of all to the fact that the budget of the parliament increased by 1.9% in 2013 compared to 2012 with the final appropriations of the parliament reaching a total amount of € 1 750 463 939. the necessary transparency on expenditure is also still lacking: it remains impossible to have an overview of the secretarial expenses of individual members, and the secretary-general did not respond to a number of questions put by members during the discharge procedure. parliament also continues to fund political parties and foundations, with more than €2 million in 2013.
in writing. ‒ mr president, i am voting in favour of the 2013 budget report, so that the path taken to cut parliament's and the institutions' expenditure is also the right one to send important signals in a context of great difficulties within the union. we know that the efforts made are not enough, but we can only hope for a start. the rationalization of expenditure is a central point of our policy.

in writing. the committee of the regions represents an important added value for the european decision-making process. respect for and implementation of the principle of subsidiarity are fundamental to ensuring that european policies are consistent with the territories they affect. the committee of the regions hosts representatives of those institutions which have the greatest influence and awareness on the quality of life and well-being of citizens, managing fundamental policies such as health, services and welfare. the resources allocated to it and managed by it are for the benefit of an activity which is closely linked to that of the european parliament. the committee's efforts to achieve global savings are welcome, provided that they do not jeopardize its activities. through its opinions, the committee brings awareness of national, regional and local identities to europe. it is essential for us to hear the voices of the institutions closest to the citizens.

in writing. i declare my vote in favour of the statement by mr ryszard czarnecki, already approved by the committee on budgetary control, on the report on the discharge for the implementation of the budget of the european asylum support office (easo). the current immigration emergency, which has italy at the forefront, must lead, as the italian government has rightly pointed out, to a new european solidarity also in the matter of asylum. the work of easo can be a very useful tool, in the hope that the political will of the other member states will also recognize this fundamental need.
in writing. at the last european council on 23 april, the heads of state or government gave the european asylum support office an important task. they agreed to send agency teams to the member states on the front line of asylum management to assist the relevant institutions. the most immediate observation is that if there were a fair system for distributing asylum applications and more solidarity between member states, the european union would probably not need easo. but since this is a utopia, the asylum office should really go to the aid of those national institutions and regional offices that are now collapsing. the 10 million and 500 thousand euro in its annual budget must be used to ease asylum procedures, which often take years, and to ensure that refugees are given the protection to which they are entitled.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr czarnecki's report in favour of the european asylum support office, as the court of auditors stated that it had not found any particular inconsistencies with regard to its general budget. however, it is noted that the recruitment procedures show a lack of transparency and we therefore call on easo to remedy this.

in writing. ‒ having regard to the court's report on the annual accounts of the european asylum support office (easo) for the financial year 2013, and having regard to the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions of the office, i have decided to support the request of the rapporteur, mr czarnecki, to grant discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget for the financial year 2013. however, i would urge easo to take note of the court's observations indicating the improvements to be made in the area of the reliability of accounts, internal controls and budgetary management, as well as in the area of recruitment procedures and their transparency. i believe that in general, in accordance with the principle of annuality of the budget, easo should pay greater attention to the principle of sound financial management, i.e. in accordance with the principles of economy, effectiveness and efficiency, in the use of the appropriations at its disposal to carry out the tasks entrusted to it.

in writing. ‒ the european banking authority (eba) is responsible for contributing to the development of high-quality common regulatory and supervisory standards and practices, for monitoring and assessing market developments in its field of competence and for promoting the protection of depositors and investors. the role of eba in promoting a common supervisory regime across the single market is essential to ensure better integration, efficiency and security in the union banking sector, thereby contributing to economic recovery, job creation and growth, as well as to preventing future crises in the financial sector. the authority should, however, fully exercise its consumer protection powers under its current mandate. in the light of the foregoing, and having regard to the statement of assurance as to the reliability of the accounts of the eba and the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions provided by the court of auditors for the financial year 2013, i have decided to endorse the report and therefore to grant a discharge to the eba for the financial year 2013.
in writing. ‒ ladies and gentlemen, whereas, according to its financial statements, the final budget of the european banking authority ('the authority') for the financial year 2013 was eur 25 967 360, representing an increase of 25,16% compared to 2012 due to the authority's recent establishment; whereas, according to its financial statements, the initial contribution from the union to the agency's budget for 2013 was eur 10 386 944, representing an increase of 25,16% compared to 2012; whereas the court of auditors, in its report on the annual accounts of the european banking authority for the financial year 2013 ('the court's report'), has stated that it has obtained reasonable assurances that the authority's annual accounts are reliable and that the underlying transactions are legal and regular; whereas the authority's task is to contribute to the development of high-quality common regulatory and supervisory rules and practices and to the uniform application of legally binding union acts, to encourage and facilitate the delegation of tasks and responsibilities between competent authorities, to monitor and assess market developments in its field of competence and to promote the protection of depositors and investors; that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i chose to endorse this resolution because the new rules on money market funds are expressly designed to avoid contagion of the short term funding market, thus ensuring greater stability in the eu´s financial market.
in writing. - i voted against the measure. fcms with constant net asset value represent a potential risk as they are unconnected to the market and its fluctuations. this would be essentially a shadow banking activity which, especially for italian local authorities in need of liquidity, could represent an excessive risk.
in writing. ‒ common monetary funds (cfm) are an important source of short-term funding for financial institutions, corporations and public administrations, with some eur 1 trillion in assets under management. the aim of this regulation is to ensure greater investor protection, liquidity of the fund to meet investor redemption requests and to make the structure of the fund sufficiently secure to cope with possible adverse market conditions. i therefore decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation which has the shared objective of creating a legal framework for the common monetary fund, in order to ensure greater protection for investors, while at the same time strengthening financial stability by preventing contagion risks. i also think that the further objective of the proposal is very important, namely to ensure that the liquidity of the funds is adequate to meet the demands of investors for redemption and to make the structure of the funds sufficiently secure to cope with possible adverse market conditions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation on the single monetary funds (smfs) to provide short-term financing to financial institutions, companies or public administrations with the ultimate aim of supporting the european economy as a whole. they are both a means of risk-sharing for the beneficiaries and short-term cash management tools on the demand side. fcms are used by a wide range of entities, including charities, building societies, local authorities and large professional investors such as corporations and pension funds wishing to invest excess liquidity for a short period: they therefore represent a key link between the demand for and supply of money in the short term. in a situation of economic and financial crisis, i share the need to regulate fcms and establish common rules of operation in order to safeguard the integrity and stability of the internal market and to honour investor redemption requests, especially in situations of stressed markets.
in writing. ‒ i voted against because i do not support the management of the single monetary funds (smfs), which can contribute to generating and amplifying systemic risk and instability in the financial and macroeconomic system.
in writing. - i will vote against the motion. the common monetary fund regulation touches on technical and sensitive aspects of finance. many experts believe that there is a risk that emfs with constant net asset value represent a potential risk, since they are detached from the market and its fluctuations. this would be essentially shadow banking, which we do not need, and the limits on how these funds can access derivative financial instruments are not sufficient.
in writing. ‒ the emfs are an indispensable financing instrument, worth around eur 1 trillion and accounting for around 15% of eu funds. the economic crisis has brought to light extreme fragility and several systemic flaws that required more detailed regulation. i voted in favour of measures to ensure that these instruments are more stable and reliable.
in writing. mrs gill has submitted a report which i wholeheartedly support, since i consider it a priority to continue the work begun by the committee on economic and monetary affairs to update and improve the community rules on financial law. the single monetary funds (smfs) provide short-term financing to financial institutions, companies or public administrations, and thus contribute to the financing of the european economy as a whole. more regulation, as proposed in this report, is an additional precaution for households and consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's position on the european common fund (ecf) because i believe that it is of fundamental importance to regulate a sector of industry representing a trillion euros, to stem the risks inherent in the shadow banking system, and to ensure financial stability. on the other hand, to enable the mmfs to play a leading role in the market for short-term securitisations relevant to the real economy and to commercial credit intermediation, and thus to address the interconnection of the mmfs with the banks promoting them. the ep's position aims to ensure that they are better able to withstand the volatility of securities and stock indices and the urge to bail out in stressed market situations. similar to bank deposits, fcms commit to their participants to provide immediate liquidity on demand, thus potentially making the distinction with banks less clear. finally, i believe that it is very important to require fcms to hold daily and weekly capital reserves among their portfolio assets in order to increase the transparency of the shadow banking system so that risks can be monitored effectively and immediate action can be taken where necessary. i hope that the negotiations with the council will be concluded swiftly and successfully.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the proposal by mrs neena gill. it aims to create a legal framework for the single monetary funds in order to ensure greater protection for investors, while at the same time strengthening financial stability by preventing contagion risks. the report also aims to make the structure of the funds sufficiently secure to cope with possible adversity.
in writing. ‒ money market funds are a short-term liquidity management tool that offers a high degree of liquidity, diversification and currency stability with a market return. i voted in favour of the proposal because it aims to create a regulatory framework for money market funds in order to ensure greater investor protection for mmfs and to improve financial stability. it shall also ensure that the liquidity of the fund is adequate to meet the demands of investors for repayment and to make the structure of the funds as secure as possible to withstand adverse market conditions. the proposal is in line with the commission's green paper (march 2012) on shadow banking.
in writing. ‒ for the single monetary funds to be able to fulfil their purpose effectively, it is necessary that the integrity and stability of the internal market be safeguarded by the implementation of uniform rules throughout the union. i have therefore decided to support the gill report, which aims to promote the establishment of a legal framework to ensure the proper management of the common monetary funds.
in writing. ‒ we believe it is important to regulate the monetary funds in europe, which are used by a significant proportion of industries, local authorities, charities and foundations as a tool to manage their excess liquidity. they provide an important source of short-term finance: in europe, about 22% of short-term debt securities issued by governments or the business sector are held by monetary funds. due to their systemic interconnection with the banking sector, they have often been identified as sensitive and highly risky instruments. this is a very controversial matter, but we believe that the time has come to give a uniform regulation to the sector.
in writing. ‒ mutual funds (mfis) are short-term cash management instruments characterised by high liquidity, diversification, value stability and market-based return. fcms are mainly used by companies wishing to invest excess liquidity for a short period, for example the time until a major expense such as payroll. these cash management instruments provide short-term financing to financial institutions, companies or public administrations on the one hand, and, by financing these entities, contribute to the financing of the european economy on the other. i voted in favour of the report by mrs neena gill on the referral of the draft legislation back to committee. i believe that it is important and necessary to establish a system of rules to protect investors and to strengthen financial stability by preventing the risk of contagion. i therefore believe that the sensitive points of the project need to be improved.
in writing. ‒ the emfs are of fundamental importance for the financing of the european economy because they provide short-term finance to financial institutions and companies. it is of paramount importance that they are regulated in a clear and comprehensible way because it has happened in the past, as in the case of the recent financial crisis, that they have shown some vulnerabilities, which can create further imbalances in the financial system. i therefore think it is right that there should be precise rules on fcms, to safeguard the stability of the eu's internal market and to ensure that all commitments are honoured even in difficult market situations.
in writing. ‒ after several months of negotiations, the european parliament finally voted in favour of a proposal, negotiated with the other political groups, which provides for the creation of a legal framework for the single monetary funds to ensure greater protection for investors, including from the risks of contagion, and to improve financial stability.
in writing. i decided to vote against because the common monetary funds with constant net asset value represent a potential risk, since they are unconnected with the market and its fluctuations. this would be essentially a shadow banking activity which, especially for italian local authorities in need of liquidity, could represent (as has already happened) an excessive risk.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the common monetary funds (cfm). i believe it is of great importance, in order to safeguard the position of investors, to clearly regulate the financial instruments in which the mmfs are allowed to invest, to provide for liquidity requirements to meet any redemption requests, to provide investors with transparent information on portfolio management and to provide for the implementation of stress tests to cope with different market scenarios. i hope that these measures will serve to increase the confidence of the citizens in the financial system.
in writing. on 29 april, the european parliament voted by a large majority to approve a measure which, instead of strictly regulating the 'shadow banking system', ends up introducing only marginal requirements which are too lenient in relation to the risk that 'shadow banks' pose to financial markets. again, another victory for the financial lobby. the rule specifically concerns cnavs, i.e. investment funds with constant net worth that contribute to generating and amplifying systemic risk and instability in the financial system. in order to mitigate systemic risk, we at m5s have called for the conversion of all cnavs into vnav funds and the elimination of instruments such as securitisations and unregulated derivatives. none of our amendments were incorporated in the text, which has actually deteriorated during the negotiations. even before the vote in plenary we tried to improve the text by asking for it. but it was useless. the text, which was blocked, was passed with the approval of all parties. the european union is a major player in the world economy, with a large number of its citizens living in poverty. the 'shadow banks' will therefore be able to continue to operate unhindered, with the same risks to market stability as before the crisis.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this measure which is supposed to regulate the so-called shadow banking system and in particular the common monetary funds (cmfs) because i believe that its text contains many non-shared elements. first of all, i would have liked to see securitisations and otc derivatives removed from the list of assets in which a mmf can invest. in addition, debt instruments guaranteed by the state authorities should not have been included among the eligible assets. i also believe that internal rating procedures are superfluous, as they are not transparent and therefore unreliable. this report ensures that cnavs remain free to operate in the eu while continuing to speculate on sovereign debt and small investors; i do not think it is appropriate to open up markets which are prone to speculation and the inherent instability of these short-term funds.

in writing. ‒ the proposal lays down quantitative limits and safeguards and surveillance instruments applicable to imports of textile products from third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols and other tariff preference schemes provided for by the union (i.e. belarus and north korea). the regulation also provides for the possibility of imposing control and surveillance measures if textile imports originating in the two countries threaten to cause significant damage to european production.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal concerns the codification of a regulation of march 1994 on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other provisions or by any other specific community import rules. those amendments are of a technical nature and are introduced following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, for the aspects related to comitology (delegated and implementing acts). i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i attach great importance to simplifying and clarifying the wording of eu legislation so that it is more understandable and accessible to citizens. this objective cannot be achieved as long as the innumerable provisions, which have been amended several times and often substantially, remain scattered, forcing those wishing to consult them to look for them both in the original act and in the amending acts. it is therefore essential to codify provisions which have been frequently amended if the legislation is to be clear and transparent. this regulation, concerning imports of textile products from certain third countries, was already subject to an alignment exercise following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon in order to ensure that all the amendments made to the text were brought together in a single act. i therefore voted in favour of the resolution because the new regulation replaces the various regulations it incorporates, preserves the substance of the acts being codified in full and therefore merely brings them together by making only the formal changes necessary for the purpose of the codification work.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the codification and recasting of the regulation on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries, which is not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other provisions or by any other specific community import rules; currently only belarus and north korea fall within that description. in particular, the regulation sets annual quantitative limits on imports of a number of textile products from these two countries and allows the introduction of union surveillance and safeguard measures. in addition, the regulation allows for the imposition of surveillance measures on other third countries where imports of textile products originating in those countries cause or threaten to cause serious injury to union production of like or directly competing products. as textiles are a sensitive sector of the european union's economy, i believe it is important that the rules applicable to them are as clear and simple as possible in order to ensure legal certainty. this operation is also in line with other actions to ensure that decision-making procedures in the area of trade policy are in line with the new regime of delegated and implementing acts introduced by the treaty of lisbon.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation on imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other provisions or by any other specific union import regime. this technical proposal aims to codify, together with the regulation on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries which are covered by union rules, two existing regulations on common rules for safeguard and surveillance measures which have been substantially amended over the years by adding certain technical corrections. the only countries from which the european union imports textiles and with which it has not concluded bilateral agreements, protocols or other specific provisions are belarus and north korea. the regulation lays down annual quantitative limits for imports of certain textile products from these two countries and allows for the establishment and implementation of european safeguard and surveillance measures where imports of textile products from third countries cause or threaten to cause serious damage to european production.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft resolution on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries, which are not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols or other provisions, nor by any other specific union import rules, as they contain no problematic provisions but only technical corrections, which are part of a positive overhaul and rationalisation of the existing legislation.

written declarations of vote
in writing. - i voted against it. i am voting against the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office. this mechanism implies a further loss of sovereignty for national parliaments. the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office does not seem to me to be in line with the principle of subsidiarity which should inspire european legislation.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the establishment by 2016 of a strong and independent european public prosecutor's office, capable of investigating, prosecuting and bringing to justice those responsible for offences affecting the eu's financial interests. the european public prosecutor's office must overcome the obstacles to crossborder judicial cooperation and pursue a common european policy because it is in the interest of citizens to have a system that works and protects the european budget. fraud in european funds and the regularity of procurement will be some of the areas of operation of the european public prosecutor's office. i believe that an innovative approach to investigating, prosecuting and bringing to justice those who commit fraud against the financial interests of the union is needed in order to increase the effectiveness of the fight against fraud, the recovery rate and taxpayers' confidence in the eu institutions. the european public prosecutor's office should not be a duplicate of national public prosecutor's offices. i think that the european public prosecutor's office should therefore determine, before the national authorities start their own investigations, whether the case falls within its competence, in order to avoid the inefficiency of parallel investigations.
in writing. ‒ the european ombudsman, which fights fraud against the eu's financial interests and thus against fraud perpetuated against all eu citizens, is certainly a priority. it is hoped that its remit will be extended to the fight against serious transnational crime, especially organised crime.
in writing. ‒ the measure in question concerns the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office. the added value of the eppo should be to converge criminal investigations and prosecutions into a single, independent office operating at european level for cases of fraud against union funds, and to strengthen criminal prosecutions, the recovery of funds and taxpayers' trust in the european institutions. the european public prosecutor's office (eppo), the establishment of which is also provided for in article 86 tfeu, would be composed of: the european public prosecutor's office shall be responsible for the prosecution of all criminal offences in the member states. i therefore decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office because i believe it is essential to bring together criminal investigations and prosecutions aimed at establishing fraud against the union in different countries in a single european office. this would allow the union to recover large sums of money, fraud is suspected to be worth some eur 500 million a year, although there are reasons to believe that the figure could be as high as eur 3 billion, but above all the trust of taxpayers in the european institutions. let us not forget that the union and the member states have an obligation under the treaties to combat fraud and other illegal activities which harm the financial interests of the union itself. in doing so, the eppo should be able to combine the effectiveness of prosecution of offences against the budget of the union with a high level of safeguards for the persons involved in the investigations. the differences between national laws must not create a breach in which crime can take root. this is why we must set up a single european prosecutor's office, which is strong and independent also from the member states themselves, where the current system, although functioning, has often proved ineffective.
in writing. ‒ the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office would lead to a further loss of sovereignty of the member states which have exclusive competence in criminal law, and would also give this body too wide powers, which is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this interim report because, in my opinion, the creation of a european public prosecutor will not only provide the eu with a more efficient system to fight fraud against eu funds, but also because it represents, another step towards a closer integration of the judicial systems of the member states. nonetheless i strongly believe that the european public prosecutor´s office should be independent from any kind of political influence.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the interim report by my colleague, ms monica mancovei, on the creation of a european public prosecutor's office. in order to provide adequate protection for the financial interests of the union, the amendment of the current regulatory framework appears to be more than necessary, especially in the light of the fact that the bodies currently in existence do not have effective powers of investigation and prosecution and that the work carried out by the prosecutors of the member states appears to be insufficient. the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office, with the power to investigate and prosecute before national courts offences affecting the financial interests of the union, will make it possible to combat fraud and illegal activities more effectively and to ensure equivalent protection of european interests in all member states. the compromise proposal on the governance structure of the institution, with a collegially composed central office, with a european prosecutor appointed by each member state, and the strengthening of the role of the permanent chambers is considered a good "point of balance" between supranational control and participation of the member states in the functioning of the office.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this interim report. the creation of a european criminal justice system, of which the establishment of a european public prosecutor is a key step, is a means of restoring and strengthening citizens' trust in the institutions and, more generally, in the eu apparatus as a whole. this support will also be necessary for the possible expansion of the offences prosecuted by the european public prosecutor, which we hope will happen with regard to offences related to organised crime, as provided for in article 86 tfeu. the report i am voting for sets out the political priorities of the european parliament and outlines the principles and conditions under which parliament could approve the legislator's proposal. in its resolution of 12 march 2014, parliament called on the council to involve it closely in its work and put forward a number of policy proposals on some of the most crucial issues at stake: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european data protection supervisor.
in writing. i am in favour of the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office because, to date, there is an alleged fraud against the financial interests of the union worth some eur 500 million per year. given that the indictment rate is only 31% (from 2006 to 2013) of the number of judicial recommendations addressed to member states by olaf, only the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office (eppo) could fill this gap. however, provided that the independence of the eppo (from any undue influence by political parties, national political, administrative or judicial authorities, including the european institutions) and the transparency of the procedures for its selection and appointment are guaranteed. in addition, in order to prevent any conflict of interests, parliament has called, by this resolution, for the european prosecutor to be appointed on a full-time basis. the european public prosecutor's office will therefore be a collegiate body composed of a european prosecutor per member state headed by a chief prosecutor and a competence shared between the new prosecutor's office and the national prosecution services. in this resolution, parliament called for the eppo to submit an annual report to the eu institutions in order to ensure transparency and evaluation of its work.

in writing. ‒ i am against the establishment of a european public prosecutor. our adversity has been long. fourteen chambers of the various sms expressed their opposition to this proposal, questioning its added value. as expressed in the reasoned opinions, the establishment of such a mechanism implies a further loss of sovereignty for national parliaments, by investing the eppo with overly broad powers, which go beyond the prerogatives of the member states and interfere in a matter of their competence, criminal law. despite the clarifications provided by the european commission in its review, the establishment of the european public prosecutor's office does not appear to be in line with the principle of subsidiarity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mrs macovei, which analyses the draft law establishing the european public prosecutor's office (eppo). each year the union loses at least eur 500 million in revenue and expenditure due to alleged cases of fraud. to close the loopholes that currently allow impunity for those who defraud the european taxpayer, the commission proposed the creation of an independent institution, the eppo, which would be tasked with bridging the gap between the criminal justice systems of european countries, whose powers are limited to national borders, and the eu bodies, which do not have the power to conduct criminal investigations. the added value of this office will be to converge criminal investigations and prosecutions into a single, independent, european-wide office for fraud cases involving union funds, and to strengthen criminal prosecutions, the recovery of funds and taxpayers' trust in the european institutions. the entire structure will draw on existing resources and should therefore not entail significant additional costs.

effectively address the challenge of food security. the initiative for this resolution was taken by the committee on agriculture, following a series of hearings and reflections on this subject, but it was then extended to include the contribution of many colleagues from a number of committees who wished to complement our work in a fruitful and effective way. food security is a matter of concern to all of us, and we cannot escape this global challenge which is affecting our agricultural and environmental policy, research, international trade and development policies. the growing demand for food is due both to a steadily increasing world population and to a change in eating habits in developing countries. we also observe the paradoxical coexistence of hunger in the world - without forgetting that too many people in europe are still living below the poverty line - and unbalanced diets that cause obesity even in poverty; at the same time, vast amounts of food are wasted in europe and around the world. the european commission itself estimates that 89 million tonnes of food are wasted in europe alone. i would remind you that this parliament, in the last parliament, already made a strong eradicate malnutrition. we need to set ambitious and binding targets to tackle food waste at every level of the food chain, from the field to the table. we need to increase transparency and fairness in the agri-food chain so that it can become truly sustainable and food secure. at the international level, we must do more as the european union to promote sustainable agriculture in developing countries and to combat land grabbing, namely the unregulated taking of land, particularly in africa. the european union will be present with its own pavilion at the expo, and a special steering committee chaired by former commissioner franz fischler has produced an interesting paper on the role of research in global food security. but today we are asking for something more, a more ambitious commitment. we need a strong and sustainable agricultural sector within the union, a development policy that is attentive to world agriculture, we need to fight against food waste and do more research member of the commission.– madam president, the commission welcomes the opportunity created by expo 2015 for an open debate on the global challenges related to food waste, sustainable agriculture and the need to fight hunger and eradicate obesity. we wish to reiterate our commitment to implementing eu policies and legislation to support sustainable food systems in close cooperation with the stakeholders, member states and the european parliament. the common agricultural policy has a great potential to make a real contribution to feeding the forecast 9 billion people by 2050, while taking care of natural resources. the principles of sustainability and producing more from less are well embedded in the long-term objectives of the common agricultural policy. concerning the point of the scarcity of natural resources in the 7th environment action programme to 2020, the european union is committed to protect, conserve and enhance the union’s natural capital. eu environment policy, and in particular the eu biodiversity strategy to 2020, the eu soil thematic strategy and eu legislation for the protection of water, air and natural habitats and species, aim at protecting, conserving and enhancing those natural resources to secure the provision of sustainable and healthy food production in the european union. in addition, sustainable food security is one of the major cross-cutting focus areas identified for research under the horizon 2020 work programme to continue until 2017. the commission is currently preparing an ambitious work programme and call for proposals on sustainable food security that aim to build more resilient and resource-efficient production and value chains. by promoting international collaboration, notably with china and africa, horizon 2020 research funding is expected to contribute to global food security. the european innovation partnership for agricultural productivity and sustainability is supported by the common agricultural policy and aims at closing the gap between research and practice. since 2012, the european commission has worked actively to identify the best possible action to take at eu level to fight food waste without compromising on food safety. the commission is committed to supporting the member states and stakeholders in their efforts to reduce food waste by helping to lift any obstacles and by promoting the sharing of best practice and transfer of knowledge and experience. at expo 2015, the commission will organise a conference dedicated to food waste prevention, focusing in particular on the importance of an effective intersectoral cooperation. the commission is committed to supporting the member states and stakeholders in strengthening resource efficiency in the food chain to prevent and reduce food waste from farm to fork. the commission is currently reflecting on the scope of the new, more ambitious circular economy package to be published by the end of this year, and will consider possible opportunities for action in the food sector as for all other sectors. any initiative taken at pan-european level has to have genuine eu added value. we will only take action where this can facilitate and augment ongoing action in the member states. while the promotion of healthy diets and lifestyles is a matter of national competence, the commission’s strategy on nutrition, overweight and obesity-related health issues and related implementing tools provide a framework and support to coordinate actions in the european union. it also promotes organic production with clear labelling rules, enabling customers to make an informed choice when making their purchases. i look forward to a debate on this important topic and i thank you.

author of the book. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, there is a phytosanitary emergency affecting olive trees in a part of the apulia region and which is of concern to the whole of europe. the spread of the quarantine pathogen xylella fastidiosa, subspecies pauca, is endangering apulian olive growing and has dramatic economic, environmental and social consequences. the european parliament, through the committee on agriculture, therefore immediately took the initiative of wanting to discuss the matter in this house, to express its concerns and to ask the commission for clarifications. in the meantime, just this week, the european commission's committee on plant health voted a decision which clarifies in part some of the issues we have raised. firstly, it shows that the xylella problem is a european problem and must be tackled by european decisions and not by national decisions. the first decision, which we welcome, is the ban on the import of coffee ornamental plants from costa rica and honduras. this shows that it is now clear that the source of entry of xylella subsp. pauca into europe was precisely that type of plant from those countries, as confirmed by the finding of these infected plants also in france. the real problem we have to consider is the need for stricter controls on imports of plant material from third countries, including for other types of diseases. we therefore ask the commission for its views on this matter. the commission's decision also takes strict measures which, while avoiding total eradication in the already infected area, which would not only be unnecessary but above all dramatic for an entire territory, its landscape, its economy and its rural environment, on the other hand, in order to block new outbreaks, it also requires, in compliance with international standards on quarantine pathogens, the eradication of certain healthy plants outside the aforementioned infected area (i.e. outside the province of lecce, for example). the two problems which the commission's decision does not solve and on which we would like to hear more commitments today are those of research and compensation to farmers. first, we need to continue to study this bacterium, which we don't know much about yet, and the possibility that we have of eradicating it. we need more public funds for this, and above all, mr president and commissioner, we need them as quickly as possible, as quickly as the spread of this bacterium can be. farmers, for their part, bear no responsibility for the spread of this pathogen, but suffer both the direct damage and the costs of implementing the measures necessary to contain the disease. that is why we are here today to ask the commission what compensatory measures it intends to give to the farmers who are the real victims of this annoying xylella.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopts a clear and distinct position on the alcohol strategy in the member states to address concerns about the misuse, unmoderate and irresponsible use of alcoholic beverages. there is no denying that harmful use of alcohol is still a cause of preventable death and a risk factor for many chronic diseases. however, an alcohol strategy in europe cannot ignore the excellence of many alcoholic beverages which are the envy of the world and which make up a large part of european exports to third countries. i am thinking of the quantity of wines and spirits with pgi, pdo and docg which, in my own country alone, enrich the cultural and historical heritage of each region and whose high quality and importance cannot be called into question, but must be protected and promoted. an alcohol strategy in europe must therefore take into account the prevention of alcohol-related diseases, but it cannot underestimate the importance and value of the agri-food sector linked to the production of alcoholic beverages. we cannot risk demonizing alcohol consumption at the expense of the cultural and socioeconomic heritage linked to wine production in many member states.
in writing. - my vote was negative. the resolution specifically calls for nutritional labelling for all alcoholics. this highly managerial and ethical approach is to be rejected for several reasons, not least because it ignores the cultural value that the (moderate and responsible) consumption of alcoholic beverages such as wine has in some european countries (italy above all). furthermore, nutrition labelling presupposes that the alcoholic beverage is consumed for food purposes, whereas today it is commonly understood as pleasure and proof of connection with the territory. this measure will ultimately benefit the large producers at the expense of the small ones.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of a new eu alcohol strategy. in europe, more than 7% of premature deaths are due to alcohol-related problems. twenty-five percent of young men between the ages of 15 and 29 lose their lives because of drinking too much. the commission must therefore start work on the new eu alcohol strategy (2016-2022) as soon as possible in order to add value to national policies. more can be done against drunk driving, effective data collection on alcohol consumption in all member states is needed, action is needed on alcohol advertising to minors, on alcohol consumption in pregnancy and on binge drinking which is increasingly taking hold among adolescents. however, a good compromise must also be found between the positions of countries such as great britain, where alcohol abuse is a serious problem of public health and order, and countries such as italy and belgium, where there is a real culture of the consumption of quality wine and beer. the aim of the strategy is not to discourage moderate consumption but to support the adoption of healthy lifestyles.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which will guide the european commission's work on this issue for the next seven years. the ppe has succeeded in getting article 23 rewritten, which was aimed at introducing a 'minimum price' which would be the same for all eu countries, i.e. an excise duty like that on cigarettes which, in addition to penalizing our producers with a higher tax burden, would have the effect of equating wine with tobacco, with the possibility of having repercussions in the future also in terms of labelling. the final vote in plenary has resulted in the amendment of two other important points. firstly, the blocking of the introduction of a minimum age for the purchase of alcoholic beverages throughout europe, which was set at 21 years. each state will therefore continue to decide for itself (in italy, for example, it is 18 years). secondly, we have removed from the text of the resolution the prohibition on using public funds to promote alcoholic beverages, and therefore wine. if this concept had been abandoned, we would no longer have been able to use european funds for the promotion of agricultural products, which have been and remain indispensable in making the excellence of 'made in italy' known throughout the world.

in writing. ‒ rana plaza, the building that housed textile factories that collapsed in bangladesh in 2013 causing over 1,100 deaths, represents the true face of globalization: the pursuit of the lowest cost and highest profit by moving production activities to places where workers are underpaid and have no rights. in the case of rana plaza, the desire to cut costs even led to the building's failure to heed the signs of collapse, which then collapsed on itself and on thousands of human lives. the true face of globalization is often hidden from the eyes of the western consumer. i therefore voted in favour of the amendments to explicitly include in the text of the resolution the names of trade marks relating to products manufactured at rana plaza and to include a binding clause on corporate social responsibility in the eu's trade and investment treaties with third countries. i also supported a specific text on the efdd rana plaza, which calls for the eu to set up a pilot project in bangladesh to produce clothes in full respect of human rights and to label these clothes so that european consumers can make informed choices.

in writing. ‒ on 18 april 2015, yet another tragedy occurred in the mediterranean sea: more than 700 migrants have lost their lives trying to reach the italian coast. another reason is that since the beginning of this year alone, more than 1,500 people have died in that stretch of sea. the text identifies several critical points in european policies for managing the flow of migrants. in particular, while eur 9 million was allocated to mare nostrum, an operation that saved 150,810 migrants in one year, only eur 2,9 million was allocated to triton, the new operation launched in november 2014. it is also rightly pointed out that europe as a whole must fight against those who are complaining about the desperation of migrants, but even more importantly, it is the union's duty to try to establish or restore a peaceful situation in the countries of origin. the call for europe to take a holistic approach to the situation and to be able to increase support for its member states which are most affected by the consequences of migration flows is also fundamental, for example with a serious plan for the sharing of asylum seekers. for these reasons, i am voting in favour.

in writing. ‒ the liberalisation of trade between the eu and the western balkan countries is ensured by a series of stabilisation and association agreements (saas) and an interim agreement (ia) in the case of bosnia and herzegovina. bosnia and herzegovina, like the balkan region as a whole, benefits from autonomous trade measures (atm). however, following the accession of croatia to the european union on 1 july 2013, bosnia and herzegovina has not yet agreed to adapt the interim agreement in order to take into account the preferential traditional trade between croatia and bosnia and herzegovina under the central european free trade agreement (cefta), which bound the two countries before 1 july 2013. after three rounds of negotiations with bosnia and herzegovina, no agreement was reached. in view of this deadlock, the commission proposes that the extension of the autonomous trade measures for bosnia and herzegovina should not be automatic but conditional on acceptance of the method used by the union for the adaptation of the interim agreement. once an agreement on the adjustment of trade concessions has been agreed, signed and provisionally applied by bosnia and herzegovina and the eu, the preferences for bosnia and herzegovina will be re-established. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the horrific massacre of christian students by the somali islamist group al shabaab on the campus of the university of garissa in kenya last april is a reminder that religious freedom in many parts of the world is still far too often at risk. it is even more disconcerting and reprehensible that this should be happening in places such as universities, where young people face the challenge of knowledge on a daily basis, experiencing living together and listening to each other. pope francis has repeatedly called on the international community not to remain silent and helpless in the face of such violence, and not to look the other way. the resolution expresses the european parliament's condolences and our strong support for the kenyan authorities in combating violence and its root causes and in supporting freedom of religion. the bloody persecutions by extremist groups, of which christians are often the victims, are a shock to the european parliament, which, together with the international community, must not remain indifferent. i therefore voted in favour of this important joint resolution.

in writing. ‒ today, 30 april 2015, the resolution on the destruction of cultural sites by isis/da'ish was voted. while strongly condemning the actions of isis and sharing several passages of the resolution, which i had a large and active role in drafting, i decided to abstain. as i have said, the central issue to be addressed and resolved is the theft and subsequent sale, on the various european black markets, of archaeological finds of enormous value. theft and illicit trafficking of artefacts are in fact encouraged by the state of war that - for the sake of objectivity and intellectual honesty - is raging not only in syria, libya and iraq, but also in other middle eastern and african states (but forgotten and left to themselves by the eu's inaction). what would be appropriate then is to put an immediate end to the armed conflict in those areas and to avoid military intervention which would further aggravate the situation. i asked for an amendment to include a passage of this kind, but unfortunately no other group supported my position. that explains my abstention.

in writing. ‒ cases of destruction and looting of sites and objects of cultural, archaeological and religious importance are becoming more frequent, especially in iraq and syria. these crimes are alarming because of the often irreparable damage they cause to the cultural heritage of all humanity, as well as to the identity and dignity of the communities and individuals most directly affected. the phenomena of looting and smuggling of these goods are very serious, all the more so as the profits often made by selling the items in europe contribute to the financing of terrorism. the resolution identifies and calls for concrete measures to combat these phenomena: security measures at the eu's external borders to prevent the illegal import of cultural goods; the allocation of a coordinating role to the commission, in cooperation with national authorities, europol, interpol, unesco and other international organisations; use of satellites to monitor and catalogue sites; supporting the activities of syrian archaeologists; training programmes for those involved in the fight against the smuggling of cultural goods; support to the international observatory on illicit trafficking in cultural property of icom; strengthening of the relevant eurojust and europol services. for these reasons, while stressing the need for effective sanctions also for the purchasers of stolen goods, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on progress made by albania in 2014. i have recently visited the country and have seen firsthand the progress made towards full european integration. the efforts made by the albanian authorities to bring their legislation fully into line with the requirements of the european union, which is a prerequisite for accession, are tangible. the recent adoption of the national plan for european integration 2014-2020 gives concrete expression to albania's will to take further steps forward on this path, through the implementation of economic, political and judicial criteria. the albanian government has demonstrated the political will to act to combat corruption and organised crime. in many areas, the strengthening of legislation in this area has shown a positive trend, especially in the fight against drugs and human trafficking. in general, the rights of disabled people, lgbti people, children and minorities are substantially respected, although more efforts are needed in this regard. there are certainly many issues to be tackled, such as the environment and the diversification of energy sources, which are vital to economic development and to greater transparency, especially in the management of public finances.

in writing. ‒ we want to highlight the valuable role played by the eib in supporting social cohesion in the eu. we call for its resources to be mobilised to encourage and incentivise public and private investment, promote competitiveness, restore sustainable and inclusive growth and stimulate the creation of quality employment in line with the europe 2020 strategy. the eib should continue to play its role as a catalyst for financing long-term public and private investment, with a consequent positive effect on lending conditions. we expect the investment plan promoted by juncker to facilitate access to finance in member states and regions with high levels of unemployment and a gdp per capita below the eu average, recalling in this connection that it is essential for the eib to cooperate with european funds in order to allow productive public investment and key infrastructure projects to be carried out. we expect priority to be given to projects with clear european added value, respecting the principle of additionality, and a positive cost-benefit analysis. we stress the importance of implementing projects which have the greatest impact in terms of job creation, projects with a higher risk which could not be funded otherwise.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament presented an own-initiative report this year, analysing aspects of the eib's activities. the text we have approved today contains many criticisms, which i share, such as the condemnation of the management of the castor project in spain and the passante di mestre in italy. i regret that the eib financed the section of the motorway known as passante di mestre after the italian authorities had publicly announced the arrest for tax fraud of the chief executive of the main subcontractor. i therefore believe that the eib should ensure that a zero-tolerance policy is applied to fraud when it is considering the use of bond loans to finance projects. i am therefore glad that these points have been included in the report, which i have supported.
