in writing. i am sure that the motion for a resolution on expo milano 2015 'feeding the planet, energy for life' represents a great opportunity for italy and europe to re-launch and to enhance its many productive, technological and scientific excellence. the themes covered are varied: the food production and distribution, the problem of food waste, the protection of biodiversity, the great challenge of sustainability, malnutrition and land grabbing. therefore, expo 2015 will allow to address these issues at the highest level of scientific knowledge.
in writing. ‒ expo milano 2015 provides the opportunity for the entire international community to reflect on the big issues related to nutrition, the environment and research. the european parliament has expressed its willingness to be involved in this great debate by this resolution. the problems of food scarcity and the unstoppable growth of the world's population require special attention. for these reasons i voted in favour of this text, which calls for the proper and responsible use of food and environmental resources.
in writing. ‒ this will be a very important week for lombardy, italy and the european union: on friday, expo 2015 will finally be opened in milan. the event, which is significant in itself, is of particular importance both for the theme chosen and for the particular historical moment in which it takes place. the theme 'feeding the planet, energy for life' aims to draw attention, through a series of thematic exhibitions, to food-related culture and traditions, raising the much-needed debate on sustainable global growth based on strengthening food security, preserving biodiversity and combating waste, malnutrition and child mortality. at the same time as expo, the adoption of the milan charter, an international agreement that aims to combat the problem of environmental sustainability, is a clear example of the fact that the mission of the event will not end on october 31, but that on the contrary expo milano wants to be the beginning of a long journey with high objectives. the unique structure of the expo makes it a truly european event: for six months, the pavilions of 137 countries will not be in milan, but in the european union as a whole.
in writing. ‒ considering that the theme of expo milano 2015 is 'feeding the planet, energy for life' and that the event can give a strong impetus to the debate aimed at improving food production and distribution, addressing the problem of food waste, promoting and developing already existing positive approaches to meet the challenge of food insecurity, malnutrition and malnutrition, as well as creating a balance between the availability and consumption of resources, i decided to support the resolution, considering that the fight against malnutrition and ensuring universal access to adequate nutritious food should continue to be a key objective of the post-2015 agenda in the context of the goal of the elimination of hunger, specifically calling for the need to end all forms of malnutrition by 2030.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution because the theme of the 2015 world expo offers the european union an opportunity to reflect on the current food landscape. nearly a billion people are undernourished, while a third of the food produced worldwide is wasted. in the light of this stark contrast, i believe that europe must make food security one of its priorities, especially in conjunction with the european year of development. the member states must act on two fronts: introduce measures for more sustainable agriculture and measures to reduce food waste, in order to eradicate hunger and ensure a fair extension of the human right to food. i am convinced that expo milano can be an important forum for meeting, fostering the generation of ideas and the exchange of good practice between european and global voices.
in writing. ‒ i thank the rapporteur for the work he has done and hope that i have made a contribution.
in writing. ‒ expo milano 2015, in addition to being a great opportunity to revive the city of milan and the whole of italy, must first of all be a great opportunity to revive the international fight against hunger, against the problem of malnutrition, malnutrition and obesity. i voted in favour of this resolution to ask the european commission, the council and all the participating states to use the theme of expo 'feeding the planet, energy for life' to set commitments to uphold the right to adequate, healthy, sustainable and informed food. the european union, which will be represented at the exhibition with its own pavilion, must do more to find solutions to the pressing problems affecting the entire food supply chain. too many people in europe and the world still live below the poverty line, but at the same time 30% of the world's food is wasted and hunger coexists with paradoxical levels of obesity. the eu must draw real contributions from the milan event to the global challenge of food security.
in writing. ‒ the theme chosen for the expo is of the utmost importance to make everyone aware of the absolute priority importance of food and nutrition for the planet. i hope that solutions will be found to improve food production and distribution, to reduce waste in the industrialized countries and to consciously address the challenges of food security, malnutrition and the balance between the availability and consumption of resources. the expo is a global and worldwide platform where different stakeholders are given the opportunity to come together to find valid solutions to the great challenges of nutrition and food in a world where there are still strong contradictions between people who are malnourished and others who suffer from health disorders due to overeating. let us remember that according to fao estimates, the world's population will increase rapidly and the increase in food production will not be enough to ensure food security for all. this is the main challenge that must be faced and solved.
in writing. ‒ the text of the resolution, which i voted in favour of, is the result of the european parliament's desire to give a strong impetus to the debate on improving food production and distribution. we have therefore asked the european commission to tackle more concretely the problem of food waste, malnutrition and the balance between the food available and its consumption. we are in a world where many people are starving and many more are suffering from the opposite problem, and that should not be happening.
in writing. i decided to vote in favour because the resolution is a detailed manifesto of the main 'key issues' in the agri-food sector and mentions the main 'political' issues concerning food and its agricultural production. that said, there are still a number of unknowns about expo, starting with how well it will be able to address the "real" issue, to chart a path for a sustainable response to the issue of food supply, which urgently needs innovation from the agricultural and agro-industrial supply chain. the imbalances between the various actors in the food chain and the access to food of the people of developing countries should be some of the issues to be tackled with great seriousness.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on expo milano 2015, to ask the commission to use this event as a moment to disseminate european best practice in nutrition and food safety, also in the light of the fact that agriculture is a strategic sector of the eu which requires a lot of eu resources. we have the opportunity today to make the world aware of the very high safety standards of european production and the quality and health of our food. i also urge the union to continue to promote and implement sustainable agri-food policies that encourage lower production costs, less food waste, the transfer of technological innovations and efficient use of energy resources.
in writing. ‒ i did not vote in favour of the resolution on expo milano 2015 because those amendments which called for the inclusion in the resolution of the principles of transparency, sustainability and protection of small farmers were not passed. i voted in favour of those amendments which stressed the need to promote a diet which is able to ensure a more rational and sustainable consumption of food resources. so no to those high-calorie foods, rich in fat, sugar and salt and lacking in micronutrients, which are the main causes of obesity. i therefore regret that the amendments which highlighted the scandalous sponsorship of multinational corporations (mcdonald's, coca cola and nestlé ferrero), the main producers of junk food, notorious for not guaranteeing sustainable food, were not passed. the expo should be an opportunity to discuss and share best practices in sustainable agriculture and promote small farms. i voted in favour of the amendment which denounced the mismanagement of contracts by allowing criminal organisations to infiltrate infrastructure works. i also voted in favour of the amendment which includes respect for social and labour rights within the principle of sustainability. it is not acceptable that paid employment should be replaced by precarious and 'voluntary' work.
in writing. i voted against the motion for a resolution because three very important key points were not passed. parliament did not object to the fact that expo 2015 is sponsored by international companies such as mcdonald's and coca cola, which produce foods that are high in fat and low in micronutrients, in contrast to the need to promote healthier eating behaviour. the amendment proposed by our group, which was initially passed to the committee on agriculture and was withdrawn at the plenary stage, called on the commission to orient eu food policies towards forms of greater sustainability along the whole supply chain, favouring 'zero-kilometre' distribution and organic and biodynamic production. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. for the reasons stated above, i did not support the report.
in writing. ‒ i think it is frankly inappropriate that the expo in milan, whose theme is "feeding the planet: energy for life", uses as its sponsor mcdonald's, a company that offends and ridicules the flagship of italian gastronomy and that is certainly not one of the symbols of adequate, healthy, sustainable and informed nutrition promoted by the expo. this universal exposition could have been a great opportunity for italy, a way to attract investment and give a boost to the economy, but unfortunately, soon there were malicious infiltrations, lobbying interests and contracts under investigation. the initial project seemed designed to create a widespread and sustainable expo, but unfortunately it was not so: over two million square metres of land and hundreds of kilometres of motorways have been cemented, when i would have expected more renovation and reuse of abandoned buildings, redevelopment of derelict areas and use of existing exhibition spaces. it could have been an opportunity to turn milan into an example for others, to which citizens could contribute with pride, but instead it is turning out to be a speculative finance operation.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution milano expo 2015, a document that addresses food issues with a multidimensional approach. i think it is appropriate to urge the commission to come forward with policies that ensure the stability and sustainability of agricultural production systems and promote a more efficient use of resources. i conclude by wishing that the commission, together with the fao, will do its utmost to encourage the worldwide implementation of the guidelines for responsible governance of land, fisheries and forest ownership in the context of national food security.

in writing. ‒ considering that the peace and stability of nigeria is increasingly threatened by the islamist militant group boko haram, which has been wreaking havoc in the country since 2009 by carrying out bombings, assassinations and kidnappings in an attempt to impose a strict form of sharia law, overthrow the government and create an islamic state, i have decided to vote in favour of the resolution as i believe that the international community must react and not stand idly by in the face of such acts of violence. finally, i believe that the european union and its member states must respect their commitment to provide various forms of political, development and humanitarian aid to the country and its people and not leave them alone in the fight against the threat of boko haram.

in writing. ‒ the attacks by boko haram militants between 3 and 8 january 2015, which targeted the town of baga and 16 surrounding towns and villages in northeastern nigeria, destroying nearly 3,700 structures and killing more than 2,000 people, represented the deadliest massacre by the terrorist group, which is engaged in a full-scale war with the nigerian government. this resolution expresses total condemnation of the barbarism and atrocities which the nigerian people, without any discrimination - christians, muslims, teachers, students, farmers, shopkeepers, women and children - have been forced to endure for too long, and expresses support for the new government and the new president buhari elected on 14 february, whose victory represents a turning point for nigeria and for the whole of africa. the eu will support the new government to take greater responsibility in taking concrete action to combat terrorism, corruption, poverty and inequalities in the country and to give back a future and hope to the nigerian people.
in writing. ‒ i am very concerned about the recent escalation of violence in nigeria by the terrorist sect boko haram, which indiscriminately targets civilians, government and military targets with attacks carried out with firearms and bombs, causing massacres of men, women and children and a high number of displaced persons. the newly elected president must take drastic action to end the violence that the boko haram sect is perpetrating in the country. nigeria needs to restore a climate of stability and security and take measures to combat corruption and inefficiency in public institutions, which are one of the main causes of the boko haram outbreak. i hope that the nigerian authorities will respond decisively to the terrorist threat and address the issues of primary need for the country, such as poverty and existing inequality, child labour and access to health care, by establishing a roadmap for more evenly developing the southern and northern parts of the country.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it seems to be destiny that yarmouk should be a place of history. nearly 1,400 years ago, a decisive battle was fought there between the byzantines and the real caliphate, today there is a much more perverse one in which the parties are increasingly confused. to know what it's like in yarmouk, you turn off the lights, the water, the heating, you eat once a day and live in the dark, so a refugee rightly describes daily life in that camp. the eu is providing only 2.5 of the 30 million needed, according to unrwa estimates, to finance the management of the ongoing humanitarian crisis. in yarmouk people are suffering and dying and the fact that our states and the arab states are not fulfilling their commitments is a shame that weighs like a stone on our consciences, but i also remember that if we had enforced the un resolutions, if we had really pushed as a union to solve the palestinian question and the shame of gaza with a two-state solution, yarmouk would not exist today and so perhaps we also have much to protest to our conscience.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, since 1957 150 000 palestinians have found refuge in the yarmouk refugee camp on the outskirts of damascus in syria. on april 1st, the camp was occupied by isis guerrillas and the refugees have been living under government missiles and the terror that the islamic state militants are spreading among the starving and fearful population for days. the situation in the refugee camp is beyond inhuman. since the start of the clashes, food, water and medicine have not arrived, and thousands of palestinians, including hundreds of children, are at risk of dying of hunger and thirst, not to mention the summary executions of the last few days. unicef is concerned about the fate of the 3,500 children still in the camp. the un and the international community must be concerned with providing protection and meeting the humanitarian needs of the palestinian refugees in yarmouk and all other camps. europe and the international community must quickly get all parties to the conflict to agree to a ceasefire that will allow aid to be brought into yarmouk and the evacuation of children and wounded families.

(the president agreed to reply to a question with a blue card (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
answer to a blue-card question. on rübig, i am happy to answer your question. i share the concern about the effects that such a procedure may have on smes, on small and mediumsized enterprises, and sometimes i find it difficult to answer this question because, unfortunately, we have always seen good intentions have consequences that are not up to our standards. i think this is the right road. i think the first concern we must have is to force the credit institutions of the european union to put small and mediumsized enterprises back at the centre of their attention. what do you mean, "what"? how can this be achieved? it also goes through a radical overhaul of the governance structure of credit institutions at the european level, not just through the redefinition of financial benchmarks.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the financial markets have repeatedly seen the manipulation of reference values for the determination of interest rates such as libor and euribor. such manipulation, by demonstrating that benchmarks can be subject to conflicts of interest and vulnerability, is a major driver of economic imbalances and causes considerable losses to consumers and investors, as well as destroying citizens' confidence in the financial sector. it is therefore clearly appropriate to restore confidence in the benchmarks, but not to confine ourselves to simply recognising the illegality of such behaviour. i therefore agree with the report, which considers that governance measures need to be improved and conflicts of interest mitigated, and which also aims to enhance transparency and the implementation of access to a wide variety of values by applying governance requirements in a proportionate manner. increased, harmonised and flexible availability of benchmarks is needed to reduce the systemic importance of some large values, so as to allow, in a proportionate and transparent way, all those who do business, invest, take a risk, obtain credit, to make informed decisions every day.
on behalf of the efdd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too would like to congratulate the rapporteur, the shadow rapporteurs and the non-governmental organisations who have helped to draw up this report. we are talking about development finance and the addis ababa conference. it is important that we come to this conference with a strong, decisive and clear position because, probably, it is not yet very clear, when discussing the problems of the world, the importance of development cooperation. today, as today, we are constantly witnessing tragedies linked to immigration, linked precisely to the trafficking of people and to the continuous deaths in the mediterranean. perhaps if more attention had been paid to development cooperation in the developing countries, in the countries of refuge, in the countries of transit, these tragedies could have been dealt with differently. we know very well - it is useless to go around - that very often our own countries go to these countries to exploit resources, to generate civil wars. and then we find ourselves, as mr neuser rightly said, talking about official development finance with the richest countries in europe, including germany, which does not even want to put in 0.7% of gross national income and is limited to 0.4. we therefore hope that the council will reach a common position and that this type of assistance will be made compulsory. i believe that in addition to official financing there is a kind of unconventional financing, alternative financing which the states support when requested by the multinationals of the same states who have an interest in going to create their own type of development in these countries. we hope that this will be a step towards decisive action by this conference.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too congratulate the rapporteur and those who have worked with him on this report. the year 2015 could be a turning point. in september, at the un, we should agree on new sustainable development goals that apply to everyone. the new agenda must be ambitious, but to make sure that these goals are actually achieved, including the unfinished work of the millennium development goals, we must have the resources to do so. the report by mr silva pereira makes this quite clear: the success of the post-2015 agenda will also depend on the level of ambition demonstrated at the addis ababa conference. and if we are to claim europe's primacy as the leading donor, we must commit ourselves once again to devoting 0.7% of gross national income to official development aid, presenting a timetable of steps to achieve this objective, which must not be conditioned by other donors. equally important, as the report points out, is the mobilisation of national resources, the most important source of finance for developing countries; we must strengthen international cooperation in tax matters and aid to this end: this is essential not only for achieving new objectives but also for overcoming dependence on foreign aid in the long term. the commission has also been very active in the fight against fraud, and i am sure that the commission will be very active in this area. the fight against these practices must be a priority for the european union. i have heard what the commissioner has said, and we will certainly talk about it again, but i think it is important that we finally talk about a genuine intergovernmental body where developing countries can participate on equal terms in rewriting the global tax rules.

in writing. member states have received €2 billion from tobacco companies over the past decade to fight cigarette smuggling. this huge contribution comes from agreements reached following a legal action brought by the european commission against philip morris, which was abandoned in 2004 after philip morris agreed to give €1 billion over 12 years to europe. later, other large tobacco companies entered into similar agreements. 90% of these funds were distributed to the member states, but it remains unknown how they actually used these funds. smoking is the leading preventable cause of death in the eu and causes about 700 000 deaths every year. the treatment of patients with diseases attributable to tobacco smoking costs hospitals around eur 3.4 billion, while the total healthcare costs are over eur 7.5 billion. the commission does not yet know whether it will renew these agreements: in any case, i think that the rules on data transparency need to be revised. where have these funds been spent? what action have member states taken to prevent the circulation of contraband and counterfeit goods? how many of the seized cigarettes came directly from the manufacturing companies?

in writing. the important dossier on the proposal for a regulation establishing a european system of self-certification for importers of certain minerals or metals originating in conflict-affected and high-risk areas, known as conflict minerals, was discussed and voted at this plenary session. the debate and subsequent vote focused on one particular point which proved to be controversial: extend traceability (self-certification) obligations not only to smelters, refiners and importers of certain minerals, but also to small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in the supply chain. this was considered by many to be essential to make effective the traceability obligations imposed on the main actors in the supply chain, which would otherwise be de facto easily circumvented. a company would have every interest in, and the real possibility of, accessing the more advantageous black market if it were to act on a voluntary basis in declaring and guaranteeing the origin of minerals. the debate was very heated and emotional and some, entrenched behind a ghostly administrative burden for smes, wanted to oppose the obligation of traceability for smes as well. fortunately, and thanks also to the work of the five star movement, the result of the vote was positive, preventing such an absurdity.

in writing. ‒ the vote on the report signed by liberal mep van nieuwenhuizen is positive. this is a regulatory text updating the rules on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments to improve transparency. the requests from some groups to delete parts of the text are improving.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. the manipulation of libor and currency benchmarks, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, have highlighted the importance of benchmarks as well as their vulnerability. the objectives of this report are therefore to strengthen governance systems and standards, to enhance transparency by making more information available to users of all benchmarks and to maintain the supply of and access to a wide variety of benchmarks by applying governance requirements in a proportionate manner. this would reduce the vulnerability to manipulation and abuse of widely used and systemically important benchmarks, increase the possibility for users to make informed choices and ensure a level playing field for all administrators, both eu and third country. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ although the text voted today is a significant improvement on the european commission's initial proposal, there are major weaknesses in some key areas, including insufficient administrative sanctions and exemptions for central banks, public authorities, central counterparties and also the media. i therefore voted against this draft legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation.
in writing. ‒ the manipulation of libor and currency benchmarks, as well as the alleged manipulation of other indices, have highlighted the importance of benchmarks and their vulnerability. in response to these revelations, the eu amended its market abuse legislation to clarify that the manipulation of benchmarks is illegal and to criminalise such conduct. in the light of these considerations, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. i believe that it introduces important measures to improve the accuracy and reliability of financial indices and, above all, fills a gap in european legislation by creating a uniform treatment between member states. in particular, this regulation aims to achieve three fundamental objectives: strengthen governance systems and standards to reduce vulnerability to manipulation and abuse; enhance transparency by informing users and making all benchmarks available to them so that they can make informed decisions; maintain the supply of and access to a wide variety of benchmarks, applying governance requirements in a proportionate manner, including by ensuring a level playing field for all administrators, both eu and third country. therefore, in order to ensure the proper functioning of the internal market and to improve the conditions for its operation, in particular of financial markets, and to ensure a high level of consumer and investor protection, i welcome the formulation of a regulatory framework for benchmarks at union level.
in writing. ‒ indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. the vote was negative because, although parliament's text is significantly improved on the commission's initial proposal, there are still important criticisms, among which we would point out an overly broad scope. the regulation exempts central banks, public authorities, central counterparties and also the media; certain exemptions for non-critical benchmark administrators have been introduced with regard to governance, conflict of interest management, transparency and breach reporting. moreover, the thresholds for judging a critical benchmark are too high (eur 5 billion) and the administrative penalties are too low.
in writing. ‒ following the scandals that resulted in millions of euro fines for several banks in europe and the us, the commission published a draft regulation on a wide range of benchmarks (interest rates and commodities) to address possible shortcomings at every stage of the production and use of benchmarks. doubts about the integrity of benchmarks can undermine market confidence, cause losses for consumers and investors and distort the real economy. the commission's text has been considerably improved by a number of amendments, particularly with regard to the definition of non-critical benchmarks, which in the first version was too light and therefore too unbalanced. the vote in favour was for a text which represents a good starting point for future negotiations with the council.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on benchmarks is part of the wider range of legislative measures to overcome the critical issues in the capital market. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the aid granted to the sampled exporting producers. this was a particularly serious act given the overall impact on financial markets. in addition to the construction and implementation of legislative measures on the most important financial infrastructures, this proposal also solves the major problem of monitoring indices. it was a very difficult negotiation: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the two major issues of the recognition of third country benchmarks and the definition of critical and non-critical benchmarks were addressed by a highly pragmatic approach, which, however, limited the scope of the proposal for a regulation. i am voting in favour of this proposal, since the total absence of regulation would lead to further criticism on the financial markets, but i hope that the institutions will make a greater effort to include in a balanced dimension some of the unresolved issues.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report signed by my liberal colleague, mrs van nieuwenhuizen. this text updates the rules on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments with greater transparency.
in writing. ‒ the abuses of indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts affect not only investors but all european citizens. unfortunately, self-regulation has not brought the desired results. governance that can effectively counter the risks of manipulation is therefore essential to make these instruments sound and reliable. that is why i voted in favour of the proposed regulation and will continue to ensure that the principles of independence and the protection of citizens remain at the heart of this reform.
in writing. the proposal put forward by mrs cora van nieuwenhuizen on the regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts deserves our attention. this is a very important measure, which aims to solve those serious cases of manipulation of reference values for the determination of interest rates, such as libor and euribor, and of reference values for currencies, which in recent years have caused considerable losses to consumers and investors, as well as destroying the confidence of citizens in the financial sector. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal with conviction, as part of the many efforts europe is making to restore confidence and rules to the economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's position on the calculation of indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts as the fundamental objective of the legislative proposal is to increase transparency and reduce conflicts of interest in particular for 'systemically important' indices such as libor and euribor. the influence they have on financial instruments and contracts - i am thinking of mortgage loans for example - is of great importance. they are collectively worth less than eur 500 billion and could therefore jeopardise the stability of financial markets in the european union. hence the need to distinguish within them between national or european-scale indices of systemic importance, which esma will be called upon to monitor, and non-systemic indices. the recent scandals involving european banks, duly sanctioned by the competent authorities, must be the starting point for legislation ensuring the integrity of benchmarks; accordingly, their directors should be required to implement appropriate governance to control conflicts of interest and to safeguard confidence in the integrity of benchmarks. i hope that the negotiations with the council will be concluded successfully in the short term.
in writing. i have given my consent to the report put to the vote today. the pricing of many financial instruments and contracts depends on the accuracy and integrity of the benchmarks. serious cases of manipulation of those securities demonstrate that they may be subject to conflicts of interest and have discretionary and weak governance regimes that are vulnerable to manipulation. in response, the eu amended the market abuse legislation to punish such conduct (updated vote under article 61 (2) of the regulation).
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation introduces a common framework to ensure the accuracy and integrity of indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. the integrity of benchmarks is crucial for the pricing of many financial instruments such as risk management, commercial and non-commercial contracts, loans and mortgages, etc. any risk of manipulation of benchmarks can undermine market confidence, cause significant losses for investors and distort the real economy. i voted in favour of the text because i believe that this eu regulation is necessary to improve the functioning and governance of benchmarks and to ensure that these benchmarks are robust, reliable, representative and not subject to manipulation. we now await negotiations with the council for a final legislative text with broad agreement.
in writing. ‒ we support the report on the proposal for a regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts and welcome it in particular in the light of the recent manipulation of libor and other currency benchmarks, which has highlighted the importance and vulnerability of these values. we agree with the rapporteur in identifying the three main objectives of future regulation, namely strengthening governance systems and standards, increasing transparency and maintaining a wide range of benchmarks, which guarantees a level playing field for eu and non-eu administrators. we particularly welcome the balancing of requirements between critical and non-critical benchmarks, which we believe is a good compromise that can be used to the best advantage in the negotiations with the council. the requirements shall include a proportionate approach that takes into account the different markets and economic realities involved using different types of data. it is necessary to establish a set of criteria valid throughout the union, including the possibility to determine critical reference values for member states in cases where values are not displayed in more than one member state.
in writing. ‒ i believe that there was an objective need for a proposal, to which i voted in favour, to regulate indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts. to date, supervisors only supervise financial instruments, but not the production and governance of the indices that determine the risk profile and economic value of those instruments. since the use of indices is now indispensable as a reference for financial instruments, regulation was necessary.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts because i think that a very good job has been done in compiling this report. the report respects the objective we have set ourselves, in other words to restore a climate of confidence. if we were to turn to psychological terrorism in the face of such reprehensible scandals, we would be abandoning our political task. in my view, this work has as its point of balance the excellent choice of identifying what are the distinctions between critical indices and indices not considered as such. the approach taken is the right one: the solution to the problem, not the activation of further terror, of further mistrust.
in writing. i voted in favour of the regulation because it provides for greater transparency in the rules on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments.
in writing. on 19 may, the european parliament approved by a large majority a measure which would have regulated at european level the indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments, the so-called benchmarks. this need arose following the recent euribor and libor manipulation scandals involving some large banks. the objective of the regulation was to prevent any future manipulation of benchmarks in order to preserve consumers and the integrity of financial markets. unfortunately, the text that has been adopted will not achieve this because of the excessive and unjustified exemptions that have been introduced. the regulation does not apply to central banks, public authorities, central counterparties or the media. however, exemptions have been introduced for certain administrators of benchmarks on governance, conflict of interest management, transparency and breach reporting. finally, the thresholds for judging a benchmark to be 'critical' have been set too high (eur 5 billion) and the administrative penalties are too low. we in the m5s have tried to improve the text, not only in the econ committee but also before the vote in plenary, by asking at least to remove all the exemptions. but it was useless. this is yet another proof of the lack of will to give concrete answers to the problems of the real economy.
in writing. ‒ the recent scandals involving the manipulation of the euribor and libor rates by some large banks have necessitated specific regulation of benchmarks at european level. the aim of the regulation is therefore to prevent the manipulation of benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts in order to protect consumers and the integrity of the financial market. i have nevertheless not supported this report because, although parliament's text is significantly improved on the commission's original proposal, there are still important criticisms. firstly, i think that the scope of the directive is too broad. the regulation exempts central banks, public authorities, central counterparties and the media. in addition, certain exemptions have been introduced for non-critical benchmark administrators with regard to governance, conflict of interest management, transparency and breach reporting. moreover, the thresholds for judging a critical benchmark are too high (eur 5 billion) and the administrative penalties too low.
in writing. ‒ the report is shared, balanced and free from criticism. that is why i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on financing for development. i agree with the report, which welcomes the preliminary draft outcome document of the third international conference on financing for development in addis ababa, which has the ambitious task of setting the level of intervention in the next agenda on the subject. i believe that the right conditions for the eradication of poverty and inequality can be achieved above all through a universal, holistic and integrated approach, including the control and monitoring by the commission of the financing of aid programmes and projects in the fields of health, education, energy, water supply and infrastructure. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will be consulted on the matter.
in writing. ‒ the report by mr pedro silva pereira will represent the european parliament's position at the third conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa from 13 to 16 july 2015. this conference will be a key step in supporting the implementation of the sustainable development goals (sdgs) as it will have to create the conditions for financing and implementing the so-called post-2015 agenda. the european parliament's text reaffirms the commitment of the member states at the 2002 monterrey conference to allocate 0.7% of gross national income (gni) to development aid (daa), but also supports the need to create new and additional sources of financing. i am therefore glad that i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union has been and remains the world's largest donor of development aid, providing around 60% of the world's official development assistance. the awareness that there are resources potentially sufficient to abolish poverty conditions worldwide requires that funding be provided to ensure gradual but continuous development, including widespread education and a general improvement in living standards. long-term financial needs must be taken into account by effective programming and by promoting cooperation channels between the various state entities. i therefore believe it is important to look to the commission and parliament for greater support in the areas of tax administration, financial governance and public financial management, and the fight against tax evasion. the mobilisation of national resources and international public funding is a key factor in enabling the european union to play more effectively the role of promoting development at global level which is inherent in its founding values. i have found many points of agreement between the report under discussion and my own views, and i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ 2015 is a pivotal year for global development efforts, with the adoption of the sustainable development goals (sdgs), the global climate action agreement (both valid until 2030), and the third international conference on financing for development, to be held in addis ababa, ethiopia, from 13 to 16 july 2015. the union is the world's largest donor of development aid, providing some 60% of the total. the current budget allocates some €60 billion to development, divided between development cooperation (19.7 billion), humanitarian aid for the period 2014-2020 (6.8 billion), the emergency aid reserve (2.2 billion) and the european development fund (edf) of €30.5 billion. however, many member states have not committed to the 0,7% of gross national income development target and therefore the measure in question calls on them to present (taking into account budgetary constraints) multiannual calendars in order to achieve this target by 2020. in the light of these considerations, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ 2015 is a pivotal year for europe's political leadership in defining a framework for sustainable development and climate action. this is an ambitious objective and as such requires a strong and comprehensive partnership involving the use of various forms of funding. i believe that the eradication of poverty and inequality is only possible through the mobilisation of sufficient and appropriate resources, which ensure targeted interventions to support the most vulnerable groups. in the light of these considerations, i have decided to vote in favour of this report, so that the member states can maintain their role as the main donors and at the same time urge the sgp to share the responsibilities.
in writing. ‒ the report represents the european parliament's position at the third conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa. the addis ababa conference will be an important contribution to supporting the implementation of the sustainable development goals (sdgs). in a context of financial crisis, where member states are increasingly reluctant to honour the commitment made at the 2002 monterrey conference to commit 0.7% of gross national income (gni) to development aid (daa), the report adopted by the deve committee sends a positive signal in terms of the objectives to be achieved by the conference, including the need to create new and additional sources of funding. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the millennium development goals, adopted in 2000 by world leaders to reduce poverty, were to be achieved by 2015. unfortunately, we are still far from achieving them: 1.5 billion people still live in poverty, mainly in conflict-affected states; the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of poverty. unfortunately, very few industrialized countries are meeting their commitment to allocate 0.7% of their gnp to official development aid. this is the starting point, and we must ensure that the budgetary constraints imposed do not penalise this type of intervention, and at the same time intensify the search for alternative sources and resources, including the financial transaction tax. we also need to learn from the past to build strategies based on sound analysis, which set politically acceptable and decisive global development goals to eradicate poverty. at the same time, the non-financial means and methods of implementation shall be indicated. as the largest contributor of development aid, the eu must claim and play a leading role in this process.
in writing. 2015 is also the year of the third international conference on financing for development, to be held in addis ababa in july, at which the new sustainable development goals will be defined. the broad and cross-cutting support for the report on financing for development, with which parliament expressed its support for the eu's position in the run-up to the conference, demonstrates the importance of this issue for the european union as a whole. parliament strongly advocated that the eu should continue to play a leading role in development policies and remain the world's leading donor of development aid, renewing commitments already made and calling for a genuine sharing of responsibilities between member states. the eu will need to work with developing countries to develop a more robust and accountable investment regulatory framework, taking into account innovative financing modalities such as public-private partnerships that balance private sector risks with public sector guarantees. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ while encouraged by the progress made over the past two decades in lifting 660 million people worldwide out of poverty, the world bank's recent poverty data are a stark reminder of the scale of the task ahead for eradicating extreme poverty. the european union will have to work to strengthen the international community's commitment to the post-2015 development agenda. eradicating poverty, ensuring inclusive and sustainable development for present and future generations, and promoting and protecting all human rights are the core values for a peaceful and prosperous society.
in writing. ‒ the addis ababa conference, to be held in july this year, will be decisive in supporting the implementation of the sustainable development goals. the international situation, due to the financial crisis, has led the member states to question the commitment made at the monterrey conference in 2002, where it was decided to commit 0.7% of gross national income to development aid. the report adopted by the deve committee is a positive sign, since it sets out concrete objectives to be achieved in view of the addis ababa conference, also because it shows the need to find additional sources of financing for development. the report reiterates the commitment to aid: in essence, it calls on the eu to assert its political leadership in defining a framework for sustainable development, committing itself anew and without delay to achieving the 0.7% of gross national income target for development aid. the eu is also called upon to take serious action against tax havens, tax evasion and illicit financial flows, which undermine development assistance and contribute to the indebtedness of developing countries. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on green growth opportunities for smes because they are the backbone of the european economy and the key driver of economic growth and job creation. the report supports the concept of green growth and circular economy, linked to several areas of considerable relevance such as renewable energy sources, in particular: the widespread and sustainable use of wind, solar and water energy, energy efficiency, resource efficiency, waste management, emission reduction, etc. there is great potential for the green economy, but this potential cannot be fully exploited unless several basic conditions are first met, such as creating a more entrepreneurial spirit by developing open and innovation-friendly rules, introducing more diversified access to finance and creating more opportunities for knowledge sharing. the report also calls on the commission and the eib to ensure that smes, including eco-friendly and innovative ones, are the main beneficiaries of support in the implementation phase of the investment plan for europe, and stresses that to achieve this, the provision of advisory services on resource efficiency and eco-innovation needs to be strengthened.

in writing. ‒ smes are at the heart of the european economic fabric and are so in every member state. the business environment, however, varies widely from country to country and often from region to region: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. everything parliament does to improve the administrative, regulatory and economic environment in which smes have to operate must be supported. the report as a whole addresses many issues in a vague and open to interpretation, but also emphasises many aspects related to the circular economy and resource efficiency. in particular, i am particularly in favour of the concept also reiterated in this dossier of the need to shift the tax burden from labour to the use of natural resources. i believe that this is a prerequisite for the long-term success of smes in a world characterised by biophysical limits which cannot be overcome. the next revision of the small business act must give due attention to these considerations and perhaps envisage a green small business act to stimulate the adoption of entrepreneurial practices that will help the transition of the european economy in the shortest possible time.
in writing. ‒ we have today approved the own-initiative report on green growth opportunities for smes, which calls for more funding, harmonisation of national legislation, bureaucratic simplifications and effective communication to encourage more environmentally sustainable smes. we have asked first of all for more effective communication on alternative forms of financing to bank lending, such as venture capital, business angels and crowdfunding, as the green economy requires a wide range of instruments. smes are also too often confronted with overly stringent bankruptcy laws which do not allow them to start a new business easily after the failure of an economic activity. it is also important to share knowledge and to spread it: the most important points are inter-sectoral collaboration, the creation of informal networks and the invaluable role that sectoral federations can and should play in this regard. particular attention should also be paid to excessive red tape, which imposes additional burdens and creates obstacles to the functioning of the internal market: the commission has also proposed that the various national systems, which are often too different, be simplified and that more harmonized measures be introduced.

member of the commission.– mr president, the vote tomorrow will conclude a two-year-long negotiation process on the recast of the regulation on insolvency proceedings. i want to pay tribute to the rapporteur mr zwiefka and to the committee on legal affairs for their most efficient work on what i see as only a first step in this area. honest entrepreneurs deserve help when running into difficulties. the improved tools on jurisdiction will increase legal certainty and put in place effective safeguards against abusive forum shopping. i know that this issue was particularly important for parliament. the establishment of a system of interconnected insolvency registers will increase the transparency of insolvency proceedings for creditors. this is a very tangible benefit of the reform and it will foster a cultural change in the business community across europe. the revised regulation covers also preventive insolvency proceedings, which aim at rescuing businesses, as well as a larger range of personal insolvency proceedings. it clarifies jurisdiction rules. synthetic secondary proceedings avoid duplication of proceedings. the revision also provides the first legal framework for coordinating the proceedings of members of groups of companies. of course, our work is not finished with the adoption of the regulation. we will spare no efforts so that practitioners and citizens can properly apply the new instrument by the time it replaces the old regulation. the commission has also followed up on your goal, and last year adopted a recommendation on a new approach to business failure. the commission is currently assessing the actions the member states have taken in response to the recommendation. it is obvious that we need modern and efficient insolvency rules that help rescue viable businesses and give entrepreneurs and consumers a second chance. let me give you several illustrative figures. today in europe, half of all businesses do not survive the first five years of their existence. in the eu, 200 000 firms go bankrupt per year, that is 600 a day, resulting in 1.7 million direct job losses every year. around a quarter of these bankruptcies concern businesses that work cross-border, and the latest crisis has led to a surge in non-performing loans in all member states without exception. last month we held a conference in riga to look at the way ahead. it was a useful first occasion to gather views and brainstorm about the next steps. the capital markets union project, which the commission adopted recently, also contains a clear reference to the need for modern insolvency regimes as a gateway to a flourishing business and investment climate. we are interested in members views when starting to map out the next steps. i understand that consumer insolvency is of particular concern to some of you. i would like to recall that the principles laid down in the commission recommendation are also relevant in this regard. in particular in its recital 15, the commission urges member states to consider applying the principles of the recommendation also to consumers. the commission has carried out a specific study on over-indebtedness of european households and families. the findings are clear. people who lose their jobs and incomes have a higher probability of falling into the debt trap, as do people confronted with accidents of life no one can anticipate. bad financial choices come down to two basic scenarios: a credit which is too short-term, or interest rates which are too high, often to be explained by inadequate financial advice by lenders. in the framework of this study, the most frequently—named best practice reported by stakeholders relates to legislative steps to make insolvency proceedings more readily available. however, the situation is not homogeneous across the eu. for example, in a number of member states consumers do not have access to personal insolvency proceedings, and in many others the discharge periods are much longer than the recommended three-year period provided for in the commission recommendation. as regards next steps, besides the evaluation of the recommendation and the already existing material, the commission is carrying out a comprehensive comparative legal study in the 28 member states regarding consumer insolvency procedures. it will be completed in mid-january 2016 and this will provide us with a good basis to discuss next steps. i would like parliament to be fully involved in this process.

in writing. finally europe. politics has won. after the strong demands of parliament, the european commission has had the courage to tackle in a decisive way a subject which is unfortunately often underestimated by the countries not bordering the mediterranean, but which is vital for the european union, for what we have been, for what we are today and for what we represent in the world. the reception of migrants, of those fleeing war situations, of human lives that see hope in europe, is not the usual emergency: we can't turn away from living in a world that is now globalized, but we can choose how to be part of it. that's our job. and if we really want to create a 'european union' which is not only a european union in name, we must be united in facing this challenge. the commission is therefore in favour of 'mandatory quotas' for all member states and the de facto overrun of the dublin agreements, and is also in favour of thinking about how to get to the root of the problem by intervening in africa with investments that promote the development of local communities first and foremost. a 'smart solidarity' that does not make people irresponsible but makes everyone a protagonist of their own future.
member of the commission.– mr president, the commission would like to highlight the reasons for the commission delegated regulation repealing regulation no 2336/2003 on the ethanol market. the commission adopted this delegated regulation in the framework of its better regulation and simplification agenda. this commission delegated act will remove administrative burdens for operators and administrators without affecting our border protection, allowing the commission to continue monitoring the ethanol market in the european union more efficiently. at its meeting of 20 april 2015, the council confirmed it had no objection to the commission delegated regulation and the commission made a statement to confirm that it will continue to collect the necessary data for monitoring the ethanol market, with particular attention to imports at zero duty. the commission invites the european parliament to reject the motion of objection to the commission delegated regulation. this will allow the publication of the regulation in the official journal of the european union and its entry into force. this is an opportunity for the european parliament to align itself with the objective of reducing red tape for european citizens and business and of simplifying european legislation, a shared responsibility to which the european parliament, the council and the commission have committed together. the commission confirms its commitment to a better regulation agenda as illustrated by the better regulation package adopted by the college.

in writing. ‒ the text adopted represents an important step forward in the european anti-money laundering framework: it not only aligns eu countries with the most advanced international standards, but goes far beyond them. the directive contains a number of ambitious provisions which will enable europe to make considerable progress in the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing. in particular, in order to increase transparency on the ownership of companies and trusts, the text adopted introduces a centralised register of beneficial ownership information in all european countries. the directive also recognises the importance of a supranational approach to combating money laundering and terrorist financing risks in the union and moves in this direction by entrusting the european commission with the task of conducting a supranational assessment of these risks and making recommendations to member states so that they can deal with them effectively. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the measure aims to strengthen the internal market by reducing cross-border complexity, protecting society's interests from crime and terrorist acts and contributing to financial stability by safeguarding the soundness, orderly functioning and integrity of the financial system. breaking down barriers in the internal market not only facilitates the creation or development of legitimate activities in the eu, but can also provide greater opportunities for money laundering and terrorist financing. criminals engaged in money laundering activities could therefore seek to conceal or disguise the true nature, origin or ownership of the goods in question and turn them into apparently lawful proceeds. money laundering and terrorist financing pose a serious risk to the integrity, orderly functioning, reputation and stability of the financial system. to this end, european legislation has been adopted which needs to be constantly updated, due to the changing nature of the threats posed by money laundering and terrorist financing, facilitated by the continuous evolution of technology and the means at the disposal of criminals. in the light of these considerations, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the new anti-money laundering directive, which aims to strengthen the fight against tax crimes and the financing of terrorism and which introduces an amendment to the previous framework in order to strengthen the internal market and promote greater transparency of financial movements. the increasing complexity of the financial sector calls for stricter rules to ensure the security of both the european economy and its citizens, given the well-founded suspicions of money laundering and terrorist financing. i therefore welcome the proposal put forward by parliament to oblige the member states to keep central registers containing the names and information of the beneficial owners of companies and other legal entities. these records will then be made accessible only to those who can demonstrate a 'legitimate interest' in relation to money laundering, terrorist financing and associated suspected offences that could help to finance them, such as corruption, tax crimes and fraud. this will allow for a more adequate level of control over financial movements, increasing transparency without compromising the privacy and data protection rights of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ this is the fourth anti-money laundering directive, proposed by the commission in 2013 to align the european framework with international standards developed by the financial action task force. the purpose of the directive is to combat money laundering, tax evasion and terrorist financing by increasing transparency and improving the traceability of financial flows within the eu. the directive, which was voted in parliament during the last parliamentary term, was essentially watered down by the negotiations with the council during the italian presidency. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment against the risks arising from the use of radioactive substances. the wide discretion at national level also risks leading to uneven implementation between member states, creating new loopholes and possibilities for regulatory arbitrage. even if this new directive is going in the right direction, the many gaps do not allow us to give our support to the final text. so i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the commission aims to strengthen existing rules on anti-money laundering and money transfer by aligning them with international standards and fatf recommendations. the establishment of a public register of beneficiaries is a key step forward in the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing. we are dealing with a sensitive subject with important implications. international terrorist groups, which increasingly need to circulate money to keep their terror networks alive, use money laundering to conceal the true nature, origin or ownership of assets, turning them into apparently legitimate proceeds. money laundering and terrorist financing constitute a serious risk with potentially devastating consequences for society as a whole. we must keep up with the changing forms that international criminals are giving to their mechanisms, and we must do so quickly and courageously, without fear of offending some large financial group which is exploiting the weaknesses of the system for its own benefit. if not, we will have an obsolete and useless weapon against one of the most serious threats of this early millennium.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the directive which created new european instruments to combat money laundering, because i believe it is of fundamental importance to strengthen the regulatory framework and the instruments to combat a phenomenon of global scope, in line with the international rules in force, which are often non-binding. the new legislation, consisting of a directive and a regulation, took two years of work and it was only in december 2014 that political agreement was reached in the council under the italian eu presidency, which made it a qualifying battle. the 'fourth anti-money laundering directive' adds to the existing framework by introducing very important new elements such as the creation of central registers, as requested by the ep, which contain information on the actual beneficiaries of funds, accessible to the competent authorities, financial information units, banks or financial institutions. other parties than the latter may also access the central registers if they can demonstrate a 'legitimate interest'. the obligation to take other precautions in dealing with politically exposed persons is also introduced and clarified. the directive also aims to make the information of the person transferring money clearer and more accessible. personal data is fully protected.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the directive which is part of the new anti-money laundering package, aimed at strengthening the fight against tax crimes and the financing of terrorism. with the adoption of the fourth anti-money laundering directive, the european union is adopting transparency standards that are stricter than those in force at international level and is therefore at the forefront of prosecuting tax crimes. the text approved by parliament today improves the commission's proposal on one point in particular: for the first time, member states will be required to keep central registers containing information on the beneficial owners of companies and other legal entities, as well as trusts. in addition, the central registers will be accessible to authorities, so-called 'obliged entities' (such as banks carrying out their duty to properly audit customers) and, under certain conditions, to persons who demonstrate a 'legitimate interest' (such as investigative journalists or ngos) in relation to money laundering, terrorist financing and offences that could help to finance them, such as corruption, tax evasion and fraud.

in writing. ‒ the proposal under consideration concerns the revision of regulation (ec) no 1781/2006 on the information data relating to the payer accompanying transfers of funds in order to improve the traceability of payments and ensure that the eu regulatory framework remains in line with international standards. the funds transfer regulation lays down rules requiring payment service providers to communicate information about the payer throughout the payment chain in order to prevent, investigate and detect money laundering and terrorist financing. the proposed amendments aim to address some of the gaps in transparency by imposing certain requirements such as information on the beneficiary, extending credit scope to cards, telephones and it devices, verifying the identity of the beneficiary, strengthening the sanctioning powers of the competent authorities and the publication of sanctions. in the light of these considerations, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ there is no doubt that illicit money flows created by money transfers can undermine the stability and reputation of the financial sector and pose a threat to the internal market. the current regulation (ec) no 1781/2006, while ensuring that the eu regulatory framework continues to be in line with international standards, still has some legal gaps. therefore, in view of the changing threats posed by money laundering and the need to review the eu regulatory framework, i have decided to vote in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the regulation on the transfer of funds is part of the anti-money laundering package presented by the commission in 2013, was negotiated in parliament during the last legislature and approved in second reading by the council during the italian presidency. the purpose of the regulation is to prevent, investigate and detect money laundering and terrorist financing by improving the transparency and traceability of transfers of funds by authorities and law enforcement agencies. in particular, payment service providers are required to communicate data relating to the payer and the payee of a payment order. the text was adopted by a large majority in committee. we have decided to abstain, however, not only in order to be consistent with the vote on the anti-money laundering directive, to which the regulation is closely linked, but also to highlight our concerns about exemptions for certain payment instruments and persons, derogations and the wide discretion left to member states also as regards sanctions.
in writing. ‒ i shall abstain because the text did not bring the changes we would have liked after the first reading. changes to not have such unwarranted traceability on all money transfers.
in writing. ‒ in a spirit of complementarity with the vote on the prevention of the use of the financial system for the purpose of money laundering or terrorist financing, i voted in favour of this accompanying recommendation, repealing the previous regulation (ec) no 1781/2006.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the transfer of funds regulation firstly because it enriches and complements a pre-existing and very important overall regulatory framework concerning eu instruments to combat money laundering. secondly, because i believe it is essential to strengthen the regulatory framework and the instruments to combat a phenomenon of global scope, in line with the international rules, which are very important but often not binding. the new legislation, which consists of a directive and a regulation, took two years to work on and was only agreed in december last year in the council, thanks to the efforts of the italian eu presidency, which considered it a priority for the six-month period. the regulation on the transfer of funds concerns payment service providers, and therefore banks, and in this case the information data relating to the person ordering the transfer. it introduces the obligation for financial institutions to include accurate information on both the originator and the recipient of the transfer, and thus the obligation to follow the latter throughout the payment chain. the complex and hard work of the ep, and in particular of the two rapporteurs, has made it possible to achieve a more ambitious final result.
in writing. the proposal put forward by mrs cora van nieuwenhuizen on the regulation on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts deserves our attention. this is a very important measure, which aims to solve those serious cases of manipulation of reference values for the determination of interest rates, such as libor and euribor, and of reference values for currencies, which in recent years have caused considerable losses to consumers and investors and destroyed the confidence of citizens in the financial sector. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal with conviction, as part of the many efforts europe is making to restore confidence and rules to the economy.
in writing. voting in favour of the report by mr kirkhope and mr simon on the information accompanying transfers of funds was to support a proposal to improve the traceability of payments and to prevent and detect money laundering and terrorist financing, especially in certain areas where there are serious doubts about the transparency and traceability of financial funds.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text on the information accompanying transfers of funds, as after long negotiations with the council it has finally been concluded. the text adopted at second reading is likely to improve the traceability of payments and to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism through the transfer of funds. the proposed amendments relate to areas where european legislation is not yet able to take precise action.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the resolution on the information accompanying transfers of funds, which aligns eu rules with international standards set in 2013, in particular the financial action task force recommendation. the text is at second reading and follows an agreement reached in the trilogue under the italian presidency. we are particularly pleased that, with the exception of transfers of less than eur 1 000, it will be compulsory to provide the details of monetary transfers to foreign countries. we also welcome the strengthening of the chapter on sanctions and monitoring, and the fact that the rules on the protection and publication of sensitive data have been brought into line with existing eu regulations.
in writing. ‒ having regard to the council's position at first reading and the opinions of the economic and social committee and of the european central bank, having regard to the joint deliberations of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs and to their joint recommendation, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ also in the case of the information accompanying transfers of funds, there were joint meetings of the two committees responsible, the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, which voted in a quasi-plebiscite for parliament to approve the council's position at first reading. that is what happened, and i am glad of it.
in writing. ‒ i support the text for second reading. this recommendation is also the result of the work of the libe and econ committees and aims to identify money laundering and the financing of terrorism through the transfer of funds. the approach of the committees is clear: one way to fight terrorists with the same weapons is to control them economically. for this action to be effective, it is necessary that each member state imposes requirements on its territory in terms of transfer of money, such as the request for information from the beneficiary and the strengthening of the sanctioning powers for the competent authorities.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the approval of the anti-money laundering package, i also voted in favour of the regulation on transfers of funds, which aims to increase the traceability of payers and beneficiaries and their assets. the agreement reached between the council and parliament allows the existing regulation on information accompanying transfers of funds to be modernised and revised, with a view to improving the traceability of payments and bringing the eu legal framework into line with international standards, such as the recommendations of the financial action task force (fatf).
