written declarations of vote
in writing. ‒ zwiefka's report on insolvency proceedings is shared and balanced: it is a subject of great importance, especially for small and mediumsized enterprises. i believe that the proposed update of the legislation will ensure improvements, especially in cases of financial difficulties in the management of transnational insolvency proceedings, and for these reasons i supported the text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the zwiefka report deals with a very important issue, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises, namely insolvency proceedings. the legislative proposal is designed to amend regulation (ec) no 1346/2000. the process was very long, partly because it was not easy to reach agreement in the council. the text was adopted by a very large majority in parliament on first reading (589 in favour, 69 against). the updating of the insolvency legislation should bring some improvements to the business world, especially in cases of financial difficulties in transnational insolvency proceedings. the text also contains rules against phenomena such as forum shopping, thanks to more precise definitions of the concept of 'centre of main interest' of a company and that of 'establishment'. national insolvency registers should cooperate better with each other in the exchange of information, also thanks to the european e-justice portal. i am in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i support this resolution in order to make the crossborder insolvency procedure more efficient and effective, with benefits for debtors and creditors, facilitating the survival of companies and giving a second chance to entrepreneurs. each year insolvency proceedings affect some 200 000 businesses across the eu, putting 1.7 million jobs at risk. a quarter of these insolvency proceedings have a cross-border dimension. the new legislation, through creditor protection and business survival, will help to preserve jobs in this particularly difficult period.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr tadeusz zwiefka because the text aims to improve the efficiency of the european framework for the resolution of crossborder insolvency cases. the european commission figures show that the procedure affects some 200 000 companies in the union every year, or almost 600 companies a day, putting 1.7 million jobs at risk. a quarter of these insolvency proceedings have a cross-border dimension. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 established a european framework for crossborder insolvency proceedings, which applies to cases where the debtor, whether a natural or legal person, has assets or creditors in more than one member state and determines the competent court for the opening of insolvency proceedings: the main proceedings must be brought in the member state where the debtor has its centre of main interests and have effects recognised throughout the european union; the secondary proceedings may be instituted in the place where the debtor has a dependency, and have effect only in respect of assets situated in that state. the regulation, which entered into force in 2002, needs to be updated. the general objective of the amendment of the regulation is to improve the efficiency of the european insolvency framework, so as to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market and its resilience in times of economic crisis. in the light of these considerations, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ as is well known, the common framework for insolvency proceedings aims to avoid the transfer of assets or legal proceedings from one member state to another, in order to benefit from more favourable conditions and to the detriment of creditors. however, the current regulation does not harmonise insolvency laws but only regulates the conflicts of laws in the different member states. on the basis of these considerations, i have decided to vote in favour of this proposal. i believe that this proposal for a regulation, which aims to make transnational insolvency proceedings more effective and efficient, is more in line with the legislative developments in the member states and will help to improve the efficient functioning of the internal market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation because it sets out more efficient and effective rules on crossborder insolvency proceedings, which will help to achieve one of the current priorities of the european union: stimulate economic growth. these rules will help businesses to survive and give insolvent entrepreneurs a second chance.
in writing. - i support this recommendation. it deals with insolvency proceedings, a very important and sensitive subject, especially for small and mediumsized enterprises. the legislative proposal amends regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 in a positive way and we support it.
in writing. ‒ today's vote marks the beginning of a new phase for thousands of businesses. the new regulation on crossborder insolvency procedures puts an end to the traditional hostile outlook of winding-up, providing greater guarantees and protections for creditors and a second chance for firms and entrepreneurs in difficulty. other measures include the introduction of practical solutions to the so-called forum shopping, making it more difficult to circumvent the sacrosanct rights of creditors, and the introduction of electronic bankruptcy registers capable of providing timely and relevant information to creditors and courts, also in order to avoid parallel insolvency proceedings. for these reasons i voted in favour of this measure, hoping that a new phase will really begin in which the institutions will stand by firms and entrepreneurs in difficulty, not to punish and liquidate them but to help and restructure them.
in writing. i congratulate mr zwiefka on reaching agreement with the council on a measure long awaited by consumers and businesses in europe. i shall vote in favour of the following: the european insolvency system was in fact in a state of uncertainty, especially in crossborder situations, and the commission was right, more than two years ago, to propose a comprehensive reform of the sector. i would like to stress one important aspect introduced after the council and parliament readings, namely the safeguards against the so-called forum shopping phenomenon. in too many known cases, companies and debtors suddenly moved their headquarters before the opening of insolvency or bankruptcy proceedings: the regulation now introduces a legal framework of enhanced safeguards as well as the ability for courts to assess whether the move is genuine or not. the agreement we are about to ratify is a step forward in protecting the european economy. i hope that this will be an important sign of the new policy direction of growth and attention to citizens, consumers and businesses launched by the new commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recast of regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 on crossborder insolvency proceedings, firstly because insolvency proceedings in europe affect more than 200 000 companies each year, a quarter of which are crossborder. the new legislation took about three years to work on and the italian eu presidency was particularly committed to the final success of the negotiations, having succeeded in finding the right political synthesis between the council and the european parliament. the aim is to provide a second chance for entrepreneurs, covering not only bankruptcy proceedings but also hybrid and pre-insolvency proceedings, as well as the remission and restructuring of the debts of natural persons (consumers and self-employed professionals), and to set up an electronic register useful both for creditors to identify assets and obtain information and to avoid parallel proceedings. the register will be available on the e-justice portal. in order to prevent abusive practices, the concept of a centre of main interests (comi) has been clarified, which is important for cross-border groups of companies, particularly those with a specific discipline. the rules on group insolvency are supplemented by rules allowing for the coordination of proceedings in the field of groups of companies.
in writing. after several technical meetings and trilogues, we reached an agreement on second reading. the subject is of great current interest and concerns the failure of companies and insolvency. the report proposes, among other things, a more ambitious solution to the insolvency of groups of companies by proposing a compromise for a more flexible approach. for these reasons, i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting the regulation of the european parliament and of the council on insolvency proceedings. the proper functioning of the internal market requires procedures that are efficient and effective, and to achieve this the provisions on jurisdiction, recognition and applicable law in this area should be part of a union measure which is binding and directly applicable in the member states.
in writing. ‒ we welcome this purely technical report, while acknowledging with satisfaction some of the political data. first, the scope of insolvency proceedings has been extended to include hybrid proceedings and corporate restructuring. we also think it is important to stress that the current regulation introduces the possibility for business groups to act in a coordinated way between the various companies, reducing costs and time for both the private and public sectors. we also acknowledge the efforts of the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs to include a recital introducing a clause for the future which protects the interests and preferences of employees in cases of company insolvency.
in writing. ‒ having regard to the council's position at first reading and the opinion of the european economic and social committee, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i support the following text on insolvency proceedings for second reading. as early as december 2012, the commission proposed a revision of the rules on cross-border insolvency, which vary widely from one member state to another, in order to make cross-border insolvency proceedings more effective and to improve the current rules, which instead merely settle conflicts between member states without unifying or harmonising insolvency laws.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the reform of the rules on crossborder insolvency, which extends the scope of the insolvency procedure regulation and clarifies the legal concept of the centre of main interests (comi). these measures will serve to prevent abusive and opportunistic legal practices such as recourse to the courts and legislation of a milder country rather than to the one with greater jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute. the new rules also specify the relationship between main and secondary proceedings and require all states to set up public insolvency registers containing information on the course of insolvency proceedings and on the insolvent creditor and debtor.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the revision of the regulation introducing new rules on insolvency proceedings at eu level and extending its scope. the aim of the revision is to make crossborder insolvency proceedings more efficient and effective, to the benefit of debtors and creditors, to facilitate the survival of businesses and to give entrepreneurs a second chance. the new provisions will also ensure that the current insolvency regulation is consistent with the evolution of national insolvency legislation introduced after its entry into force in 2002. the data provided by the european commission show that in the european union these procedures affect some 200 000 enterprises each year; that means 1.7 million jobs are at stake. since about a quarter of these insolvency proceedings have a cross-border element, it is clear that legislative action at european level is needed to improve the procedural framework in these cases.

written declarations of vote
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a conflict minerals regulation was sent directly to the trilogue because a decisive majority was reached on some key amendments proposed by the five star movement and other groups. amendments essential to the proposal's effectiveness. the rapporteur's proposal was flawed, useless, ineffective and harmful to jobs in europe, as well as harmful to smes. it was a proposal born of that compromise downwards which destroys instead of creating, it was a proposal written by the commission for the use and consumption of the multinationals and for the benefit of the merchants of death. i have a message for the commission: you lost the battle! now parliament will have to express a new position with the council and the rapporteur will have to understand that he does not have a majority for his proposal.
in writing. ‒ in the democratic republic of congo, zimbabwe, the central african republic, colombia, burma and other countries, minerals are mined under the control of warlords who exploit local populations and enslave them to finance their trade. over the past 40 years, 60 percent of the conflicts in so-called "developing" countries have been connected with the trade in natural resources, which has enabled the financing of armed groups guilty of violence against the local population. in the democratic republic of congo alone, conflicts over mineral trade have caused 3.5 million deaths, over half a million rapes and an unspecified number of other types of violence since 1995. more deaths, more violence, more rapes will follow if we don't do something. we europeans account for 35% of world trade and are major importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold: so we have a responsibility not to look the other way. we can and must vote in favour of a binding regulation requiring public traceability of minerals imported into europe from the place of purchase: the fate of millions of men, women, children depends on our decisions. let's all vote for it together.
in writing. - i abstained. while we understand the reasons behind the measure, it is not with regulations such as these that we can hope to eradicate violence, illicit trafficking or the financing of terrorist groups in conflict areas such as, for example, that of the congo. there is no doubt that any restrictions or certification of a mandatory nature for european companies will not stop chinese companies, which will only further penetrate the african mineral resources market.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of this report to ask that importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold for the production of consumer goods be required to receive eu certification in order to ensure that they do not fuel conflict and human rights violations in war zones. i also voted in favour of an amendment to the european commission's proposal to introduce mandatory traceability for the 800 000 eu companies using tin, tungsten, tantalum and gold, which are present in many consumer products in europe, in particular in the automotive, electronics, aerospace, packaging, construction, lighting, industrial machinery and jewellery sectors. finally, as metal smelters and gold refineries represent the last stage where the origin of minerals can be effectively traced, it is necessary that they be subject to a mandatory audit, carried out by independent third parties, to check whether they apply the rules of 'duty of care' designed to help companies in the sector not to fuel conflict and human rights violations in war zones.
in writing. ‒ we managed to vote in plenary on an important amendment which aims to make it compulsory for all those involved in the processing chain of precious metals and minerals to ensure that they are not affected by human rights violations that often occur in the relevant supply chain. given the importance of the amendment, it was decided to refer the text back to the trilogue, but i am glad to have contributed to the position taken by parliament in defence of human rights.
in writing. ‒ the need to break the link between trade in certain minerals and the financing of armed conflicts is linked to the need to preserve and develop a responsible european market. in this context, i believe it is important to set up a system of self-certification for importers, so that due diligence obligations can be fully respected. at the same time, i believe that the impact of the burden of transparency and self-certification should not be underestimated, as it would risk driving operators out of conflict areas and undermining the objectives of socioeconomic development. i therefore voted in favour of this report, in the hope that a broad political consensus would be reached.
in writing. ‒ on 5 march 2014, the commission presented a legislative proposal to make it more difficult for armed groups in conflict and high-risk areas to finance their activities through mining and trading of minerals. central to this approach is making it easier for companies to source tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold responsibly and encouraging the use of legitimate commercial channels. i could only vote in favour of this report, because we must hold those who are involved in one way or another in the use of conflict minerals to account. to this end, all those involved in the processing and marketing of these products should ensure the traceability of these minerals (tin, tantalum, tungsten, gold). by voting in favour, i intend to contribute to the responsibility of not only all those involved in importing but also all the natural or legal persons involved in consumption and sale. the compulsory introduction of such transparency and certification measures throughout the production chain is essential to our fight to protect social and environmental rights and duties.
in writing. ‒ in conflict-torn areas of the world, the exploitation and trade of natural resources allows armed groups, often guilty of human rights violations against populations, to finance themselves. to remain helpless or to pretend not to see is a crime which europe cannot allow or tolerate. how intolerable a small and limited initiative, almost a witness, in the face of a huge problem with multiple implications. that is why, in accepting the invitation that has been sent to us from different quarters, we as socialists and democrats have strongly supported the need to widen the scope of the legislation by introducing a mandatory regulation applicable to companies at all levels of the supply chain of minerals and metals. this is not a victory for us: such a dramatic argument can't have winners or losers. but we are glad that our obstinacy has opened the eyes of many and, by overturning the vote of the committee, has allowed the introduction of a criterion which we believe can reduce the capacity of the warlords to support and finance those who have for years, scientifically, bled large regions of the world, to make them unstable and to be able to build their criminal empires more easily.
in writing. ‒ i voted overwhelmingly in favour of the proposal for a regulation establishing a european system of self-certification of the exercise of supply chain due diligence for responsible importers of tin, tungsten, tantalum, their ores and gold originating in conflict and high-risk areas. today's vote has in fact achieved the great objective of significantly increasing the traceability of these minerals and metals. but we must continue to fight for parliament to approve an ambitious and effective proposal which will help to break the unacceptable link between the extraction and trade of these resources and the financing of armed groups, and which will take account of the effective capacity of the various operators to monitor and assess the possible risks along their supply chain, avoiding excessive bureaucratic burdens, particularly for smes and micro-enterprises. i also believe that we will only achieve significant results from this proposal for a regulation if we can place it in the larger context of a coherent european cooperation policy.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation aims to establish a european system of self-certification of the exercise of due diligence by european importers of tin, tungsten, tantalum and gold. i voted in favour of this proposal because it aims to help break the link between the extraction and trade of minerals from conflict-affected or high-risk areas and the financing of armed groups controlling the extraction areas.
in writing. ‒ conflict minerals are minerals extracted from conflict zones and whose trade subsidizes armed groups, murder and abominations of all kinds. four elements are considered: gold, tungsten, tantalum and tin, all of which are essential to the manufacture of technological products. the report sets out the conditions for being certified as a 'responsible importer' of the minerals and metals concerned. it is based on a due diligence regime that allows eu importers to apply the principles and measures defined by the oecd and thus to counter the risk of financing of armed groups and security forces and to reduce any other adverse effects, including any serious infringements associated with the extraction, transport or trade of the minerals concerned. m5s believes that there is a balance point to not burden smes, already suffering from the economic crisis, and at the same time protect human rights. the majority of the votes in the plenary were taken on the m5s's proposal for mandatory voting in both upstream and downstream sectors, and this led me to vote in favour of the commission's entire proposal as amended in the plenary.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution opposing a commission delegated directive amending the current legislation on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment. the directive does not meet the conditions for granting the derogations it seeks to introduce, nor have the technical deadlines for the submission of exemption applications been met.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that further assessment is needed on the exemption for cadmium in general lighting and display lighting applications and that therefore the commission should come forward with a new proposal in this regard.
in writing. - i vote for it. the objection is to a commission delegated directive amending, to adapt to technical progress, annex iii to the rohs directive (restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment). the commission delegated directive: (a) 'cadmium in led ii-vi with colour conversion (< 10 μg cd per mm2 of light emitting surface) for use in solid state lighting or display systems'; (b) introduces a new and more specific exemption 39 (b) 'cadmium in cadmium-based downshift quantum dots (semiconductor nanocrystals) for use in display system lighting applications (< 0,2 μg cd per mm2 of display screen surface area) ', expiring on 30 june 2018. the delegated directive does not meet the conditions for granting an exemption set out in article 5 (1) (a) of the rohs directive for both exemptions. in particular, the reasoning given for the exemption 39 (b) is based on an outdated situation as regards the feasibility of substituting cadmium in quantum dots. in addition, the application for renewal of the exemption was received by the commission 5 months later than the deadlines set by the rohs directive. nevertheless, the commission accepted it.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on cadmium in general lighting and display lighting applications. the resolution raised objections to the commission delegated directive of 30 january 2015 amending, for the purposes of adapting to technical progress, annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council as regards the exemption for cadmium in general lighting and display lighting applications. i think that, given that cadmium is a highly dangerous toxic substance, extending an existing derogation while granting a new derogation for this substance should be avoided in order to protect the environment and public health. furthermore, the derogation could also send the wrong signal to industry, discouraging it from investing in innovation and research to find alternatives to cadmium. finally, the derogation could lead to market distortions due to imports of cadmium-containing electrical and electronic equipment from third countries to the detriment of innovative and environmentally sensitive companies operating in europe. for all these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of parliament's objection.
in writing. - cadmium is a carcinogenic chemical element. the so-called rohs (restriction of hazardous substances) directive severely restricts its use in electrical and electronic equipment placed on the market in the european union. the exemption for its use in general lighting applications and display system lighting (e.g. leds) expired on 1 july 2014. the european commission would like to renew this exemption and our m5s delegation, together with a very large majority in the european parliament, opposed this choice in order to protect the health of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ on 30 january 2015, the commission delegated directive amended annex iii to directive 2001/65/eu on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (rohs directive), annex ii of which limits, inter alia, the use of cadmium in such equipment. in point 39, annex iii provided for a derogation for cadmium in leds expiring on 1 july 2014. the commission, after receiving a request to extend that exemption until 30 june 2017, approved the delegated directive. however, it was found that: (1) the commission's statement that the led products (with or without cadmium) referred to in recital 39 do not exist and that consequently an impact assessment could not be carried out is erroneous and (2) the request for exemption was received after the deadline and was considered excessive by the experts appointed by the commission. the european commission is therefore invited to take into account the position and objections raised by the ep and to carry out a reassessment with a view to submitting a new delegated act. in the light of these considerations, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution objecting to the commission delegated directive of 30 january 2015 amending annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council as regards the exemption for cadmium in general lighting and display lighting applications. in fact, as recent technological developments have led to the introduction of new equipment on the union market, in particular a new complete line of television models based on cadmium-free quantum dots, i share the concerns regarding the extension of the exemption from the prohibition on the use of cadmium. in addition, according to the information available and the expertise of some independent consultants, given two televisions of the same size, the one equipped with a display system with cadmium-free quantum dots appears to show a lower energy consumption than the model with cadmium-containing quantum dots, and colour rendering tests, compared to the relevant standard, have shown that display systems based on cadmium-free quantum dots allow for equivalent if not better results. i therefore join the call in the text of the resolution that we should proceed swiftly with a reassessment of the existing exemption with a view to its abolition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution as it calls on the commission to review its delegated act which provides in point 39 of annex iii for the extension of the exemption until 2017 for cadmium in leds and one until 2018 for cadmium in quantum dots. the commission delegated act is not justified as the market is fully ready to produce general lighting applications and display systems without any presence of cadmium, which is hazardous to human health. the same independent consultants who assessed the application on behalf of the commission came to the same conclusion and openly recommended not to grant the extension. i voted against recital f and paragraph 5 because one of the exemption applications submitted by lighting appliance manufacturers was submitted after the deadline and despite this infringement of the regulation was still accepted by the commission.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the resolution, bearing in mind the objection to the commission's delegated directive amending, in order to adapt it to technical progress, annex iii to the rohs directive (restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment).
in writing. in view of the rapid technological advancement of the market and the new assessment required of new products and findings based on cadmium-free quantum dot technology and considering the request for exemption 39b as obsolete, i welcome the motion for a resolution on the commission directive amending annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu on the exemption of cadmium in lighting applications for display systems.
in writing. taking into account that the rohs directive limits, among other things, the use of cadmium in electrical and electronic equipment (restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment), it can be seen that the market has undergone important developments since then, especially in terms of available techniques. in fact, it can be expected that the properties of cadmium-free quantum dots in terms of energy saving are similar to those of cadmium-containing quantum dots. in view of this, and with a view to protecting the right to health, i have expressed my favourable opinion.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the delegated directive on the exemption for cadmium in general lighting and display lighting applications. in view of the important developments in the market, regulation allows for useful and systematically managed technology development. this document initiates a new assessment which does not result in market distortions, as the current exemption remains in force until its withdrawal plus a subsequent grace period.
in writing. ‒ we support the resolution on the exemption of cadmium from the lighting applications of display systems as we consider that the commission delegated directive of 30 january 2015 does not comply with the conditions for the exemption of cadmium contained in article 5 (1) (a) of the directive on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment. we therefore support the request to the commission to submit a new version of the delegated act which takes account of the position of the rapporteur and of parliament as a whole.
in writing. ‒ having regard to the commission delegated directive of 30 january 2015 amending, for the purposes of adapting to technical progress, annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu of the european parliament and of the council as regards the exemption for cadmium in lighting and display applications,i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i shared the objections to the commission's delegated directive. a further assessment is necessary following developments in the commercial availability of products based on cadmium-free quantum dot technology. i am in favour of the resolution: as it stands, the delegated directive cannot enter into force. even if the directive does not enter into force, and it is important to stress this, there will be no market distortion, as the current exemption remains in force until it is revoked plus a subsequent grace period.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the commission delegated directive amending annex iii to directive 2011/65/eu. although cadmium was classified as a hazardous substance to be banned in electrical and electronic equipment placed on the market, as laid down in directive 2011/65/eu, this material was exempted as provided for in annex iii to that directive. the exemption of cadmium, which is argued here, is due to the fact that this material is the basis of quantum dots, a state-of-the-art technology that offers considerable advantages in terms of energy efficiency and colour rendering. the vote in favour of the delegated directive therefore allows us not to hinder scientific progress in this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution as it calls on the commission to review its delegated act which provides in point 39 of annex iii for the extension of the exemption until 2017 for cadmium in leds and one until 2018 for cadmium in quantum dots. the commission's delegated act is not justified at all as, contrary to the commission's findings, the market is fully ready to produce general lighting applications and display systems without any presence of cadmium, which is hazardous to human health. the same independent consultants who assessed the application on behalf of the commission came to the same conclusion and openly recommended not to grant the extension. i voted against recital f and paragraph 5 because one of the exemption applications submitted by lighting appliance manufacturers was submitted after the deadline and despite this infringement of the regulation was still accepted by the commission.

oral explanations of vote
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to remind you that this resolution must be linked to the fact that we decided in 1992 to introduce maternity leave at european level, so it is not appropriate to say that this decision should be left to the states alone, because it is a question of increasing welfare, particularly as regards the mother, the child, the father and the conditions of maternity and reconciliation. but we cannot stand still at the 14 weeks provided for in the 1992 directive which is still in force. we must also go further to ensure greater protection not only of the health of women and children, but also to allow a reconciliation, especially in times of great economic and employment crisis, when we see increasing poverty among women and children, difficulties in entering the labour market and remaining in it. and so we have to understand that giving these opportunities today means, among other things, also having higher productivity - for those who are concerned about costs - and this also makes it easier for many women to access the workforce. we must say today, as we said in the resolution, that the commission must take up a new initiative and above all we ask the next luxembourg presidency to take up a new legislative initiative, and the commission's mediation will be necessary. we cannot let go after two legislatures of the possibility of finally making a suitable directive.
written declarations of vote
in writing. ‒ i believe that the principle of equal treatment between women and men implies the absence of any discrimination, whether for maternity or for paternity, and the need to have equal family responsibilities. for these reasons i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls on the council to fulfil its obligations in relation to the maternity leave directive and urges the member states to resume the stalled negotiating phase.
in writing. ‒ even today, maternity leave is managed in very different ways in europe, and there are very different levels of protection. in the last parliamentary term, parliament called for the minimum leave in each eu country to be increased from 14 to 20 weeks with full pay. we know that the discussion on this extension has stalled in the council and that the commission will withdraw the proposal if the situation does not improve. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. a well-calibrated maternity leave can help to improve the gender balance in the labour market, without forgetting the clear demographic challenge facing europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because the extension of maternity leave and the introduction of paternity leave are both necessary and fundamental measures to combat gender inequalities and to encourage people to have children and to create families. i believe that the union must also harmonize as many rules as possible, starting with those relating to the rights of individuals.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that this resolution by the committee on women's rights and gender equality has been adopted, which deplores the council's failure to act on the maternity leave directive and reaffirms the will of this parliament to end the deadlock and play an active role in the legislative process. it is important to continue this directive, on which our assembly adopted a position at first reading five years ago. we will continue to work on this subject so that women's right to maternity leave and reintegration into work is recognised and protected without any discrimination. we are therefore calling for the introduction of a minimum of 10 working days of paid paternity leave and for men, fathers, to be able to exercise their right to work and family. if this proposal for revision is withdrawn, our group will be promoting a legislative initiative to revise the current legislation in order to improve the health and safety of pregnant women, women who have recently given birth or women who are breastfeeding, thus addressing the demographic challenges and reducing the disparities between men and women.
in writing. - i voted yes. the principle of equal treatment for women and men implies the absence of any discrimination, including as regards maternity, paternity and having family responsibilities, but a quarter of the member states do not provide for paternity leave; if one considers that the birth rate is decreasing in the european union and that this trend is aggravated by the crisis, as unemployment, precariousness and uncertainty about the future and the economy are pushing couples, and in particular younger women, to postpone the decision to have children, the trend towards an ageing population in the union as a whole is further reinforced. sharing family and domestic responsibilities between men and women is an indispensable condition for the achievement of gender equality. the resolution deplores the deadlock in the council over the maternity leave directive and calls on the member states to relaunch the negotiations. the willingness to draw up a separate directive establishing paid paternity leave of at least 10 working days and encouraging measures, legislative and otherwise, enabling men, and fathers in particular, to exercise their right to achieve a work-life balance is reiterated.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution in question to ask the european commission not to withdraw the proposal for a directive on maternity leave and to urge the ministers to resume talks and agree on a formal position. what kind of europe are we living in if those who create life are punished? what kind of europe are we living in if childbirth is synonymous with poverty? we cannot help the mothers by simply cancelling the proposal for a directive. since 1992, when the maternity leave directive was adopted, we have not made any progress. women cannot wait, they deserve to be women, mothers and workers at the same time without being discriminated against. it is also appropriate to provide for paternity leave of at least 10 working days in addition to maternity leave.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution to break the deadlock in the directive on maternity leave. european legislation on this subject is fixed at 1992 and should be updated; many member states have already introduced higher levels of protection.
in writing. ‒ as the europe 2020 strategy underlines, smart, sustainable and inclusive growth cannot be pursued without focusing on achieving the right balance between work and family. on the other hand, it is a given that the increase in female employment is an important factor in gdp growth, and on the other hand the data show that the european countries where more children are being born today are also those where female employment rates are highest, confirming that it is perfectly possible to reconcile family and working life, provided that there are adequate protection mechanisms. the maternity leave directive, which pursues exactly this objective, was approved by parliament at first reading on 20 october 2010, and it is serious, and not in line with the principle of loyal cooperation under article 4 teu, that the council has not yet adopted a formal position. the question we have approved urges the council to take up its responsibilities and to adopt a formal position on the directive, with the aim of overcoming the deadlock and, if possible, opening negotiations with parliament. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which seeks to unblock the maternity leave directive, which has been stalled in the council since it was approved by parliament in 2010. the main aim of the directive is to establish the duration of maternity leave (parliament proposes 20 weeks) and the amount of the allowance to be paid, which parliament proposes to be equal to 100% of earnings. considering the many disparities still existing between men and women, especially in the workplace even in normal situations - just think, for example, that women's pensions are on average 39% lower than those of their male colleagues - it is clear that, in the face of motherhood, women's natural duties risk limiting their rights as well. the harmonization of the rules on maternity leave is therefore a crucial step towards reducing gender-based discrimination. we therefore hope that the proposal for a directive (com (2008) 0637 final) can be unblocked before it risks being withdrawn by the commission in june under the refit programme.

oral explanations of vote
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is estimated that there are almost 80 million people in the european union who have severe or moderate disabilities. the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, which was ratified by the european union but not by all member states (there are still three missing), is nevertheless an absolute reference point because it guarantees the recognition of the universality of human rights and the need to ensure the full active inclusion of persons with disabilities, without discrimination. however, there are still gaps in data and in access to goods and services and employment, and often citizenship rights. i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that we are making real progress with this resolution, firstly by asking the commission to approve the disability package for these policies in order to have a dedicated budget line. but above all, as chairman of the committee on culture and education, i am prepared to cooperate with the other committees, for example on the issue of the integration of quality and the integration of the disabled in schools and universities. finally, we call for greater involvement of parliament and associations in monitoring the convention.

in writing. ‒ according to 2014 estimates, some 80 million people in the european union have some form of disability and they are therefore one of the largest and most vulnerable groups of people within our society. it is a heterogeneous group whose full integration into social and working life is a major challenge for all of us. the union's policy is still lacking today. the commission proposed an eu anti-discrimination directive in 2008 but it is unfortunately still blocked by the council. nevertheless, we believe that full inclusion and equal participation of people with disabilities is possible. a truly free, welcoming and barrier-free society can be created by promoting the implementation of human rights at all levels of the definition, from programming to monitoring of eu policies, thus binding the commission to take parliament's proposals into account. legislative proposals must involve representatives of disabled people in their drafting and must affirm the right to paid work and adequate training from primary school as essential elements to enable disabled people to lead independent lives and contribute to the society in which they live.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. persons with disabilities have equal rights, including inalienable rights to dignity, equal treatment, independent living and full participation in society. unfortunately, even in europe, they face discrimination and obstacles to the exercise of their rights on an equal footing with others. the resolution adopted by parliament therefore called on the commission to present an ambitious proposal for european accessibility legislation, fully involving disabled people throughout the legislative cycle. the resolution also stressed that this proposal should cover a wide range of policy areas relating to accessibility of goods and services for all eu citizens, promoting independent living and the full inclusion of people with disabilities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i have always been committed to ensuring that persons with disabilities enjoy equal opportunities, fundamental rights, equal access to services and the labour market, and the same rights and obligations as citizens of the member state to which they belong in terms of social security, in line with the principle of equal treatment and non-discrimination.
in writing. ‒ the resolution we voted on represents an important step towards the full implementation of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, going in the direction of strengthening the role of the european parliament in monitoring and implementing that convention, in close liaison with the un committee responsible for analysing progress on the implementation and application of the convention. the resolution also calls for the rapid adoption of two pieces of legislation of major importance for disabled people: the commission has also adopted a proposal for a european accessibility act and a directive on the protection of persons at risk of discrimination. the resolution also calls on the member states to respect the obligation, arising from article 12 of the convention, to guarantee in their national legislation the right of persons with disabilities to vote and stand as electors. more generally, the resolution also promotes the inclusion and full participation of people with disabilities in social life, including through their representative organisations. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ in the eu, 80 million people live with some form of disability. unfortunately, as the numerous petitions to the ep have shown, these people often face discrimination and obstacles to the exercise of their rights. as regards employment, in the 20-64 age group less than 50% of disabled people are in employment, compared with over 70% of non-disabled people, while for women with disabilities this figure falls to 44%, compared with 65% of non-disabled women. the eu has formally ratified the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities (crpd), which has been signed by all 28 eu member states and ratified by 25 of them. the resolution calls on the commission to formally consult all relevant institutions, agencies and organisations and to come forward with an ambitious proposal on electronic accessibility, recommends that eu funds be used for this purpose and calls on those member states which have not ratified the convention to do so without delay. in the light of these considerations, i voted in favour.

oral explanations of vote
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i must congratulate my colleagues on having just voted on a motion for a resolution which is practically in line with the commission's implementing decision. at this point i wonder what the real role of parliament is. we have been working for days to confirm the same decisions of the commission itself? i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in the preparation of the next report, but i am saying that it should be a matter for the council to decide. there is also no willingness to reconsider the proposed measures in the light of the scientific evidence that has been presented so far from various quarters, and by that i mean the exclusion of vines from plants that are potentially host to xylella or the damage to health and the environment due to the use of plant protection products on a large scale. the implementation of this decision will allow the eradication of healthy trees within a radius of 100 metres of the infected tree and will prohibit the planting of all species as potential hosts, irrespective of any controls and monitoring. we are therefore talking about short-sighted measures which will certainly have european consequences because of the social, environmental and economic consequences. but mine is a prediction that is unfortunately all too easy. for this reason, as the chief of staff suggested to me in a recent meeting, we have decided to join forces and voice our concerns with the main italian and european farmers' and environmental organizations: i am talking about federbio, i am talking about copagri, the cia, and pan europe. we have just finished presenting and drafting a common and shared position paper, which we will then present to the commission. these alternatives are supported by, among other things, community directives and are also endorsed by academic and scientific figures. i doubt that the competent authorities can turn a blind eye to this and not take responsibility.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, our lands (salento) and our farmers have been hit hard by an epidemic which european rules and controls have not been able to stem. our farmers are victims, not perpetrators. olive trees are not only the main source of income, but also a strong identity trait. apulia and the salento, without their great centuries-old olive trees, would be like paris without its famous tower. the decision of the committee on plant health not to pursue the crazy idea of eradicating millions of olive trees in the infected areas is therefore a positive one. but it 's not enough . we need at least three interventions. first, resources under horizon 2020 to develop scientific knowledge that will enable us to eradicate this still poorly understood disease. secondly, urgent measures by the commission to compensate farmers and operators for the serious damage they have suffered. and thirdly, the rational management of the buffer zones.
written declarations of vote
in writing. ‒ considering that the nature of xyella fastidiosa is not fully known and that there are different conflicting scientific opinions on the measures to be taken to combat this bacterium, and also taking note that efsa itself has stated the likely low effectiveness of eradication as a conflicting intervention, especially in cases of spread that have already occurred, i have decided to abstain in voting on this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the joint resolution of the main groups in parliament was not convincing: while noting the commission's shortcomings in its delay and superficiality in dealing with the xylella emergency (which italy had flagged in time), it did not invite the commission to review the current eradication plan in place, the reliability of which efsa itself now expresses its scepticism. i therefore abstained on the final vote, instead supporting only resolution b8-0450/2015 calling on the commission to review its plan for the containment of the disease.
in writing. ‒ i have chosen to vote in favour of this resolution because i believe that the commission should put in place more effective prophylactic measures against infected products from third countries and that it should seriously consider compensating producers for the eradication measures and the loss of income that the xylella fastidiosa epidemic has caused so far and is still causing.
in writing. ‒ xylella fastidosa is not an italian problem, but a european one. the commission has also received information from the french authorities, which has confirmed that the plant health plan for the area of the outbreak is in place. such unjustified measures, which are in fact designed to protect the environment, add to the damage and require coordinated action by the european institutions. the european parliament's work on this resolution has made great strides in clarifying the problems we have raised. as a first response, the ban on the import of infected plants (which have also been found in france and other countries) solves the problem at its root. similarly, avoiding the total eradication of plants from the infected area by implementing less radical measures is of fundamental importance from a social, economic and environmental point of view. finally, the most important aspects are related to increased investment in scientific research and economic compensation measures for farmers and nurserymen to compensate for losses.
in writing. - i abstained. the nature of the pest is not fully understood and there are therefore conflicting scientific opinions on the phytosanitary measures to be taken. among these is the eradication of infected and potentially infected plants. the lega nord has clearly spoken out against this measure, which is a key element of the commission's proposal. although eradication has been a useful measure in the past for similar, though not identical, phenomena affecting other plant species (e.g. the vine, which was subject to a plant eradication plan), recent efsa positions acknowledge the substantial ineffectiveness of the intervention, especially in the face of the spread of the disease that has already occurred. as these trees are centuries old and, in any case, enter production after many years (decades, compared with the production levels of a historical plant), which also constitute a fundamental element of the rural landscape of those lands and therefore represent a not negligible economic, tourist and social value, our precautionary position is amply justified.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution in question to urge the commission and the member states to compensate farmers, particularly in puglia, for the eradication measures and the loss of income, including from tourism-related activities. i also call on the commission to use all possible funds and instruments to help the economic recovery of the affected areas and to encourage farmers to take preventive measures. no treatment for the diseased plants is currently available. the commission should therefore promote and intensify research efforts, increase international cooperation and address the matter as a matter of urgency. i welcome the eu's decision to restrict imports of plants from affected areas in third countries, such as coffee plants from costa rica and honduras, but i also stress that the commission's reaction times are often not fast enough to prevent plant diseases from spreading within the eu. in order to safeguard the territory, the eu's official plant health control system should be reviewed and, if necessary, the commission should introduce more restrictive import measures.
in writing. ‒ the xylella fastidiosa bacterium is a pest that is seriously affecting olive groves in the south of our country. i voted against the motion for a resolution because it provides for the eradication of all plants potentially susceptible to infection, even if they are healthy, within 100 metres of the affected areas, in order to create a 'buffer zone'. this is an exaggerated preventive measure, lacking any clear scientific support, which will bring the economy of the entire region to its knees by hitting a flagship of italian production in the area.
in writing. ‒ xylella fastidiosa is an immediate and highly dangerous threat to the production of certain crops in southern europe and the epidemic affecting olive trees in apulia has already caused serious damage not only to producers but to the entire olive production chain. the olive sector in apulia accounts for 11.6% of the value of the region's total agricultural production, or eur 522 million, and for 30% of the value of italian olive production. the first outbreak was notified to the italian authorities in october 2013, but the situation has since deteriorated drastically. efsa, given the difficulty of controlling xylella once it has spread to a production area, stressed the need for prevention measures. the commission is therefore invited to prevent the import of infected material, to compensate producers for eradication measures and income losses, to carry out information campaigns, to set up an open database listing the competent authorities in the member states and at eu level, and to inform the ep periodically, or when deemed necessary, of the threat posed by xylella or other organisms. in the light of these considerations, i have voted in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the italian case of xylella fastidiosa. i share the criticism levelled at the european commission regarding the delays in handling the problem, as well as the inadequacy of the measures adopted until april 2015, which were only aimed at fighting the epidemic and not at preventing the import of infected material from non-eu countries. i share the wish to introduce measures to prevent or restrict the import of infected plants, such as those already adopted for infected coffea plants from honduras and costa rica, and any other useful action. the central point is still the request to the commission and the member states to provide compensation for the producers of the plants which will be eradicated in terms of damage not only to agricultural production but also to the cultural, historical and tourist heritage. i think it is right to use all the funds and instruments at our disposal to raise funds and to allow the economic recovery of the affected areas to take place as quickly as possible. efforts to improve research to increase scientific knowledge and identify appropriate treatments to eradicate these diseases, as well as to create an open database for the exchange of information and best practices, should also be increased.
in writing. ‒ the xylella epidemic affects one of the most important agricultural sectors, particularly in puglia, a region traditionally agricultural. the risk is that not only the agricultural sector will be brought to its knees, but also the whole production chain, including processing and marketing. unfortunately, there is currently no cure and simply eradicating the infected plants would not be enough to eradicate the disease, so efforts must be focused on prevention and research. on the one hand, therefore, it is necessary to activate all the plant protection procedures which will make it possible to contain the epidemic and prevent the risk of its further spread. on the other hand, research efforts should be stepped up, simplifying the use of funds and funding available to the institutes, to identify the pathogens and vectors causing the spread of the disease. in the meantime, the commission and the member states must take all the necessary steps to ensure that producers and territories are compensated, as they are suffering losses not only in terms of future agricultural production but also in terms of cultural and historical heritage.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on the xylella fastidiosa epidemic affecting olive trees. xylella fastidiosa is seriously damaging not only italian olive growers but also tourism and marketing activities related to this sector in general and is at risk of spreading to other countries of the union. immediate measures to combat the epidemic are needed, but equally important is the prevention strategy: in this resolution parliament calls on the commission to review the european system of official plant health controls in order to prevent this and new outbreaks from third countries from affecting european territories. we need a strong response from the european union, which can only respond with strong and coherent policies to the challenges that the globalised world of interconnected markets poses to us and will continue to pose in the future.
in writing. ‒ the xylella fastidiosa outbreak, in addition to having dramatic economic, environmental and social consequences, is putting apulia's olive growing at serious risk. the european union must take action to do everything possible to tackle the problem and prevent it from spreading to other regions. the european commission will also have to invest more in research to study and analyse this bacterium with a view to finding solutions to eradicate it.
in writing. ‒ xylella fastidiosa is a bacterium that is affecting olive groves in southern italy, particularly in puglia. the resolution calls for the removal of all plants within 100 meters of areas affected by the bacterium; this is considered an excessive precautionary measure which is not supported by any concrete scientific evidence. i voted against because the final version adopted by parliament does not incorporate some of the key amendments we have proposed. the final version of the resolution risks, therefore, putting local businesses, large and small, in serious difficulty and compromising one of italy's excellences.
in writing. ‒ the xylella fastidiosa emergency has clearly shown the limits of the european union's border management system. that is why, in the face of the disaster we are experiencing in the puglia region, we wanted to send a strong signal of support to the thousands of farmers involved - the first victims of this tragic situation - by proposing compensation for the eradication measures and the resulting loss of income. we also called for a review of the eu's official plant health control system and for more restrictive measures to be introduced for risky imports, so that such a tragedy would not happen again in the eu.
in writing. unfortunately, we are all aware of the enormous damage caused by the bacterium xylella fastidiosa in the apulia region, where farmers, farm owners and nurseries have been struggling for two years now with this phenomenon, which has led to decimation of production, blockade of the market, embargoes from algeria, morocco and france, and above all, they now see a new axis falling on their already difficult situation: a new plan to contain the risks will include the preventive felling of some 296,000 plants currently under seal as host plants for the bacterium. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the olive oil sector is not left to the detriment of the environment. in the face of this difficult emergency, i therefore fully support the call for the eu to intervene as soon as possible with compensation and support for the serious losses suffered by farmers and landowners, while also promoting the exchange of good practice and giving concrete evidence of a european union ready to intervene in national emergencies not only with measures of strict enforcement but also with interventions that translate into support, understanding and sharing of the ills, risks and the common search for their overcoming, for a return to the promotion of the great excellence that characterizes the member states and the union itself.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the xylella fastidiosa epidemic affecting olive trees, which was adopted following the debate on 30 april. xylella poses a serious threat to european agriculture, especially in southern europe, because of its unstoppable spread, the lack of effective plant treatments and the number of plant species susceptible to infection. the eu needs to strengthen prevention measures, given the origin of the bacterium from plants imported from costa rica. i therefore supported parliament's call for strengthening eu legislation on plant health controls and for equipping states with the necessary resources to control and prevent the entry into the eu of plant diseases from third countries by suspending imports of plants from infected countries. i have approved the request to the commission to compensate producers for the eradication measures and the income losses suffered, using european resources for the economic recovery of the affected areas. i think that we need to think further about the need to re-skill our agriculture and reorient it towards less invasive practices. i could not therefore help sharing the concerns about the intensive use of pesticides and the call for financial support for farmers who adopt agronomic practices to combat the bacterium and its vectors.
in writing. i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the xylella fastidiosa epidemic affecting olive trees in apulia, causing serious economic, environmental and social consequences. our aim must be to prevent the spread of the pest, but it is essential to have a proper aid and subsidy scheme for farmers to compensate them for the serious damage suffered as a result of the xylella emergency. at the same time, border controls must be strengthened and funds for scientific research increased.
in writing. ‒ in the light of the phytosanitary emergency that has been affecting olive groves in southern italy for some months now, but which could potentially spread to other crops and regions in europe, we intend to urge the council and the commission to resume the discussion on the revision of the system of official plant health controls on eu imports in a way that protects and safeguards the european territory, while avoiding a negative impact on global trade. we believe that it is necessary not only to provide adequate compensation for the economic losses suffered by producers, but also to strengthen research efforts by promoting greater international cooperation and making funding available to all national research institutes. it is necessary to improve scientific knowledge of xylella fastidiosa and to identify with certainty the pathogens and vectors that cause the spread of the disease, which is potentially dangerous for all european crops and areas.
in writing. ‒ as a southernist and a politician from a region that has been hit hard by the problem, i can only express my support for the work done by my colleagues on the xylella fastidiosa problem, which is an immediate and highly dangerous threat. the problem cannot and should not be limited to the production of certain crops in southern europe, including olive, almond and peach (as well as ornamental plants), but must be considered a threat that could lead to devastating and unprecedented losses, with major economic, environmental and social consequences for thousands of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ the resolution on xyella fastidiosa which we adopted by a large majority in the plenary is of the utmost importance in view of the catastrophic situation which the bacterium is creating in apulia and especially in salento. the commission will have to take account of what is stated in the resolution, especially when it comes to the eradication of olive trees already infected and healthy ones but only if within a hundred meters of the new outbreaks. it was also very important that the resolution should call for compensation for farmers who have been affected by the epidemic and who are now in a very difficult economic and financial situation. as indicated, there is a need to push for more incisive studies and scientific research on bacterial resistance; we could also consider a specific emergency fund for this situation, given the gravity of the situation. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new products.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the xylella fastidiosa epidemic affecting olive trees. it is time for europe to act to solve a problem which has seriously damaged a crop and a by-product which has made us famous throughout the world. the bacterium in question, which was introduced into italy by the importation of ornamental coffee plants from central america, has affected the olive groves of which puglia is rich, forcing growers to uproot and burn the plants because they are infected and dangerous for wildlife. i agree that the commission should be able to increase import controls, compensate for damage and allocate adequate resources, for example under the horizon 2020 programme, to carry out research and analysis on xylella fastidiosa and its vectors and to identify remedies.
in writing. ‒ the xylella fastidiosa outbreak spreading in southern italy has caused serious damage to the agricultural sector, particularly to olive groves in puglia. in these circumstances, greater coordination and synergy between the union emergency measures and national and regional interventions to prevent, control and eradicate the bacterium is desirable. it is important that the means used to combat the pathogen are proportionate to the objectives, so as to preserve the territory and the environment as much as possible. i also hope that the sacrifices made by farmers will be taken into account by providing appropriate and adequate forms of compensation. i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this resolution in the hope that it will contribute to a better understanding and solution of the problem at european level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the epidemic of xylella fastidiosa, which is decimating olive trees in large areas of the apulia region and threatens to spread to other areas. in the text we call on the european commission to take two urgent measures: to compensate producers who have suffered losses as a result of olive tree eradication operations carried out to contain the spread of xylella fastidiosa beyond the borders of italy, in a timely manner; intensify research and prevention efforts, including through increased funding and international collaboration. the text also supports the eu decision to restrict imports of plants from affected areas in third countries, in particular imports of coffee plants from costa rica and honduras. however, in order to prevent such outbreaks from spreading further within the union, it is also necessary to review the eu plant health control system by introducing, if necessary, additional restrictions on imports.
in writing. ‒ the joint resolution was too weak and, in my view, more harmful than helpful to mediterranean biodiversity. the problem is certainly not the quantity or quality of pesticides that will be used to kill the pathogen, not least because it is not yet scientifically clear whether the disease has developed for the reasons that led to the first eradications. further studies are needed on the agent causing the rapid drying of olive trees and there is a reasonable suspicion that the neglect of olive trees is the cause of the epidemic. the common agricultural policy is a penalty for small producers, and that is a fact: the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to provide for the possibility of a reduction in the number of olive trees planted in the community. the resolution tabled by the five star movement was intended to emphasize the risks of desertification and destruction of agricultural heritage that the current eradication programme entails. it would have been much more useful, at least to cast doubt on the italian and european authorities, at least to ask the right questions. once again, may europe live.
in writing. xylella infection is seriously endangering millions of olive trees and the economy of entire territories. the bacteria from latin america is destroying a heritage of centuries-old plants. the current large-scale eradication programme adopted by the commission is of concern given the potential risks of desertification and destruction of agricultural heritage coupled with the lack of clear scientific evidence of the real effectiveness of the strategy adopted to prevent the spread of the pathogen. i therefore believe that it is essential to consider alternative solutions which also safeguard the agri-food sector and the environment in the regions concerned. it is also important to provide concrete support to the farmers concerned to enable them to adopt appropriate agricultural practices to combat xylella and its vectors, while ensuring adequate compensation for lost livelihoods and income in the event of eradication of olive trees and other plants potentially host to the bacterium. for the reasons set out above, i therefore supported motion for a resolution b8-0450/2015.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe that the european union needs to commit itself to supporting farmers who are facing the xylella epidemic. the commission will have to put in place preventive and control measures, but at the same time help those who are most at risk from this disease in economic and social terms.
in writing. ‒ thousands of olive trees uprooted or cut down to dead trunks. this is the sad scenario that is unfolding in salento, in puglia, where the xylella fastidiosa bacterium has affected olive groves and created a real collective psychosis. this resolution calls for more funds for research and for areas affected by this bacterium and for increased border controls and compensation for all farmers harmed by the spread of the bacterium. the commission has been asked to impose a ban on imports of infected coffee plants from honduras and costa rica and to increase controls at the borders and within the member countries themselves to prevent the spread of the bacterium, which affects not only olive trees but also many other types of plants. in addition, the commission was invited to develop comprehensive guidelines for the implementation of disease prevention and control measures, which could also be used as a support tool by the competent authorities and services of the member states. however, this text lacks a cost-benefit analysis of pathogen eradication strategies, which could result in healthy trees being eradicated simply because they are potential hosts, regardless of any controls.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution on the outbreak of xylella fastidiosa. the resolution calls on the commission to take targeted measures against the spread of xylella, inter alia to prevent the import of infected material into the eu. i think it is particularly appropriate to ask the commission to apply more stringent measures, such as allowing imports from only production sites not affected by the epidemic. i would like to conclude by reiterating my call on the commission to review the implementation of the european plant health control system in order to protect and safeguard our territory against the epidemic.
