president-in-office of the council.– madam president, i am grateful for this opportunity to discuss with you the youth labour market situation in the european union. the presidency attached great importance to improving the conditions of groups facing the biggest challenges to accessing or remaining in employment. these groups include, in particular, young people, and among them especially those without proper education and skills. fighting youth unemployment and ensuring sustainable labour market integration remains a top priority for the eu. indeed, the europe 2020 strategy has put a special focus on implementing effective measures to address youth unemployment. the reality is that youth unemployment is still at a very high level in several member states, leading to underutilised talents, the loss of human resources and, in some cases, leaving damaging consequences for the rest of the working life. in this context, the youth guarantee, together with the financial provisions of the youth employment initiative, are highly relevant: both measures seek to support the fight against youth unemployment in the most affected regions, namely those with youth unemployment rates above 25%. as a positive example, i would like to underscore the experience of latvia. latvia is one of the countries which started the implementation of the youth guarantee as of january 2014. we can already see the first results: the youth unemployment rate decreased by 3.8% in 2014. a lot depends on the programmes implemented by the member states. nevertheless, it is already clear that more needs to be done. despite the promising stimulus, the youth employment initiative and the youth guarantee are not a panacea to solve europe’s youth unemployment problems. they are part of a range of tools to address the issue. as we all know, the shorter implementation period of the youth employment initiative compared to the multiannual financial framework cycle means that concrete progress in the first years will be crucial for the overall success of the initiative. this can help to tackle the problem faced by the millions of young europeans who are without a job and who do not have adequate access to education or training. therefore, i am convinced that the honourable members of the european parliament share my view that any further delay in the implementation of the youth employment initiative is likely to weaken the impact of actions undertaken by member states to combat youth unemployment. one of the main obstacles in the implementation of the youth employment initiative is the lack of sufficient cash flow to provide advance payments to beneficiaries. the presidency wants to highlight the importance and timeliness of the current legislative proposal to accelerate the implementation of the youth employment initiative. i therefore fully agree with the european parliament that making funding available to member states earlier in the implementation process is a key condition for improving the performance and generating tangible results soon. sufficient liquidity at the beginning of the implementation process will allow for faster delivery of the relevant policy measures set out in the national youth guarantee implementation plans. we can be proud that the current amending legislative proposal has been finalised in record time. the council adopted the draft proposal yesterday. today, immediately after your vote, we, together with president schulz, co—signed the text already. after the publication, which will occur in the coming week, member states will be able to receive pre-financing. in total, the initial pre-financing made available from the specific allocation for the youth employment initiative will be increased to about eur 1 billion in 2015. i would like to take this opportunity to reaffirm that the council will continue to actively monitor developments concerning the youth employment situation and the implementation by the member states of the youth guarantee and the youth employment initiative. at the same time, we need to keep in mind that the causes behind youth unemployment are complex. the increase in funding is complementary to other measures and reforms that member states have to make in order to tackle the different crisis-related and structural problems behind the youth employment situation. all in all, to significantly reduce unemployment, we need to do more to create new jobs. last but not least, let me also underscore the important role the social partners play in this context.

zanda kalniņa-lukaševica,president-in-office of the council. madam president, the last point in today’s agenda: japanese whaling activities in the antarctic. the issue of japanese whaling activities in the antarctic is not new, but it gained new prominence in 2010 when australia filed an application with the international court of justice against japanʼs programme called jarpa ii. in its application, australia contested the legality of jarpa ii as being incompatible with the international convention on the regulation of whaling. the international court delivered its judgment on 31 march 2014 and found against japan on a number of counts. we read this judgment with great interest, as we consider it offers a definitive interpretation of the convention and its schedule, and clarifies the legal framework for scientific whaling. it is an important milestone for all contracting governments to the international whaling commission (iwc), certainly when it comes to assessing the necessity of having recourse to lethal methods of sampling where non-lethal alternatives exist. the presidency, at that time, on behalf of the eu and its member states, expressed this view at the meeting of the international whaling commission held in september 2014, in portorož, in slovenia. we supported the adoption of resolution 2014-5, called ‘whaling under special permit’, which offers, among other elements, directions for the scientific committee to consider when assessing new and existing special permit research programmes. yesterday, the iwc scientific committee began its meeting in san diego. japan has submitted a proposal for a new special permit research programme in the antarctic ocean, which is currently being reviewed under what is known as the ʽannex p processʼ. the findings of the expert panel set up by the scientific committee will be reviewed and the scientific committee should make a recommendation to the iwc. the european union and its member states have always favoured an approach that would preserve both the independence of the scientific committee, as a scientific forum, and the policy prerogatives of the iwc as the ultimate decision-making authority under the international convention. under this approach, policy matters should not be discussed in san diego. we remain ready to engage politically with japan at the appropriate level and in the appropriate forum, once the scientific committee has issued its recommendations to the international whaling commission.
i come from a geographical area known as the cetacean sanctuary, an international marine area with a significant presence of these ecologically vital mammals. i shall not go into the importance of their protection, which is recognised by the european union, which prohibits their capture. but not everywhere. japan has announced that it will resume its antarctic whaling program on scientific grounds, despite a ruling by the international court of justice in the hague just a year ago that it was necessary to suspend the practice as lacking scientific purpose, not least because let's face it so-called scientific evidence often ended up on the shelves of japanese supermarkets. yeah, let's not hide behind a finger: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's research is not disguised as a purely commercial activity. japan's intention is therefore in clear contradiction to the international moratorium on commercial whaling of the sea giants imposed in 1986 by the international whaling commission, a body set up to protect endangered cetaceans. we cannot stand by and let this madness continue with the complicit silence of the institutions. europe is opposed without a doubt. the trade agreements between the eu and japan are being discussed these days. i believe that europe must also be more ambitious in this area of agreement and must make it a condition for the cessation of illegal fishing.

already mentioned this. it could be achieved by reorienting public expenditure towards more growth-enhancing investment and by swiftly implementing the investment plan for europe. second, a renewed commitment to growth-enhancing structural reforms and reforms in product, services and labour markets that increase productivity and foster investment, which are key to enhancing the euro area potential growth. reforms implemented in recent years in some member states are starting to bear fruit, and accommodative monetary policies help facilitate their implementation and enhance their effectiveness. third, the continued pursuit of fiscal responsibility. the current broadly neutral aggregate fiscal stance is appropriate in the light of the gradual recovery. yet, in order to address both the short- and medium-term challenges europe faces, member states with fiscal space should seize opportunities to step up useful investment, while those with large deficits can consolidate debts. everywhere, the composition of public finance can be designed in a more growth-friendly manner. these three actions have been the economic priorities of the juncker commission since its first day in office. they were the guidance given in the 2015 annual growth survey, and the package of country-specific recommendations we adopted last week fully reflects these key priorities to reinvigorate growth and employment in the european union. under this new commission, we have revised our policy coordination process to promote better implementation of the recommendations. so far, about 55% of the recommendations to member states from last year have recorded at least some progress in their implementation. the ongoing recovery is an opportunity for all stakeholders to redouble their efforts. let us not miss this opportunity, and let us make sure we act on the new recommendations.

and you in particular, mr commissioner, to be an active spokesman - to stress that our objectives, which are always very ambitious, must be equally ambitious and equally tenacious in the implementation phase, otherwise we set ourselves great goals but then we do not achieve them because we do not put the necessary instruments and resources in motion. i am thinking in particular of the third energy package. i was in parliament, like other colleagues, when we launched it, but we are very short-changed, as we know, in the implementation phase. not all the rules have been implemented in all countries, in all member states: in some cases, yes, but in others, these objectives are still very far away. and there is a great asymmetry between the realities of the different countries, which makes our european market very lame. that is why i emphasize this attention to the need to proceed with more concrete action in our policies. in particular, the question concerns the implementation of the obligations provided for in the so-called remit (the regulation on the monitoring of the wholesale energy market). this 2011 regulation provides that from this year onwards acer the european agency which has been entrusted with the task of coordinating national energy regulators will be given the task of monitoring the wholesale market in addition to the tasks it already has as the body coordinating the regulators. and already this year it should examine a very considerable number - i do not know if we are calling it here, in the question - but it is a very, very considerable number of contracts, of transactions that have been carried out, but about which we are not sure that they meet the criteria, the rules of transparency, the rules of fairness that we envisage. the commission has therefore given acer a very difficult task to undertake, and it must do so as from october this year. but we have found, in the hearings we periodically hold in committee with all the agencies dealing with matters also within our competence, that it has absolutely no manpower and adequate resources to do so. we therefore ask the commission: what do you think? if this monitoring fails, what happens in the european market? is there more certainty or is there more uncertainty? is there more transparency or is there more opacity? that is why we are asking for an assessment of this situation, for a forecast of what will happen if acer is not able to do this. we also stress that the partial authorization which has been given to supplement the resources it currently has with some 15 units is insufficient. they've calculated with a very careful study that you need at least 45 units of a certain level. i know that the commission has adopted - in writing. ‒ we welcome this report, which is necessary as the increasingly challenging security environment for the union, characterised by new risks and threats that no member state can face alone, requires a strengthening of the common security and defence policy (csdp) to make it a more effective strategic instrument and a guarantee of the security of eu citizens and the promotion of european interests and values. we also stress that the annual financial envelope remains too small to cover all planning, conduct and support tasks, especially as several missions are launched almost simultaneously, but that at the same time it is crucial to consider what and how much potential savings for the eu and individual national budgets would result from promoting union-wide synergies in the military sector, including in transport, training and medical assistance. the lisbon treaty provides for new provisions for the eu in the field of csdp, which have not yet been explored. the council could therefore have recourse to article 44 teu, which allows a group of member states to proceed with the implementation of a csdp mission in order to develop a faster decision-making process.
in writing. ‒ given that the security environment presents increasingly challenging challenges inside and outside the union, characterised by new risks and threats that no member state can address alone, a reinforcement of the common security and defence policy (csdp) is required to make it a more effective strategic instrument and a genuine guarantee of the security of the citizens of the european union and the promotion of european interests and values. i voted in favour of the resolution, considering that the union must strengthen security at its external borders and that there is, however, provision for adequate democratic control at the level of the union's institutions over all missions and operations, whether civilian or military.
in writing. ‒ the recent threats facing the eu on an almost daily basis call for a reinforcement of the common security and defence policy to make it a real instrument of protection and guarantee for eu citizens and to implement actions that no member state could afford to undertake on its own. i agree with what is said in the report, which i voted in favour of: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the csdp's mandate to include the military and civilian sectors. there must always be structured cooperation with regard to csdp missions and operations, with full transparency on expenditure so that the credibility of the actions taken is not clouded. the ep will be responsible for monitoring the budgeting of the various csdp operations and missions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy, which expresses parliament's concerns on the eve of the june european council about the deficit in the csdp financing system. it calls for more flexibility and consistency in funding and identifies the lack of transparency in the financial allocations for missions and operations as one of the main problems. i also share the call for a review of the athena mechanism to ensure that the procedures and rules allow the union to be more flexible and efficient in the deployment of eu civilian missions and military operations.
in writing. - i voted against this report. it is the opposite of the peaceful vocation which marked europe after the horrors of the two world wars and after the commitment not to repeat the mistakes of the past. the eu should instead urgently realise that the display of muscle is useless and even counterproductive in the management of conflicts, the lasting solution of which is possible only through a strictly peaceful and multilateral approach. the alleged importance of muscularity is underlined by this report, which does not at all draw the necessary line, namely the clear demarcation between civilian missions and possible military missions, and thus opens the way to a dangerous ambiguity in the way the eu's presence is manifested in conflict zones. the prospect of the eu budget being burdened with chapters related to military expenditure, such as those for the creation of tactical groups, for the financing of the military and technological base of defence or for the extension of the athena mechanism, is also dangerous. it means taking additional resources, through taxation, from citizens and taxpayers already exhausted by an economic crisis managed on the basis of austerity, and using them for purposes that have nothing to do with increasing prosperity.
in writing. i voted against the report on the financing of the common security and defence policy (csdp) because i consider it unacceptable and irresponsible to use eu financial resources to strengthen the eu's military dimension, which is described as a strategic tool to strengthen the union's role in preventing and managing international crises. the report, after expressing serious concern at the budget cuts that have affected the defence sector in recent years, calls for more funds to be allocated to csdp policies, by strengthening the mechanisms for the automatic financing of military missions. in particular, it calls for further expansion of the common expenditure linked to military cooperation through the athena mechanism, which is currently insufficient to cover the costs of military operations. it also called for consideration to be given to attracting financing from third countries or international organisations, including nato, with which it also recommended closer cooperation. beyond the strong reservations about the foreign policy approach supported by this report, i believe that in the context of the severe economic crisis in which the european citizens are still plunged, it is absurd and a sign of grave irresponsibility to devote to militarism vital resources which could be used to combat unemployment, poverty and social exclusion, the roots of instability inside and outside europe.
in writing. ‒ the report voted today contains a worrying fact: as much as €190 billion is spent within the eu on defence. given the widespread social impacts of austerity in the member states, and considering that such vast resources could fuel both european recovery and resolving instability at its root, by addressing social emergencies in theatres of crisis, this expenditure seems utterly insane. the eu cannot think of implementing its own military policy, nor should it seek to do so. the lack of financial resources, the inefficiency and ineffectiveness of decisions and the difficulties in including military missions in the union budget simply run counter to the european legal framework, which is not prepared to decide on or implement military measures, especially in the presence of a cfsp and a csdp that are not yet integrated and in the light of the lack of a real political union. the increase in the defence budget, which would be spent on 'petersberg missions', also seems to contradict the union's integration objectives: the european union's position is that the eu should be able to take the lead in the fight against terrorism, and that the eu should be able to take the lead in the fight against terrorism. for all these reasons, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ while there are parts of the text that can be shared, there are also parts that are unclear and do not take account of the actual situation in which individual member states pay; that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the union and the member states must work to ensure that security and defence capability is safeguarded and, at the same time, that the defence industry sector is properly supported, as it is a key sector of the economy both in terms of volume and innovation capacity.
in writing. - i voted against it. this report too is too 'crushed' on the imposition of a single line for all member states. it is considered that an internal market based on common rules is necessary for the development of a competitive european defence technology and industrial base (editb) and that it is crucial to ensure the necessary capabilities and thus the security of eu citizens. the setting is wrong: the means are already there and they are those of the member states, and if the eu cannot take a stand on the relevant defence issues and merely bases its foreign and defence policy on the choices made by nato and the usa, it will be useless to create yet another bureaucratic creature. it seems to me that the purpose of this report is to give further advantages to the large industrial groups in the defence sector, perhaps outside europe.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe. the report highlighted that, to be truly effective, peacekeeping and security missions under the common security and defence policy (csdp) must be able to respond quickly and immediately. the existence of a genuine european defence market is a key element in achieving these objectives. however, the european defence market is too fragmented, resulting in an increasing dependence of the european defence industry on extra-eu exports. i therefore believe that the member states should do more to achieve a more integrated european market, which would limit the duplication of defence research programmes and activities and increase european competitiveness in this field. i hope therefore that the june council, as the report emphasizes, will be able to take concrete measures and provide specific guidelines in this regard.
in writing. ‒ this report, while presenting several aspects on which i cannot agree, also highlights some important issues such as better optimisation of expenditure, the search for synergies and cooperation between states and a more careful and profitable management of the cost-benefit ratio with taxpayers' money. i therefore preferred to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is a priority not to underestimate the wave of armed conflicts and wars as well as the increasingly worrying threat of terrorism within and outside the eu. i am in favour of the union tackling the current situation through a coordinated and united approach, making sure that the articulation of budgetary policies is more geared towards strategic choices, in particular the review of the defence procurement package.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the impact of developments in the european security and defence capability markets in europe, sharing its views and believing that the increasingly serious and numerous threats posed by terrorist groups to the european union as a whole require a unified response by pooling civilian and military resources and coordinating action. in particular, in order to ensure an adequate level of security and defence in the face of the spending cuts caused by the economic crisis, it is essential to make the most of the potential synergies arising from cooperation between member states. in such a context, the establishment of a properly functioning, competitive and efficient internal market for defence products would make a significant contribution to achieving the objectives of the csdp, including by fostering research and technological innovation, which are prerequisites for the modernisation of the european defence industry. it should also be noted that increased cooperation between member states would certainly help to avoid duplication of efforts and programmes for defence equipment, which have been carried out independently by each member state, further reducing the costs of such policy and ensuring a more rapid and effective response to internal and external challenges and threats.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the impact of developments in european defence markets on security and defence capabilities in europe because it focuses on the key issue of increased cooperation between member states in this area. i believe that there is a need for greater convergence of national and european defence and security policies, especially in order to deal with the new and more modern threats from cyberspace and new technologies. it is important, especially through better implementation of the horizon 2020 and cosme programmes, that smes are facilitated in taking advantage of funding opportunities for the development of european projects related to security and defence. in this connection, i am concerned that european companies in this sector are being forced to find new markets abroad, with the result that know-how, production and intellectual property are being transferred to other countries. i join the call on the commission to step up its efforts to increase crossborder cooperation, so as to avoid the implementation of protectionist practices by some member states, and to support technological innovation, which is the key to a modern and advanced defence and security industry.
in writing. the report expresses parliament's concern at the widespread cuts in the defence budget in most member states. the lack of coordination can jeopardise the functioning of these policies, leading to the renunciation of strategic means and the loss of opportunities that could be offered by a better synergy of defence policies. the document also expresses concern at developments on the european defence market, which are increasingly open to external dependencies in the sector, at a time of increasingly challenging security conditions. for these reasons, i give my consent to this report, aware of the real need for decisive action.
in writing. ‒ we welcome this report, which is necessary given that investment in defence research and technology by all member states, as well as joint investment in defence research and technology within the framework of european cooperation, has declined at an alarming rate over the last few years, and whereas the success of peace and security missions in the framework of the csdp depends to a large extent on their ability to respond quickly and immediately, and whereas therefore a key aspect is the need to create a genuine european defence market, to eliminate duplication and reduce red tape. we are also concerned about the risks of external dependencies in the european defence sector at a time of increasingly complex and challenging security conditions, in particular the combined effect of the lack of coordination of member states' defence budgets, the continued fragmentation of the market despite the new internal market rules, the increasing dependence of the defence industry on extra-eu exports and the increase in foreign investment in the european defence sector in certain countries.
in writing. ‒ whereas the new legislation on the european defence market was introduced with the 2009 defence package and all 28 member states have transposed the new provisions into their national legal systems; whereas the crux of this new legislation is the introduction of a regulatory framework based on transparency, non-discrimination and competition that addresses the specificities of the defence sector; that the member states have agreed on the need to develop a european market for defence equipment and services; whereas the european council has called for the establishment of a security of supply regime at union level; the european council in brussels on 14 and 15 december adopted a resolution on the situation in the middle east and the situation in the middle east.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which expresses parliament's concern about the widespread and largely uncoordinated cuts to the defence budget in most member states. i believe that this lack of coordination puts the security of the european union at risk, leading to the renunciation of strategic means and capabilities and to the loss of the opportunities that could be offered by the coordination of defence policies and the pooling and sharing of defence means in terms of the realisation of the eu's strategic autonomy, the security of its supplies and the defence of its citizens and its interests.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think we should not be surprised that eritrea is the emblematic example of the objective contradictions in which the european union's development and cooperation policies are exercised. why a contradiction? because on the one hand we are providing more resources for the country's livelihood in an attempt to curb the exodus of refugees and to help solve the social problems that exist, and on the other hand we are doing all this in a country where human rights are widely violated. it is difficult to get out of this contradiction, because not providing resources means making the situation of the most needy groups more difficult, but providing them in this situation also means not having any guarantee that this money will reach the people in need. what then? we must introduce new constraints in the commission's proposal, and this must be in writing. firstly, development aid must be accompanied by a monitoring action by the eu delegation in eritrea and together we must call for the immediate opening of the human rights chapter. only in this context is the decision taken by the european commission acceptable.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the tensions in eritrea are also of great concern to europe, which has been forced to confront the migration emergency in recent weeks. after syria, we are talking about the second country of origin of migrants, who try to cross the mediterranean sea. most eritreans have no hope for their future and detention is a very common experience, affecting a large number of individuals - women, men, boys and even children. this is a very difficult issue, which is also denounced by a united nations investigation, which highlights the many human rights violations committed in eritrea. according to the un report, the government also used tensions with neighbouring countries as a pretext to ignore human rights and to subject every aspect of the citizens' daily lives to military control. the european union must re-launch a dialogue with asmara to try to resolve the issue of migration flows at its roots, but at the same time it must make economic aid conditional on a significant increase in fundamental freedoms in the country.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, cyberattacks are certainly one of the greatest challenges to the security of the international community in the 21st century and are a powerful geopolitical weapon in the service of possible new forms of war, far removed from those to which we have unfortunately become accustomed, but no less dangerous. they increasingly threaten our fundamental rights and our way of life. unfortunately, there is a huge gap between a security system, which is essentially based on national strategies and borders, and the global nature of the network and its threats, which are increasingly less random and more and more the work of professionals behind whom criminal organizations and even governments hide. the european union must therefore move from declarations of principle by european leaders to concrete commitments to develop coherent and effective legislation. a striking example of the gap between words and deeds is the ongoing trilogues on the directive on computer network security. the commission proposal, which was significantly strengthened by the european parliament at first reading, is certainly a first step towards the creation of a common european strategy, providing for significant forms of operational cooperation and prevention and rapid response mechanisms, thus ensuring a resilient european network. unfortunately, the adoption of this directive, despite the efforts of the european parliament to find a compromise, is currently jeopardized by the attitude of the majority of member states, who are obviously still too jealous of their own security powers and too short-sighted to focus on the new global nature of cyber threats. only with common european strategies, effectively coordinated at international level, will we be able to combat this new form of warfare to ensure an open and secure digital space and to take full advantage of the opportunities offered by the internet and technologies, without compromising freedoms and without affecting our habits.
madam president, i have listened carefully to the whole debate and i must say that, as a representative of my political group, and as mr schwab, who spoke on behalf of our group, i am not satisfied with the way the commission and the european council are approaching this problem, it seems to me that there are many words, many sentences, but few actions. cyberattacks are here, they're increasing, causing enormous economic damage. now they're touching the media, threatening freedom of speech, and we're not just dealing with phrases, plans and, say, theses. there must be concrete actions and concrete steps. i was involved in this security when i was a member of the czech government, and i have to say that the czech republic is very prepared for cyberattacks in this matter. in the last few days, we've been running a special lab in brno, which has just been secured by both the state on one side and the local university, and we're going to simulate individual cyber attacks and we want to be prepared for them. i believe that the key is to strengthen the resilience of critical infrastructure, prevention is the key, in my opinion. of course, it is possible to talk about what the commissioner has been talking about, i.e. strengthening repression in the form of increased money, strengthening the powers of europol, but this should not lead to a police state, i.e. let us strengthen europol, but not at the expense of the rights of our citizens. as i said, i think repression can play a role, but it's not the key. the key is prevention, and that's where we really have to catch up, we're not ready for that as europe, and it's now up to the commission and of course the council to start being very active on this issue, for the states to start talking to each other, to start cooperating, for each country to have a clear authority that monitors cybersecurity. of course, we also need to complete the legislation that is still on the table.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, attacks on the media are not entirely new. they are often politically motivated, target highly visible victims to maximise the perpetrators' notoriety, and are embedded in a generally broad and highly complex geopolitical context. recent cyber threat studies have shown that the media is one of the most attacked sectors. the recent attack on tv5monde by isis-linked hackers, besides representing a serious attack on the foundations of our democracy, is definitely alarming and should not be underestimated just because it did not cause any casualties. this unprecedented attack has raised cybersecurity risk to new levels of severity. the new scope and breadth that attacks can reach as a direct result of the increasing dependence of connected sectors on technology and connectivity should make us think. it is therefore essential that, beyond the nis directive, the eu cybersecurity strategy and the european agenda on security, the digital single market is also designed and implemented with a 'security by design' approach... mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the regulation we are voting on tomorrow is the adoption of the financial discipline: a mathematical calculation by the commission which sets a rate of reduction of direct payments for 2015 to constitute the crisis reserve for the 2016 budget. our group will vote in favour of the draft report by mr siekierski, which we have already approved in the committee on agriculture under the simplified procedure. however, this debate gives us the opportunity to stress that the mechanism of financial discipline is the result of a reduction in the agricultural budget decided with the financial perspective 2014-2020, which left the agricultural budget without any margin to respond to crises. but as has been said, crises are becoming more frequent - as the one caused by the russian embargo shows - and prices are also becoming more volatile. it is the farmers themselves, through the reduction of the first pillar of the cap, who have to pay for these crises. in the long term, commissioner, we must therefore rethink the instruments for crisis management, new and stronger instruments which can provide a safety net for farmers and thus enable them to compete fearlessly on the global market. finally, commissioner, in the last parliament parliament had argued that financial discipline should only be applied to farmers who receive more than eur 5 000, in order to better protect small farmers. unfortunately, in the final agreement the threshold was set at eur 2 000. we continue to think that a higher threshold would be a fairer way of doing things, that it would not reduce payments to small farmers, and that it would only charge those for whom a small reduction in their cap payment would not have an excessively negative impact.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, counterfeit products are harmful to consumers and they are detrimental to the economy, to quality production and research. we therefore consider it crucial to have a strategy for the promotion and protection of intellectual property rights which is at the same time sensitive to the possible impact on the accessibility of certain sensitive products such as medicines and which does not restrict individual rights. these are the principles on which we based our own-initiative report on the strategy for the protection and strengthening of intellectual property rights in third countries, which was voted on in the committee on international trade on 14 april. the report responds to the commission communication of july 2014 which sought, for the first time, to propose new action in this area after the failure of acta. intellectual property rights have undergone a remarkable evolution in the last decade, due to the impressive speed with which technological innovation has spread, including in emerging countries. for this reason, an effective strategy must first take account of these developments and propose coherent interventions. it is estimated that 39% of total economic activity in the european union and 26% of employment, i.e. 56 million jobs, are currently generated by companies investing in and using intellectual property rights. in the report we are putting to the vote in parliament today, we first of all appreciate the approach taken by the commission, especially because it takes account in a balanced way of the divergent interests of the holders of intellectual property rights on the one hand and of the consumers on the other. in general, no legislation works well unless all the actors involved are encouraged and involved. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud, and it is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data. counterfeit products are no longer just luxury goods, but also everyday products such as toys, medicines, cosmetics and food, thus posing a risk to consumers' health. that is why we are asking the commission in the report to make a constant effort to involve, to be transparent, to communicate and to coordinate all the actions. the main points of our report are as follows: the need to differentiate between physical counterfeiting of trade marks and patents and infringements of copyright; the call for closer cooperation between regulators and customs; the establishment of a constructive dialogue involving the various stakeholders; the strengthening of the european observatory on infringement of intellectual property rights with full management independence; the need to adapt the price of generic medicines to the situation in the individual countries in which they are marketed in order to allow everyone to have access to the products; the need to emphasise that geographical indications are as important as other types of intellectual property, insofar as they ensure the traceability of products for the benefit of consumers and safeguard the skills of producers; a greater presence of intellectual property rights helpdesks in developing countries. in conclusion, we believe that communication is a good first step, but it must necessarily be followed up. it is also crucial that the european union should have a coherent internal regulatory framework in this area, which would ensure not only greater effectiveness but also greater negotiating power, both in bilateral relations and in multilateral discussions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, intellectual property rights have developed along the historical path of constitutional charters, are linked to the universality of rights and form the basis, with equal dignity to others, of the development of european and international civilization. to be able to preserve the originality of one's creative moment coincides with the creation of the work itself and with its translation into a good of life, abstract and concrete, and is a conquest of the western world. this need is even more evident today, when scientific, literary and artistic production are not separated from innovation and affect competitiveness, employment and cultural diversity. the health and safety of consumers are closely linked and represent the ultimate aim of scientific thinking, which must develop in accordance with the centrality of man. for example, the authenticity of medicinal and food products is constantly under attack by the underground economy and organised crime, and it is not just a 'made in europe' problem. i agree with the report and i hope that the european union will adopt a really effective action plan, which will as soon as possible renew the legal framework of reference which no longer meets the modern need for protection and which also includes third countries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure under consideration concerning the fixing of the adjustment rate for direct payments for the calendar year 2015 as provided for in regulation (ec) no 1306/2013. in order to support the agricultural sector in the event of a crisis, a reserve is to be established by applying, at the beginning of each year, a reduction to direct payments through a financial discipline mechanism. the amount of the reserve to be included in the commission's draft budget for 2016 shall be eur 441,6 million. the adjustment rate for direct payments shall apply only to direct payments exceeding eur 2 000. in bulgaria, croatia and romania direct payments are being phased in during the calendar year 2015. the financial discipline will therefore not apply in these member states.

in writing. ‒ the report, the result of careful work, lays the foundations for the new strategy for equality between men and women, a characteristic element of any society that wants to call itself mature. the report covers a wide range of issues, from the fight against violence against women to the different needs of women in relation to work, the right to health as a universal right and sexual and reproductive rights. it is important that the european union recognises these needs and takes them on board, and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ my vote on the draft report on the european union strategy on gender equality is a negative vote. and it's a painful no, because i know perfectly well that, in fact, equality between men and women in all areas of life is progressing too slowly. but this equality will never be achieved by devaluing the value of the family, which is a serious cultural backwardness in europe. it is not through the recognition of gay families or of same-sex parenting that men and women will be guaranteed the same rights. it is not by a law that prevents adopted children from knowing their natural parents that women will be more like men, nor by being able to abort unwanted children. for all these reasons i could not vote in favour of this resolution. equality between men and women is achieved through legislation that protects life from conception to its natural end, through aid to families, to working mothers, by establishing equal pay, by promoting the reconciliation of private and professional life, by guaranteeing equality in education. that is what every member state should do, even without being told to do so by the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ the report comes at a crucial moment for the european union, as this year marks the 20th anniversary of the adoption of the beijing platform for action and the revision of the millennium development goals, and the report presents data on progress made in gender equality worldwide. the eu objective is to make steady progress towards effective equality between women and men, whereas, unfortunately, traditional gender roles and stereotypes still profoundly influence the distribution of tasks in the family, in education, at work and in society in general. according to european commission figures, only 5% of ceos in the eu are women. the next five years are crucial for a more concrete and thorough implementation of this strategy in all areas, which is part of a larger set of equalization objectives that the european union must be able to guarantee to its citizens, such as ethnicity, social class, sexual orientation, religion, nationality or age. the report sets out key objectives for the implementation of rights recognised by the eu treaties. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the measure in question because it contains sensitive and controversial provisions on ethical issues that would need to be explored further. the ppe group has therefore decided to vote against the eu strategy on equality between men and women as it is not in line with the group's guidelines.
in writing. ‒ i believe that gender equality is a serious issue and as such should be treated without ideological bias. it is true that, unfortunately, in 2015 we still have to remember that human beings have equal rights regardless of their gender. however, at least as regards the european parliament's powers, it is also worth recalling how some issues have been forced into this report because they are not directly relevant. i have decided how to vote on the basis of these considerations.
in writing. ‒ once again we are faced with the attempt to use a relationship and a subject as important as equality between men and women, forcing some concepts that cannot be shared. some people here argue that it is the progress and development of man and our society that should provide for the right to abortion as a fundamental human right, to change the concept of parenting beyond natural law, to ensure sexual and reproductive health, without explaining, however, with what limits. i think that the european parliament should try to give a definite and effective answer to the real problems of everyday life, such as the situation of young people who have no jobs or the means to start a family and have children. we should re-establish the right priorities in our political agenda.
in writing. ‒ the report presents the european union's strategy for achieving the main objectives on equality between women and men after 2015. the right to equal treatment is a fundamental right recognised by the eu treaties, emblematic and deeply rooted in european society, essential for the further development of european society, and should apply in legislation, practice and case law as well as in real life. i therefore voted in favour of this report. the eu has historically made important strides towards women's empowerment and gender equality, but in recent decades there has been a slowdown in policy action and reform across the union in relation to gender equality. i therefore believe that the next strategy will have to give new impetus and take concrete action to strengthen women's rights and promote gender equality. i am voting in favour of the noichl report because it calls for access to information, prevention, safe, effective and accessible contraception, safe and legal termination of pregnancy and sterilisation, and assistance for adoption.
in writing. ‒ the report comes at a crucial time, twenty years after the adoption of the beijing platform for action and the revision of the millennium development goals, to assess progress on gender equality worldwide. unfortunately, everything suggests that the results will not be fully satisfactory and that progress is still too slow. european policy must no longer be limited to setting itself objectives which, however ambitious, remain ambitious. it must instead produce and develop effective, coherent and realistic strategies to eliminate all forms of discrimination against women and men in their diversity. the data is still disappointing. one in three women in the eu has experienced psychological or sexual violence at least once in her life after the age of 15. 74.2% of men are currently employed, compared with 62.5% of women. and the same is true of other forms of discrimination. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is time for a bold step forward, to put the union at the forefront of the battle to abolish all forms of discrimination.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because it calls on the commission to develop a new specific strategy for women's rights and gender equality in europe, aimed at creating equal opportunities, with a view to ending all forms of discrimination against women in the labour market. the new strategy should strengthen the rights of different groups of women, including women with disabilities, migrant and ethnic minority women, roma women, older women, single mothers and lgbt women. it must raise awareness in society of the problem of violence against women, as well as of prevention, access to justice and support for victims. the resolution also calls on the commission to recognise the importance of sexual and reproductive rights, to work towards the implementation of sex education programmes in schools and to provide counselling and contraceptive facilities for young people. it calls for accessible services in the areas of sexual and reproductive health, abortion and safe and legal contraception. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment-related aspects of the environment.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament has once again had to vote on a report containing a number of positive elements with a view to achieving equality between men and women, but irreparably tainted by the inclusion of insidious and unacceptable provisions. in this report too, the european parliament shows that it has forgotten the value and the meaning of the family. in a europe which wants to be the standard-bearer of universal rights, the only rights forgotten are those of children. i was therefore forced to vote against this report, not only on the substance, in that we strongly support the right of a child to grow up in a family with a father and a mother, but also on the technical side, in that family law falls within the competence of the individual member states and not of the european parliament.
in writing. the path towards gender equality is a priority that europe cannot afford to underestimate: the road to full equality and equal rights and opportunities for women and men is still too slow and i expect a breakthrough from this european legislature. combating social discrimination, fighting hard against abuse and violence, closing the gender pay and opportunity gaps, and encouraging new and more inclusive labour policies are just some of the immediate actions europe needs to focus on to deliver a higher level of protection and rights. there can be no equality unless we decide to invest in education to respect and recognize the equal dignity of all the resources that our society has, regardless of gender, religion, culture, sexual choices of the individual. to capitalize on human value and to give back freedom, consideration and respect to those who today still do not always have it: i am convinced that this objective can be the starting point for achieving europe's main growth objectives.
in writing. ‒ it is a fact that equality between men and women in all areas of life is progressing only slowly. in adopting this report, we called on the commission to develop and adopt a new specific strategy for women's rights and gender equality in europe, which aims to create equal opportunities, with a view to ending all forms of discrimination against women in the labour market and all forms of violence against them. i strongly support and believe in the importance of fighting violence against women and girls. i call on the european union to consider joining the istanbul convention. in today's vote we called on all member states to sign and ratify the convention and through the new strategy to take active action to end violence and injustice against women.

in writing. ‒ although i have always been a strong supporter of women's rights, in view of the prospect of a wider integration of women into the economic and social life of the community, i have decided not to support the report signed by mrs noichl. in my view, the text of the document is not fully consistent with the purpose it should have pursued, which is to provide the european commission with guidelines for the definition of a concrete and far-reaching strategy for gender equality for the coming years. while i agree with the references to the need to strengthen the european union's efforts on equal pay for men and women, to combat gender-based violence, to the need to improve the degree of women's participation in decision-making, i believe that the paragraphs in the text which deal with matters which, as laid down in the treaties, fall within the competence of the member states have undermined the reliability of this report. the rapporteur's lack of willingness to engage in dialogue during the drafting of the document has, in my view, contributed to undermining its quality.
in writing. ‒ this report sets important objectives for the eu and the member states. the risk of backsliding on women's rights is always lurking: in times of crisis, such as the economic crisis of recent years, it is the weaker parties who suffer the most, and unfortunately this has been the case for women in many areas, first and foremost in the field of employment. the only way to keep up is to keep walking, and to keep walking. this is our role and, more generally, the role of the institutions: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. there are many things to do: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work is a welcome step towards the creation of a european network of national authorities responsible for the protection of workers from carcinogens at work. these are actions that not only help women, but that serve all of us to create a better environment, not just a more equitable one, but a more prosperous one, a richer one. and it is precisely where some hesitate or lag that the eu must lead, continuing to raise the bar of rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the noichl report because i found many controversial aspects in it. first of all, when you read the title, you expect to be confronted with a certain type of subject which has been my personal political battle for several years, namely the promotion of equality between women and men. none of that. once again, questions have been inserted which have little or nothing to do with this subject. this is yet another move to tackle matters which fall within the strict competence of the member states, and on which the union can only intervene when its action is considered more effective than that undertaken at national, regional or local level. for this reason, and since this is not the case, i think it is appropriate that the principle of subsidiarity be respected.
in writing. ‒ gender equality cannot be reduced to the mere recognition of equal rights, but must above all translate into the vigorous application of good practices that reduce the discrimination suffered by women in everyday life. these disparities are most evident in the workplace, where women continue to earn less than their colleagues. i therefore join parliament's call for a new directive to reduce the pay gap and encourage women's participation in decision-making, including through the introduction of leave measures for both parents. i share the ambitious proposals in the report on equality between men and women and therefore voted in favour. europe can become a voice for gender issues with a new strategy that includes provisions for the prevention and condemnation of all forms of violence against women and the promotion of educational programmes aimed at combating the stereotyped image of women.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the european union strategy for equality between women and men because i believe that better defined policy guidance is needed for policy-making on this issue for the period 2015-2020. clear objectives, concrete actions and more effective monitoring are needed to make progress in the fight against discrimination in the labour market, education and decision-making. the data show that the eu is still a long way from achieving equality: 33% of women have suffered physical and/or psychological violence, while the average wage gap in europe is 16% and the pension gap is 39%. in this resolution, parliament therefore stresses the need for specific action to strengthen the rights of disabled women, migrants, women from ethnic minorities, roma women, elderly women and single mothers. particular attention is then paid to the need to ensure a balance between family and work life, stressing the importance of flexible forms of work which can enable women and men to combine work and family life according to their needs.
in writing. ‒ the road to achieving effective gender equality is still long and requires a 360-degree approach. i voted in favour of the report, which offers wide-ranging suggestions relating to - but not exclusively - work, social and political life. in particular, this report is based on the idea that women must have control over their sexual and reproductive rights through easy access to contraception and voluntary termination of pregnancy. gender quotas can also play a role in the exercise of effective gender equality: in particular, in the boardroom, in the world of entrepreneurship and research, they can be a necessary stimulus to overcome the current disparities in pay, access and career opportunities. i voted against the amendment proposed by the ppe, which proposed a deliberately reduced and reductive approach and which, among other things, completely omits the issues of quotas, sexual and reproductive rights, contraception and abortion. the 'philosophy' implied in this amendment shows that, although it is difficult to find anyone who is openly opposed to gender equality, there are still those who are putting obstacles in the way of achieving effective equality.

in writing. ‒ the vote on the report on the 'strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries' was negative for several reasons. firstly, this report contains several very different aspects which, in my view, should be dealt with separately because they present different problems: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. secondly, i think that the approach adopted and followed towards developing third countries is wrong. the latter are required to put in place strict forms of protection of intellectual property, whereas these countries would need looser forms of protection, as several studies have shown, in order to allow knowledge and know-how to circulate more easily and freely. this would be a real step towards their emancipation and development. on the contrary, it has a neo-colonial attitude, based exclusively on a commercial logic of opening up new markets, which seems to favour only european countries. my vote therefore had to be negative.

in writing. ‒ some 26% (56 million people) of total employment in the european union and 39% of total economic activity (eur 4.7 trillion) are generated by high-gdp sectors. this shows the need to protect them and to pursue a coherent approach in the different areas of union action, both in relation to the internal market and exports to non-eu countries, and the importance of involving all stakeholders in the sector, including smes. to do this effectively, we need to differentiate protection strategies by geographical area and distinguish between physical and digital product protection policies in order to optimise the provisions needed for each sector. the protection of intellectual property requires that the amount and destination of ipr funding, in particular with regard to the eu ipr helpdesk, be clearly and precisely established; we also hope that the regrettable lack of a single eu patent will be addressed as soon as possible. it is also important to use this opportunity for debate to encourage research and innovation, in particular to overcome the problem of access to medicines and the challenge of hydrogeological disruption and global climate change, thus giving us an advantage in solving the major problems of our near future.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. the report sets out parliament's position on the european commission's communication on intellectual property, which sets out a strategy to ensure better protection of intellectual property rights in third countries. the report has the merit of underlining that the commercial nature of many ipr infringements and the increasing involvement of organised crime in this type of infringement have become a problem of primary importance. it also pointed out that the un convention against transnational organized crime does not currently have a protocol on the fight against counterfeiting. i therefore hope that, along the same lines as the report, the commission and the member states will intensify their efforts in this direction.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution which - while positively intended to remedy the lack of major agreements on the commercial aspects of intellectual property rights in international agreements - has some weaknesses. these concern in particular the definition of standards that would apply to third countries, the control of intermediaries' liability and the management of piracy in the foreign branches of european companies. the resolution also calls for the commission to provide more support to the large european pharmaceutical companies selling generic medicines in third countries, without any clear policy to promote access to these products at cost-of-living prices in these countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries. the eu's competitiveness is based on creativity and innovation, which is supported by intellectual property rights (ipr). the high-ipr sectors account for 39% of economic activity (worth some eur 4.7 trillion) and 26% of employment in the eu (about 56 million jobs). the commission has also received comments from the united kingdom and the united states on the alleged infringements of intellectual property rights. it should also be noted that the eu, as a member of the wto, is bound by the constraints and standards of the trips agreement and that ipr compliance is an integral part of the eu-us ttip agreement, currently under negotiation. the strategy therefore aims to combat ipr infringements, to inform and raise awareness among consumers and to promote and protect them at international level (e.g. wto). the commission also proposes to establish a european observatory on infringements of intellectual property rights.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that european companies must be guaranteed the safeguarding of their economic interests when they carry out their activities abroad, particularly in developing countries. this protection must be ensured at european level for two reasons: on the one hand, the union's economic strength is based on the creativity and innovation of its enterprises. on the other hand, infringement procedures are too time-consuming and costly for individual firms, especially small and medium-sized ones, to support. the introduction of such measures would not only protect economic interests but also the health and safety of consumers and the environment. counterfeiting is no longer limited to luxury goods, but also affects everyday goods: toys, medicines, cosmetics and food products, which can be seriously harmful to health and the environment. in 2013 alone, 36 million items were seized with a value of over €760 million, and 10% of these items were medicines. the problem is therefore serious and a specific strategy is needed to tackle it.
in writing. ‒ developing smart growth by stimulating an economy based on research and innovation is one of the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy. it is therefore necessary to strengthen cooperation between schools, universities, businesses, research centres and ipr holders, also in order to prevent counterfeiting, which no longer affects luxury goods only, but also everyday goods such as toys, medicines, cosmetics and foodstuffs. in order to reduce the risk of infringements and to avoid negative consequences for consumer health and the economy, it is important to establish a comprehensive legal framework that is also in line with the interests of third countries, accompanied by policies to combat organised crime, money laundering and tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ the report is moving in the right direction by identifying the main instruments to improve and strengthen the instruments to ensure greater protection of intellectual property rights in third countries. over the last decade we have seen significant changes in intellectual property rights: the substantial changes in the technology sector, including the pivotal role of the internet, the growing importance of emerging economies, and the challenges in key sectors such as pharmaceuticals, require a serious rethinking and a comprehensive rewrite of the approach to the discipline. in this respect, the commission's effort to standardise the approach both within the eu and towards third countries is commendable. as far as parliament is concerned, i think it is very important to stress that while protecting the interests and competitiveness of eu pharmaceutical companies and their capacity to innovate, we must make medicines accessible to people in the country where they are marketed, by adjusting their prices to their living standards. i firmly believe that while respecting labour and protecting intellectual property, the right to be able to take care of oneself remains an absolutely paramount and priority value.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the strategy for the protection and strengthening of intellectual property rights in third countries. i believe that, as the report emphasizes, a common and coherent european union strategy is needed to ensure that protection is greater and more effective both inside and outside the union. we must renew our commitment to ending the current fragmentation of the common market and to promote and promote our products in third countries as well, and finally give the eu a clear position in trade treaties and multilateral fora. the commission's green paper, which proposes to extend the protection of geographical indications to non-agricultural products in the union, is also moving in this direction. our aim must be to protect europe's creative industries and traditional know-how adequately, combating counterfeiting and boosting their competitiveness, while seeking a balance between the legitimate interests of intellectual property owners and end users. we must therefore adopt a flexible approach which takes account of the needs of individual countries for certain specific products, such as pharmaceuticals, for which access must be guaranteed to all.
in writing. ‒ the report on the strategy for the protection and enforcement of intellectual property rights in third countries is part of a very important debate which has repercussions both on the european and national scene. this is a crucial issue because of its implications for industrial policy, particularly in the field of innovation. in fact, a debate is emerging more and more clearly on how to boost growth and investment in europe. it is essential to include in this debate clear guidelines for these investments: innovation is certainly a key element for an increasingly specialised european labour market with many excellencies. a europe that invests in innovation is also a europe that is more competitive than other major international competitors. however, without adequate protection of intellectual property, it will be impossible to achieve the smart growth that underpins the eu's investment programmes and the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy. it is also a problem of particular importance to smes, the driving force behind the european economic fabric. for this reason, i believe that this debate is fundamental to the construction of a virtuous path towards solid growth in europe, with innovation and knowledge as its main drivers.
in writing. ‒ technological developments have dramatically transformed the way in which intellectual property rights are enforced. despite this, few agreements have been concluded since the entry into force of the international agreement on trade-related aspects of intellectual property rights in 1994. the draft report therefore seeks to fill in some gaps, such as the inclusion of international agreements on intellectual property rights at the level of the world trade organisation. i agree with the rapporteur's proposals, which largely reflect the commission's guidelines, but i voted against them. there are elements which are not in line with the m5s's positions, such as the exclusive responsibility of national authorities for the respect of intellectual property rights and strong support for pharmaceutical companies by the commission, which export medicines to third countries.
