the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the text we are voting on tomorrow forms the basis for the conclusion of the doha amendment by the european union and sets out the conditions for the joint fulfilment of the commitments by the european union, its member states and iceland, a point which will be discussed in detail by my colleague, mr giovanni la via. the text, as you know, sets out the obligations of the second kyoto commitment, the so-called doha amendment, from 2013 to 2020 and, above all, requires member states to take the necessary measures to complete the national ratification processes by the third quarter of 2015. although the draft council decision on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol and the joint fulfilment of the commitments is certainly a positive step, it must nevertheless be stressed that it is mainly the countries of the european union that are participating in the second commitment period, while some of the most polluting countries are unfortunately not taking part in it. in this context, i believe that the union should use all the political, diplomatic and economic instruments at its disposal to reach an international agreement in paris at the end of the year, as comprehensive as possible, also in order to break this long tradition of the european union, which very often takes on all its climate commitments alone. in this sense, the g7 meeting last week marked, albeit with lights and shadows, some important steps towards this goal. in particular, i would like to mention the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by 40 to 70% by 2050 compared to 2010 levels and the commitment to limit the global temperature increase to 2 degrees celsius, which seem to be important points, and there are others that are important. the g7 meeting also showed the will, especially at the german level, to phase out the use of fossil fuels such as oil, gas and coal during this century. chancellor merkel called it the decarbonization of the global economy. i am not sure that the commissioner has been able to give us a clear answer to this question. we know that several european countries have increased their use of fossil fuels with a high environmental impact, including lignite in particular, in a counter-tendency. so if this is the scenario in the european union, with lights and shadows, we find on the other side of the ocean obama who seems to give signals that also go in the direction of an effective counter to global warming, at least in the intentions because as we know, the policy of obama in the words of even the last weeks of some distinguished political commentators, the policy of obama in fact, seems to have the weak point precisely on the environment and so i believe that, as concluded the g7 communiqué, the challenge can only be overcome with a global response. so even if the g7 countries were to eliminate all carbon dioxide emissions tomorrow, the problem of climate change would not be solved. the emerging countries must also make their contribution: the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area. in this context, the kyoto ii protocol, which requires the parties to communicate - i do not have time to mention everything now - is an important step in the right direction and i really hope that the paris summit can finally be the day when we can welcome a binding global agreement to which we will all contribute with europe, dear commissioner, always strongly at the forefront of this process as a global leader.
the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner cañete, ladies and gentlemen, the report we are about to discuss concerns the signing by the european union of an agreement between the union and its member states, on the one hand, and iceland, on the other, on iceland's participation in the joint fulfilment of the commitments of the european union and its member states for the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change. i will not repeat what i said to mrs gardini, re-creating the history of the kyoto protocol and commitments, but i would remind you that at the 20th conference of the parties in december 2014 in lima, the call made encouraged all 192 parties and the kyoto protocol to ratify the amendment. as of 14 may 2015, this amendment had been ratified by 31 countries. but before it can enter into force, it needs to be ratified by 144 other parties. in particular, i would point out that iceland is already a party to annex 1 of the kyoto protocol and has achieved its individual target for the first commitment period, during which it was to limit the increase in emissions to less than 10% on average. finally, during this period, iceland's emissions decreased on average. in 2009, iceland expressed its intention to fulfil its commitments in a second commitment period jointly with the european union and its member states. iceland also participates in the european union emissions trading system (ets) and the eu regulation on the mmr monitoring mechanism for greenhouse gases. so it has fully embarked on this path, as the other 28 member states of the european union are doing. iceland is therefore interested in joint fulfilment with the european union and its member states, irrespective of whether it is a member of the union or not. in conclusion, i believe that this agreement will be a strong signal, highlighting the coordinated european efforts to combat climate change at international level, especially in view of the forthcoming cop 21 in paris. the european union, as mentioned above, is a world leader in the fight against climate change and has always supported an ambitious climate policy. we are leading internationally and we are leading politically in the fight against climate change, and we need to do that with greater commitment and even more commitment in the run-up to paris, by stepping up efforts for an agreement that is ambitious, comprehensive and legally binding. in this overall framework of commitments, iceland has so far done its part, it is continuing along the path together with the other 28 states of the european union and for this reason i think it is appropriate, in this context, to invite all colleagues to support this ratification, which supports our european action on climate change and can also contribute with iceland's small contribution to the current international debate on reducing emissions at global level. i therefore call on all members to support the ratification of this agreement, which marks a further small step towards even more ambitious agreements which we hope to reach at the end of the year in paris.
on behalf of the efdd group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the ratification of the doha amendment and the agreement between the european union and iceland to continue together the kyoto protocol meet with general agreement and are almost a formality which we will carry out with tomorrow's vote, without taking anything away from the two rapporteurs who have done a very good job. there is no doubt that all the attention now is obviously on paris and the conference of the parties next december. there is a strong and justified expectation, a unanimous feeling: we must not forget that the european union is a major player in the world economy. a long way has been traveled since kyoto. but we are very, very far from the goal. the strategies have changed and the words have changed, and they no longer speak of future scenarios, but of current phenomena: it's not just emissions reduction anymore, but also mitigation, adaptation, resilience, transformation. the declarations by the g7 to keep the global temperature rise to within 2 degrees are important but not enough. it is clear that a breakthrough is needed in the negotiations and agreements. we need a strong and binding commitment from all the states and we need it now because we have no more time.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we also agree, of course, on the timeliness and importance of ratifying the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol in order to partially remedy the failure of the copenhagen summit in 2009. it is important that the 20% reduction targets by 2020 be maintained and that the eu's effort in this direction can be shared with other contracting parties to the protocol which would adopt the amendment under discussion. however, there is a strong doubt that this process, although necessary, will prove futile for two reasons: the first concerns the risk that the amendment will not enter into force in good time, since it has so far been ratified by 32 contracting parties, a figure which, although this vote will bring it up to 61, is still far from the 144 ratifications needed for its entry into force. the second risk is that the protocol will end up being adopted only by those contracting parties, such as the european union and its member states, for which the 20% reduction target for 2020 does not entail any immediate additional effort. so the risks are real and they demonstrate the importance of a serious, binding, ambitious and global agreement in paris.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the news that came yesterday at the end of the g7 summit about the commitment of the heads of state and government to limit the increase in global temperature to two degrees above pre-industrial levels gives particular importance to our debate this afternoon. the ratification of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol, which does not present any political problem in its substance, allows us to return to the paris conference with the united nations on climate change. we need the agreement to be reached by the end of the year to prevent the world temperature from rising by more than 2 degrees celsius above pre-industrial levels to be global and binding, and the commitment of the g7 gives us reason to hope that this will happen. however, this objective can only be achieved if the so-called emerging and developing countries also accept a binding global pathway to reduce missions. we therefore welcomed with cautious optimism the bilateral, non-binding agreement signed by the united states and china a few months ago. today, another element on the path to positive involvement of emerging and developing countries is the g7's reaffirmation of the commitment made in copenhagen in 2009 to establish a $100 billion global climate fund. the conditions are there, mr president, mr commissioner, for paris to turn from words to deeds.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, many of our colleagues have already said that the adoption of this amendment to the kyoto protocol in the run-up to the paris cop is a good sign of commitment to combating climate change, but the decision taken yesterday by the g7 allows us to approach our discussion with cautious optimism. yesterday there was a clear recognition, as has already been said, of the binding objective of limiting global temperature and the confirmation of the funding for initiatives in the poorest countries, but that is not enough. i want to take this opportunity not only to highlight the importance of reaching a binding global agreement in paris, which is fundamental to the sustainability of our planet, a subject on which we are all already convinced, but also to reiterate how even more important it is to act now to involve the most polluting emerging economies in joining this agreement. that is why, mr commissioner, the diplomatic action we are going to be able to take in the coming months is central, also, let me say, to dispel the doubts of those who, by calling for greater pragmatism, ultimately want to maintain the status quo. but without an agreement with all the major international players, we could perhaps be first in class, like europe, but i agree with those who say that our efforts will be worthless and will even risk becoming another element of distortion of the global market, which i believe is no longer needed.

member of the commission. madam president, i would like to thank the rapporteurs and the alternate rapporteurs who have spoken on this matter. and as i said in my first speech, parliament's decision international agreement on climate change under the auspices of the united nations and that we are keeping our commitments, which is especially significant this year, ahead of cop 21 in paris. many of the honourable members have referred to the g7 agreements in this debate, and let me make a point. the commission welcomes the g7's fundamental commitments to take the necessary measures to ensure that global warming does not exceed 2 °c above pre-industrial levels. but more specifically, the g7 statement also includes a medium-term reduction target at the top of the intergovernmental panel on climate change recommendation of between 40 and 70%, and a long-term target of 100 per cent emission reduction by 2100. as you all know, the 2050 target is a target which the european union wants to see incorporated into the paris agreement, because this medium-term target will allow us to assess whether our collective efforts are sufficient to avoid a 2°c increase in global temperature and to periodically review the level of our ambitions. this decision, which is contained in the final joint communiqué, is therefore an important step towards the paris climate summit in december. furthermore, it is positive that all g-7 countries except japan have already submitted their national adaptation and mitigation commitments, the so-called indc, although japan announced yesterday that they are in the final phase of internal consultations, so we expect their indc to be approved in the coming weeks. the countries that ratified kyoto at the time, the 28 of the european union plus austria, norway, switzerland, iceland, liechtenstein and new zealand, accounted for 14% of emissions. at present, 37 countries have submitted adaptation and mitigation commitments, representing 30% of global emissions, which suggests that we are on track to have all parties to the convention able to submit mitigation commitments and that these cover 100% of emissions. it is true that at the moment only the 28 countries of the european union plus switzerland, mexico, russia, liechtenstein, andorra, canada, morocco, norway and the united states have ratified it, but we are already at a 30% emissions level. the g7 also reiterated the binding nature of the agreement and expressed its determination to provide financial support for the green climate fund and other mechanisms to help the most vulnerable countries. if we add to this the fact that it was agreed that a world economy free of fossil fuels and the production of clean energy by 2050 would be possible during this century, the overall assessment of the g7 agreements is frankly positive and puts the european union in a very positive negotiating position, especially if, when we arrive in paris, we have already presented - or will present very soon - our new ets system, the european system of emission allowances. some people want us to introduce it immediately, we are working on it at the moment, but in any case the european union will arrive in paris with a new system of emission allowances in which we have to deal with all the issues that affect this regime and in which we cannot improvise by making singular modifications, but we have to set up a system that is positive, that has a functioning carbon market and that, in turn, prevents the so-called carbon leakage or relocation problems of our industries, which has also worried many of your honourable members. in short, we think that paving the way for the ratification of the kyoto process is very positive, especially as a signal to negotiate this ambitious, binding agreement at cop 21 in paris, on which we are currently still working. we have worked to get the g-7, all countries, to submit their indcs; we are now working to get all the g-20 countries to submit them as soon as possible, and it is hoped that, by the time we get to paris, a large number of countries will have submitted mitigation and adaptation commitments that make up a much more ambitious scheme than in the past.

oral explanations of vote
written declarations of vote
in writing. ‒ the kyoto ii package incorporates a reduction in co2 emissions that the eu has already set for itself and achieved following the introduction of the 2009 climate-energy package. the ratification of kyoto ii until 2020 is nothing more than a symbolic accession to a protocol from which the major co2 producing countries have already withdrawn precisely because of its ineffectiveness, and for these reasons i did not intend to support the report with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i strongly supported the adoption of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol, which is an important signal from the eu in the fight against climate change. this comes less than 7 months after the start of cop 21 in paris and just days after g7 members committed to take action to limit global temperature rise to 2 degrees by 2050. the extension of the kyoto targets to 2020, as well as the global commitment to reduce co2 emissions by 40-70% by 2050 compared to 2010, appear to be achievable targets and are the key preconditions for the establishment of a binding post-2020 climate agreement. however, the importance of a strong diplomatic effort to involve as many partners as possible, and in particular to commit emerging countries to binding emission reduction targets, should not be underestimated.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the eu's commitment under the kyoto protocol to significantly reduce its co2 emissions is one of the cornerstones of the union's action and that it is therefore necessary to continue along this path.
in writing. ‒ reducing emissions is essential to safeguarding the future of our planet and to counteracting the damage caused by climate change (tropical climate, extreme marine weather, alternating droughts and floods). the union and the member states have committed themselves to achieving the objectives of the kyoto protocol: today we must ratify the doha amendment, which sets the stage for our efforts, and the regulation which will allow us to technically meet the second-period targets of a 21% reduction in emissions by 2020 compared with 2005 levels. the regulation provides the necessary basis for the technical legislative acts for the implementation by the eu and the member states of the second commitment period. it is undeniable that the decision to ratify the doha amendment and the fulfilment of the commitments by the union will be of great importance: this is a strong signal in the fight against global climate change, which attests to the union's leadership in this area. the political, economic and environmental importance of the kyoto protocol means that ratification by the member states should be completed by the third quarter of this year, so that they can take a definite, unified and consolidated position at the unfccc conference in paris.
in writing. - i voted against the measure. kyoto ii incorporates the -20% co2 that the eu set for itself with the 2009 climate and energy package. it barely covers 15% of global co2 emissions.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the recommendation on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change and the joint fulfilment of the commitments thereunder. the 1992 united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc) sought to limit the rise in global temperature, but it was clear as early as 1995 that the agreement would not be enough. countries around the world have therefore started negotiations to improve the global response to climate change and in 1997 adopted the kyoto protocol, which sets an internationally binding emission reduction target. the eu and its member states have therefore committed to delivering on their commitment to reduce their overall greenhouse gas emissions in the first period (2008-2012) by 8% compared to 1990 levels. the doha amendment establishes a second commitment period of the kyoto protocol (kp cp2), which begins on 1 january 2013 and ends on 31 december 2020, and provides for legally binding emission reduction commitments under which the european union. i am therefore glad that the european parliament voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change, signed in 1997, establishes an internationally binding emission reduction target. the eu ratified the same protocol in 2002. the so-called 'doha amendment' establishes a second commitment period of the kyoto protocol ending on 31 december 2020. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the recommendation voted on today on the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol is an important signal from the european parliament to the governments of the member states and also to the countries adhering to the kyoto protocol. it is a sign of the eu's renewed commitment to combating climate change. the amendments introduced include the possibility for countries which consider it appropriate to go beyond the emission targets set. the formal ratification of the doha amendment is necessary as it makes a crucial contribution to the pursuit of ambitious global efforts to keep the global temperature rise below 2°c. the european union has been waging an intense battle against climate change in recent years, with its policies and legislation, but a global commitment is needed and the countries involved, many of which are still reluctant to take on the burden of reducing emissions. the adoption of the amendment is an important step ahead of the international climate conference scheduled for paris at the end of the year, where it will be essential to reach a global agreement. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure on the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol. the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc), which was signed in 1997, sets an internationally binding emission reduction target. the european union and its member states committed themselves to reducing their overall greenhouse gas emissions in the first period (2008-2012) by 8% compared to 1990 levels. a 20% target was proposed in the council conclusions of 9 march 2012 for the second commitment period (2013-2020) of the kyoto protocol, and was subsequently accepted by the eu member states at the doha climate change conference in december 2012, which was attended by 192 states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the conclusion of the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol because i am convinced of the importance of reducing the impact of pollution on the atmosphere and i am also convinced that the individual member state would not be able to set itself and achieve such an ambitious target. this amendment provides for a reduction of the average annual greenhouse gas emissions by the member states and iceland for the period 2013-2020 of 80% compared to the baseline year, which is normally 1990. i hope that in the not too distant future we will be able to persuade the countries which have the greatest impact on the world's air pollution to join us, whereas now the whole or almost the whole burden of climate policy rests on europe's shoulders. however, it is only through common climate and environmental policies that the objective of keeping the global temperature rise below 2 degrees will be achieved. i congratulate the rapporteur.
in writing. ‒ the doha amendment to the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change and the joint fulfilment of its commitments establishes the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol. the amendments to the text of the protocol made by the doha amendment include the inclusion of a new gas (nitrogen trifluoride), the simplification of the procedure to allow a party to adjust its commitment by increasing the level of ambition during the commitment period, and a provision to prevent a party's emissions for the period from 2013 to 2020 from exceeding its average emissions in the period from 2008 to 2010. the amendment does not change the environmental objectives and obligations of the member states as enshrined in the 2009 climate and energy package legislation, but it will send a strong signal about the eu's leadership in this area. i therefore voted in favour of this report in the light of these facts.
in writing. ‒ in december 2012, at the doha climate change conference, the 192 parties to the kyoto protocol to the un framework convention on climate change adopted an amendment to the kyoto protocol, which is intended to make the kyoto protocol more binding. this doha amendment establishes a second commitment period of the kyoto protocol, starting from 10 january 2013 and ending on 31 december 2020, with legally binding emission reduction commitments. under the doha amendment, the eu, its member states and iceland commit to limiting their greenhouse gas (ghg) emissions in the years 2013-2020 to 80% of their baseline year emissions. for these reasons, i vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ the kyoto ii package incorporates a reduction in co2 emissions that the eu has already set for itself and achieved following the introduction of the 2009 climate-energy package. the ratification of kyoto ii until 2020 is nothing more than a symbolic accession to a protocol from which the major co2 producing countries have already withdrawn precisely because of its ineffectiveness, and for these reasons i did not intend to support the report with my vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the eu-iceland agreement on iceland's participation in the second commitment period under the kyoto protocol is a demonstration of the importance of the union's role in the fight against global warming at international level.
in writing. ‒ the participation of iceland, a virtuous country which has significantly reduced its emissions over the past five years and which is a positive model for most of the technologically advanced states, in the agreement which marks the start of the second phase of the kyoto protocol is certainly to be welcomed and supported politically. the participation of the republic of iceland in the joint achievement of the objectives set out in the doha amendment should encourage us to be ambitious and not to be satisfied with the results achieved: there is still a long way to go to build a technologically advanced and environmentally sustainable civilization. we need to create a legal framework that is binding on all countries, pushing them to achieve their goals in a clear and fair way, adapted to the economic and environmental conditions of their territory. we can do this together, by sharing best practices and devising new development models. the fight against climate change is not a fight between countries or between peoples: it is a struggle of human civilization against the polluting factors that threaten its prosperity and development. it is a fight we can only win if we work together, united for the good of that great common home that is our planet.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement which will allow iceland to participate in the second commitment period under the kyoto protocol established by the doha amendment. this means that the countries that make up the european union and iceland will jointly meet their emission commitments. i am in favour of iceland's participation because it has already demonstrated by its participation in annex i of the kyoto protocol that it is able to meet and deliver on its commitments, reducing its emissions by an average of 2%. the fact that iceland is not part of the european union further underlines the coordinated european efforts in the fight against climate change at the international level. the conclusion of this agreement with iceland will not affect the content of the accession negotiations between the two countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu-iceland agreement on iceland's participation in the second commitment period under the kyoto protocol. iceland is a party to annex i to the kyoto protocol and in 2009 expressed its intention to fulfil its commitments in a second period of implementation of that protocol. i believe that the eu-iceland report on environmental policy represents a further opportunity to renew our joint commitment to tackling climate change at international level.
in writing. ‒ this agreement will allow iceland to participate in the joint implementation of the kyoto protocol on the same basis as the member states. as parties to the kyoto protocol, the union and the member states are subject to a number of monitoring, reporting and verification obligations under the kyoto protocol. for those contracting parties which have agreed to fulfil their commitments jointly, some of this information must be submitted jointly. the commission will request information from iceland that will enable the union to fulfil its reporting obligations. in addition, iceland will have to participate in the system of registries of the union and its member states that are relevant for the fulfilment of the obligations under the kyoto protocol. this requires iceland to apply union legislation not applicable to third countries, in particular as regards the monitoring, reporting and verification of emissions, as well as the operation of the registry and the accounting of transactions related to the implementation of the commitments of the union, its member states and iceland under the second commitment period of the kyoto protocol in line with the joint fulfilment deadlines and internationally agreed standards. for the reasons i have given, i voted in favour.
in writing. i am in favour of the conclusion of the agreement in question, signed by the union and iceland on 1 april 2015, as in 2012 the 192 parties to the kyoto protocol to the united nations framework convention on climate change adopted an amendment to the protocol (the doha amendment). that amendment established a second commitment period, from 1 january 2013 to 31 december 2020, with a binding emission reduction target for the parties (including the european union, the member states and iceland). the 144 ratifications required for its entry into force are now only 32. this shows how far we are from the finish line. in any event, the eu and its member states have chosen to fulfil the commitments under the kyoto protocol jointly. the commission notes that the icelandic authorities have not provided any evidence that the icelandic authorities have not fulfilled their obligations under the agreement. once the joint commitment is fulfilled, those parties are considered to have met their emission obligations under the kyoto protocol. if not, each party becomes responsible for its individual emission level.

in writing. ‒ almost two years after croatia's accession to the eu, it is important to ensure that the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states and the protocol of 16 october 2001 thereto are fully operational for croatia. those instruments are designed to facilitate assistance between judicial, police and customs authorities through a series of mechanisms, such as the temporary transfer or transit of detained persons, the transmission of notifications, the direct exchange of information between the authorities concerned, the making available of stolen goods for return to the owner, and the hearing of witnesses or experts, including by videoconference. the convention also deals with measures of major importance in the fight against crime, particularly organised crime, such as the setting up of joint investigation teams, the use of infiltration operations and the interception of telecommunications. the recommendation, which is adopted by this legislative resolution, is a necessary measure to resolve certain technical issues related to croatia's accession to the abovementioned convention and protocol, and therefore, on the basis of the foregoing considerations, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure under consideration concerning the accession of croatia to the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters. the text is technical in nature and aims to make the necessary adjustments following the accession of the republic of croatia to the convention and the protocol in accordance with article 3 (4) and (5) of the act of accession of croatia to the european union as the 28th member state on 1 july 2013.
in writing. ‒ croatia's accession to the european union implies its automatic accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states. however, the council shall adopt a decision fixing the date on which those conventions enter into force for croatia. the publication of this convention will remove any doubt as to its entry into force on the twentieth day following the date of its publication. in the absence of controversial political issues, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ on the basis of article 3 (4) and (5) of the act of accession, the commission recommends that the necessary adaptations be made for the participation of croatia in the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union and its protocol of 16 october 2001. i welcome the commission's recommendation and hope that further progress can be made, for example in the reform of the judiciary and public administration, the fight against corruption and organised crime, and the protection of minorities.
in writing. ‒ the 2012 act on the conditions of accession of croatia to the eu has simplified its accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states under article 34 of the eu treaty. it is no longer necessary to negotiate and conclude specific accession protocols, article 3 (4) and (5) of the act of accession simply states that croatia accedes to the conventions and protocols by virtue of the act of accession. the act of accession provides for the council to adopt a decision fixing the date on which those conventions enter into force for croatia and to make any necessary adjustments to the conventions by reason of the accession of the new member state. annex i to the act of accession lists the six protocols and conventions concerned in the field of justice and home affairs. the list includes the council convention of 29 may 2000 pursuant to article 34 of the treaty on european union on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the eu and its protocol of 16 october 2011. i voted in favour of the report because the aim of the recommendation is to make the necessary adjustments as a result of croatia's accession to the convention and the protocol referred to, in accordance with the act of accession.
in writing. ‒ it is essential to facilitate and improve assistance between judicial authorities in criminal matters also vis-à-vis croatia. i can only vote in favour of any action which will make available as soon as possible all the instruments provided for in european law for the exchange of information and cooperation between european states in this field. we must insist on this direction in order to prosecute crimes and offences more effectively and more quickly, while respecting the fundamental principles of the different legal systems of the member states and respecting individual rights. the fight against crime, in particular organised crime, money laundering and financial crime, cannot be confined to the narrow confines of national borders but must go beyond them. all my actions in this struggle will always be informed by the need to ensure that it acquires a greater european and cross-border character.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the convention which croatia will now join in order to facilitate assistance between judicial, police and customs authorities in criminal matters.
in writing. i voted in favour of mrs sippel's proposal on croatia's accession to the convention on legal assistance in criminal matters. the objective of this recommendation is to make the necessary adjustments as a result of the accession of croatia to the convention and the protocol referred to in article 3 (4) and (5) of the act of accession.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of croatia's accession to the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union. the specific objective of the convention, the final text of which was adopted on 29 may 2000, is to complement, and not replace, existing conventional instruments in other legal areas, with a view to improving judicial cooperation in criminal matters through rapid, effective assistance compatible with the fundamental principles of the internal law of the member states and with the principles of the european convention on human rights of 1950.
in writing. ‒ the 2012 act concerning the conditions of accession of the republic of croatia to the european union simplified the procedures for the accession of the new member state to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states pursuant to article 34 of the treaty on european union. i voted in favour of the sippel report because i think it would be desirable to facilitate relations with croatia, including in the area of legal aid for criminal offences.
in writing. ‒ the objective of the recommendation adopted here today is simply to make the necessary adjustments following the accession of croatia to the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union, in accordance with article 3 (4) and (5) of the act of accession. this is a purely technical matter which raises no legal or political problems.
in writing. ‒ the objective of this commission recommendation for a council decision is to make the necessary amendments by virtue of the accession of croatia to the convention and the protocol referred to in article 3 (4) and (5) of the 2012 act concerning the conditions of accession to the european union. the act simplified its accession to the conventions and protocols concluded by the member states pursuant to article 34 of the treaty on european union (former article k.3 teu). it is no longer necessary, as in the past, to negotiate and conclude specific accession protocols (with the consequent ratification of the 28 member states). article 3 (4) and (5) simply states that croatia accedes to the conventions and protocols by virtue of the act. for the reasons i have just mentioned, i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mrs sippel's report because i believe that more clarity is needed on the entry into force of the convention of 29 may on mutual assistance in criminal matters between member states, to which croatia automatically acceded following its accession to the eu.
in writing. ‒ this is a mandatory step when a new member state joins the eu and i naturally voted in favour. croatia merely accedes to the eu convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters. it is then for the council to make the adjustments to the convention which are necessary following the accession of croatia.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr sippel, which is purely technical in nature and which essentially allows croatia, the last country in chronological order to have acceded to the european union, to accede to the convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters between the member states of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i recognise the importance of facilitating assistance between the judicial, police and customs authorities of the member states in criminal matters.

oral explanations of vote
written declarations of vote
in writing. - i do not agree with the policy that europe is pursuing against russia. the only result of the decisions taken so far by the eu has been the creation of the sanctions system which is causing enormous economic damage to the european market, particularly the venetian and italian markets. the european union's persistence in its positions will only worsen the disastrous economic situation we are experiencing. for all these reasons i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i share its conclusions. i believe that russia is acting in a hostile manner towards the international community and the eu. i hope, however, that relations between us and the russian federation will be normalized so that we can create a strategic partnership in the future.
in writing. ‒ russia is a natural partner of the european union and the eu's policy of building a mutually beneficial strategic partnership, based on shared values of democracy and the rule of law, as well as common economic interests, has been corrected. however, the russian leadership chose not to reciprocate the trust that the union had given by committing serious violations of human and political rights (incarceration of political opponents, severe restriction of freedom of the press and of opinion, discriminatory campaigns against religious, political or lgbt minorities) and violating the principles of good neighbourliness by occupying the georgian regions of abkhazia and ossetia, by intervening militarily within the territorial borders of ukraine and illegally annexing crimea, by supporting serious initiatives of political destabilisation in ukraine, moldova, georgia and armenia, by repeatedly violating the union's air and maritime space, by endangering the security of civilian flights, and by violating agreements on non-violent regulation of military proliferation and regulation of the war apparatus. the situation has reached such a level of severity that it is intolerable: the solution is political and we must use the diplomatic and economic soft power that the union and its allies have to target the russian leadership and contain the impact on the civilian population.
in writing. ‒ i voted against, the report is biased and full of anti-russian prejudices. the anti-russian policy imposed on the eu by the americans must be reversed, russia is an important partner for our companies and moscow is certainly not an enemy, but it should be more involved in european development policies.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the state of eu-russia relations to underline that the european union must re-examine its relations with russia, which currently appear to be compromised by the latter's destabilising actions. with its aggression against ukraine and its annexation of crimea, the russian leadership has put eu-russia relations at a crossroads. it is now up to the kremlin to decide the direction: cooperation or greater isolation. i am convinced that the russian people, like all of us, want peace, not war, and, as prime minister putin said in his recent meeting with italian prime minister renzi, want an end to the reduction in trade with the eu due to sanctions. change in russia must come from within, it can and will. in the meantime, we must send a strong message to the russian leadership, stressing our closeness to the victims of its aggression and to those who defend the values on which the eu is founded.
in writing. ‒ the landsbergis report, while initially considering russia a strategic partner, concludes that the doors of dialogue with moscow must be closed. the report does not mention that, since the 1990s, europe and the west have gradually relaxed relations with russia, but have never opened up their discussions on their respective needs. the european union has rightly called on moscow to respect human rights, but has failed to point out that the same anti-russian interlocutors, financed by the west, often fail to comply with the requirements of the eu acquis. in general, i am opposed to the approaches to analysis and the prospects for action advocated by the report, and i therefore voted against. russia's strategic capacity, not just economically, makes it a subject with which the eu cannot fail to find a peaceful solution to its disputes. in my view, there is no other solution than diplomacy and soft power. the european union has a duty to help the people of europe to find a way to live in peace and security.
in writing. ‒ i have the impression that there are too many nostalgic for the cold war in the european parliament lately. i do not share this view. i believe that the eu should have a more effective and as far-reaching foreign policy as possible, but that does not mean that we should take counterproductive actions. the eu has so far been distinguished by its use of soft power and i believe that it is appropriate to continue along this path: more dialogue, less sanctions, and that's the way it's going to be. more convenience, and less self-flagellation. we have always left the iron fist to others, and we should continue to do so.
in writing. ‒ the strategic partnership that the european union has established with russia is based on shared values and is characterised by a model of enhanced cooperation that benefits both parties. the ukrainian issue has destabilised some political and trade balances, but it is clearly in the interest of both sides to continue the dialogue in the light of the important common global challenges. i therefore hope that good neighbourly relations will be restored and i shall vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the landsbergis report opens by looking at the efforts made by the eu in recent years to achieve peaceful and open relations with moscow. the report concludes that the door to dialogue with moscow must be closed in the face of repeated violations, from the nagorno-karabakh issue to south ossetia and today's crimea. the european union has rightly called on moscow to respect human rights, but has failed to point out that the same anti-russian interlocutors, financed by the west, often fail to comply with the requirements of the eu acquis. the eu and the whole west's relations with russia have improved over the years with moscow being listed among nato, oecd, g-8 or g-20 partners. the conditionality that is being applied today to moscow is unacceptable, but it should be the same for other international actors with whom the eu has stable relations. i believe that russia's strategic capacity, not just economically, makes it a subject with which the eu must find a peaceful solution to its disputes. i voted against the report because i am opposed to the approaches to analysis and the perspectives for action advocated by it. i believe that any international comparison tool, if it goes beyond the typical eu instruments, risks distorting its function and proving to be counterproductive.
in writing. ‒ with this report, europe concludes that it wants to close the dialogue with russia; it is argued that all the efforts made by the eu to try to maintain a relaxed relationship with moscow have failed, given the multiple human rights violations that russia has committed and is the protagonist of, starting with the nagorno-karabakh issue, passing through crimea and ending with the violation of freedom of the press, expression and rights related to sexual identity. it is perfectly acceptable to find most of moscow's behaviour reprehensible, but it is not acceptable to consider the closure of the dialogue with russia and the eu's abandonment of its soft power as the only viable alternative. what i also find unsatisfactory is the fact that we are using two weights and two measures depending on economic expediency, if on the one hand we want to be intransigent with russia now, on the other hand we are much more willing to accept behaviour from other european partners which is completely outside the acquis communautaire.
in writing. - a shortsighted and crazy relationship. the eu's current stance on this issue is simply suicidal for the majority of eu citizens. chasing the united states into this new cold war is crazy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the state of eu-russia relations because i believe that russia has deliberately acted in recent months to destabilise its neighbours and, consequently, the european union. i am very concerned about the developments in ukraine, and in particular about the situation in crimea, whose illegal annexation has created an atmosphere of growing tension in the whole region, with serious repercussions on the good relations between russia and the eu. the control of the media and intimidation of journalists are a source of tension, as is the gradual increase in pro-russian propaganda and the repression of dissent and free information. i therefore call for full disclosure of all murders of political opponents and activists. on the human rights and lgbti front, i share the need to commit to taking strong action to eradicate homophobia and discrimination in society. i share the call to russia, which remains a strategic partner for the eu, to cooperate in accordance with international law in order to revive international dialogue and cohesion, and i hope that russia will be ready to restore and respect the territorial integrity and sovereignty of ukraine.
in writing. in this report, the european parliament reaffirmed russia's direct and indirect involvement in the armed conflict in ukraine, the violation of georgia's territorial integrity and a policy of political destabilisation and economic coercion of neighbouring states. we must firmly condemn any violations of human rights and the rule of law, and instead reward dialogue and cooperation between the european union and russia so that the democratic international order can be fully restored.
in writing. ‒ the report on the state of eu-russia relations covers a number of issues which are currently rather sensitive and complex. on the one hand, relations with a world power which are strained and limited by embargoes and various sanctions with a number of situations to be resolved, on the other hand, a long relationship and a closeness on certain trade issues which deserve to be dealt with. in putting these two realities together, i found abstention to be the most balanced and appropriate choice.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the eu-russia relations, which have been damaged by recent events, would benefit from a proactive, forward-looking approach. i have therefore decided not to vote for this report, which i believe proposes a nihilistic and closure strategy.
in writing. ‒ with today's vote we express our deep concern at the recent escalation in relations with russia, which has always been a strategic partner of the european union. we hope that in the long term constructive relations are possible and desirable for the benefit of both sides, bearing in mind that mutual sanctions are harmful to both economies, that common challenges and interests on the world stage must be addressed jointly and that the fragmented nature of the perception of security in europe can only be overcome through strengthened dialogue. we therefore stress that resumption of cooperation can be considered on condition that russia respects the territorial integrity and sovereignty of ukraine and fully implements the minsk agreements (which include full border control by the ukrainian authorities, unconditional withdrawal of russian troops and armaments and immediate suspension of assistance to rebel groups), while also putting an end to the destabilisation of military and security activities at the borders of eu member states. we reiterate that unconditional respect for the rule of law, the protection of freedom of expression and the rights of minorities are essential and founding principles of the european union and we therefore call for their strict application.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to abstain from voting on the above-mentioned report because i believe that the european union cannot afford to interrupt the dialogue with russia. the isolation of russia is harmful to europe as a whole and to the whole system of international relations. if we are concerned about the prosperity and peace of the continent, we must redouble our efforts to rebuild a relationship with that country.
in writing. ‒ in firmly reaffirming that russia's policy towards ukraine cannot ignore respect for ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity, i recognize that at the same time it is necessary to reassure russia on an important point: the eu is also committed to the development of a common foreign and security policy. i believe that a balanced policy of ukraine towards the west and at the same time towards russia is both necessary and beneficial for both sides. i have decided to abstain from voting on this resolution because i believe that it does not take adequate account of the delicate balance achieved in the framework of the minsk ii agreements. at the moment, the only correct way of resolving the crisis is to show the political will to enter into negotiations. to avoid further tensions, official channels for inclusive dialogue with moscow must be kept open. the eu and nato enlargement towards the east is seen by russia as a direct threat to its security and it is the duty of the western countries to understand and share russia's sensitivity on this point. russia is a strategic partner and the eu needs a broad and clear relationship with this great power, which will allow the necessary cooperation in many areas.
in writing. ‒ russia is a key partner for europe without which it is not possible to build an area of security and prosperity. at the same time, recent events in ukraine, not to mention the 2008 military aggression against georgia, together with recent laws restricting press freedom and lgbt rights, are putting eu-russia relations to the test. in recent years moscow has tried to build up political support within the union by funding far-right parties such as the national front in france and jobbik in hungary. i voted in favour because mr landsbergis' report expresses a balanced view of the actions which the eu and the member states are called upon to take in eu-russia relations.
in writing. ‒ in the recent period, and i regret this, we have seen an escalation of tension in relations between the eu and russia. i acknowledge that there have been actions taken by russia that have not respected international law and have created hardship for the people and damaged the economy. despite what has happened, i have chosen to abstain on the resolution because i believe that we must have a long-term vision and aim at a constructive relationship between the eu and russia, in the interests of both and with the prospect of working together on global challenges such as climate change, the middle east peace process, the fight against terrorism and organised crime and cooperation on new technological developments. moreover, the current sanctions are harmful to both economies and the existing relations, which are fragmented, weaken both on the world stage.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by the committee on foreign affairs on the state of relations between the european union and russia. i believe that the key role of europe as a mediator in the difficult relations between the united states and the russian federation should not prevent it from taking a clear and unambiguous position on certain points of view expressed by its partners. while it is good to keep the path of dialogue open, this cannot and must not prevent the eu from expressing a critical view of the policy of president putin, who, through strategic choices that we all know by now, has deliberately violated fundamental democratic rights and values. but a rightly critical assessment of putin's policy must not turn into a condemnation of russia that leads to a total closure of relations between this state and the european union. if we are serious about the prosperity and peace of the continent, we must redouble our efforts to rebuild relations with the russian people.
in writing. ‒ i voted against because i consider russia a strategic partner for the european union and i do not share the current european foreign policy towards a country with which we should be engaging in dialogue rather than seeking confrontation.
in writing. ‒ russia remains an important partner of the european union in several areas, including energy security, trade and the fight against terrorism and organised crime. i have therefore decided to vote against the report because i do not think it will help to promote a constructive debate to continue and, above all, to strengthen cooperation between the european union and russia in the long term. i hope that both sides will make a greater effort to try to bring the current crisis in ukraine to an end as soon as possible, in mutual respect of the minsk peace agreements, and thus to prevent any further deterioration in relations. both the russian blacklist, which prevents 89 european politicians and officials from entering russian territory, and the report adopted by the european parliament today risk being counterproductive and having the only effect of exacerbating the climate of growing tension.
in writing. ‒ the landsbergis report is a very serious attempt to sabotage the facts and the peace. it deliberately misrepresents the role of the us and the eu in triggering the crisis in eastern europe. i voted against it. here's what really happened in ukraine and triggered the crisis: yanukovich won democratic elections; the oecd, which is in charge of election monitoring, "promoted the ukrainian vote as 'transparent and honest', http://www.repubblica.it/esteri/2010/02/08/news/ucraina_8_feb-2224351/, after which 'the western encouragement to the anti-government activists of the maidan was certainly neither discreet nor low-level, with the appearance on the square of the foreign ministers of france and germany and senator mccain', http://www.lastampa.it/2014/03/04/culture/opinions/opinions/forcing-of-obama-and-the-italian-life-xd9avm3wxx7uw4vxetfibp/pagina.html. the west should play the mea culpa for helping to overthrow a democratically and lawfully elected head of state: the report, however, reverses the situation and says that russia is challenging the order of the international democratic community. the report also urges the eu to provide financial support to anti-government (or non-governmental) voices in russia. this is called interfering in the internal affairs of a sovereign country. the eu wants to deal with russia in the same way as it dealt with yanukovych's ukraine. the eu is now definitely the eastern branch of nato and wants to lead europe into world war iii.

written declarations of vote
in writing. ‒ the report contains controversial aspects which at least deserve a less biased examination, which is why i do not find it balanced and do not agree with it. i've decided not to support you with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the recent geopolitical crises have shown the vulnerability of the european union in terms of security and energy supply. to meet this challenge, it is necessary to overcome the idea that each individual member state adopts its own national energy policy in an uncoordinated and unintegrated manner with respect to a general framework of priorities defined at community level. the draft report we voted on today clearly identifies these priorities: diversify sources of supply, improve energy efficiency, develop modern transmission infrastructure and integrate renewable resources more efficiently. the commission will also be working on a new strategy for the energy sector, which will be based on the principle of the internal market and the principle of solidarity between member states. this is a fundamental project which lays the foundations for a future energy union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is important that the eu should work towards having its own energy security strategy to ensure a constant and regular supply of energy.
in writing. - i voted against it. the eu's energy policy is wrong and uneconomic. it is pushing away the russian supplier, which is currently the cheapest gas in the world, and is relying on the costly and insufficient development of renewables.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the european energy security strategy. the well-known russian events show that the security and prosperity of the european union require the rational and efficient use of energy, through a constant, accessible and sustainable energy supply. the european union therefore considers the establishment of a european energy union to be of the utmost importance. the eu's energy strategy should also focus on key issues such as the achievement of a fully integrated internal energy market, moderating energy demand, decarbonising the energy mix and research and innovation, the development of renewable energy and its storage. the report touches on all these points and that is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the report by mr saudargas. the negotiations in the itre committee led to substantial improvements in the initial draft of the report, which allowed it to be rebalanced but not to change its nature; the text remains imbued with a strongly anti-russian and profuse spirit. instead, a focus on energy efficiency and renewables and a moderate and cooperative approach should dominate the union's energy security strategy.
in writing. ‒ energy security remains the major challenge facing the european union in the coming years. the instability in the regions that supply us with energy makes it necessary to achieve an energy union which can be achieved by defining a long-term strategy that can chart the path to increase domestic production. in this scenario, not only is it essential to increase the production capacity and storage of renewable energy but also energy efficiency, where there are more critical considering that it will be difficult to reach the 20% target by 2020. efforts and commitments at all levels are needed, especially by local authorities, which could provide a significant impetus for investing in sustainable public transport and in making public buildings more efficient. the 2014-2020 structural and investment funds can be a very important source of funding to deliver these actions and to trigger the energy mix that will enable the transition to a low-carbon economy and the achievement of european objectives. i therefore voted in favour of the report, but unfortunately the text did not reach a majority in the house.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the european energy security strategy because, although i share the basic approach of rational and efficient energy use, aimed at achieving an energy security situation which would also enable the union to emancipate itself politically from the yoke of its own needs, i felt that i could not express myself in favour of certain points. i do not agree with the total demonization of the use of shale gas which could help to lift us at least partly from dependence on unstable countries. to call it even a low-profile technology before its potential benefits and potential dangers have been scientifically explored seems to me frankly overstated. i also disagree with what has been said on nuclear energy, because even if the subject does not directly concern italy, i believe that the countries which have made use of this technology have had advantages and, aware of the risks inherent in this type of source, i am once again against demonizing it.
in writing. ‒ energy security means political independence, the independence of sovereign states, and the stabilisation of economic growth and democracy in europe. given that the eu still imports 53% of its energy needs, mainly from geopolitically unstable regions, and that some member states are dependent on a single external source of energy supply, the use of oil and natural gas for foreign policy purposes undermines the eu's economic growth and stability. therefore, the signing of an additional protocol would allow for the establishment of a long-term strategy to promote eu energy independence, increase the bargaining power of member states, develop energy technologies, diversify and consolidate supply options, increase consumption efficiency and develop interconnections to link regional energy markets. in this context i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the european energy security strategy provides an opportunity to consider the energy situation in europe. this is a delicate debate and a balanced approach must be found between the need to develop a green vision of the economy and society and the demands of european industry. in this context, security is certainly one of the fundamental elements to be considered also for future generations. the following points should be made about the progress made in recent years in the differentiation of energy sources: in fact, thanks to the increase in renewable sources, the dependence on less secure sources such as nuclear is falling sharply. as regards the issue of security from a geopolitical point of view: so there's a second reason to do, which is about dependency on a business partner. the russian federation. the european union is now heavily dependent on oil, gas, coal and uranium. efforts to diversify further, which also involves reducing costs and risk, must therefore be stepped up. i therefore believe that it is necessary to intensify the debate on this subject both for reasons of economic opportunity and for the proper protection of consumer rights.
in writing. ‒ the strategy was adopted by the commission on 28 may 2014, following a request by the european council to establish a short- and long-term action plan to reduce energy dependence on external sources. the initial text focused on fossil fuels, regasifiers, drilling, new gas pipelines and carbon storage. the commission's communication has a clear political direction: the commission has also proposed that the member states should try to avoid as far as possible the use of russian gas from other sources of supply and at the same time increase domestic energy production, particularly through nuclear energy and the extraction of fossil fuels. this goes hand in hand with the financing of new crossborder infrastructure works, which should improve the interconnection of the european energy network. as m5s, we have managed to amend the text by adding key concepts such as appropriations for energy retrofitting of buildings, emphasising the importance of renewables for european energy security, supporting the eu fracking moratorium and the elimination of fossil and nuclear subsidies. unfortunately, the final text, while approving the moratorium on fracking and the energy conversion of buildings, nevertheless contains several negative elements, such as public subsidies for nuclear energy and an excessive demonization of russia. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ another report that puts the eu out of the global game. instead of building a global dialogue on this issue, they prefer to put the screws to our companies and businesses.
in writing. the ukrainian crisis, as well as the recent call for gazprom, have undoubtedly been two important warning bells that the union cannot and must not underestimate. in the light of all this, and with energy import figures in the eu at 53% (and which unfortunately see italy even more exposed, with energy imports for 80% of consumption needs), trying to act with the utmost urgency to put in place a european energy security strategy can only be a plan that is not only shared, but today increasingly urgent, necessary and a priority. i therefore wholeheartedly support mr saudargas' report, which highlights the main emergencies we are committed to tackling and, above all, the actions and measures which the eu and its member states must take as soon as possible to reduce energy demand and create an internal market which protects us from any political speculation on energy supplies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the european strategy for energy security in the eu because the creation of a single energy market is a key issue, responding to economic, industrial, environmental and geopolitical challenges. the eu currently imports 53% of its total energy consumption, mainly oil, gas and solid fuels, from countries with complex geopolitical situations. the russian crisis shows once again the dangers of dependence on a single source of supply. this situation is politically and environmentally unsustainable. the diversification of energy sources is an essential condition for reducing dependence on fossil fuels. we need a new energy paradigm, a new vision for the future, which focuses on european production of renewable energy, energy efficiency and demand moderation, combining production, economic and environmental objectives. i also share the call for the role of local authorities in the definition of energy policies in the regions. it is precisely in this connection that i voted with conviction in favour of the s&d group's call for a moratorium on drilling and shale gas. the diversification of sources must not jeopardize the protection of the environment and the states have a duty to protect our seas by listening to the voice of those areas with a great tourist vocation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because energy policy must be tackled with an effective strategy. more than half of our energy needs are imported from third countries. in 2013, 39% of gas imports came from russia, 33% from norway and 22% from the north african countries algeria and libya. if we look at the situation of those who are our partners today, we understand the urgency of the need to emancipate ourselves. the russian blacklist is just the latest demonstration of the need to diversify external supply. the world geopolitics is changing, the effects on europe are manifesting themselves on several levels. the energy sector is one of the most affected, hence the need for reform. for the safety and well-being of our citizens, energy must harness new technologies, not old diplomatic relations.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report on the european energy security strategy. i consider this a matter of great importance, because of its crucial role in confirming europe's strong political and economic position, and so sensitive, because of its specific nature and the different requirements of the various member states, also because of the high costs involved.
in writing. ‒ following the crisis in ukraine, in may 2014 the european commission became a promoter of a european energy security strategy. the itre committee then decided to draw up an own-initiative report on the subject, with mr saudargas in charge of its preparation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. for these reasons i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the recent conflict in ukraine has certainly reminded european states of the importance of security of energy supply and has underlined the close link between the energy market and its geopolitical context. despite some progress in recent years, the european union still faces challenges such as instability in its energy-supply regions, a fragmented internal market and the fight against climate change. the eu imports 53% of its total energy consumption and many member states still depend on a single external source of supply, which hinders europe's economic growth and endangers internal and eu security. the report adopted today sets out a number of priority actions to moderate energy demand by increasing domestic energy production and developing new energy technologies, with the aim of building a fully integrated and efficient internal market. the commission will continue to promote new energy efficiency, focusing on alternative sources. new technologies could help reduce energy dependence by diversifying and consolidating supply options. as regional integration is a key element of energy security, the eu will need to step up its efforts to implement strategic energy infrastructure projects, fostering solidarity and coordination mechanisms.
in writing. ‒ the european commission, following the crisis in ukraine in may 2014, proposed a european energy security strategy. the itre committee then decided to draw up an own-initiative report on the subject, and asked mr saudargas to draw up it. although i believe that the european union must play a key role in european and international energy policy, i believe that the text, as drafted and presented in this chamber, does not fully reflect the initial forecasts. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe that the eu must complete the single market by adding the energy union to it, and this can only be done by diversifying energy sources and focusing on renewable resources. in the past russia, europe's main supplier of gas, oil, uranium and coal, has blocked the supply of natural gas to ukraine because of disagreements with the country. this has caused inconvenience in many member states which are interconnected to the russian federation via the network crossing ukraine.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the rapporteur when he stresses the importance of energy security for the eu and how vulnerable the energy market can be if we refer to current geopolitics. it is important to stress that, despite the progress made in recent years, there is a need for energy security in the eu. even now, the eu itself imports 53% of its total energy consumption and some member states are still dependent on a single external supplier, which shows how fragile the balance can be and can jeopardise the eu's economic growth. i am in favour of creating an efficient internal energy market by competing among different suppliers with the aim of having reliable services at lower prices but for that very reason, and i have therefore abstained, i do not support the proposal to close trade relations with some partners, because that would undermine the ultimate objective of having reliable energy supplies at competitive prices.
in writing. ‒ i voted against because i think the text is too optimistic in identifying the use of important renewable sources as the solution to most of the problems of energy supply at european level. i also believe that the text tends to cross borders in areas which should be primarily the responsibility of the individual member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the european energy security strategy because i consider it of paramount importance that the eu should have a regulatory framework that enables it to ensure the security of energy supply by phasing out its dependence on fossil fuels. i regret that the resolution has been rejected, depriving the european parliament of its voice on this issue. the document contained important proposals to move towards decarbonisation of the economy (such as renewed support for binding targets for the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, energy efficiency and the share of energy produced from renewable sources, as part of the 2030 climate package), environmental protection (moratorium on new shale gas exploration, recognition of liability for nuclear operators for environmental risks) and strong support for research to develop new energy technologies. it is necessary for parliament to continue the debate on this subject with an approach based on the combination and integration of energy policy and sustainable growth. i hope that the future debate on the european commission's recent proposal for the creation of the energy union will follow this path.
in writing. ‒ i voted no by helping to reject the saudargas report on energy security. it retained all the essential elements of the european commission's communication, which was more political than aimed at guaranteeing real and lasting energy security and still in the wake of the fossil fuel paradigm. the plant started from the desire to no longer buy russian gas and to supply it by building infrastructure to import it from other areas; through the development of clean coal/ccs, nuclear and drilling to extract more fossil fuels and produce more indigenous energy in the eu. these negative aspects of the report were overwhelming the positive elements that the m5s, thanks to the work of the itre committee, had brought: binding targets for renewables, energy savings and greenhouse gas reduction; the commitment to financially support the energy retrofitting of buildings. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the use of fossil fuels in the transport sector. these parts are my only regret. however, the m5s amendments approved by the itre committee and the vote in plenary against fracking are the sign of an existing majority in the european parliament. i will work to ensure that this will leave its mark on the legislative process.
in writing. ‒ we have today rejected the european energy security strategy adopted by the commission on 28 may 2014 following a request by the european council to establish a short and long-term action plan to reduce energy dependence from abroad. although considerable progress has been made in the negotiations, including greater references in the text to energy democracy, decentralised production, the role of local and citizen initiatives, energy efficiency, the essential role of renewables in the european mix, the need to eliminate subsidies to fossil fuels and the reduction of dependence through measures to moderate demand, the text remains highly controversial. this difficult rebalancing has not been sufficient, and some important questions remain: the text covers all supply and mix options and does not close the door on nuclear or shale gas; the improvements to the text have not changed its nature, which remains very much focused on anti-russian and profossional attitudes. the focus on energy efficiency, renewables and demand moderation should have been dominant in such a strategy.
in writing. ‒ i regret the outcome of today's vote, as i believe that ensuring energy security is one of the main objectives of the european union and this own-initiative report would have been a step in the right direction. it is our task to reduce considerably the eu's dependence on fossil fuels and in particular the dependence of those countries which rely on a single supplier. the eu must lead the shift towards diversifying sources of supply by investing in research and development to increase the potential of renewables and energy efficiency. energy is the engine of sustainable growth in europe and a potential source of new high-quality jobs and new export markets to support our smes. i would also like to stress that growth and development in this area must go hand in hand with environmental protection legislation. it will be our task in the coming months to develop the ideas contained in the commission's communication on the energy union, promoting coherent and effective legislation that can meet the challenges of the future.
