in writing. ‒ the european union is founded on the values of respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law, respect for human rights and the protection of minorities. the death penalty is incompatible with all these values and its possible reintroduction by a member state, in this specific case hungary, would therefore constitute a clear violation of the treaties and the eu charter of fundamental rights. we therefore strongly condemn the repeated statements by hungarian prime minister orbán aimed at provoking a debate on the possible reintroduction of the death penalty in hungary, thus institutionalising and fuelling a concept which is in clear violation of the values on which the union is founded. we also deplore the public consultation on immigration initiated by the hungarian government, which ends up feeding xenophobic prejudices. we therefore call on the european commission to immediately activate a thorough monitoring process on the situation of democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights in hungary, assessing any serious or systematic violations of community values within the meaning of article 2 teu, and to submit a thorough report to us by september 2015.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as i believe that prime minister orban's statements to reassure the eu that the death penalty is not being introduced, which is contrary to fundamental values and eu law, have ended the recent controversy on the subject. i think, however, that there is some concern about the presence of extremist parties that are questioning the european project.
in writing. ‒ i have been following the recent events in hungary closely and the speeches of the hungarian prime minister viktor orban where he spoke about what happened in his country and the debate on the death penalty. i think that he made it clear, also in his meeting with the president of the european parliament, mr martin schulz, that the hungarian government was not prepared to take any measures to reinstate it. i recognize the lack of need for public consultation on immigration and the questions posed to hungarian citizens, some of which are tendentious. i do not share the accusations against the eu on immigration at a time when it is finally trying to implement an immigration policy based on the principle of solidarity and quotas. i have decided to abstain on the resolution because the hungarian government must be given time to correct its actions and not to isolate a member state too harshly.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because the situation in hungary is no longer bearable. the orban government continues to challenge the european union and the international community with continuous acts of arrogance. the situation inside the country is becoming more and more intolerable, with real intimidation of all minorities. the european parliament must take up its responsibilities and work to make hungary the great democratic state it was before orban and his government came to power.

in writing. ‒ my vote in favour of the european parliament resolution on the commission's 2014 progress report on turkey because the time has come for the country to align itself with the parameters of the european union, which necessarily requires the implementation of appropriate and effective reforms. the efforts which we are sure turkey will make to strengthen its institutions and the process of democratization and modernisation are an opportunity which cannot be missed. turkey has been a strategic partner for the eu since accession negotiations were launched in 2005 and a process based on a commitment to reforms was launched. a lot of progress has been made, but many questions remain unanswered. in short, turkey must do much more to meet the copenhagen criteria. finally, i hope that the results of the recent elections will favour the reforms needed to bring turkey closer to the european union.
in writing. ‒ while i appreciate the basic message of the report, that the country must do much more to fight corruption, respect media freedom, freedom of expression and the independence of the judiciary, i chose to abstain. i particularly disagree with the various calls for increased funds to be used in specific areas in turkey and the call for new negotiating chapters to be opened. what i would like instead is a moment of reflection to see whether turkey's accession is really in the interests of all parties.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the 2014 progress report on turkey, a country with which the eu opened accession negotiations in october 2005 and which has committed itself to respecting the copenhagen criteria. the resolution welcomes the commission's report and shares the view that turkey remains an important strategic partner and that the negotiations represent an opportunity for both sides. however, concerns are expressed about the independence of the judiciary and the repeated bans on the media.
in writing. ‒ turkey is a large democratic country, not yet ready to join the eu, but different from the arab world that many of us often confuse with it. other countries that were part of the ottoman empire are now part of the eu, and we should take note without prejudice of the different developments that turkey has had in recent years. i believe that dialogue must not be interrupted, and with it the common plans for the future. i think that this report is fairly balanced and objective in this respect, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ eu-turkey relations bring benefits to both sides in economic, energy security and foreign policy matters. in the light of turkey's progress in its efforts to meet the copenhagen criteria, maintain good neighbourly relations and gradually align with the eu, there is still much reform to be done. the eu has also been active in the fight against corruption, and has been involved in the negotiations with turkey on the eu's accession to the european union. in this context, the eu can seize the opportunity to promote peace, democracy, security and prosperity in europe by inviting turkey to place the reform process to establish effective democratic legislation based on respect for fundamental freedoms at the heart of its domestic policy. on the basis of these considerations i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled following various statements by the council and the commission on the progress made by turkey.
in writing. ‒ it is right to ask turkey to make greater efforts to have more democracy. it is still a grave mistake to insist on turkey's membership of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the 2014 progress report on turkey and share the view that turkey is a strategically important political, economic and cultural partner for the european union. i believe that efforts between the european union and turkey to achieve closer cooperation must be stepped up and i hope that the turkish government will see the need to intensify the negotiations and commit itself to respect for democratic principles and human rights. i am concerned, however, about the adoption of laws which undermine the freedom of the media and which therefore infringe the principle of freedom of expression and the right to privacy. the situation remains critical in terms of gender equality, too, due to high rates of violence against women and poor protection by the authorities. i therefore hope that the government will address the gender gap and implement policies to increase the participation of women in civil society. finally, i believe that political dialogue with the eu must also respect the sovereignty of the member states and that turkey must refrain from any action which could jeopardise good neighbourly relations.
in writing. i believe it is crucial that the eu remains the benchmark for reform in turkey. this country has continued to implement the reforms undertaken in recent years, although a new constitution, based on provisions promoting a pluralistic, inclusive and tolerant society, would be the foundation of the reform process and would provide a solid basis for fundamental freedoms and the rule of law. i have supported this proposal because i consider it an important step in the process and i also urge the turkish government to guarantee media freedom as a priority and to provide an appropriate legal framework to guarantee pluralism in accordance with international standards.
in writing. ‒ i supported the text of the resolution because i believe it adequately and objectively addresses the state of progress in turkey from a socio-political point of view. despite the fact that cases of violations of citizens' rights continue to occur in the country, the european union can only be pleased with the positive developments achieved. the text of the document, which i consider to be complete and objective, clearly outlines the current situation in the country, setting out in a proactive manner the lines of cooperation between it and the european union.
in writing. ‒ turkey is a key partner for the european union, certainly one of the most important, both because of its geographical proximity and because of its converging economic and security interests. while we remain strongly interested in the continuation of the negotiations for turkey's accession to the european union, which is, however, conditional on the fulfilment of the formal criteria laid down by the treaty of lisbon, we cannot deny a certain concern about some recent events which have undermined turkey's international image. we are particularly concerned about the limited independence of the judiciary and the lack of freedom of expression. we also strongly urge that the peace process with the kurdish minority be accelerated and that a lasting solution to the issue be found as soon as possible. in any case, we are convinced that the solution to the country's undeniable problems is greater involvement of the international community, and specifically of the european union. the relaunch of the dialogue with turkey could lead to important progress both within the country and in the wider scenario of a crucial area of the world.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that turkey should put the reform process at the centre of its domestic policy choices and commit itself more strongly and 'unequivocally' to respecting the democratic values and principles of the eu, including freedom of the press, freedom of expression and the independence of the judiciary. i believe that the european commission should review with turkey the way in which its accession negotiations have been conducted so far, and give more thought to how to improve and intensify its relations with that country.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mrs piri's motion for a resolution because i believe that turkey is an essential partner for the eu in maintaining stability and security in the region. at the same time, in recent years, i have noticed a particular deterioration in the respect for the right to freedom of expression and information in the country, which risks further slowing down the eu accession process.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report and welcome the progress made by turkey as highlighted in the commission's report. turkey is a key partner for the eu in various areas of trade and industry, energy security, foreign policy cooperation, immigration and regional stability. in this light, i believe it is in the interests of both parties that closer cooperation between the eu and turkey should be established, with a mutual commitment to intensify negotiations, in view of the common strategic interests and the clear benefit that could be gained from a strengthened dialogue with turkey on economic issues and from greater integration between turkish and european businesses for the benefit of growth and employment.
in writing. ‒ the complex 2014 progress report on turkey was discussed during the last plenary session, but it was decided to postpone the vote, given the sensitivity of the issue and the lack of uniformity among the different currents in parliament. the resolution tabled by the committee on foreign affairs, which i decided to vote in favour of, highlights the positive results achieved by turkey in 2014, a country which has now become a strategic, economic and energy partner of increasing importance for europe, but on the other hand, critical issues remain and these must be resolved with a view to ever deeper cooperation. the negotiation with the eu itself represents a significant opportunity for turkey to develop a strong, pluralistic democratic system with strong institutions for the benefit of all turkish citizens and for closer relations with the european union.

close bond of friendship that ties the european union and its member states to nepal. the european union and its member states have already expressed the deep sympathy and solidarity of the european union for the human losses and injuries, and the physical devastation of homes, infrastructure and heritage sites. a disaster of this size calls for more than words. the eu and its member states were quick to act and show tangible solidarity with the nepalese people. immediately after the earthquake and following the appeal by the nepalese government, there was a clear expression of eu solidarity. the commission provided eur 3 million in humanitarian aid to support, in particular, emergency shelter, healthcare, and logistics and coordination. this amount was doubled to eur 6 million following the visit by the commissioner for humanitarian aid and crisis management, christos stylianides, who travelled to nepal together with valerie amos, the un under-secretary-general and emergency relief coordinator, to express eu solidarity. the european unionʼs civil protection mechanism was also activated to support the rapid deployment of relief material and experts from eu member states. the eu also provided consular support to eu citizens in nepal. in addition, the commission fast-tracked the disbursement of eur 16.6 million from existing development funds. this frontloaded cash allows the nepalese authorities to address the most pressing needs. we are also envisaging, under the instrument contributing to stability and peace, support in bringing necessary supplies to the remotest districts, which are very difficult to access after the earthquake. this support would also address the need for temporary learning spaces, as many schools have been destroyed. concerning your question on the partial reinstatement of custom duties, i would like to inform you about the actual situation. as per the memorandum of understanding between the government of nepal ... (the president interrupted the speaker to ask for quiet in the chamber)we are talking about the earthquake in nepal and how the european union can help. when we talk about the reinstatement of customs duties, we need to know that, as per the memorandum of understanding between the government of nepal and the un, which was signed several years ago now, humanitarian relief items are exempt from customs duties. initial confusion about this in the first few days after the earthquake was overcome and the government applied this approach more coherently following commissioner stylianides’ visit, streamlining procedures. at the end of may, however, the government replaced a general waiver by a list of relief items that remain exempt from customs duties. the un system, which the eu supports, has been actively gathering information from aid agencies on the application of this approach. this will serve as evidence for the meeting the un will have with the authorities so as to resolve the issue. if these efforts at local level are not successful, the commission stands ready to advocate, with the government, building on the contact that has already been established in the response to the earthquake. the eu is now actively participating in the ongoing post-disaster needs assessment, which should be ready by mid-june and which will serve as a basis for the recovery strategy. the eu will participate in the donor conference on reconstruction to take place in kathmandu on 25 june. (the president again called for quiet in the chamber) nepal also needs political stability to push forward its economic development and now its reconstruction. we hope that the long-overdue constitution could be adopted as a key step forward in nepal’s peace process. this should then be followed by establishing more decentralised, strong and accountable institutions. the long-overdue local elections should take place to restore legitimacy at local level. nepal also needs to address a number of human rights challenges, in particular the need to guarantee inclusivity to all and deliver justice to the conflict victims. many members asked about human rights. gender, non-discrimination and children’s rights are key priorities of the eu human rights strategy in nepal. the eu has been a long-standing supporter of civil society in addressing discrimination and violence against women and promoting better social economic conditions for women, as well as promoting the rights of children. the government of nepal has taken measures to prevent the trafficking of children. for instance, since the earthquake, the government has been more watchful of any possible trafficking and has been trying to raise public awareness against it. some of the districts most affected by the earthquake are the source districts from which trafficking of girls has taken place. (the president called for silence in the chamber) the eu supports a number of human rights organisations working on women’s and children’s rights which are active in the fight against human trafficking. the eu has been funding programmes to combat case-based discrimination and the untouchability issue, including supporting dalit-led organisations and empowering other vulnerable groups such as women and children in slums. as one of the major donors, the eu will continue to monitor the distribution of aid, as well as responding to human rights issues such as impunity and discrimination. nepal has survived a terrible tragedy. time will be needed for full recovery. therefore, the eu and other international partners will continue to support nepal and its people in these endeavours. i thank you very much for your interest in the situation in nepal. in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the recent revelations of corruption cases at the fifa summit. on 27 may 2015, swiss authorities arrested 14 fifa executives in zurich on charges of money laundering, racketeering, bribery and fraud for a total damage of over usd 150 million. a criminal investigation has been launched into the awarding of the world cup in russia and qatar. despite the arrests, fifa president joseph blatter managed to get himself elected for a fifth term and then resigned a few days later due to further developments in the investigation. the resolution also calls for the eu to take action to ensure that the eu's sporting and cultural heritage is protected and that the eu's sporting heritage is protected.
in writing. ‒ the revelations that have emerged in recent days regarding fifa's behaviour are quite disconcerting. i love sport, i play it when i can and i follow it with passion, and i have to say that certain accusations hurt those who, like me, believe that sport is and should be the symbol and emblem of fairness. the fact that the facts must be ascertained, and i am a convinced guarantor, i voted in favour of this resolution to leave it written in black and white that sport and corruption should never be associated, and that football must remain beautiful because it is clean. i hope that the accusations will prove to be unfounded or that, if they are not, those who have done wrong will pay in an exemplary manner.
in writing. ‒ first of all, i can only express my regret about the events that have involved fifa, the arrests and the ongoing criminal investigation into the awarding of the 2008 and 2022 world cups. this situation has seriously damaged the integrity of world football and sport in general, not only at the professional level but also at the amateur level, undermining trust in sporting institutions. let us not forget that such organisations are of fundamental importance in the global promotion of educational and cultural values, inclusion, peace, solidarity, loyalty and respect for human rights. i therefore call for a reform of fifa, through the implementation of strict ethical standards and a code of conduct for its management and the executive committee, in order to ensure greater democracy, transparency, legitimacy and accountability in the future. it is the responsibility of the eu, each member state, sports organisations and sponsors to support good governance in sport and to cooperate in countering transnational threats to the integrity and ethics of sport, such as doping, match-fixing, violence and all forms of intolerance and discrimination.
in writing. ‒ corruption, money laundering and betting have unfortunately steadily entered the world's most popular sport, with a devastating effect on the entire football world, from the highest level of professional football to local amateur clubs. i therefore voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution on the recent revelations of corruption at the fifa summit, because it is time to turn the page, adopt a zero-tolerance policy on corruption in sport and remove any shadow over the events of recent years. we therefore strongly call for an unreserved commitment by fifa to a thorough review of past and present decisions and the adoption of new reforms such as: the amendment of the statute, codes, structure, operational policies and, above all, the introduction of mandate limits leading to total transparency in the future. the integrity of football is at stake and fans are looking forward to a new season in which the bad guys are out of the stadium for good.
in writing. ‒ the recent corruption allegations against the international football federation (fifa) have seriously undermined the credibility and integrity of world football. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because it is necessary to adopt a policy of zero tolerance for corruption in football and to introduce deep structural reforms within the fifa organisation itself.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on what happened on 27 may 2015, when 14 fifa executives were arrested on serious charges of money laundering, racketeering, corruption and fraud amounting to about 150 million euros. in reality, this serious event has only re-emphasized an organization whose lack of transparency and corruption have long been known. the european parliament now hopes that sporting organisations and member states will cooperate in all ongoing investigations and that the investigation of past corruption practices will lead to the release of all those who may be responsible. the request to fifa to finally make public the full text of the garcia report on the controversial procedure for the allocation of the 2018 and 2022 world cups is also fully acceptable. it was therefore appropriate that the european parliament should have spoken so strongly on a matter which invades a sector which has a great influence on millions of europeans.
in writing. the scenario that emerges in the wake of the fifa scandal is truly disturbing: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud, corruption, criminal enterprise, sports fraud, the exploitation of workers employed in the construction of the infrastructure for the world cup in qatar and, last but not least, the arrogance of power. it is time to say enough about this charade that has been perpetrated against millions of sportsmen, passionate followers of football, the most popular sport in the world. the positive values inherent in sport, and among them football, have nothing to do with the corrupt and paramafioso management of fifa. we therefore call for every initiative to be taken to ensure transparency and democracy within the governance systems of the football world, starting with fifa. it is also necessary to clarify the alleged illegal allocations of the last world cups and, if appropriate, invalidate the allocation of the 2018 and 2020 editions should it become apparent that they are the result of corrupt activities. on the contrary, the positive values of sport should be reinforced by encouraging educational projects and sports activities based on the promotion of integrity and ethics in both individual and collective behaviour. we need loyalty, honesty and fairness, otherwise, as a game, we don't like football anymore.
in writing. ‒ it is right and proper to condemn the increasingly dirty world of football following the investigations that are upsetting fifa. it calls for greater transparency and control.
in writing. sport is by its very nature a vehicle for healthy values in society, a messenger of peace and social inclusion, a means of involving young people and educating them in fair play, respect for others, and moral integrity. at a time when sport, and especially football - the most popular game in the world - is becoming a symbol of corruption and reckless economic interests, as is unfortunately the case with fifa these days, the profound positive social impact and its intrinsic meaning risk being distorted and threatened. europe must therefore help to remind people of the true universal values underlying sport and take all the measures in its power to overcome these last regrettable events, restoring as soon as possible confidence in the world of sport and regaining a sense of responsibility and reputation. i therefore welcome the motion for a resolution and i greatly appreciate the efforts already made by the eu in this direction by launching the erasmus+ programme which is aimed at these objectives.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on the recent revelations of high-level corruption in fifa because i believe that the recent investigations into corruption within fifa, culminating in the arrest of 14 executives, clearly show how big a problem transactional corruption in sport is. criminal activity, which takes various forms, influences decision-making processes relating to sporting events, indelibly tarnishes the image of sport, obscuring its educational values of promoting peace, solidarity, the fight against racism and respect for human rights. all sports, and football in particular, have a profound social impact and cannot be tainted in any way by a corrupt and predatory culture. i therefore welcome the call to the governing bodies of sport to promote reforms and measures that bring greater transparency, democracy and control of decision-making processes involving important economic and sporting interests. the self-regulation of professional sport must be based on the principles of good governance, transparency and respect for the law. finally, i believe that cooperation and dialogue between sports authorities, public authorities and police forces at all levels should be strengthened, and that mechanisms should be set up to prevent such incidents from happening again.
in writing. following recent news of corruption in the top echelons of the international football federation (fifa), the european parliament decided to express its opinion by means of a motion for a resolution. the us-led investigation has implicated the fifa secretary general, and presumably the presidency, in possible corruption cases in the awarding of the world cup to south africa, russia and qatar, for 2010, 2018 and 2022 respectively. i voted in favour because i believe that corruption is a vile act, to be condemned in all sectors, both public and private, and even more so in the case of such high-level sporting events. sport and its values must be free from purely economic logic.
in writing. ‒ beyond its purely health-related aspects, sport contributes to social inclusion and integration, promotes cultural exchanges and creates jobs within the european union. the fifa affair is a serious case of corruption and criminality in this discipline that risks tarnishing the image of this sport as a whole. i believe it is necessary to stop similar cases, to intensify the reform process and to improve transparency in both the decision-making processes and the remuneration of the federation's officials. i therefore think it appropriate to vote in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ following the recent scandals involving some senior fifa officials and given the transnational nature of corruption in sport, this resolution is intended to highlight the need for more effective cooperation between all stakeholders. the new eu sports programme, under erasmus+, is moving in the right direction: the commission will continue to support new transnational educational projects that address cross-border threats to the integrity of sport, such as doping, match-fixing and violence, as well as all forms of intolerance and discrimination, and will aim to promote and support good governance in the sector. corruption often has implications, not just financial, that go beyond the community's borders, and for this reason it is one of the priorities of the european commission's action in the stockholm programme. we call today on the fifa executive committee to implement the structural reforms needed to ensure greater transparency in decision-making and higher ethical and conduct standards, which are essential to restoring international credibility to the world's most loved and played sport. we also call on interpol, europol and eurojust to launch their own investigations into possible cases of corruption by fifa officials in the eu.

in writing. ‒ on 27 may, swiss authorities arrested 14 fifa executives, including the vice-president, in zurich, on the basis of a us department of justice arrest warrant, on charges of money laundering, racketeering, bribery and fraud, amounting to more than $150 million. those investigations have shown that fifa has operated for many years as an irresponsible, non-transparent and notoriously corrupt organisation, and that these conditions are systemic, widespread and constant rather than being isolated cases of wrongdoing, as claimed by former fifa president joseph blatter. the arrests of fifa executives and the resignation of president blatter have created the conditions necessary to radically reform the structures and practices of the federation, so as to improve its governance and fight corruption within it without delay. it should be noted that the integrity of sports organisations is of paramount importance, as sport, both professional and amateur, plays a key role in the global promotion of peace, respect for human rights and solidarity. the commission should also be able to provide information on the implementation of the union's policy on the fight against corruption and on the implementation of the union's policy on the fight against corruption.

first vice-president of the commission.– mr president, let me react to some of the remarks and comments made. first, on greece, i insist the commission will continue its efforts to find a compromise which is acceptable to everyone, which is based on the idea that we should not let the greek people suffer more, and find a way out of this problem. those of you who have argued – i refer especially to mr nuttall and ms le pen – that that they are great friends of the greek people and are arguing against the euro and saying that we should leave the euro, should perhaps reconsider their friendship or their position, because the greek people by a vast majority do not want to get rid of the euro. they want to find a solution within the euro and, if you declare yourselves to be such great friends of the greek people, you might perhaps even follow their wisdom in that. now i can see somebody sitting next to ms le pen making a signal as though you are completely crazy. so your friends call you crazy. (interjection from the floor: ‘the euro is a disaster, sir’) sir, with friends like you, i would rather have enemies. (interjection from the floor: ‘better than the eurozone’) another subject that surprised me is that mr nuttall complained about the fact that his meps could not reach the european parliament yesterday because of a strike. i was under the impression that his party did everything possible to get rid of the european parliament. you cannot have it both ways, mr nuttall. (interjections from the floor: ‘no, he said british meps’; ‘they are all trying to enter britain, sir, they are all trying to flee europe’) i would hope that not all british meps forgot about their wonderful, wonderful legacy of being open to the world, of being self-confident enough not to be thinking in terms of building gates along the borders of europe. this brings me immediately to my second point, which is on migration. either we will find european solutions, or we will not find solutions and keep on working with the problems we have today. that is my deep conviction. i think to create the impression that, by keeping people out, we will solve the problem is not only morally suspect but is politically impossible. it will not happen. we are not australia. we are not located in the middle of an ocean. we cannot apply the same solutions. by the way, what are you going to say to the family fleeing war in damascus, or in other places in syria or elsewhere? ‘you have no right to asylum, you should stay there, you should be killed there? no, you should stay in the region.’ yes, go and say that to countries like jordan. go and say that to a country like lebanon, where one quarter of the population are refugees. sir, i think you need to rethink this idea that, by simply keeping people out, we will solve the problem. europe will need to take its responsibility to find a sustainable solution based on our values. if we compromise our values on this issue, we will compromise our values on all other issues that we need to deal with, including issues pertaining to our own citizens. (applause)so i plead with the council to follow the commission’s reasoning tomorrow. give us better reasoning, give us better solutions or follow our reasoning. the commission will stick to its proposition. i feel reinforced today by the position of the majority of this parliament to stick to this proposition. we have tried before with voluntary schemes. they have failed. i think it is an issue of political and moral integrity to see that and to draw the right conclusions from that. i wish the members of the european council the inspiration to take this seriously. on the specific issue raised by mr verhofstadt on hungary, the commission is now in close consultation with the hungarian government to know what these technical reasons are; why, etc. we are not even sure that there is a suspension. there are all sorts of rumours, so we are trying to find out exactly what has happened. we will certainly demand of all member states that they apply the rules and, if there is an emergency situation – there are indications that hungary is facing a sudden enormous surge of refugees; that can be an emergency situation – we have instruments at our disposal to assist member states to address that emergency situation. but simply stopping admission is not one of the instruments allowed by european rules. we are there to assist member states and we are also fully committed to assisting hungary in this. we are in the process of talking to them about this, but we do urge all member states to simply respect the rules we have agreed jointly. we will certainly continue to follow this very closely with hungary. finally, i want to reiterate, on behalf of the commission, that this european council needs to take bold steps forward in terms of the migration issue. if we do not decide today, more people will die and we will not be able to start implementing the rules and the necessary measures we will need to discuss in july. the commission will appeal – jean-claude juncker will appeal – to all other members of the european council to take responsibility on the basis of the commission’s proposal, with strong support from the european parliament. in writing. today we are talking about the european council summit which will be held here in brussels in the next few hours. the agenda includes key issues such as immigration and the greek crisis. these are urgent questions. the solutions which this council is about to discuss call on all of us to consider the future of europe, and to take action on the basis of the union itself. and that is precisely why it is imperative that common commitment, shared responsibility and solidarity be the guiding principles of the coming days. we must give back its soul to a europe that now breeds fear. going beyond technicalities and parameters to bring back the community of people we love and that holds us together. the answer to immigration cannot be that the problem does not concern us, just as the answer to the economic difficulties of the member states cannot be an exit. we have heard today in this house the difficulty of taking quick decisions in such situations. i do not agree, and i would like to thank vice-president timmermans for saying the opposite, that 'time is running out and we must get straight to the point'.
in writing. the greek crisis is clearly demonstrating the limits and negative consequences of austerity policies applied in times of crisis. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. what greece and europe as a whole need is a paradigm shift that focuses intervention not on cuts but on growth, through investments that promote competitiveness and give workers and small and mediumsized enterprises oxygen. the greek case also highlights the need for a union which is not merely monetary but economic and social, which acts with the aim of full employment and the defence of the rights of citizens.
in writing. for years parliament has called for greater involvement of the european union as a whole in tackling the phenomenon of waves of migration from countries in africa and the middle east which are burdened by devastating political, social and economic conditions. unfortunately, attention to these demands was often only given when there were major human tragedies, and then faded away a few days later without any concrete proposals for solutions. parliament has demanded a different response this time and the commission must be credited for the start of a wide-ranging and detailed work which culminated in proposals based on the equitable distribution of burdens and responsibilities among all the european countries. a proposal, perhaps for the first time, which is truly european and not just a help to those states which, for geographical reasons, are faced with the phenomenon directly and on the front line. it is important, therefore, to stress that this time 'europe', as it is generically referred to in many media, has lived up to its role, making proposals which we consider an important step in the right direction. it is now up to the member states, meeting in the european council today and tomorrow, to demonstrate that their membership of the european union is much more than economic union and is based on deep-rooted and shared values.

in writing. ‒ sotirios zarianopoulos is accused of having, using threats of physical violence, illegally broken into the premises of the greek public television station ert-3 on 4 march 2010 to interrupt the noon news and read a statement. the alleged offence has no connection with the position of sotirios zarianopoulos as a member of the european parliament, as the alleged offence is linked to an action by the greek trade union pame and sotirios zarianopoulos was not a member of the european parliament at the time of the events. under article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, an opinion expressed in the exercise of the mandate of a member of the european parliament is defined as a subjective assessment having a direct and obvious link with the exercise of parliamentary functions, but the alleged actions of sotirios zarianopoulos do not fall within this definition as the criminal proceedings do not concern any opinion or vote expressed in the exercise of the mandate of a member of the european parliament. there is no reason to assume that the proceedings are based on the intention to prejudice the political activity of the member (fumus persecutionis), also considering that the proceedings were initiated several years before the member's term of office began. for these reasons i voted in favour of the waiver of immunity.

in writing. ‒ the president of the berlin court of appeal has submitted a request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of udo voigt. pursuant to article 9 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union, members of the european parliament shall enjoy in their national territory the immunities accorded to members of their national parliaments. udo voigt is accused of incitement and collective insults launched in a publication published by the national democratic party, at the time of the 2006 fifa world cup. the charges are clearly unrelated to udo voigt's position as a member of the european parliament and are attributable to his position as president of the national democratic party. in the absence of any further comments, recitals (65) to (68) of the provisional regulation are confirmed. the proceedings cannot be suspected of being an attempt to obstruct the parliamentary activities of mr voigt (fumus persecutionis), since they were initiated some years before he took up his seat in the ep. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the waiver of immunity.

in writing. ‒ the legal rules of the european parliament must also be applied in the case of udo voigt. immunity is normally waived where the offence falls within the scope of article 9 of the protocol provided that there is no fumus persecutionis, i.e. a sufficiently serious and specific suspicion that the case is being brought before a court with the intention of politically harming the member concerned. the hearing in the legal affairs committee did not reveal any fumus persecutionis, since the events took place before voigt was a member of the european parliament. the alleged offence and subsequent legal action have nothing to do with voigt's tenure as a member of the european parliament. the unanimous vote in the legal affairs committee also shows this, hence my vote in favour of the waiver of immunity.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi). the global economic and financial crisis has had a profound impact on investment in europe, with a decrease of around 15% compared to 2007, amounting to around eur 430 billion. in some eu countries, including italy, the decline was more pronounced. to respond to this problem in a timely manner, the juncker plan provided for the establishment of the efsi. the fund will be financed through an eu guarantee of eur 16 billion and eur 5 billion of direct eib financing and, thanks to the expected multiplier effect, will be able to mobilise eur 315 billion of investments, including eur 75 billion for smes. the investment will be concentrated in a few key areas of the european economy (infrastructure, energy, research). the management of the fund will be carried out by a number of bodies (the steering committee, the investment committee) and technical advice will be provided by a european investment advisory hub. finally, a reserve list of investment projects is created in order to provide investors with transparent information on potential projects to benefit from the fund.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf). i believe it is essential to provide support for redundant workers and selfemployed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major changes in the structure of world trade due to globalisation, as a result of the continuing global economic and financial crisis, in order to assist them in their reintegration into the labour market. since it started its activities in 2007, the egf has proved to be an effective and efficient tool for people who have lost their jobs. it is a concrete expression of european solidarity and a practical tool to help people recover from large-scale redundancies. in particular, the egf allows member states to support targeted measures adapted to the circumstances of the workers concerned. since its inception it has helped and continues to help some 91 000 redundant workers by providing them with assistance in training, finding a new job or other forms of support. it is necessary to ensure that the egf continues to play a crucial role in the fight against unemployment.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) provides support for people who have lost their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade due to globalisation, such as the closure of a company or the relocation of production to a country outside the eu, or as a result of the global economic and financial crisis. the egf may finance up to 60% of the cost of projects to help redundant workers find other employment or start their own business. for all these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of the mobilisation of eur 630 000 to cover the fund's technical assistance. the objective of the technical assistance is to finance monitoring and information, to create a knowledge base/interface and to provide advice to member states in relation to the use, continuity and evaluation of the egf.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the circular economy has been discussed for decades, both in the scientific community and in civil society, as well as among social movements. finally, in the european parliament too, we are talking about this subject, we are talking about progress, basically, we are talking about the future of our economy. the report by mrs pietikäinen is a report which contains measures which are very much to be welcomed and which really looks in the direction of a circular economy, but in which there is a gap, in my view: you don't talk about circular economy until you talk about incineration. this practice, in addition to being a source of pollution dangerous to human health and the environment, also affects the possibility of implementing a waste reduction policy, which is one of the most important measures in the hierarchy of solid urban waste management. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. in this context, the measures proposed in the resolution risk being distorted and reduced to partial and weak measures, which do not allow the full achievement of a circular economy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the circular economy is a unique opportunity to help launch the economic and social development of europe and to launch it into a new phase of sustainable development, a phase in which waste is a resource, businesses are at the heart of the sustainable revolution and production and business models are circular precisely because they recycle raw materials and their efficient use. but it would be wrong to confine the circular economy to environmental policy. so you understand that the circular economy is not just what we want to do with the waste, so it's not just what percentage of separate collection we want to achieve, where we want to give it. the circular economy is undoubtedly the revision of waste legislation, which is an essential part, but it is much more. we must consider it as a strategic axis of economic development and - let me say this - even european industrial and social finance, because it means, for example, designing and manufacturing products in such a way as to increase their durability, recyclability and repairability, supporting the secondary raw materials market and changing, and at the same time reorienting, business and enterprise models. what then? it will be important for the european institutions to identify areas where there are clear legislative and economic-financial barriers to transition and to take action there with clear and pragmatic rules. vice-president of the commission.– mr president, thank you very much for this very good discussion. i would like to thank the rapporteur, sirpa pietikäinen, for a very good and interesting paper. as both first vice-president timmermans and i have said, the commission takes this exercise very seriously, we are passionate about this issue, and we also recognise the big challenge ahead of us, because the circular economy is not a simple issue at all. we want to be very humble with this large entity in order to choose the right things which need european-wide regulation. we also have to recognise where we do not need european-wide regulation. many colleagues here asked what i meant when i said that we have to avoid over—regulation. what i meant is that there are very good examples in europe even now, especially in the industrial sector, of business models which represent the circular economy. if we over-regulate something, it means that those good examples will be killed, and we have to avoid this. our aim is to set a target, and we want to be flexible on how to get there because the target itself is the main issue. for us, the circular economy is a matter of competitiveness; it is a matter of innovation; it is a matter of job creation, investment and growth. as europeans, we need to find a way to create a better environment for the circular economy. in the united states they do not necessarily have that need, because they have some points they can rely on, and on which to build their competitiveness, but when looking at europe, we have an economic necessity, an imperative, to be successful in this. when looking at asia, especially china, they have an environmental necessity, similarly to us. so this is a competition situation – whether europe is ahead of, for instance, the chinese, when creating incentives to business and consumers to boost the circular model of our economy. so let us continue on this file. this is also very important from the internal market viewpoint. if we manage to create an internal market for used raw materials or a secondary market for raw materials, then we can again build incentives for healthier, more environmentally, socially and economically sustainable development on this issue. the public consultations will last until 20 august. i hope you will all pass a message to stakeholders to be active, because we need good examples, we need assistance and advice from the private sector – but also from the ngo sector – on what is the best way to boost the circular economy on our continent.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on integrated multimodal ticketing in europe. in this resolution parliament stressed the benefits to users of the single ticket for a 'multimodal journey' using different modes of transport. the advantage of being able to use integrated ticketing systems would also attract more passengers to public transport, increasing the use of public transport. it is currently too difficult to obtain tickets for crossborder travel, particularly when these include different modes of transport, such as trains and buses. in the modern online society, it is therefore necessary to be able to issue more integrated tickets to make life easier for travellers. providers of transport services and of itinerary planning services should therefore further develop existing synergies, for example by providing multi-modal and cross-border travel itinerary planning services, and the commission should work to put in place the necessary measures to support and facilitate such efforts.
in writing. ‒ despite efforts already made, target 22 of the 2011 white paper, which aims to ensure seamless door-to-door multimodal travel using intelligent, multimodal and interoperable systems for timetable search, information, online booking and ticketing, has not yet been achieved. the report by mr dieter-lebrecht koch therefore aims to implement an integrated multimodal transport system in europe by improving information, planning and ticketing services for multimodal transport. by receiving comprehensive information, the traveller should be able to choose a personalised travel solution that represents the most sustainable, fast or economically viable alternative with a single ticket. in the light of the foregoing, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal on the issue of integrated multimodal tickets in europe. the objective is to provide comprehensive information at union level on the travel offers of public and private companies operating in the air, rail, sea and road transport sectors, thereby enabling travellers to benefit from a multimodal, cross-border and seamless travel solution. by receiving comprehensive information, the traveller should be able to choose, book and pay online for a personalised travel solution that is the most sustainable, fast or cost-effective alternative and to travel with a single ticket, regardless of the number of modes of transport used during the journey.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe that creating an integrated and multimodal ticketing system in europe is an important goal to be achieved in order to allow citizens to move around more easily, accessing more accurate and effective travel information. thanks to the single market and the free movement of persons, union citizens and visitors from third countries are increasingly faced with transnational travel using different means of transport. unfortunately, the information available is often tied to commercial agreements between the different private companies and is often restricted to regional or local level. the union's institutions therefore have a duty to encourage private airlines to coordinate more efficiently, so as to facilitate travellers' movements and at the same time increase tourism and hence economic growth. in addition, achieving this objective will help to tackle traffic problems such as congestion and pollution by encouraging the use of public transport. i therefore believe that the possibility of travelling using an integrated multimodal ticket is the first step towards an improvement in the conditions of travellers which will have a positive effect on the economy, tourism and the environment.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report by mr koch, who has identified a number of essential points for improving the integration of services between the different modes of transport. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's policy on the environment and its implementation in the member states. to date, given the inefficiency of some modes of transport, citizens continue to prefer individual transport. to remedy this problem, citizens should be given the opportunity to obtain comprehensive, accurate and neutral information on both timetables and availability of multimodal and crossborder transport links, in the context of facilitated travel, while also offering high standards of comfort, booking and purchasing tickets in electronic form. another crucial area that will need to be improved is equal access without barriers for all, people with disabilities or reduced mobility, the elderly and vulnerable people. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's transport policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report by the european parliament is based on the need to be able to travel with a single ticket, which allows the use of different means of transport for a so-called door-to-door journey. in 2011, the european commission, in its white paper on transport, expressed the need to create a single travel document covering all modes of transport from long to short distances. despite the priorities it had set, we are still far from achieving this project. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal from the european parliament which aims to promote a single transport document. this will require the commission to submit a proposal calling on providers to make all the necessary information available on a fair and supportive basis and to create a platform at european level to facilitate cooperation between stakeholders.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report which stresses the importance of information services and which aims to remove the current obstacles.
in writing. ‒ the transport sector is a key sector for the eu, from the point of view of the economy and employment but also from the point of view of integration between member states. this report provides several ideas for the possible modernisation of this sector, with multimodal tickets valid for air, rail, sea and road transport, with both public and private operators. the aim is therefore to make cross-border transport between all member states easier, whatever the means used. this will benefit consumers economically and organisationally, and the increased synergies between private and public operators and between local and national authorities will also have a positive impact on energy efficiency. in the light of these considerations, i voted in favour of the koch report.

in writing. ‒ the long-term objective of this proposal is to provide comprehensive information at union level on the travel offers of public and private companies operating in the air, rail, sea and road transport sectors, thereby enabling travellers to benefit from a multimodal and cross-border travel solution. by receiving comprehensive information, the traveller should be able to choose, book and pay online for a personalised travel solution that is the most sustainable, fastest or cost-effective choice and to travel on a single ticket, regardless of the number of modes of transport used during the journey. i therefore voted in favour of the report, considering that the mobility of citizens within the union is an essential condition for the exercise of fundamental freedoms and that citizens should therefore be able to obtain comprehensive, accurate and neutral information.

in writing. ‒ mobility is a fundamental part of modern life that is not limited to national borders. ticketing planning requires an integrated european approach, in line with the european transport policy and the roadmap for the eu-wide delivery of information on multimodal mobility and ticketing planning already presented by the commission. i believe that greater integration of the different modes of transport is needed to make mobility more efficient. online information, electronic booking and payment systems that integrate all modes of transport should facilitate and promote multimodal mobility. in the light of these considerations, i have decided to support this proposal by voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the tran committee, i strongly supported and voted in favour of the report by mr koch, which, being an own-initiative report, is intended to invite the european commission to come forward with a legislative proposal in this area. the tourism sector must be considered as one of the driving forces of the european economy and facilitating travel within the old continent is one of the means of promoting our magnificent countries, in addition to the potential benefit in terms of circulation with a careful eye also to respect for the environment. the report focuses on information systems, hoping that multimodal ticketing will be possible in the future: a single ticket for multiple journeys, including different means of transport within the eu. better information sharing will enable european citizens to organise their travels better and move from one place to another without undue difficulty. the report identifies the creation of a single platform at european level as the tool through which all local and regional authorities will be able to enter details of the means of transport under their responsibility. the sharing of information can be a first real step towards improving the mobility of all people transiting our continent.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report, which highlights the importance of information, planning and ticketing services for multimodal travel at union level.
in writing. ‒ the introduction of information, planning and ticketing services for multimodal travel at european level could help to reduce transport sustainability, energy efficiency and traffic problems. at present, given the high fragmentation of the european market, travellers are not informed in a comprehensive and real-time manner about the travel alternatives (air, rail, sea and road) offered by public and private operators. it is therefore important that adequate european financial support is first guaranteed to promote innovation in this area and to address, through new technological solutions, the many difficulties in the provision of these services across the eu. in order to gradually introduce interoperable electronic ticketing systems throughout the union, i think that the starting point should be the establishment of a platform for the exchange of information and good practice involving operators throughout the eu. however, caution should be exercised in setting specific time targets for the installation of intelligent systems for the transmission of real-time information in all local public transport. i have therefore decided to abstain from the final vote, as i have some doubts about the approach taken by the report on this and other points.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the issue of integrated multimodal tickets in europe, which highlights the benefits for users of being able to buy a single ticket for a 'multimodal journey', i.e. combining different modes of transport. the text suggests the introduction of an integrated ticket for travelling across eu borders, allowing for the use of various types of transport, thus increasing the attractiveness of public transport. in addition to making life easier for travellers, the integration of information, travel planning and ticketing services could be a response to the challenges posed by the european transport sector (such as sustainability, multimodality, improving safety in all modes of transport, efficiency, creating quality jobs), benefiting the economy, society and the environment. in this resolution we therefore call on the commission to take the necessary measures to support and improve the existing synergies between different transport and route planning service providers, for example through multi-modal and cross-border travel route planning services. it is hoped that the advantage of being able to use integrated ticketing systems will attract more passengers to public transport.
in writing. ‒ european transport policy must address key issues such as sustainability, cost-effectiveness, energy efficiency and traffic congestion, which is why i believe it is essential to support all information, planning and ticketing services for multimodal travel at union level. integrated information services enable greater mobility, reduce traffic congestion through more efficient use of public transport and alternative means of transport such as bicycle rental or car-sharing. greater support for such technologies must be ensured through existing research programmes and the completion of the digital single market also to consolidate the european industrial base. i fully share the emphasis in this report on the end user and the expected social benefits, the objective of the european institutions is to reduce the environmental impact and increase the safety of transport, including through the provision of information adapted to the needs of all travellers, including disabled people. a final point of note in this report is the emphasis on fair and non-discriminatory market access and a clear definition of end-user rights: consumer protection, data protection and privacy are essential issues for all european citizens.
in writing. ‒ the report we adopted today aims to implement an integrated multimodal transport system in europe by improving information services, planning and the distribution of multimodal tickets. the long-term objective is to enable travellers to choose, book and pay online for a personalised travel solution that is the most sustainable, fast or cost-effective alternative and to travel with a single ticket, regardless of the number of modes of transport used during the journey. the implementation of such information systems is certainly an important step forward for travellers who increasingly use the internet and smartphones. a key step towards a sustainable, citizen-centred transport system for safe, efficient and effective urban mobility.
in writing. ‒ the non-binding resolution adopted today by a large majority in the european parliament is a first step in the right direction to enable european citizens in the near future to buy a single ticket for a 'multimodal journey' using different modes of transport. an integrated ticket for travelling across eu borders that allows for the use of multiple modes of transport could also increase the use of public transport, with clear environmental benefits. i hope that the technological advances of recent years will soon enable this project to be implemented, which is primarily intended to make life easier for travellers.

in writing. ‒ i believe, in the light of the above, that to prevent further loss of life at sea and to apply the principles of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility, more and more predictable financial resources will be needed in the medium and long term. i am voting in favour of this.
in writing. ‒ managing the current massive migratory phenomenon, which is mainly concentrated in the mediterranean sea, with considerable effort on the part of local authorities and the people involved, requires appropriate economic resources to enable the eu to respond in the most appropriate way. i have therefore decided to support with conviction the decision of the european parliament to adopt draft amending budget (dab) no 5/2015. the corrective draft aims to provide the union with additional resources for the management of migration and refugee flows. the reinforcements provided for are mainly intended to support the work of the three agencies directly concerned with these matters: the european agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders (frontex), the european asylum support office (easo) and the european police office (europol) are also involved.
in writing. ‒ a major victory for my country, italy, is the draft amending budget no 5/2015. this proposal for amending the 2015 budget, for which i voted in favour, provides for a strengthening of european resources for the management of migration flows, of which italy has been one of the most affected countries. this reallocation of resources will support the frontex agency, the asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because it is a question of mobilising resources to cover at least part of the costs incurred by those member states which are at the forefront of immigration.
in writing. ‒ through draft amending budget no 5/2015, the three european agencies frontex, easo and europol as well as the asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund will receive extra appropriations for migration management following the increase in the size of refugee flows to the european union. i have decided to vote in favour of this increase in resources, even though it does not correspond to the actual needs and is not sufficient on its own to deal with the current migratory challenges and the worrisome deterioration of the crisis in the mediterranean.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft amending budget on the need to respond to migratory pressures with more resources for 2015. the proposal will provide the three eu agencies responsible for managing migration flows (frontex, easo and europol) and the two specialised european funds (including the asylum and integration fund) with additional resources, amounting to almost eur 70 million, to strengthen their staff and resources. the european parliament called for a significant increase in the 2015 budget for migration management in the wake of the tragic events that have led to thousands of people losing their lives trying to cross the mediterranean. the commission's proposal for an increase was below parliament's wishes to meet the real needs in terms of resources and staff of the agencies involved, but it is nevertheless an important measure in view of the rapid implementation of the european agenda on migration published in may and currently under discussion in the eu institutions. the increase in funding for frontex, which is intended to triple the current allocation for operations triton and poseidon, aimed at preventing migrant deaths at sea in the western and eastern mediterranean, should be emphasised.
in writing. ‒ we have today approved amending budget no 5 presented in may by the european commission to respond to the migratory pressures that the european union, and italy in particular, has been under during these first months of the year. the appropriations provided for amount to some 75 million in commitments and 70 million in payments, obtained through a transfer from the galileo programme. in particular, some 27 million will be earmarked for frontex, which will also see its staff increased, as will the european asylum support office and europol. unfortunately, these additional 70 million euros will certainly not solve the problems of migration, but i can only support this amending budget, which could in any case improve, if only slightly, the current difficult european situation.

in writing. - i vote for it. the 'milk package', which has been in force since october 2012, is the only community initiative aimed at producers to provide them with the necessary tools to face the challenges facing the dairy sector, especially after the end of the quota system. implemented subsequently through the new cap in 2013, it establishes producer organisations and inter-branch organisations in the dairy sector for the first time. although it includes some important instruments (chain structure, production planning, inter-professional cooperation, new contracting, etc.), its uneven application within the eu and in many member states, as well as the difficulty of the relationship between producers, processors and, above all, large-scale distribution, have prevented its proper implementation.

in writing. ‒ the milk package in force since october 2012 has provided producers with a range of tools to meet the challenges facing the dairy sector, and has also strengthened contractual relations and negotiating power. it is also true that the implementation of the measures introduced by this package has not been uniform in all member states, thus undermining the soundness of the sector. the initial objective was to create a profitable, sustainable and competitive sector with response tools that allow fair compensation of milk producers, in particular for small farms which are particularly vulnerable to changes in income and risks due to high capital costs, perishability of production, price volatility and energy and factor costs. unfortunately, the abolition of milk quotas on 31 march has begun to create a solution of instability to the benefit of the large farms. in my view, it is necessary to confirm the previous decisions on milk quotas and to provide for new financing opportunities, also with the help of the eib, in order to encourage investment and modernisation of farms and to enable young producers to grow their business.

in writing. ‒ in 2003, with the mid-term review of the cap, the eu member states agreed to end the milk quota system as from 31 march 2015. the milk package approved in the last legislature has proved inadequate in providing milk producers with the necessary tools to meet the new challenges facing the sector. for these reasons i voted in favour of this proposal which calls on the european commission to put in place measures to better manage the crisis facing milk producers.
in writing. ‒ the context in which this report is set is that of changes and prospects in the dairy sector, especially after the mid-term reform of the cap, the common agricultural policy, in 2003 which provided for the definitive end of the milk quota system as from march 2015. for italian producers this was a double-edged sword: on the one hand, those who were forced to limit their production were no longer forced to do so, and on the other hand, the abolition of quotas would lead to an inevitable increase in supply (especially from the best-equipped member states), with a consequent drastic fall in prices. in addition to the quota issue, the text touches on other important points for the dairy sector, but it leaves out others that are essential for us, such as, for example, the question of powdered milk and dairy products derived from it, which is not even mentioned, and the whole of the pdo and pgi talk which, although mentioned, never refers to the suffering that these products are facing because of a very competitive and sometimes unfair foreign market. so, although the text itself does not present any particular problem, i felt i had to abstain, given the absence of passages that could have made it a more courageous text.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the external impact of eu trade and investment policy on public-private initiatives in third countries. the report focuses on public-private partnerships (ppps), an important tool for economic growth and job creation both within and outside the european single market, for which there is currently no internationally recognised definition or global regulatory framework. the report therefore calls on the commission to promote an internationally recognised definition of public-private partnership, as a long-term relationship between public promoter and private investors for the provision of quality and accessible public services and infrastructure. the commission must ensure that european smes operating abroad can compete on the same terms as foreign national firms, by means of clear regulations and easy access to information on tender criteria and by eliminating all discriminatory and unjustified trade barriers in public procurement, services or investment.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the commission's own-initiative report because i believe that the positive and negative aspects of public-private partnerships (ppps) are fairly and comprehensively highlighted. ppp means a long-term working relationship between the public authority and a private partner to finalise a project in the public interest. this type of cooperation brings benefits to both parties as it allows for greater efficiency and timeliness, better value for money, new job opportunities for union citizens and new resources for private enterprises. benefits that are enhanced by the possibility of sharing the risks. so, considering that the interaction between the public and private sectors is an innovative solution that brings benefits to the economy as a whole and that these benefits will be distributed to citizens, consumers and private businesses, i believe that it is constructive to support sustainable growth also through such investments in third countries as they could represent a first step towards a new global economic growth. however, since there is still confusion about an internationally recognised definition of ppps, i think it is the commission's duty to try to define this type of practice better.

in writing. ‒ this is an initiative report by the inta commission on public-private partnerships (ppps), i.e. long-term contracts between the public authority and a private partner, under which the private sector finances a public service using its own resources and sharing the joint risks. the partnership is therefore a business relationship between two parties, one public and one private, to implement and finalise a project that responds to a public interest. as ppps are a tool for economic growth, innovation, competitiveness and job creation, both in the single market and beyond, and play a strategic role in the modernisation of infrastructure, particularly energy, water, road and digital infrastructure, i have decided to vote in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ public-private partnerships (ppps) are long-term agreements between the government and a private partner in which the private partner provides and finances public services with its own capital and shares the associated risks. ppps therefore refer to commercial relations between a private sector company and a government body with the aim of completing a project that will serve public users. the ppp can be used to finance a range of initiatives such as major infrastructure such as roads, ports and prisons, which would otherwise have difficulty in obtaining the resources needed to implement them. as regards the impact on third countries, i am convinced that increased participation by european businesses in major international projects, through ppps, would lead to considerable benefits both in terms of job creation and economic growth throughout the eu and in the host countries. the resolution urges the eu institutions to take the necessary measures to promote the participation of european enterprises, in particular smes, in ppp projects. for all these reasons i thought it appropriate to support this proposal.
