in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the melo report which analyses the development of the fruit and vegetable sector after the 2007 reform. the fruit and vegetable sector is of fundamental importance for the eu and our territories: it represents 18% of the total value of european agricultural production, amounting to over eur 50 billion. for these reasons i believe that the commission should remove the existing bureaucratic obstacles which prevent effective aggregation of the producer organizations of the member states and which would lead to a maximisation of the operational management of this sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that public-private partnerships are an innovative solution to support the growth of european enterprises and therefore i believe that the trade agreements concluded by the union with third countries should contain precise provisions in this respect, which do not discriminate against our companies.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the measure. in the eu, the fruit and vegetable sector accounts for 18% of the total value of agricultural production, uses only 3% of the cultivated area and is worth over €50 billion. in this sector too, the issue of aggregating supply and organising the supply chain is very important for an adequate presence on the market. producer organisations (po) and their associations (pa) can be a useful instrument in this respect under community rules, encouraged by the recent reform of the cap, but are used in the fruit and vegetable sector only in those geographical areas where there is a more developed farmer figure, more oriented towards the market for its products (northern italy is an example). the rate of organisation among producers thus remains on average low and, in some member states, considerably below the eu average. the report lists a number of useful calls to the commission to increase aggregation between producers and to remove the main obstacles (many of them bureaucratic) to the operational management of the op.
in writing. ‒ the importance of the eu fruit and vegetable sector is undeniable, both in terms of added value and employment. the health benefits of fruit and vegetables for the public should not be overlooked. however, this sector is characterized by frequent market crises, as even small surpluses of production can cause drastic price falls. in addition, serious crises such as the one caused by the e. coli bacterium or the current one, generated by the russian embargo, have shown the vulnerability of the sector. that is why, as the report we voted on shows, the commission should consider the introduction of new crisis management instruments, which are currently underused and underperforming. the community support measures should be extended until the normal market situation has been fully restored, also in relation to the russian embargo: producers should not be charged for the cost of crises caused by causes external to the agricultural sector. finally, the commission should intensify its efforts to combat unfair trading practices in the food chain, which reduce incomes and threaten the efficiency of the sector, in order to guarantee a decent income to fruit and vegetable producers, a prerequisite for securing the future of the profession and attracting a young workforce.
in writing. ‒ over the past 20 years, the cap has reduced the regulation of agricultural markets, particularly in the fruit and vegetable sector, allowing market forces to steer production at the expense of distributors, processors and short-chain operators. the 2007 reform strengthens the role of producer organisations (po) and associations of producer organisations and sets the funding limits at 4.1% of the value of the marketed production of po. the report by mr nuno melo highlights the importance of ensuring legal certainty by simplifying the rules applicable to fruit and vegetables and the procedures for establishing and recognising the various op at national level. it also called for a focus on human capital and the selection of qualified managers who could compete in competitive international markets, such as those of third countries with which the eu has trade agreements, and where unfair practices, which ops are already forced to face at national level, are accentuated. the committee calls for greater transparency and democratic control over the allocation of community funds, so as to increase mutual trust between the operational programmes and combat unfair practices, which are frequent in the large-scale distribution of fruit and vegetables. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the fruit and vegetables sector after the 2007 reform. the sector has been liberalised by reducing market regulation, by abandoning instruments such as export refunds or the fixing of minimum prices for certain products, which processing undertakings were required to pay to farmers. alongside this process of liberalisation, the eu has confirmed and strengthened the role of producer organisations (po) and associations of producer organisations (aops) with the aim of enabling farmers to act in their own interests, for example by collectively selling their products or by adding value through farm conversion. the increase in the rate of organisation in almost all member states in recent years indicates that the union's policy of supporting the creation and development of po has been effective. the report therefore calls for incentives and encouragement for the creation of po and poa in the eu member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the fruit and vegetables sector because the reform implemented in 2007 strengthened the role of producer organisations and associations of producer organisations with tangible results. the rate of organisation has increased, with a share of fruit and vegetables marketed within the eu between producer organisations and associations of producer organisations reaching 43%. the public consultation carried out by the commission highlighted that the majority of respondents were in favour of continuing the scheme launched in 2007, albeit with some corrective measures. the regions where producers have reported higher productivity and competitiveness rates are those where the rate of production organisation is higher, but this is still not widespread among producers. for this reason, it is necessary to continue to encourage the creation of organizations and associations and their merger, by simplifying the regime applicable to the fruit and vegetable sector and by allocating funds to encourage the improvement of the management capacity of organizations. the population employed in agriculture is also ageing and it is of paramount importance to give a new impetus and appeal to a fundamental activity such as agriculture.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mr melo's report because i agree with the need to strengthen the incentives to encourage the creation of pos and ppas and their mergers. the purpose of producer organisations, as well as associations, is to enable farmers to defend their interests, for example by selling their products or by adding value by becoming a holding. it is also important to improve the human capital of the op by investing in it to make the agri-food sector competitive and international, as well as to protect farmers from unfair commercial practices of the large retailers.
in writing. ‒ with the 2007 reform of the fruit and vegetables sector, the commission wanted to strengthen the role of producer organisations (po) by providing them with a wide range of tools to prevent and manage market crises and by creating incentives to encourage their merger with associations of po (poa) for greater transnational cooperation in the sector. nevertheless, in order to further make the po an attractive instrument, it is still necessary to reduce the excessive complexity and lack of legal certainty that characterise the current regime for fruit and vegetables. i voted in favour of this report to call on the european commission to combat unfair trading practices in the supply chain which affect the performance of producers, reduce their incomes and threaten the efficiency and sustainability of the sector and to strengthen incentives to encourage the creation of po and ppas and mergers between them.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of the report on the fruit and vegetables sector, which represents 18% of the total value of agricultural production and uses only 3% of the cultivated area, with a value of over eur 50 billion.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report on the state of the fruit and vegetable sector after the 2007 reform. the fruit and vegetable sector provides european citizens with fresh, high-quality products, but in recent years it has been in a sharp recession, as evidenced by the 6% decrease in the area under cultivation. despite the importance of the sector for the health of its citizens and the direct and indirect employment it provides, the eu continues to import because production is insufficient, due to high costs and the russian embargo has made the situation worse. most producers are smes, unable to cope with the contracting power of large retailers and suffering from ridiculous profit margins. i therefore share the call for the promotion of producer organisations and associations of producer groups, including at cross-border level. the rate of organization is still too low, with large differences between the various member states. they should be encouraged, as they increase the competitiveness and innovation of the sector, encourage youth initiative and strengthen the negotiating power of producers. the call for policies to shorten the supply chain and promote direct sales to the territories, as well as the call for the creation of stable instruments for crisis management such as the russian embargo, are also welcome.

first vice-president of the commission.– mr president, let me just react to a number of comments that have been made. first of all, i have to say that there is broad support for working closely together on a commission work programme that is targeted and, of course, that chooses political priorities after a debate. political priorities are something you debate, and you look for majorities to get them, clearly. at the same time i also see the willingness in this institution, just as much as i know it exists in the council and in the commission, to reach an interinstitutional agreement – hopefully before the end of this year – on better law-making. of course, better law-making is not the answer to all our problems: better law-making will not solve the crisis in greece; better law—making is not the way to tackle putin. i accept all these points. but better law-making is a way of trying to answer the plea of an endless number of smes across europe which are telling me whenever i go to a member state: ‘please help us cut red tape; please help us create more clarity; please help us understand that it is possible to create clear legislation, not legislation where member states then have endless possibilities of gold plating so that we are completely lost.’ these are things that are important. they are important to smes; therefore, they are important to employment and to growth. yes, of course this is not earth—shattering – this is not going to change the nature of europe. but it is going to make a difference for hundreds of thousands of people who are trying, day by day, to work very hard to create a living for themselves, their families and the people who work for them. therefore, this is an important thing for me. the way we create legislation is important to hundreds of millions of europeans. even if they do not know it is important to them, it still is, because the outcome is something they have to deal with. and let me be very clear on impact assessment. let me be very clear on more scrutiny. this does not lead to taking away the power of politicians. we do not change that. it leads to better-informed politicians. i do not know what would be the problem with better-informed politicians. better scrutiny and better impact assessment means that the politicians, when they decide, are better informed about what they can decide. i would say to mr eickhout: do not turn things around. do not use the argument that ‘the politicians should be in charge’ to dismiss impact assessment and to dismiss scrutiny. that would be changing the argument you are using against me completely around. both are wrong. the commission does not want to use impact assessment and scrutiny to disempower politicians. on the contrary, we want to help politicians to be better informed. we see across our member states that sometimes scrutiny or analysis leads to a conclusion, and the experts then say this means that this measure is going to be more costly for this or that reason. then parliaments still decide, but we think that this cost is justified for bigger political goals, and therefore we do it anyway. but at least people know what you decide, and i think there is nothing wrong with that. as regards more transparency: i am all for it. but one of the reasons why we – the two institutions – need more transparency is also to show our customers, i.e. the recipients of our legislation, where we are responsible – parliament and commission – and where the member state is responsible. there is still a tremendous amount of gold-plating going on. and again here, member states have the full right to do that. if they want to create stricter legislation, it is entirely up to them – they have the full right to do it. but then do not blame europe for it. be honest about it, be transparent about it. i think the proposals we will discuss in our interinstitutional agreement will help us become more transparent. this also applies – and i say this clearly to mr szájer as well – to delegated acts and implementing acts. there, i hope we can reach an agreement which will create more transparency. as far as the commission is concerned, we will put all draft delegated acts on the internet for a period of four weeks, so that everybody in the outside world can see what we are proposing. for the implementing act it is slightly more difficult, because sometimes – like when you change the price of a product – you cannot give that over for public debate for a long period of time. everyone will understand that. but we will try to put the maximum amount of primary and secondary legislation up for public scrutiny, so that everybody knows what we are doing. hopefully, then, we will avoid another ‘olive oil can’ disaster or something like that. it might help by putting it in the public sphere. of course, we will need to act on a number of things that are very important, and migration is one of them. i am sure tomorrow, when the debates are held on the results of the european council, president juncker will want to come back to this. but the commission sticks to its proposals. we believe, also after debate with your parliament, that we are on the right track with these proposals. if you ask me what the difference between legal and illegal migration is, clearly somebody who is abusing the asylum system because they want a better life in europe is an example of illegal migration. asylum policy should be for people who flee because they fear for their lives. i think we have less support in europe for asylum policy, because many of our citizens know that the system is being abused and because we are not able, if we discover people abusing the system, to make sure they return to the countries they came from. if we want a credible migration and asylum policy, we have to make sure that the rules are actually applied, so that people who deserve asylum get asylum – unfortunately too often the system fails them – and that people who do not deserve asylum are sent back to where they come from, and also that we have agreements with third countries to do that. but we also need – and this is simple demographics – possibilities for the european union to have traditional, legal forms of migration. there needs to be a possibility for people to apply for a visa, at an embassy in the country where they live, to come and live and work in europe. they should not be at the mercy of smugglers, nor should they run the risk of drowning in the mediterranean, but rather they should have a fair chance – if europe needs people like them – to apply and then come to europe. in that sense, i believe legal migration is also part of the solution. let me conclude by saying that for me, the important thing here is that our two institutions work closely together, because i do not think anybody disputes our goal that we should perform better in delivering results for our citizens. sometimes these are huge – big earth-shattering results – but very often they are small results. but a number of small results will create more growth, more jobs, better social protection and a better future for hundreds of thousands of young europeans who are still unemployed today. i think that that is a goal worth fighting for.
the agenda includes the report by sergio gaetano cofferati, on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2007/36/ec as regards the encouragement of long-term shareholder engagement and directive 2013/34/eu as regards certain elements of the report on corporate governance (com (2014) 0213 - c7-0147/2014 - 2014/0121 (cod)) (a8-0158/2015)
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking the colleagues who have contributed to the drafting of this report. they are due thanks and not rituals, because, as they know firsthand, the journey has been very long and difficult. the vote was postponed for the first time in committee. then, after the committee had voted, it was sent back to the chamber following a decision by the conference of presidents. the vote scheduled for june in the house has therefore been postponed to july and we shall finally be able to vote tomorrow. we have bought time, but i think it was a wise choice that allowed us to look deeper into the merits of complex and controversial issues, on which there were, quite legitimately, divergent opinions. so thanks to the shadow rapporteurs of the juri committee, thanks to olle ludvigsson, who was the rapporteur of the econ committee, and to his colleagues who acted as shadow rapporteurs. but before i quickly get to the content of the directive, i would like to say something to the commission. i consider this directive to be a piece of a larger mosaic, one which should correctly and effectively define the profile of the governance of the european enterprise of the future. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval. we're working in the direction he pointed out. it is hard work, but it is very positive. today we are dealing with the shareholders, then we will have to move on to the stakeholders to give the company the social dimension that the then president referred to, or rather built with his proposal. i therefore expect the commission to take further initiatives of this kind in this direction. in the meantime, as i said, we have managed to define the long-term orientation of the companies and their shareholders and, above all, to increase transparency on key elements of the management of the company, its corporate governance. we have agreed and it is very important that companies can identify their shareholders; i am, of course, talking about publicly traded companies. measures to improve shareholders' voting rights are also envisaged: it is not only an element of democracy but also an element of efficiency in the management of any enterprise. the transmission of information along the chain of intermediaries will also make the work of shareholders more effective and also more aware. then there are measures which, if properly applied, can increase the transparency of the relationship between institutional investors, asset managers and companies, so that the commitment policy defines for companies their return, in the short term but especially in the long term, thus avoiding the risk of being used simply for financial purposes. there are also measures that will increase the transparency of the activity of proxy advisors, an important function in any system. now, we have thereby confirmed the transparency requirements that were envisaged by the commission. and that, i believe, is an effective and conscious choice. the same applies to transactions for related parties, which must be subject to controls which will be differentiated according to the legislative system of each member state of the union. the changes which parliament is proposing will therefore make it possible to take account of these national differences without these becoming a factor in calling into question the unity of european policies. there is also the issue of directors' remuneration, which has been widely discussed. we were very much in agreement on this subject, but there were differences of opinion on how to give it the right substance. we have found the solution to the case and the shareholders will vote but their vote may be binding or advisory, depending on the decisions taken by each country. and last but not least, the country-by-country reporting. the fight against tax evasion can and must be done through the use of new instruments: the annual reporting of publicly traded companies is one of them. the kaili report had already suggested this: we have used this route, that of the shareholder directive, as the first legislative appointment to introduce a hypothesis of an immediate revision of the accounting directive. i would like to thank again all those who have contributed to this report and i shall of course be very interested in your comments.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today the fight against tax evasion and avoidance is finally at the heart of the european debate and is becoming a priority. but in an age when huge flows of capital can be moved easily from one part of the world to the other with the click of a mouse, it is clear that these are global challenges and that to overcome them we need global tools of confrontation and global solutions, to re-establish a very simple principle: taxes are paid where profits are generated. in this european year of development, we will make decisions that shape the world we leave to future generations: the new sustainable development goals, the climate conference and, in a few days' time, the third international conference on financing for development in addis ababa. these ambitious objectives will only be achieved if we ensure adequate financing through official development assistance but also through a more effective mobilisation of national resources. and that is where taxation and the fight against tax evasion and avoidance become crucial. estimates are cautious, but it is estimated that illicit financial flows out of developing countries amount to as much as a trillion dollars a year. a shocking fact: almost ten times the total of development aid; resources withheld from services to citizens. the obstacles facing developing countries in combating tax evasion and avoidance are numerous. and they themselves tend to grant incentives and exemptions in a ruthless tax competition which is harmful to them. with this report we are asking the commission to come up with a real action plan to support developing countries in creating more robust and fairer tax systems. we therefore call for increased support for the developing countries, by providing financial and technical assistance, which is still insufficient. we call for the transformation of the un tax committee into a genuine intergovernmental body with additional resources to finally ensure that developing countries participate on an equal footing in the reform of the global tax system. we call for support for international initiatives for the reform of the global tax system, such as the beps process promoted by the oecd; but we must take greater account of the needs of developing countries. two instruments are of particular importance: we call for the adoption of the country by country reporting standard for multinational companies in all sectors, including the mining sector, and for complete information to be made available to all countries and made public. it is time for the commission to make a proposal to that effect. i would be surprised if tomorrow someone voted against what we have already unanimously approved in committee. in addition, when automatic exchange of information is applied, a transition period should be provided for countries that have not yet fully developed the necessary capacity to collect and share all the required information. we also call for transparency on the actual ownership of companies, trusts and similar institutions. there is the longstanding problem of tax treaties between developed and developing countries, which do not ensure the equitable distribution of tax rights between the country of residence and the country of source. the model developed under the auspices of the un provides a more balanced approach. we also call for the impact assessments of european tax policies on developing countries to be carried out in order to strengthen policy coherence for development and for a definition of tax havens at international level by 2015 with a blacklist and sanctions. i was surprised that someone wanted a separate vote, i thought we all agreed here that this problem must be taken seriously. and last but not least, let's pay special attention to gender issues: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem, including the introduction of a new system of social security for women. i thank all the shadow rapporteurs for their spirit of cooperation and also the secretariat and my office for their support. i hope that tomorrow this report will be adopted by the largest possible majority, so that the voice of this parliament can be heard before addis ababa and so that we can show that we are at the forefront of the fight against global flight and avoidance, and that we can have a development agenda that is truly ambitious and capable of tackling the root causes of poverty and inequality.

community. yemen occupies a strategic position along the gulf of aden and the red sea, at the crossroads of the horn of africa and the middle east, on the route connecting the mediterranean to the al-qaeda in the arabian peninsula, already rooted in somalia, and more recently also daesh, are benefiting from the vacuum of state authority in the country to regroup and regain strength. this is a threat for all countries in the region. the regional powers need to choose cooperation and common security issues. the only alternative to a more cooperative regional order is chaos. saturday, 4 july marked the 100th day since the exile of president hadi and the launch of the saudi-led coalition airstrikes against the continuing advance of houthi and pro-saleh forces in yemen. the country is facing a humanitarian catastrophe, with more than 3 000 yemenis killed, over 14 000 injured, and 21 million people, or 80% of the total population, in need of humanitarian assistance, and a major food crisis about to unfold. just to give you a comparison: there are now more people in need in yemen than in the entire sahel region. the eu’s position is clear, as portrayed in the foreign affairs council conclusions of april 2015. we have also repeatedly – most recently in a joint statement by the high representative/vice-president and commissioner stylianides last friday – made the case that there is no other way out of the current crisis than through an inclusive political process under un stewardship favouring a genuine and constructive dialogue among the different parties. the continuing advance of the houthis and forces loyal to ex-president saleh, in contravention of un security council resolutions, is clearly unacceptable. but only a broad political consensus based on the parameters set by un security council resolution 2216 can provide a sustainable solution to the crisis, tackle the threat of terrorist groups and prevent further regional instability. any long-term solution should address the underlying causes of instability, which are deeply rooted in local historical and socio-economic power structures. the eu fully supports the efforts of the un special envoy, ismail ould cheikh ahmed, to recreate trust amongst the parties for a meaningful political deal. the consultations held in geneva from 15 to 20 june could be a first step towards a return to an inclusive political process. we see a strong case for the gradual approach followed by the special envoy, first setting the conditions for a long pause in hostilities, leading to a sustainable ceasefire, coupled with a monitored withdrawal from key cities by the warring forces. the eu has been reaching out to all the parties in yemen, including the houthis. we believe it is critical for all the actors in the conflict to set a realistic path to peace in line with the parameters set by un security council resolution 2216. our message to all parties is clear: engage in the un-led dialogue process, with no preconditions, in good faith. all their legitimate concerns will be duly taken into consideration in a broad political settlement. the humanitarian impact of the ongoing fighting, bombardments and disruption of essential services on the civilian population, in particular on children, is reaching alarming proportions and exacerbating an already dire humanitarian situation. the targeting of civilian populations and infrastructures, including un warehouses or hospitals, is also clearly unacceptable. in this volatile environment it is all the more crucial that humanitarian assistance reaches the people of yemen. the european union has been steadfast in its support of the un efforts towards a lasting, predictable and sustainable humanitarian ceasefire. such a pause should allow the urgent delivery of humanitarian assistance and essential supplies, including fuel, food and basic commodities, according to the principles of impartiality, neutrality and independence. it is essential, to this end, that access to yemen for commercial shipping be further eased and that measures taken to implement un security council resolution 2216 be proportional and predictable. a un-led inspection mechanism should be urgently rolled out to enable faster and more streamlined clearance procedures for ships bound for yemen. in parallel we are calling on all parties to ensure respect for international humanitarian law and international human rights law, in particular by protecting civilians. everyone should refrain from direct targeting of civilian infrastructure, notably medical facilities and water systems, and from using civilian buildings for military purposes. it is also of the utmost importance that all parties ensure the safety and security of medical personnel and relief workers and facilitate the passage of aid convoys and ambulances to the most affected populations without discrimination. the eu humanitarian aid office – echo – has already mobilised eur 25 million in humanitarian assistance for yemen to respond to the most urgent needs. we are also engaged in diplomatic efforts to ensure unrestricted access to humanitarian workers and aid relief so that vital assistance can be immediately delivered. more needs to be done, but international assistance will remain a drop in the ocean if commercial shipping cannot resume and bring the 80% of goods that yemen imported before the conflicts and if yemini warring factions continue to hamper the delivery of aid. ultimately, the solution to this crisis has to be a political one, and every day that passes further entrenches polarisations and sees the risk of a protracted conflict with sectarian undertones grow. the eu will remain committed to playing its full role in supporting the un and in reaching out to the parties and to regional players to set a swift path for peace. thank you for your attention and i look forward to hearing your views on that.

the committee on budgets madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i am here today in place of mrs herranz garcía, who cannot be in the chamber and whom i thank for her work on this dossier. the report concerns the european commission's proposal for the recasting of three regulations: no 3954 of 1987 setting maximum permitted levels of contamination of food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other case of radioactive emergency; regulation no 944 of 1989 laying down maximum permitted levels of contamination of secondary foodstuffs following a nuclear accident or other emergency and regulation no 770 of 1990, which also lays down maximum permitted levels in contaminated feedingstuffs following nuclear accidents or in the event of a radiation emergency. we believe it is important that the european union has up-to-date legal instruments, with quick decision-making procedures adapted to all circumstances, to deal with situations such as those experienced after the chernobyl or fukushima accidents. the legal basis of the 2010 proposal required only the consultation of the european parliament: the new proposal under consideration today introduces some new elements which establish a clearer link with european food safety legislation. in its explanatory memorandum, the commission acknowledges that, taking into account the evolution of primary community law on food safety and the need to ensure the consistency of all legislative measures concerning the conditions for importing food and feed from third countries affected by a nuclear accident or radiological emergency, the measures that have been developed in the post-chernobyl context will need to be aligned with the regime of implementing powers and procedures laid down in this regulation. this could also involve, if necessary, a change in the legal basis. the rapporteur, therefore mrs herranz, proposes an amendment to the legal basis of the regulation which gives parliament the power of codecision. food safety is the ultimate objective of the european commission's proposal and the regulation must reflect the evolution of community law, especially since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the proposal sets out in its annexes the maximum permissible levels in the event of a radioactive accident or emergency, which were confirmed in 2012 by a group of experts established under the euratom treaty of the commission. in the event of a radioactive accident or emergency, the commission shall adopt an implementing act to make the maximum permitted levels of radioactive residues in food applicable. the commission will therefore have a great deal of flexibility to adapt, if necessary, the values indicated in the annexes if circumstances so require. the new comitology means that for the first time the commission will be assisted by the section of the standing committee on plants, animals, food and feed dealing with radioactive contamination. the author of the draft report considers that the use of implementing acts to deal with critical situations arising from a nuclear accident is the most appropriate way of acting quickly. where the urgency of action is essential to ensure the safety of consumers, the commission shall provide for a specific emergency procedure. as regards the implementing acts adopted in the event of an accident, the draft report provides for the possibility of reviewing them as often as necessary to reflect the evolution of contamination. the commission's proposal should be supplemented by the introduction of certain procedures on the general principles of food law, including the introduction of an early warning system to enable information to be exchanged quickly. in the light of the foregoing, i naturally ask that the report by mrs herranz garcía be supported.
member of the commission. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. i am here today on behalf of my colleague and friend, commissioner arias cañete, who cannot be in strasbourg for reasons of urgency, because he is attending the annual acer conference in ljubljana instead of strasbourg. i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs esther herranz garcía, and your colleague, mr giovanni la via, for a positive, comprehensive, informed and balanced report. the aim of today's proposal is to update or adapt the existing regulation on the establishment of maximum levels of radioactivity in food and feed in the event of a nuclear accident or radiological emergency. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of nuclear installations is not compromised. it is therefore important that clear and efficient procedures are established and developed at eu level to set maximum levels of radioactivity in food and feed for the european market in the event of a nuclear accident. the procedures must be consistent with the new rules governing the exercise of implementing powers by the commission. but they must also allow the commission to react quickly when it is informed that maximum levels in food and feed may have been reached or even exceeded. the council already set these maximum levels after the chernobyl accident. but they have now been reviewed by scientific experts on several occasions. in the interest of maximum protection for the eu population, the commission has proposed a revision of the existing legislation to consolidate the existing regulations, to adopt the new committee procedure to ensure that maximum levels are set in accordance with the lisbon treaty and to introduce more flexible procedures to allow targeted responses to all nuclear accidents or radiological emergencies. the herranz garcía report sets out constructive changes aimed at providing greater flexibility if, in the interests of targeted responses to nuclear accidents, lower limits than those set in the present regulation have to be applied. in the light of the experience of the fukushima accident, this aspect has been raised and discussed during the negotiations in the council. the commission also considers that the proposal should clarify the relationship between the proposed euratom regulation and the existing food safety legislation on the basis of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the commission can support some, but not all, aspects of the amendments. firstly, we cannot support the proposed change in the legal basis. the commission proposal is based on the euratom treaty as a lex specialis. the euratom treaty is the legal basis for all acts which the proposed regulation is intended to repeal. the court of justice of the european union recently delivered its judgment on the drinking water directive, confirming our legal view that article 31 of the euratom treaty is the correct and only legal basis. we cannot accept another legal basis, namely the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which replaces the euratom treaty. the request for a report to the european parliament on the review of the maximum levels of radioactivity, in order to take due account of the current scientific progress made in the world, should be answered as follows: this review of basic standards is indeed a common practice. once the international panel of scientific experts the international commission on radiological protection has produced a new list of dose coefficients for ingestion in approximately three to five years , the commission will request the expert group for an opinion on the validity of the currently valid maximum values and, on the basis of this opinion, decide whether to revise the regulation. we'll be glad to get back to you on that. as regards the proposal to include tritium and c14 in the list of radionuclides, the group of experts has already stated that the maximum levels for these nuclides may be ten times higher than for caesium-137, for example. furthermore, it is not usually practical to take account of this type of contamination. however, if an event should actually occur, for example with tritium in a fusion reactor, the commission would set maximum levels ad hoc by means of an implementing regulation following the committee procedure. we will also take care of that. your report says that the maximum levels should be set in such a way as to protect the most vulnerable groups of the population - children, people working in agriculture. i would point out that the commission proposal specifically provides for maximum levels for children. however, we believe that maximum levels of radioactivity should be set for the population in the eu as a whole. it would be unwise to regulate the eu food market on the basis of the situation of a minority of people who, for example, are subsistence farmers. for these groups of persons, the commission may adopt, on the basis of the applicable law, specific recommendations addressed to the member states concerned, as it did after the chernobyl accident, for persons intending to consume large quantities of wild mushrooms and berries or game in certain regions particularly affected by the continuing contamination with radioactive caesium. overall, we thank you for your expert report. he supports our work and we are happy to continue the steps we have taken.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i, as the shadow rapporteur on the own-initiative report, have already had the opportunity to discuss with my colleagues the potential benefits of this fund. there is a small problem, however, which we should try to draw attention to, because at the moment these funds are decided within a bureau whose composition does not reflect the forces present in this parliament. we therefore asked in an amendment that the board which decides on the specific fund in question should be sympathetic to all groups. the gue/ngl, efdd and the new enf groups are currently missing. i believe that if we want to demonstrate how democracy is done, we should first of all respect the democratic composition of parliament, otherwise we are making a fool of ourselves. i therefore expect that this amendment will be supported, because our support for it depends on it, but also on the credibility of this fund, which will otherwise be severely criticised by us.
mr president, i voted for this material, i supported, let us say, the mandates given by the european parliament to the commission. i am convinced that any free trade agreement always contributes to the economic prosperity of the partners who conclude it. the debate that was held here, and which was very informative, and i listened to it very carefully, was unfortunately burdened with many ideological clichés and was not always about the concrete, substantive aspects of the negotiations. i am glad that the material finally got through, that the european parliament supported the ttip resolution. i will wait for the commission to negotiate the final version of this treaty and i am prepared to support it. of course, the detail is important to me, i'll wait for the specific details. there are also concerns in my region, for example in the plzeň region, about the us gold miners in šumava, so all these details need to be discussed further.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted against the lange resolution with conviction for a fundamental reason called democracy. yesterday we heard a lesson in democracy from alexis tsipras, from manolis glezos on the importance of respecting popular sovereignty at european and national level. the ttip is the negation of all that. it is a trojan horse of the multinationals, through mechanisms such as regulatory cooperation or the new isds formula, invented by the schulz-malmström compromise. above all, the resolution adopted yesterday ignores the concerns raised by activists and researchers on the precautionary principle, on the rights and jobs issue, on the health and agri-food production issue. there are many reasons for saying "oxi" to ttip. it is no coincidence that i am the first to sign an amendment, which has unfortunately been rejected, calling for the suspension of the negotiations. i think that the european parliament made a serious mistake yesterday.
mr president, first of all, a little clarity. we did not approve ttip yesterday. parliament yesterday delivered to the european commission its recommendations for the continuation of negotiations with the united states. if the commission does not respect the priorities we have clearly stated, we are prepared to vote against the agreement. i believe that the report we have voted on responds in a timely manner to the concerns of the european citizens, which i consider to be absolutely legitimate in view of the lack of transparency with which the negotiations have started. we have made it clear that the agreement must lead to greater protection of geographical indications, improve access for our agri-food products to the american market, not undermine european social and environmental standards and ensure a high level of consumer protection. as regards isds, the compromise reached remains too ambiguous, failing to provide for a firm rejection of the inclusion of isds mechanisms in ttip, which could give foreign investors greater procedural rights than domestic investors and jeopardise the sovereign rights of the european union, its member states and regional and local authorities, by referring to international arbitration tribunals which are often not transparent.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe it is important for the european union to try to conclude a good trade agreement with the united states, which is our main economic partner, which can bring immense benefits to all parties involved. i am also convinced that the compromise presented by president schulz on the isds issue is a solution that will allow the problems related to this subject to be resolved.
in writing. ‒ any criticism of ultra-liberal single-mindedness cannot be accused of being populist. the debate on the ttip negotiations has developed in society and has raised many concerns, not only among ngos, trade unions, farmers, producers and various trade associations, but also among ordinary citizens. and we have a duty to listen and to give voice to these demands. as an s&d group we have achieved important results in economic, social and environmental terms, but not the most important: a clear no to the isds. that is why i voted no.
in writing. ‒ i am voting against the inta committee's own-initiative report, which contains suggestions to the european commission for the conduct of the ongoing negotiations with the usa. the opposition of the northern league to ttip is well known. we are particularly dissatisfied with a number of issues, such as the risks to the agricultural and agri-food sector and the tough competition with far more dynamic and less taxed us companies. the text of the report also contains some interesting points. it is not a document devoid of content, but it certainly reflects a positive approach to ttip. clearly we cannot approve a report which says little about the need for greater recognition and respect for our geographical indications in the usa (where there is a system based on trademarks that usurp our know-how). the report uses many paragraphs on a subject that is tearing up the claims, the isds mechanism. this is undoubtedly an important aspect, but the search for a compromise at all costs on isds by the main political groups has caused attention to be diverted from other issues of concern to the lega nord, which is a priority.
in writing. ‒ ttip, as designed so far, will have the effect of putting the health of citizens, safety standards and the social and employment systems of all europeans at serious risk. the fact that the isds dispute settlement system is maintained will also remove any obstacle to the overpowering power of multinational companies, which will be able to assert their interests also in decisions taken by states. i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) are characterised by a number of factors which, taken together, make the subject highly controversial. the high technical complexity, the difficulty of predicting the real effects of an agreement, the limited transparency in the forms and content of the negotiations, the strong ideological implications of the subject, these and other factors explain the contradictions and lead to following the negotiations with great attention and at the same time great caution. as parliament will be called upon to approve or reject the final text of the agreement 'as a whole' in the coming years, it is appropriate at this stage, rather than formulating overall assessments of ttip and/or the negotiations that have taken place, to seek to influence the course of future negotiations to the greatest possible extent, with a view to the full protection of the fundamental rights and principles of the union. the effective realisation of a fair and inclusive social model centred on people and work rather than capital and profit is a priority for the union at this historic juncture, and ttip will only be acceptable if and to the extent that it is functional to that objective. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report containing the european parliament's recommendations to the commission on the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip). the report highlights: (1) the strategic importance of such an agreement in eu-us relations; (2) the protection and safeguarding of investments; (3) the establishment of a democratic and transparent isds mechanism for the settlement of investment disputes between investors and states; (4) the inclusion in ttip of specific chapters on energy, smes and intellectual property; and (5) the recognition and strong legal protection of geographical indications. the report also calls on the negotiators to ensure that future negotiations are transparent in order to reach an ambitious and transparent agreement.
in writing. ‒ by approving this text, we are sending guidelines to the commission to continue the negotiations. i am convinced that in an increasingly globalised world, only through specific rules can smes, their activities and their commercial expansion be protected. the eu needs such an agreement because it will be a powerful engine for its reindustrialisation: we are waiting for a proposal that will protect the interests of businessmen, consumers, families and the environment. the interconnection between markets is increasingly marked, up to 40% of industrial products are obtained from imported basic products, and this agreement can become a useful instrument in creating shared standards and ensuring an anti-dumping policy so that free competition is implemented on equal terms. this does not mean that the high principles and values which i personally believe in, such as food safety, health, the social model, the environment and data protection, are not subject to compromise unless a higher level of protection is achieved. finally, a geopolitical consideration: the eu without this agreement could find itself displaced from the main axis of world trade and development, namely the trans-pacific. in any case, before we approve the treaty, we will carefully assess every aspect of it.
in writing. ‒ ttip can be a trade agreement with great potential and benefits for the european market and european businesses. the benefits in terms of economic and trade, growth and employment through the facilitation of entry into the american market by our economic realities. making our european businesses and products more competitive - especially those of excellence - must be one of the highest priorities on our political agenda. i therefore intend to vote in favour of this report. i hope that through this agreement we can offer good opportunities for our smes, improve the agricultural market and, above all, identify appropriate rules for the indication of the origin of products for the proper protection of our consumers. what some european governments still refuse to recognize and approve within the european union. i am also a member of the italian parliament and i do not hide my hope that we can protect made in italy better and put a stop to the enormous damage caused by italian sounding every year in our country. damage caused by the lack of shared standards.
in writing. ‒ ttip is an economic agreement on free trade and investment, which, by removing trade barriers, should facilitate the buying and selling of goods and services between the eu and the us, create jobs and further interconnect the two largest economies. designed as a response to the economic and financial crisis we are experiencing, ttip is increasingly proving to be a tailor-made agreement by and for the us, requiring a downward harmonisation of the high standards that the eu and its member states currently have in sensitive areas such as agriculture, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, food, textiles and animal welfare. one of the main points of contention is the inclusion of isds in the negotiations. such a system would allow us multinationals investing in europe to bypass any national or european court and sue member state governments directly before these new private international courts whenever they feel that national laws pose a threat. i voted against the final text, which is an agreement the socialists have made with the epp, alde and ecr and against the will of those of us who have opposed it from the beginning.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because i was and am convinced that the treaty is an opportunity to be seized, for the good of our companies, our production system and our workers. but at the same time, i wanted to express my disagreement with the compromise on isds. the treaty must become an opportunity and not be wasted or sold. i am convinced that there are no valid reasons, especially for the s&d group, which has always opposed systems and arbitration not exactly public, to forget that we are the europe of law and respect for the rule of law, so that no one can question the absolute impartiality of our courts, which are fully capable of settling any issues that may arise, without harming the rights of companies that intend to invest. i would remind you that the prerequisites for admission to the union include the impartiality of the courts and equality before the law. by voting for the isds mechanism, europe is acknowledging that its own member states do not meet this requirement. i hope that this misrepresentation can be corrected by referring the judgments back to the appropriate public bodies.
in writing. i voted against this resolution because ttip is a threat to the standards, safety and health of european citizens. i am concerned and outraged by this negotiation which is a threat to democracy and the rule of law. the resolution adopted by the plenary session removed the isds, one of the main sticking points in the debate, but replaced it with another system which, in fact, favours multinationals by giving them the privilege of directly suing member state governments whenever they consider that national laws pose a threat to them. we consider the new dispute settlement system adopted to be totally inadequate to prevent it from having direct and indirect effects on the ability of states to legislate in the interests of citizens. neither the italian nor the american system requires an additional mechanism for the settlement of commercial disputes. the european and us judicial systems are robust and strong and already offer the highest quality of protection for investors and citizens. since neither this recommendation nor the isds surrogate is acceptable to us, my vote was against it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives the commission a clear mandate for negotiating a transatlantic trade and investment partnership agreement. the agreement is a key instrument in bringing the pursuit of sustainable growth back to the centre of european action, while making a significant contribution to strengthening transatlantic relations with the united states. we want this agreement to be transparent and reliable, capable of bringing only benefits to european businesses and investors, removing those barriers which still prevent them from exploiting our full potential in the american market. we will continue to ensure that the negotiations are conducted in accordance with the mandate and that the interests of the european citizens are fully protected.
in writing. ‒ today's vote on the tpp was not about whether or not to support the agreement; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject. it was a vote to set the framework and conditions for a good agreement that does not lower our european standards on the environment, social standards, animal welfare and cultural diversity. and that is why i voted in favour. the text states, without exception, that our standards are not negotiable unless the aim is to achieve a higher level of safety. the protection of personal data is explicitly stated that data confidentiality should not be compromised and ttip should have a personal data protection clause. the resolution also calls for the ratification and implementation of the basic standards set by the international labour organisation.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of mr lange's report. this report sets out the strategic importance of the economic relationship between the european union and the united states as an opportunity to promote its principles and values, anchored in a framework based on shared norms between the two parties. it defines common strategies and visions on world trade, investment and trade-related issues, such as strong standards, norms and regulations, in order to develop a broader transatlantic vision and a common set of strategic objectives; ttip provides an opportunity to shape and regulate the international trading system in a way that ensures that both blocks thrive in an interconnected world, while safeguarding the prerogatives and distinctiveness of our peers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the negotiations on the transatlantic partnership on trade and investment. the proposed objective is to integrate the two markets through a us-eu free trade agreement in order to lower customs duties and remove non-tariff barriers and obstacles. it should be remembered that microenterprises are particularly affected by non-tariff barriers and sectors. given that small and mediumsized enterprises represent the most significant part of the european economy, opening the us market to smes, without compromising community standards in any way, will be a source of growth for europe's gdp. the benefits of this in a free trade area will therefore also be reflected in local communities, with a subsequent increase in the employment rate.

in writing. ‒ the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) is without doubt one of the most important issues on which the european parliament is called upon to express its views. the us remains the eu's main trading partner and the largest export market. according to available data, 88% of companies exporting to the us are small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) and 10 million jobs in europe depend on exports to the us. on the other hand, it is worth remembering that there are still a number of aspects which i believe deserve special attention during the negotiations, such as geographical indications (gi) and the protection of consumer health. after lengthy negotiations, the international trade committee (inta) approved draft recommendations, in which it reiterated its wish to conclude an ambitious agreement with the aim of guaranteeing market access in the areas of trade, services, investment and public procurement. the committee also calls for a balanced approach, including transitional periods, quotas and even exemptions for a number of sensitive products. i think this draft report is a good compromise and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of its adoption.

in writing. ‒ the new eu-us trade agreement, better known as ttip (transatlantic trade and investment partnership), currently under negotiation, represents a major opportunity for our companies. a comprehensive and ambitious agreement between the eu and the us could make it easier for businesses, especially smaller ones, to export to the us, import services, goods and inputs and compete in new markets. some estimates also show that ttip could lead to an overall gain of around 0.5% of gdp for the eu and 0.4% for the us between now and 2027. this would add as much as €86 billion to the eu economy and €65 billion to the us economy. it is important, however, that a balanced and transparent agreement is reached which promotes a win-win economic environment without compromising the health and safety of consumers and the competitiveness of our industrial system. i therefore decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ this economic agreement on free trade and investment aims, through the removal of trade barriers in a wide range of economic sectors, to facilitate the buying and selling of goods and services between the eu and the us, create jobs and further interconnect the two largest economies. it was designed as a response to the economic and financial crisis we are experiencing, but it is increasingly proving to be a tailor-made agreement by and for the us, requiring a downward harmonisation of the high standards that the eu and its member states currently have in sensitive areas such as agriculture, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals, food, textiles and animal welfare. one of the main criticisms is the integration of the investor-state dispute settlement system into the negotiating process. such a system would allow us multinationals investing in europe to bypass any national or european court and sue the governments of the member states directly, which could be induced to relax or even abandon the enactment of laws to protect labour, health, the environment, etc. further liberalization would harm italy more than any other european country.

in writing. ‒ on 3 march 2015, the council transmitted to parliament the draft decision on the renewal of the agreement for scientific and technological cooperation between the european community and the government of the republic of india. the current agreement expired on 17 may 2015 and may be renewed for a period of five years by mutual agreement between the eu and india. the new agreement would not introduce any changes to the previous one, but it is expected that the term 'european community' will be replaced by 'european union', which is necessary following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. the scope of the agreement covers all research and development activities under the horizon 2020 framework programme for research and innovation, as well as the eu's participation in indian projects. the costs incurred for cooperation between the parties shall not entail any transfer of funds from one party to the other. scientific and technological cooperation relating to india's status as a developing country is exempted from the agreement. i vote against because of india's non-accession to the nuclear non-proliferation treaty. india is estimated to have between 80 and 100 nuclear warheads. the question of nuclear non-proliferation is of considerable importance to the five star movement and therefore, for this reason too, i vote against it.

in writing. ‒ the eu research and innovation programme provides that the conditions for the participation of associated countries are determined by an international agreement between the union and the associated country. in view of the importance of scientific and technological cooperation between the faeroe islands and the union and the interest in strengthening research and innovation in the context of the creation of the european research area, the agreement will establish the participation of the islands as an associated country. all its legal entities will participate in the indirect actions and activities of the european commission research centre and in research activities under the same conditions as legal entities in the eu states. the established legal entities will participate in research programmes of the faroe islands. from the date of application, the islands will make a contribution to the annual budget of the union for each year of the programme. the financial contribution from the faroe islands will be added to the amount allocated annually in the eu budget for commitment appropriations to meet financial obligations arising from different forms of measures for the implementation, management and operation of horizon 2020. although we are talking about a research programme, i will abstain for the following reasons: periodic whaling of humpback whales, which is frowned upon by the international whaling commission, and the commercial exploitation of overfishing practices.
in writing. ‒ the union's research and innovation programme 'horizon 2020' provides that the terms and conditions of the participation of associated countries are governed by an international agreement. the accession of an associated country to the joint research programme shall ensure that all its legal entities can participate in the research activities of the union programmes under the same conditions as legal entities of the member states of the union. from the date of application of the agreement, the faroe islands will make a financial contribution to the annual budget of the union which will be added to the amount allocated each year in the annual budget of the union for commitment appropriations to meet the financial obligations arising from the different forms of measures necessary for the implementation, management and operation of horizon 2020. although in principle there is nothing against the possibility of including the faroe islands among the countries associated to horizon 2020, two aspects remain to my mind central to the relationship with this country, namely the annual killing of globicephaly and the poorly selective fishing practices. it is to emphasise the distance between these practices and the eu's internal conservation policies that i have decided to abstain from a vote that would otherwise have been in favour.
