in writing. ‒ i abstained on the agreement on scientific cooperation with the faroe islands. science, technology, research and innovation must not know borders, but these islands are certainly not a partner of which the eu can be proud. deaf to international disgust, they perpetrate repeated annual massacres of hundreds upon hundreds of globe-headed whales, which, like all cetaceans, are strictly protected by the eu through annex iv of the habitats directive. the faroese claim that the hunting of the globe-headed whales is part of their ancient "cultural traditions". these traditions, however, did not include the use of motor boats, reconnaissance aircraft, gps and telephones: the hunting has turned into the barbaric and unnecessary extermination of a huge number of animals. the meat of the globe-headed bats - once a precious food source - is thrown away. perhaps the maintenance of 'cultural traditions' could be tolerated if very few animals were killed by traditional methods, but the faroese custom of cruelly and needlessly slaughtering hundreds of globe-headed animals will reverberate its horror on anyone in the international community who has dealings with them. no agreement between the eu and the faroe islands can ever have my approval if it does not contain the prerequisite of banning the slaughter of globe-headed whales.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that encouraging the long-term commitment of shareholders in listed companies will bring greater stability to their management and, consequently, to the whole economic and financial system.
in writing. ‒ greater transparency on the ownership and management of shares by the controlling bodies of listed companies is an important element in order to give stability to the markets and to ensure real competition, not by means of poorly transparent manoeuvres, but by means of a real capacity to improve the supply of its products and the efficiency of its production and marketing systems. clear, binding, uniform rules throughout europe are needed to enable investors to have full knowledge and control of company dynamics, management remuneration and the production chain. a non-binding opinion would risk harming the most virtuous companies, thus failing to affirm that principle of equality before the law, the application of which is fundamental to the good health of the market and above all to the civil coexistence of our society. the revision of shareholder rights, although it may cause some unrest in the world of intermediaries, is necessary to improve the functioning of the stock market, to make it more fair and transparent and to ensure fairness in the relationship between company and shareholders. we must therefore all make sure that the european parliament today expresses itself clearly and authoritatively in this direction.
in writing. - i vote for it. the attempt to regulate the activities of listed companies better is worthwhile. the encouragement of the long-term commitment of shareholders could simply be incentivised without giving them a favourable position in relation to other shareholders, without creating any dominant position within the company. the report is very positive on the rest. commitments by the parties concerned to ensure greater transparency in the notes to the accounts (in relation to information to external parties, list of subsidiaries, information to customers, nature of activities and geographical location, etc.) are very important, taking into account the differences between member states. these rules could help to increase public/consumer and investor (including institutional) confidence by removing the veil of opacity that often surrounds the activities of large companies, whether listed or not.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2007/36/ec as regards the encouragement of long-term shareholder engagement and directive 2013/34/eu as regards certain elements of the report on corporate governance. with this report parliament has taken an important step forward in steering businesses and investors towards a more informed decision-making process and ensuring greater transparency in the governance of european companies. in addition, this vote has approved important instruments to combat tax evasion and avoidance, such as the country-by-country reporting obligation, which requires multinational companies to publicly declare the taxes they pay in each country in which they operate. i think that parliament has thus sent an important signal, particularly after luxleaks and the other scandals.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague giving a mandate for negotiations with the commission and the council on the revision of directive 2007/36/ec on the requirements relating to the exercise of certain rights of shareholders in listed companies. the aim is to improve and increase long-term investment. the report's transparency is a particularly positive element.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the encouragement of long-term shareholder engagement and certain elements of the corporate governance report. the aim of the proposal is to strengthen the long-term perspective in the management of listed companies by giving minority shareholders, and in particular institutional investors, a more transparent and easy-to-manage role. the idea is that if investors are more involved and if their engagement is more long-term oriented, companies will give greater priority to long-term issues, which in turn will benefit the end-users of institutional investors and asset managers, as well as businesses and society as a whole.
in writing. ‒ the economic crisis we are experiencing has been triggered by another crisis, the financial crisis, which in turn has been caused by the disconnect between society's long-term objectives and the much more short-sighted objectives of a significant part of the financial world. the problem is that following the logic and dynamism of the stock market, we risk losing sight of the fact that behind each share is a company that produces goods and services, employees, customers, one or more reference territories, a pipeline and each of us is involved in that world. the european parliament has wanted, with this report, for which i voted in favour, to take a first step towards aligning the objectives of medium and large investors with those of the economy as a whole in seeking to create widespread and sustainable prosperity. i congratulate the rapporteur.
in writing. ‒ the cofferati report represents an improvement on the original commission proposal and the council's general position, despite the important points on which it was necessary to compromise in order to reach a compromise acceptable to all groups. the reference to country-by-country reporting on taxes paid is a significant step towards greater transparency of listed companies to avoid cases in the future such as the recent lux leaks. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report and instructed the rapporteur to open negotiations with the commission and the council.
in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2007/36/ec as regards the encouragement of long-term shareholder engagement and directive 2013/34/eu as regards certain elements of the corporate governance report has made a number of steps towards harmonising the management of listed companies. in particular, the long-term perspective in their management has been strengthened. one of the main problems not yet addressed by the european legislative corpus was the excessive focus of firms exclusively on short-term returns and profits. in this way, attention to the short term was detrimental to longterm planning and therefore investment was insufficient and suboptimal. the solution is to give minority shareholders, and therefore institutional investors, a more influential role in a more transparent environment. in addition, the participation of all the actors involved in the business, such as employees, consumers and local communities, was encouraged. for these reasons, dialogue between shareholders has been encouraged and provisions for the more rapid identification of shareholders have been promoted. i therefore believe it is important to support these initiatives to stimulate the european economic fabric at this delicate time.
in writing. ‒ this text, which is fundamental in many respects, is the result of a compromise that necessarily excluded certain issues, but which also allowed a valid text to be brought to the plenary to move the governance of companies towards more ethically sustainable working methods. for example, unless there are changes during the negotiations with the commission and the council, companies will be obliged to declare in which countries they pay taxes, avoiding future lux leaks scandals, or, again, the control mechanisms for managers whose remuneration will therefore be linked to results will be increased. so, although i regret the absence of some important elements, such as the obligation to disclose the ratio between the remuneration of directors and the average remuneration of employees, i thought i should vote in favour of this text for the many other steps forward it proposes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament's position on the shareholder rights directive because i consider it of fundamental importance to legislate at community level on substantial aspects of the governance of listed companies, on transparency and on the way directors' remuneration is determined, and on transactions with related parties with a view to fostering relations with shareholders. i personally believe that the introduction of country-by-country reporting, which was not included in the original ec proposal, on the initiative of the ep rapporteur mr cofferati and strongly supported by the s&d group, is a genuinely innovative and characteristic element of the legislation under preparation. the report also calls for the commission to take a more active role in the fight against fraud and for the commission to provide a more effective instrument for the fight against fraud. finally, i hope that all the achievements for which the ep has fought, and therefore greater transparency in the commitments of investors and asset managers, the remuneration of directors of listed companies and the link between it and the performance of the companies they manage, will be vigorously defended during the trilogue with the council.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of mr cofferati's report. the document focuses on the need to ensure greater transparency in the activities of companies in order to regain the trust of eu citizens and promote shareholder engagement. the text approved contains important tools to combat tax evasion and avoidance and also provides for the introduction of rules requiring companies to explain how their directors' remuneration policy contributes to the long-term interests of the company.
in writing. ‒ the objective of the proposal for a directive adopted today is clearly to improve financial stability and to encourage long-term investment. we believe that greater involvement of shareholders in corporate governance is one of the levers that can contribute to an improvement in the financial and non-financial performance of companies. since shareholder rights are not the only long-term factor to be taken into account in corporate governance, it is appropriate to provide for additional measures to ensure greater involvement of all stakeholders, in particular employees, local authorities and civil society. in order to facilitate shareholder engagement in listed companies, listed companies should have the possibility to know the identity of their shareholders and to communicate directly with them. we therefore call for greater transparency both to ensure and improve the identification of shareholders themselves and in relation to the activities of large companies, and in particular to profits made, taxes paid on profits and subsidies received, salaries and remuneration of directors, which is essential to regain confidence and promote the involvement of shareholders and citizens of the european union in companies.
in writing. ‒ i thank mr cofferati for his work and support him as he puts forward a long-term perspective on the management of listed businesses by focusing not only on shareholders but also on employees, consumers and local communities who play a very important role.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report presented by mr cofferati on long-term shareholder engagement and the report on corporate governance, which aims to contribute to the long-term sustainability of eu companies, create favourable conditions for shareholders and improve cross-border exercise of voting rights by increasing the efficiency of the equity investment chain in order to contribute to growth, job creation and competitiveness in the eu. the central themes of the text presented are the remuneration of managers, the identification of shareholders and the publication of certain data such as the tax returns of companies: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the information is not disclosed to third parties.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks scandal, a very high level of transparency is needed, including ambitious measures against tax evasion and avoidance. it is important, however, that this report has defined the long-term orientation of the companies and shareholders and, above all, has established the key elements of the management of the company and its corporate governance. in order to ensure transparency of the tax strategies of large companies, it is necessary to introduce country-by-country reporting for large companies and listed companies and to clarify the activities and taxes paid. in addition, it is essential to ensure a good level of transparency for the engagement of institutional investors and asset managers in the companies in which they invest, ensuring an effective link between the remuneration of directors and their contribution to the long-term success of the companies entrusted to them. the fight against tax evasion can and must be done through the use of new instruments: the annual reporting of publicly traded companies is one of them.
in writing. i voted in favour of the cofferati report because, although it contains significant gaps, it introduces two important innovations: the obligation for multinational companies to declare profits generated and taxes paid in each country in which they operate, and a system of incentives to promote the long-term participation and social sustainability of companies. however, in negotiations between the groups, the text was considerably weakened, sacrificing important provisions on corporate governance. the final text has removed all reference to the involvement of employees and their right to express an opinion on the remuneration policy of managers, which will instead be expressed by the majority of shareholders, with a non-binding vote. the ceiling on the bonus of managers and the obligation to disclose information on the ratio of the average remuneration of managers to employees were also abolished. the directive is even at risk of being watered down further by the states because of the wide margin of discretion which was left in the transposition phase. this directive is nevertheless an important step forward in the fight against tax evasion and short-term finance. i hope therefore that the member states will not compromise its effectiveness further at the implementation stage and, above all, at the negotiation stage with the council.
in writing. ‒ the financial crisis has highlighted the need to reform the internal governance system of listed companies as short-term risk-taking has been identified as a key factor in the current economic crisis and the high share turnover rate. the revision of directive 2007/36/ec on the requirements relating to the exercise of certain shareholder rights in listed companies therefore aims to improve stability and increase long-term investment by encouraging shareholders of listed companies to be more active and engaged and to focus on the long-term performance of the company. the cofferati report represents an improvement on the original commission proposal and the council's general position, particularly as regards the reference to country-by-country reporting on taxes paid; this is a major step towards greater transparency of listed companies to avoid future cases such as the recent luxleaks.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text on the revision of the shareholder rights directive because i believe that revising these rules can be crucial to boosting long-term investment and to reviving the european economy. i think it is particularly appropriate to introduce country-by-country reporting on taxation by large companies. it is necessary to introduce mechanisms to ensure full transparency in taxation for multinational companies, in the context of the wider battle to abolish tax havens. i remember that the provision of this mechanism was a priority for us socialists and democrats and i consider the provision of the cbcr a great political victory for my group. finally, i agree with the need for shareholders to have a say in the remuneration of the directors of listed companies.

mr president, the european union has finally decided to improve the system for trading greenhouse gas emission allowances. the recession and the allocation of emission allowances have long led to an excess of allowances, with a consequent collapse in the price of carbon. it goes without saying that a low carbon price does not stimulate industry to make its plants more efficient and to avoid using polluting fuels, such as coal, and it is an obstacle to the transition to cleaner energy funds. the surplus allowances will eventually be put into a reserve, the so-called market stability reserve, which will aim to stabilise the carbon market, lead to an increase in the price of carbon and thus encourage industries to pollute less and invest in more efficient infrastructure and cleaner energy sources. it would have been preferable to introduce the reserve in 3017 in order to correct the functioning of the market as soon as possible. however, considering that the commission's proposal envisaged 2021 as the beginning of 2019, as provided for in the agreement, this is a good result overall. and it is an important signal from the european union, especially in view of the forthcoming conference in paris.

in writing. ‒ the report and the text on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the market stabilisation reserve in the eu greenhouse gas emission trading scheme are a useful step towards putting the system adopted by the european union in 2003 back on track. the union's emissions trading system (eu ets) has been particularly affected by distortions since the beginning of the economic crisis, which have progressively led to an imbalance between supply and demand. the risks of omitting these failures are high and would impede the achievement of a harmonised and cost-effective emission reduction system. the amended text has the advantage of addressing the key points that need to ensure the transition to a low-carbon economy, acting directly on the supply and demand side to ensure the true value of allowances. this report, which i fully support, must be a welcome sign of the overall reform of the ets system which the commission is about to introduce. a reform that must combine environmental sustainability, technological innovation and industrial competitiveness.

in writing. ‒ greenhouse gases are a major factor in altering the planet's environmental balance and are the main cause of global warming. reducing greenhouse gas emissions means not only stopping pollution, but also preventing tropical climate change and limiting the impact of natural disasters, with positive consequences for the health and safety of citizens, the environment and economic savings. we must not only reduce emissions of polluting gases (the 40% reduction target for 2030 is certainly a positive step, an important step on the road to full environmental sustainability, not the final goal), but also improve electricity grids, integrating them and supporting measures to make them more efficient. the implementation of energy-saving technologies is useful in reducing the high energy demands in the union by making consumption more efficient and making the use of electricity cheaper for citizens.

in writing. ‒ to ensure compliance with the kyoto protocol's obligations to reduce emissions of climate-changing gases, the eu has created an emissions trading market through the emission trading scheme directive (directive 2003/87/ec). the very idea that the price of gas emissions can be left to market laws is wrong. moreover, to date, the main beneficiaries of this market - treated like any other market - have been stock market speculators, large banking groups, financial companies and insurance companies. the text also does not include measures which we proposed to raise the price of co2 rapidly, so as to potentially accelerate the stimulus to energy innovation. i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a parliament and council decision on the establishment and operation of a market stabilisation reserve in the eu's greenhouse gas emission trading system (ets). on 22 january 2014, the commission presented a proposal for a market stabilisation reserve, together with a communication on the 2020 to 2030 framework for energy and climate policies. the commission proposal aims to make structural changes to the emissions trading system (ets) to deal with the surplus of emission allowances, currently estimated at over 2 billion, and to remedy the shortcomings of the system so that it can achieve the objective of reducing greenhouse gas emissions in a cost-effective and economically efficient manner, as required by the ets directive. since the surplus of allowances is detrimental to the long-term effectiveness of the system, it is necessary to take action by adopting measures to correct the deficiencies of the ets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a decision because i believe that the agreement reached with the council is an appropriate and balanced agreement. in order to achieve the objectives of effective reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, the emissions trading system (ets) needs to be made more effective. the surplus of allowances, unfortunately, jeopardises the long-term effectiveness of this system, making the trading mechanism obsolete and therefore an effective reduction in emissions. moreover, the lack of flexibility on the supply side of the quotas does not allow, at this stage, to deal adequately with market fluctuations and unforeseen shocks on the demand side. the aim of this proposal is therefore to correct the errors which have been made in the construction of this system of trade. the introduction of a market stabilisation reserve will therefore make it possible to guarantee industry a more stable and predictable market where supply fluctuations will be regulated by appropriate rules. for all these reasons i welcome this proposal because i believe it is important to insist on and try to improve a european emission control system which is efficient and at the same time ensures that companies are competitive on the market.
in writing. ‒ the ets is the main instrument for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, based on cost-effectiveness and economic efficiency. however, the current surplus of allowances is detrimental to the long-term effectiveness of the system, undermining its proper functioning and significantly increasing the price of carbon. in this context, the proposal for a market stabilisation reserve, by correcting a structural deficiency in the ets, would provide industry with a medium- to long-term perspective. i therefore intend to vote in favour of this proposal on the basis of these considerations.
in writing. ‒ m5s has challenged the idea that the pricing of climate-changing gas emissions can be left to market laws. stock speculators, large banking groups, financial and insurance companies have profited. added to this is the risk of exposing the carbon market to tax fraud, such as those that have exposed at least €5 billion of tax evasion by european taxpayers. our amendments to end the ets by 2020 have not been passed. we supported the amendments proposed by environmental ngos to limit the activation of the mechanisms of the reserve with a tighter scissors; increase the quota to be moved to/from the reserve from 100 m to 50 m; to cancel the 900m allowances blocked from backloading by bringing the entry into force of the reserve forward to 2017. these measures would have allowed a higher co2 price to be formed quickly by accelerating the stimulus to innovation for reducing emissions. although the amendments to bring forward the start date and to cancel part of the surplus allowances were passed by a majority in the envi committee, the final text does not take them into account. none of the points supported by our amendments has been incorporated into the agreement, and for these reasons i am voting against.

in writing. ‒ i had to abstain on the possibility of associating the swiss confederation to the horizon 2020 framework programme but above all to the iter activities. the latter is a large-scale scientific experiment to demonstrate the validity of fusion as a source of energy. iter has seven global partners: china, the eu, india, japan, south korea, russia and the united states. the problem with this project is the cost: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the research results are not distorted by the new technologies. the five star movement has not yet taken a position on the iter project, and that is why i abstained.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf, set up to provide additional support for workers who suffer from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade) which refers to the application submitted by finland in relation to 568 redundancies at broadcom communications finland, a company operating in the electronics and electrical engineering industries. in recent years, asia has emerged as the largest employer in this sector. in europe, by contrast, the number of employees has begun to decline. this trend seems to affect the entire electronics industry in finland, as demonstrated by nokia's announcement in 2011 of large-scale redundancies. the surpluses therefore appear to be linked to changes in the structure of world trade. i therefore voted in favour of this measure. i regret that italian companies are not able to benefit more from the egf because of the lack of support from local and national institutions, which submitted only 14 applications in total between 2007 and 2014.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on tax avoidance and tax evasion as challenges to governance, social protection and development in developing countries, which calls on the commission to present a communication to support developing countries in the fight against illicit financial flows and tax evasion. tax evasion and avoidance are among the main obstacles to the mobilisation of national revenues for development. the report therefore calls on the commission to step up financial and technical assistance to developing countries, to adopt solutions designed to improve transparency and cooperation in the fight against tax fraud and to publish country-by-country information, taking into account the needs and limitations of developing countries. the report also stressed the importance of the oecd base erosion and profit shifting (beps) action plan, which aims to redefine international tax rules, particularly for developing countries, which are heavily dependent on corporate tax revenues, but stressed that beps is too narrow in scope and too focused on the interests of rich countries.
in writing. ‒ the text of the report is ambitious and complements the report on financing for development. it calls for the impact assessments of fiscal policies on developing countries to be carried out in order to strengthen policy coherence for development, and for particular attention to be paid to gender issues, as the withdrawal of resources from these countries is reflected primarily on women. the importance of having complete and public information on the beneficial owners of corporate profits is also stressed, in order to avoid that behind complex networks there is theft of public funds, corruption, tax evasion or the financing of illicit trafficking or terrorism. the commission is also asked to continue and strengthen support for developing countries by providing financial and technical assistance and to ensure that good governance in tax matters is part of the policy dialogue with them. i voted for it with conviction.
in writing. ‒ every year, the income of developing countries is depleted by more than a billion dollars (about 10 times the total amount of economic aid received!) from illicit financial flows and tax evasion and avoidance, money laundering, corruption (including in agreements, often "tailor-made" and not very transparent, on natural resources, not only in the mining sector), and the use of shell companies. and, again, from unfair tax treaties, tax incentives and exemptions and a general "race to the bottom" in corporate tax rates, which has benefited foreign investors more than the countries concerned. the resolution calls for a series of concrete measures with a significant impact, such as country-by-country reporting by multinational companies, so that all relevant tax information is made public (controlled companies with their financial results, taxes paid, assets and number of employees, etc.); the automatic exchange of information between countries; the establishment of public registers of beneficial ownership of companies, trusts, foundations and other bodies, without restrictions on access; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of their employer. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on tax avoidance and tax evasion as challenges to governance, social protection and development in developing countries (dcs). in those countries, illicit financial flows are generally derived from tax evasion and avoidance activities; however, they are not equipped to combat such illegal activities. it is important for the pvs to obtain public revenues through taxation and taxation. at european level, the european investment bank (eib), the european bank for reconstruction and development (ebrd) and the financial institutions of the member states provide important support to private enterprises in the ldcs. the commission is invited in this report to rapidly propose an ambitious action plan, in the form of a communication, to support developing countries fighting tax evasion and avoidance and to help them establish fair, balanced, efficient and transparent tax systems, taking into account the work undertaken by the oecd development assistance committee.
in writing. ‒ the benefits of effective and transparent taxation go beyond increasing the resources available to the state, creating a link between political institutions and public and private services that is necessary to achieve sound and good governance in developing countries. in addition to these objectives, the economic and financial crisis requires an increase in national income to cope with the growth of public debt. we are aware that developing countries face considerable administrative, political and technical constraints in the collection of taxes; the fight against corruption, tax evasion and avoidance is one of the main objectives of growth and international cooperation. the commission should take concrete and effective measures to support these countries and their regional structures in the field of tax administration in order to make tax policies fair, balanced, transparent and efficient. that is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i think everyone is aware of the situation in which many developing countries find themselves, which cannot even reach the minimum tax level necessary to finance their basic functioning and public services. many of these attract investment by offering tax incentives and exemptions that are neither transparent nor based on a proper cost-benefit analysis, thus resulting in unfavourable outcomes in terms of tax systems and causing harmful tax competition. it is therefore necessary, and that is why i voted in favour of this report, to adopt urgently concrete and effective measures to support the pvs in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance and in the development of fair, balanced, efficient and transparent tax policies. the judicial system and anti-corruption agencies in these countries should also be strengthened. in addition, in view of foreign investments, a database should be established containing all easily searchable information concerning the beneficial ownership of companies, trusts and other institutions in order to prevent other shell companies and similar legal entities from being used for money laundering, the financing of illicit or terrorist activities, the concealment of the identity of corrupt individuals or the concealment of public funds and profits from illicit transactions and illegal tax evasion.

in writing. ‒ the circular economy is the new economic model that europe must commit to in the coming years. its implementation presents obstacles and challenges, but they must be met with confidence and determination if a new system is to be established that will benefit everyone. the european commission and the ellen macarthur foundation estimate that over 2 million new jobs could be created, and that businesses could save between €250 and €465 billion a year. moreover, human health, ecosystems and biodiversity would benefit. the report under consideration sets ambitious targets such as increasing resource efficiency (30% more by 2030) and higher targets for waste recycling (70% of municipal solid waste and 80% of packaging materials). as a member of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, i wholeheartedly support the text we voted on today, which is a first step in this complex but essential transition process.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the circular economy because i believe that the work done is going in the right direction, although important amendments concerning, for example, the ban on incineration and the introduction of mandatory national waste management plans were not passed in the committee on the environment (envi). the text as a whole represents an ambitious package and a good starting point for the european commission to provide a serious legislative proposal which will allow, in the long term, the adoption of an alternative economic model to the utilitarian one. the final text adopted by parliament calls unequivocally on the european commission to come forward with a proposal that can replace the current development model of unlimited growth, while knowing that resources are limited, and that can start the process of transition to a circular economy, based on sustainable consumption.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the transformation of our economic system into a circular economy system would bring enormous benefits to the union in terms of both the environment and the economy and employment, allowing for a significant reduction in co2 emissions and the creation of a large number of new jobs.
in writing. ‒ raising the targets in existing waste treatment directives is useful to accelerate the transition to the circular economy model. in the circular economy, there is no waste: waste is no longer just waste, it becomes a resource. raw materials are no longer extracted, used once and thrown away. with the circular economy, waste disappears through reuse, repair and recycling applied at every stage of the commercial chain. extending the productive use of materials, reusing them and increasing their efficiency is useful not only to tackle waste management issues from a non-emergency perspective, but also to strengthen the eu's competitiveness on the world stage. the impact of this approach on the european real economy is positive because research and innovation, which are key to the success of the plan, are closely linked to green economy investments on the ground: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of accidents at work.
in writing. - i vote against it. the concept of circular economy, like others of its kind (such as cradle-to-cradle, industrial ecology and natural capitalism), suggests the development, through innovation, of industrial-scale strategies aimed at a complete decoupling between physical growth in throughput and non-physical (financial) growth in gdp (so-called 'green' or 'sustainable' growth). the mainstream of the sustainable development movement is based on the deep conviction that, with the right technological innovations, economic growth and environmental protection can be complementary rather than in conflict; however, this view ignores, misrepresents or underestimates the biophysical limits to human production and consumption that are drawn by system dynamics and thermodynamics. finally, it should be noted that a constant process of resource efficiency through innovation has been underway since at least the early modern period, but that this relative decoupling has not prevented the overall growth in the production and consumption of raw materials from being neutralised; there is a risk that a sharp increase in relative decoupling could, by virtue of the jevons paradox, lead instead to an intensification of the exploitation of raw materials, made cheaper by the acceleration of capital movements brought about by the reduction in the unit cost of production obtained through more efficient technologies.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resource efficiency report. the european parliament has adopted the text as a step towards changing the economic model to which we are accustomed, namely the 'take, produce and throw away' model. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for fundamental rights (fra) is based on the principle of equal treatment for men and women. the commission has announced a proposal for a review of waste legislation. the commission must be obliged to present it by 2015, including clear and unambiguous definitions, the development of waste prevention measures, the application of the 'pay as you throw' principle and the strict limitation of incinerators. i hope that the commission will be able to take these inputs and be able to push member states towards a paradigm shift towards an economic system where the materials and energy used to manufacture products retain their value for as long as possible, thereby reducing waste and resource use and at the same time creating economic opportunities and competitive advantages on a sustainable basis.
in writing. ‒ the report of the honourable member indicates to the commission what actions should be included in the proposal that the commission is preparing on the circular economy and the revision of european waste legislation. the own-initiative report is ambitious and highlights that the unsustainable use of resources is causing immense environmental damage and at the same time represents a major economic risk. a more efficient use of resources is therefore absolutely necessary. it could also be a significant source of employment in europe. i voted for it with conviction.
in writing. ‒ economic development based on the linear growth model is no longer sustainable or viable, not only because of the scarcity of available raw materials but also because of the amount of waste that this type of 'take, produce, use and throw away' system has generated. a reversal of the trend is therefore inevitable, and a new process is needed which considers waste as a resource to be fed back into the production cycle. there are about 600 million tonnes of waste in europe with the potential for reuse, and if we want to build an economic system based on sustainable growth and efficient use of resources, we must encourage the reuse and recycling of products. the transition to a circular economy will require a redesign of a new production model that will provide a strong impetus not only in terms of technology, but also in terms of societal organisation, financing methods and policies. new targets and objectives for waste recycling should therefore be identified. we therefore hope that the commission will soon present an ambitious package of circular economy measures needed to stimulate growth and protect the environment. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the strategic own-initiative report on the circular economy. the text under consideration contains a number of proposals aimed at ensuring a more efficient use of resources and minimising the volume of waste. the main points are: (1) binding 30% targets and the creation of indicators for resource efficiency; (2) the revision of the ecodesign directive; the commission has also proposed a tax on landfills and incinerators.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that it appropriately encourages a more efficient use of resources and contains sound proposals to steer the economy towards the necessary reduction in the volume of waste. given that europe still imports most of its energy from third countries, i believe that in order to move towards greater energy independence we need to promote a more efficient use of resources. this process will lead to greater environmental, social and economic benefits. if we are to reverse the trend towards unsustainable waste and avoid irreversible damage to the environment, it will be important to identify the weaknesses in our production system and to find appropriate solutions. as argued in the report, investing in the circular economy is not economically counterproductive but rather, in the long term, such investments will lead to increased savings coupled with the potential to reduce unemployment levels and create new business opportunities. european companies will therefore increase their competitiveness, their profits and will be the linchpin of the process leading to the circular economy. it will therefore be important to establish common rules and effective implementation mechanisms so as to ensure a transition towards a more sustainable european economy in all its member countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mrs pietikäinen's report, which calls attention to the need to tackle the global challenge of resource depletion, and the eu as we know is highly dependent on imported resources, more than any other region in the world. unfortunately, unsustainable use of resources brings with it serious risks such as climate change, desertification, deforestation and biodiversity loss. to remedy this, a policy framework to support resource efficiency combined with ambitious environmental targets and strict rules is needed. first of all, it is essential: stop the continuous extraction of raw materials, such as water, which is used not only during the production cycle but also as a public good; increasing the life cycle of products, their durability, reusability and recyclability; review waste legislation, seeking to tackle the illegal export of post-consumer waste and formulating clear collection and recycling targets; developing a strategic framework on resource efficiency in buildings as well as indicators, standards, methods and quality requirements for spatial and urban planning; the commission has also set up a network of experts to help the member states to develop their environmental policies.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because a more efficient use of resources would reduce resource dependency and bring environmental and economic savings through the creation of new green and local jobs. i am glad that parliament has accepted the amendments proposed by m5s to eliminate direct and indirect subsidies to fossil fuels and to eliminate all environmentally harmful subsidies. the resolution calls on member states to increase resource efficiency by 30% by 2030, to fully implement the cascade of resource use and sustainable sourcing, to fully implement the polluter pays principle and producer responsibility, to use renewable energy and a waste hierarchy, and to apply taxes for landfilling and waste incineration. as regards waste, i regret that the resolution does not include a general ban on incineration and landfilling, despite the fact that incineration is clearly a linear economic practice. but overall the text is commendable and i could only vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i shared the approach of ms pietikäinen's report on resource efficiency and the transition to a circular economy because i believe that the circular economy is one of the key challenges of the future and an urgent one for the eu and all member states. europe continues to produce and waste an enormous amount of waste, causing the well-known environmental and waste disposal problems: some of this waste must be reusable. the circular economy principle aims to turn waste into raw materials for other businesses, and as such it needs to be adequately supported. in addition, the circular economy helps to create jobs and develop industries active in recycling and reuse, while ensuring a less consumer-driven approach. i therefore share the call on the european commission to come forward with legislative proposals not only in the field of waste but also in other key areas of the circular economy such as food waste, eco-products, manufacturing and packaging, promoting the reuse and recyclability of products that are consumed. finally, they agree on the objectives of reducing municipal solid waste and recycled packaging and on the call to increase european resource efficiency by 30% by 2020.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation laying down maximum permitted levels of radioactivity for food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other case of radioactive emergency. as the report points out, it is absolutely essential that the european union has up-to-date legal instruments containing decision-making procedures capable of dealing with emergency situations such as those experienced after the chernobyl and fukushima accidents. the use of implementing acts to respond to nuclear accidents or other types of radioactive emergencies is the most appropriate way to adequately address this need. i therefore believe that in cases of extreme urgency it should be possible to adopt an implementing act without prior examination. in addition, parliament should reserve the right to co-decide on the modification of maximum permitted levels of radioactivity for food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other case of radioactive emergency, should it be necessary to review them in the light of new scientific knowledge.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal states that the maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination established in 1987 and to be applied following a nuclear accident or any other case of radioactive emergency which may result in significant contamination of food and feed are not yet in line with the most recent scientific advice available at international level. it therefore lays down the procedures for adopting them. if adopted as proposed by the commission, the regulation could lead to binding rules for all member states, aimed at preventing food and feed products from being placed on the eu market if they do not comply with the established maximum levels of radioactivity. the main problem, of course, is the scientific method of determining these limits, and we intend to monitor the way in which these limits are set.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation laying down maximum permitted levels of radioactivity in food and feed following a nuclear accident or any other case of radioactive emergency. it is desirable that the eu has up-to-date legal instruments with agile decision-making procedures adapted to all situations in order to deal with situations such as those experienced after the chernobyl and fukushima accidents. the proposal sets out in its annexes the maximum permissible levels in the event of a radioactive accident or emergency, which were confirmed in 2012 by the group of experts established by article 31 of the euratom treaty.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe it is essential that the european union takes the necessary measures to deal with the risks of contamination following a nuclear accident. as has been shown, prolonged consumption of food products with high levels of radioactivity has extremely harmful consequences on the cells of the human body. we must therefore strive to increase food security within the union in order to prevent radioactive contamination from increasing. the european parliament therefore calls for the establishment of appropriate maximum permitted levels in the event of a radioactive accident or emergency. these levels were confirmed in 2012 by an expert group established by article 31 of the euratom treaty and were included in the european commission's 'publication radiation protection 105'. finally, it will be necessary not only to monitor products from the country affected by the accident but also to increase controls for neighbouring countries, which are also at risk of radioactive fallout on their own foodstuffs. while we hope that disasters like chernobyl and fukushima will not happen again, it is important that we do everything possible to prevent radioactive contamination.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which provides for the use of implementing acts to deal with critical situations arising from a nuclear accident or other type of radioactive emergency, and which calls for the need to act quickly, especially to protect consumers. the general objective is to establish rapid and effective cooperation between the institutions in the event of an emergency and to take account of developments in community law on food safety by laying down the conditions for importing food or feed from third countries affected by a nuclear emergency.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council regulation setting maximum permitted levels of radioactivity following a nuclear accident, as i share the need for up-to-date legal instruments and appropriate decision-making procedures to deal with such emergency situations. i think it is important to amend the legal basis of the regulation in order to give the european parliament the power of co-decision.
in writing. ‒ this regulation builds on a 2010 commission proposal to bring together three pieces of legislation on the permissible levels of radioactivity in food and feed. since they were adopted on the legal basis of the euratom treaty, the european parliament would have been involved only for consultation. in 2011, however, the parliamentary assembly in plenary decided to request the amendment of the legal basis, citing the health protection nature of the measure on the basis of which the amendments must be made by a joint decision between the council and parliament. this gives us members the power to intervene on the merits of the proposals and thus to make support for the initiative conditional on the transposition of specific requests. for these reasons we supported the amendment of the legal basis but did not confirm our vote for the final measure, since the commission, with the support of the major political groups, has managed to keep unchanged the maximum permitted levels of radioactivity in food and feed, which were set back in 1987 and are far higher than those set by the fao and in force in the usa.

in writing. ‒ the resolution analyses the building of a capital markets union, although at first reading the text seems to move in the direction of identifying the prospects so that the phenomena that contributed to the very serious economic crisis are not repeated in the context of the capital market, on a more critical reading i believe that the entire text is extremely deficient and biased. firstly, the fundamental problem of the crisis, namely the single currency and the costs it represents for the member states of the union, is not mentioned, and the juncker plan is also mentioned, which, as i have said on several occasions, is nothing but a political marketing operation which i have already strongly opposed, not to mention the fact that many references are made to the needs of smes, but it is deliberately omitted to mention that it is the banks that bear a great deal of responsibility for the failure of many companies that have been prevented from accessing credit. for all these reasons i voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ the green paper 'building a capital markets union' adopted in february this year sets out the first part of a strategy that the union will pursue in the coming years. this can and must be consistent with the commitment made in the juncker plan for investment. we are waiting for the commission's action plan in september, and today this resolution which i support has the merit of highlighting the centrality of action in this area. the last decades have seen an increase in the size of the financial sector at global and european level. in the face of this growth, investment in the real economy has declined, with a significant decline particularly during the economic crisis. a crisis that has weakened financial integration across the continent by segmenting and dividing the sector on the basis of fiscal and regulatory barriers. the capital markets union project aims to address these critical issues. through greater integration and harmonisation of markets, the aim is to free up all those unused resources in the system, trying to channel them into the service of the real economy. in addition, effective diversification of funding channels will be important to stimulate and strengthen the size of small and medium-sized enterprises.

in writing. ‒ i vote against the econ resolution on the capital markets union. the text, which is very technical, seems to indicate that there are prospects for avoiding a repetition of certain phenomena in the capital market which contributed to the very serious economic crisis. the document is seriously flawed in that it does not mention the most important issue, namely the single currency and the costs it represents for the member states of the union. the report also mentions as important the 'reforms' that member states should undertake to reassure markets. the text is complemented by the agreement reached on the so-called 'juncker plan' (a mere political marketing operation which we voted against with conviction). the report makes many references to the needs of smes, but it fails to mention that it is the banks that bear a great deal of responsibility for the failure of many companies that have been prevented from accessing credit. finally, we are not convinced by some calls which are too general to allow for the standardization of regulations in the sector, or indeed a genuine single market for capital.

in writing. ‒ for many decades italy has suffered the damage of a relational capitalism that privileged personal relationships over merit. we are not talking about the importance of the word given and the handshake, but about favourable treatment of friends of friends, while no one, however good and endowed with good ideas, had to succumb. a capital markets union, a priority for commissioner hill, would be a great opportunity to increase competition in the financial sector, to the benefit of both businesses and consumers, and above all by improving the efficiency of the system itself, with benefits also for the shareholders of banks (which in italy, through the foundations, are ultimately the public bodies to which we all pay taxes). this architecture, as described in the resolution, has my vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ the capital markets union represents a major challenge for both the european institutions and market players in the european context. the aim of this project is to develop a european capital market which is complementary to the banking market. long-term financing therefore represents an opportunity for growth and job creation, which is crucial for a europe that has only emerged from the economic and financial crisis that gripped it in the last year. moreover, these investments produce far-reaching benefits throughout society, with important economic, social and environmental consequences, as opposed to mere short-term speculation. the emphasis was also placed on small and mediumsized enterprises, the real engine of our continent. the entry of institutional investors into the capital market has therefore been encouraged, who now hold a large amount of savings but have great difficulty in participating. i am voting in favour of this proposal because it reduces the funding gap between countries by making it easier to pass on the monetary policies of the european central bank. finally, greater diversification of sources of finance will reduce idiosyncratic risks within europe.

in writing. ‒ i am in line with the ppe group in favour of building a capital markets union, which is why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution. the union i want to support is the one which allows for greater financing opportunities, especially for smes. i therefore agree with mr balz when he says that we must make sure that smes can actually benefit from this union, that we must improve the investment climate in europe.
in writing. ‒ the resolution adopted today is the european parliament's first reaction to the commission's green paper on the creation of a capital markets union. i decided to vote in favour of the text because i believe that a genuine european approach is needed to identify and remove obstacles to crossborder investment within the eu and thus stimulate growth in the 28 member states. i therefore hope that the action plan which will be outlined by the commission following the public consultation will aim at maximising the benefits of a single capital market, improving access to finance for all businesses and especially smes and strengthening the competitiveness of the european union by creating a solid basis for financial stability.
in writing. the capital markets union (cmu) aims to intensify the financialisation of the economic system through greater standardisation of financial products and greater use of financial instruments - such as securitisations - which were at the root of the 2008 crisis, replacing the traditional banking channel. such standardisation will necessarily be to the detriment of the real economy and smes, which, on the contrary, need solutions which respect their specificities and which facilitate their business by reducing the bureaucratic and administrative burdens on them. that is why we rejected the motion for a resolution in strasbourg in favour of the introduction of the cmu. the development of finance has no positive correlation with economic growth. the result would be a financial system that is more exposed to systemic risks and lacks firewalls to deal with them. on the contrary, the return to growth requires solving the credit crunch, boosting aggregate demand and creating a favourable environment for public investment, especially in innovation. besides, the timing is premature. the cmu would enter into force when banking sector reforms such as the bsr and the regulation of shadow banking have not yet been finalised and, finally, the necessary consumer protection measures are not in place.
in writing. ‒ i do not share the positions taken in the resolution under vote, i do not think that the proposed measures are worthy of the purpose it seeks, and i do not share at all the persistent denial of a direct link between the mass landings off the coast of north africa and terrorism; i voted against this text for all these reasons.
in writing. ‒ the proposed measures are certainly not worthy of the purpose of the report. fighting terrorism with pnr certainly seems ridiculous, not to mention the constant references to the disconnect between islamic immigration and terrorism. i vote against.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the resolution on the european agenda on security. in recent years, threats to the internal security of the union have become more complex and difficult to predict and have shown that it is difficult for a single member state to be able to respond to them. the report therefore underlined that terrorism, radicalisation, crossborder organised crime and cybercrime are serious threats that require coordinated action at european level. in responding to these challenges, it is important to seek the right balance between prevention policies and repressive measures. in addition, security measures should always be implemented in accordance with the principles of the rule of law and the protection of fundamental rights, such as the right to privacy and data protection, freedom of expression and association and due process. in short, the european security agenda must not restrict the rights and freedoms of the european model.
in writing. ‒ the agenda follows the internal security strategy and i voted in favour of the libe report on this. the agenda focuses on the three pillars of organised crime, terrorism and cybercrime, and the report on the agenda provides for a fair balance between the need for security and the need to safeguard rights and freedoms. the emphasis is on prevention without going beyond repressive measures and, in particular, the usefulness of encrypted data for non-criminal purposes is affirmed and therefore the need for citizens to continue to make use of this tool. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to abstain on the motion for a resolution on the european agenda on security. on 28 april 2015, the commission adopted a communication setting out the key safety priorities and principles for the period 2015-2020. the report asks the commission and the council to indicate how they intend to implement the agenda, how they plan to cooperate with parliament and whether they have received assessments from the agencies concerned on the human and financial resources needed. however, the ppe group considered the content of the report in question to be insufficient and not in line with its prerogatives.
in writing. ‒ of the two motions for resolutions on the agenda, only one was adopted. the one i supported because i thought it would be more effective, given the delicate subject we are dealing with, did not find the support of the majority. threats to the internal security of the union are becoming increasingly complex, well-designed, asymmetrical, unpredictable and uncontrollable. the member states alone cannot handle these continuing attacks, much less fight them. the response must not only be consistent, rapid and effective, but also take account of the multi-level and multi-state nature of these terrorist groups. as regards terrorism, the prevention of radicalisation needs to be stepped up through dialogue with local communities and civil society at national level, in order to block extremist ideologies. in the light of the recent terrorist attacks in brussels, paris, copenhagen and saint-quentin-fallavier, it is urgent to focus on a number of priorities: enhance eu border security, improve internet reporting capabilities, combat illicit arms trafficking and enhance information exchange and operational cooperation between national law enforcement and intelligence services. other issues on which we are trying to find concrete solutions are cybercrime, cyber-enhanced crime and organised crime.
in writing. ‒ we are well aware that threats to the internal security of the european union are becoming increasingly complex, international, fast-changing and difficult to predict. terrorism, radicalisation, crossborder organised crime and cybercrime are just some of the challenges facing the eu, which must act in a timely, coordinated and flexible manner. i agree with the european agenda on security for 2015-2020 which has set out some very good starting objectives, firstly by helping member states to further develop mutual trust and to improve the exchange of information and good practice, as well as the inclusion of very strong human rights clauses in cooperation agreements and the safeguarding of the principle of the best interests of the child in all security legislation. i also agree with the cooperation between europol, eurojust and the future european public prosecutor's office to ensure greater democratic control, the application of the law and justice throughout the territory. i hope that the eu can achieve a good degree of autonomy in security, also developing devices and services for critical infrastructure and public services. and to do that, investment in research and innovation is essential.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text because of the importance of having a european security strategy. given that the threats to european security today are almost always cross-border, europe must understand that it must tackle these challenges in a unified way, with an effective information-sharing system that is the result of cooperation between judicial and police forces. the proposal voted in plenary focuses mainly on the fight against organised crime, terrorism and cybercrime, but despite the high levels of concern usually raised by these issues, it succeeds in proposing solutions that also aim at safeguarding fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the european agenda on security because i believe that the implementation of eu security policy is a shared responsibility of all political and social actors in the european union. in the current geopolitical context, threats to the security of the european union are rapidly evolving and, above all, they are no longer identifiable according to traditional criteria but are becoming less and less conventional and unexpected. i therefore welcome the european commission's proposal for a european agenda on security for 2015-2020 which will undoubtedly be an effective and efficient tool in the fight against new international challenges such as terrorism, cross-border organised crime and cybercrime. i particularly appreciated the general structure of the agenda which puts the respect for human rights and the rule of law at the forefront and the need to strike the right balance between measures to combat international threats and respect for freedom and the principles of justice. i share the call on the commission to put more decisive measures on the agenda to combat radicalisation, violent extremism and ideologies that are dangerous to the security of european citizens, and i welcome initiatives aimed at social integration and inclusion.

in writing. ‒ in line with the ppe group, i have decided to abstain from voting on the report on the european agenda on security, because the text presented reflects the too naive and superficial approach taken by the socialists, greens and liberals. the ppe cannot support a proposal which severely restricts the police and armed forces' action against criminals and terrorists, as the left in parliament wants. at a time like the present, when the security of european citizens is threatened on a daily basis, we need more and more intelligence, police and legal instruments to guarantee national security. to deny the correlation between migration waves and security threats is to deliberately and naively deny a problem that is right in front of everyone's eyes. for this reason, measures should be taken to improve the exchange of information, strengthen cooperation and provide support to member states. to do this, we must first consult the agencies actually working in this field, asking in particular what their needs might be, also in terms of staff and the additional costs they have had to bear, because of the ever-increasing requirements. there is still a lot of work to be done in the area of security.
