in writing. ‒ the report signed by mr kukan highlights the strategic importance of the european neighbourhood policy as a useful tool for creating interdependent relations between the european union and the states which are party to the initiative. i particularly appreciated the reference in the text to the need to ensure tangible and concrete improvements for the citizens of the partner countries, as well as the reference to the need to make the neighbourhood policy more solid and effective. in view of the foregoing considerations, i have decided to vote in favour of this document.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the european neighbourhood policy is a key step in the security challenge and in building a fruitful partnership with our neighbours. the new neighbourhood policy will have to be based on greater flexibility and differentiation: the partners have different aspirations and the agreements must be tailored to the specific characteristics of each country. the main challenges of the new programming are the fight against radicalism, poverty and the strengthening of security. the goal is to have a prosperous and safe neighborhood. we must use the principle of more for more, but bearing in mind that this can lead to contradictions, if countries lagging behind in their democratic transition receive less, this is at the expense of the population. the aid must be balanced between the eastern and southern neighbourhoods and i think it is particularly appropriate to give special attention to tunisia, which has made real democratic progress and which could be put into crisis by the recent tragic events. it is important to maintain the strategic dialogue, we must not separate the enp from foreign policy because a safer neighbourhood means greater security in europe.
in writing. - our safety depends on that of our neighbors. a reformulation of the european neighbourhood policy is necessary to reflect the current geopolitical situation in the area. i think the eu should make a little self-criticism because it has failed to create the circle of friends it had set itself when it launched its neighbourhood policy. we must increase the programmes of technical assistance and cultural exchange which can facilitate better mutual understanding.
in writing. ‒ the european neighbourhood policy (enp) is an essential part of the european union's foreign policy. i believe it is of paramount importance to support its objectives in order to create an area of prosperity, stability and security, based on the common values and principles of the european union. the eu must be able to identify, together with its partners, priorities for enhanced cooperation, integrating different areas of intervention such as the prevention of natural disasters, the strengthening of infrastructure and regional development, migration flows. i believe that the security component should be emphasised and that this revision proposal calls for closer coordination between the european neighbourhood policy and the activities of the cfsp and the csdp. in addition, the eu is invited to focus on strengthening the capacity of partner countries for border control. i therefore decided to support this proposal.
in writing. ‒ the house has long been calling on the commission to take action to make the necessary changes to the enp, the european neighbourhood policy, which was set up in 2003 to cooperate with europe's neighbours by land and sea, establishing a privileged relationship that would surely bring stability, security and development to all those involved in the policy. since 2011, when the 'more for more' clause was introduced - the more countries commit to cooperation, the more they benefit - the geopolitical situation has changed a lot, which is why i voted in favour of the report proposed by the committee on foreign affairs, which suggests the path the eu should take in the context of the enp. in particular, i agree with the call to maintain the principle of differentiation in relations with individual states, to strengthen coordination between the enp and activities under the common foreign and security policy, and to support partners in implementing more and stricter security controls in order to have a better capacity to defend themselves against terrorist and criminal attacks.
in writing. ‒ although the initial proposal for this report was highly problematic, the final compromise reached by the legal affairs committee was an improvement and was accepted by the italian stakeholders themselves, albeit with reservations. this report is intended to be a basis for the commission, when it presents its proposals we can get into the more important and incisive issues for the italian market and to protect the interests of small and mediumsized enterprises not consumers. i therefore consider that, all things considered, this text is a good starting point and i support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the dissemination of culture in its broadest sense is one of the pillars of the union, as is the legal protection of its authors and artists. the issues raised are of great relevance, as the need for copyright legislation to be adapted to the digital age has become apparent. the report on the implementation of the directive on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society has been the subject of a lively debate. the contents of the report, concerning freedom of opinion, have provoked strong reactions from the public. today's vote concludes a healthy process of democratic dialogue in which political representatives respond to the concerns and needs of european voters. for these reasons, i support the solutions and the guidelines contained in this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i am convinced that, given the enormous change in the technological environment, which has profoundly changed the market for works of art, there is a need for harmonisation of copyright, especially with a view to a digital single market, in which digital works of art will play a fundamental role.
in writing. ‒ the digital revolution has radically transformed society, the way we live, travel, work and communicate. the european union must be at the forefront of this transformation by overcoming the digital divide and defending the fundamental rights of digital users, as exemplified by the free panorama regulation in italy. citizens have the right to the protection of their personal data and to the security and confidentiality of their communications. at the same time, we have to realize that the internet has great creative potential that we can now unlock. the reduction of legal differences between the member states in the field of copyright is beneficial for the free circulation of images, the audiovisual market, the promotion of landscape and cultural tourism, and the fluidity of the world of amateur and author photography. researchers will have lower costs to sift through and analyse large amounts of data with positive implications for their work. online courses may include more copyrighted material. we will have more transparency on copyright fees and the destination of the money collected. the world today is like a great global city deeply interconnected or a vast sea full of currents and information: it is up to us europeans to decide whether we want to be at the centre of it or be pushed to the margins.
in writing. - i vote for it. the compromise reached by the legal affairs committee, which was an improvement on the initial proposal, was 'accepted with reservations' by the main italian stakeholders. the own-initiative report is intended as a suggestion to the commission; the commission will be able to go into more detail on the important issues when it presents its proposals (the role of service providers and intermediaries, geo-blocking, the use of recorded material in public places, etc.). the protection of works must be given priority in copyright matters, preserving intellectual property from the abuses and fraudulent uses that are often seen on the internet. at the same time, the wide use of digital tools must allow for the full (and, where appropriate, cross-border) use of content. the text seems to be a good starting point for exclusive rights and exceptions. the overall opinion is therefore favourable.
in writing. ‒ the report examines key aspects of intellectual property and goes far beyond this, to redefining the boundaries and the way in which related rights are exercised in the information society. our society aims to be 'intellectual property rights intensive', and this fact should make us aware that we are acting on (as well as on) the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. i am thinking of freedom of expression, the protection of personal data and intellectual property, and i am referring symbolically to the threat to freedom of panorama. taking pictures of a public place, a monument or architecture and being able to share them should be the prerogative of every european citizen. the perception of the beauty - or even the problematic - of our urban environment must be elevated, not restricted, and freely transmitted and shared. obviously, there are remedies when privacy is violated or when the footage is commercialized. it therefore requires a massive effort (given the vastness of the subject) but at the same time surgical, to redefine and rationalize, before even deciding how much and how to liberalize, protect, discipline, modify. we are on the verge of a real redefinition of the work of art and of the intellect in general.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that copyright should be protected. but if we do not recognise a coherent and harmonised approach within the eu, it will always be easy to circumvent national rules. the dissemination of culture and knowledge is in the public interest and it is necessary that their authors and performers receive legal protection for the works they compose. it would be an excessive burden to ask them to pay 28 lawyers, one from each member state to defend their works. it is precisely against this situation that i am fighting, supporting harmonization also in the abovementioned field, which is the lifeblood of national and european culture and ingenuity. the duration of copyright, for example, is still very different in the various member states and there is an urgent need for harmonisation by the european legislator. as regards the right to a panorama, however, i take a different view: the commercial use of photographs, film or other images of works permanently located in public places shall not be subject to authorisation. it is in the interest of the whole community to be able to admire public property and to be able to photograph it without having to ask for permission and without having to pay.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this motion for a resolution because i believe that this directive represents a further and important development of the ambitious digital agenda project. i believe that copyright and related rights protect and stimulate both the development and marketing of new products and services and the creation and exploitation of their creative content, thus contributing to an improvement in competitiveness, employment and innovation in various industrial sectors in the eu. i therefore believe that it is necessary to encourage the harmonization in the individual member states of the terms of protection of copyright and related rights for each type of work and for each related right.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the implementation of directive 2001/29/ec because i share the need to adapt the existing framework in the light of developments in the digital age and to reduce the fragmentation of legislation on important issues such as the duration of copyright protection. it is important to address these challenges in order to help to consolidate the freedoms of movement that are the hallmark of the single market. i believe that there is a need to provide adequate protection for copyright and related rights, balancing the needs of users with the interests of the copyright holders.
in writing. this resolution on the revision of the copyright directive contained paragraph 46, which stated: 'the commercial use of photographs, film or other images of works permanently located in physical public places should always be subject to prior authorisation by the authors or a person delegated by them.' since this amendment was aimed at excluding freedom of panorama, i voted against it, bringing to the plenary the voice of the many citizens who have mobilized in recent days to remove from the final text the proposal to restrict the right to photograph public space freely. once this amendment was removed from the text, i was able to vote in favour of the whole report. apart from the amendment excluding freedom of panorama, the rest of the resolution provided the commission with some useful ideas to consider in the reform of the infosoc directive, a directive which was intended to harmonize certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society, but which now - after 11 years - needs to be revised in the light of the current methods of creating, producing and using content on the computer, which are determined by technological progress.
in writing. ‒ i support this own-initiative report, albeit with some important reservations, but overall the text seems to be a good starting point. the proposal will serve as an incentive for the commission when it submits its proposals.
in writing. ‒ with this resolution we have sent a strong message to the commission: copyright must be adapted to the digital age by ensuring the right balance between the rights and interests of creators and consumers. we must ensure that the creators are properly remunerated; we need to provide users with legal certainty for their daily actions. finally, we must ensure inclusive access to culture and knowledge. we have managed to reject the proposal to restrict the right to freely photograph public space. europe is a territory rich in cultural heritage that bears witness to our history and the evolution of our culture, and i firmly believe in the potential of sharing our landscapes and our cultural heritage.
in writing. i voted in favour of mrs reda's report on the harmonization of certain aspects of copyright and related rights. the infosoc directive introduced minimum levels of copyright protection without setting rules for the protection of the interests of users and the public, and thus without harmonising copyright law at european level, which has led to further fragmentation of national copyright legislation. this report will continue to promote investment in the creative sector, giving industries the opportunity to use digital technologies and end-users better access to them.
in writing. ‒ considering that the implementation of the infosoc copyright directive has not led to the harmonisation of copyright which many parties wanted, i have decided to support this report, which calls for coordination of certain aspects of copyright and related rights in the information society.
in writing. ‒ the completion of the single market, including its digital economy aspects, is of crucial importance for europe. the benefits to consumers of an integrated digital society are well known. the objective importance of the creative and cultural industries for the european economy is equally well known, amounting to eur 500 billion of gdp and 7 million workers. for these enterprises and workers, creativity and culture are real 'factors of production'. copyright is therefore a driving force for the cultural and creative industries, so that they continue to be a strategic sector for competitiveness, growth and employment in europe. the report therefore not only ensures fairer and easier access to cultural content for consumers, but also protects the right of artists and producers to fair remuneration for the product of their work. a protection of cultural investment which is essential for a europe united in diversity. the safeguarding of europe's 'cultural diversity' requires particular attention to the specificities and customs of the regions, which the report clearly emphasises. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution to promote sustainable, inclusive and culturally pluralistic growth in the eu.
in writing. ‒ harmonising copyright protection is of paramount importance to ensure that creative industries in europe continue to develop. in a context where infringement of intellectual property is on the agenda, i thank mrs reda for her work and hope that i have made a contribution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr reda on the harmonisation of certain aspects of copyright and related rights. this report, which i initially found dubious, was a report on the need to strike the right balance between copyright protection in the digital age, which also helps to ensure respect for europe's cultural diversity, and access to content and services by citizens. after several negotiations in committee, the epp succeeded in getting a text adopted which reflects the balance of rights indicated in the compromises. one point in the text that i find particularly interesting is the possibility given to industry to embrace digital technologies to ensure better access for the end user. the digital game is one that europe is playing on several fronts, and the creative sector will also benefit from important results.
in writing. - i voted against it with conviction and regret. i regret that, because julia reda had written a very good report. i am convinced of that, because it has been changed to the point of being unacceptable. first of all, the underlying 'philosophy' is unacceptable: culture is considered a commodity produced for profit. michelangelo didn't paint the sistine chapel to charge for admission. this relationship suffocates in the cradle the artistic inspiration of any author. the ability to rework other people's content is also reduced to the ability to make caricatures and pastiches. if ancient rome had copyright laws like these, it could not have passed down buildings and statues, since they were frequently reworkings of greek models. latin writers like plautus or terence, instead of occupying a prominent place in the history of literature, would have ended up in trouble for copyright infringement held by greek authors. with such rules, the entire italian renaissance would not have been because the starting point and inspiration of artists and literati were the works handed down from ancient rome and greece. unfortunately, the majority of the european parliament voted against art and culture when it adopted this report.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the eu's new approach to human rights and democracy which focused on the evaluation of the activities of the european endowment for democracy (eed) since its establishment. as enshrined in article 21 of the treaty on european union and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, the promotion and support of democracy, the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights and freedoms are fundamental objectives of the european union. despite its short period of activity and limited funds, the european democracy fund has fostered and encouraged the process of democratization in countries undergoing political transition by promoting dialogue in diversity and non-violence, encouraging social and political participation, and protecting activists and journalists working in the territories to ensure and accelerate the start of a democratic process. the resolution underlines the uniqueness and added value of the eed and lays the foundations for the development of new and innovative means and instruments for democracy assistance. that is why i voted for it today.

in writing. ‒ the defence and strengthening of democracy are essential objectives of the union, within and across its borders. the european union has a long history of supporting the development of the countries of central and eastern europe, and the community has a long history of supporting the development of the countries of central and eastern europe. the european democracy fund (edf) - despite the short time since its establishment, the fact that 12 countries (unfortunately including italy) have not yet secured their contributions and some other critical points - has played an appreciable role in supporting the development of democratic regimes in the eastern and southern european neighbourhood, for example by supporting, with concrete interventions, freedom of expression and association, freedom of the media and the fight against corruption. the resolution recognises the strategic role of the eed and lays the foundations for its further strengthening (including in terms of human resources), in particular by focusing on support for victims of social and/or political marginalization, women's movements, minorities, grassroots movements, trade unions, vulnerable or emerging political movements, and new media activists. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i am convinced that this fund has achieved its objectives. despite the difficult period in which it is operating, the short time of its activities and the limited funds, its activities to promote and encourage democracy seem to have been well promoted. democracy remains one of the fundamental principles of the eu's foreign policy and property rights remain the key to promoting a genuine democratic culture. a large number of member states have recently completed the process of democratization, and have accumulated a great deal of experience in this field. this same experience could easily be transferred to those who have yet to reach a more mature stage of their political and social stage. the edd's work must, however, be directed towards ensuring internal and external coherence in relation to the efforts made to achieve democracy, including by informing potential beneficiaries of the fund of what is at stake.
in writing. ‒ in recent years, multiple political, economic and security challenges have jeopardised the processes of democratisation and the assertion of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the eu's neighbourhood. i am aware that democracy assistance activities are by their nature complex, as the political transformations taking place in the countries concerned are not linear. therefore, welcoming the eed's continued commitment to promoting democracy in complementarity with the european external financial instruments, i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i think it appropriately underlines our concern about the difficult situation that has arisen in burundi. president nkurunziza's decision to run for a third term in the general elections has caused great dissatisfaction among the opposition, who have started to rebel and protest against the outgoing president as they consider his candidacy unconstitutional. the situation reached a climax on 13 may when a group of soldiers, led by general niyombare, attempted a coup d'état, taking advantage of the president's absence. despite the coup being swiftly reversed by nkurunziza's return home, violence in the country has not ceased and the repression of protests has already caused over 70 deaths and the flight of over 120,000 residents to neighbouring countries, with the high risk of a domino effect. in the context of a serious economic crisis such as that in burundi, one of the poorest countries in the world, it is important that all parties concerned find a peaceful and lasting solution, in order to respect the arusha agreement and the constitution, in order to resume a democratic process that goes beyond personal interests and to the benefit of the people of burundi.
in writing. ‒ the decision of the burundian government to hold new elections despite the critical political and security situation has aggravated an already complex political and humanitarian situation in burundi and the surrounding region. i am aware of the role of the international community in the region as guarantor of the arusha accords and that institutions such as the international criminal court are very important in the conduct of independent investigations into the violence and crimes committed in burundi. i therefore believe that only through dialogue with the burundian government can a lasting political solution be found in the interests of the security and democracy of that country, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the political and humanitarian situation in burundi has deteriorated dramatically in recent months and, as many non-governmental organizations have reported, the protests have been triggered by president pierre nkurunziza's announced decision to run for a third term, contrary to the country's constitutional charter. tensions have increased, forcing more than 130,000 people to flee to neighbouring countries and creating further instability in an already fragile region, prompting the government to postpone the upcoming elections. the resolution, for which i voted in favour, calls on the parties concerned to respect the commitments they have made in the framework of long-standing international and regional treaties, recalling that there can be no impunity for those responsible for serious human rights violations.
in writing. ‒ the political and social situation in burundi has worsened further since the political elections on 29 june, when president pierre nkurunziza announced that he would run for a third term. the re-election would not respect the arusha agreements signed between the hutu and tutsi ethnic groups in 2000, which were intended to end the bloody seven-year civil war that has claimed more than 300,000 lives. according to the country's constitution, each president can be elected for only two terms, so the re-election of president nkurunziza would be against the constitution. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution because i hope that a solution can be found to the political crisis in burundi.

in writing. ‒ by supporting this resolution, parliament expresses its utter disapproval of the decision of the burundian government to hold presidential elections. president nkurunziza's third term runs counter to the spirit of article 96 of the burundian constitution and is in open violation of the arusha peace and reconciliation agreement which stipulates that a president can only serve two terms. the june 29 election was already held in a climate of intimidation, violence and the restriction of the main fundamental freedoms of the opposition and civil society, including freedom of expression and information. the situation is not improving, but is worsening day by day, both politically and humanitarianally, in burundi and the surrounding region. we are calling for the postponement of the presidential elections on 15 july in the interests of the security and democracy of the burundian people. we call for those responsible for acts of violence and repression to be subject to targeted restrictive measures, including asset freezes, as well as visa and travel bans.

in writing. ‒ next 11 july marks the 20th anniversary of the srebrenica massacre, which led to the deaths of over 8 000 bosnian muslim men and women and was defined by the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia as an act of genocide. it is imperative for the european union to pass on the memory of this tragedy and to commit itself to ensuring that such horrendous crimes are not repeated. the resolution i have signed calls for the european union to continue its efforts to bring the countries and peoples of the balkan region closer together, so as to ensure a more stable future from today. policies for economic development, culture and education have a key role to play in supporting a process aimed at ensuring peace, human rights and inter-religious debate in an area where difficult relationships and delicate balances undermine the unity of civil society itself. the european union must be ready to support this work of reconciliation.

in writing. ‒ reconciliation needs justice to be possible and justice needs truth to be authentic. bosnia-herzegovina still needs reconciliation, justice and truth today. what happened in srebrenica 20 years ago is an indelible stain on our european conscience: there is no justification for what was the worst crime committed in europe since the end of the second world war. the coordinated, systematic, planned slaughter of thousands of men, women and children from above can only be described in one word: it was genocide. if the union were to ignore a fact of such moral and political gravity which took place so close to the capitals of our member states, it would betray the fundamental principle of the process of reconciliation itself: the will to ban war and ethnic and religious conflicts forever. we have a moral obligation to ensure truth and justice for the victims and we cannot accept that those responsible for the massacre are still unpunished: we must therefore support the association of mothers of the srebrenica and zepa enclaves and all those who work tirelessly to honour the memory of the people killed and to ensure that their killers are brought to justice.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament's resolution on the commemoration of the srebrenica massacre. 11 july 2015 marks the anniversary of the genocide in which 8,000 muslim men were executed by the serbian army under the command of general ratko mladić, operating under the authority of then president of republika srpska radovan karadžić. the massacre has been recognized as genocide by both the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia and the international court of justice. the resolution commemorates the victims of the genocide (1 800 of whom are still unidentified), reaffirms the eu's commitment to bosnia and herzegovina and notes that regional cooperation and the process of european integration are the most appropriate approaches to promoting reconciliation in the region.

the digital single market strategy recently adopted by the commission. the eu is committed to promoting human rights in all areas of its external action. nowadays, given the increasing importance of ict in our daily lives and the expansion of internet access and access to mobile telephony, the promotion of human rights online and offline and the linkage between new technologies and human rights are key to our endeavours towards promoting human rights and democracy worldwide. we therefore share the european parliament’s view that icts are key in safeguarding and fostering human rights and fundamental freedoms. we also share the concern voiced in the report that certain fundamental rights, notably the right to freedom of expression and information, the right to privacy and the protection of personal data, may be violated as a result of unlawful or arbitrary surveillance, censorship, the unlawful interception of communications, or the collection of personal data, in particular when carried out on a mass scale and not for legitimate purposes. this requires us all to unite in our efforts to protect fundamental rights. we need to promote the development of democratic oversight capabilities in order to monitor activities by intelligence and law enforcement services, lest these are used to suppress dissent and free speech. this is firmly anchored in the eu guidelines for freedom of expression online and offline, and we are highly committed to promoting these guidelines in our relations with third countries. that is also why the commission is very supportive of, and welcomes, the appointment of the united nations special rapporteur on the right to privacy. it is very important to ensure that our response to terrorist attacks does not impact negatively on fundamental rights, notably freedom of expression and information and the right to privacy. the european security agenda adopted by the commission this year has made clear, therefore, that the commission will strictly test any security measures for compliance with fundamental rights, while ensuring their effectiveness. the eu is committed to assisting human rights defenders, civil society activists, and independent journalists to use icts to fight for freedom. the eu is also active in defending media freedom and pluralism, and has launched two new independent projects within the framework of the european centre for press and media freedom, with the support of this parliament. the projects will address media freedom violations in the eu and neighbouring countries and promote action to support threatened journalists, complemented by digital training. the european union has also adopted sanctions to prevent authoritarian regimes using technologies to crack down on human rights defenders, for example in the case of syria. in addition to country-specific sanctions, the eu is reviewing its export controls to prevent exports of sensitive technologies that could be misused in violation of human rights. in december 2014 we introduced new controls on exports of intrusion software and of internet monitoring technologies, and we are further exploring options to extend export controls to rapidly evolving cyber-surveillance technologies that might be used for internet monitoring and/or telecommunication surveillance in violation of human rights. as ms schaake writes in the report, there is indeed a need to mainstream the impact of technologies on the improvement of human rights in all the eu’s external action. the commission and the external action service are working together towards this goal. icts have helped to promote freedom on a global scale, and preserving the benefits of freedom is a shared responsibility for all of us – the private sector, civil society, governments, international organisations and individuals. the european union stands, therefore, ready to reiterate its commitment to promote unhindered, uncensored and non-discriminatory access to icts.

member of the commission.– madam president, i would like, on behalf of the commission, to thank the european parliament, and in particular, ms boylan, for the report on the follow-up to the european citizens’ initiative ‘right2water’. as the commission has made clear in its response to the initiative, water is not a commercial product like any other, but rather a heritage which must be protected, defended and treated as such. access to it cannot be taken for granted, although many people in europe do so. the commission has always underlined that an important condition for providing access to water is the preservation and protection of water resources. this is a cornerstone of eu environment policy. the eu directives on drinking water and urban wastewater treatment, as well as the water framework directive, set the standards for water and sanitation and provide the basis for integrated water resource management. as your report states, globally, access to water and sanitation is a global issue of huge importance. fifteen years on from the un millennium declaration, the statistics are still challenging: 748 million people still do not have access to safe drinking water and 2.5 billion people lack access to basic levels of sanitation. therefore i welcome sustainable development goal 6, which aims to ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all. the sdgs are at the core of the post-2015 agenda. the eu stands ready to play its full part in its implementation, both through its external action as well as its internal policies and actions, and i hope that we will be able to gather momentum with all partners to achieve universal access in the not too distant future. i wish to reaffirm the commission’s position on the importance of the human rights dimension of access to safe drinking water and sanitation, including within the eu itself. firstly, the commission recognises the importance of water as a public good. the provision of water services is in general the responsibility of the local authorities, as they are closest to the citizens. secondly, the commission has clarified the principle of neutrality. treaty rules require the eu to remain neutral in relation to national decisions governing the ownership regime for water undertakings, be it public or private. moreover, eu rules on concessions acknowledge the specificity of water. works and services concerning drinking water and sanitation have been excluded from the scope of the concessions directive, and the subsidiarity principle regarding the choice of method of water management has been fully recognised. this also applies to trade deals. no eu trade deal has ever restricted eu member states’ freedom to organise their public services – including water – the way they choose. ttip – the transatlantic trade and investment partnership – will be no different. thirdly, i re-confirm the commission’s commitment to a number of actions which will ensure that these principles remain at the heart of its policies, and i welcome the emphasis placed in the committee’s report on the importance of member states implementing eu legislation. the commission will build on existing legislation and policies to continue to increase and improve access to safe drinking water and sanitation for the whole population through environmental policies and infrastructure funding. let me now emphasise again the positive impact the citizens’ initiative has had on putting water issues high on the political agenda. we welcome your numerous calls on the commission for action. the commission is carefully considering them in the context of a number of actions, for example in the evaluation of the drinking water directive, the preparation of the water re-use initiative and the upcoming review of the water framework directive, and the ongoing dialogue with the stakeholders – including the initiators of the citizens’ initiative – on benchmarking water quality and services. to conclude, i would like to add an important element. eu water policies and activities over the past decades have allowed access to adequate sanitation and drinking water services for the large majority of eu citizens. challenges remain. member states play a big role in the implementation of eu legislation, while further targeted action by the commission is under way. we all have to play together in ensuring full compliance with eu water legislation, thus helping to ensure access to clean water and sanitation for all citizens throughout the eu. we welcome the strong support and additional calls from this house for more ambitious action, in particular to involve citizens and to provide more transparency. also, the call for access to safe drinking water and sanitation is much welcomed and will be taken into account in future commission work. as regards the european citizens’ initiative tool itself, i am pleased to note that this major innovation introduced by the lisbon treaty is now up and running and involving citizens more closely in eu agenda-setting. however, there is still clearly room for improvement. in the report on the application of regulation no 211/2011 on the citizens’ initiative published on 31 march 2015, the commission took stock of this situation after three years of application. the report identified a number of issues in the current functioning of the instrument as a basis for further discussion and reflection on how to improve it. the commission is now awaiting input from stakeholders, in particular the own initiative report of the european parliament on eci. this report will feed into the commission’s analysis on how to improve the functioning of the european citizens’ initiative and make the tool as effective as possible. the commission is looking forward to further cooperation with parliament on both these important issues: the follow-up of the right2water initiative and the evolution of the tool.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, parliament has a great responsibility to shoulder today: the commission's task is to make clear to our trading partners and competitors, across the atlantic or in asia, that we are not prepared to trade the health of our citizens, our families and future generations for food of dubious origin and quality! we are well aware that the directive deals with farm animals and that our farmers are facing strong foreign competition today, due to uncontrolled practices such as cloning. but we also know that europe bases its value on the quality of its products and not on mere quantity. the question of the production and marketing within the european union of products derived from cloned animals is a matter of concern to us and one to which we must pay due attention, but without underestimating the health and welfare of animals, of their offspring and what unstable dna can do to human health. there are known cases of premature death of clones, mutilation of offspring, and poisoning of surrogate mothers who have undergone heavy hormonal and antibiotic treatments. but if we know all this, there is still doubt about the nutritional value of a cloned food, or rather a food derived from the offspring of a clone - which is what we then import from third countries - and what consequences it may have for humans after continuous administration. we are therefore called upon to protect the welfare of the citizens, to take responsibility for marketing, importing or using such food. are we ready to turn our families and future generations into guinea pigs? mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i should like to begin by thanking mrs sommer and mr moi for their commitment to this difficult work on a subject as sensitive as animal cloning, which at first sight seems to involve only scientific aspects, but which in reality has profound ethical implications and clearly has a strong impact on public opinion which has debated and continues to debate it. the main arguments on which our position against animal cloning and its use for agricultural purposes is based are essentially two: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of animals during transport. efsa stated in 2008 and has repeatedly reiterated its position that there are serious health risks to cloned animals which often lead to their death. in fact, there are success rates of between 6 and 15% in cattle, experiences of difficult births for the offspring, of neonatal death. unfortunately, the technological progress of recent years has not brought the improvements we all expected. secondly, we cannot ignore the views of our european citizens: recent surveys have found that over 80% of european citizens are against animal cloning and an equally high percentage of consumers are against the consumption of food derived from animal clones. there are certainly parts that could be changed. our position - but i think the vote as a whole is parliament's position - should be supported.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the tragic events of our time show that national borders are no longer the limits of a single state, but constitute the external frontier of the european union as a whole. this is especially true of trade. take the case of xylella. the epidemic now raging in southern italy, in puglia, was spread by plants imported into europe at the port of rotterdam. what does that mean? that decisions taken in a single port, in a single passage, can have repercussions throughout the european territory: false declarations as to the origin of the imported goods; false designations of types; abuse of the transitional arrangements. these are all illegal practices by which low-quality products are introduced into the union. low-quality products that evade controls and security measures, deceptive products that compete with local products on our store shelves, counterfeit products that penetrate through stretches of our customs network. we have a duty to protect genuine products, local products, because they represent quality, history, traditions, jobs and social welfare. the rules are there to protect us, but they must be applied seriously, effectively and above all consistently. so we welcome these tools which enable the various national authorities responsible to monitor and verify what is coming into europe, to exchange information and best practice more effectively. this will give a considerable impetus to the interpretation of community rules without any doubt or uncertainty, and will help us to ensure that the borders of the european union represent a real wall for all those who would like to do illegal business.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this regulation is the result of important work on a fundamental subject, namely the strengthening of the european internal market, which is something we are fighting for every day. these rules will actually improve the detection, investigation and prevention of customs fraud, increase the exchange of information and available evidence, and, in my view, make the system even more effective. two aspects in my view deserve to be highlighted: firstly, this regulation provides customs officials with new means of verifying whether the declared origin of the goods is consistent with the actual journey made in the container, because this is often not the case. this is a very important aspect, both for the proper functioning of the free movement of goods and for the protection of european consumers. secondly, the member states must be able to provide the commission with the data necessary for the verification of potential fraud; this was not the case before, as the documentation was carried out only by economic operators. the negotiations were long and complex, but i think we can all be satisfied today with the work that this legislation has produced, and i congratulate all those who have worked towards this objective because the result has been focused.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking mrs jaakonsaari for her excellent work on this complex and difficult subject, which has been met with much resistance, but the conclusion is an important one for the many reasons which have already been mentioned in the debate. i would like to return briefly to three aspects which i consider to be the most significant. the first, of course, is consumer certainty: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the products are not altered or counterfeited, and that the products are not presented in a way that is different from what they are perceived to be. the second theme concerns competition between companies too, all counterfeiting has an immediate, almost automatic effect, altering relations between companies, between those who behave honestly, produce according to the rules, respect them and those who, on the other hand, put second-level products on the market, do so through alteration processes that lead to negative consequences, both on the people who then consume, but also on the economic relations between companies. finally, there is one aspect that i would not like to be forgotten, and that is the contrast with crime: where there is counterfeiting, there is normally the presence of illegal activity that fuels crime. so anything that is transparent, anything that is compliant, also helps to fight crime.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the amendments to regulation 515 of 1997 are only apparently technical, but they have a significant political value in the current international economic and social context. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud and abuse of customs legislation, and these are putting a quality production system such as the european one at risk every day. all this requires greater attention and control on the part of europe, in order to guarantee consumers safe products and fair and fair competition for businesses, as we are being asked to do, even at this hour, by the agricultural world. to achieve these goals, we need to strengthen our anti-fraud mechanisms, making them more effective, more transparent, making full use of the new opportunities of digital, thus ensuring maximum traceability of goods. amendments to this regulation can be a useful part of a wider strategy to crack down on the many unfair practices in european and international trade.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of janusz korwin-mikke. on 13 march 2015, the president informed, pursuant to rule 9 (1), that he had received a letter from the prosecutor general of poland requesting the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of mr janusz korwin-mikke. having examined the documentation, the commission considered that it should submit to the ep a decision to waive the immunity, considering that the allegations clearly have no relation to the office of mep. at the time of the incident, janusz korwin-mikke was driving his car in a residential area of piotrków trybunalski, exceeding the speed limit of 50 km/h by 32 km/h, according to a speedometer located in the area. furthermore, there is no reason to suppose that a fumus persecutionis exists.
in writing. ‒ the parliamentary committee responsible for privileges and immunities, after examining the case of the polish member's violation of the traffic code, ruled that there was no direct link between the office of parliamentarian and the offence in question, denying the immunity of the same from the judicial procedure requested. the action of a member of parliament does not constitute a political opinion or a vote expressed in the exercise of his parliamentary functions, but a fact which is entirely unrelated to the exercise of political office. i fully agree with the position of the committee of inquiry, as the case has been the subject of a thorough and transparent investigation which has found that there was no specific intention to cause political damage to the member concerned. the procedure sought against him is the proper application of national law.

in writing. ‒ although members of the european parliament normally enjoy immunity, it is possible to waive this privilege in any case, provided that the offence committed is not connected with the performance of the person's public duties. in this case, i think it is appropriate to proceed with a case against mr korwin-mikke, who is accused of exceeding the legal speed limit while driving his car. i have therefore decided to support this report which involves the waiver of his parliamentary immunity.

in writing. i am absolutely in favour of a total ban on the marketing of animal clones, embryonic clones and food products for human consumption derived from animal clones and their offspring. it is a matter of precaution, not only of concern for possible ethical implications, but also of respect for animal health and welfare standards. the cloning technique still raises concerns, which are further exacerbated by the fact that no third country has established reliable traceability and labelling or identification and registration systems for the purpose of importing the offspring of clones or food products derived from them. furthermore, there are no international standards on sanitary and phytosanitary measures for cloning, and no scientific studies on the effects on human health of the prolonged consumption of food derived from animal cloning. finally, i can only stress the importance of taking due account of public opinion against animal cloning and the consumption of food derived from cloned animals.
in writing. ‒ the european food safety authority (efsa) has repeatedly highlighted how the health and welfare of a significant proportion of animal clones has often been seriously and lethally compromised. in particular, abnormalities in clones and the unusually large size of cloned foetuses result in difficult births and deaths at birth. i voted in favour of this measure banning the cloning of animals for food in the european union because i believe it is essential that european consumers should not risk eating food from a cloned animal or its descendants on their plates.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation because it prohibits the use and marketing of cloned animals and their offspring. we voted to make the ban on the use of cloning for the production of farm animals permanent, rather than temporary as proposed by the european commission, by means of a review clause to be used in the event that the progress of scientific research requires an update of eu legislation. to date, the success rate of experiments is only 10 percent, while the mortality rate is high and many animals are born with deformities or immune problems and then die prematurely. we also decided that the ban should apply to the marketing of products from cloned animals or their offspring and that the eu should provide for clear labelling to ensure that products are traceable. for these purposes, we have chosen the regulation as the legislative instrument, not a directive, so as to ensure that in such a sensitive matter there are the same rules in all the member states.

in writing. ‒ the controversial issue of animal cloning for agricultural purposes has always raised not only strong concerns related to health, animal welfare and consumer choice, but also ethical issues, as well as a long-term regulatory challenge. although animal cloning for food production purposes is not allowed in the european union, agricultural cloning for commercial purposes takes place in several countries including argentina, australia, brazil, canada and the united states, and may also be carried out in chile, china, new zealand and uruguay. the growing trade with these countries therefore requires new and increasingly stringent regulations due to the lack of reliable traceability and labelling, or identification and registration systems, for import purposes. in view of the recent conclusions and recommendations of the european food safety authority, which have recognised the existence of risks to animal health and welfare, we are today approving this proposal for a directive which aims to ensure regulatory consistency with the wto framework and a level playing field within the internationally regulated system.

in writing. ‒ the hearing procedure is not provided for in the lisbon treaty. this is a practice developed over the last 20 years which has required candidates for the office of commissioner to appear before the parliamentary committees corresponding to their portfolio before parliament's vote of confidence in the commission. the public hearings of candidates for the european commission give the european parliament the opportunity to learn about each candidate's priorities and to assess their qualifications. if the debate reveals problems, parliament could thus oppose the nomination of the candidate and ask for his replacement. the report aims to draw conclusions from the last round of commissioner hearings and to propose some ideas which could lead to a change in procedures. i believe that a deadline should be set for the member states to propose their candidates; apply clear guidelines for the evaluation meeting of coordinators following the hearings and ensure transparency and visibility of the letters of approval. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the role of the european parliament in choosing the college of commissioners is essential. the new rules for the hearing of commissioners will bring greater efficiency and transparency and bring citizens closer to the world of politics. the european parliament has decided to set a deadline for member states to nominate their candidates, who must be at least two, one man and one woman. in addition, the publicity of the letters of approval will be ensured and the evaluation will be completed within 24 hours.

in writing. ‒ in today's globalised and interconnected world, the internet is a familiar experience for billions of people. being cut off from the internet means having drastically reduced opportunities to communicate, to inform themselves, to further their studies, to improve their economic situation, to form an autonomous civic and political consciousness. the right to internet access must be recognised as a human right because it is now an integral part of the right to social inclusion and non-discrimination of every citizen. the global spread of high-speed communications systems cannot ignore the serious violations of privacy and freedom of expression that some institutions, public and private, can commit by exploiting ict. strong and clear union action is needed to protect the security of communications and the freedom of expression and information of all ict users: the new technologies must be a tool for promoting freedom and democracy, never a means for mass surveillance and control. in this sense, the union is morally obliged to ensure its protection of whistleblowers and humanitarian activists who reveal abusive surveillance systems in third countries: freedom and security are not adversaries but must march together, in europe as in the rest of the world.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on family businesses, given the importance and the major socioeconomic role they play at both national and european level. the lack of a definition of family businesses in terms of turnover means that they can be classified as either micro or multinational and this may create uncertainty in the targeted policies to be adopted. i believe that the role played by these companies is of great importance for our economic growth and the reduction of unemployment. the report proposes to extend the sme instruments to medium-cap family businesses. it is also hoped that the commission will present a work plan setting out appropriate measures for the growth of these enterprises. to this end, i believe that an analysis of the existing rules is necessary to identify the obstacles to their growth and possible internationalisation, allowing family businesses easier access to information on european legislation and funding.
in writing. - i voted against the niebler report on family-controlled enterprises. this is not because we are against this type of enterprise but because a paragraph has been inserted in the report asking the commission to extend the beneficiaries of funds for smes to medium-cap family-controlled enterprises (mid-caps) and to make them use the existing specific instruments for smes (which by definition are only those which meet certain budgetary, turnover and number of employees criteria). it is already very difficult for small businesses to apply for these instruments, and the application approved in this report makes the reality for smes even more difficult: mid-caps have more resources both in terms of organisation and human resources, while small and medium-sized enterprises have much more difficulty applying for european funds or funding through programmes such as cosme or horizon2020. this goes against our objective of protecting a category as fundamental to our country as smes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the protocol amending the marrakesh agreement establishing the world trade organisation. the trade facilitation agreement (tfa), concluded by the 159 wto members (including the eu and member states) at the 9th ministerial conference in december 2013, is the first multilateral agreement concluded by the wto since its establishment 20 years ago. the aim of the agreement is to simplify and speed up the movement and clearance of goods worldwide and requires greater cooperation between customs authorities. the text of the agreement includes rules on issues such as transparency and information requirements for customs authorities, appeal and review procedures, tariff and fee regulations, documentation requirements and special and differential treatment for developing countries. the agreement will enter into force when ratified by two thirds of wto members. the european parliament's consent to this agreement is required to ensure that the eu meets its obligations as a wto member and to contribute to the successful conclusion of the 10th wto ministerial conference to be held in nairobi in december.

in writing. ‒ the budapest convention, which entered into force on 1 april 2005, contributes to the functioning of the internal market in transport by harmonising contractual and inland navigation rules at european level. austria and poland have expressed their interest in becoming parties to the convention. their participation will promote the large-scale implementation of this legal instrument for the benefit of citizens and businesses. belgium ratified the budapest convention on 5 august 2008. a retroactive authorisation is therefore necessary in order to regularise the current irregular situation. the draft decision therefore authorises belgium and poland to ratify the budapest convention and austria to accede to it. i voted in favour of this report on assent.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of a temporary and emergency system for the relocation of 40,000 asylum seekers from italy and greece, who are under intolerable pressure, to other eu countries over a period of two years. however, this emergency relocation is only a first, provisional step towards implementing the principle of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility between all member states. i therefore ask the commission to present a legislative proposal on a permanent relocation mechanism by the end of 2015. we must also look at the long term, considering the problem of the dublin system, the community regulation on political asylum, which is rendered ineffective by the non-equalisation of national asylum systems. dublin says that refugees must apply for asylum in the country of first entry. and this is a problem, because there are only a limited number of countries that have an external border. reforms are therefore urgently needed to overcome the shortcomings of the current dublin system and to arrive at a new system of fair distribution for all member states.
in writing. ‒ the report states parliament's support for the establishment of a permanent mechanism for compulsory relocation of refugees; this should be triggered automatically when a particularly intense flow of migrants occurs, as is the case today. italy and greece are in fact obliged to take in thousands of refugees, and the treaty itself refers to the principle of solidarity in this matter. the report states that relocation measures are only a first, emergency step towards a system of equitable sharing of the responsibility for reception among all member states.

in writing. ‒ the proposal voted on today finally takes a 'european' approach to the issue of immigration. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as regards the particular plight of unaccompanied minors, i think it is important that the clarification has been introduced that the new mechanism should not reduce the protection already provided by the court of justice (which means that the protection obligations fall on the country where the child is actually present, even if different from the country of first arrival or the country where he or she has applied for asylum). other concerns remain, such as the scope of the decision, which is limited in number and strictly limited by the nationality of the refugees; the possibility of suspending the mechanism as a 'sanction' against italy or greece (but, in fact, to the further detriment of the applicants for protection); the absence of a time limit for the procedure, which starts from the arrival of the migrants, protects them. nevertheless, this decision in itself represents an important step forward and a very useful instrument in practice. i therefore voted in favour.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr high representative, i wish i could look to the future with a little more optimism for the middle east peace process, but i would be lying to myself. that is because the situation today tells us that the control of power in israel, as in palestine, is firmly in the hands of the most dangerous party of all: the party's over! this is true in israel, where the new netanyahu government appears to be crushed by its own electoral rhetoric, increasingly isolated and partly held hostage by the nationalist and ultra-orthodox parties that support it. and so every effort seems more catalyzed towards maintaining the status quo. to prevent a reconciliation between the palestinian factions, between hamas and fatah, in order to have no interlocutor; the european parliament has been very active in the negotiations on the nuclear agreement with iran, and i am sure that the council will be very active in the negotiations on the nuclear agreement with iran. the palestinians too have their own grave responsibilities, first and foremost, a ruling class now light years removed from the people they represent; abbas's resignation may be an act of desperation or a tactical move, time will tell, but it certainly sows uncertainty in the short term. we are therefore left in the grip of this eternal postponement, while gaza remains a vast, desolate open-air prison and illegal settlements continue. our role cannot be merely to finance infrastructure and projects which are often destroyed, it is good to involve the arab countries, it is good to revive the role of the quartet and to work on the conditions for regaining confidence, but if we do not get out of this quagmire with a strong, decisive and energetic policy on both sides so that there are no more, we will have neither a two-state solution nor an authority in the context and unfortunately we will sow the seeds of extremism and daesh even more.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, let us be clear: even in the present phase, which is still marked by pessimism, the analysis of the facts reminds us that the two-state solution has no alternative. a long time ago, shimon peres had to say that it is not true that there is no light at the end of the tunnel in the middle east, quite the opposite! he said there was light, but there's no tunnel. it was a bitter remark that comes to mind every time the difficulties between israel and palestine are repeated and the conflict, with greater or lesser intensity, has never stopped. and it is this perception of the intangible nature of conflict, of its inevitability independent of the world's efforts, that leads some to look for alternative solutions, to think that, before even going through it, you have to find the right tunnel. but the truth is that there is no alternative solution, because of all the viable ways to peace, there is only one. the tunnel is there, but we have to convince israelis and palestinians to go through it. the conditions for peace between israelis and palestinians have been known for years, perhaps for decades, and have been the basis of all the various peace negotiations, from madrid to oslo, from camp david to taba, from the road map to geneva. the impetus for the peace process, the two-state approach, is clearly indicated in the european parliament's resolution. i understand the difficulties you yourself have described, madam high representative, but it is the task of the european union to take stronger and more decisive action to this end. we must also be aware that if we are to put out the fires in the middle east, this is the first decisive step to take.

author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the principle of national jurisdiction requires that the sovereignty of a state be respected within its own borders, and the principle of the responsibility to protect requires that the state protect its own citizens and that other states intervene to that end where the sovereign state is unable or unwilling to do so. in this sense of international solidarity, which is legally required, we now call on the russian government to release two ukrainian and one estonian citizen who have been detained following summary trials that have failed to meet the standards of due process, including the refusal to respond to allegations of torture against the officers who conducted the interrogations. in the kohverla case, russia is accused, among other things, of crossing the estonian border and kidnapping an officer on duty. the trials of kolchenko and sentsov took place in crimea, a territory unilaterally annexed by russia and not recognized by the international community. this would therefore result in a lack of competence at territorial level. the civilian defendants were also tried by military courts with a clear lack of jurisdiction. the european parliament therefore calls for the basic principles of international law to be respected and for the release of those who are illegally detained.

author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, angola has been at the centre of controversy in the past over diamond mining. in 1998 the united nations imposed sanctions on countries that bought rough diamonds without a certificate of origin attesting to the correct mining process, in order to safeguard the safety of miners. rafael marques de morais was sentenced for denouncing this sadly well-known reality, that is, for a crime of opinion, in clear violation of the right to freedom of thought. the angolan government is turning to the courts of justice to muzzle human rights activists in the country. in the de morais case, international observers who attended the trial behind closed doors reported serious violations of the principle of due process. it is therefore important that the european union demands monitoring of diamond mining activity so that it is carried out in the most transparent way and in compliance with safety standards, while at the same time protecting activists who, in the exercise of their freedom of expression, denounce serious violations of human rights.

in writing. the white paper set out in 2011 an ambitious agenda for transforming the european transport system by setting targets to make it clean, safe, efficient and reliable. however, the level of integration of the eu transport market remains low compared to other elements of the economy. in fact, despite the funding made available by the efsi and the connecting europe facility, little has been done to date to improve the connectivity and efficiency of passenger and freight transport, multimodal networks of different modes and services. there is still much to be done in the field of energy efficiency to make transport sustainable and at the same time to make europe independent of oil and fossil fuels. concrete measures should also be implemented to ensure the application of the 'user pays' and 'polluter pays' principles. a common vision of change cannot be achieved without collaboration and coordination between all the actors working at not only european, but also national, regional and local levels. of course, this includes citizens and industry.
in writing. ‒ the european commission, in adopting the white paper 'roadmap to a single european transport area towards a competitive and sustainable transport policy' in 2011, identified the initiatives and measures to be taken in the context of transport policy in the decade 2011-2020. with 40 specific actions to be implemented by 2020, the commission aims to create a transport system with fewer barriers to market entry, better integration between different modes of transport, coherent infrastructure design and widespread use of new technologies. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report on the implementation of the 2011 white paper to ask the european commission to propose concrete measures and initiatives for a better implementation of the strategy and to insist on the need to maintain the levels of ambition set by the 2011 objectives. the report also stresses the importance of transport for the economy and for the mobility of citizens, while stressing the need to invest in infrastructure. the completion of the trans-european transport network is an essential requirement for a sustainable and efficient european transport system, which needs to be strengthened through the connecting europe facility (cef) and the european fund for strategic investments (efsi).
in writing. ‒ by adopting the report on the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport, we are calling for a european transport policy that prioritises sustainable and energy-efficient modes of transport, such as rail. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by rail. i supported this position because it is the only way to improve the quality of life of people living along transit routes and at the same time to ensure efficient transport of goods across europe. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the transport of dangerous goods by rail. the ban on excessively noisy freight wagons that we are calling for by 2020 will further promote the rehabilitation of old rolling stock and braking systems in freight wagons, and thus make a significant contribution to reducing noise emissions.
in writing. ‒ the resolution proposes good targets, such as reducing europe's dependence on oil imports, reducing transport emissions by 60% by 2050, using less polluting and more energy-efficient modes of transport, and opting for more sustainable solutions. all shared goals. however, i voted against this resolution because it calls for the priority approval of infrastructure projects to complete the rail network envisaged by the ten-t core network, with a strengthened role for the commission to ensure the effective and rapid completion of these priority european rail corridors. the resolution considers that eu funding should reflect the investment needs for the completion of the ten-t core network, and that the cef and other funding should stimulate investment in transport infrastructure with priority given to sustainable transport modes such as rail. i am opposed to investing in the major works planned for the ten-t networks, and financed through the cef, because one of these works is the turin-lyon tav, a project whose costs are excessive compared to their usefulness, with a huge environmental impact and damage to human health, not necessary to improve the quality of transport between france and italy and whose documents are inaccessible and managed in an opaque way.
in writing. i congratulate the committee on transport on the work it has done on this report, which is looking very carefully at the possible new stages in the development of the transport sector in europe. i think it is important to stress a passage in the text that has just been voted, which calls on the european commission to update its strategy in the light of the emission reduction targets and the new energy and climate policy proposals, in particular with regard to the achievement of the binding target of reducing national greenhouse gas emissions by at least 40% by 2030 compared to 1990 levels.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's own-initiative resolution on the implementation of the 2011 white paper on transport: i am very pleased that the commission has taken this initiative, and i hope that the commission will take it up with the council and the council. i believe that the eu has a duty to ensure that its citizens and future generations have safe, modern and efficient transport systems, which are also environmentally friendly and conducive to road traffic. i therefore welcome parliament's call for a transport policy in line with the 2030 environmental objectives: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. i believe that transport policy must be people-centred, and i therefore supported the call for a 40% reduction in the number of people seriously injured in road accidents, for improved road safety and for passenger rights to be protected. as transport is a driving force of the european economy in the global market and a primary source of employment, i fully share parliament's call for safe and dignified working conditions for workers in the sector, promoting quality work.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that it is essential for society, for the scientific world and for the european economy in general, to solve the problem of gender discrimination in science and academia. it is a very serious matter that women, in a developed continent like europe, represent only 18% of full-time professors, despite being 59% of graduate students.
in writing. ‒ the term 'glass ceiling' was coined in 1986 and refers to the invisible, prejudiced barriers that prevent women from rising to positions of responsibility in their careers. the academic career of women also remains markedly segregated vertically. in 2010, the proportion of female students (55%) and female graduates (59%) was higher than that of male counterparts, but men outnumbered women among students and phd holders (in the case of phds, the proportion of female students was 49% and that of female holders 46%). women also represented only 37% of the academic staff. the under-representation of women is even more evident in the fields of science and engineering. gender diversity in senior positions is shown to produce innovative ideas, increased competitiveness and better performance, and more efficient corporate management. more women in management also signals to the market that the company understands the complexity of global dynamics and is ready to compete. we need to overcome prejudices and stereotypes of the past and adopt legislation to ensure gender equality in all aspects of social and working life.
in writing. ‒ once again, the call is for equal rights for men and women, regardless of age, religion, marital status and educational background, especially in certain sectors where women are lacking (science, engineering, management, etc.). the principles themselves could be argued for, but as the cvs explain, the eu is imposing this on individual member states, without taking into account the principle of subsidiarity, which is dear and essential to us (e.g. "consider the creation of gender equality plans as a necessary condition for access to public funding for research, the scientific and academic sectors"). the following table is added: the term "glass ceiling" was coined by journalists at the wall street journal in 1986 and refers to the invisible, prejudiced barriers that prevent women from rising to positions of responsibility in the course of their careers. abstention from voting
