in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the european parliament's draft legislative resolution on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending protocol no 3 on the statute of the court of justice of the european union. in october 2014, the court of justice proposed to double the number of judges of the court (an additional twenty-eight). the council immediately agreed to the new proposals. however, it is not understood how in 2013 nine judges were sufficient to solve the problems of the court while in 2014 another twenty-eight are needed. the report stressed the lack of good faith in such a change in the number of judges, linking it to the council's decision, which was in favour of the proposal as it would allow each member state to appoint its own judge. i therefore voted against the council's position because it shows a profound disregard for european taxpayers' money, since each judicial office costs more than one million euro a year and the salaries of all of them would increase the eu's structural expenditure by more than twenty million euro a year.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice of the eu has proposed a legislative revision to appoint 12 new judges, due to the increase in workload. the ep voted in favour at first reading but the council failed to appoint any judges, so the court proposed to double the number of judges from 28 to 56. apart from this inconsistency, i believe that the european union should not appoint judges in the same way as it appoints political commissioners. the judges are not commissioners of the member states and should not be appointed as such. judges must be chosen for their technical and legal expertise and for their independence. only in this way can the quality of decision-making, honesty, impartiality and resistance to any pressure to which they may be subjected be guaranteed. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation, as i believe that the european parliament should reject the council's position for a number of reasons: firstly, because it shows a profound disregard for the money of the european taxpayer. secondly, for reasons also related to the dignity of justice itself, the eu should not in fact appoint judges in the same way as political commissioners. i also believe that the proposal of the court of justice, if implemented, could have serious long-term repercussions for the judicial system of the union. in fact, many elements of the proposal would require serious and impartial analysis and impact assessment. however, no cost-benefit analysis has been carried out. i also agree with the proposals for improvements to analyse the overall functioning of the union's judiciary, such as the recruitment of judges by open competition between professors of law of recognised merit and between judges of the higher courts of the individual member states, the appointment of each judge for a term of office of nine years only, with no renewal or extension, and full respect for gender equality in the recruitment of judges.
in writing. ‒ the gradual expansion of the powers of the court of justice of the european union since its establishment and the increasing assertion of european law in national legal systems have meant that the number of legal proceedings to be conducted by the general court has steadily increased. the failure to introduce measures of a procedural and organisational nature to improve the management of the burden of questions submitted to the court has had a negative impact on the length of the proceedings. i therefore welcome the proposal to increase the number of members of the european supreme court, so as to facilitate the work of the judges by making it faster and more effective, but at the same time more accurate and attentive, and also allowing european citizens to receive answers and protection of their rights in a reasonable time.
in writing. ‒ in 2011, the court of justice of the eu launched a legislative initiative to amend its statute and allow the appointment of an additional 12 judges to the court justified on the basis of an increase in the workload and the consequent need to reduce the workload per judge and the length of time. in the previous parliament, the ep adopted a first reading position confirming the court's request. however, the council did not appoint any of these 12 judges because the member states did not reach an agreement on the choice of judges. the court of justice has also been the subject of a number of legal proceedings, including the dismissal of the president of the tribunal and the dismissal of the president of the tribunal. the council immediately accepted these new proposals. the proposal would also double the number of referenda and assistants to over 100 and at a time when the eu is imposing severe austerity measures to balance member states' budgets, this is completely unjustified. for the reasons stated above, i vote against.
in writing. when the court of justice of the eu proposed a legislative revision in 2011 to appoint 12 new judges, citing the increase in workload, the ep voted in favour at first reading, thus approving the court's request. however, the council was unable to appoint any judges as no agreement was reached between the member states. the court therefore proposed doubling the number of judges from 28 to 56 in three stages, a proposal which was immediately accepted by the council. parliament must now ratify this new proposal. for our part, and in line with the rapporteur's position, we have tabled amendments to confirm the initial position, namely an increase of 12 judges. the increase in expenditure that would entail the hiring of such a high number of judges would require an increase in expenditure of over eur 20 million. more than 100 staff would have to be hired to support the judges. finally, i would like to make it clear that the judges of an independent body such as the court of justice should not be chosen by political appointments, but should be judged on their experience and independence, thus ensuring an impartial, independent and transparent decision-making process, all of which is lacking in this legislative initiative. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ europe forces italy to close the small courts, but then doubles its judges. this is what emerges from the hypocritical vote by which the european parliament, bending to the council's wishes, reformed the eu court of first instance by increasing its membership from 28 to 56. each new judge, with his office, will cost taxpayers one million euros a year. the reform, which arose from the court of justice's request to increase its staff to cope with excessive workload and the resulting delays, has become an opportunity for member states to increase the number of seats. the judges, however, should not be 'commissioners' of the member states and should not be appointed as such. the speed of justice does not require more judges but a more effective organization of the courts, perhaps alongside the specialised courts already provided for in the treaties. on the contrary, this reform, which was the prelude to the abolition of the civil service tribunal: the court of justice, which had been the first to give european rulings on mobbing and harassment in public offices. there are no more words... but only the vote against this scandalous reform.

in writing. ‒ the report we have adopted today starts from the consideration of the progressive enlargement of the powers of the european court of justice: in recent years, the number of cases brought before the community courts has increased considerably, which has also led to a greater number of pending cases and bureaucratic delays. in the absence of reform aimed at renewing the procedural and organisational measures, including an increase in the number of judges at the tribunal itself, the duration of proceedings would only risk increasing. in order to ensure fair and speedy trials, we therefore accept the gradual increase of an additional twenty-eight judges, one for each member state, despite the higher costs which will certainly result from the adoption of this criterion of national representation. we need an efficient legal system and for that reason we can also accept the abolition of the civil service tribunal. finally, we welcome the inclusion of a gender balance criterion and a review clause which will make it possible to assess the impact of this reform on the management of the court's work, which remains the guardian and beacon of european values and integrity.
in writing. ‒ i consider that a reform of the statute of the court of justice of the european union is necessary in the light of the current inability of the court of justice to ensure the conditions for respecting the right to a reasonable period of trial enshrined in article 6 of the echr and article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which is impossible due to an overload of cases before the court, in particular in competition and state aid matters. i have therefore decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the recommendation for the second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 on certain provisions for fisheries in the area covered by the gfcm agreement. in particular, in order to safeguard the development, conservation, rational management and best use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea at levels considered sustainable and with a low risk of depletion, it was necessary to request member states to grant derogations for the use of trawls and seines and the prohibition of coastal trawl fishing in the black sea. parliament accepted the differentiated procedure, which provides for management at national level, with the right of control by the commission, justified by the profound diversity with the mediterranean basin. in addition, the commission will only authorise the vessels after verifying that the conditions laid down in the cgpm recommendation are met. the member states will therefore be able to maintain their national frameworks if they comply with the conditions laid down in the regulation under consideration, and i have therefore voted in favour of the text.

in writing. ‒ following the establishment of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), the european union acceded to the agreement concluded therein, which provides a framework for multilateral cooperation aimed at promoting the development, conservation, rational management and best use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea at sustainable levels. parliament has now discussed the amendment of regulation 1343/2011 amending certain provisions for fishing in the gfcm agreement area previously adopted by virtue of accession to the gfcm. the amendments are intended to incorporate into european legislation the recent conservation and control measures adopted by the gfcm, including measures for the sustainable exploitation of red coral and for the incidental capture of seabirds, turtles, seals and cetaceans, but also some exceptional derogations for trawling in the black sea. we have now reached the conclusion that the derogation from the trawl ban cannot be used as a precedent in future legislation. the commission will also be vigilant to ensure that the risks arising from the derogations do not materialise. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the marketing of genetically modified food or feed is a matter of concern to all european citizens. the commission cannot impose such an important choice on the member states, each country must be free to introduce or not to introduce into its territory food or feed containing or based on gmos. to this end, a proposal was submitted to amend regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 by introducing article 34a, which would allow states to ban food or feed containing or based on gmos without, however, invoking environmental or health reasons which are subject to the exclusive assessment of the european food safety authority (efsa). but such a course would have exposed the states to legal proceedings for hindering the free movement of goods. we tabled amendments to commit the commission not to authorise new gm food or feed and not to renew expired authorisations until agreement was reached on a new proposal but of course it was rejected. for these reasons i have decided to abstain.

in writing. ‒ my vote in plenary confirms what was approved in the envi and agri committees and therefore the rejection of the commission's proposal. while it is true that the existing legislation on the authorisation of the marketing of products containing gmos needs to be revised and that this process needs to be further democratized, the solution to this problem cannot be found in proposals which risk being difficult to apply by contradicting principles guaranteed by the union, such as free movement within the internal market. for these reasons, and given the impracticability of the present proposal, we expect the commission to commit itself to formulating a new proposal compatible with the internal market and the eu's international trade obligations, and able to take into account the needs of european production along with the possible consequences for the environment and human health.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i am concerned about the lack of an impact assessment and the compatibility of the measures taken by the member states with the internal market, wto rules and the feasibility of the proposal. in particular, since the adoption of the proposal was not preceded by an assessment of all the possible consequences and options available, the rapporteur considers that the proposal is in conflict with the commitments to 'better regulation' and 'transparency' made by the new commission, and i agree. i also agree with the rapporteur that the proposal could have far-reaching consequences for the functioning of the internal market in food and feed and for the competitiveness of the agricultural sector in the union, as the eu is still heavily dependent on the supply of protein from genetically modified sources, and considering that the proposal is likely to have an indirect negative effect on imports, i am of the opinion that the proposal could seriously damage livestock production and also have a negative impact on agriculture in the eu. finally, since border controls no longer exist in the eu agricultural sector, reintroducing such controls between member states would be tantamount to erasing the economic gains of the european customs union and the single market.

in writing. ‒ on 22 april 2015, the commission presented a proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 concerning the possibility for member states to adopt measures restricting or prohibiting, under certain conditions, the use on their territory of gmos and authorised genetically modified food and feed (opt-out). this proposal does not appear to be preceded by a careful assessment of all the possible consequences for the competitiveness of the agricultural sector in the union. given that the eu is still dependent on the supply of protein from genetically modified sources, this proposal could have a negative impact on imports and agriculture in the eu. i therefore vote in favour of mr la via's report, which rejects the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report because of my serious concerns about the european commission's proposal. the new rules, which increase the discretion of member states on the use of gmos in agriculture and trade, raise serious doubts about their effectiveness and their compliance with the rules governing the single market. the introduction of several regulations would be contrary to the need for greater integration and would jeopardise the interconnection between the different food production chains. the measure could also negate one of the founding principles of the single market: the free movement of goods. the lack of frontiers also raises serious doubts about the controls that would govern the introduction of gmo products into the various markets. the division of the single market would also threaten competitive balances. different access to gm feed, on which the european agricultural sector is heavily dependent, could in fact alter the competitiveness of one member state compared to another. the disparity between the various markets could damage the international trade negotiations conducted by the ec as a unit. in the agricultural field, the negotiators should represent at the same time the different interests of the countries favouring the use and marketing of gmos and those opposing it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament legislative resolution on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 as regards the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of gmos on their territory. firstly, i am afraid that, as trade in gmos crosses national borders, the regulation proposed by the commission may prove impossible to enforce, since the reintroduction of border controls between pro- and anti-gmo countries would be incompatible with the single market and the customs union. furthermore, since the adoption of the proposal was not preceded by an assessment of all the possible consequences and alternatives available, i believe that the proposal is in conflict with the commitments to 'better regulation' and 'transparency' made by the new commission. finally, i have serious concerns about the far-reaching consequences that the proposal could have for the functioning of the internal market in food and feed and for the competitiveness of the agricultural sector. as the eu is heavily dependent on protein supplies from gmo sources, the proposal could also have an indirect negative impact on imports.
in writing. ‒ fearing that the possibility given to member states to decide whether to ban or restrict food and feed containing genetically modified organisms could make imports difficult and, consequently, harm the feed industry and community agriculture, i felt it necessary to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ in april, the european commission adopted a proposal for a revision of the gmo regulation which would, among other things, allow member states to restrict or prohibit the use of gmos that have already been authorised on their territory. i voted in favour of rejecting the commission proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 1829/2003. i agree with the rapporteur that the proposal was not preceded by an adequate impact assessment. i also believe that the implementation of this proposal could have negative consequences for the functioning of the internal market and the competitiveness of the agricultural sector in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report rejecting the proposal adopted by the european commission for the revision of the gmo regulation, because it was not preceded by an impact assessment taking into account all the possible consequences, including negative ones, that could fall on agriculture. the proposal would allow each eu country to restrict or prohibit the use of gmos already authorised on its territory, which could have an indirect negative effect on imports. i am also not in favour of reintroducing border controls for agricultural products from the european union: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the use of genetically modified food and feed, in which parliament rejects the european commission's proposal that would allow individual member states to restrict or prohibit the sale and use on their territory of gm food or feed already approved at eu level. we believe that this decision should be taken at european level and not by individual member states, to avoid the renationalisation of restrictions and prohibitions in this area leading to a dangerous fragmentation of the internal market and the customs union. the commission proposal could prove unfeasible or lead to the reintroduction of border controls between countries in favour of and those against gmos, given the divisions that exist on the subject. in the resolution adopted today, we therefore call on the commission to present a new legislative proposal which takes account of these concerns and provides an assessment of the potential consequences or other viable options.
in writing. ‒ we are very much in favour of states having the possibility to ban gmos. the european commission's proposal seems to be moving in this direction. it just looks like: the commission has not, however, been able to establish that the prohibition is in fact effective. we in the m5s had tabled amendments to the legislative proposal in the envi committee precisely to make it applicable. the envi committee, on the other hand, tabled a simple resolution in plenary rejecting the european commission's proposal. we abstained to stress our distance both from the impracticable possibility of a ban originally proposed by the european commission (we want a practicable ban!) and from its simple rejection. this rejection of the proposal precludes the possibility of states banning gmos, especially in view of the fact that the commission has already announced that it will not present a new legislative proposal on the subject. my vote could have been in favour if our amendment had been adopted, which would have committed the european commission not to authorise new food or feed based on gmos and not to renew expired authorisations until agreement had been reached on a new proposal to make national bans possible.
in writing. ‒ i share the concerns expressed in the report by mr la via on the use of gmos in the eu and for this reason i believe that the commission's proposal should be rejected. the institutions can and must make every effort to protect the health of citizens: effective measures are required, based on a careful assessment of all possible consequences of the use of the gmo and of available alternative options. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. a common effort is needed to promote an open discussion on new technologies, which will help to safeguard the tradition of european agri-food production and to meet the growing needs of european citizens and beyond to meet their food needs. only through a thorough debate on new technologies and their impact on the lives of each of us can we make progress in the interests of all.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a commission regulation on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory. parliament rejected the proposal as it did not add anything new to the existing level of protection. in fact, any national bans on the use of genetically modified food and feed would be impossible to implement because of internal market and wto rules. i have had the opportunity to listen to the concerns of citizens and consumer associations about the risks of consuming gmos. i hope that president juncker will stick to his programme and that the commission will come forward with a new proposal on this. the revision of the rules for the authorisation of gmos in europe is necessary but must better reflect the opinion of the majority of citizens. until then, the commission cannot use its powers to authorise new gmos.
in writing. since the beginning of my mandate, i have been fighting to make europe a gmo-free area. gm food and feed should not enter european territory. the eu imports 32 million tonnes of soybeans each year for its own livestock feed, and 90% of it is genetically modified. the commission proposal would give individual member states a false freedom of choice because it would expose any country that chose not to trade in gm food and feed on its territory to the denunciation of multinational companies. in this way, millions of tonnes of gm feed would continue to reach europe, feeding our animals and, indirectly, us. it is therefore necessary to reject it, but it is not enough: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the foodstuffs are not genetically modified. a behavior that could only see me not satisfied with simple rejection and, for this reason, i chose to abstain.
in writing. ‒ proposals to encourage and facilitate the opening of the european market to the marketing of food produced by so-called innovative technologies and food from so-called traditional third countries have been the subject of heated debate in the european parliament. the novel food market raises a number of legitimate concerns as regards the protection of consumer health. the economic potential of the expansion of this market must not be sacrificed to the necessary guarantees of protection for citizens, established in accordance with well-defined scientific standards and above all geared to respect for the precautionary principle. the political orientation of the european commission and the council, however, shows a very different picture. the problem of the vague definition of what should or can be defined as a food of 'traditional origin', which also includes the marketing of insects, is compounded by the real risk of seeing foodstuffs in our supermarkets with additives obtained from gmos, products containing nanoparticles in high percentages, foodstuffs with nutritional substitutes of synthetic origin, and also failing to comply with the appropriate information requirements. i voted against because this danger must be stopped, in the interests of both the health of european citizens and the environment itself.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on novel foods. the agri-food sector is a constantly evolving sector which needs an up-to-date regulatory framework to keep pace with technological developments. at present, the human consumption of certain insect species, classified as novel foods, is already permitted in several member states, including belgium, the netherlands, denmark and great britain. the report we have adopted has brought the legislation up to date. while simplifying the current authorisation procedures for novel foods, the text ensures a high level of protection of human health and consumer interests through a systematic centralised risk assessment by efsa and the application of the precautionary principle. at the same time, additional specific labelling requirements are provided with the aim of informing final consumers of any specific food characteristics or properties of these new products. the text adopted ensures consumer protection and keeps legislation up to date with scientific and technological progress in the field. that is why i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the report provides for the possibility of authorising new or traditional foods provided that they are not disadvantageous and not necessarily nutritionally advantageous to existing ones. where efsa or the commission has requested additional documentation from applicants and they do not provide it, the assessment shall not be suspended but shall proceed with the documentation available. the meaning of the term 'significant number of people' who would need to have consumed a food for at least 25 years for it to be recognised as a traditional food, remains undefined. coverage is granted for animal clones but not for offspring. finally, the application of the precautionary principle in the event of scientific uncertainty as to the safety of a particular food is mentioned only in recital 17, whereas the precautionary principle is indicated in the article as one of the parameters on which the commission will base its opinion. the actual consideration of this claim can already be deduced from the way in which the nanoparticles have been treated, which, applying the indications in the recital and the efsa conclusions, should have been reduced to a maximum of 10% and prohibited if the lack of sufficiently sensitive instrumentation would prevent the achievement of the stated objective. so i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because the current authorisation procedure, before marketing, has been criticised as being too costly and time-consuming. one of the objectives of the commission's new proposal is to simplify and streamline the regulatory process, thereby reducing the administrative burden on applicants, the authorities of the member states and the commission itself. furthermore, the commission has rightly recognised that long delays in the procedure, as well as the costs of submitting the application, have created a barrier to innovation and participation by smes. therefore, while a simplified authorisation procedure will undoubtedly reduce the costs for applicants, it will inevitably be an effort that can entail considerable burdens, while encouraging the competitiveness and innovation of food business operators should remain the main objective and therefore obtain the appropriate level of protection. as regards the insect controversy, the aim is to regulate an area which has hitherto been the subject of a regulatory vacuum. no authorization has been granted, contrary to what the newspapers say.
in writing. ‒ considering that the authorisation of a novel food constitutes a barrier to trade and prevents the access to the eu market of products that have a safe and historically proven food use in their country of origin, i fully support the implementation of the new regulation, which, in addition to ensuring food safety, aims to streamline and simplify the authorisation procedure for novel nutrients through a list of novel foods authorised in the union. this new regulation will bring benefits in many ways: it will reduce the administrative burden, time and cost of the authorisation process and increase the competitiveness of the european food industry, in particular smes.
in writing. ‒ the review aims to facilitate the procedures for authorising the placing on the market of novel foods and traditional foods from third countries. it should be recalled that this proposal follows on from the earlier proposal that was rejected in march 2011 due to the failure to reach an agreement on the use of animal clones for food. although the market for novel foods could expand mainly due to the influence of traditional foods from third countries, between 2004 and 2014 the number of authorisations granted by the commission or individual national authorities was around 100 and 3 cases of rejection were officially reported. furthermore, beyond immediate food or food preparations, all food additives, including those from gmos (although gmos are excluded from the scope of new foods as they are already covered by regulation 1829/2013), micro-organisms such as yeasts, or individual compounds with particular properties play an important role in the novel food market. following the rejection of our amendment which would have prohibited the use of nanotechnologies in view of the current toxicological uncertainties and the impossibility of assessing their presence in concentrations below 50% of the total, i decided to vote against.
in writing. i fully support the proposal for legislation to monitor and guarantee the trade in novel foods. the union must reiterate its role as guarantor of the health and well-being of its citizens and consumers, and as such, safeguard through appropriate checks that the new foods that arrive on our tables are safe for human and environmental health.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to abstain from voting on the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on novel foods because i am not completely satisfied with the compromise reached with the council. the subject of novel foods is a very sensitive one. on the one hand, we have the fundamental values of the protection of human health, the defence of healthy food and the characteristics of european products and the protection of consumer rights. the commission has also taken the view that the european union should be able to take action to combat the spread of the disease by means of a community action programme. i think that regulation is necessary because of the technological progress that has taken place over almost 20 years since the 1997 regulation, knowing that these new products would still be on our tables because of globalisation. however, its content must take account of the principles of precaution, protection of the environment and health. i therefore supported the amendments seeking greater powers of control by parliament, a discipline that imposes specific regulations pending, the indication of the origin of the product from cloned animals and a request for a moratorium on food produced by nanotechnology, which were unfortunately rejected by the house.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of mr nicholson's report. after a long negotiation we have managed to find a good compromise, which is necessary to replace the old regulation, which dates back to 1997. new products are now part of the common diet. moreover, both in italy and in europe we have a large community of foreigners and we must therefore adapt the food consumed on our continent, also aligning it with the needs and tastes of citizens of other countries who have had access to the european continent. the overall framework of the standard will enable our industries to be more competitive, innovating and bringing new products to the market. finally, i would remind consumers that the european food safety authority (efsa) will monitor everything that is placed on the market, guaranteeing the highest levels of safety for european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on novel foods. the commission adopted a proposal for a revision of the novel food regulation in 2013 which aims to ensure food safety, protect public health and ensure the functioning of the internal market for food products, while promoting innovation for the food sector. the ultimate aim of this proposal is to update the categories of novel foods, taking into account the impact of new technologies on food products, to revise the authorisation process in order to improve efficiency and transparency, and to simplify procedures for food imported from third countries with a proven history of safe food use.
in writing. ‒ the rules on novel foods date back to regulation no 258 of the european parliament and of the council of 1997 which is currently totally inadequate in relation to scientific and technological progress affecting the food sector. this progress has led to the development of a number of new food products or food ingredients with intentionally modified primary molecular structure not covered by the 1997 regulation. this therefore requires an amendment. the report by mr nicholson, to which i shall vote in favour, is intended to encourage a new harmonised procedure at eu level by the food safety authority (efsa) which should carry out an assessment of cases where a food has an effect on human health, also taking into account new genetically modified food on the eu internal market.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the draft report, as it sets clear deadlines and definitions for the whole process of placing novel foods on the market, taking into account the precautionary, environmental and food safety principles, and also provides safeguards against adverse impact on human health. the proposal, which is necessary to ensure food safety, aims to protect public health and ensure the functioning of the internal market for food products, while supporting innovation in the food sector. it aims to streamline the authorisation procedure in order to improve its efficiency and transparency. the definition of novel food is also clarified, taking into account new technologies that have an impact on food production. finally, a faster and more appropriate safety assessment is introduced for traditional foods from third countries with a reliable history of food production.
in writing. ‒ the european commission adopted in december 2013 a proposal for a revision of the novel food regulation with the aim of updating the categories of novel foods, revising the authorisation process and simplifying procedures for food imported from third countries. since the entry into force of regulation (ec) no 258/97, a wide range of new food products and food ingredients have been developed, including foods containing, consisting of, or produced from micro-organisms, fungi and algae, or foods with an intentionally modified primary molecular structure. this kind of food has called into question the adequacy of the current definition of 'novel food'. i therefore believe that an amendment to the regulation is absolutely necessary in the light of scientific and technological progress in the food sector. i voted in favour of this report in order to achieve as soon as possible greater clarity on the definition of 'novel food' and to provide for stricter provisions on consumer protection. my vote does not involve any judgment on the merits of the use of algae and insect-based foods, which i personally find objectionable.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i support the european commission's decision to update the regulation on novel food categories and to simplify and improve the authorisation procedures for food imported from third countries.
in writing. ‒ the proposal voted on today aims to encourage innovation in the food sector, through a new and simplified procedure for new products and ingredients entering the market. that is why i voted in favour. the previous legislation was from 1997, so it was necessary to update the rules to keep pace with technological developments over the last 20 years. one of the most significant changes concerns the inclusion in the definition of 'new food' of foods with altered molecular structure, fungi, algae, insects and food obtained from cell and tissue cultures. the new legislation will increase transparency, as the commission will have to publish a summary of all new applications for authorisation and a list of rejected applications. the eu list of authorised novel foods will then be made available to the public.
in writing. the aim of the report is to facilitate the procedures for authorising the placing on the market of all foods produced using technologies developed after 1997 and defined as innovative, as well as traditional foods from third countries. i voted against this regulation because there are serious concerns about food containing nanoparticles. since a 50% tolerance threshold has been established, it was decided to allow percentages in food that are 2.5 times higher than what is considered advisable and to disregard the migration of nanoparticles that may be contained in food contact packaging. efsa itself had suggested a limit of no more than 10% in accordance with the precautionary principle, given the lack of scientific evidence on the behaviour of these particles on the metabolism of humans. food additives, including those derived from gmos, micro-organisms such as yeasts, individual compounds with special properties (methylcellulose in gluten-free products) also play a too important role in novel foods. once again, the precautionary principle protecting european consumers is being overridden in the name of profit.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the girling report on the emission of certain air pollutants because, although there were conditions for doing more, the overall assessment is positive. the limits for pollutants have been lowered compared with the envi proposal, but ammonia and methane (with the exception of internal emissions) have been kept within the scope of the directive. unfortunately, mercury was not included, but at least the request was sent to the european commission for an impact study to be followed by a legislative proposal. the situation with regard to air pollution is serious, the air we breathe every day is becoming more polluted and it is, in my view, essential to have a strong nec directive which can drive ambitious air quality policies in all sectors.
in writing. ‒ the eu commission's proposal to set higher national limits on emissions of the main pollutants is right. air pollution causes about 400 000 premature deaths in the eu each year. the new rules could save up to 40 billion euros by 2030 to combat environmental pollution. europe wants to set itself ambitious targets, including for the cop21 in paris. the new national emission limits (necs) are for sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), non-methane organic compounds (nmocs), methane (ch4), ammonia (nh3) and particulate matter (pm up to 2.5 micrometres). the new rules will also help to reduce mercury (hg) emissions. it is right to exclude methane produced naturally by cows from the directive. but now we must continue to fight against food waste, also to reduce pollution and soil consumption. in fact, about one third of the world's food produced for human consumption is lost or wasted along the food chain. this amounts to some 1.6 billion tonnes of food being wasted. and we must not forget that in many countries around the world, we eat far too much meat than we actually need in our diet.
in writing. - i vote against it. revision of the air quality directive, which sets new national emission ceilings (necs) from 2020 to 2030. the commission proposal is as follows: - makes the intermediate thresholds mandatory until 2025; - extends the scope to other gases (methane ch4, ammonia nh3, mercury hg). we are all aware of the extreme difficulties that local authorities have in complying with the current limits, especially in certain unfavourable geographical areas such as padania. we therefore consider it unnecessarily burdensome to set mandatory reduction thresholds even at the intermediate stage, by 2025. the addition of methane and ammonia, which has a significant impact on the agricultural (livestock) sector, is particularly controversial. but it's the addition of methane that's the discriminant for our final vote. as a greenhouse gas, we interpret its inclusion in this directive as a (yet another) clever attempt to mix anti-pollution legislation with that related to climate policies (as the saying goes: pears with apples).

in writing. ‒ parliament voted today on a very important report which aims to reduce harmful emissions from a number of pollutants in the years ahead by limiting the impact of these substances on human health and the environment. the cost of poor air quality is higher in terms of human lives than road accidents, making it the leading environmental cause of premature death in the eu. poor air quality also has an impact on quality of life, as it causes asthma and respiratory problems, and has a major impact on health expenditure in the various member states. in the light of these figures, we cannot but rejoice at the important result achieved today. i am also pleased that it has been possible to exclude enteric methane from the scope of the directive, thus meeting the strong concerns expressed by small and mediumsized farmers. i hope that in the coming months the text voted by parliament will not be stripped of its essential content, because firstly our citizens are demanding rules that are strongly protective of their health and, secondly, it is important that the eu sends a strong signal also in the run-up to the 2015 paris conference on climate change (cop21).

in writing. a proposal for a revision of regulation 211/2011 is introduced by this report which defines the eci, the european citizens' initiative. the eic is the only real instrument of direct democracy introduced by the treaty of lisbon; the commission's proposal is to draw up a legislative proposal which, if supported by one million signatures, can become a commission legislative initiative. the various problems of the eci have become apparent over the years, so much so that the number of initiatives has seen a steady decline in comparison to the only three successful initiatives (stop vivisection, right2water and one of us) which received, unfortunately, an absolutely unacceptable response from the commission - just think that some promoters of ecis have sued the commission in the european court of justice for the disappointing answers provided. but let us not despair, because parliament's report is aimed at helping to revise the eci so that it can become what it is not now: an effective instrument of direct democracy. we therefore propose in this report a reform of the eci which aims to remove obstacles, whether they are technical/bureaucratic or political. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ europe often tends to close itself in palaces. this shows a certain disregard for the instruments of democratic debate and debate on the fundamental issues of its citizens. the european union has one tool, the european citizens' initiative (eci), but it has proved to be costly, bureaucratic and frustrating for both the promoters and the signatories. the european parliament resolution on the european citizens' initiative (eci) aims to call for a revision of regulation 211/2011, which regulates the main instrument of direct democracy introduced by the lisbon treaty. the ice must become a really useful and effective instrument. this would require simplifying bureaucratic procedures, eliminating any possible conflict of interest for the commission, which not only legally checks the eligibility of ecis but also decides whether to follow them up or not, and finally standardizing the system for collecting signatures in the various member states. in the end, however, this is a small step forward in strengthening the instrument of direct participation of citizens in the process of forming laws, which we cannot but appreciate.

in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative (eci) allows europeans to play an active role in the decision-making processes that affect them. one million european citizens, residing in at least one quarter of the union's member states, can invite the commission to submit a legislative proposal they consider necessary to implement the treaties of the european union. the eic thus confers on citizens of the union a right of initiative similar to that exercised by the european parliament and the council. this is an exceptional opportunity which must be encouraged and supported. however, since the entry into force of regulation (eu) no 211/2001 in april 2012, several practical difficulties have been reported. only 3 of the 31 registered ecis reached the final stage. i voted in favour of this report in order to improve the operation of the ice, to simplify its procedure and to remove some of the obstacles which have proved to be the most difficult for the ice organisers.

in writing. ‒ more than ten years have passed since the birth of the adriatic region, which brought together 26 regions of this area. the italian presidency extended this project by launching in 2014 the european strategy for the adriatic and ionian region (eusair) involving four member states (croatia, greece, italy and slovenia), three candidate countries (albania, montenegro, serbia), and one potential candidate (bosnia and herzegovina). the report, which i support, highlights the four pillars on which eusair insists: the commission will continue to support the development of the maritime sector through the following measures: innovative growth in the maritime sector (blue growth), strengthening infrastructure and connectivity (connecting the region), better protection of the environment through increased cooperation (environmental quality) and development of the tourism potential of the region (sustainable tourism). the plan aims to realise the opportunities of the region's maritime economy through improved energy connectivity, but also to stimulate research and innovation for the benefit of small and medium-sized enterprises by improving european connections, such as the baltic-adriatic and scandinavian-mediterranean corridors.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region. the countries of the adriatic and ionian region have been particularly affected by the economic crisis, with rising unemployment and indebtedness, and have experienced a sharp decline in both public and private investment. the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region represents a major opportunity as it allows for the targeting of investments, which have been particularly lacking in recent years, towards specific sectors and allows some countries in the region, candidates for eu membership (albania, montenegro, serbia) or potential candidates (bosnia and herzegovina), to move closer to the european union by aligning their policies and working closely with eu member states. the strategy is based on four pillars: the commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the environment and to promote sustainable and competitive tourism. the main priorities identified in the strategy are: the development of the fisheries and aquaculture sector, the improvement of links with the european corridors, the protection of the marine environment and the biodiversity of the ecosystem, the diversification of the tourist offer and sustainable tourism management, the integration of the western balkans into the eu and the coherence between the eu macro-regional strategies.

in writing. ‒ the adriatic-ionian macro-region strategy covers eight countries equally represented by eu member states (greece, italy and slovenia) and non-eu countries (albania, montenegro, serbia, bosnia and herzegovina). the region is home to more than 70 million people and plays a key role in strengthening europe's geographical continuity. the italian government played a key role in promoting the strategy, which was adopted during our semester. it is structured around four interdependent pillars of strategic importance, all equally relevant to the objectives of sustainable growth: blue growth, connecting the region (transport and energy networks), environmental quality and sustainable tourism. the connecting the region pillar was the one that created the most conflict. in the committee, we included the completion of the baltic-adriatic corridor among the objectives in the final compromise text. we have succeeded in getting our amendment through the plenary to add a specific mention to its completion 'along the whole adriatic-ionian backbone'. this is an important and in many ways unexpected result. it is now up to governments to turn our initiative into action, giving substance to a strategy which we believe has important potential that is still largely untapped.

in writing. ‒ macro-regional strategies can be seen as a tool dedicated to promoting economic and social cohesion, with the main objectives of reducing disparities between regions, promoting real convergence and encouraging growth and employment. the adoption of an eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region (eusair) is the result of the interest shown by the countries involved. the strategy covers four eu member states (croatia, greece, italy and slovenia) and four ipa countries (albania, bosnia and herzegovina, montenegro and serbia). the overall budget for the period 2014-2020 is eur 118.154.690, including the european regional development fund (erdf) (eur 83.467.729), the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa ii) (eur 15.688.887 million) and the national contributions (eur 18.998.074 million). this is the third eu macro-regional strategy and can therefore benefit from the experience and lessons learned from the european union strategy for the baltic sea region and the european union strategy for the danube region. i voted in favour of this report so that the strategy for the ionian adriatic region can be a great opportunity for development.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution under consideration. cohesion policy is one of the key instruments for the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy. it continues to make a positive and substantial contribution to achieving the europe 2020 strategy objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. the proposal identifies four priorities: (a) implement greater synergies between cohesion policy and the europe 2020 strategy with the specific aim of increasing the quantity, quality and impact of investment in research and innovation through a coordinated use of cohesion policy instruments; (b) to create a greater interconnection between the european fund for strategic investments and the structural funds for european investment; (c) adopt strengthened multi-level governance so that local, regional and other civil society actors are better involved in the europe 2020 strategy; and (d) improve the territorial approach of the europe 2020 strategy so that the direct effects of this policy are greater and more felt at local level. finally, it is explicitly requested that the ep be involved in a timely manner in all major discussions on the planning, implementation and evaluation of the strategy.

in writing. ‒ as is well known, the european structural and investment funds have the important objective of supporting the economic development of all eu member states by addressing the strategic investment gap that the private market cannot cover. the need to coordinate and work in synergy with other european policies requires that these funds be accompanied by sound economic management. i support this report which calls on the commission to make limited, exceptional and responsible use of article 23 of the common provisions regulation (cpr), which deals with the so-called macroeconomic conditionality and provides, where necessary, for macroeconomic adjustment, reprogramming or, in the last resort, suspension of the european structural and investment funds.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document because i believe that, given the long-term and multiannual nature of the esi funds' programmes and objectives, it would be more useful to dissociate them from the various mechanisms designed to ensure sound economic governance at both european and national level, which have a much shorter time horizon, usually one year. this would make it easier to allocate resources and would lead to an improvement in the investment situation on the european continent, especially in the areas most affected by the economic crisis.
in writing. ‒ article 23 of the cpr needs to be revised because of the risky practical consequences of the rescheduling and suspension of esi funds. the original objectives of the european union's cohesion policy, concerning development and adjustment of growth in the different areas of the union, have made it one of the main instruments in maintaining territorial investment in times of crisis and socio-economic instability. the importance of pursuing territorial, social and economic cohesion cannot be put on the back burner in the name of abstract efficiency of governance. local and regional authorities cannot be penalized by a suspension of the funds which would lead to a rapid deterioration in the social and economic situation of the affected territories where other levels of administration with adequate resources available cannot act quickly. the union's intervention must always be based on solidarity and sustainability, and be careful to provide responses that are proportionate to real needs and to prevent regions that are already disadvantaged or affected by the economic crisis from paying the highest price for changes in european economic planning. reprogramming must therefore be limited to the minimum necessary and must not be independent of the socioeconomic situation of the territory concerned, with transparency and objectivity of the procedure and respect for the original objectives of eu cohesion policy.
in writing. - i abstained. the inclusion of the macroeconomic framework in the definition of cohesion policy is a positive step, and should not be understood as respecting the parameters of austerity. in general, considering that the results achieved by the member states in implementing the csfs (country-specific recommendations) are poor, as demonstrated by the commission's assessments of the progress made in implementing the 279 csfs issued in 2012 and 2013, i do not advocate a more general and comprehensive review of all cohesion policies.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the european structural and investment funds and sound economic governance, which contains guidelines for the implementation of article 23 of the common provisions regulation. the report stresses that parliament is in favour of the abolition of macroeconomic conditionality provisions in their entirety, which puts greater pressure on member states already in financial difficulties. moreover, macroeconomic conditionality and its application should not jeopardise or threaten the achievement of the fundamental principles of cohesion policy, such as economic, social and territorial cohesion. however, due to the resistance of the commission and the council, the principle of macroeconomic conditionality was once again inserted in the common provisions regulation (cpr). with this own-initiative report we cannot delete or amend the provisions of article 23 of the crp as they appear in the regulation. however, the report can ensure that they are applied in the most justified and balanced way possible.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the scope of the regulation concerning the mechanism of economic cross-compliance; this is the possibility for the commission to request a member state to review and propose to amend its partnership agreement and relevant programmes, where necessary to implement council recommendations or to maximise the impact on growth and competitiveness of the european structural and investment funds (esi funds) in member states receiving financial assistance. the report could have expressed a clear and unequivocal opposition to the mechanism itself, but instead it confines itself to a series of weak recommendations. an amendment which we tabled calling for the use of cofinancing resources to be deducted from the budget deficit to ensure budgetary parity was also rejected. i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ the guidelines published by the european commission on the implementation of macroeconomic conditionality raise many concerns and reignite the political debate that had led to the adoption of the esi funds' regulations (for the 2014-2020 programming period) subject to compliance with economic governance procedures. the commission's power to require member states with macroeconomic imbalances to reprogram part of the funding and (as provided for in article 23 of the common provisions regulation) to suspend payments could, if implemented, severely impair the effectiveness of the union's cohesion policy and affect the economic development of regions, for many of which the structural funds are the only source of public funding. i believe that the question of the possibility of excluding from the calculation of public deficits investments cofinanced by the esi funds should be reopened in the appropriate places. i am not going to go into the details of the commission's proposals. in view of the effects on the territories of the provisions of article 23, i join parliament's call on the commission to involve parliament, including in an advisory capacity, in the reprogramming and possible suspension of funds processes to ensure the correct application of the macroeconomic conditionality clause.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i agree with the vast majority of my colleagues on the concerns about the practical consequences of the reprogramming and suspension of the esi funds under article 23 of the crp: the right balance should be sought between the different views of the mechanism of macroeconomic conditionality. i am also convinced that parliament's participation should be formalised as the main democratic guarantor of the correct application of the provisions - in line with article 23 - and that it should be given the right to be consulted at all stages with regard to the adoption of requests for reprogramming or any proposals and decisions on the suspension of commitments or payments. i stress the need for constant, clear and transparent cooperation at interinstitutional level. finally, we cannot allow regional or local authorities to be penalized by reprogramming or suspending the funds, with the result that their economic and social situation deteriorates. i am convinced that these changes will ensure a proportionate response to avoid further disadvantage to regions already in difficulty.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy has so far fulfilled the fundamental task of promoting employment and improving socioeconomic situations within the member states, and has also stimulated investment in line with the achievement of the union's macroeconomic objectives. however, many questions remain about article 23 of the common provisions regulation, which would provide for the reprogramming and suspension of the esi funds. i agree with the rapporteur that frequent reprogramming would be counterproductive and should be avoided in order not to disrupt the management of the fund or to undermine the stability and predictability of the multiannual investment strategy. therefore, the application of article 23 should only take place in exceptional situations to allow for the achievement of a sustainable and effective cohesion policy and under the supervision of the european parliament, as the main democratic guarantor of the correct application of the macroeconomic conditionality provisions of the cpr.
in writing. ‒ the report addresses the scope of article 23 of regulation 1303/2013 concerning the macroeconomic conditionality mechanism, i.e. the possibility for the commission to ask a member state to review and propose to amend its partnership agreement and relevant programmes, where necessary to support the implementation of relevant council recommendations or to maximise the impact on growth and competitiveness of esi funds in the member states receiving financial assistance. the argument was already widely criticised during the negotiation of the regulation in 2012-2013, as the economic policy of a member state could thus have a negative impact on the implementation of individual regional and national operational programmes. following the weak report of the rapporteur, who preferred to limit himself to a series of rather weak recommendations, without in the least questioning the link between cohesion policy and sound economic governance, and following the rejection of an amendment on the revision of the investment clause, i decided to vote against.
in writing. ‒ i am sorry to say that i voted against the report because i thought, and i do, that it was a good opportunity to raise the issue of a golden rule for investments made as part of the co-financing of the structural funds. we have lost a great opportunity to give substance to the words which we too often repeat rashly and without fully understanding their meaning. we as a parliament have been against macroeconomic conditionality from the outset. after a long battle, we have been forced to accept this rule, at the behest of the commission and the council. we, the socialists and democrats in particular, remain convinced that the stability and growth pact, as it stands, is detrimental to a real investment policy and we therefore call for its revision, in particular to exclude resources from the co-financing of the esi funds. we have unfortunately lost, but this is certainly not the end of the battle to enable the states and regions to make the best use of the funds, free from the rigidities of an austerity policy which has led to the loss of investment and jobs.
in writing. ‒ i voted strongly in favour of the resolution on the simplification of cohesion policy for the period 2014-2020, because it is a pressing need to increase the spending capacity of the regions and the effectiveness of cohesion policy as a whole. the new regulations already offer possibilities for simplification and reduction of administrative burdens. the ec initiative aims to help member states use funds and invest effectively, focuses on strengthening the administrative capacity of implementing bodies, reducing territorial disparities and helping regions experiencing a slowdown in growth to make up the gap, and assessing simplification measures. nevertheless, national and regional managing authorities are faced with an excess of rules to follow, hence the urgency of greater rationalisation and harmonisation of rules, but also flexibility, proportionality and results-based management. the current context based on a multi-fund strategy is welcome. it would be desirable to move to common procedures, just as there should be a single flow of funds meeting all needs at local level, a sort of one-stop shop with a single source of funding up to the local and regional level.
in writing. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the current legal framework for the european structural and investment funds (esif) aims to strengthen coordination with other eu policies and instruments. the original role and objectives of cohesion policy and its importance as a tool for maintaining investment in europe's regions, especially in times of crisis and instability, must not be lost sight of. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the report, considering that the achievement of the strategic objectives of the esi funds should not be hampered by economic governance mechanisms.
in writing. ‒ mr lopez's report stresses the importance of investment and economic cohesion instruments to promote development and employment in the member states. i consider these issues to be of fundamental importance in the light of the serious socioeconomic situation in the european union at present and therefore i am voting in favour of the motion for a resolution. in this context, it stresses the need to clarify the mechanisms for implementing the esi funds, which are multiannual in nature and are in sharp contrast to the european annual cycle.
in writing. ‒ reiterating also in this chamber that, in an era of economic crises and financial instability, europe must make every effort to ensure the full implementation of cohesion policy, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the european parliament should play an active role in monitoring the implementation of article 23 of the common provisions regulation (cpr). the guidelines examined in this report relate exclusively to the first part of article 23 of the regulation on the reprogramming or suspension of the european structural and investment funds of an optional nature (esif). in view of the fact that regional or local authorities may be penalized by reprogramming or suspending the above-mentioned funds, with the consequent deterioration of their economic and social situation, we must ensure a proportionate response in order to avoid bringing further disadvantages to regions already in difficulty. i voted in favour of this report because the commission seems to agree that it is necessary to reduce the reprogramming to the minimum necessary. in my view the sole objective of article 23 of the cpr should be to achieve a more sustainable and efficient cohesion policy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i believe that good economic governance and an effective cohesion policy are fundamental tools for dealing with and overcoming the economic crisis affecting the member states of the european union. the report calls on the european parliament to be the main democratic guarantor of the correct implementation of article 23 of regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 concerning the mechanism of macroeconomic conditionality.
in writing. ‒ the macroeconomic conditionality provisions, i.e. the measures to link the european structural and investment funds to sound economic management, were a highly controversial aspect of the regulation laying down common provisions for cohesion policy 2014-2020, which had been rejected by a wide political spectrum in the previous legislature. however, since the final text of the regulation contained this principle, parliament had obtained that the corresponding provisions were used only as an extrema ratio. i therefore share the rapporteur's approach, which stressed the need to apply the macroeconomic conditionality provisions in the most justified and balanced way possible, in exceptional cases. while recognising the need for effective economic governance, i believe that such mechanisms should not stand in the way of the broader objectives of economic, social and territorial cohesion, especially in times of economic crisis and instability. it would not be acceptable for regional or local authorities to be unfairly penalized, through reprogramming or suspension of the funds and the consequent loss of a key source of public investment, because of macroeconomic failings on the part of central governments for which they have no responsibility. for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ cohesion policy aims to strengthen the eu's economic, social and territorial cohesion and, in particular, to reduce the gap between regions by promoting balanced and harmonious socioeconomic development, in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. during the last parliamentary term one of the most controversial aspects of the negotiation process for the regulation laying down common provisions for the structural and investment funds was the 'macroeconomic conditionality' defined in article 23. the practical implications of renegotiation and possible suspensions of funds due to the macro-conditionality clause must be carefully assessed and, given the sharp drop in investment we are witnessing, only cohesion policy can guarantee that member states and regions will keep their commitments to reduce disparities and improve employment. it is our duty to continue to insist that the flexibility clause be applied to investment. we need a full revival of public and private investment in jobs, enterprises and the well-being of citizens.
in writing. i voted against this parliament's report on the application of article 23 of the regulation on the european structural and investment funds, which introduced a macroeconomic conditionality mechanism to make the disbursement of these funds subject to compliance with budgetary constraints and the implementation of the economic recipes indicated by the commission in the country-specific recommendations. a mechanism which would trigger the suspension of funds for the regions in the event of unsatisfactory progress in the implementation of structural reforms by central governments, with the counterproductive effect of worsening the economic situation and exacerbating social tensions in regions already experiencing economic difficulties. this is an absurd and unacceptable ploy, which has been strongly criticised in recent years, designed to put further pressure on central governments which show difficulties in complying with budgetary constraints or slowdowns in implementing reforms which are unfeasible or otherwise politically, economically and above all socially unsustainable. already in the econ committee, called upon to draw up an opinion on the subject, then rejected because it was incoherent and contradictory, confirming the split in this parliament on all governance issues, i was strongly opposed to any principle of macro-conditionality, in particular calling for the power of suspension to be limited exclusively to cases of fraud, corruption and mafia infiltration.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the application of macroeconomic conditionality. parliament has obtained the safeguards it had requested, so that in the event of macroeconomic imbalances in the member states, the commission will be able to ask for suspension of payments only as a measure of last resort. in the face of the objectives of economic governance, we must not ignore the objectives of cohesion policy.
