the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr vice-president of the commission, we are now almost at the end of the legislative process which has involved me for the last year and a half, but which had already begun in the previous parliament and which i hope will be completed tomorrow with final approval: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. i am quite satisfied with this approach, not only because it is the first legislative report on which i have had the pleasure of working here in the european parliament, but also because i believe that a good compromise has been found between the two main objectives of this regulation, namely to ensure an efficient and liquid market for securities financing operations, but even more to ensure transparency and clear rules in order to prevent systemic risks in the financial market. the crisis that erupted in the united states in 2007 and quickly spread to europe has shown clearly not only how strongly interconnected the global banking system is, but also how many connections there are between the traditional banking system and the so-called shadow banking system, that is, the set of entities that, while performing functions similar to those traditionally performed by banks, do so outside the system of rules to which credit institutions are subject. the ecb board has said that "too big and too indebted, this shadow banking system". in fact, some of the operations carried out by the shadow banking system can result in a level of excessive indebtedness, thus increasing the risk and the danger of the entire system. it has been estimated that shadow banking may have represented some eur 51 000 billion in 2011, or four times the gdp of the whole of europe. securities financing is one of the main links between the shadow banking system and the traditional banking system and that is why the financial stability board and the group of experts led by liikanen, and then the european commission, have offered a series of recommendations aimed at ensuring transparency and security, while preserving the necessary liquidity of this market, which is, however, an important market in ensuring the possibility of financing and the possibility of using liquidity. the regulation we are about to adopt aims to improve three important aspects of this market. first, the proposed regulation requires that all transactions be reported in a central database: this will allow us to understand the scale of the shadow banking and the link between it and the traditional financial system. secondly, there is a need for greater transparency between investment funds active in this market and investors, and finally for better regulation of reuse or rehypothecation of securities. efforts have also been made to simplify and take advantage of other regulations affecting financial markets, such as emir. the need for transparency and security in the operations of the european central bank was also discussed. i think that a good compromise will be put to the vote in the house tomorrow.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the shadow banking system since the great crisis of 2009 is the system in which systemic risk has largely been concentrated. this would have required a much more radical and non-compromising approach, because, unfortunately, transparency is not enough. the use of leverage and the reuse of collateral had to be further restricted in order to secure more financial transactions. since the 2009 crisis, the commission has taken the right direction towards genuine financial regulation. unfortunately, the last two measures, namely the banking structural reform and the measure we are discussing now, have been shelved and there is no political will to do real regulation, because they prefer to move towards a capital market union and deregulation with the use of still systemic products, such as financial securitisations, not remembering the lessons learned in 2009. we must not bow to the financial markets which impose conditions on us, because politics must be able to regulate finance.
vice-president of the commission. – mr president, we are delighted that so many members are able to support this legislation, which will increase transparency in the financial markets. looking ahead, the commission is keen for the reporting rules to be finalised as rapidly as possible. this will enable us to get the system properly up and running. once the data has been collected, we can get started with our analysis, hone in on potential risks and make sure that these are effectively managed. this legislation provides for a report to be drawn up by the european securities and markets authority (esma) by the end of 2016 that will assess the financial stability board (fsb) recommendations on minimum haircuts. the commission will publish its report a year later, setting out progress in international efforts to mitigate the risks associated with securities financing transactions. this will include a view of the appropriateness of the fsb recommendations for eu markets. but today i would urge members to support this legislation to increase transparency so that we can have an oversight that is proportionate, help investors make informed investments and make our markets safer.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i really appreciate the comments i have heard in the house tonight about the substantial support by all of us for the measure we are voting on tomorrow. i also understand the concern of some colleagues, and particularly mr valli, who spoke last, that he was perhaps a little too severe about the fact that we have missed the opportunity to put a limit on the level of leverage that can be used, and also to put a limit on the number of times that the instruments can be reused and reused. in fact, the financial stability board is working on it, and we're waiting to see what comes out of this analysis, because it's too risky to over-regulate, especially the wrong kind of regulation of a market that is also valuable in providing liquidity to financial markets. in short, i think we can be satisfied with the current text, on which there has been a broad convergence of parliament, and i would therefore like to thank first of all my colleagues, the shadow rapporteurs, for their really constructive contribution, and their staff. i also thank the european commission, in particular dg fisma, and finally the council, the italian and latvian presidencies, with whom this important achievement has been brought home.
in writing. the recent financial crisis has highlighted the existence of an excess of speculative activity as well as the existence of serious regulatory gaps in the financial system. the eu has adopted a number of measures to increase the soundness and stability of the banking system, including strengthened capital requirements, rules to improve governance, supervision, and resolution regimes. however, there is a need to improve transparency and control not only in the traditional banking sector but also in sectors where non-banks carry out credit activities, the so-called 'shadow banking system', whose size is alarming. we cannot therefore ignore the risks involved in securities financing operations. in particular, the lack of transparency prevented regulators and supervisors, as well as investors, from properly assessing and monitoring banking-like risks and the level of interconnectedness in the financial system in the run-up to the financial crisis or during the crisis. this regulation responds to the need to increase such transparency through stricter rules on disclosure to counterparties on re-use. in order to ensure compliance with those requirements, effective and dissuasive administrative penalties and measures should be provided for, in accordance with the principle of proportionality.
vice-president of the commission.– mr president, the commission attaches great importance to the issues faced by smes, in particular access to affordable financing, which is at the core of the capital markets union action plan and the review of the capital requirements regulation. i therefore welcome that so many members have raised this issue by way of oral questions. in particular, i would like to thank vice-president tajani for his involvement and contribution, and there is some time to discuss it today in plenary. the commission is committed to thoroughly assessing how eu financial regulations impact access to finance for smes and for banks and, in particular, how they impact local and regional banks. we have just closed a target consultation on the potential impact of the banking regulation on the financing of the economy, which covers the impact on sme lending as well as issues of proportionality and simplification. the responses are currently being analysed by the services of the commission. with the recent publication of a call for evidence, the commission has also launched a comprehensive review of the cumulative impact and overall coherence of financial legislation, in particular to assess interactions and whether they give rise to any unintended consequences. as regards assessing the potential benefits and strengthening alternative forms of lending, it is the commission’s standard practice as part of the better regulation agenda to conduct impact assessments in support of our proposals. this includes an analysis of the potential benefits and costs to different stakeholders, including smes. this was also the case for the crr and crd iv proposals in 2011. thanks to an amendment introduced by parliament, the capital requirements regulation contains a requirement for the commission to assess the impact of own funds requirements on lending to smes and natural persons and to report back to you and the council by 28 june, 2016. we are currently carrying out that analytical work, and the issue will be debated in the conference scheduled for 14 december on the impact of crr and crd iv on bank financing of the economy in which members of the european parliament are also warmly invited to participate. early next year, the european banking authority will provide technical advice to the commission. we will use this, as well as evidence from different sources, to deliver an objective and a reliable report to parliament and the council by the deadline. our first priority in the capital markets union action plan is to facilitate the financing of innovative companies, start-ups and non-listed firms. we will create an appropriate framework to enable innovative forms of business financing such as crowd—funding, private placements and loan originating funds to grow, while at the same time responding to the key risks. we will also launch a comprehensive package of measures to support venture capital and risk capital financing in the eu. we will explore ways to build a pan-european approach to better connect smes with a range of funding sources. with respect to work currently conducted by the basel committee to review the approach to credit risk, the goal is to reduce the importance of ratings provided by external credit rating agencies in determining regulatory capital requirements. this needs to be done without affecting the conservative capital requirements. the basel committee’s consultation paper includes ideas on how to replace ratings with other risk indicators and contains a preliminary illustrative calibration. in light of the predominantly negative responses received, we understand the basel committee is currently reviewing its approach but maintaining the original objective of reducing mechanical reliance on external ratings. the commission is closely following this debate as an observer at basel and generally shares the goal of reducing mechanical reliance on in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the european union agency for the training of law enforcement officers (cepol) and repealing and replacing council decision 2005/681/jha. cepol is the agency responsible for training law enforcement authorities. it is not a training institute in the traditional sense: its courses are held throughout the eu and are mainly implemented by a network of national police academies. the proposal for a regulation modernises cepol's legal basis and aligns it with the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty, entrusting cepol with the implementation of the principles of the new european training programme for law enforcement authorities. as the european parliament has repeatedly called on the commission to bring cepol's existing legal framework into line with the lisbon treaty and the new ambition set out in the european training programme for law enforcement authorities, so as to enable cepol to implement the european training programme for law enforcement authorities effectively and to respond to the interest of the wider law enforcement community, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to 'lisbonise' the decision of the gai council establishing a european union agency for the training of law enforcement officers (cepol), i.e. to repeal and replace it with an eu regulation. cepol is the agency responsible for training the member states' law enforcement authorities: the courses are held throughout the eu, mainly through the network of national police academies. while the alignment with the existing legal framework is certainly positive, we believe that the governance structure of cepol could be further streamlined, primarily through better coordination with initiatives already under way and the relocation of the agency from budapest to the hague so as to cluster with the other agencies active in matters already there. this would help to free up funds which are desperately needed at the moment, particularly in the area of migration policy. the proposed regulation, on the other hand, provides for an increase in the budget of cepol (due to changes in its responsibilities). for these reasons i abstained.

in writing. ‒ i believe that there is a need to improve control and transparency both in the traditional banking sector and in credit intermediation sectors such as securities financing. for all these reasons i voted in favour of this measure.
in writing. - i vote for it. this regulation lays down rules on the transparency of securities financing transactions (sfts) and re-use. a reporting and safeguarding obligation is introduced for sfts; trade repositories shall be registered with esma. any right of counterparties to reuse financial instruments received as collateral is subject at least to the conditions set out in this regulation (the enf amendments call for a reuse ban). the commission may adopt implementing acts on the equivalence and recognition of trade repositories with regard to a third country. infringements are subject to administrative sanctions, unless a member state provides for criminal sanctions instead. this measure is part of the measures taken after the financial crisis of 2007-2008 to close regulatory loopholes in the financial system and to address inefficient supervision, opaque markets and excessive complexity of financial products. the crisis has highlighted the need to improve transparency and oversight not only in the traditional banking sector but also in sectors where credit intermediation similar to banking takes place, known as 'shadow banking'.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the reporting and transparency of securities financing transactions. it is well known that financial crises have led to a proliferation of speculative activities that have exploited regulatory loopholes in the system, ineffective supervision, opaque markets and excessive product complexity. the so-called 'shadow banking' has emerged, which tends to escape the control of the bodies responsible for the traditional banking sector and may have a real risk of causing other serious financial crises to recur. there is therefore a need to improve transparency and information in order to limit, within the physiological and instrumental limits of the capital market, the accumulation of leverage. the objective of this legislation is therefore to increase the transparency of securities financing transactions by means of efficient reporting of trading data. the adverse effects are very serious because of the proliferation of otc derivatives transactions. as stated in the report, i agree that it is appropriate to report information on financing operations concluded by each operator, financial or non-financial, and i therefore voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ in the econ commission we supported an approach to strengthen transparency requirements. we have in particular called for the elimination of all exemptions for banks and all those involved in this type of transaction, for increased reporting requirements, for the removal of professional secrecy and for stricter sanctions. we also asked for the introduction into the regulation of a reuse ban, i.e. a ban on the re-collateralisation of securities offered as collateral in a new securities financing operation, in order to avoid the creation of collateral chains and contain the risks of contagion, and the application of minimum haircuts on collateral of 6% in order to reduce excessive leverage and limit the risk of contagion of operations. our improvements were not included in the final text which was further weakened during the trilogues with the council and the commission on exemptions, information requirements and sanctions. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i remember that the global financial crisis of 2007-2008 showed a lack of prudence in the financial system. the union has already adopted a number of measures to increase the soundness and stability of the banking system, and it should be noted that securities financing transactions are used by other financial counterparties, such as credit institutions, and by non-financial counterparties, and create specific risks for entities that hold shares or are clients of such counterparties. credit institutions should therefore report their securities financing transactions. in order to ensure an efficient regulatory framework for shadow banking, progress in the introduction and application of internationally consistent obligations remains essential: the commission should submit regular reports to the european parliament and the council with a view to strengthening the supervision and regulation of the shadow banking system and, therefore, to present the state of play of measures taken by the union and by the main third-country jurisdictions.
in writing. ‒ the global financial crisis has heightened the perception of excessive speculative activity, serious regulatory gaps in the financial system, the ineffectiveness of current supervisory instruments and the negative influence on the economy of the so-called 'shadow banking system'. the crisis has therefore highlighted the need to improve the transparency and control of financial transactions in securities. the lack of transparency and harmonised tax rules between member states has so far caused significant difficulties for national regulatory and supervisory authorities in assessing and understanding the real risks that individual operators pose to the system. i support the report because the new rules proposed for the regulation in question require the reporting of information on financial transactions concluded by all market participants. risk information will be accessible through the relevant european and national authorities. the regulation is an essential legislative instrument because it aims to strengthen financial stability in the european union by increasing the transparency of certain market activities and by introducing rules on financing operations, which ensure an efficient regulatory framework for the entire banking system.
in writing. ‒ the proposal was put forward last year by the european commission alongside the more well-known bank structural reform to prevent banking activities from moving from the traditional system to the shadow banking system, as it is less regulated. the package was intended to be the last piece of the financial system reform agenda after the 2008 financial crisis, but in practice the proposal did not introduce any real regulation. the commission has also made it quite clear that it has no intention of regulating shadow banking. on the contrary, it is now promoting it with the proposal to create the capital markets union. after supporting in the econ committee an approach to strengthen transparency requirements and after proposing amendments (which were not included in the compromise text) which provided for the elimination of all exemptions for banks and all parties involved in this type of transaction, to increase disclosure requirements, to impose stricter penalties, a regulation on the prohibition of reuse and the application of mandatory minimum collateral margins of 6% in order to reduce excess leverage and limit the risk of contagion of transactions. that is why i think it is appropriate to vote against.
in writing. ‒ excessive speculative activity in european financial markets, the complexity of the products traded and the lack of an adequate regulatory framework were some of the main causes of the 2008 financial crisis. the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the reporting and transparency of securities financing transactions builds a fence to these problems by an important work of synthesis between the main disciplines present in this field at european level. in particular, european standards are being raised in the shadow banking system, which has been an amplifier of the financial crisis through the spread of toxic products in national financial markets. another important element is the increased cooperation between the authorities involved in the supervision of financial markets at european level, such as the central banks of the european system and the competent authorities. this text thus adds a fundamental element to the regulatory framework which the european union is adopting both to monitor markets more closely and to give the economic fabric of financial markets a new central role.

in writing. ‒ on 17 june 2015, the council and the european parliament reached a political agreement on the proposal for a regulation on the reporting and transparency of securities financing transactions, known as the 'securities financing transactions regulation'. the commission's proposal, presented in january 2014, aims to implement the action framework approved by the financial stability board, the international body responsible for monitoring the global financial system, which consists of 11 recommendations on risks associated with securities lending and repo transactions in the shadow banking system. the proposal for a regulation focuses on improving the transparency of securities lending and repurchase transactions in order to enable the competent authorities and all market participants concerned to have a proper understanding of the functioning of the market, the extent and nature of potential risks, and to develop effective and efficient intervention tools to prevent systemic risks. i believe that the international financial system should be adequately controlled by clear and easily applicable measures. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the global financial crisis has highlighted the existence of excessive speculative activity and serious regulatory gaps in the financial system, as well as the ineffectiveness of supervision, opacity of markets and excessive complexity of products. due to the lack of harmonised transparency rules, national authorities have often encountered many difficulties in comparing micro-level data from different member states and thus in understanding the real risks that individual operators pose to the system. it is necessary to avoid such distortions and obstacles in the union. this regulation responds to the need to increase the transparency of securities financing transactions. this new regulatory framework will enable securities financing transactions to be efficiently reported in trade repositories and communicated to investors. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ global flight tracking systems currently cover only 30% of global air traffic and the implementation of such a system requires the international telecommunication union (itu) to provide a corresponding allocation of bandwidth for the necessary radio spectrum. the resolution calls on the commission to take action to ensure that this is done and to support the development of this technology by regulating it. i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because the tragedies of air france flight af447 and malaysia airlines flight mh370 have highlighted the need to put in place new systems to determine the position of public transport aircraft at all times, even in remote locations. i also find it very important that through such global air traffic management surveillance systems are facilitated in determining the position of an aircraft in the event of abnormal behaviour, an emergency or an accident and, even more importantly, these systems could also be an important tool in increasing aviation safety and reducing infrastructure costs. finally, i fully support the commission's action to rapidly develop a global performance-based flight tracking system, which will enable air navigation service providers to determine the position of public transport aircraft at all times, even in remote locations.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the development of satellite technology for the use of global flight tracking systems because, in view of the tragedies involving air france flight af447 on 1 june 2009 and malaysia airlines flight mh370 on 8 march 2014, i consider it absolutely necessary to introduce new systems to establish the position of a public transport aircraft at any time, even in remote locations. i also believe that such surveillance systems can increase the level of safety, because they will make it easier to locate an aircraft in the event of abnormal behaviour, an emergency or an accident. it is also necessary to establish close cooperation between all stakeholders to ensure the establishment of effective and high-quality systems.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution is tabled on behalf of the tran committee and is linked to an oral question to the commission on the implementation of satellite technologies to ensure global traceability of flights. tracking systems currently cover only 30% of global air traffic. one of the best technologies currently available is called "satellite ads-b" (automatic dependent surveillace - broadcast) and has been identified as such by the icao (international civil aviation organization). however, the implementation of such a system requires the international telecommunication union (itu) to provide a corresponding allocation of bandwidth for the necessary radio spectrum. this will be discussed at the next world radiocommunication conference in 2015 (wrc15). the resolution calls on the commission to take action to ensure that this is done and to support the development of this technology by regulating it. i can only vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ in light of the tragedies of air france flight af447 in 2009 and malaysia airlines flight mh370 in 2014, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution. i believe that the use of new global flight monitoring systems (ads-b technology) can make it much easier to locate an aircraft in the event of abnormal behaviour, an emergency or an accident. in addition, the use of such technologies would significantly improve the efficiency of search and rescue operations even in the most remote locations. i therefore hope that the european commission will be able to follow up rapidly the development of such systems, through close cooperation between all the parties concerned, in particular the world of industry and the world of specialised research centres.

in writing. ‒ the modernisation of european public administrations and the increase of their interoperability represent an important step towards completing the digital single market and effectively implementing the europe 2020 strategy. the support for today's vote is a further step towards enabling citizens, but also other entities such as small and medium-sized enterprises, to benefit fully from the potential offered by interoperable electronic services and the resulting reduction in administrative burdens and costs. it should be remembered that improved efficiency in public administration has a direct impact on the economic environment and is therefore essential to boost competitiveness, growth and employment. the priorities of the decision adopted today are therefore in this direction. the establishment of the isa2 programme for the period 2016-2020 aims to remove obstacles to interoperability by developing and promoting a comprehensive approach at union level. the actions designed to achieve this aim are aimed at facilitating cross-border or cross-sectoral electronic interaction between european public administrations and between them, on the one hand, and businesses and citizens, on the other. finally, we must remember how more efficient online public services increase the trust of citizens and businesses not only in digital services but also in institutions.
in writing. ‒ interoperability is about making the services that public administrations (pas) provide to citizens more efficient and effective: it cannot therefore be applied to obsolete systems. interoperability which must be promoted alongside free and open source software is not just a means of saving on software licences: it is, however, an important tool for raising the quality standards of security, responsiveness, system interconnection and accessibility, together with the spread of free and open source software. the new union programme should not be a mere continuation of the previous ida, idabc and isa but an improvement of them, by virtue of the progress achieved in the field of ict and the deepening of cross-border cooperation between pas.

in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on interoperability as a means of modernising european public administrations, businesses and citizens. as the report indicates, the union's strategic objective must be to define support programmes for structural investment that ensure the interoperability of systems and technologies used to ensure a higher quality of public services, while creating an environment of increased competitiveness for businesses and, consequently, greater satisfaction of citizens' needs. to achieve these goals, europe must step up its efforts to fully and permanently unlock the potential of data. it is essential to make digital public procurement effective by removing the many obstacles related to the lack of standardisation and interoperability of telematic platforms. through these actions, the union will therefore be able to improve the effectiveness, efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the services it offers to businesses and citizens.

in writing. ‒ the success and completion of the internal market also rests on freedom of movement, which allows european citizens to work within the union and businesses to operate throughout europe. this requires strengthening the ability of users to interact electronically with member states' administrations and the interaction between public administrations in different countries of the union, which must be enabled to exchange information and cooperate in order to ensure efficient cross-border public services. the european commission had already launched several programmes in the mid-1990s to facilitate the process of modernising public administrations: ehealth, as well as e-invoicing and e-procurement, are concrete examples of interoperability. the european commission's proposal to establish the isa 2 (interoperability solutions for european public administrations) programme for the period 2016-2020 will build on the previous programme and facilitate cross-border electronic interaction between european public administrations and between them and businesses and citizens in an effective and efficient manner. the programme has been and will be an important and tangible instrument for the achievement of the digital single market and the flagship initiative 'digital agenda'. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the main purpose of the electoral law is to lay down the principles and rules necessary for the election of the european parliament. the last council decision to this effect was taken in 1976. that is why it is essential and necessary to analyse and possibly adapt the procedures for electing the european parliament in the light of the evolution of the union itself. the possibility of relying on rules which reflect the present social structure is in fact fundamental to the respect of the rights of the european citizens themselves. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the basis of the results of the consultations with the member states. although in some respects the report which has been tabled meets the requirements set out above to a considerable extent, i have decided to abstain from voting in view of the role and function of the creation of european political parties. in view of the value and traditional importance of national parties in relation to the citizen, abstention from voting is intended to represent a possibility of constructive modification of the proposed reform.

in writing. ‒ i supported this proposal because the reform of the european electoral law represents an important step towards adapting the electoral act of 1976 to the present situation and making the democratic mechanism in europe more effective. since the union sets out only a few general guiding principles in this respect, the differences between the various national legislations on electoral procedures have for a long time weakened the notion of european citizenship, the concept of electoral equality and, above all, the role of active citizenship within the union. a move towards greater uniformity and harmonization at european level is therefore not only desirable but necessary. the european parliament, by adopting this own-initiative report, aims to increase the visibility of european political parties, mainly by making their affiliation more visible than national ones, and by making the european elections more transparent. the introduction of thresholds in the larger countries will also help to avoid the creation of micro-groups and thus excessive fragmentation. the decision to introduce a common deadline for the submission of electoral lists will make it possible to conduct more effective electoral campaigns and the fixing of a single deadline for the closure of polling stations, valid for all member states, will make the electoral result less influential.

in writing. ‒ although the european elections renew the same parliament, which is the representative assembly of the european people, it is national laws that govern the election, referring only to some basic principles enshrined in eu law: the commission has also proposed that the council should be able to adopt a decision on the appointment of a new member of the commission. over the years, since 1976, there have been about ten attempts to improve the european electoral law, but the council has always vetoed them. although the improvements proposed by the agreed text are modest, the effort to make the elections 'more european' and more homogeneous is appreciated. in particular, gender balance, the introduction of transnational lists and increased visibility of european political parties are useful tools to overcome the erroneous habit of experiencing the european elections as an internal "poll" of national political forces or as a "vote of sentiment" and instead understand their nature as a fundamental democratic exercise of continental scope capable of shaping the political and economic course of the entire union. for the first time we have the opportunity to build a european electoral law: let's not waste it.

in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i voted in favour of the report on the reform of the eu's electoral law, considering the proposals put forward by the rapporteurs at the bottom of the document to be valid. the effort to bring together the political forces as closely as possible in order to form a real 'european political consciousness' is both welcome and appropriate, since the process of democratic representation in europe is still in its infancy and requires the organization of balanced parliamentary representations consistent with the internal constitutional systems and the strengthening of government stability while avoiding fragmentation. the legislative role of the parliament has been strengthened and the formation of european political parties has given rise to a greater political awareness, but there are many open issues on which this reform will bring about important adjustments. i support the proposals to harmonize the minimum age for active and passive voters, to introduce mandatory thresholds recognised by the constitutions as a legitimate means of functioning, to introduce the right to vote for citizens outside the eu, and to introduce transparent procedures for the selection of candidates. i consider them to be real progress which increase the democratic dimension of the european elections.
in writing. ‒ the report is the first step in the revision of the european electoral law, which dates back to 1976. the proposal contains many improvements, including measures to harmonise the timing of elections in the various states, the possibility of introducing electronic voting, the possibility of voting for those who are temporarily abroad (soldiers and workers in general) and elements of greater transparency for those taking part in the electoral competition. but the report also has some critical aspects, in particular the call for the introduction of a european electoral district and a call for the role of european parties as promoters of a european political consciousness. i therefore opted for abstention.
in writing. ‒ the role of the european parliament has gradually changed since the 1979 elections and its powers have increased considerably. today, parliament is co-legislator with the council in most areas of the union's activities, especially since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, which made members of the european parliament direct representatives of the citizens of the union rather than representatives of the peoples. that is why we need a reform of the electoral procedure for parliament which increases the democratic and supranational dimension of the european elections, so that they are no longer just the sum of national elections and that european political parties take on the role of real political parties, and are not the sum of national parties. in this way parliament itself will gain greater legitimacy and will be closer to the electorate. it is important that the harmonization should cover a number of rules, including the affixing of the logos and names of the european parties to the ballot papers as a sign of belonging to the same political family. i welcome the fact that the italian text adopted has incorporated the linguistic clarifications which distinguish the terms necessary for the establishment of electoral lists from the lists of voters entitled to vote.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. since 1976, eu citizens have been able to vote for their representatives in the european parliament by direct universal suffrage. however, the electoral procedures vary from one member state to another, thus contradicting the objective of creating a common europe where elected representatives act as 'representatives of the citizens of the union' (article 14 (2) teu). article 223 (1) tfeu provides for the possibility for the ep to reform the 1976 european elections act by making proposals on which the council will be called upon to give its opinion. the ep proposed strengthening the visibility of european political parties, introducing a common deadline of 12 weeks before the election cycle for the establishment of lists at national level, introducing a mandatory threshold for the allocation of seats, introducing a common deadline of 12 weeks for the appointment of the leaders of european political parties, introducing gender equality and introducing the possibility of electronic voting, via the internet or by mail. the ppe group also called for the council to set up a joint electoral college in which the lists would be headed by the candidates of each political family for the post of president of the european commission.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for reform of eu electoral law. the 1957 treaty of rome already provided for the possibility of developing a uniform electoral procedure based on direct universal suffrage, and i think it is necessary to strengthen the transnational dimension of european elections, since at the moment elections are based on national issues and therefore european political parties cannot sufficiently fulfil their constitutional mandate and contribute 'to forming a european political consciousness and to expressing the will of the citizens of the union'. the rapporteurs examined a wide range of potential reform measures that would enhance the democratic dimension of european elections by improving the functioning of the european parliament and the governance of the european union, all through enhancing the visibility of european political parties, introducing the right to vote for all union citizens residing outside the eu and introducing the possibility of electronic voting, among many measures that i support.
in writing. ‒ with the european elections coming up in 2019, the parliament and the council are working on the reform of the electoral law, which aims to increase the democratic dimension and legitimacy and strengthen the decision-making process in the european union. the european elections are currently governed largely by national laws and the procedures for nominating candidates vary considerably between member states. european citizens must be able to exercise their right to vote under similar conditions and in accordance with democratic principles. it is therefore appropriate to introduce transparency requirements and democratic standards in national electoral procedures in order to ensure good governance at european level and to increase the trust of the electorate in the eu institutions. i welcome the report on the reform proposal because it presents some effective measures to enhance the democratic dimension of european elections, such as strengthening the visibility of european political parties during election campaigns, introducing a homogeneous threshold aimed at reducing party fragmentation within parliament, strengthening the online electronic voting system and facilitating access to voting for european citizens residing in third countries. the reform will thus also strengthen the political dimension of european integration.
in writing. ‒ the report is the first step in the revision of the so-called european electoral law. the report amends a 1976 act. the main aspects are: harmonisation of the time limits for voting in the various member states (submission of lists, first votes, closure of polling stations) - the closing time is fixed at 9 p.m. on the last day of the election cycle, while maintaining the national specificity in the choice of day (s) of the week; the right to vote for citizens living outside the eu for work purposes; electronic voting at the discretion of the member states (this measure constitutes aid for disabled persons, soldiers on mission and workers abroad who are not forced to return/are not prevented from voting); strengthened transparency measures for parties participating in the electoral competition; the possibility to display the logo of the european family of reference next to the logo of the national parties, both on the ballot papers and on the electoral material; the commission is also proposing to establish a european electoral authority to improve the exchange of information during the pre-electoral and electoral phases. i shall abstain on the insertion of certain amendments, including those relating to a single european constituency alongside those already in place.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the reform of eu electoral law because i believe it is important to have a european electoral law before the 2019 elections in order to increase the transnational and democratic dimension of european elections, implement the concept of citizenship of the union and promote the direct representation of citizens in the ep. the ep called for an electoral law that would promote the visibility of european political parties in the national context, introduce a threshold for single constituencies and those with more than 26 seats, guarantee both pluralism and the functioning of parliament, allow citizens resident in third countries to vote by electronic voting and by mail, and strengthen the link between european elections and the appointment of the president of the commission by explicitly indicating the list of candidates. i consider the call for the principle of gender equality and the participation of women in institutional life to be a victory and i support the call for member states to present gender balanced electoral lists. i regret, however, that no reference was made to the obligation to have closed lists representing gender equality in the member states. i very much hope that the council will accept this proposal.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft reform of the eu's electoral law to make european elections more visible and interesting for european citizens. the legislation currently establishing common provisions on european elections dates back to 1976, when the role of the european parliament was profoundly different from that of today: the european parliament has become a co-legislator in almost all matters falling within the union's competence. however, the european elections in the 28 member states remain national elections, on national issues and personalities and not on european issues. the 2014 elections marked a breakthrough in this respect, introducing the head of each european party's list, which made the person nominated by their respective political forces as president of the european commission visible to citizens. the reform voted on today codifies this proposal and adds others aimed at strengthening the european dimension of electoral campaigns, such as the presence of the symbols of european parties on the ballot paper, precise deadlines for the submission of lists, gender equality on lists, the introduction of electronic and postal voting and the possibility of creating transnational constituencies to facilitate the vote of citizens residing in another country.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on the future aviation package because i believe that, in view of the commission's legislative proposal, due by the end of 2015, it is appropriate to identify the multiple challenges that particularly affect european airlines and airports, both large and regional. the latter, in particular, play a very important role in the development of the territories, and of the peripheral ones specifically. the aviation sector is growing rapidly and it is therefore of paramount importance to implement the existing single european sky legislation efficiently, taking into account the needs of civil and commercial users. i therefore believe that the competitiveness and liberalisation of the air transport sector cannot be achieved without airlines respecting workers' rights, social standards and norms. in the airline industry, social dumping is very much in evidence, as many airlines use temporary workers, fake selfemployed workers and precarious contracts to increase competitiveness, to the detriment of workers' rights. the safety of airspace and airlines must necessarily be combined with the safety of working conditions, the necessary vocational training of staff and collective bargaining.
in writing. ‒ airline lobbyists thank the european parliament after today's vote on the aviation package. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the motion for a resolution on the aviation package. the package is badly needed to make the european aviation sector more sustainable and competitive, to strengthen european airlines, airports and the aviation industry, to ensure a level playing field in the global market and to define a long-term strategy for the european aviation sector.
in writing. ‒ given the importance of the sector, which contributed to 2.4% of european gdp in 2012 and directly employed 2.6 million people, we welcome the joint resolution on aviation. in addition, the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between ryanair and ams was signed on 28 june 2014 and entered into force on 1 january 2014. we therefore ask that the european parliament's position stress the importance of the sector as a factor of internal growth and industrial innovation. we call for a proactive policy by the european commission to ensure fair competition in the air travel market, with particular reference to competition from third countries with more lenient subsidies and state aid legislation. we are concerned about the introduction of new contractual practices and conditions which could harm the safety of passengers, and we call for greater social guarantees and more timely medical assessments for pilots. recalling that the aviation sector is not regulated by the world trade organisation, we call for a multilateral agreement, within the framework of the international civil aviation organisation, to establish common rules requiring emission reductions. the sector is responsible for 13% of european co2 emissions.
in writing. ‒ the aviation package should provide the necessary impetus to make the european aviation sector more sustainable and competitive by strengthening airlines, airports and the european aviation industry. this will ensure a level playing field on the global market and define a long-term strategy for the european aviation sector. aviation supports 5.1 million jobs and contributes €365 billion, equivalent to 2.4% of european gdp. despite the current economic crisis, global air transport is expected to grow by around 5% per year in the long term until 2030. the eu's common aviation policy also aims to make europe the safest airspace in the world. i therefore welcome this resolution.
in writing. ‒ as a member of the itre parliamentary committee, i am particularly attentive to the development needs of the industrial sector in europe. in particular, the aviation industry is a strategic pillar for economic growth (and hence for employment opportunities) as it is one of the most sensitive and easily adaptable to the current technological development. in addition, as a member of the envi committee and as a person who is sensitive to environmental issues, i am in favour of the measures that will be implemented to reduce the consumption and emissions of aircraft. i call on the house to join forces to achieve these objectives, starting with the vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the aviation sector makes a very large contribution to the eu economy, amounting to 2.4% of gdp. this is a fast-moving sector, set to grow by around 5% per year until 2030. the european commission intends to present, on 2 december, an aviation package to identify the challenges facing the aviation and related services sector. the joint motion for a resolution aims to urge the commission to propose policies to support and develop the european aviation industry. innovation, competitiveness, passenger rights, safety and the importance of clear and transparent rules on staff working conditions are all key issues that will need to be put at the heart of the eu executive's proposal. i hope, therefore, that my vote in favour today will help to define an ambitious european strategy, capable of facing the increasing competition from non-eu countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the future aviation package because i agree with the european parliament's decision to increase the sustainability of the european aviation sector and improve its competitiveness. the european union must work to promote innovation in the field of air traffic management, remotely piloted aircraft systems and alternative fuel solutions. the aviation package also brings improvements to the safety of air transport, which is of paramount importance to european citizens.
in writing. ‒ with a view to the commission presenting a package of proposals on aviation by the end of the year, parliament adopted a resolution on the challenges facing the sector, calling for a boost to its competitiveness. to this end, it is crucial to ensure fair competition in the international aviation sector and to ensure a level playing field for airlines and airports in the eu, in particular through agreements negotiated with the eu's main trading partners that also address unfair practices that distort the market, such as subsidies to third country airlines. the resolution stresses the need to press for the implementation of the single european sky rules, aimed at remedying the current fragmentation of european airspace and removing obstacles for our airlines. finally, i strongly support the importance of maintaining a high level of social standards and good working practices to protect workers in the sector and the safety of passengers. for these reasons, i voted in favour.

europeans for the proper treatment of animals. the current european union strategy for animal welfare adopted by the commission in 2012 is still in progress. the priority of the commission is therefore to work on completion of the remaining actions. furthermore, there is work to be done on the strengthening and enforcement of existing rules, on improving dialogue with stakeholders and on exploring ways to better include animal welfare considerations in our international activities. on enforcement: the european union has at its disposal a very extensive set of rules for animal welfare, covering many species, including broilers, laying hens and pigs; many activities, such as transport, slaughter and animal testing; and also products, for example, cat and dog food or seal products. we need to prioritise the critical issue of putting the existing rules into practice. learning from our experience over recent years, we must focus our efforts on tackling widespread non-compliance. pigs, as foreseen by the animal welfare strategy. secondly, i look forward to the outcomes of the ambitious pilot project on best practices on animal transport, supported by parliament. the project runs from 2015 to 2018. thirdly, i would like to mention the commission proposal to revise european union legislation on official controls, which has the potential to improve enforcement of animal welfare requirements, for example, through our proposals to establish european reference centres for animal welfare.on stakeholder dialogue: i would like to see this dialogue amongst the wide variety of actors concerned with animal welfare developed further. i intend to promote, or first attempt to see if there is an appetite in the community for, this kind of exercise. on the basis of the of consumer awareness and education. we will be ready to evaluate our next steps after the eurobarometer survey has been analysed.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that with this new directive on insurance distribution we are making a small but important step forward in strengthening the single market and deepening financial integration in the union. it was of course a difficult birth. a lot of work has gone into it and i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and the whole negotiating team and thank the commission for its contribution. and so i think the end result is positive and that it allows us to move towards the creation of a genuine single market for insurance products and reduce the costs of cross-border access, while at the same time identifying common principles to strengthen product transparency and consumer protection. the decision, as is well known, firstly extends the application of the directive to include direct distribution, and this is important in order to ensure regulatory consistency across all sales channels, and at the same time i believe that a fair balance is maintained between the application of the rules and proportionality for minor insurance products, if sold as an ancillary product. i also think that some of the achievements of parliament are important: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's insurance market is not distorted by the introduction of a single standardised document, which gives consumers all the relevant information about the product they are about to buy, and, above all, i would like to add this positive element of cross-selling, namely the possibility of guaranteeing a real choice for consumers by putting an end to tying practices in certain insurance sectors. so, all in all, this is a major achievement of which we should rightly be proud.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the report on the proposal for a directive on insurance intermediation is part of the wider review of all financial markets following the crisis. two elements are to be highlighted: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme and will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. this directive harmonizes the insurance market, but allows the national legislator to apply higher levels of protection. this double contribution will enable european citizens to benefit from rules which are comparable between the various countries but which also reflect the specific features of the insurance market in the member state. it is equally important to stress that insurance intermediaries already have a lot of bureaucratic responsibilities which impose burdens on business activity, without any increase in income in recent years. consumer protection and business sustainability are two elements that must therefore be balanced, also to allow for adequate claims management.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have repeatedly stated, including in this house, that the principle of consumer protection is a fundamental value. recent financial market imbalances have highlighted the divergences in western economic systems as a source of vulnerability. induced events often destabilise the european economic system, generating panic in markets and loss of consumer confidence. i therefore support the proposal for a directive which harmonises insurance regulation, makes the link with banking discipline more coherent and strengthens the resilience of the european financial system to self-induced and hetero-induced events. i join in the effort to increase the level of consumer protection, with reference to directives 92 of 2002 and 65 of 2014 on investment products, to which this regulation must be absolutely aligned. in fact, if i think of the r.c. auto italia and south italy sectors, whose prices are much higher than in other countries, on average 45% higher, i am more convinced that the objective of saving on insurance, combined with the mitigation of distortive factors in competition for the insurance sector, necessarily means a european strengthening of consumer protection in the insurance sector, with the creation of common standards throughout europe.

in writing. ‒ the eu's accession to the enlarged commission of the southern bluefin tuna convention will allow europe to become a full member of the convention, with an active role and greater decision-making power. i therefore intend to support this text with my vote.
in writing. ‒ accession to the enlarged commission of the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) confirms the eu's international role in this organisation dedicated to the conservation of bluefin tuna. the european union has been a non-cooperating contracting party to the enlarged commission of the ccsbt since 2006. the european union has pursued a policy of very active participation in all regional fisheries organisations, with the aim of contributing to the rational and sustainable management of marine resources and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. some of these organisations deal with all fish stocks in a specific area, while others manage highly migratory species particularly tuna over large geographical areas. the most significant for the european union is the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat), which is responsible for the conservation of tuna and tuna-like species in the atlantic ocean and adjacent seas. the commission for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna (ccsbt) is important for our seas because it manages southern bluefin tuna in all its distribution areas.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of the proposal is to authorise the exchange of letters between the eu and the enlarged commission of the southern bluefin tuna convention (scctb). the signature of this international legal instrument will allow the eu to become a full member of the ccsbt enlarged commission from its current status as a non-cooperating non-contracting party (which does not allow it to have voting rights, but it must respect the technical stock management guidelines). the committee therefore welcomes the possibility of at least having an active role in management decisions.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the proposal for the union's accession to the enlarged commission of the convention for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna. the exchange of letters should be terminated in order to complete the legal procedure. the union can no longer afford to maintain the current role of non-contracting party, which has been in place since 2006. such accession is consistent with the policies of the european union, since it has the competence to adopt measures for the conservation of marine biological resources under the common fisheries policy and to conclude agreements with third countries and international organisations. but above all, this action line will promote consistency in the union's conservation approach across the oceans and reinforce its commitment to the long-term conservation and sustainable use of fisheries resources worldwide. i would remind you that the main interest for the eu is the similarities between the management of southern bluefin tuna (sbct) and that of atlantic bluefin tuna (iccat). finally, let us not forget that vessels flying the flag of the member states of the union exploit the resources in the southern bluefin tuna area. it is therefore in the interest of the union to play an active role in the application of the convention.
in writing. ‒ the ccsbt convention, or commission for the conservation of southern bluefin tuna, to which the european union has been a cooperating non-contracting party since 2006, was open only to states and excluded regional economic integration organisations such as the european union. in october 2013, at its 20th meeting, the ccsbt amended the resolution on the enlarged commission to allow regional economic integration organisations wishing to become members of the enlarged commission through an exchange of letters in which the requesting body firmly commits the ccsbt to the terms of the convention and to the decisions of the enlarged commission of the ccsbt. the aim is to enable the eu to participate fully in the activities of the southern bluefin tuna convention (sbct). i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the langen report, which analyses the updating of the text in force since 2002 on insurance intermediation, is agreeable and well thought out. i believe that the choice of a directive rather than a regulation will ensure, in the implementation of the text, the prerogatives of each individual member state, ensuring the right balance between the legitimate interest of the market and the needs of consumer protection. for all these reasons i intend to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i strongly supported the report by mr langen on insurance intermediation. this new directive, the result of three years of work, is a small but decisive instrument towards a stronger single market for insurance products. the directive regulates direct distribution by giving uniform rules, legal certainty and regulatory consistency to all sales channels in the sector. it will be implemented in the union within 24 months of its entry into force. the many advantages, primarily for consumers: in addition to specific measures for their protection, common principles are recognised to ensure greater transparency. it also reduces the costs of cross-border access to insurance products, allowing european citizens greater choice. other important measures concern the registration and qualification of insurance companies and the provision of a strengthened product supervision system. it is a new achievement in the consolidation of the financial integration of the european union.
in writing. - i vote for it. insurance distribution is a sector which is subject to a level of harmonisation which differs from the general rules of the internal market of the union. in this case, we are faced with the expressed intention of achieving a minimum of harmonization in the insurance sector (and this is already a positive thing for our delegation). the text also focuses on consumer standards, which must be maintained at a certain level of protection in each member state. in our view, this directive seems to strike the right balance between the legitimate interest of the market (in accordance with the principle of freedom of establishment) and the need to protect users of insurance services. this directive should bring about an internal market for life and non-life insurance products and services. the text defines the scope of the directive, the areas excluded and the tasks of the member states' authorities (exchange of information, provision of single points of contact). the directive, which does not intend to impose any new burdens on undertakings, will have to be reviewed five years after its entry into force, also to assess whether the principle of proportionality has been properly applied. the amendments made by the agreement with the council include the title of the directive itself, which will become: insurance distribution, not insurance brokerage. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i voted in favour of the supplementary report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on insurance intermediation, as i consider the principle of consumer protection to be a key value. i therefore support the proposal for a directive which harmonises insurance regulation, makes the link with banking discipline more coherent and strengthens the resilience of the european financial system to self-induced and hetero-induced events. i support the objective of increasing the level of consumer protection, in particular through greater transparency in the price and cost of insurance, better and more comprehensible information and rules of business conduct, to prevent consumers from buying products which do not meet their needs. i am firmly convinced that the objective of saving on insurance policy, together with the mitigation of the factors distorting competition in the insurance sector, necessarily requires a harmonization of the system at european level and a european strengthening of the protection of the end user.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a recast of the insurance intermediation directive (directive 2002/92/ec). the aim of this proposal is to improve the regulation of the retail insurance market, to ensure a level playing field between all participants involved in the sale of insurance products and to strengthen the protection of insured persons. the new directive should extend the scope of directive 2002/92/ec to all distribution channels. clarify the exercise of the freedom of establishment, the freedom to provide services, and the powers of supervisory authorities; identify, manage and mitigate conflicts of interest; increase the level of harmonisation of administrative sanctions and measures in case of infringement of the key provisions of the directive in force; improving the adequacy and objectivity of consumer advice; ensure that the professional qualifications of sellers correspond to the complexity of the products sold; simplify and harmonise the procedure for cross-border entry into insurance markets across the eu. finally, the new directive should ensure greater transparency and information for the benefit of consumers.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a directive on insurance intermediation aims to improve the regulation of the insurance market. the proposal aims to ensure a level playing field for all those involved in the sale of insurance products and to offer greater protection to those who sign such contracts. i have decided to vote in favour of this report because, thanks to the changes in the regulations, consumers and investors who decide to buy insurance products will be able to obtain numerous benefits. first, greater transparency will be ensured: insurance agents will have to be more transparent in terms of the price and cost of their products, with an obligation to provide the customer with detailed and comprehensible information, so that consumers can make more informed decisions. secondly, the new rules on transparency and business conduct will ensure that consumers are not sold products which do not fully meet their needs.
in writing. ‒ this is an update of the insurance intermediation directive (imd 1) dating back to 2002. the text was amended and voted on in the econ committee during the last parliamentary term. during the current session, trilogues were held with the council and the commission (always with the same rapporteur). the most important new features introduced by imd 2 are: extending the scope of the legislation to all categories of intermediaries, those performing ancillary functions and, in particular, to insurance undertakings operating in a direct selling model; introduction of many transparency rules and much more information for consumers; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. increased alignment with mifid. however, the original proposal provided for the introduction of a full disclosure requirement on the level of remuneration received by intermediaries. this obligation does not appear in the final text. the intermediaries will then be free to continue to receive commissions without the obligation to disclose. this is the only critical point in the directive. the imd 2 is, however, a step ahead of the imd1 in other respects. that is why i have decided to abstain in plenary.
in writing. ‒ the resolution contains the compromise text reached between the european parliament and the council and aims to improve the regulation of the insurance retail market and to regulate distribution activities through greater harmonisation of national legislation. i voted in favour of the resolution because it will bring considerable benefits both to the insurance industry and to european consumers. in particular, it will help to ensure a level playing field between all those involved in the sale of insurance products, strengthen the protection of insured persons and simplify and harmonise the procedures for ensuring the exercise of the activity of insurance intermediaries in the european single market.
in writing. ‒ the report under review is part of the broader audit spectrum of all financial markets following the financial crisis. the two main elements are the creation of a more cohesive and integrated single market and greater consumer protection. this directive succeeds in harmonizing the insurance market, but allows the national legislator to apply higher levels of protection in particular cases. the citizen will thus be able to benefit from rules which are comparable between the various countries, but which also reflect the particularities of the insurance market in the member state. the main elements introduced are: rules to encourage the exchange of information in european formats; the distinction between investment services and insurance services to provide greater security for citizens who decide to stay away from the most dangerous financial operations; and finally, in view of the fact that some operators were able to open agencies in member states where they were subject to inferior forms of control and then operate in other states with a considerable competitive advantage, with this directive, the legislators moved the control centre to the country where the operations take place as a priority, so that the italian citizen can be safe from possible fraudulent operations.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep legislative resolution welcoming the agreement with the council on the insurance intermediation and distribution (idd) directive, because it completes the single market for insurance services and specifically tackles the excessive fragmentation of insurance intermediaries and products caused by the financial crisis, promoting fair competition and strengthening consumer rights. member states will have two years to transpose the new legislation into national law. the latter sets very ambitious objectives and is an important step forward compared with the insurance intermediation directive, since it also extends the scope to insurance distribution. the new directive aims to create a level playing field in the market for retail insurance and its intermediaries, to reduce the costs of cross-border access (by increasing choice), and to establish a single registration system for intermediaries. it also introduces a principle of proportionality for insurance intermediaries. finally, the ep helped to introduce qualifying aspects into the directive, namely the rules aimed at strengthening the qualification requirements for intermediaries, the transparency of sellers' fees, the standardisation of information documents, aimed at explaining the risk, type and scope of insurance products.

in writing. ‒ this directive on insurance intermediation is of the utmost importance for strengthening the single market, increasing transparency and improving consumer protection. the adoption of this text will make it possible to give citizens more choice by providing them with all the information they need to understand what they are buying. the directive, which is based on national insurance distribution schemes, sets minimum standards for distributors, allowing member states' legislators to apply higher levels of consumer protection. this directive ensures greater regulatory consistency across all sales channels, while maintaining the right balance between the application of the rules and proportionality for minor insurance products, if sold as an ancillary product. it must be increasingly clear to citizens what they are paying for a purchase or investment in an insurance product. our objective of balancing consumer protection with corporate sustainability has been achieved through this text.
in writing. ‒ imd 2 updates the 2002 directive on insurance intermediation. the most important new features in imd 2 are: extends the scope of the european legislation to all categories of intermediaries; introduces many transparency rules for the benefit of consumers; requires higher professional standards for insurance intermediaries; calls for greater responsibility for instruments sold to consumers; ensures alignment with existing european legislation. however, the original proposal also provided for full disclosure of the level of remuneration received by intermediaries (whether fixed or variable). this obligation no longer appears in the final text. intermediaries will therefore be free to continue to receive commissions without being required to disclose them. the negotiation process for this text was very long. this was amended and voted on in the econ committee during the previous legislature. during the current one the negotiations with the council and the commission were concluded, but this delay did not allow us to make any changes to the text of the directive. in all, we are satisfied with the outcome of the negotiations. imd 2 is certainly a step forward from imd 1. however, the critical issue of the lack of transparency on remuneration remains. that is why we thought it appropriate to abstain during the vote in the house.
