in writing. ‒ in the european union, more than one in four children is at risk of poverty or social exclusion. the increase in inequality and child poverty are therefore realities that we cannot ignore. among the elements that have underlined this trend are austerity policies and their effects on socioeconomic conditions and the labour market in the various countries, which have again demonstrated the link between wealth redistribution and employment policies and the widening of the social gap. in this context, the report, which i support, aims to give greater visibility to the fight against child poverty, reminding us that an integrated approach is needed to tackle this problem. while we must strengthen the social protection system within the union so that it can guarantee all children access to health care and quality education, housing and balanced nutrition, we must also put families, especially the most disadvantaged, in a position to offer their children the best possible living conditions by increasing existing opportunities in the labour market and ensuring that parents have a better work-life balance.
in writing. ‒ austerity policies are creating social disasters in europe: it is now clear to all that the cuts in social services and investment by the states have doubled the number of families living in poverty and social exclusion in europe. the people most affected by austerity are children and single mothers: the proportion of children living in absolute and long-term poverty (over 3 years) is increasing. in countries like estonia, greece and italy, the number of children who can't eat meat, chicken or fish for two consecutive days in a month has doubled. increasing poverty also affects access to childcare, education and health services: since 2008, the number of families unable to send their children to nursery or higher education and who have to forgo medical or surgical treatment because of lack of money has increased in all member states. increasing inequality and poverty are exacerbating social fragmentation and school dropout, depressing consumption and risking triggering far-reaching recessionary spirals. it is therefore clear that austerity has failed: we need to reverse course and realize that no accounting data is worth as much as the health of our children.
in writing. ‒ the report recommends the development of a roadmap for the implementation of the three-pillar approach adopted in the recommendation 'investing in children: breaking the vicious circle of social disadvantage', by developing precise and specific indicators of the level of child poverty and the areas most affected by it. the member states will thus have to implement the specific recommendations issued by the commission in the context of the european semester. the goals are noble and shared (combating child poverty, children's access to free public education and adequate care at affordable prices...), but i do not see how they can be achieved by insisting on the failed and undemocratic governance model represented by the european semester. moreover, to demand a greater role for the commission in the field of social assistance is to presage excessive interference in the competences of the member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report considering that the fight against child poverty needs to be given greater visibility at the highest european political levels if the eu is to achieve the europe 2020 target of reducing the number of people living in poverty by at least 20 million by 2020, and considering also that social inequalities, which have increased due to irresponsible and financially unsustainable public and budgetary policies, are a major factor in the increase in child poverty, and that in nineteen member states children are the most at risk of poverty. in accordance with the united nations convention on the rights of the child, all children should be guaranteed the right to education, health care services, housing, protection and participation in decisions affecting them. finally, i would stress the need for the commission to invest in publicly funded and publicly supported education, designating specific teaching methods for the most vulnerable social groups, because i believe that education can be a key priority in ensuring that children acquire the skills that will enable them to access skilled jobs.
in writing. ‒ child poverty in europe is increasing at an alarming rate. in numerical terms, between 2008 and 2012, the number of children at risk of poverty or social exclusion in europe increased by almost one million, with an increase of half a million in the period between 2011 and 2012 alone. child poverty deprives millions of children of access to education, health care services, protection, recreation and leisure, balanced nutrition and a normal family environment. the main factors that contribute to child poverty are poor management of wealth redistribution strategies, ineffective state income support measures, inadequate provision of care services and the precarious employment situation of parents. i therefore agree with the rapporteur's proposal to devise important policies to combat this phenomenon, aiming to stem the causes of such poverty and to increase the effectiveness, quantity and scope of social support specifically aimed at children. it will also be necessary to promote labour laws guaranteeing social rights and a minimum wage, in order to provide greater security for families and to combat precarious work.
in writing. ‒ the objective of the proposal is to increase and strengthen in terms of quantity, amount and effectiveness the support to social rights, in particular in relation to the situation of children, but also to parents (such as unemployment benefits or increased maternity and paternity rights), by promoting labour laws that guarantee social rights and family security and combat precarious work, illegal recruitment and exploitation of workers, by implementing or strengthening universal social benefits for children as an inherent right of the child. for these reasons, my vote was in favour.
in writing. ‒ social inequalities are a major driver of child poverty and, according to recent data, are increasing in europe, although reducing social exclusion and poverty is one of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. the european parliament, in its resolution, which i voted for, calls on the commission and the member states to take urgent measures to deal with these problems. in particular, there is a call for more investment that has an impact on children, for example in education and training, including through better use of the european social fund, the european fund for aid to the most deprived and the eu programme for employment and social innovation. it is also felt that children should also be a priority in the programming and implementation of regional and cohesion policies. the european parliament called on the commission to develop indicators for analysing child poverty, with reference to access to education, childcare, health services and housing. only with clear data on the scale of social exclusion and child poverty can we put the right policies in place.
in writing. ‒ according to the un convention on the rights of the child, all children must be guaranteed the right to education, health services, housing, protection, leisure and family life. however, within the eu, the convention is far from being fulfilled. child poverty in europe is growing alongside rising social inequalities. the latter generate intergenerational disadvantages and the negative effects of poverty and social exclusion on children can last a lifetime. poverty is multidimensional and must be understood not only as the lack of coverage of children's basic needs, but also as the lack of access to education and the inability to participate in recreational activities. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is essential to give children the opportunity to live in an environment which enables them to grow and develop the cognitive, communication, social and emotional skills which are essential for their future.

in writing. ‒ the concept of marginalised communities was introduced in the erdf regulation in 2013 with the aim of combating the consequences of marginalisation affecting individuals and communities, such as linguistic and religious minorities, migrants, refugees, people with disabilities and the elderly. marginalisation in this case means that these people are systematically excluded from social and political processes, or that they lack access to basic public infrastructure and services. the task of cohesion policy is precisely to tackle discrimination and to try to change the situation, first by extending the possibility of funding also to actions and projects aimed at supporting marginalised communities, improving access to public services, setting up accountable, transparent and democratic structures and encouraging member states to use the esf to support informal and lifelong learning projects, as well as cultural and innovative projects.
in writing. ‒ the report highlights how the economic crisis and budget cuts have worsened the social situation, leading to difficult situations in terms of housing and health. it is highlighted that the european regional development fund and the european social fund play a specific and important role, with at least 20% of the esf allocated in each member state to the specific objective of promoting social inclusion and combating poverty and all forms of discrimination, thus representing a crucial tool in promoting greater inclusion of marginalised communities. cohesion policy, it is stressed, can and must add value to the work already under way in the member states. by focusing on improving employment opportunities, participation in society and investing in skills, especially in the regions that need them most, cohesion policy should ideally lead, among other benefits, to greater social inclusion and poverty reduction, providing member states with the flexibility to implement individualised support in line with local needs and ensuring that funding is used in areas where unemployment is highest and where funding is most needed. for these reasons, i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ provide as soon as possible a precise and, if possible, comprehensive definition of 'marginalized communities' and promote a process of protection and integration aimed at promoting their integration into the european social fabric. there is no comprehensive definition of 'marginalized community' at european level. the first step is to understand the phenomenon of exclusion by analysing its specific connotations. the typical and specific situations and needs of the different realities should be examined and the living and working conditions, access to education and health care systems, the level of employment, school dropout rates should be assessed. in this context, europe's task is to establish a set of common indicators that will allow the concept of 'marginalized communities' to be reconstructed in a uniform and shared way. cohesion policy thus becomes a driving force for development by supporting the economic, social and territorial inclusion of minorities. the next step is to extend these measures to all minorities who are currently excluded, so that the process of breaking down moral and material boundaries can be implemented. to do this, a shared strategy is needed, starting from the common elaboration of the concept of 'marginalized communities' to measures that reduce the distances of diversity in the name of formal and substantive equality.

in writing. ‒ the challenges facing us today require a global response, and the main forum within which to strengthen international governance and promote the interests of the european union remains the united nations. the european union's contribution to the international arena in the fields of diplomacy and security, humanitarian aid and economic aid, and its concrete commitment to promoting environmentally sound and sustainable policies, place it at the forefront of the united nations. however, in order to make the most of this potential and to ensure that its international action has a real and effective value, the union must act as united and compactly as possible. this is done by making its voice heard on issues of fundamental importance, such as reform of the un system, and by expanding its influence, especially in areas where it has the tools and capacity to take a leading role, such as action for sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ the european union has a great responsibility to the world, both as a major macro-regional actor and as a rich and developed reality that is a virtuous example of democracy, peaceful coexistence between different cultures and stability. the eu can and must play a leading role in the world in protecting human rights, promoting a sustainable and inclusive development model, supporting democracy and civil liberties, encouraging the fight against climate change, disseminating knowledge and expertise, moving towards a more just and cohesive world, and countering dictatorships and international terrorism. but europe can only do this if it speaks with one voice: you have to throw your heart over the obstacle and take the step forward. start a federal constituent phase that will provide the union with a genuine european government with exclusive powers over defence, foreign policy and international emergencies. only then will the voice of the european citizens be given even more authority and respect. only then will the eu's contribution to the un be more useful and effective.
in writing. ‒ i abstain because, although the report's comments on the current administrative management of the un's internal functioning and decision-making processes are positive, expenditure commitments and reporting on activities appear to be too opaque and ineffective. however, the eu's mere 'increased presence' in the un bodies would give it too much legitimacy as a political entity able to represent the interests of the european peoples. the united nations is a very important institution, and it is not just the united nations that is to be reformed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the 'role of the eu in the united nations' because the european union is actively involved, under the aegis of the un, in promoting peace, security and progress through its common foreign and security policy. the eu and its member states therefore have a crucial role to play in promoting the principles and objectives of the un and in solving the common problems of humanity. the un must remain a strategic reference point for the external action of the european union, which, taking all its member states together, is the main net contributor to the budget of the world organisation. the strengthening of the eu within the un is a step in the right direction, not least because it consolidates some of the most important acquisitions introduced by the lisbon treaty.
in writing. ‒ the report by mr väyrynen supports a process of un reform which would allow the eu to play a more prominent role both in the security council (cs) and in the general assembly, taking into account all the powers granted to the union in the un framework and referring to the proposal for the eu's seat in an enlarged security council. the un reform is proposed in three main areas: enhanced representativeness and a stronger role for the general assembly, accompanied by a reform of the cos that expands its responsibilities as a world government; enhanced transparency and gender equality for all un institutions, starting with the secretary-general; the european council also adopted a resolution on the future of the european union. the permanent members are invited not to veto the coc's reform proposals, in particular the institution of the veto, in cases of genocide or crimes against humanity. the commission is also proposing that the next secretary-general should be a woman, which would be unprecedented in the history of the united nations. my vote on this report was in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union is one of the main regional organisations. its activities are fully in line with the principles of the un charter: pursuant to articles 3 and 21 teu, the union shall define and implement common policies and actions aimed at ensuring a high level of cooperation in all areas of international relations, and shall include peace, security, development and global human rights among the objectives of its external action. these are interrelated challenges that can only be addressed through strong and coherent action by the entire international community. the role of the union's foreign policy as a unified and authoritative actor within the united nations system can be decisive in this respect. this is particularly true for the defence of peace and security, for the resolution of regional conflicts and the 'malfunctioning' of states and, of course, for the fight against terrorism, organised crime, the proliferation of firearms, explosives and weapons of mass destruction. it would therefore be useful to reform the un system in order to give the union a permanent seat in an enlarged security council. i voted in favour of this in the hope that we can move in this direction.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the role of the eu in the united nations. the european union and its member states share and promote the values and principles of the united nations charter (article 21 (1) teu). parliament therefore welcomes the eu's important contribution to development and humanitarian aid worldwide and recalls that the eu has become a genuine international actor with 'privileged observer' status at the united nations and that the eu has committed itself to actively supporting a comprehensive reform of the un system in order to strengthen its legitimacy and regional representation. parliament stressed in particular its conviction that the security council should be reformed and the eu's important long-term objective of having a seat in an enlarged security council. parliament reiterated its call on the vp/hr for foreign and security policy to seek common eu positions on issues within the competence of the security council and supported the objective of establishing a multilateral investment protection regime.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr paavo väyrynen on the role of the eu in the united nations, because i agree with what is explained and analysed in the report. the eu's objectives and strengths lie in security and peace, which are linked to the development of global human rights. in this context, the eu's strength lies in its ability to mobilise resources across the full spectrum of diplomatic, economic and humanitarian development areas. the european union should be able to guarantee its integrity and peace mobilization in international relations in accordance with the principles of the 1975 united nations charter. the eu and its member states play an active role and contribute to the work of the un system in different formats and ways.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this important report, which is even more important today because of the situation we are experiencing, generated by the recent terrorist attacks. i agree with the proposals put forward. first of all, there is a need for reform of the un, both in terms of its internal organs and in terms of its objectives and instruments. it is also essential that the union acquires a greater say in this system, coordinating more effectively with the member states and increasing its influence through its role as a privileged observer. i also believe it is important to improve early warning tools to strengthen prevention, as well as to strengthen the role of the international criminal court.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on strengthening the eu's role in the un system because i believe that many of the problems facing the european union in the areas of peace and security, environment and sustainable development, immigration and human rights, international trade and economic growth require global solutions. therefore, i believe that the eu must work through effective and coordinated activities that strengthen its own influence and that of its member states within the united nations system, which is the world's main forum for improving global governance and the best forum in which to promote the eu's values and interests.
in writing. ‒ the european union is a central pillar of the un system and has already amply demonstrated over the years the positive contribution it can make to the activities of the un. the european union and the united nations have worked together in a determined and constant manner over the past few years to strengthen the principles of multilateralism in the world. the need for increased cooperation with the un and for a stronger eu voice at the un has been repeatedly underlined within the union institutions. even in the light of new global crises and the many challenges of global governance, the eu must work to further strengthen the un's action and make the decision-making process of the entire un system more effective, making the most of partnerships with un agencies, funds, programmes, commissions and specialised committees and playing a more coordinated role within the general assembly.
in writing. ‒ the eu's role in the un needs to be completely reviewed. i hope that some member states will denounce this hypocrisy, the scandals and the power games that have been played out. the way the whole si case was handled is proof of that.
in writing. the european union is the most successful historical example of regional integration and cooperation in the world. the ideal and practical contribution which europe can make to world peace must be strengthened by every means, especially in view of the many global crises which are now unfolding. i therefore agree with the report by mr vayrinen, who has presented a very ambitious text on behalf of the committee on foreign affairs, which contains a number of points of great interest. i think it is important to reiterate, as the resolution does, that the eu should seek to strengthen global governance within the un system and increase its own influence and that of its member states within that system. the european union must actively support a comprehensive reform of the un system in order to strengthen its legitimacy, regional representativeness and transparency, accountability and effectiveness in responding to today's complex and articulated challenges. i am confident that the work of high representative federica mogherini will be up to this important objective.
in writing. ‒ i voted strongly in favour of the resolution on the role of the european union in the united nations how best to achieve the union's foreign policy objectives, because i believe that the eu is a key player in the international context and plays a predominant role in ensuring and supporting global peace, stability and security processes. there is no doubt that the eu's foreign policy objectives are closely linked to those of the un, and that the un is the eu's most important forum for global governance and for resolving conflicts and disputes. the international situation is becoming increasingly unstable and there are outbreaks of tension, if not outright conflict, in various parts of the world. the situation in eastern ukraine, the civil war in syria, the advance of terrorist organisations such as isis or boko haram represent global threats that must be addressed and resolved under the aegis of the un. finally, i believe that the problem of environmental sustainability is a serious one for future generations and that it cannot be postponed any longer. i therefore hope that the un climate conference (cop21) will be a fruitful cooperation between the eu and the un, so as to ensure that a binding and universal agreement is reached.
in writing. i voted in favour of this important motion for a resolution on the role of the eu in the united nations. in view of the growing challenges on the international scene, i believe that dialogue between the eu and the united nations is of paramount importance. in this context, the provision in question proposes the means for reviving the role of the general assembly and a reform of the un security council. in particular, this proposal calls for the improvement of the international instruments which can be activated and used under the auspices of the united nations for early warning and peacekeeping operations. for its part, the eu, also taking into account the recent atrocities and human rights violations perpetrated by certain extremist and terrorist groups, must offer concrete support to peacebuilding and peacekeeping operations and strengthen its mediation efforts in conflict resolution.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the report on the role of the european union in the united nations and how best to achieve the union's foreign policy objectives. the un system aims to improve global governance and is the best forum in which to promote the values of the european union. the european union in turn shares and promotes the values and objectives of the un charter, for example by promoting peace, security and progress (think of the common foreign and security policy cfsp and the common security and defence policy csdp), by promoting the economic, social and environmental progress of developing countries, by combating social and food inequalities and poverty, and by providing humanitarian assistance. in addition, the union, together with its states, constitutes the main financial contribution to the un's general budget. it is therefore appropriate to step up joint efforts between the eu and the un, promoting shared values and supporting governments, civil society and people in the poorest countries. greater and more intensive eu-un cooperation will facilitate the participation of civil society in the political process, improve the lives of future generations and ensure equitable and sustainable development for all.
in writing. ‒ given the importance of the united nations as the most relevant and comprehensive assembly for the improvement and definition of global governance, i can only welcome a proposal aimed at improving its functioning. the recent events in paris, the deterioration of the situation in syria and the continuing serious instability in the middle east make it clear that there is a need for an effective multilateral approach to global issues under the aegis of the un. a stronger and more efficient model of international cooperation is in fact consistent with european foreign policy and would help achieve its objectives. given the primary role played at international level, especially with neighbouring countries, i support the provision for a permanent seat for the eu in a reformed security council. in this context, recalling the provisions of chapter vii of the un charter on the promotion and inclusion of regional organisations, we call for a strengthened role for the european union and its counterparts both within the un and in global governance more generally. given my political commitment, the personal struggles i have fought in this area and my consistency with the values of the european union, i share the wish that the next un secretary-general should be a woman.

in writing. ‒ the eu is committed to multilateralism centred on a strong and effective united nations. this commitment is based on the conviction that in order to be able to respond to global crises, challenges and threats, the international community needs an efficient multilateral system, based on universal norms and values. to cooperate better with the un, the eu should seek to strengthen its influence. in the context of the general assembly, for example, the eu should play a more prominent role in order to gain greater visibility and political authority. the european parliament, through this report, wishes to underline the importance of reviving the work of the general assembly and is convinced that the security council must be reformed. parliament also called for improved early warning instruments and a stronger un mediation capacity, with coherent and achievable mandates for peacekeeping operations. i hope that the european union will have a single common representative in the security council and that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the world's steelworks produce 1.8 tonnes of steel, but we consume only one and a half tonnes. we have 300 million overcapacity. the surplus is increasing but the market is not able to absorb the supply. by 2030, the eu's share will fall to 9% of world production; china will account for 51%. of the world's top 50 producers, at least 30 will be chinese, and only 4 will be european. but we must also consider the availability of the planet's iron reserves, which are estimated to be 65 years old. the reserves are also running out in the steel raw materials sector. in order to forge more steel, must we naturally inflate global economic demand, for example by building large unnecessary buildings and producing more unnecessary cars? we are called upon to propose alternatives to this economic and ecological failure. we must understand how much steel we really need and produce it in a way that respects safety, health and the environment. this also means closing obsolete plants and investing in research aimed at sustainability, encouraging the conversion to the green economy and the circular economy.

in writing. ‒ article 11 of the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 provides for the possibility of using the flexibility instrument to finance exceptional expenditure which could not be financed within the available ceilings of one or more headings. this is the case with regard to the immigration issue, since the measures envisaged by the eu commission exceeded the limits for the year 2016 provided for under heading 3 (security and citizenship) and, to a lesser extent, also under heading 4 (global europe). it was therefore decided to use this special instrument for an amount of eur 1.5 billion. the payment appropriations will amount to eur 734 million in 2016, eur 654 million in 2017, eur 83 million in 2018 and eur 58 million in 2019. although i am against the overall agreement on the eu budget, i believe that this measure is necessary for an immediate european response to the management of the immigration emergency, which now affects different european fronts.
in writing. ‒ the various crises that the european union has been facing for years, from economic to migration, have led to frequent use of the european budget's flexibility instrument. this is also the case for financing and implementing the actions included in the european agenda on migration in 2016, which required an increase in resources of eur 1,530 million, made possible by the amounts not used in the budgetary years 2014 and 2015. the fact that all available budgetary surpluses have already been allocated to tackle the refugee crisis in europe means that no additional amount can be carried over to the financial year 2017, so that in case of emergency situations the budgetary flexibility can be increased to a maximum of eur 471 million per year. the need to reopen the political debate on budgetary flexibility is quite clear, because in times of difficulty and uncertainty political and economic developments may require frequent adjustments and the union will need to be able to intervene, to strengthen its policies and, if necessary, to trigger extraordinary measures. i voted in favour of the report in the hope that we will start thinking about this.

in writing. ‒ following the severe floods in central europe in 2002, the eu established the eu solidarity fund (eusf) to enable the union to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergency situations and to show solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters. unfortunately, the bureaucratic procedures for accessing the funds are very complex and the quotas that can be agreed are really very small. i have put two questions to that effect: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and the commission, calling for an increase in the appropriations for the fund and for simplification of procedures. the report adopted examines article 4a of the regulation establishing the solidarity fund, which provides for the possibility of mobilising the fund up to a maximum amount of eur 50 000 000 for the payment of advances and the entry of the corresponding appropriations in the general budget of the union. this report calls for an amount equal to the ceiling of eur 50 million in appropriations, commitments and payments to be mobilised in the general budget for 2016 for the payment of advances. i hope that this measure will speed up the european union's response to major natural disasters. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ the solidarity fund is an important support instrument that europe makes available to member states affected by major natural disasters. its effectiveness depends mainly on two variables: the flexibility and rapidity of activation. as this report considers and improves both aspects, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the eu solidarity fund (eusf) was established to enable the union to respond to emergencies caused by major natural disasters and to show solidarity with regions affected by such events. the fund may provide financial support to member states and countries engaged in accession negotiations which have been affected by major natural disasters, i.e. where the total direct damage caused by the disaster exceeds eur 3 billion, equal to 0,6% of the gni of the country concerned, whichever is the lower. it may also be mobilised in the event of a regional disaster. the mff regulation for the period 2014-2020 (article 10) allows the mobilisation of the fund up to an annual ceiling of eur 500 million, above the limits of the relevant headings of the financial framework. the proposal aims to enter in the general budget of the union for 2016 an amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the timely and efficient payment of advances in the event of disasters occurring in the coming year. the aim is to speed up the disbursement of aid to the countries concerned by paying an advance before the final decision is taken.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the joint draft general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016, approved by the conciliation committee, which provides for commitment appropriations of eur 155 004.2 million and payment appropriations of eur 143 885.3 million. the report aims at the full use of the margins of the priority programmes for growth and jobs and provides an additional allocation to horizon 2020, eur 500 million to support farmers, especially in the dairy sector, and a joint statement on the continuation of the youth employment initiative.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the agreement between parliament and the council on the general budget of the european union for 2016, whereby our proposal for the allocation of the union's financial resources reflects the need to address the priorities for action that have recently emerged. we have succeeded in having the maximum of available appropriations devoted to the migration and refugee crisis, in line with the commission's proposal and against the cuts proposed by the council, totalling over one billion euro. the commission will also continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance to the countries of central and eastern europe, including the countries of the former soviet union, the countries of the former soviet union and the countries of central and eastern europe. particular attention was paid to research and innovation, the real engines of competitiveness, to consolidate efforts in building technologically advanced digital infrastructures. it is therefore a budget that looks to the future and is based on the idea of inclusive and sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ the outcome of the conciliation, given the points that emerged in the final approval, does not allow me to express a positive vote because two key issues were not taken into account. firstly, parliament has ignored the council's request to determine the substantial budget lines which are not priority and which can possibly be reduced, making it more difficult to reduce waste in a real and effective way, and thus not allowing any significant cuts on many items which in our view could be reduced. moreover, instead of focusing on the delicate issue of payments, the council has persisted in postponing the aforementioned problem, which is constantly reappearing every year; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i therefore decided to vote against the report for the reasons stated above.
in writing. ‒ the final approval of the agreement on the 2016 eu budget was voted on today; the final figure is 155 billion in commitments and almost 144 billion in payments, a sort of middle ground between parliament's proposal and the council's. parliament succeeded in securing an increase in heading ia which partly offset the efsi cuts to horizon 2020, while there was substantial convergence in identifying the immigration issue as a top priority. in heading v (administrative expenditure) the council has succeeded in obtaining modest reductions and has insisted that the european parliament should also commit itself to a reduction of its staff of 5%. however, i do not consider the agreement reached satisfactory and i believe that the conciliation process has failed on two key issues: the council has not been able to agree to the request from parliament to identify those lines which might not be considered as priorities and which could therefore be reduced, while the council has been unwilling to accept the request to continue postponing the issue of payments, demonstrating a total lack of commitment and credibility. the final result satisfies parliament on the surface, but says nothing in substance about the dramatic issue of payments, which will be repeated in the coming years until it reaches a certain breaking point.
in writing. ‒ the health of citizens is a key priority for the european union (eu), and the commission's draft implementing decision to authorise the use of diethyl sulphate is therefore both unreasonable and contrary to fundamental principles. phthalates are chemicals obtained by industrial distillation from petroleum, which are commonly added to plastics to make them flexible. but they 're not all the same . some are considered harmless to human health, while others are very dangerous. diethyl sulphate (dehp) is an endocrine disruptor; this substance is already classified as toxic to reproduction and is included in the list of substances of very high concern under the reach regulation, i.e. those substances for which there is scientific evidence of the likelihood of serious effects on human health or the environment. the resolution calls on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision and to submit a new draft. the health of the citizens is always the first priority for us in the five star movement, and that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i do not share the positions taken in this resolution, which is a mere act of opposition to the authorisation of the uses of di-2-ethyl sulphate (dehp), which is entirely self-serving, by the greens and the gue. that's why i didn't want to support you with my vote.
in writing. ‒ objection to a draft commission implementing decision: requests that the commission withdraw it and submit a new one rejecting the applications for authorisation of the formulation of recycled soft pvc containing dehp. in september 2014, echa recommended the authorisation of dehp for use in specific applications, including recycled soft pvc. the reasons given by the greens and gue, the promoters of the objection, seem to be mostly dictated by their usual prejudice towards the chemical industry. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the objection under article 106 of the regulation concerning the authorisation of uses of di-2-ethyl sulphate (dehp). dehp is classified as a toxic substance of very high concern because of its endocrine disrupting properties in the environment. such endocrine-disrupting activity has been scientifically demonstrated and has adverse causal effects on human health. in fact, exposure to dehp during the adolescent developmental phase can cause irreversible effects on the body, with serious and severe reproductive consequences that may occur for the first time even after many years. the text which was debated in the house proposes that the commission withdraw its draft implementing decision and submit a new one, in which it undertakes to reject applications for authorisation for the use of materials containing dehp. for these reasons i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision and to submit a new draft rejection of applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled soft dehp pvc, or diethyl sulphate. phthalates are chemicals, obtained by industrial distillation from petroleum, that are commonly added to plastics to make them flexible. phthalates are found in everything from floors to disposable bottles, from synthetic textiles to clothing to toys. these are substances classified as toxic and are substitutable for a number of other less dangerous substances.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection, under rule 106 of the rules of procedure, to the granting of an authorisation for dehp uses. the european commission has presented a draft decision, which has not yet been approved by the member states, authorising the recycling of old dehp-containing plastics into new pvc products. dehp is considered a dangerous and toxic substance that interferes with the endocrine system of mammals, as has been scientifically demonstrated, and is banned under the reach regulation concerning the registration, evaluation, authorisation and restriction of chemicals. parliament was concerned that it had not been demonstrated that the risks to workers' health were adequately controlled and stressed the seriousness of the adverse effects that dehp could cause. the ep therefore rejects the granting of an authorisation for dehp uses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution because dehp has been identified as a substance of very high concern as it meets the criteria for a substance with endocrine disrupting properties for which there is scientific evidence of the likelihood of serious effects on human health. in addition, scientific studies have shown that exposure to dehp during sensitive developmental time windows can result in irreversible effects on developmental programming with serious consequences for development and reproduction. finally, considering that the commission has a responsibility to protect european citizens while promoting innovation, including on safer chemicals and substances to promote a resilient economy, i invite the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision and to submit a new draft rejecting the applications for authorisation.
in writing. ‒ i fully agree with the rapporteurs on the rejection of applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled soft pvc containing dehp, mainly because the applicants did not demonstrate the level of risk to the health of workers handling this type of substance and did not provide a full analysis of the alternatives available on the market to replace dehp, and the socioeconomic analysis did not demonstrate any clear economic benefits. therefore, also in view of the hazardous nature of dehp as a toxic substance for health, which is included in annex xiv to the reach regulation, it seems to me appropriate to reject the applications for authorisation and to safeguard the protection of human health and the environment.
in writing. ‒ phthalates are chemicals, obtained by industrial distillation from petroleum, which are commonly added to plastics to make them flexible. there are phthalates in floors and wall coverings, even in office desks and toys. there are low molecular weight, which are the most dangerous for human health and the environment, and high molecular weight, which are considered safe by the european authorities. this substance, already classified as toxic, can be replaced by a number of other substances which are less dangerous. the draft resolution considers that the draft implementing decision exceeds the implementing powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 and calls on the commission to submit a new draft rejection of applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled soft dehp pvc. my vote can only be in favour.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this report because there is no doubt that the rules on osh in several member states need to be brought up to more advanced and stricter standards. in this sense the commission's action can be meaningful and effective.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the draft commission implementing decision concerning the granting of an authorisation for the uses of di-2-ethylsulphate (dehp) under regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 because i believe that the envi committee has taken the right decision in banning the use of this substance by the objection voted today. i believe that health is an absolute value which the european commission has a duty to promote and defend, even at the expense of certain economic freedoms. in the light of the available scientific evidence and the tests carried out, i agree to follow up on the various scientific reports that classify dehp compounds as toxic to reproduction and as endocrine disruptors. we have a duty to protect european workers from the possible consequences of long-term exposure to these substances: i think it is impossible to accept the logic that the socioeconomic benefits of using a certain compound for the production of pvcs may outweigh the health risks, especially in the absence of exhaustive investigations into their phytosanitary impact. i therefore welcome the large majority of parliament's rejection of the proposed implementing act and call on the commission to definitively ban the use of this substance in the circular economy.
in writing. ‒ i thank the rapporteur for his work and i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection under article 106 of the regulation concerning the authorisation of uses of di-2-ethyl sulphate (dehp) because this substance has been found to be toxic and dangerous to the health of european citizens after various scientific studies. i therefore consider the european parliament's decision to reject the european commission's application for authorization for the use and recycling of dehp-containing materials to be correct.
in writing. ‒ the report, which i supported with my vote in favour, identifies the ways in which many multinational companies have evaded or avoided taxation due to host countries, causing serious damage to the economy and the community as a whole. the report also shows very clearly the responsibility and the full involvement in this scandal of jean-claude juncker, who is currently, in my view, unacceptably, president of the european commission.
in writing. ‒ the report contains an in-depth analysis of the 'modus operandi' through which a wide range of multinational companies have been allowed to engage in tax avoidance and/or evasion practices. the european council also called for the european parliament to be given the right to vote and to stand as a candidate in elections. it indicates some, though not sufficient, measures to prevent such practices, proposing inter alia a cover for those who provide information on such practices, including journalists. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i voted in favour of the report on tax ruling and other measures of a similar nature or effect. i am a firm believer in the need to guarantee the principles of transparency and the protection of savings. i have already pointed out on several occasions that the lack of tax harmonization between the member states leads to phenomena of competition and tax dumping which seriously affect economic competition and the proper functioning of the single market. the reality is that there is a difficult coexistence of 28 different corporate taxation regimes and the difficulty of harmonising the corporate tax base. these and many other requests are answered in the proposal for a directive and in the report, for which i voted in favour, aware of the need to eliminate asymmetries between tax systems as soon as possible and to improve cooperation within the eu, since these critical issues are a burden for other taxpayers, including smes and citizens.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks revelations, the european parliament decided to set up a temporary committee to look into the issue of taxation and tax agreements. unfortunately, this committee is not an inquiry committee and it does not aim to highlight the clear political responsibility of juncker, as confirmed by the recent revelations in spiegel, which only reiterate what everyone knows, but which no one wants to admit, about the work of the former luxembourg prime minister. it was clear from the outset that this committee would have difficulties in carrying out its mandate. for example, all tax agreements should be public and verifiable by european citizens. in the light of the above, the m5s europe delegation decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure in question. the so-called 'luxleaks' scandal at the end of 2014 brought to light controversial tax practices in many member states. the public outcry led to the establishment of a special committee on tax and other measures, which was set up in february 2015 to shed light on tax systems in all eu member states, to examine ways to end unfair tax practices and to fight tax fraud in europe. in this report, the european parliament reiterates that multinational companies in all sectors must disclose in a clear and comprehensible manner in their balance sheets, broken down by member state and by third country in which they have an establishment, a range of aggregated information, including their pre-tax profit, income tax, number of employees, assets held and basic information on tax rulings (country by country). finally, it is explicitly emphasised that smes which are not multinational are exempted from these obligations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because i appreciated the objective of fair taxation. however, i have serious doubts about what many of my colleagues have tried to say in reading this report: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. at the same time, it is understandable to try to attract investment by leveraging tax attractiveness, especially through the increased efficiency of public machinery in some (other) countries. i hope, therefore, that we can achieve cooperation which will make it possible to pay the right price in the right place, and not to have to waste time on diversions which do not bring any economic benefit to the territories.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament reaffirms its will to put an end to aggressive tax planning by multinational companies and to adopt a new set of tax policies and to ensure a fair tax system, based on the principle of taxation in the country where profits are generated, thus avoiding distortions of the internal market and unfair competition. i also welcome the commission's commitment to promote the automatic exchange of tax information as a future european and international standard for transparency.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has decided to set up a special committee to look into the issue of taxation and tax agreements. the text of the report was quite satisfactory, as many of the points listed as necessary are the same ones we have been advocating for some time, such as public and understandable country-by-country reporting, a full ccctb to be achieved immediately, an automatic and comprehensive exchange between member states on tax agreements. the text also contains a harsh criticism of the actions of some eu countries which have never shown any sign of cooperation, as well as the european commission itself, which has flattened out the council's positions. the multinationals, the main perpetrators and beneficiaries of these agreements, are also attacked for their behaviour. the text approved by the taxe committee at the end of october is therefore a good one, even if we were too soft on the transparency issue, because in our view all tax agreements should be public and verifiable by european citizens too. for the reasons given, which i do not think are of little importance, i shall abstain.
in writing. ‒ through the practice of advance tax rulings, the tax authorities of a member state provide a company with the manner in which corporate income tax will be calculated and, on the basis of this decision, companies choose the most tax-friendly country. this widespread practice in the european union is damaging competition in the european single market and member states' budgets, and the negative effects are felt by european taxpayers, including small and medium-sized enterprises. the resolution condemns this practice of aggressive tax planning by multinationals and calls on the commission and the member states to put an end to it. i voted in favour of the resolution because i believe that the measures proposed to curb this practice, which is widespread in all the member states, can be effective. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.
in writing. ‒ tax ruling is one of the first major responses by the european institutions to the luxleaks scandal. it was the european parliament which, through its econ and taxe committees, spent the most money denouncing this scandal. since there is free movement of capital in the european single market, the current system of national collection should be abandoned in order to allow for an appropriate exchange of information between the competent authorities. the report also calls on the member states to review the laws which allow for favourable tax regimes at national level, making these countries de facto tax havens. these operations at a time of financial crisis and economic difficulties for many european households are unacceptable. taxation should be paid in the states where the activities are carried out, not in those where there is a better tax treatment. parliament strongly urged that solidarity between member states be respected and that a return to a system of trust between states, industry and citizens be achieved through a body of laws harmonizing the tax systems of the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on tax rulings because certain tax practices should be managed within the member states; in addition, there is a real risk that a collective eu response to tackle tax evasion would place the union itself at a disadvantage vis-à-vis other global competitors.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this report which contains an analysis of the practices through which a wide range of multinational companies have been allowed to engage in tax evasion and/or avoidance. the scandal surrounding luxembourg and president juncker plays a role in this.
in writing. i congratulate mrs ferreira on the important result achieved by the report of the taxe special committee set up by the european parliament. the s&d group, from the very beginning of the work of the special committee, has played a very important role in highlighting the priorities for a fairer and more transparent european tax policy. the tax haven scandal and the frequent phenomena of tax avoidance must end: europe cannot tolerate the persistence in some member states of mechanisms which are so distorting to the single market and to our social model. the cris report makes very concrete proposals which we now hope the commission will take up, also in view of the specific commitments made by president juncker to this effect before parliament.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on tax ruling and other measures of a similar nature or effect because i believe that the proposals made by the taxe special committee on tax ruling transparency and coordination, the common tax base, whistleblower protection and, finally, country-by-country reporting are all very timely and necessary to tackle in a concrete and precise way such annual problems as tax evasion and avoidance in the eu, and consequently multinational companies pay fairly and above all where profits are generated. we are faced with a paradox, which the taxe committee has well highlighted, on the one hand the multinationals who say they are willing to pay taxes and in return demand a level playing field, and on the other hand the need to create equal rules throughout the eu. therefore, i fully agree with the taxe conclusions that the synthesis of this paradox will have to be found in the revision of the corporate tax regime in the eu, in the substantial reform of the corporate tax framework, through the creation of a corporate tax base (ccctb), through appropriate legislative instruments and effective action to counter the tax dumping practiced by many member states.
in writing. as we know, there is no internationally agreed definition of tax rulings, except for a reference by the commission, which defines them as a communication, agreement or any other instrument or action with similar effects. i have decided to support this measure because the function of such decisions should be to provide legal certainty to the taxpayer by reducing the financial risk to honest businesses. unfortunately, their use is instead linked to the dynamics of corporate tax avoidance which has a direct impact on national budgets and on the distribution of the tax burden between categories of taxpayers. i welcome the work of the special committee responsible for this matter, but i also believe that it is vital that all member states, as well as the european institutions, continue to work to prevent harmful tax practices and to promote fairer and more effective corporate taxation in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the report on tax ruling and other measures of a similar nature or effect. the 28 tax systems in the european union differ considerably in terms of both the tax base and the rates. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to apply the principle of subsidiarity to all taxation, including the taxation of goods and services, and that the member states should be able to apply the principle of subsidiarity to all taxation of goods and services. it is therefore essential to develop a fair tax policy as an integral part of the policy of the member states in order to have a harmonized tax situation. the commission notes that the tax rulings are not intended to be used as a basis for the assessment of the taxable profit of the beneficiary of the measure.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the tax proposal as it is also aimed at curbing the current economic crisis. the luxleaks scandal on the one hand and aggressive tax planning by multinational corporations on the other was high on the political agenda of the member states, the eu, the oecd and the g20. however, no significant progress has been made to date. the report by mr ferreira and mr theurer aims to point out that in this context many countries have finally introduced measures to combat tax evasion, in particular the limitation of the deductibility of interest, anti-abuse rules, measures to exclude from public procurement companies that engage in misconduct, and the publication of tax planning mechanisms aimed at restoring greater credibility to the tax system. at the same time, a cooperative approach is certainly desirable, without which further opportunities for tax avoidance in the internal market would be opened up.
in writing. ‒ by adopting this report, we want to underline the need for a balanced and fair fiscal policy as an integral part of structural reforms in the member states. sufficient resources will need to be made available to effectively prevent and detect aggressive tax planning, tax evasion and tax avoidance, and to combat such practices, which lead to a substantial erosion of the tax base. taxation and competition policy must be seen as two sides of the same coin in the internal market. the lack of political will to achieve convergence of national tax policies often leads member states to opt for a bilateral approach, whereas a common approach would be more effective. in the absence of a cooperative approach, unilateral measures contribute to greater complexity, giving rise to new asymmetries and, consequently, to further opportunities for tax avoidance in the internal market. we therefore call for a coordinated approach and the promotion of greater reciprocity. we call on the member states to respect the principle of taxing profits where they are generated and on the commission to fulfil its role as guardian of the treaties by ensuring full respect for eu law and the principle of loyal cooperation between member states.
in writing. ‒ i thank the rapporteurs for their excellent work and, in the interest of greater transparency in tax legislation and rules, i have decided to vote in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks scandal, which broke on 5 november 2014 and exposed questionable tax practices by audit firms in a particular member state, the use of secret agreements involving complex financial structures to obtain drastic tax breaks was exposed. a balanced and fair fiscal policy should therefore be developed as an integral part of structural reforms in the member states. it was therefore necessary to agree on the obligation for multinational companies to declare profits in different states and on a common tax base. i voted in favour of this report so that transparent and law-abiding behaviour can prevail.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament resolution on tax ruling and other measures similar in nature or effect, as i believe it is necessary to combat tax evasion and avoidance in the european union. the main objective of the report is to increase tax transparency and fairness, but without putting european companies at a competitive disadvantage. parliament supported the introduction of the ccctb (common consolidated corporate tax base) and the country-by-country reporting for multinational companies of a wide range of information such as profits, taxes paid and tax agreements.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on tax rulings, which are tax practices put in place by large multinational companies to keep taxpayers' contributions artificially low. the eight months of work by the taxe committee have made it possible to analyse the aggressive tax planning practices, considered to distort competition, implemented by multinationals in some member states. it has therefore become necessary to propose a legal framework to restore tax justice by ensuring that multinational companies provide disaggregated country-by-country data on profits made, taxes paid and subsidies received by states, and meet tax obligations in the places where they make profits. the s&d group considers the fight against unfair tax practices to be a political priority: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. among our proposals in the report i would mention in particular the relaunch of the project for a common corporate tax base, the automatic exchange of information on tax rulings and support for the oecd working group's plan of recommendations on taxation.
in writing. ‒ i abstained in the final vote on the report presented by the special committee set up by the european parliament to examine the taxation and tax agreements secretly granted between 2002 and 2010 by the luxembourg government to multinational companies (luxleaks scandal). we have long been calling for clarity for those responsible for and beneficiaries of these agreements and for the banks involved to clarify the reasons given for avoiding or evading millions of euros in taxes. the european situation is paradoxical: we have millions of citizens who are suffocated by taxes as a result of austerity policies, and on the other hand tax havens (facilitated by the absence of customs duties) which create situations of unfair competition between member states. the current commission president, mr juncker, has been the linchpin of the whole luxembourg system. although the report adopted has positive and agreeable features, unfortunately (1) it makes no reference to the political responsibilities of juncker (former prime minister of luxembourg, as well as its minister of finance for almost 20 years) and (2) the special committee was too soft on the issue of transparency; we believe that all tax agreements should be public and verifiable by european citizens.
in writing. ‒ if this is the result of eight months of investigations into the luxleaks scandal and the need for decisive action to tackle the unacceptable phenomenon of tax evasion and abuse by large multinational companies and unfair competition between states, i am convinced that the expectations and questions of european citizens have remained largely unanswered. although the recommendations of the taxe report contain important countermeasures to combat tax avoidance, such as public country-by-country reporting extended to all multinationals, the introduction of a consolidated common corporate tax base and essential protective measures for whistleblowers, we are still far from achieving full transparency, which is the first step towards ending this problem. the report not only fails to denounce the undeniable political responsibility of those who have endorsed and encouraged these practices, also thanks to a regime of total secrecy, but it continues to keep citizens, investigative journalists and civil society totally in the dark about the privileged treatment reserved for multinational groups through tax rulings concluded with governments, which will remain accessible only to tax authorities. for these reasons, while recognising that some important steps have been taken, i could not vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a report which clearly defines the instruments to be put in place to make tax justice more efficient. it provides for measures to improve tax coordination and cooperation in europe to combat aggressive tax planning through transparency and a code of conduct on taxation.
in writing. ‒ following last year's luxleaks revelations, parliament decided to set up a special committee to look into the issue of taxation and tax agreements. the outcome of the work is summarised in this report, which analyses the current situation and makes recommendations for the future. the final text is quite satisfactory, as many of the points listed as necessary are the same as those which i have been advocating for some time: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the tax base is not too high, and that the tax base is not too low. the text also contains a harsh criticism of the actions of certain countries which have never shown themselves to be cooperative, and of the commission itself which has flattened itself on the council's positions. the multinationals, the main perpetrators and beneficiaries of these agreements, are also attacked for their behaviour. the text adopted is therefore a good one, providing for adequate protection for whistleblowers and highlighting the negative role of consultancy firms and banks. what is lacking, however, is a clear reference to political responsibilities; i would also like to say that the commission is not too soft on the transparency issue, because in my view all tax agreements should be public and verifiable by the public.
in writing. ‒ the recent terrorist attacks in paris have highlighted the problem of the religious radicalisation of european citizens and of so-called foreign fighters, european citizens who have gone to syria to join the ranks of terrorist organisations. the situation must be tackled on several fronts; the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the protection of the environment from harmful substances. despite what the rapporteur has said, the text focuses on repression, including on the internet; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. in addition, excessive measures risk violating the rights of all european citizens; "whoever is willing to give up his fundamental freedoms for the sake of a little temporary security, deserves neither freedom nor security". for these reasons i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i do not share the views expressed in this report on the prevention of radicalisation and the recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations by my colleague, mr dati. the paris massacres show unequivocally that terrorism in europe is a threat that must be fought and condemned in every place and by every means. the text in question, on the other hand, merely condemns terrorists and extremists in a mild manner, rejecting the idea of closing borders and reintroducing controls. this text is far from the reality and the needs of our citizens and for these reasons i did not intend to support it with my vote.
in writing. ‒ the report voted on today comes at a time when it is essential to rethink the role that the european union can play in preventing the radicalisation of certain sections of the population, especially the younger ones, who are more vulnerable to this phenomenon. the tragic events in paris in recent days and the flow of european 'foreign fighters' who have been travelling to syria and iraq for years show us how crucial it is to focus on prevention and how important it is to do so in the context of action as coordinated and shared as possible at european level, aimed at removing the causes of radicalisation and not just its effects. the report stresses the importance of daily and widespread work, taking action where the risk of violent extremism is highest, such as in deprived neighbourhoods, through action to promote social inclusion and reduce the sense of marginalisation, or in prisons, which too often become centres of radicalisation. in addition, it is of course necessary to promote control over the emergence of radicalisation phenomena by facilitating the exchange of information between the authorities and by strengthening surveillance of the internet, which is too often used by terrorist networks as a recruitment platform and for the dissemination of fundamentalist ideas.
in writing. ‒ it would have been wiser and more useful, in view of recent events, to postpone the vote on this text, if only to update it and, why not, to tighten it up. this report does not condemn the terrorists with the necessary firmness, nor those who support morally and financially the extremism that underpins them. criticises the possible closure of internal borders (but is it true or not that the most wanted man in europe is now moving freely between member states?); the commission has already made a number of proposals, some of them quite extravagant, which would introduce - at our expense - social inclusion programmes for so-called foreign fighters returning to their own country after training in syria or the middle east. today, the middle way that pleases this union and this parliament is no longer sustainable or desirable: the time has come to take serious and concrete decisions, for example by abolishing schengen altogether, which is not a secondary cause of the 'free movement' of terrorists. what are we waiting for?
in writing. ‒ mr president, i abstained on the vote on the own-initiative report by mrs rachida dati because, although i believe it is necessary to stop the radicalisation of those who go to fight in syria alongside terrorist organisations, it was not possible to vote in favour of the text proposed by the rapporteur, which was too vague. in fact, although it is very complicated to prevent a european passport holder from re-entering europe, at the same time it is more important than ever to find a way of blocking foreign fighters. i am convinced that, alongside the important measures provided for in the text, aimed at strengthening the exchange of information and deterrence measures to prevent the departure of european citizens, it is now essential to monitor foreign fighters when they return to their eu country of origin.
in writing. ‒ terrorist activity is an extremely serious phenomenon, whose global nature and increasing threat level place it high on the political agenda of the union and the member states. this phenomenon must be tackled with toughness and speed to be defeated. we must go where terrorism is nurtured, preventing the recruitment and training of new recruits. terrorism is like a torrent: it's not enough to contain it or contain it, you have to lock it at the source. facilitate the exchange of good practices on de-radicalisation, dismantle terrorist recruitment networks on the ground, prevent radicalisation through education and social inclusion (with a particular focus on online activities and the role of prison recruitment), strengthen the links between internal and external security in the eu, prevent the departure and anticipate the return of radicalised european citizens recruited by terrorist organisations, strengthen deterrence against terrorist radicalisation and exchange of information between the various police and intelligence forces. only by activating this global approach will we defeat terrorism. repression alone without education and social inclusion is far from sufficient.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are discussing yet another summit on migration, and therefore yet another disappointment. another disappointment from the european governments. the political declarations of the malta summit were to address the root causes - and i stress the root causes - of migration: the commitment to respect fundamental rights, reduce poverty, promote peace, development, inclusive economic growth. well, in fact, none of that! no measures to really address the root causes of migration; no mention of unhypocritical cooperation between member states; no reference to solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility between member states; no mention of the amendment of european asylum legislation, which we all agree is now bankrupt. no mention of legal pathways to the european union, which would protect those in need of reception and thus international protection and would protect european citizens who are receiving them; the commission has not yet taken a decision on the budget for the european union. the fear is that once again economic and financial aid will prove to be just a tool for externalizing borders, wasting an opportunity which could actually be used to ensure better management of migration flows.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the outcome of the malta summit was disappointing. it is good to sit down with the african countries and try to deal with the situation together, but the usual security approach prevails on the european side. nothing on the legal access villas for asylum seekers and migrants, the only real way to fight traffickers; nothing about resettlement or relocation. all efforts seem to be directed at preventing new arrivals. the trust fund itself seemed to be plagued by unacceptable conditionality: offered in exchange for repatriation or border reinforcement. it can be a useful tool, but only if you make sure that the money actually gets to the people who need it to eradicate poverty and inequality and not for border management, to outsource our borders. i would not like that to be the idea of some governments who have just put the necessary 3 million to sit on the board. what is 1.8 billion when remittances from africa are estimated at 23 billion? when every year hundreds of billions of dollars of tax evasion and avoidance by our companies come out of the developing world? before we ask and demand from our partners, we must work to be credible about the consistency of our internal and external policies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the paris massacre turned the agenda of last week's g20 summit around, forcing leaders to commit to finding solutions to the terrorist threat. however, the european positions and those within nato itself on how and with whom to intervene are still far apart. i believe that after the tragedy in paris there is no longer room for divisions and tactics and that, as president mattarella said this morning, the threat of terrorism requires a united europe more than ever, capable of acting decisively in syria, lebanon and libya and of coordinating national intelligence systems. the situation is delicate and complex and must therefore be tackled with a shared strategic vision, capable of looking at the long term and taking into account the entire regional chessboard. only if we succeed in giving new life to our european identity will we be able to defeat the threat of isis and manage the migration phenomenon, also addressing its origin. and here, as the valletta summit has shown, we need stronger cooperation between europe and africa to combat illegal immigration and therefore the criminal networks that exploit it.
