in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure in question. the signed agreement provides for visa-free travel for citizens of the union and citizens of the republic of trinidad and tobago when travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa exemption applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) regardless of the purpose of their stay, except for stays for the purpose of gainful employment. the visa waiver agreement not only allows citizens to fully benefit from the acp-eu partnership, but also to participate in it by travelling more economically and practically.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendation because i believe that the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver is the culmination of the deepening of relations between the european union and the republic of trinidad and tobago, and a further instrument to strengthen economic and cultural relations and intensify political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. finally, i would like to emphasize the impetus given by the visa-free regime to bringing the peoples of europe and the caribbean closer together, since the agreement allows citizens not only to benefit fully from the acp-eu partnership but also to participate in it by travelling more economically and more conveniently.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of the short-stay visa waiver agreement between the european union and the republic of trinidad and tobago as it will be able to boost tourism and help strengthen trade relations. the visa waiver will simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs and facilitate investment. the economy of the republic of trinidad and tobago is one of the most dynamic and prosperous in the caricom region, owing to the presence of resources such as oil and gas, high levels of direct investment and growing tourism. the country is therefore a preferred destination for foreign direct investment. in addition, the republic of trinidad and tobago is committed to promoting a diversified and competitive economy, which is technology, innovation and knowledge-based. with its outward-looking approach and its open and liberal trade policy, the republic of trinidad and tobago is a full partner of the union. in this sense, the agreement will strengthen relations between the two parties and give new impetus to trade.
in writing. ‒ crossing borders has never been a marginal issue. council regulation (ec) no 539/2001 listed the third countries whose nationals were required to be in possession of a visa to enter the host state. with the negotiations launched in november 2014, the regulation is being drastically amended. under the visa-free agreements, citizens of the state of trinidad and tobago no longer need to hold a visa, but can cross the border with a valid ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passport. according to the agreement, the stay must be short and not for work purposes. a national of one of the signatory states may travel to the territory of the other state for a maximum of 90 days in any 180-day period. since i believe that this resolution can bring benefits to the current agreements on the short-stay visa waiver, i am voting in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the draft implementing decision concerning the memorandum of understanding between the office for harmonisation in the internal market (ohim) and eurojust. the purpose of the memorandum of understanding is to promote cooperation between ohim and eurojust in accordance with their respective mandates. under the provisions of the memorandum, the exchange of information or experience does not include the transmission of operational information, including data relating to an identified or identifiable person. the ep shares this approach and calls on the council to monitor the application of this guarantee. the memorandum also provides that disputes concerning interpretation or application are to be settled by consultation and negotiation between representatives of eurojust and ohim, thus excluding third party arbitration. finally, in the event of serious non-compliance, either party may temporarily suspend the application of the memorandum of understanding pending consultations. the ep also called on the council to adopt the memorandum as such.

in writing. ‒ the liberalisation of trade between the eu and the western balkan countries is ensured by a series of stabilisation and association agreements and an interim agreement in the case of bosnia and herzegovina. these agreements provide favourable conditions for the balkan states, allowing unlimited duty-free access to the eu market for most products. unlike free trade agreements, which provide for preferences to be granted by all parties, the autonomous trade measures constitute a unilateral preferential regime in favour of the western balkans. the preferences granted unilaterally by the eu to bosnia and herzegovina are an exceptional condition, designed to support this country and help it on its path of progressive european integration. however, the continuation of this facilitated treatment should be conditional on bosnia and herzegovina's prior acceptance of the eu-led approach of transparency and internal reforms for the enlargement of the free trade area.

in writing. ‒ in recent years, member states have been working together to establish a european energy union, with the aim of creating an environmentally friendly electricity grid. the debate on this subject, however, sees the clash between different interests and approaches of a predominantly political nature. the different needs and views expressed made the discussion of the dossier rather complex, leading in some cases to procedural strains and the approximate treatment of certain subjects. at the other extreme are those who consider the environmental and public health externalities of the use of highly polluting and harmful materials by industry to be negligible. on the other hand, those who consider environmental policy, energy policy and industrial policy to be inseparable, arguing for example for the need to make more intensive use of the circular economy. i voted against because i believe in the need to reduce the costs of industry and its use of polluting materials in the name of protecting the environment.
in writing. ‒ the fight against climate change, the subject of the recent united nations conference in paris, is one of the key issues for the near future. the european union's action must be directed towards strengthening international choices, towards an energy transaction based on the progressive abandonment of fossil fuels. my vote in favour of the gróbarczyk report is motivated by the conviction that energy policy choices are crucial to supporting the eu's long-term competitiveness and reducing its energy dependence on exporting countries. the aim must be a new energy model for europe based on demand reduction, energy efficiency and renewable energy. we must work towards a genuine eu external energy policy, focusing on the transparency of future agreements with third countries and security of supply. the stability of the new energy system will necessarily depend on the involvement of businesses and citizens, including through the creation of new investment opportunities in energy.
in writing. ‒ this report is decidedly biased and calls on the member states to give up their energy sovereignty in favour of a european centralism which has not only always proved inefficient but has always been very disadvantageous for our territories and our citizens. for all these reasons i voted against.
in writing. ‒ in the light of recent international developments and the objectives agreed in paris at cop21, the transition to an energy union based on security of energy supply, on an increasingly integrated and sustainable energy market, remains one of the european union's highest priorities. i very much welcome the report voted on today, which represents an important step towards building an increasingly secure and resilient european energy system, based on ambitious targets aimed at the fundamental shift towards a new energy model, based on the progressive decarbonisation of the economy. consistent with the socioeconomic and environmental challenges we face, increasing energy integration at home, coupled with increasing efficiency in the use of resources, is the key to reducing the union's over-reliance on supplies from third countries, while also bringing us into line with the principle of diversification of energy sources, which is also of paramount importance to ensure our security and competitiveness in this area. on the other hand, much remains to be done and we must act consistently. i therefore share the concern expressed by this parliament about the doubling of nordstream, which is operating in the opposite direction to those principles.
in writing. ‒ the development of renewable energy sources is crucial to making the eu's energy independence a reality. the union and its member states currently import more than half of all the energy they consume: excessive dependence on imports is found in crude oil (over 90%), natural gas (66%) and coal (72%). the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the volume of imports from the prc into the union during the review investigation period. this consumption represents 60% of eu gas imports. the reduction of the union's energy demand and the development of renewable energy are essential elements for achieving energy independence and for meeting the targets set by cop21 in paris.
in writing. - i vote against it. the energy union is designed to take away the last remaining strategic sovereignty of the member states: the freedom to determine the energy mix, as enshrined in article 194 tfeu. measures such as a collective purchasing mechanism, the unification of key contractual clauses, or the ex-ante and ex-post intervention of the commission (in practice: a veto power) on intergovernmental agreements with third countries are a clear violation of article 194 itself.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on progress towards a european energy union 2015/2113 (ini), as i see the european energy union as the next institutional and political challenge. the european union is indeed strengthened by the conclusion of the historic agreement at the conference on climate change (cop 21), but we all know the cost of non-europe and the current existence of economic, regulatory and administrative barriers to energy consumption, which do not protect but rather exacerbate energy poverty. i therefore agree with the report and stress the importance of achieving the right balance between the objectives set out and a resilient and secure ecosystem, emphasising the key role of the following themes: the trading of emission allowances (ets); the necessary introduction of real driving emissions testing; the decarbonisation of the transport, maritime and land-based aircraft sectors, which are still excluded from binding commitments; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the recycling of waste.

in writing. ‒ the gróbarczyk report is part of the juncker commission's energy union macro-initiative. the report presents diametrically opposed views, which see on the one hand the forces that deny climate change, fossil fuel generation, including highly polluting (coal) and unconventional (shale gas, oil from oil sands), support the large extractive and generation industry. at the other extreme are those who consider energy policy to be inseparable from the fight against climate change, who aim to reduce the impact of energy costs through the circular economy, who see renewable energy as the main objective for the energy transition, who are against nuclear fission and who favour energy efficiency as the first source, demand reduction, decentralised production and self-consumption. the rapporteur did not hesitate to use procedural instruments (for example, a series of concatenated splits which completely reversed the meaning of one of our amendments on nuclear energy) which were very close to being incorrect, and which were deeply bitterly experienced by various political groups. i have decided to vote against the report, as it is a bit controversial.
in writing. ‒ the energy union will have numerous benefits both economically and sustainably across the eu. as regards energy security, it will make the eu less dependent on external sources and may make energy agreements more transparent; it will also help create new jobs, make european industries, transport systems and the construction sector more sustainable and decarbonised. finally, it will reduce household energy costs. in the resolution, which i voted for, parliament supports the commission in taking measures to achieve the energy union through adequate investment in strategic infrastructure and the promotion of innovation and modernisation; strengthening regional cooperation and in particular mediterranean cooperation; promoting and disseminating best practice at local level and enhancing policy coordination across the eu.
in writing. ‒ on 18 april 1951, the treaty of paris was signed, establishing one of the founding pillars of the european community and the future union, the ecsc, and establishing for the first time in history a shared management of coal and steel resources. today, more than 60 years later, in a changed context, the need to complete an energy union also remains. i am convinced that the report we have adopted is an important step towards a european energy union, because it sets out ambitious measures to achieve greater energy savings and efficiency, the development of renewable energies and, above all, the need for strategic coordination at european level to diversify energy sources and their supply routes. on this last point in particular, i agree with the position expressed in the text and express concern about the proposal to double the capacity of the nordstream pipeline: a unilateral decision that could have detrimental effects on the energy security of the union. the achievement of a single, harmonious and more secure european energy area must pass through shared and coordinated energy choices and policies at european level. only in this way will it be possible to guarantee a future of greater stability and energy independence for the citizens of europe.
in writing. this report follows the saudargas report, which was dealt with in the first half of 2015 and which was unsuccessful. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's energy policy and its implementation in the member states. the amendments to the text of the report, as presented, contain a set of strongly contrasting positions, ranging from financial support for nuclear and non-conventional energy shale gas to the absence of a position on decarbonisation, to the circular economy which has decarbonisation and renewable energy as objectives for a real energy transition. unfortunately, it has not been possible to influence the text in such a way as to limit or cancel the financing of nuclear and non-conventional energy. nor has it succeeded in getting the european parliament to take a unanimous position in favour of a gradual decarbonisation of our economy. i voted against it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the european energy union, as i believe it is essential to develop and ensure the functioning of the energy market at european level. member states should work towards the creation of an integrated internal energy market, both in terms of regulation and interconnections; increase security of supply both through diversification of supply, for example by exploiting recent discoveries in the mediterranean basin, and through the development of inland sources; ensure energy efficiency and promote the development of renewables by integrating them into the market in a balanced way. a true energy union is the basis for european growth and reindustrialisation.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the report, even though it contains many positive elements on renewable energy and energy efficiency that stem largely from our work in the itre committee: in particular, for the first time, the concept that investment in energy efficiency is as important as investment in energy infrastructure is being accepted. the report calls for the hidden and externalized costs of energy to be calculated during impact assessments (the hidden costs of nuclear and fossil fuels are very high; those of renewables are virtually non-existent) and reiterates the binding 2030 targets of the european parliament on emissions, energy efficiency and renewables, while the eu council is content with non-binding and low-profile targets. but the negative elements dominate this report. in particular, too much space is given to nuclear and fossil fuels. the eu's energy security is wrongly conflated with the building of infrastructure to import fossil fuels, whereas it would only be achieved if the eu could produce most of the energy it needs: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the energy sector is not left to the detriment of the environment.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament today approved the report 'towards an energy union', which i followed as shadow rapporteur for the s&d group. i am very pleased that the report has been adopted by a large majority in the plenary and i think that the text represents a complete success for my group. i find the consolidated budget to be truly balanced where it focuses decisively on renewable sources and energy efficiency, relaunches the commitment to a fully integrated market while paying particular attention to carbon leakage and ensuring competitive and uniform prices in all member states. i particularly share the condemnation of the doubling of the nord stream gas pipeline, a project which seriously jeopardises the security of europe's energy supplies and isolates ukraine from the european gas distribution network.
in writing. the report is strongly pro-nuclear, but with considerable effort, we in the five star movement have succeeded in getting the final text to include more ambitious european targets for renewable energy and energy efficiency. the european parliament also deleted from the document, thanks to an amendment by the five star movement, the part of the text which provided eu funding for nuclear energy. the report has no legislative value. it is, however, an important policy document which will have an impact on the eu's energy choices and which affirms the will of the european parliament. i therefore voted against the report as a whole, because other content which we consider unacceptable has not been deleted. the text argues that renewable, fossil and nuclear sources should be considered and promoted in the same way under the concept of 'technological neutrality'. again, the problem of energy security and independence is solved by promoting the construction of large-scale infrastructure, such as gas pipelines, so that the eu is able to import fossil fuels from as many suppliers as possible. i do not share these concepts and i have expressed them in my vote.
in writing. ‒ the creation of an intensive electrification system for the industrial sector is essential and indispensable for a complete energy transition. the eriksson report aims at a european electricity grid by 2020 that is in line with recent technological developments in generation, consumption and finally transmission. the report focuses on the enormous potential of renewable energy and its undeniable benefits, but notes that the results achieved to date are conditioned by a strong disconnect in the organisational network. the interconnection of the european electricity grid will undoubtedly lead to an increase in the exploitation of these resources, the solution of the problem of structural discontinuity and the achievement of greater benefits. for these reasons, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ achieving the 10% electricity interconnection target is an important milestone for the broader european energy markets union project. the achievement of the energy union requires efficient and solidarity-based instruments, and better interconnection responds to the need to ensure the achievement of those common objectives from which we all benefit, a stronger and more resilient network. it is not just about cheap electricity and lower prices for businesses, but about strengthening a network that unlocks synergies capable of consolidating the internal system and removing imbalances. the interest in eliminating the various energy islands (poland, great britain, the iberian peninsula) is moving in this direction. a balanced approach, a transparent process and a commitment to maintaining high levels of ambition are essential in a project that aims to ensure stability, competitiveness and growth. i support this report, which combines the economic and geopolitical dimensions and sets out a strategy for strengthening the union.
in writing. ‒ most eu member states have outdated and poorly integrated internal electricity networks. the union is currently largely still to reach the modest 10% cross-border interconnection target of the europe 2020 document. a european electricity grid would mean a price reduction of at least eur 2 per mwh, security of supply close to 100%, a greater ability to withstand cyber or military attacks on the electricity grid (today the resilience to such attacks is too low) and other tangible benefits, such as reducing electricity price volatility for the benefit of citizens and the competitiveness of european industry and businesses in the global economy, together with an estimated savings for european consumers of between eur 12 and eur 40 billion per year by 2030. we therefore urge the european commission to encourage investment in the best available techniques which offer considerable financial benefits over the entire life cycle of the networks, save time and provide technological leadership in the long term, and to undertake a general review of the technical and management system of the european electricity network.
in writing. ‒ in october 2014, the council unanimously set a target of 10% cross-border electricity grid interconnectivity by 2020 (and 15% by 2030), in order to complete the internal energy market and improve energy security in the eu. this objective (political, not based on scientific grounds) is in itself acceptable. it should be said that the lack of interconnectivity really only concerns certain member states (basically the usual ones: the energy islands) to which priority will be given. despite the vote in favour, it is worth pointing out two concerns first: 1) the interconnectivity objective is seen as a pro-rhythm to the achievement of the energy union, which we oppose at its root (see the gróbarczyk report); 2) in general, eu energy policy is 'polluted' by climate policy: the model of 'energy austerity' pursued is an obstacle to reindustrialisation and hence to prospects for economic growth, but with zero environmental impact (in absolute terms, global co2 emissions will not decrease, whether or not co2 is a problem). i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the report on 'achieving 10% electricity interconnection - a european electricity grid ready for 2020', as i consider it strategic to achieve the 10% electricity interconnection target and to improve the functioning of the internal electricity market in the eu; the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the energy union's objectives and to monitor the implementation of the energy union's objectives. an integrated approach to the issue is essential in order to strengthen national networks in order to fully exploit the capacity of interconnections and to make the best use of existing interconnection lines and the capacity of existing national infrastructures. the frequent congestion of transmission networks can be associated with cross-border lines but also due to the weakness and obsolescence of internal networks and the limited availability of national networks.
in writing. ‒ the proper functioning of the internal energy market also depends on the interconnections that guarantee electricity security within the union, especially in crossborder areas most exposed to energy crises. having an interconnected network in europe is essential, as it allows for secure, sustainable and lower-cost energy. in 2002, the union set itself the target of achieving 10% energy interconnection by 2020: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. these are mostly countries that are more isolated from the single energy market. there have been several delays both due to the long authorisation procedures, especially for high voltage lines, and due to lack of funds. the latter difficulty could, however, be overcome by recourse to the connecting europe facility, a financial instrument which should, as requested by parliament, pay particular attention to projects aimed at addressing the most serious shortcomings in the current integrated electricity market. the report also calls on the commission to consider using the eib and other financial instruments to achieve the community objective. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the measure in question. parliament recognised the 10% interconnection target as an important step in the right direction and stressed that interconnectivity is one of the key preconditions for the completion of the internal market in electricity. parliament considered that particular attention should be given to projects addressing the most significant gaps in the integrated electricity market in the union. parliament also considered that the purely quantitative 10% target should not be isolated, because accessibility to interconnections and networks is also necessary to ensure that interconnection arrangements work in practice.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal to prepare a common european electricity grid by 2020. i am very close to the environmental and energy issues, and i am in favour of an optimized european energy system with renewable energies, greater energy efficiency and a sustainable energy mix leading to energy savings, and an internal energy market which allows energy to circulate freely. these conditions are important for the achievement of a stable and secure energy system. in particular, i believe that electricity interconnection is one of the key prerequisites for completing an integrated internal eu electricity market which, if well defined, will contribute to achieving the climate objectives that i particularly care about; in particular, it is a strategic principle that should lead to a more resilient and robust network, better able to respond to all forms of disruption and change. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it is important for the proper functioning of the internal energy market to improve electricity interconnection, by eliminating bottlenecks in the grid, building new transmission lines and developing new local smart grids. a fully integrated internal electricity market would increase security and independence from other countries, reducing electricity price volatility to the benefit of citizens and the competitiveness of european industry and businesses in the global economy.
in writing. ‒ the eriksson report gives an opinion on the achievement of the 10% minimum target for electricity interconnections proposed by the committee and seeks to form a position on this by placing it within the main axes of the european union's energy and infrastructure policy. the project of intensive electrification of our industrial system is essential for the energy transition, therefore for the fight against climate change and towards energy independence. it is essential to actively drive the evolution of the european electricity grid, making it intelligent, highly interconnected and open to technological developments occurring both on the generation side and on the consumption and transmission side itself. a network without a high degree of interconnection cannot fully exploit the potential offered by renewables. the essential problem with such a general policy objective, 'one size fits all', is that while it points in the right direction, it does not take into account the territorial, geographical, energy diversity of the member states. however, i think the report is good and therefore i shall vote in favour.
in writing. this report, which focuses on the commission communication 'achieving 10% electricity interconnection - a grid ready for 2020' is one of the main axes of the european union's energy and infrastructure policy. creating the optimal conditions to be able to fully electrify our industrial system is a key element towards the energy transition, decarbonisation and the fight against climate change. interconnection therefore appears to be crucial to allowing technological evolution and infrastructure choices that must create the conditions for the full exploitation of energy from renewable sources. however, interconnection projects must take account of spatial and geographical variables characterising the member states and should, in the selection of projects, have an approach which respects the sensitivities of the inhabitants of the places involved, as well as taking into account the results of environmental impact assessments. in essence, interconnections are possible, but not at any cost and above all by respecting the rules which are often trampled underfoot by the interests generated by the high costs of these projects. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ energy infrastructure is one of the priorities of the european energy agenda. an interconnected european energy network is essential to ensure europe's energy security, to strengthen competition in the internal market, thereby making prices more competitive, and to help achieve the objectives that the european union has committed itself to achieve in terms of decarbonisation and climate policy. this communication examines how to achieve the 10% target for electricity interconnections by 2020. the objectives on which the text focuses are: improvement of the situation in the 12 member states with a level of interconnection of less than 10% (ireland, italy, romania, portugal, estonia, latvia, lithuania, united kingdom, spain, poland, cyprus and malta); projects under the trans-european energy networks (ten-e) regulation and the connecting europe facility (cef) which will contribute to the achievement of the interconnection objective; financial instruments to support electricity interconnection projects; modalities for strengthening regional cooperation. for all the reasons mentioned above, i voted in favour of this resolution and i hope that the interconnection of electricity markets will be a political priority for the european union to pursue at all levels in the years to come.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on electricity interconnection and the achievement of a european electricity grid by 2020. since 2002, the union has been committed to the achievement of a stable, independent, inclusive and transparent internal market in electricity in order to ensure security of supply, the use of renewable sources and the competitiveness of the electricity industry for the benefit of european citizens. a fully integrated internal market will facilitate trade and services in electricity by reducing price volatility, create jobs in a sustainable economy through investment in the best technologies, and help reduce energy dependency and isolation. however, i believe that a unitary 10% interconnection target risks being misleading and not appropriate to the different market dynamics or geographical situations of all member states. the objectives must not be set in a single word but must be based on the specific circumstances of each country. i think that regional cooperation is of fundamental importance as a means of achieving interconnection throughout europe.

in writing. ‒ progress is the microfinance instrument launched by the european union. its nature as an instrument of social policy is (and must remain) of higher priority than economic policy. progress is focused on target groups which have not received sufficient attention from the economic system: long-term unemployed, welfare recipients, migrants, people working in the informal economy or living in disadvantaged rural areas, and women. the commission shall be empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with article 264 concerning the establishment of a european data protection supervisor. it is an effective instrument which is clearly superior to traditional social assistance systems because it enables beneficiaries to be activated, to be brought to a state of autonomy which reintegrates them into the socioeconomic context of their territory, thus lightening the assistance burdens of their country of origin, putting them back in play and improving their self-esteem and confidence in their own abilities. we must support this instrument and take it as a positive example to be promoted in the member states.

in writing. ‒ the progress microfinance facility is designed to help those who have difficulty accessing the credit market to obtain a loan of up to eur 25 000. progress, which receives union funds, does not directly finance entrepreneurs but allows certain eu microcredit providers (public or private banking institutions, non-bank-type bodies and non-profit microcredit providers) to increase credit activity by issuing guarantees, thus sharing the risk of loss. through this facility, those wishing to start a small-medium-sized business are guided and instructed by financial intermediaries, who, in addition to granting credit, provide specific technical assistance for each beneficiary. in this regard, provision has been made for the creation of a website and a database to disseminate information on how to access microcredit and on selected financial intermediaries, in order to enable a wider public to benefit from this instrument. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the proposal, given its many advantages.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report. the european commission will present in january a proposal for a regulation on the revision of technical measures, which will be based on the need to adapt the existing regulatory framework to the objectives of the new common fisheries policy (cfp). the report in question precedes the commission proposal and contains precise indications and suggestions for future technical measures and multiannual plans for fisheries (conservation measures). the objective of the technical measures is to avoid catching juveniles and other incidental catches. these measures are now spread over more than 30 regulations and constitute a complex set of provisions which are often inconsistent and sometimes contradictory. the present report proposes a simplification and rationalisation of these measures, which should be set out in a clear legal framework and designed on the basis of sound scientific foundations. the commission's text on technical measures should therefore contain a series of general proposals applicable to the whole community fleet, to which specific measures for certain fishing areas, including the mediterranean sea, should be added.

acting president of the council. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, allow me first of all to apologize to the luxembourg minister for the environment, mrs dieschbourg, who would have liked to be with you, but is already in brussels for the preparations of tomorrow's environment council. ladies and gentlemen, even three days after the end of the cop 21 which i had the good fortune to attend, with our minister of the environment, i am still struggling to fully realize the miracle of paris. i think you will agree with me that this agreement is indeed a historic achievement. this is the first time we've adopted a universal climate agreement that contains the architecture needed to keep global warming well below 2 degrees celsius and in which every country in the world is committed to doing their part. such an agreement is the result of an unprecedented political commitment to tackle the challenge of climate change. i would like to commend the french presidency of the conference of the parties for its exceptional commitment. throughout the year, it has pushed the climate agenda through all the chambers, and with great patience, impeccable impartiality and great control of the situation during the cop, it has succeeded in presenting an agreement which not only has consensus but is also ambitious, sustainable, dynamic and legally binding. of course, the french presidency was able to complete its work thanks to the willingness of the parties to move forward. the european union and its member states have always led the way by adopting and defending an ambitious position. i take this opportunity to thank the european parliament for its own commitment and support in this matter, calling for an ambitious agreement to phase out global co2 emissions by 2050 or shortly thereafter. the other major emitters, such as china, india and the united states, have also shown a great willingness to make the agreement work, as have, of course, countless non-governmental actors, such as cities and municipalities in some parts of the economic world and, of course, ngos. i should also like to highlight the performance of the european union in paris. we have spoken with one voice from start to finish, and this has made us an indispensable partner in the negotiations. several key features of the agreement, such as the ambition mechanism, were developed from concepts put forward by the european union. our influence has been real because we have been able to forge new alliances, such as the one that gave rise to the high ambition coalition, because we have been able to present compromise solutions linking sometimes very divergent positions. although the agreement is still very recent and more detailed analyses of it still need to be developed, i would like to briefly describe the main points. first, it was decided in paris that global warming must be kept well below 2 degrees and that we must strive to limit it to 1.5 degrees. the paris agreement specifies that this implies that peak emissions must occur as soon as possible and that climate neutrality must be achieved in the second half of this century. secondly, the paris agreement specifies that national emission reduction contributions indcs will be at the heart of the paris agreement. all parties will have to highlight their contributions, the vast majority have already done so, and they will have to maintain them by revising them upwards every five years. thirdly, the paris agreement contains very important elements of solidarity for developing countries, and especially for the poorest and most vulnerable among them, on adaptation, loss and damage, capacity building and, of course, also financing. on finance, we have committed ourselves as developed countries to a concrete roadmap to reach $100 billion by 2020. in addition, a new, more ambitious target will have to be set by 2025 at the latest. finally, we agreed in paris on a transparency framework that will create the necessary confidence that all countries will meet their commitments. the paris agreement, as you can see, is therefore a big step forward. it is the first global climate agreement and sends a very strong signal to all non-governmental actors, whether local authorities, businesses or civil society, whose growing commitment i welcome - a signal that this transition to a low-carbon economy is becoming a must. but let us not forget that the paris agreement is only a framework which has yet to be defined and clarified in several respects. so there's a lot of work to be done. this is the task we will have to tackle in the months and years ahead, before the agreement enters into force in 2020.
member of the commission.– madam president, this is a historic moment. thanks, to a great extent, to the efforts of the european union, the world has its first ever universal, legally binding global climate deal. this is a new chapter in global climate governance as we move from action by few to action by all. the paris agreement is important on many levels: first of all, in order to be efficient in our fight against climate change. but more generally, the deal reached over the weekend is a major win for the whole international community. it shows that multilateralism can still work when faced with a truly global challenge. this is a vital lesson for the years ahead of us. europe has gone through turbulent times over the last few years. today, let me assure you of one thing: we should all be proud of europe. paris is the culmination of europe’s efforts for a global agreement on climate change. after many years of relentless efforts, we got a deal. and not just any deal: the paris agreement is ambitious and balanced, and it includes our key objectives. i would like to thank the members of the european parliament delegation to cop21 – led by delegation chair giovanni la via and vice-chair matthias groote – for their invaluable support throughout the conference. i must also pay tribute to the french presidency of cop21, and the remarkable way in which they managed a very delicate and challenging process. the cooperation between member states, ministers, the european parliament delegation and my fellow commissioners was excellent throughout the negotiations. the european union spoke always with a single voice under the excellent steering of the luxembourg presidency. when we do so, we succeed. we were instrumental as ambitious bridge builders, and we were instrumental in building a broad coalition of developed and developing countries in favour of high ambition – the high ambition coalition – which was critical in securing the global deal. all of a sudden, the debate was not about developed versus developing, as it was in copenhagen. it was about the willing versus the unwilling. the result in paris will decisively accelerate the transition from fossil to clean fuels. this trend is now irreversible. when i came to this house last october on the occasion of the debate on the pargneaux report, i made it clear that paris had to deliver an ambitious, robust and legally binding global agreement which puts the world on track to limit global warming to below 2°c. i set out then my three ‘essentials’ for a successful outcome: first, a long-term goal; second, a robust review cycle with the flexibility to strengthen ambition over time; and third, strong transparency and accountability rules. after two weeks of intense and sometimes exhausting negotiations, the paris agreement delivers on all these key essentials. for the first time ever in a legal agreement, we reaffirmed our long-term goal to prevent the adverse effects of climate change. governments agreed to the goal of keeping the increase in global average temperature to ‘well below’ 2°c above pre-industrial levels. the commission also welcomes the recognition in the agreement of the need to pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°c, a point which was crucial for many of our partners in our progressive alliance. the qualitative long-term goal aims for emissions to peak as soon as possible, with rapid reductions thereafter, towards achieving a balance between anthropogenic emissions by sources and removal by sinks of greenhouse gases in the second half of the century. the direction of travel has been set. the agreement sends a clear signal to investors, businesses and policy makers that the global transition to clean energy is here to stay. as i said during the conference, you can have the best long-term target in the world, but without a robust revision mechanism raising the level of ambition over time, you will never achieve it. that is why the european union has always insisted on a five-year review cycle. in paris, we agreed to come back every five years, to take stock, to look at the latest science, and to ramp up our commitments accordingly. we also fought hard for strong transparency and accountability rules. we know these are the foundations of a credible international regime. without multilaterally agreed rules, there will be no trust or confidence that countries will deliver on their commitments. under the paris agreement, countries have a legally binding obligation to pursue domestic mitigation measures with a view to achieving their contributions. an enhanced transparency and accountability system is also set up, including the submission by all countries, every two years, of greenhouse gas inventories, an expert review and a facilitative, multilateral consideration of progress. these elements fully correspond with the european union’s priorities and ensure a fit-for-purpose transparency and accountability framework for emission reduction commitments. the european parliament has consistently recognised climate finance as a key issue in these negotiations. i am proud that the paris agreement includes a solidarity package which contains provisions on climate finance and on addressing needs linked to adaptation and to loss and damage. developed countries will continue with their collective mobilisation goal of usd 100 billion per year until 2025, when a new collective goal will be set. under all circumstances, the european union is committed to enhancing its level of support.other countries are encouraged to provide financial support. so, in addition to all countries taking on commitments to reduce emissions, there is also no longer a strict division between developed and developing countries with regard to the provision of public finance. we must recognise this historic moment. but the hard work has just begun. today we may celebrate. tomorrow we must act. in early 2016, the commission will work on implementing the paris agreement in the european union, and i look forward to working with the european parliament on this. the commission will also continue its work to implement the 2030 climate and energy framework. following this summer’s legislative proposal for the revision of the european union emissions trading system for the post-2020 period, the next step is to address the sectors not covered by the ets. the commission will also make legislative proposals on effort-sharing, land use, land use change and forestry (lulucf). we will also bring forward a communication on decarbonising the transport sector. also, our upcoming energy proposals – for renewables, market design and energy efficiency – will play an important role in making the energy market cleaner and more efficient. our wider climate diplomacy efforts will not stop. we will embark on further discussions and negotiations with our international partners on the detailed aspects of the paris agreement. it is crucial to build on the momentum of this historic agreement through our continued cooperation with stakeholders and with other countries on the implementation of indcs, including capacity building for monitoring and reporting. when we meet again in morocco, in a year’s time, we should all be able to report tangible progress. this is what the world expects from us. dear members, paris is also a success for this parliament. you have been a key player over the years in steering debate across europe and putting in place the right legislation. i count on your continued support in the future.

in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and voting in the house, i voted in favour of the report on the renewal of the mandate of the president of the european banking authority. i believe that the correction of macroeconomic imbalances will be achieved by strengthening governance and coordinating economic policies, in order to take advantage of the effectiveness and flexibility of the stability and growth pact. the european banking authority (eba) is responsible for ensuring an effective and uniform level of regulation and supervision in the european banking sector. it is therefore necessary to prevent macroeconomic imbalances primarily by strengthening and stabilising economic governance, while ensuring continuity of action by the authorities involved. the renewal of the mandate of the current president of eba goes in this direction, helping to ensure the integrity, efficiency and smooth functioning of the banking sector. the consequences of economic fragility that imbalances in a non-harmonised banking sector can produce should not be underestimated and maximum cohesion of the three supervisory authorities should therefore be ensured in order to support the creation of the single set of banking sector rules to ensure a level playing field and a high level of protection for depositors, investors and consumers.

in writing. ‒ a european-wide micro-prudential supervisory system was established at the end of 2010, comprising the european banking authority (eba, based in london), the european securities and markets authority (esma, based in paris) and the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa, based in frankfurt). in 2011, the presidents of the three authorities were appointed for a five-year term, renewable once. the respective boards of supervisors have proposed the renewal of the mandate of both andrea enria (eba), gabriel bernardino (eiopa) and also steven maijoor (esma). the econ committee of the european parliament only held a hearing of the candidates, and then voted last week to renew the mandate of all three by a large majority. we voted against, firstly, a method of renewal which is almost automatic and devoid of any real motivation; the role and value of these authorities has so far proved to be rather marginal, and therefore continuing in the wake of five unsatisfactory years certainly does not seem to be the best decision that could be taken. so my vote is negative today.

in writing. ‒ the european securities and markets authority (esma) is responsible for overseeing financial markets and credit rating agencies in order to ensure the stability of the eu financial system by working in collaboration with the european banking authority (eba) and the european insurance and pensions authority (eiopa) to build a uniform regulatory framework for financial markets in the european union. the management board of esma has re-confirmed the current chairperson, mr steven maijoor, for a new five-year term. in his role as head of esma, steven maijoor will continue to lead and plan the work of the organisation's steering committee, which is composed of representatives of the national supervisors of the eu countries. i wish president steven maijoor well in his work to further and improve investor protection measures and the stability of the financial markets in the european union.
in writing. ‒ a european-wide micro-prudential supervisory system was established at the end of 2010, comprising the european banking authority (eba, based in london), the european securities and markets authority (esma, based in paris) and the european insurance and occupational pensions authority (eiopa, based in frankfurt). in 2011, the presidents of the three authorities were appointed for a five-year term, renewable once. the board of the european securities and markets authority has proposed to renew the mandate of mr steven maijoor. the econ committee of the european parliament only held a hearing of the candidate, and then voted last week to renew the mandate by a very large majority. i voted against, firstly, a method of renewal which is almost automatic and devoid of any real motivation; the role and value of these authorities has so far proved to be rather marginal, and therefore continuing in the wake of five unsatisfactory years certainly does not seem to be the best decision that could be taken.
in writing. ‒ under article 23 of the europol decision, the council is considered to have the competence to conclude international agreements with third countries or international organisations. agreements are generally based on a mutual commitment to exchange operational, strategic or classified information. the proposal put forward by the rapporteur, mr fontana, calls for the establishment of a new form of cooperation with the state of bosnia-herzegovina. i have decided to abstain, given that the negotiations for a reform of the gai decision establishing europol were concluded on 29 november. as a result of these changes, new and stricter rules will soon be applied. i therefore thought it appropriate to postpone the creation of new cooperatives until a later date, so that the new rules can also be applied to new agreements.
in writing. ‒ given bosnia and herzegovina's geographical location and strategic role in the balkans, i believe that greater cooperation between this country and europol will ensure more effective policies and counter-action against organised crime. for all these reasons i have voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the cooperation agreement between bosnia and herzegovina and europol is a welcome development, useful in the context of improved strategic and operational cooperation between the eu member states and allied countries with a view to greater efficiency in the fight against terrorism, mafias, smuggling and international crime.
in writing. ‒ the report concerns the proposal for a strategic cooperation agreement between europol and bosnia and herzegovina which also provides for the exchange of sensitive personal data. it is therefore very important to ensure that the agreement is concluded within the framework of the new europol regulation which recalls the new european data protection legislation, which will be adopted shortly. we therefore thought it appropriate to wait before approving the cooperation agreement, which is also extremely important. i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal under consideration concerning the approval of the conclusion of the agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between bosnia and herzegovina and europol, which includes personal data. such information could be in the field of expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures and crime prevention methods, as well as supporting information in the context of individual criminal investigations. parliament also considered that the council should refrain from adopting the draft decision until the new europol regulation had entered into force.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the report by mr fontana on the draft agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between bosnia and herzegovina and europol, as also agreed with the council.

in writing. the draft under consideration concerns the proposal to approve the conclusion of an agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between bosnia and herzegovina and europol in relation to personal data. this historical situation requires us to work closely with the countries of the balkan peninsula, which have become the crossroads of the migratory flows to europe. in this context, i hope that this agreement will be a step towards ever closer cooperation and will allow for future integration with the whole area. i have decided to give my favourable opinion because i believe that this agreement will enable both parties to conduct more accurate investigations through the exchange of operational, strategic, technical and/or classified information.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on operational and strategic cooperation between bosnia and herzegovina and europol. pursuant to decisions 2009/371/jha and 2009/934/jha, europol is required to conclude agreements with third states which are included in a list established by decision 2009/934/jha, which includes bosnia and herzegovina. the aim of these agreements is to prevent and combat organised crime, terrorism and other forms of serious crime involving two or more states and which may involve the exchange of operational, strategic and technical information. in order to ensure effectiveness in preventing and combating serious crime, europol has initiated the procedure for the conclusion of an agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between bosnia and herzegovina and europol (the so-called operational and strategic agreement), which provides for the exchange of information, including the results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, crime prevention methods and the provision of advice in support of individual criminal investigations.

in writing. ‒ the current contingencies dictate the need to ensure full sharing, at intra- and extra-european level, and an adequate exchange of information, in order to effectively combat cross-border criminal networks. i have therefore decided to support the report by mr fontana, which supports the council's decision to authorize an agreement negotiated by europol, the european police office, and bosnia-herzegovina, a candidate country for membership of the community.

in writing. ‒ the draft under consideration concerns the proposal to approve the conclusion of an agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between bosnia and herzegovina and europol, which includes personal data. the european parliament and the council have entered into informal negotiations on a new europol regulation (2013/0091 ((cod)) which provides for significant changes to the procedure for the conclusion of international agreements. once the new europol regulation enters into force, parliament's favourable opinion will be required for any eu police cooperation agreement with third countries. the report considers that the council should refrain from adopting the draft decision on operational cooperation with bosnia and herzegovina until the new europol regulation enters into force. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the text voted today concerns the conclusion of an agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between europol and bosnia and herzegovina in the fight against crime and terrorism. the terms of the agreement provide for the exchange of information on criminal investigation procedures and classified documents, as well as the provision of advice and support. i have decided to vote in favour of this report in order to increase the effectiveness of the prevention and combating of the most serious forms of international crime in europe and in bosnia-herzegovina.
in writing. ‒ pwa international is yet another case where single market failures have led to a company crisis and the loss of 108 jobs. i am voting in favour of the mobilisation of the egf to the amount of eur 442 293 for the 108 redundancies in this company. the globalisation adjustment fund remains a key instrument for supporting citizens, the eu should first of all tackle market distortions as a whole rather than just trying to treat the victims of its ill-considered policies.
in writing. ‒ as has already happened in the past for alitalia employees, it is right that irish workers in the affected production facilities also benefit from the european globalisation adjustment fund so that they can be effectively assisted in re-entering the labour market by updating their training and at the same time giving them economic support. the egf should, therefore, be mobilised in order to provide financial assistance to workers in undertakings which have suffered serious physical or mental disorders as a result of these events.
in writing. - i vote for it. there are 108 redundancies in the sector of 'repair and installation of machinery and equipment', amounting to eur 442 293. pwai was founded in 1989 as a joint venture between united technologies corporation and lufthansa technik airmotive ireland. in the 1990s, ireland specialised in aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul, which was very useful to ireland at that time, but made it particularly vulnerable to the recent trend to locate maintenance, repair and overhaul activities close to the expanding centres of world aviation, namely asia, and to the negative effects of global trade agreements.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today in order to support the reintegration into the labour market of 108 workers made redundant as a result of globalisation by ie/pwa international, a company active in the repair and installation of machinery and equipment. the recent trend to locate maintenance, repair and overhaul of machinery and equipment close to the growing centres of world air transport, namely asia, has made this sector very vulnerable in ireland. the negative effects of global trade agreements have worsened this situation of vulnerability. i also note that the maintenance, repair and overhaul of machinery and equipment has been severely affected in europe, particularly in ireland, with the closure of sr technics in 2009 and lufthansa technik airmotive ireland in 2014, which led to the loss of approximately 1 520 jobs. the vote in favour of this report will make it possible to facilitate the rapid reintegration of these redundant workers into employment by means of personalised support measures. i regret that italian companies are not making adequate use of this fund because of the lack of support from local institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mobilising the egf for ireland. the measure in question refers, in the context of the 2015 budget, to the mobilisation of the fund for a total amount of eur 442 293. the request is based on the reintegration into employment of redundant workers at pwa international ltd, an enterprise in the economic sector classified in nace rev. 2 division 33 (repair and installation of machinery and equipment), as well as the integration into the labour market of 108 young unemployed persons not in education or training (neets). it should be noted that the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide support for workers affected by the consequences of major structural changes in world trade. among the causes of the crisis is the closure of pwai following the decision to consolidate the company's operations in north america and asia, as a result of the tendency to locate maintenance, repair and overhaul activity in proximity to expanding centres of world air transport and the negative effects of global trade agreements.
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade flows. on 6 november the commission adopted a proposal for a decision on the mobilisation of the egf in ireland to facilitate the reintegration into employment of redundant workers at pwa international ltd and the integration into the labour market of 108 young unemployed and neets. i support this proposal as the commission has concluded that the application complies with all the applicable provisions of the egf regulation and therefore fulfils the conditions for a financial contribution from the egf. according to the irish authorities, the event that triggered the redundancies at pwa international coincided with the closure of pwai following the decision to move some activities such as maintenance, repair and overhaul to north america and asia.
