in writing. ‒ this is ireland's request to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to provide a contribution of around eur 450 000 to support 108 workers in the repair and supply of aircraft equipment. i have always supported the approval of the egf as a basic rule, although i am aware of its limitations and of certain critical points: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. in fact, the egf should be mobilised when more than 500 units have been used up, whereas here we are well below that figure, and a derogation from the regulation has been chosen. the irish government has tried to provide an explanation by arguing that this request is part of a wider crisis in the whole sector, which would also involve other firms, already subject to previous egf contributions: i am not convinced that the commission has not been able to take account of the fact that the council has not been able to reach a decision on the budget for the year in question.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of rejecting the list of invasive alien species proposed by the commission, which not only does not include the most invasive and problematic species, but instead includes species that would cause no harm to the biodiversity of our territories, human health or the economy.
in writing. - i vote for it. the first list of the commission has been criticised by several national competent authorities, stakeholders and the public, who now have serious doubts about the future effectiveness of the eie regulation, in particular because many of the most problematic invasive alien species are not listed, while other species have been included that are not likely to cause significant adverse effects on biodiversity, ecosystem services, human health or the economy or for which the measures to be taken would entail disproportionate costs.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the draft commission implementing regulation adopting a list of invasive alien species of union concern under regulation (eu) no 1143/2014. the commission shall adopt, by means of implementing acts, a list of invasive alien species of union concern, identified as such because the damage they cause in certain member states is such as to justify the adoption of appropriate measures applicable throughout the union. this list shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in each member state. however, in compiling this list, the commission did not ensure that the methodology to be used for risk assessment is applied in the same way in all member states. furthermore, the reasons for including a species in the draft union list are not based on a risk assessment and appear to be based on political rather than scientific criteria. the resolution therefore asked the commission to withdraw the draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i am in favour of the article 106 objection concerning the list of invasive alien species, as i believe that the establishment of a list of such species does not address the problem of invasive alien species exhaustively in order to protect native biodiversity and ecosystem services and minimise the effects on human health or the economy that such species could have.
in writing. the resolution opposes a draft list of 36 invasive alien species proposed by the commission to prevent their introduction and manage their spread within the union. the objection raised by the resolution deplores the absence from this list of many invasive species which have not yet been included by the commission for lack of time. the commission was obliged to submit the list by 2015 and was therefore forced to propose a list, even if it was not yet finalised. this list will be completed by the commission once the risk assessment for the species not yet present has been completed. i think that the commission has a duty to ensure that the council of ministers is able to take the necessary steps to ensure that the community's financial interests are not undermined.
in writing. ‒ i vote in favour of the objection as many of the most problematic invasive alien species are not listed, while other species have been included which are not likely to cause significant adverse effects on biodiversity, ecosystem services, human health or the economy or for which the measures to be taken would entail disproportionate costs.
in writing. i have decided to vote in favour of the objection under rule 106. the commission did not ensure that the methodology to be used in the risk assessment was applied in the same way in all member states. i therefore believe that it is not possible to ensure that member states use the same type of tests and apply the same general rules. finally, i would point out that several terrestrial plants and mammal species were not included in the list despite a careful risk assessment.
in writing. ‒ the appearance of exotic species, whether animals, plants, fungi or micro-organisms, in new places is not always a cause for concern. however, if these species reach a considerable number, they can become invasive and the serious negative effects that this can have not only on biodiversity but also on society and the economy must be prevented. it was therefore decided to establish a list of invasive alien species of european interest which will be binding in all its elements and directly applicable in each member state. in drawing up the list, the commission did not deal fully with all the scientific aspects, leaving out very important aspects. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution calling on the commission to withdraw the draft implementing regulation and to submit a new draft to the committee responsible.
in writing. ‒ i support this resolution by voting in favour of rejecting the authorization of genetically modified maize nk603xt25, owned by monsanto. i am against the use of gmos in our crops, and i am convinced that we must continue to protect the market and the public from the invasion of these modified varieties produced by multinationals and continue to support the authenticity of our own production in our own territories.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the objection against the authorisation of this gmo maize from monsanto. we are opposed in principle to any new authorization of gmos, all the more so in the present legal context. the commission is using the pretext of approving the right of member states to prohibit the cultivation of a gmo on their territory (a theoretical right, as we saw at the time, when we voted against the measure) to unblock the authorization of new gmos, despite the fact that the usual deadlock in the committee responsible is still in place, due to the cross-vote of member states in favour of and against gmos.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the motion for a resolution on commission implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279 of 4 december 2015 authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of, or produced from genetically modified maize nk603 × t25 (mon-øø6ø3-6 × acs-zmøø3-2) pursuant to regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 of the european parliament and of the council. in this resolution, the european parliament opposed the placing of these products on the market. the corn in question expresses the cp4 protein epsps, which gives it tolerance to the herbicide glyphosate, which is on the world health organization's list of probable human carcinogens. in addition, by this vote parliament underlined that any implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified organisms under regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 in its current non-functioning version should be suspended until the commission has submitted a new legislative proposal that takes into account the concerns expressed repeatedly at national level and by this parliament. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the resolution.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the objection against the authorisation of this gmo maize from monsanto. the european commission is daily showing itself to be distant from the people and the workers of europe, putting at risk not only health but also the economy, history and traditions, and at the same time always favouring the big multinationals.
in writing. i think it is very important that my colleagues in the committee on the environment should propose that the implementing decision on the placing on the market of six types of genetically modified maize be repealed. parliament's scrutiny is decisive in these cases of procedural and substantive control over commission implementing acts, and it is rightly stressed that any implementing decision authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified organisms should be suspended until a new regulation on the sensitive subject of gmos is adopted, which this house rejected only a month ago.
in writing. ‒ on 17 may 2010, monsanto europe sa submitted to the competent authority of the netherlands an application, in accordance with articles 5 and 17 of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003, for the placing on the market of foods, food ingredients, and feed containing or produced from genetically modified maize nk603 × t25. commission implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279 of 4 december 2015 authorises the placing on the market of those products in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 of the european parliament and of the council. i voted in favour of the objection because i consider that commission implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279 is not in accordance with union law, as it is not compatible with the purpose of regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 and regulation (ec) no 396/2005 (8) which is, on the basis of the general principles laid down in regulation (ec) no 178/2002, to provide the basis for ensuring a high level of protection of human life and health, animal welfare, the environment and consumer interests in relation to genetically modified food and feed, while ensuring the effective functioning of the internal market.
the committee on budgets has adopted a number of amendments. ‒ i welcome the vote today by the european parliament on a resolution calling on the commission to withdraw its authorisation for the use of tolerant nk603xt25 maize glyphosate in food and feed. in the resolution we wanted to highlight the fact that glyphosate, a herbicide, is classified by the who as 'probably carcinogenic' and to call on the commission to suspend all authorisations for gmo food and feed until the authorisation procedure, currently under review, has been improved. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of genetically modified organisms (gmos) in food and feed. and the authorization we are discussing today is an attempt by the commission to circumvent this decision to allow the introduction of new gmo foods without waiting for new legislation to finally clarify this sensitive issue.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution which strongly calls on the european commission not to authorise the use of genetically modified roundup ready liberty link maize, monsanto's feed designed to tolerate glyphosate irradiation. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. i find it scandalous that the only body democratically elected by the people cannot give binding opinions on this matter and that the resolution is merely a political statement. the commission itself did not even dare to wait for this, contrary to all institutional practice, when it approved the use of nk603 x t25 maize at the beginning of the month, even before the plenary could express its opinion. since the beginning of my mandate i have been fighting to make europe a gmo-free area and with this vote i reiterate a no-no to the entry of transgenic food and feed into european territory.
in writing. ‒ the luxleaks investigation revealed a number of irregularities by the luxembourg government in the secret granting of tax breaks to large multinationals. in light of this, in december 2014 the european parliament authorised the drafting of a report on improving the rules on transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate tax policies. many of the aspects and proposals presented in the report were already analysed when the taxe report was adopted, such as: improving the exchange of information, a clear definition of the concept of tax havens, and the preparation of measures to combat tax evasion. as stated in the taxe report, while some of the proposed measures are sustainable and meet the requirements of transparency, no form of liability has been envisaged vis-à-vis the individuals and states individually concerned. that's why i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the text aims to promote transparency and avoid future scandals such as the 'luxleaks' scandal involving the luxembourg government and president juncker himself. unfortunately, there is no mention of the obvious political responsibility for what has happened and a chapter is introduced on the convergence of taxation between the different member states, which i do not agree with, which is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the dodds-niedermayer report contains recommendations to the european commission on a subject of great importance, linked to the work of the taxe special committee, or closely related to the "luxleaks" affair. the issue of convergence in corporate tax policies in the eu may raise some questions for those of us who look at the matter from a euro-critical point of view. the commission notes that the luxopco tax ruling does not provide for any exemption from corporate tax for luxopco's activities. in this sense, therefore, we can more than welcome calls for transparency and greater coordination between the member states. on the other hand, we are not convinced by the chapter on the convergence of taxation between the various member states. in addition, as in the case of other similar texts, we must remember that these lists of good intentions are, in fact, late and will take many years to be put into practice and to bring about concrete results and fairness and transparency within the union. our group has tabled a number of amendments aimed, among other things, at emphasizing the specific direct responsibilities of successive juncker-led governments over the years. i abstained. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval.
in writing. ‒ after careful reflection and debate in the house, i voted in favour of the report with recommendations to the commission on how to bring transparency, coordination and convergence to the union's corporate tax policies. i believe that in a european context characterised by a lack of investment and growth, a truly protective system of community rules also concerns areas of which there is little perception, namely the 'economic and financial health' of the union. moreover, it is only through a structured system of rules that transparency, coordination and convergence in corporate tax policies can be achieved. the commission notes that the tax rulings were issued in the form of a tax ruling, which was issued by the luxembourg tax administration on the basis of a ruling by the luxembourg tax administration. i agree with the report and the recommendations it makes, particularly those on the mandatory notification of new tax measures and the extension of automatic exchange of information to all rulings. there is also an urgent need for a common definition of 'tax havens' and of 'stable corporate organisation'.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks scandal, the european parliament decided in december 2014 to authorise the drafting of a legislative own-initiative report, which was aimed at improving transparency, coordination and convergence in corporate tax policies in the union. many of the recommendations in the text were already included in a previous report, including public country-by-country reporting, automatic notification of certain tax measures, improved information exchange, the introduction of a common consolidated corporate tax base, as well as measures to ensure legality such as better protection for whistleblowers, a clear definition of what falls under the category of tax havens and the measures needed to combat their fraudulent use. despite some points of obvious importance, the report is not satisfactory on others; the absence of any reference to political responsibility of individuals and member states, which in fact facilitated the spread of these harmful practices for years, is an example. i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ i agree with the legislative own-initiative report by mr dodds and mr niedermayer on promoting transparency, coordination and convergence in corporate tax policies in the european union, which, due to corporate tax avoidance, special tax arrangements and inefficiencies in collection, is losing hundreds of billions of euros a year. i believe that such practices should not be considered acceptable, especially in the difficult economic circumstances in which europe finds itself at this historic moment, where it is essential that all economic actors contribute in a more than equitable way. the failure of some multinational companies to contribute creates a situation of inequality, in which smaller national companies struggle to compete, in contravention of the principle of the single market. moreover, national governments are also affected by this behaviour, as they are forced to consider reducing public services or increasing taxes for citizens in the face of a decreasing tax base, thus causing a clear disadvantage to the population.
in writing. ‒ following the luxleaks scandal, the econ committee has drawn up a series of recommendations aimed at improving transparency, coordination and convergence in corporate tax policies in the union. these are reflected in the taxe report, including public country-by-country reporting, automatic notification of certain tax measures, improved automatic exchange of information, the introduction (in two stages) of the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb), increased protection for whistleblowers, a clear definition of what falls under the category of tax havens, and the measures needed to combat the use of this harmful practice as well. as in the case of the taxe report, the intention was clear here too to ignore the political responsibilities of individual prominent individuals and individual member states, which in fact have for years facilitated the spread of these harmful practices, which is unacceptable to us. our amendments stress the political responsibility of juncker and the benelux countries and propose the withdrawal of the licence of those companies (banks in particular) which operate through tax havens. for the reasons stated above, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ although the european union has made important steps towards economic integration, such as economic and monetary union and banking union, further efforts are needed with regard to greater coordination of fiscal policies at union level, within the limits set by the european treaties. the coordination of policies on corporate taxation is an indispensable factor in the integration process. i voted in favour of the european parliament's resolution because i believe that it makes very important recommendations to the commission to combat aggressive tax planning and tax evasion, such as: the creation of a country-by-country tax data collection system; increased transparency on tax rulings, whistleblower protection and coordination on corporate tax policies; the creation of a consolidated common tax base as a system of simplification and harmonisation of the definition of tax assets; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year.
in writing. in december 2014, the european parliament decided to authorise this legislative initiative report in order to promote transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate tax policies in the european union. this decision was a direct reaction to the luxleaks scandal. the eu loses around €50-70 billion a year due to corporate tax avoidance through profit shifting alone. such practices should never be considered acceptable, especially in difficult economic circumstances such as those facing europe at this time, in which parliament considers it all the more essential that all economic actors contribute equally. the failure of some multinational companies to contribute creates an environment of inequality, in which smaller national companies have difficulty competing, and this is totally contrary to the principle of the single market. from the point of view of fairness, the recommendation clearly shows a desire to completely disregard the political responsibilities of individual prominent individuals and individual member states, which have in fact facilitated the spread of these harmful practices for years. for this reason, although some of the proposed measures are acceptable, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ despite some shared considerations, i will abstain as there is no evidence of a clear denunciation of the luxleaxs case and of a clear correlation with the political responsibilities of the luxembourg government.
in writing. ‒ businesses are still too often faced with unjustifiable tax differences. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the tax system is not a barrier to the free movement of goods and services, but rather a system which is as integrated as possible and compatible with the needs of the development of businesses. in this sense, transparency, coordination and convergence of policies are the right direction to take. the report contains several measures which go in that direction, and for these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep's own-initiative report on transparency, coordination and convergence in the union's corporate taxation policies because i believe it is of the utmost importance to make progress on corporate taxation in europe, so that it is fair and above all that companies, particularly multinational companies, pay taxes in the countries where their income is actually generated and thus tackle aggressive tax planning at its roots. the ep has vigorously placed taxation issues, which are the responsibility of the member states, at the centre of its debate during this parliamentary term. the commission has therefore renewed the mandate of the taxe committee of inquiry into tax rulings, and is focusing on the introduction of a common tax base which should be the cornerstone of a common corporate taxation (ccctb) in order to promote, through this and other coordination and convergence actions in the tax sector, sustainable development and the strengthening of the competitiveness of smes. the ep's recommendations to the ec call for country-by-country reporting for all multinationals, mandatory notification of tax measures, greater transparency of free ports, protection of whistleblowers and an exhaustive list of countries to be considered tax havens.
in writing. the luxleaks scandal has highlighted the fact that many multinational companies have implemented non-transparent practices in order to reduce their tax liability by up to almost 1%. unfortunately, such aggressive tax planning practices are widespread throughout the eu. i think it is vital to coordinate national tax policies as much as possible, because as we know, legislation on this matter is the prerogative of the member states. i have decided to vote in favour of this proposal because the measures listed could bring about greater transparency, coordination and convergence in the union's policies on corporate taxation.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to create methods for introducing greater transparency and convergence of the union's corporate taxation policies. i am in full agreement with this report and can therefore only vote in favour of it. in fact, a study commissioned by the european parliament shows that the eu loses around €50-70 billion a year due to corporate tax avoidance through profit shifting alone, a figure that then rises to around €160-190 billion, if you take into account special tax arrangements and inefficiencies in collection.
in writing. ‒ we strongly support this measure, which became indispensable following the revelations, known as "luxleaks" by a group of journalists in november 2014, which revealed that many multinational companies had concluded secret agreements with the luxembourg authorities that allowed them to reduce their tax obligations, in some cases, to almost 1%, in the face of the creation of little or no economic activity in that country. we are proud of this report because it creates a new agenda for tax justice, because it introduces more transparency and coordination and convergence mechanisms, which are necessary to combat tax fraud, tax evasion and aggressive tax planning.

in writing. ‒ according to a study commissioned by the european parliament, the eu loses around €50-70 billion a year due to corporate tax avoidance through profit shifting alone. this amounts to approximately eur 160-190 billion, taking into account also special tax arrangements, inefficiencies in collection and other elements. such practices should never be considered acceptable, but in difficult economic circumstances such as those facing europe at the present time, the report considers it all the more essential that all economic actors contribute equally. in november, parliament adopted the commission's special report on tax agreements, calling for compulsory reporting of profits and taxes of multinationals in each country. today, the commission is being asked to call on member states to share tax information, to declare tax rates negotiated with companies and to protect whistleblowers who have helped uncover scandals such as luxleaks. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the report is concerned with recommendations to the commission on transparency, coordination and convergence of corporate tax policies in the union. the report seeks to curb the use of tax evasion practices for companies, which are increasingly damaging the member states' coffers. although it is necessary to implement some of the proposals contained in the report as soon as possible (such as a common european tax identification code, legal protection for whistleblowers, measures to ensure that all profits are taxed where they are generated), i considered it appropriate to abstain because of some shortcomings. the commission has not established that the contested tax rulings are imputable to the state. in addition, downward trade-offs have been reached in several cases, for example by introducing the common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) in two stages, whereas it should be introduced without intermediate stages. for these reasons i did not support the report and i preferred to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the approved report contains a number of recommendations to the commission on how to promote transparency, coordination and convergence in corporate tax policies in the union. together with the final report of the taxe committee and the amendment of the directive on the automatic exchange of information on tax rulings, it indicates the european parliament's will to combat aggressive tax planning and corporate avoidance, a scourge that causes huge losses to member states every year and creates a kind of tax dumping, benefiting multinationals at the expense of smes. i therefore believe that certain proposed measures should be implemented and put into effect as soon as possible: the proposal for a common european tax identification code; the proposal for legal protection of whistleblowers; ensuring that profits are taxed where value is created. however, there are some criticisms and shortcomings in the text which i have approved, which have led me to abstain: the country-by-country reporting should be public and easily accessible, while the ccctb consolidated common tax base should be introduced without intermediate steps. the commission also found that the tax advisor's report did not provide any evidence that the tax advisor had engaged in tax evasion practices.

in writing. ‒ we express our strong support for this resolution, which has become necessary after the un secretary-general convened the first world humanitarian summit, to be held in may 2016 in istanbul. in fact, the world is facing humanitarian crises unprecedented in number, scale and persistence. funding has indeed grown, but needs have grown faster. furthermore, security risks can be increased by the perception that humanitarian aid is being used for political or economic reasons. we particularly welcome the rapporteur's work because it is based on the idea that the european union, as the leading donor and key player in humanitarian action globally, has both the responsibilities and the strength to take a leadership role in finding more efficient and effective ways of meeting the needs of people affected by conflict and disaster.
in writing. ‒ there are ongoing humanitarian crises around the world that are unprecedented in both scale and duration. constant and prolonged man-made conflicts and recurring natural disasters have fuelled a sharp increase in the number of people in need of humanitarian aid. this has pushed the humanitarian response system to its limits. in a context where the gap between humanitarian needs and the operational and financial resources available to respond to them is likely to widen further, un secretary-general ban ki-moon has called for an unprecedented first world humanitarian summit (whc). the humanitarian system will be restructured and adapted to a rapidly changing emergency scenario in order to make humanitarian action more efficient, effective and fit for future needs. the conference will focus on humanitarian financing, risk management, a culture of innovation in humanitarian aid and the essential role of ngos. i am voting in favour of the idea that, with less than a year to go from the summit, we can start doing something concrete to reduce and manage future humanitarian risks.
in writing. ‒ the base metal industry, such as steel, copper, brass and others, plays a key role in many industrial sectors and activities. the production and processing of these metals is currently in crisis, caused not only by environmental policies but also by the absence of investment policies to ensure the development and growth of this sector. the main objective of the martin report is to strike a balance between the need to invest in the base metals industry and the environmental impact, while also trying to minimise the possible damage to workers and inhabitants. this calls for greater transparency of information on emissions, investment and the health of the surrounding population. i have decided to vote in favour of the report because i believe that it is essential not only to improve the exchange of information on this subject but also to achieve a compromise between the needs of development and the social and environmental impacts of development.
in writing. ‒ while the causes of the decline in employment in the eu steel industry, which is likely to affect other key sectors, are properly analysed, the proposals to remedy this are too weak and lack the impact and strength needed to reverse the trend. i am convinced that only by giving back to the member states the instrument of monetary and exchange rate policy and by boosting domestic demand will the conditions be created for a genuine and lasting economic recovery. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which deals in detail with the various sensitive points for the development of a sustainable european base metals industry. the basic metals (steel, aluminium, copper, tin, nickel, lead, cobalt alloys, molybdenum, magnesium and titanium) play a central role in european industry and are used in a number of strategic sectors: the automotive, aviation and energy industries; it is therefore important that decisive action be taken to start a process which will stimulate growth and competitiveness in a sector in which the european union cannot allow further dependencies to develop. the document stresses the need for greater internal integration of the energy market and the identification of investment strategies for development and innovation. it is good that the role that the implementation of a circular economy can play at each production site is highlighted, increasing efficiency and competitiveness through the valorisation of by-products from the secondary metals and recycled metals market. work is needed to ensure that the right economic incentives are developed, including through the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), for the development of this new production model.
in writing. ‒ the european steel industry has been hit by a severe crisis caused by the fall in demand, which in 2014 is 40 million tonnes lower than in the year of the beginning of the global economic and financial crisis. the reduction in demand has led to a historic trade deficit in europe, creating dependency and loss of industrial know-how, with repercussions also in the automotive, construction and low-carbon technology sectors. a strong european response is needed to these events because the proper functioning of the metal industry is fundamental not only to the well-being of our citizens but also to the maintenance of european independence. combining investment in innovation and research with the circular economy and sustainable production means achieving high quality production, minimising waste and producing knowledge and technologies that are not off-the-shelf but can withstand global market fluctuations and relaunch the base metals sector with a renewed and functional perspective.
in writing. - abstention from the vote. the commission also found that the union industry was not able to fully benefit from the measures in force. this capacity adjustment has been of such a scale that any recovery in european demand will result in a historic trade deficit in europe, generating dependency and loss of industrial know-how that will inevitably affect the automotive, construction and low-carbon technology sectors. the closures in the european aluminium sector, on the other hand, occur in a context of an increase in european aluminium demand in recent years, which has led to an increase in imports. climate policy is not the cause of the difficulties of these industries, but it is certainly one of the aggravating causes, as it has proved to be an accelerator of the process of relocation. to begin to remedy this, rather than foolishly insisting on the same sorcerer's apprentice policies, urgent measures must be taken to counter climate dumping by third countries: for example, by replacing the ets with a permanent border adjustment measure (carbon tax). the measures requested in the report are in the right direction, but they are fresh water.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report today to stem the bleeding of capacity and jobs that has hit the european steel industry, largely due to the fall in demand which in 2014 remains 40 megatons below that of 2007. this capacity adjustment has been of such a magnitude that any recovery in european demand will result in a historic trade deficit in europe. steel and aluminium are two significant examples of the difficulties encountered in these professions which must at the same time continue the energy and environmental modernisation which would require an investment policy for which few of them have the means today. however, climate policy is not at all the cause of the difficulties of these industries, but this could happen in the future if the investment crisis continues and if a european industrial policy on raw materials and base metals is not activated. this industrial policy must have the tools and means to cope with the increase in the price of carbon which all the international institutions involved in the fight against climate change are calling for.
in writing. ‒ the base metals industry plays a key role in strategic sectors of our economy such as the automotive and energy sectors. dumping practices by third countries such as china have led to improper competition on the european market, which has created serious difficulties, particularly in the base metals sector. this, together with other factors such as electricity supply contracts, is causing european companies to under-invest in efficient and innovative long-term solutions, thus risking losing competitiveness and making the european economic system overly dependent on other countries. the resolution adopted aims to ensure minimum levels of protection for the european market by modernising trade defence instruments to ensure 'fair' competition between european and non-european producers on the internal market and subjecting operators to equivalent rules, so as to ensure, inter alia, compliance with carbon emission quotas. the resolution, inspired by principles of transparency, also focuses on the right of access to information by civil society and local communities, and pays particular attention to environmental protection. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because we europeans should be proud of our steel industry and should commit ourselves to defending it by applying all the instruments of trade defence, especially when we are talking about the growing unfair competition from outside europe, as in the case of china. we are well aware that the exponential growth of chinese exports to europe is a fact and that recognising china as a market economy would make it virtually impossible to apply the legal measures to protect european industry against that country. we are well aware that china has never so far succeeded in meeting the requirements for being recognised as a market economy, which are for example the absence of state interference, the absence of state-induced distortions on enterprises, the adoption of bankruptcy legislation that ensures legal certainty and stability or the respect of independent accounting principles in line with international standards in this field. i would remind you that recognition would mean that all anti-dumping measures to protect our industry would be abolished.
in writing. ‒ the subject in question although it may appear highly technical has innumerable implications in several areas of primary importance, all of which are closely interrelated. firstly, these metals are the basis of many industries and activities of undisputed importance. secondly, policies in the base metal industry are as a direct consequence likely to have a significant impact, either directly or indirectly, on european employment. in this connection, we must not forget that on the one hand this sector is under heavy international pressure (not to mention the very rapid steps taken by the chinese government!), and on the other hand it is characterized by the high energy requirements of these industries. the report in question - thanks also to the contribution made by the rapporteur, who has a great deal of personal experience in the field - is a good summary of the balance between the conflicting needs. in particular, the call for a fairer policy for indirect emissions compensation between member states and the introduction of border carbon adjustment should be noted, in order to combat international competition which is not subject to the ets constraints. for these reasons, i shall be voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european steel sector is not only of great historical importance for european integration, but also plays a key role in the development of the whole economy, both in terms of technology and in overcoming supply difficulties. however, the steel sector in europe is experiencing one of the most severe crises with the reduction of over 40 million tonnes of steel production capacity since 2008 and the loss of over 60,000 direct jobs and 100,000 indirect jobs. this crisis is making manufacturing industries more dependent on imports from third countries and is causing a loss of industrial know-how with immediate repercussions on millions of jobs and the competitiveness of the sector. the european parliament's resolution, which i voted for, proposes actions to revive the european steel industry on the basis of its sustainability, such as the need for immediate action against climate change and high energy prices, support for investment in the production of low-carbon metals, european measures to protect trade in base metals.
in writing. ‒ the martin report highlights, among other things, the fundamental issue of trade relations with major global partners, which have a major impact on the survival of our production fabric in this strategic sector. the european steel industry is going through a phase of deep crisis: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the steel industry is able to meet the demands of the market. there is an important passage in the report which refers to the possible recognition by the european union of the market economy status of china: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the price of steel is not affected by the price war. the acquisition of such status would have a disastrous impact on the effectiveness of european trade defence instruments and, consequently, on their ability to protect businesses and jobs. there are geopolitics and trade policy at stake, but in either case we cannot allow our companies, our workers, our citizens to pay the price. i firmly believe that european industry must be able to compete in the world on the basis of clear rules and on the same terms as its trading partners. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. the report by mr martin, of the french socialists, focuses on the base metal industry. the role they play for european industry is very high. they are fundamental to many sectors and, as a result, have direct and indirect effects on employment and on a large part of the european economy. it should not be forgotten that they are used by industries with high energy requirements and therefore a balance must be found which allows industry to remain competitive without compromising energy and emission reduction policies. perhaps the most innovative contribution of this report is the call for the standardisation of indirect emission compensation policy among member states, also introducing a tool such as border carbon adjustment which aims to counter international competition which, as is often the case, operates under less stringent regulatory systems than those of the eu. i think this report has succeeded in balancing environmental commitment while safeguarding the rights of workers without prejudicing industrial needs. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep report on the development of a sustainable european base metals industry because i strongly support the idea of a strong, innovative and competitive european base metals industry, but also a clean one that generates quality jobs. i share the need for a european industrial policy in this sector that addresses the environmental and product competitiveness challenge and addresses the growing investment gap in new clean technologies, which would enable european industry to innovate and set production standards at world level. i share the call for a border adjustment mechanism extended to the whole supply chain, which avoids the offshoring of pollution and the shifting of european production to countries with less environmental sensitivity and lower co2 costs. i believe that european leadership in the fight against climate change must also be exercised by ensuring that competing producers apply our legislation in trade with the eu: the determination of the polluting characteristics of imported products is therefore essential. finally, i agree with the reference to the problem of long-term energy contracts and voluntary national offsetting of direct emissions, which generates unfair competition between european producers.

in writing. the industrial importance of common metals is indisputable, as these are steels and special steels, aluminium, copper, brass, nickel, lead, zinc, titanium and more. they are the raw material for many industrial sectors and therefore have a strategic impact of enormous scope on european employment, both directly and indirectly. these are energy intensive activities which need to be taken into account in energy policy and in the reduction of co2 emissions. the sector is currently facing unfair international competition, mainly from china. this is a price clash with economies which must not be subject to the innumerable restrictions on labour protection and emission reductions to which european companies are subject. the most innovative aspects of the proposal are aimed at this, namely the requirement that the policy of compensation for indirect emissions be equitable between the member states and the introduction of a system for adjusting the carbon content at the border, with the aim of countering precisely that international competition which is not subject to the restrictions of the emissions trading system. in the light of these developments, i voted in favour of this report.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, 20 years after dayton, it is time we all looked ahead. looking ahead means looking at a common future inside the european union. the 20 years since 1995 have now proven beyond doubt that dayton has delivered on its main objective of bringing peace and stability to bosnia and herzegovina and enabling post-conflict reconstruction. but many challenges remain. much remains to be done to consolidate reconciliation. the dayton peace agreement has also become fundamental to rebuilding peace and advancing reconciliation in the broader region. it has played an important part in the efforts to rebuild dialogue and cooperation in the western balkans. some of the countries of the region, once enemies, have become signatories to the agreement and over time have become friends and close partners investing in their joint future in the european union. the western balkans region has moved a long way forward in the two decades since dayton. many countries of the region are candidates for eu membership, and bosnia is a potential candidate. bosnia has made considerable progress in its relations in the region – good neighbourly relations. the eu has been one of the largest donors to bosnia, both during the war and in the post-war reconstruction period. its presence largely focused on advancing political and economic reform and establishing a framework for the implementation of the eu’s stabilisation and association process, following the thessaloniki summit in june 2003 and the eventual integration of bosnia into the eu. in addition, at the end of 2004, bosnia also became the first country where instruments of both the cfsp and the esdp were deployed on the ground. the eu continues today to safeguard the dayton agreement through eufor althea. however, bosnia is no longer a security consumer state, but a security provider. it has effectively contributed to un and nato missions and, since 15 september 2015, it can also effectively contribute to eu csdp missions after signing its framework participation agreement in the eu crisis management operations. progress may be uneven at times, but the strong desire of the majority of the country’s citizens will continue to guide political leadership in the right direction. the country’s citizens demand socio-economic and other reforms to improve their daily lives. they call for progress on the eu path to give themselves and their children the perspective of life in a free, democratic, stable and prosperous society, a society which protects minorities and fully respects human rights and freedoms. these are european values which the people of bosnia and herzegovina share. we in the european union are fully committed to assisting bosnia and herzegovina in achieving this goal. in december 2014 the eu council agreed to engage in a renewed approach to overcome the stalemate that then hindered bosnia and herzegovina’s eu path. political institutions and leadership across the country have given their clear and unequivocal commitment to taking forward the reform required for progress on the eu path. much has been achieved in 2015 on the basis of this commitment. the stabilisation and association agreement entered into force on 1 june 2015. subsequently, bosnia and herzegovina’s various government levels agreed the scope and depth of reforms to be undertaken. in this respect, the first ever eu-bosnia stabilisation and association council took place last week with positive results, as indicated in the joint communiqué published on the day. the initial focus has been on the socio-economic area, but the reform process already covers a much broader agenda. we have worked closely with international partners – in particular with the us and international financial institutions – to help make these reforms happen. we will continue these joint efforts to empower the authorities in bosnia to take forward the transformation process effectively. this will not be easy, but it is certainly possible, and its success is fully in the hands of bosnia and herzegovina. at this point, bosnia and herzegovina is considering a possible application for eu membership. this is an achievement in itself and would have been difficult to think of only a year ago. but to make an application credible, bosnia will need to continue to prove its credibility by delivering on commitments made. over the last 12 months, together with the bosnian authorities, represented today by the chair and the members of bosnia’s presidency, we have engaged effectively. in this process the eu has responded with concrete deliverables to positive, constructive and concrete efforts undertaken by bosnia. it is now up to bosnia to give us good reasons to take a further step. in dayton the future of bosnia and herzegovina was shaped by the country’s leaders, together with the neighbours and the international community. 20 years after dayton the responsibility falls on bosnia and herzegovina and, following the steady steps of the past year, it is important not to jeopardise all that has been achieved so far. we truly hope that we will soon be able to open a new chapter in the history of bosnia and herzegovina. the eu is committed to doing all that is necessary on our side as soon as bosnia makes a credible step towards us. thank you for your attention. i am looking forward to hearing your views.
thank you, minister schmit, who will be with us in the replay. this is your last speech on behalf of the luxembourg presidency. we thank you for your availability during these months.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the overall context of internal security in the european union has changed dramatically in recent years, exacerbated by the fact that the member states are the world's main arms exporters. we're talking about over 36 billion in exports in 2013. weapons which can hardly be traced back to legal trade flows, that is the real problem, which are directed at the security of the european union, but are not actually intended to feed what can be legal trade with the due ifs and the due buts. all these weapons and trade have fuelled and are fuelling terrorism and armed conflict. on the other hand, the rampant corruption in third countries affects the security of our citizens, with arms smuggling and trafficking entering europe unhindered by the almost complete absence of checks at the entry points. it is absurd that we are closing the frontiers, saying no to schengen, but at the same time we are able to have a certain amount of illegal arms within our european territory with a certain amount of peace of mind. so i am certainly in favour, as my colleague has said before, of more controls, of certainly having more information shared within the various european structures. i also believe that there should be a separation between weapons for military and civilian use, because technologies such as remote piloting systems, applied robotics and surveillance technologies could not only be detrimental to human rights, but could also pose a significant threat to europe's strategic interests and our digital infrastructure. i would like to conclude by saying that, as we have seen, isis uses european passports and weapons in the various attacks, and i believe that we should block trade with the countries that buy and sell arms to isis.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the sale of arms is always a difficult and very sensitive subject, and it is even more so in these years in which europe has seen the resurgence of wars and the return of terrorism with such virulence. i think we have to look very carefully at two phenomena that have been occurring in recent times. the first concerns the steady increase in the turnover of companies producing arms, not only those which are exported but also those which are stocked in europe. the second is the systematic, blatant violation of the eight criteria of the 2008 common position. they're breaches in plain sight. for this reason, a regulation is needed which not only establishes the authorities but also restricts the space for those who produce and sell arms and, above all, sets rules for the states concerned in this process. i would therefore like to highlight four of the aspects which have already been dealt with. the first is about transparency: it is unacceptable that the major european countries do not provide data on arms sales, unacceptable, also because behind it is the hypocrisy of those who say they want to fight war and terrorism and then do not do the minimum necessary to be able to govern this process. the second is the one concerning intermediation: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. the third thing, which is very important, is that along with the sale of arms there is the sale of technologies, which are equally dangerous. finally, the sanctions. without sanctions, member states will continue to adopt uncritical attitudes and behaviour which are contrary to the arguments they support.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, mr valero's report stresses the need to speed up the adoption of new european measures on arms exports by the member states. i believe it is essential that the european union develops an effective and coordinated system of arms control which can bridge the deep differences between national legislation. common position 2008/944/cfsp provides a comprehensive legal framework for arms exports, but greater efforts are needed by member states to apply all eight criteria set out in that document. i would also like to point out that there are currently no common control procedures in specific technical areas, such as the conversion of military weapons into civilian weapons, the treatment of deactivated weapons and weapons for theatrical use, including in relation to their possible trade. in this respect, my country, italy, has adopted strict technical and administrative requirements to prevent illegal practices in the handling of weapons. these aspects should also be taken into account in the development of common and effective rules on arms exports, all the more so at a particular time in the light of the security situation we are living in.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, as mr albert dess said a moment ago, the agriculture committee of this parliament has considered this debate necessary in order to ask the executive to clarify certain ambiguities in the legislation on the legal protection of biotechnological inventions. there is a broad consensus on the non-patentability of essential biological processes for the production of plants and animals, as clearly stated in article 4 of directive 98/44/ec. however, recent decisions by the european patent office require greater clarity on the legal interpretation of european patent law. innovation in agriculture and the development of new plant varieties are crucial to respond to the challenges of food security and climate change and at the same time can give a significant boost to european small and medium-sized enterprises. while patents are designed to stimulate competitiveness and innovation by safeguarding economic investment, they can in some cases act as a brake on innovative development, particularly where essential biological processes are involved which have been used freely by farmers for years. we hope that, in view of future decisions by the european patent office, clarity will be found in finding the right balance between the protection of intellectual property and the legitimate access to and use of biological material derived from essentially biological processes.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, as you have heard, all the political families are concerned about this behaviour of the commission, which sometimes misinterprets directives. in this particular case, the opposition to the use of patents which has been expressed to you stems precisely from the fact that the commission has applied to the european patent office, particularly because the subject of this further request for interpretation is a very sensitive one for us, it concerns biodiversity, because the idea of patenting plant material is not only wrong, it is dangerous. we would draw your attention to two points. first, who can promote mass patenting? the big companies. in this area, innovation and research towards biodiversity have always been the heritage of small businesses, which have done a worthy job and which for this reason must be protected and helped. second theme: if we are moving towards a concentration produced by patents, it is clear that this will not stop with the products under consideration today, but will become the criterion, the system to be adopted for the entire chain, from agricultural production to food production, introducing negative innovations that would contradict, in contrast to what was the important step forward that the union has made in the defence of biodiversity and in research and innovation related to this species. answer to a blue-card question. i would point out that, unlike what has historically happened in the industrial production sectors in agriculture, innovation and research have never been developed towards the new by the large companies. it has always been the small producers who have built niche positions, which then expanded, to look with interest, with positive competition, at biodiversity issues. if we open up a space where the larger companies can fit in, we're going to have the opposite effect here of what has historically been the case in industry, where the big ones will destroy innovation.

egypt refrain from mass trials and, consequently, handing down mass sentences. we of course noted our strong opposition to the use of the death penalty under all circumstances. we will be continuing discussions with egypt on justice in the relevant dialogue, in the framework of the eu-egypt association agreement. we will thus seek further improvements, including on judicial proceedings: not least with regard to minors who are detained with adults, rather than in juvenile detention centres, and who are tried as adults rather than by juvenile court judges. you will be aware that ibrahim halawa was 17 years old when arrested. we also systematically address mass trials, which violate due legal process as they fail to determine individual criminal responsibility by bringing identical charges against groups of accused. in addition, such mass trials bring prolonged detention conditions which are in breach of article 9 of the international covenant on civil and political rights. we are very pleased with the good cooperation with this house in our effort to improve the human rights situation in egypt and count on your continued support. author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the maldives archipelago is not only the place of the beautiful beaches, blue lagoons and wide cliffs we all know, but also the place where many rights are violated. many workers, especially from bangladesh and india, employed in luxury facilities are exploited and underpaid. there is also a continuing abuse of the judicial system, with many political opponents being wrongfully accused and imprisoned. as if that were not enough, the growing religious intolerance is increasing the climate of terror and shrinking the space for any kind of public discussion. the government continues to violate international obligations on issues related to torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, discrimination against women, and political and civil rights. however, the worst human rights violation in the maldives at the moment concerns the reintroduction and possible application of the death penalty as a tool of political repression. we call on the european union and therefore on all the member states to recall our firm stance against the death penalty and the fact that the death penalty violates the most important right, namely the right to life, and inflicts the additional sentence of psychological torture.
author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are deeply concerned about the progressive deterioration of democratic standards and the growth of authoritarian tendencies in the maldives, as well as the repression of political opponents and the intimidation of the media and civil society. we want to insist that the maldivian government must respect the decisions of the united nations, which called on the authorities to release former president nasheed immediately. furthermore, members of the opposition facing charges must be guaranteed due process, in accordance with the maldivian constitution and international due process obligations. we call for an immediate end to all forms of violence, including against peaceful protesters, and for an immediate end to political interference in the maldives' judicial system. urgent reforms are needed to ensure the independence and impartiality of the maldivian judiciary, with the aim of restoring internal and international confidence in its functioning.

member of the commission.– mr president, i am speaking here on behalf of my colleague, high representative/vice- president of the european commission federica mogherini, who cannot attend today’s go unnoticed by the european public at large. the european union is increasingly concerned about the risk of radicalisation in the maldives and about the number of maldivians who are, unfortunately, joining da’esh or other fundamentalist groups in syria and iraq. the eu is ready to work with the government of the maldives to further the fundamental values of democracy, human rights and the rule penal code. we hope this will help highlight those areas where respect for rule of law should be improved, in line with international standards. progress in the rule of law can be an important step for the government to show its willingness to cooperate with the international community on the critical issues of democracy and human rights. i hope to see this in practice.

the agenda includes seven motions for resolutions on malaysia.
author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union's free trade agreements are based primarily on economic criteria, taking account, within the framework of coherent policy, of respect for environmental and social standards, including human rights. human rights are mentioned in the preamble to the agreement, but it is not binding. malaysia, unfortunately, is still far behind in terms of the human rights of indigenous peoples and minorities and there are many violations. land rights are a major concern of ngos, the state plans to build fifty dams in the east of the country by 2030 to serious damage to the environment and the lands of the indigenous people. these could displace tens of thousands of people and flood hundreds of square kilometres of rainforest. there are big corruption problems, sarawak state is the object of speculation by all foreign investors. according to ngos, 80 percent of the rain forest has already been destroyed to make way for palm oil plantations. malaysia is actually one of the most corrupt countries in the world. now i say, let us use the instrument of free trade agreements to strengthen this defence of human rights because this is our chance.
author of the book. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there has been a significant restriction of freedom of speech in malaysia due to criminal laws used to silence critical voices. particularly concerning is the sedition act, which has allowed more than a hundred people to be charged and arrested since the beginning of 2015. anwar ibrahim, a former opposition leader, was convicted of sodomy, as recalled in february 2015, and denied adequate medical care. malaysian cartoonist ulhaque has been charged under the sedition act for tweeting critical of the government in reference to ibrahim's conviction. media are facing increasing difficulties in reporting corruption allegations against the prime minister and malaysian lgbti people are criminalised under the anti-sodomy law. it should be remembered that malaysia is a member of the united nations security council and the current chairman of asean. the european parliament's request is clear: the european union has a duty to release the prisoners, to withdraw the draft national security council law, particularly with regard to the broad powers granted to the prime minister, and it is right to maintain a balance between safeguarding national security and, for us, the imperative of protecting civil and political rights.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the sedition act, the printing presses and publications act, the peaceful assembly act, the communications and multimedia act, the list of legislative acts and the various reforms of the penal code affecting the exercise of freedom of expression and assembly in malaysia is unfortunately very long. the country also suffers from high social dumping, corruption is rampant right up to the highest levels of government, and a forced politicization of the judiciary has led to trials against the opposition and political dissidents and even journalists, as happened for example with former opposition leader anwar ibrahim, now in prison on a downright ridiculous charge, which also shows how much the islamic courts and sharia have taken over the country. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environment is protected. as the european union, we are a market of over 500 million people, we are an economic superpower and our trade agreements can be the ultimate weapon to become a human rights superpower as well. we can do this. if not now, when? europe, wake up and demand from our partners respect for those sacrosanct rights which are granted to every man.

in writing. ‒ 2015 marks the 25th anniversary of the start of eu-vietnam relations. these relations have rapidly expanded from trade and development aid to a more comprehensive bilateral relationship. the eu is vietnam's largest export market and vietnam has systematically adopted a strongly pro-european approach over the past decades and has actively engaged with the eu as a member of the association of southeast asian nations (asean) in a wide range of areas including trade and investment, development, economic and political affairs, and climate change. for the above reasons, parliament welcomed the conclusion of the comprehensive partnership and cooperation agreement with vietnam, stressing the great strategic importance of vietnam as a key partner of the eu in south-east asia and asean. i therefore hope that the eu and vietnam will both derive maximum benefits from the ratification of this agreement, which i supported by voting in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the completion of europe's economic and monetary union because i believe it is a clear and timely text which can accurately outline parliament's instructions to the european commission on the future of the single currency. the report by the five presidents entitled 'completing europe's economic and monetary union' certainly demonstrates the european executive's will to move forward with the integration of the euro area, which will, however, need to have a single fiscal policy to govern the euro. the macroeconomic imbalances in the eu today are precisely due to this: the lack of european economic policy instruments capable of operating in the real economy. we cannot live by the european semester alone.
in writing. ‒ the resolution under vote is entirely ideological, biased and totally in defense of the eu's monetary policy which has generated the current crisis and brought our country to its knees. i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ completing europe's economic and monetary union is as urgent and important as ever. we should be proud to have the euro, the common currency of 330 million european citizens and 19 states. however, it is not enough: we need an economic government of the union, to complete monetary and fiscal union, and to establish a common treasury for the euro area together with the legal parameters for the convergence of the different legal and financial systems of the member countries. this cannot be done without strengthening democratic legitimacy and citizen control over the institutions involved. the social aspect of the process must be prominent, implying a redistributive logic of the burden of financial shocks and a greater resilience of the emu system to global macroeconomic imbalances. in supporting the development of emu we must emphasize that its realization is not the end of a journey but one of the fundamental steps in the completion of the european union to realize the common project of a european federal state.
in writing. - i vote against it. the resolution is ideological and fully committed to defending the eu's monetary policy.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this resolution to complete europe's economic and monetary union. i would like to make two points. the first concerns investment, which is known to be held back in the euro area by at least three factors: the commission has also taken note of the weak demand dynamics, the build-up of debt and the fragile confidence of the private sector. the eurozone needs to not only support demand but also tackle debt and fragile confidence. the european central bank must put in place monetary policy measures that can help support the economic recovery of the euro area. the second point concerns a proposal recently adopted by the college of european commissioners to improve the economic governance of the euro area. the euro area member states should have a unified representation in the international financial institutions, in particular the international monetary fund. if each member state of the eurozone speaks for itself, or worse if they contradict each other, the eurozone will never have the weight it should have. the completion of economic and monetary union depends very much on how it is implemented, whether the coordination mechanism is created to prepare the unified positions that the president of the eurogroup could and should present to the international monetary fund on behalf of all the member states of the eurozone.
in writing. ‒ this is a resolution with an oral question on the future of economic union which, despite the breadth of the subject, forcibly limits the focus to the democratic aspects related to the marginal role played by the european parliament in emu governance matters, deliberately omitting all the substantive and most controversial issues, and thus forgoing the opportunity to express parliament's position on the process of implementing the report of the 5 presidents. it is a renunciation of any serious debate on this matter in parliament and i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution tabled to take steps towards european monetary and economic union. the commission has done well to encourage this transition which is still to be made by presenting a package containing the steps towards the completion of economic and monetary union (emu), consisting of two communications, a recommendation relating to a council recommendation and a proposal for a council decision and a commission decision. with these measures, while recognising that some steps have been taken in the right direction, i think that further efforts will be needed to address the current shortcomings in achieving this objective. i therefore agree with this report and i vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on economic and monetary union because i believe that it is a priority to achieve a union that is capable of achieving more growth, employment and prosperity for all citizens, but that is also built on solid foundations, able to face not only domestic but also global challenges, and able to absorb shocks by having sufficiently resilient economies. i am aware that employment and social developments have been examined in detail in the country reports during the year, but i would like to stress the urgency and the need to improve the labour market and social performance, especially to restore confidence to all unemployed young people.
in writing. ‒ the resolution on which we are called upon to vote today represents yet another missed opportunity for parliament to address issues of the utmost importance! despite the breadth of the subject, it artificially focuses only on the democratic aspects related to the marginal role played by the european parliament in emu governance issues, deliberately neglecting all the substantive and most controversial issues. parliament thus forgets the opportunity to express its position on the process of implementing the report of the five presidents. once again, form was preferred to substance: the text is the unsatisfactory result of a compromise reached in a few hours between the main political groups and adopted at the cost of the mass withdrawal of the amendments which were on the substance. this resolution (which therefore in no way reflects the position of the econ committee, which is clearly divided on governance issues) has the effect of stifling any possibility of political debate and silencing the voice of smaller groups. the resulting text, which we are asked to vote on today, is, it is emphasized, a text which says absolutely nothing. i can only vote against.
