in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the ep resolution on completing emu because i believe that we must move forward vigorously with the implementation of the report of the five presidents, building on the latest communications adopted by the ec which fall within the so-called phase 1 of the roadmap, aimed at strengthening emu. there are currently shortcomings in the institutional framework of the euro area and further efforts are therefore needed. it is a matter of political will, as the treaties already allow progress to be made towards completing emu, but this will have to be done with greater democratic control by the ep, to ensure the ownership of the euro area governance by the european citizens. i therefore shared the ep's call for the opening of negotiations on an interinstitutional agreement (iaa) on european economic governance, including the european semester and the monitoring of the implementation of the macroeconomic adjustment programme with the ep, the council and the eurogroup, as provided for in the same report by the five presidents. to this end, i consider the democratic control of the ep to be of particular importance, particularly with regard to the recommendations concerning the euro area. the strengthening of the euro area will also depend on the completion of the banking union, through the european deposit insurance scheme.
in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution. i believe that the european semester is the most efficient form of coordination of european economic policies. i support, however, the demands of this parliament that the commission should be involved to the fullest extent permitted by the treaties in the decision-making procedures of the european semester. i believe in a europe of the peoples, economically and politically integrated, and this is not possible without the ever greater participation of the european parliament, the only institution directly representing the citizens.
in writing. ‒ despite the many steps forward made, further efforts are needed to complete economic and monetary union (emu) and to address the current shortcomings of the euro area institutional framework. the president of the eurogroup, jeroen dijsselbloem, said that monetary union must be completed by creating a real banking union with a deposit guarantee and by increasing the european fund for strategic investments. the eurogroup president also stressed that debt continued to hamper growth and that fiscal policies should continue. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution but i hope that the package published by the european commission containing the steps for completing economic and monetary union (emu) will leave more room for the parliamentary scrutiny and debate at european level which are necessary to ensure democratic accountability for decisions taken in the context of emu and, consequently, to ensure citizens' ownership of the governance of the euro area.
in writing. ‒ the economic recovery of our continent is unfortunately still very fragile and to boost growth we must make the best use of the instruments at our disposal, so it is necessary to strengthen economic governance and fully achieve the economic and monetary union of our continent. we have created emergency mechanisms, new institutions to strengthen economic cooperation, but that is not enough. we must first complete the banking union, to give strength to our banks, but also and above all to savers. new instruments are also needed, such as the european fund for strategic investments. this is a first step in the right direction, but it needs to be strengthened to allow greater credit flows to enterprises and more action is needed to strengthen domestic demand.
in writing. i voted against this report on the future of economic and monetary union, as it is an empty and inconclusive text which does not in the least call into question the current proposals to complete and further strengthen the construction of the eurozone, despite the fact that the failed experience of the euro, as evidenced by the crisis of recent years, suggests that it is going in the opposite direction. the report is essentially a sham attempt to find solutions to the very serious and intolerable problem of the complete lack of democratic control over key economic policy decisions inherent in the current framework of economic governance. the report also fails to address a key consideration on the sustainability of the single currency and the need to radically rethink the current governance framework, putting national sovereignty over democratic monetary and fiscal policy choices at the centre and defining a plan for a controlled and orderly dissolution of the eurozone. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ despite the breadth of the subject, this resolution, which i rejected, forcibly limits the focus to the democratic aspects related to the marginal role played by parliament in emu governance matters, deliberately omitting all the substantive and most controversial issues, and thus forgoing the opportunity to express parliament's position on the process of implementing the five presidents' report. the final text is the unsatisfactory result of a compromise reached in a few hours between the main political groups, which also involved the mass withdrawal of amendments that went too far into the substance. this is a resolution which has stifled any possibility of political debate and the voice of smaller groups and which in no way reflects the position of the econ committee, which is clearly split on governance issues. in the econ committee we had tabled a number of amendments which highlighted key issues related to the failure of the euro, the inadequacy of the governance framework and the instruments available, and which reiterated that the lack of democracy can only be addressed by recognising the democratic sovereignty of the member states over monetary and fiscal policies. these amendments, like most of those tabled by all the political groups, have simply been ignored or rejected.
in writing. ‒ the annual report on human rights and democracy in the world not only allows an assessment of the actions taken in the past year, but also ensures that european citizens are better informed about european policies in this field. the work presented by the rapporteur, mr preda, calls on the european institutions to make more effective and effective use of the instruments provided for the respect of human rights and democracy in third countries. the european union should first of all support and encourage the process of democratization and the building of democracies on the ground. it should also make further efforts to protect specific areas of action, such as freedom of conscience, freedom of belief and respect for the rights of women and children. i voted in favour because the report not only gave a positive account of the instruments used in 2014, but also proposed additional forms of intervention to ensure better implementation of european human rights objectives.
in writing. ‒ respect for human rights is at the heart of the eu's principles and i am convinced that it should be included in all agreements with third countries, but this is a well-established practice that the eu often willingly ignores, preferring to give priority to the economic interests at stake or failing to assert its political weight adequately. the solutions proposed in this report are too weak and i believe ineffective in achieving the ultimate aim which is pursued, and for these reasons i have not voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the eu annual report on human rights and democracy in the world is a key instrument for the union's external action, which, in accordance with article 21 of the treaty on european union, must be developed around the principles of democracy, the rule of law and the universality of human rights, allowing them to be promoted on a global scale. the european union must therefore ensure that our external action is consistent with our internal policies, on the assumption that respect for fundamental rights and freedoms must be the guiding principle of the union's action on the international scene. if europe is to continue to be the guarantor of human rights in the world, it must first set an example of respect for these rights within its own borders. in this connection, i welcome the fact that human rights are increasingly at the heart of the dialogue between the european institutions, particularly within parliament, and i think it is highly desirable that every instrument designed to protect them is effectively deployed. not only that: the promotion and protection of fundamental rights must be integrated into all union policies in the external dimension, with particular attention to neighbourhood policy and development cooperation.
in writing. ‒ it is worrying that human rights and the democratic values of freedom of thought, speech, religion and association are so threatened today in many parts of the world, particularly under authoritarian regimes. in the face of the shrinking of public and democratic space in the world, and considering that an increasing number of human rights defenders are undergoing physical and psychological attacks, it is clear that, in order to live up to its commitment to promote human rights and democracy in the world, the eu and its member states must speak with a single and coherent voice, so that their message is heard. enhanced cooperation between the commission, the council, the eeas, the parliament and eu delegations is necessary in order to improve the overall coherence of the eu's human rights and democracy policy and its centrality in relation to all union policies with an external dimension, in particular in the areas of development, security, employment, migration, trade and technology. human rights and democracy in the world will not be able to take firm root if democratic countries do not act in a manner consistent with their values in all possible circumstances, including those of economic and financial bargaining.

in writing. ‒ twenty years ago, the dayton agreement launched a slow process of stabilisation and reconstruction in bosnia and herzegovina. a lot has changed since 1995: bosnia and herzegovina has gone from being a war-torn state to a potential member of the european union. bosnia was the first country to have cfsp support deployed on the ground and eufor althea is still contributing to the safeguarding of the dayton treaty clauses. the agreement stopped the war but much more needs to be done to create a democratic and inclusive society. progress in bosnia and herzegovina is uneven and slow. a vigorous constitutional reform, the resolution of the country's major socioeconomic problems and the removal of divisive tendencies and paralysing ethnic ideologies are fundamental conditions for the construction of a strong democracy. the european union will do its part, but it is essential that there are strong endogenous drivers within the country as well as greater participation of civil society in this change. over the past 12 months, the eu's engagement with the bosnian authorities has been reinforced to ensure that progress made so far is not jeopardised and to renew its commitment to building a fully functioning democratic state.
in writing. ‒ the dayton peace agreement ended the bloody war in bosnia and herzegovina, the bloodiest and most devastating conflict to have struck the periphery of europe in the last thirty years. today we can acknowledge the positive transformation that the federal republic of bosnia and herzegovina has undergone over the last twenty years, from a country just emerging from the ravages of war to a state aspiring to join the european union. the eu is committed and must continue to be committed to the european perspective and to the continuation of the accession process of bosnia and herzegovina and all the countries of the western balkans. regional cooperation and the process of european integration are the most appropriate approaches to promote reconciliation and to overcome hatred and divisions between the peoples of the area. the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement is an incentive to encourage the country's authorities to pursue the necessary reforms, giving priority to the socioeconomic needs of the citizens alongside political reforms aimed at democratizing the system of government and ensuring real equality and democratic representation of the three peoples constituting the federal republic of bosnia and herzegovina and all citizens of the country.

in writing. ‒ the arms export discipline is regulated not only at european level, by common position 2008/944/cfsp, but also at international level, thanks to the arms trade treaty. nevertheless, the share of arms exports by member states is still very high and, unfortunately, in particular political situations such as those in the territories of ukraine or syria, such arms end up in the hands of terrorists and oppressive regimes. the valero report illustrates perfectly how, even in the presence of a specific regulation on this subject, there are still ambiguities and limitations which should be resolved. a coordinated approach by the member states is therefore required in respecting and resolving legislative ambiguities, as well as in providing for a sanctioning regime and an independent control system. for these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of the amendments drawn up and proposed in the report, in the hope that a more effective arms export regime will be established.

in writing. ‒ after careful consideration and debate in the house, i have voted in favour of the report on arms exports: the union shall contribute to the implementation of common position 2008/944/cfsp. i believe that the international arms trade and its regulation are of strategic importance and a means of strengthening international stability and security, in the difficult balance between the controlled proliferation of arms and the existence of the natural right of individual and collective self-defence. i am convinced that the major exporters have a great responsibility in terms of the overall impact, and they must respect the standards of transparency, information and common positions. it is well known that the military strategy of terrorist organisations is strengthened precisely in the gaps of european harmonization, so the rules laid down in the common position must represent the minimum standard which in any case allows the adoption of stricter national rules. i therefore voted in favour.

in writing. in the context in which we live, this relationship takes on even more importance. i voted in favour because i share the need for greater controls and for greater information sharing between the various member states, the latter and europol and eurojust, as well as with third countries, in order to reduce the illegal arms trade. i also believe that there should be a separation between weapons for military and civilian use, because technologies such as remote piloting systems, applied robotics and surveillance technologies could not only be detrimental to human rights, but could also pose a significant threat to europe's strategic interests and our digital infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ as is often the case, even in the case of arms exports and the very serious consequences associated with them, it is not so much a question of a lack of rules as of their application. common position 2008/944/cfsp on arms exports is a legally binding framework that sets out eight criteria that member states should apply when licensing conventional arms exports. however, it is clear that something is seriously wrong, as the report on the vote today also points out. situations such as ukraine, syria, iraq, libya and yemen show how arms exported by member states sometimes end up in the hands of terrorists, repressive regimes or countries that use children in hostilities. some 500 000 people die every year from gun violence and the member states are major arms exporters! as this report points out, the problem is that the common position is not being respected! for this reason, i agree inter alia with the need for stricter application of the criteria by the member states; on the establishment of an independent european arms control authority; the commission has also set up a mechanism to monitor the possible diversion of exported arms. my vote is in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because the eu member states are among the world's leading arms exporters, with eur 36,711 billion in global exports in 2013, of which eur 10,735 billion between member states and eur 25,976 billion to third countries; common position 2008/944/cfsp on arms exports is a legally binding framework which sets out 8 criteria that member states should apply when licensing exports of conventional arms. the resolution notes that developments in recent years indicate that something has gone wrong. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of children in the production of weapons. the resolution stresses the need for stricter application of the criteria by member states, clarification of the criterion requiring that exports be prohibited where there is a clear risk that the technology will be used for internal repression, the creation of an independent european arms control authority, the introduction of mechanisms automatically freezing the ability of member states to export to countries to which an embargo has been imposed.

in writing. ‒ i shared the ep resolution on arms exports: i am therefore very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to implement common position 2008/944/cfsp, because i believe that their uncontrolled distribution poses a risk to the security of citizens and a serious threat to international peace and stability. given that every minute a person dies worldwide from causes related to armed violence, it is not difficult to understand the need for better regulation of the international arms trade and for greater responsibility on the part of states at the global level, especially those that make this sector one of the main economic activities. the recent terrorist attacks in paris, the ongoing wars in syria, iraq, yemen and libya and all the other conflicts in the world have shown that weapons very often end up in the hands of terrorists, used against the civilian population and to train child soldiers. i believe that the common position on the arms trade is the right legal approach to bind the member states to closer coordination of national policies on the subject. finally, i welcome the creation of an independent arms control authority under the aegis of the eu high representative for foreign affairs and security policy.

in writing. ‒ researchers must have unlimited access to plant biological material. closing the sector as in the recent decision (g2/12 and g2/13) of the enlarged board of appeal of the european patent office (epo) which allows plant characteristics to be patented even when they are developed, or could be obtained, by essentially biological plant breeding techniques is wrong and dangerous. without unlimited access to plant biological material, it is impossible to innovate and develop the plant breeding sector: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's food supply is not affected by the crisis. the impact on european competitiveness will be negative, with risks of downstream effects in terms of the plurality of food supply, the quality of the production available to consumers and a reduction in internal market competitiveness.
in writing. - i vote for it. the international system of plant variety rights based on the upov convention, as well as community legislation, establishes as a fundamental principle that the owner of a plant variety may not prevent others from using the protected plant in order to promote the use of protected varieties in other production activities. in that resolution, the ep noted that granting too broad protection through patents could stifle innovation and progress and harm small and medium-sized producers by blocking access to plant and animal genetic resources, especially in the breeding sector. the selection of plants is an essential prerequisite for the security of food supply and, to some extent, energy supply. the text under vote today reiterates this concept, while also acknowledging that this objective has not been fully achieved and stressing that products obtained by conventional reproduction techniques (some of which, nevertheless, have been the subject of numerous applications for registration with the european patent office in recent years) should not be patentable.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on "patents and patent protection for plant discoveries". in this resolution, parliament stressed that the prohibition of the patentability of products obtained by conventional breeding techniques is essential to stimulate innovation, particularly for small enterprises. plant breeding is an innovative process that has been practised by farmers and farming communities for a long time and access to biological material is essential to stimulate innovation and the development of new varieties, in order to ensure global food security, address climate change and prevent essentially biological, such as plants, seeds, indigenous traits and genes, from being excluded from patentability. the commission will then clarify existing eu rules, in particular the directive on the legal protection of biotechnological inventions, and forward these clarifications to the european patent office (epo), in order to ensure that products obtained by conventional breeding techniques cannot be patentable.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on patents and patent protection for plant products. continued research on plant products and access to plant biological material is important to stimulate innovation and the development of new varieties in order to: ensure global food security, address climate change and prevent plant breeding monopolies, while providing greater opportunities for smes. on these points, from food safety to standards to meet the needs of small and mediumsized enterprises, i believe that europe must do a lot. it is right to point out that essentially biological processes should be excluded from patentability and i agree with the proposal to call on the commission to clarify urgently the scope and interpretation of directive 98/44/ec in order to ensure legal certainty as regards the prohibition of patentability of products obtained by essentially biological processes. i therefore agree with the proposal in general and i intend to support it for that reason.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that products obtained by essentially biological processes should be excluded from patentability and used to stimulate innovation and the development of new varieties.
in writing. ‒ patents on products derived from conventional breeding methods or on genetic material necessary for conventional breeding undermine the exclusion laid down in article 53 (b) of the european patent convention and article 4 of directive 98/44/ec which states that 'plant varieties and animal breeds and essentially organic processes for the production of plants or animals shall not be patentable'. this is a principle of the utmost importance! allowing such patents threatens the industry's innovative capacity to develop new varieties and poses a threat to global food production and food security. it will have a negative impact on european competitiveness and may result in monopolies on the food market, reducing the variety of products offered to consumers. the recent decision of the enlarged board of appeal of the european patent office (epo) to grant patents on plant characteristics even when they are developed, or could be obtained, by essentially biological plant breeding techniques should therefore be condemned. for this reason, we are voting in favour of the joint resolution on the request from the agri and juri committees for an oral question on the subject of 'patents for plant discoveries', even though it could have been structured better and provided for greater protection.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which states that products obtained from organic processes, such as plants, seeds, indigenous traits and genes, should be excluded from patentability. plant breeding is an innovative process practised by farmers and farming communities since the birth of agriculture, access to organic material is essential to stimulate innovation, food security and small businesses. for these reasons, the european commission urgently needs to clarify the existing european rules on the legal protection of biotechnological inventions so that it can forward these clarifications to the european patent office (epo) and thus ensure that products obtained by conventional breeding techniques cannot be patentable.
in writing. ‒ the prohibition on patenting plant varieties and essentially organic plant production processes is of great importance, not only from a legal point of view but also from an ethical point of view. for this reason, the recent decision of the enlarged board of appeal of the european patent office to grant patents on plant characteristics even when they are developed, or could be obtained, by essentially biological plant breeding techniques is of considerable concern to us as it poses a threat to world food production and food security itself. the decision will have a negative impact on european competitiveness and may result in monopolies on the food market, reducing the variety of products offered to consumers. the threat to farmers, on the other hand, is even more serious. for these reasons, this resolution seems to us weak and unacceptable, first of all because it does not adequately address the need for the eu to ensure that there is a general derogation for farmers in its legislation on patents relating to plant and animal breeding.

in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution. the subject in question is important from an ethical and scientific point of view and deserves our attention to ensure that the rules in force are strictly observed. this measure calls on the commission to clarify as a matter of urgency the scope and interpretation of directive 98/44/ec, in particular articles 4 and 12, in order to ensure legal certainty as regards the prohibition of patentability of products obtained by essentially biological processes and to clarify that selection with patented biological material is allowed.
in writing. ‒ article 29 of regulation (ec) no 2100/94 on the community plant variety right is incompatible with article 12 of directive 98/44/ec on the legal protection of biotechnological inventions. a plant variety may be protected by a plant patent, but may also contain one or more biotechnological inventions protected by a patent, for example patented genetic components. the danger is that patentability of naturally obtained plant parts could create a monopoly in the food market, thus having a negative impact on competition. to resolve this contradiction, parliament considered it necessary to amend regulation (ec) no 2100/94 by aligning the rules laid down in regulation (ec) no 2100/94 with those laid down in directive 98/44/ec. i voted in favour of this amendment, which i considered necessary, and i hope that the commission will soon clarify the objectives of the existing eu rules on this matter.
in writing. the 'patentable biotechnologies' directive provides that plant varieties, animal breeds and essentially biological processes for the production of plants or animals are excluded from patentability. the european patent office (epo) has recently decided to overturn the directive by allowing patenting of plant products developed using organic selection techniques. as a result, the availability of biological material from many plant varieties will become the prerogative of the biotechnology industries, reinforcing the ongoing trend of the seed market being concentrated in the hands of a few industries. this resolution is intended to combat these abuses, but it is weak because it does not fully defend the rights of farmers. if a crop is contaminated by patented plants, the farmer who owns that field could be sued by the patent holder. we must have the courage to defend the peasants in a strong way. against the overpowering power of agrochemical companies we cannot accept half-measures, and that is why i voted against this resolution. access to plant genetic heritage must be safeguarded in a decisive way.
